column2: share, offer, dedicate, *Kwaaba mapopwe aaya bweelede.* = Share this maize in the right manner. *Mukaintu wa Joojo ulaaba cakulya kubeenzu bamuswaya.* = Joojo's wife shares the food with those who visit her. *Ncibotu kulyaaba kuli Leza.* = It is good to dedicate yourself to God. Extensions of the verb are as follows: (1. passive) -abwa (2. perfect) -abide (3. causative) -abya (4. prepositional) -abila (5. completive) -abilalyo (6. intensive) -abisya (7. repetitive) -aba-aba (8. mutuality) -abana
All verbs follow a *similar pattern* of extensions, although not all may be included after each verb depending on the frequency of actual use.

share with one another, rt. -aba, *Kamwaabana mungu ooyu, bana.* = Children, share this pumpkin with one another. *Basimuswaangano bakaabana mizeezo mibotu mumuswaangano wabo.* = The participants shared good ideas in their meeting. (1. -abanwa, 2. -abanidwe, 3.-abanisya, 4. -abanina, 5. -abaninalyo, 6. -abanisya, 7. -abana-abana)

distribute, rt. -aba, *Kwaabanya nyika cilakatazya.* = It is difficult to share the land. *Mwiiyi naakasika wakatwaabanya mabbuku toonse.* = When the teacher arrived, s/he distributed books to all of us.

be dedicated, *Ndililyaabide kuya kumulela a bana benu.* = I have dedicated myself to looking after you and your children. *Ooyu mukaintu ulyaabide kubamba mukwasyi wakwe.* = This woman has dedicated herself to looking after her family.

give to, rt. -aba, *Kobaabila mbede yabukoko bakaapanyoko.* = Give this clay drinking-container of beer to your grandmother. *Baama bakandiyiisya kuti ndileelede kubalumba bantu akubaabila cakulya ncejisi.* = My mother taught me that I ought to thank people and share with them the food I have.

split stones or wood by repeated blows, *Musankwa waaduula nkuni zyamucitofwu.* = The boy is splitting firewood for the stove. (1.-aduulwa, -2. aduulide, 3. -aduuzya, 4. -aduulila, 5. -aduulilayo, 6. -aduulisya, 7. -aduula-aduula) Also: -andaula, -pandaula.
  • cut cloth, *Ndajana musimbi uwaduula mulembo kutegwa asume cibaki.* = I found the girl cutting the cloth to sew a blouse.
  • operate, *Basilisi baaduula mulwazi.* = The surgeons are operating on the patient. Also: -pandula.

fill up, *Kamwaaka mapopwe musaka.* = Fill the sack with maize. *Komwaaka cakulya mulwazi nkaambo takonzyi kulisanina alikke.* = Put the food in (the mouth of) the patient because he cannot feed himself. *Mwana naalila liya, me nkumwaaka mpopwe kumulomo kuti aumune.* = When the child cried at that time, I stuffed a cob of maize in it's mouth so that it would be quiet. (1.-akwa, 2.-akide, 3.-akisya, 4.-akila, 5.-akilalyo, 6.-akisya, 7.-aka-aka, 8.-akana.)
fail to know, *Ndaakanika kuzyiba muntu wakabba mali angu.* = I have failed to know the person who stole my money. Also: -zimininwa, -alilwa, -kakilwa.
fill for, rt. -aka, *Komwaakila musankwa nyemu musaka atole kubacembele.* = Fill the bag for the boy with groundnuts so that he can take it to the old woman.

take out from, remove, as meal from grinding stone or porridge from a pot, Kwaakula musozya wazukila. = Take the samp out of the mortar as it is ready. (i.e. The first pounding has removed the outer skins from all the grain pellets.) (1.-akulwa, 2.-akulide, 3. -akuzya, 4. -akulila, 5.-akulilalyo, 6.-akulisya, 7.-akula-akula, 8.-akulwidana) Also: -apula
take out for, rt. -akula, Komwaakulila mapopwe aali muncili Cheelo. = You take out the maize for Cheelo which is in the mortar. Also: -akwida.
take back, take out again, rt. akula, Cilakatazya kwaakulula nyama mubwa njaabikka kale mukanwa. = It is hard to take out a piece of meat which a dog has already put in its mouth. Also: -akununa
take out, Kunyina muntu ukonzya kwaakununa nyama iili mukanwa lyaciwena pe. = No person is able to remove the meat which is in the mouth of the crocodile. Also: -akulula
take out for, rt. -akula, Komwaakwida musozya mwana, wazukila. = Take out the samp from the mortar for the child, it is ready. Also: -akulila

be difficult, impossible, Joni caala kusamununa cibaki nkaambo cilaata. = Joni finds it impossible to take off the shirt because it is too tight. Cilaala kukanana mulaka umbi kuti kakunyina uyiisya. = It is difficult to speak another langauge if there is no teacher. Cakaala kusika ku Lusaka nkaambo twakabula moota. = It was impossible to reach Lusaka because we had no car. Mutinta, caala kujika nsima, omupati oonse! = Mutinta, are you unable to cook nsima, you who have grown up! (1. -alilwa, 2. alide, 3. -alisya, 4. -alila, 5.-alilalyo, 6. -alisya, 7. -alaala.)
  • steal from or deprive one of something with violence, Samboko wakali-vwubide lubono lunji, pesi babbi bakamwaala lubono loonse. = Samboko was very rich with much wealth, but thieves violently deprived him of all his goods.

roll on ground as a sign of deep respect, Bakaalaala nibakali kukombela mvwula kumalende. = They rolled on the ground when they were praying for rain at the rain-shrine. Also: -alabana
  • roll in pain or while drunk, Simayoolo ulaalabana nkaambo wakolwa bukoko. = Simayoolo is rolling about because he is drunk with beer.

roll over and over, as deep sign of respect, Bantu banji nobakali kukombela mvwula kumalende bakatalika kwaalabana ansi mukulomba mvwula. = Many people when they were praying for rain began to roll on the ground when they were pleading for rain. Also: -alaala. (3.-alabanisya, 4.-alabanina, 5.-alabanina-lyo, 6.-alabanisya, 7.-alabana-alabana)
  • roll in pain or while drunk, Mwida mwali kucisa, ndali kwiide kwaalabana. = I had abdominal pains, I was just rolling about.

roll on ground, rt. -alabana, Boonse babwa nibakazyila kukuvwima, bakaalabene buyo muduze akaambo kakukatala kapati. When all the dogs came back from hunting, they were just rolling about on the verandah with tiredness.

lean backwards, Kwaalama kukkala kutegwa musilisi akulange kabotu. = Lean backwards so that the doctor can. examine you properly. (2.-alamide,/-aleme, 3.-alamika, 4.-alamina, 5.-alaminalyo, 6.-alamisya, 7.-alama-alama)
cause someone to lean backwards, rt. -alama, Ndakamwaalamika mulwazi kutegwa bamujwe kabotu lino. =
*roll over and over*, *Mu-Iwazi wakali kwaalamuka naakali kuciswa mwida.* = The patient was rolling over and over when he had a stomach pain.

*make roll over*, *Wakasintama alimwi kumujatauka wajana mubili ulakasaala pele nguzu kunyina ubombotoka buyo kumwaalamuna.* = He bent down and touched him and found the body was warm but had no strength and was lifeless as he rolled him over.

* turn over and over in pain*, *Wali kwiide kwaalauka mutwe nkuwali kucisa.* = He was just rolling in pain due to the headache he had. *Chinkonti wali kwaalauka masiku oonse nkaambo kakaambo nkaakaambilwa jilo kakamucisizya moyo kapati.* = Chinkonti kept on tossing about the whole night because of the matter he had been told about which had wounded his heart deeply. Also: *-alabana.*
  • *praise oneself*, *"Ndime Haananombe. Kuti banyama bangu kabakkwene taku cinga candilemena," mbwaakalyaalauka munene.* = "I am the one who has cows. If my animals are enough there is nothing that can be a problem to me," proclaimed the old man.
*turn over*, *Kamunjila, mufwunde munyama, twamwaalawida kale.* = Enter, you may skin the animal, we have already turned it over for you.
*lean back*, rt. *-alama*, *Nitwakasika twakajana mucembele ulaaleme atalaa bbwe.* = When we arrived we found the old woman leaning back on a stone.

*contract a polygamous marriage.* *Michelo wakaalika jilo.* = Michelo has taken another wife yesterday. (1.-alikwa,/-alikilwa, 2.-alikide, 3.-alikizya, 4.-alikilwa, 5.-alikilalyo, 6.-alikisya, 7.-alika-alika)
*be in the state of polygamy*, rt. *-alika*, *Mulumi wabo ulaalikide.* = Their husband is a polygamist. *Siminzyaakwe ulaalikide.* = His uncle is a polygamist.
*be joined in marriage by a second wife.* *Bina Mainza tabacili balikke, bakaalikilwa.* = Mainza's mother is no longer the only wife, she has been joined by a second wife.
*be taken as another wife*, *Nchimunya wakaalikwa kuli Ba Michelo jilo.* = Nchimunya was taken as another wife by Mr. Michelo yesterday.

*be unable*, rt. *-ala*, *Camwaalila kuyupa nyemu.* = She was unable to shell the groundnuts. *Candaalila kutanta mulundu nkaambo ndilaciswa.* = I am unable to climb the hill because I am sick. *Bukali bwakwe bwakali bwakuti walo wakali kukonzya zyoonse zyaalila banamunji.* = His fierce energy was such that he was able to do things which ordinary people were unable to do.
*be impossible for*, *Cana cakaalilwa kulunduka akaambo kakufwunga kapati.* = The child was unable to run because it was so fat.

*going up and down or through various places*, *Maulu akacisa akaambo kakwaaluluka malundu mulweendo lwangu.* = My legs pained because of ascending and descending the hills on my journey. (1-alulukwa, 2.-alulukide, 3.-alulusya, 4. -alulukila, 5.-alulukilalyo, 6.-alulukisya, 7.-aluluka-aluluka.)

*throw, as little burnt clay sticks which children mould and throw into water to teach them how to fish with spears.* (which is a Gwembe Valley children's game) *Ndakajana bana balaama mumulonga wa Zambezi.* = I found the children practicing how to spear fish in the Zambezi river.

say, speak, *Kwaamba ncomuyanda.* = Say what you want. *Kwaamba, ndilalindila kuti undaambile.* = Speak, I am waiting for you to tell me. (1. -ambwa, 2. -ambide, 3.-ambya, 4. -ambila, 5. -ambilalyo, 6. -ambisya, 7. -amba-amba, 8. -ambana)
  • accuse of witchcraft, *Lyali lyansiku kuti muntu wamwaamba bulozi, kwamana waba muzike wakwe.* = In past times if a person accused another of witchcraft, the accuser then became that person's slave.

slander one another, rt. amba, *Mutani kwiide kwaambana aumwi ncaatacita.* = Do not just be slandering each other about deeds which have not been done. Also: -tamana.
  • gossip about one another, *Ba Mutinta a Masowe balikwaambana.* = Mutinta and Masowe have been gossiping about one another. Also: -vwiyana
quarrel about, rt. -amba, *Bantu abaya baambanina myuunda.* = Those people are quarreling about fields. Also: -zwanganina

converse, rt. -amba, *Kamwaambaula kabotu kutegwa bamvwe bali musyule.* = Speak clearly so that the people behind may understand. *Konga ayebo kwaambaula twaambo tumwi.* = You should also make some contribution to the conversation. (1.-ambaulwa, 2.-ambawide 3.-ambauzya, 4. -ambaulila, 5.-ambaulilalyo, 6.-ambaulisya, 7. -ambaula-ambaula, 8. -ambaulana, or ambauzyanya.)

propose to a girl, rt. amba, *Jolezya wakaambila beenzinyina balombe bobile kuti bakamugwasye ikwaambauzya musimbi umwi.* = Jolezya told two of his friends to help him to propose to a certain girl. *Akaambo kakubota kwakwe, Michelo wakacimvwa kwaambauzigwa kubasankwa.* = Because of her beauty, Michelo was tired of being proposed to by men. Also: - bandisya.
  • talk to, *Kamumwaambauzya mweenzu kutegwa atalendelelwi.* = Talk to the visitor so that s/he does not feel lonely. *Ndakajana bamaama balalyaambauzya balikke muncikini.* = I found my mother talking to herself in the kitchen. *Muvwimi naakajaya lubondwe wakalyaambauzya wakati, "Ndilamufwunda munyama ooyu."* = When the hunter killed an impala he said to himself, "I will skin this animal."

talk with one another, rt. -amba, *Tamweelede kucilekela limwi kwaambauzyanya mwalubizyanya.* = You should not stop talking completely to one another when you have offended each another. *Kuti kamutaambauzyanyi inga kamuya kwaambauzyanya akabi.* = If you do not talk to one another now, you will talk to one another at a disaster. (i.e. at a funeral you will be reconciled)

talk to, rt. -amba *Nindasika cifwumofwumo, bataata bakandaambawida twaambo tusiyene-siyene.* = When I arrived this morning, my father talked to me about different matters. *Kwainda buyo woola lyomwe kuzwa ciindi Chimbwali naakaambawide amwanaakwe.* = Just one hour had passed since Chimbwali had talked with his son. (1.-ambawida, 2.-ambawide, 3.-ambauzya, 4.-ambawida, 5.-ambawidalyo, 6.-ambauzya, 7. -ambawida-ambawida, 8. -ambauzyanya.)
  • talk to with the intention of correcting, *Bausyi Mutinta bamwaambawida naakakaka kutwa buntele.* = The father of Mutinta reprimanded her when she refused to pound the groundnuts.
  • talk without proper articulation, *Koleka kwaambawida mumfwundo nkaambo bantu bayanda kumvwa kabotu ncoamba.* = Do not talk indistinctly be cause people want to hear what you are saying.

e dialogue with another in a friendly manner, rt. -amba Notwakaswaana amweenzuma jilo twakaambawidana twaambo tunji, = When I met with my friend yesterday we discussed many things together.
  • discuss in an unfriendly manner, Ngulube zyakalya cimbwali zyakapa kwaambawidana akati kaba Joojo a Mutinta. = The pigs which ate the sweet potatoes caused unfriendly talk between Joojo and Mutinta. Also: -bwentelana.
¢ can be discussed, rt. -amba, Eeci cilaambika nkaambo tacitonawi, = This can be discussed because it is not taboo.
e tell, /z -amba, Sena banyoko bakakwaambila kuti musimbi wakafwa? = Did your mother tell you that the girl died?
¢ be told, rz -amba, Mooba wakasika mpoona mpaakaambilidwe. = Mooba arrived right there at the place where he had been told.
« pray to the ancestral spirits for someone, Usyi wakamwaambilila mwana wakazyila Kkumakuwa, = The father prayed to the ancestors for his child who had returned from work from Europe (or America).

e report, state, Bataata abalo mbambabo, nengambilizya mbuli mbwandipenzya bateelela buyo, kunyina acomwe ncobacita. = That is how my father is, even when I tell him how he troubles me he just listens, he doesn't do a single thing. (1.-ambilizigwa, 2.-ambilizidwe, 3.-ambilizizya, 5.-ambilizizyalyo, 7.-ambilizya-ambilizya, 8. -ambilizyanya.)

e speak up loudly, rt. -amba, Kwaambisya kutegwa mbungano imvwisisisye ncoamba. = Speak up so that the whole gathering can hear clearly what you say.
  • speak with emphasis, Ndaambisya kuti cilatondwa kuyandana zyankwela amucizyi wako. = 1 strongly insist that it is taboo to love your sister sexually.

o have agreed upon, rt. amba, e.q. Ndakafwuma kuya nkukona kucibaka ncitwakaambizyenye amweenzuma kuti tukayaane. = 1 set out early going there to the same place where I and my friend had agreed to meet.

e defecate as a baby, Kuti mwana waambuka, banyina beelede kufwambaana kumusinda. = If a child defecates, the mother should be quick to clean it. (1.-ambukwa, 2.-ambukide, 3.-ambusya, 4.-ambukila, 5.-ambukilalyo, 6.-ambukisya, 7.-ambuka-ambuka, 8.-ambukilana.)
¢ defecate on, Mwana waambukila abulo. = The child has defecated on the bed.

¢ unwind, as strings around a cake of tobacco, Kocaambunana cilundu catombwe. = Unwind the strings around the cake of tobacco. Also: -zambulula, -zambununa, -lambulula (1.-ambunanwa, 2.-ambunanidwe, 3.-ambunazya, 4.-ambunanina, 5.-ambunaninalyo, 6.-ambunanisya, 7.-ambunana-ambunana.)

¢ complain about something, Taala wakandaambwiida bubi nindakauma mwana musyoonto. = My father complained severely to me when I beat the little child. (2.-ambwiidwa, 2.-ambwiide, 4.-ambwiida, 5.-ambwiiidaalyo, 6. -ambwiidana)
e quarrel with one another, Taakwe nobakali kwaambwiidana nokuba kutondekana minwe. = There was never a time when they were quarreling or pointing fingers at one another.
cause to be talked about, rt. amba, Ino cikwaambya makani ali boobu ninzi? = Now what causes you to discuss such matters?

preserve vegetables by compressing or drying in the sun, Kamwaampa kampubu kutegwa tutakapengi cisyu cilimo. = Dry the blackjack so that we will not suffer from lack of relish in the dry season. Mumwezi wa Mukubwe-kaangala inga micelo iligwa mainza iyanda kukuba. Aboobo bamakaintu balatalika kwaampa zisyu. In the month of April the fruits which are eaten in the rainy season are finished. And so the women begin to preserve them for relish. (1.-ampwa, 3.-ampisya, 4.-ampila, 5.-ampilalyo, 6.-ampisya, 7.-ampa-ampa, 8.-ampilana)
  • pat lightly with the palm of the hand, Wakamwaampa lubayi kumeso. S/he patted her/him on the face. Ndakalyaampa ankumo cakukkomana nindakabwezela mali jilo. = I clapped myself on the forehead in joy when I picked up the money yesterday. (1.-ampwa, 2.-ampide, 3.-ampya, 4.-ampila, 5.-ampilalyo, 6.-ampisya, 7.-ampa-ampa, 8. -ampilana.) (note: the word ampa can also be used as a pronoun meaning 'target' or 'destination', Kotijaana kusikila limwi uka-sike ampa mpoowambilwa. Run until you reach the spot where you were told.)
  • say or do something vigourously, Musankwa wakatamikizigwa kumisya musimbi, waampa ansi kukazya. = The boy who was accused of impregnating the girl, denies the case entirely. (i.e. when people want to show that what they say is the truth they pat the ground with the palms of their hands and raise their arms upwards.)
  • lose weight, (-li-ampa) Mutinta wakalijisi mubili mubotu pesi sunu waka lyaampa. Mutinta had a healthy body, but nowadays she has lost a lot of weight.
  • intensify, become widespread, Mudima waampa ansi. The darkness increased over the earth.

grope, feel things over with hands, search around for, Mwana watalika akwaampa-ampa akali lukolo. = The baby began to grope for where the breast was. Kamwaampa-ampa nokusiya mulaimvwa nyeleti mpiibede. = Even though it is dark, grope about and you will feel where the needle is. Wakali kwaampa-ampa munkomo kayeeya kuti ulajana mali, pesi kunyina ngaakajana. = He searched around in his pocket hoping to find money, but he found nothing. Also: -jatauka, -yayaanga.
pat or stroke continually, rt. -ampa-ampa, Wakamwaampaampaula caluyando. = S/He stroked her/him gently with love.
be bent upwards, as hand or head of hoe, Meno aakwe akaile kwaampamana mbuli jamba libi. = His teeth are bending upwards like a bad hoe.
be in a bent state, rt. ampamana, Eeli jamba lilaampamene, talilimi kabotu. = The hoe-head has become bent upwards, it does not dig well.

cause to bend, as hand or head of hoe, Michelo walyaampamika jamba. Michelo bent the blade of the hoe. (1.-ampamikwa, 2.-ampamikide, 3.-ampamisya, 5. -ampamikilalyo, 6.-ampamikisya, 7.-ampamika-ampamika)

rebel, Mwamubona musankwa mbwaampanya kukazya? = Have you seen how the boy is rebelling by refusing to cooperate?
  • take an indirect course, Syuumbwa natanda munyama tagami, ulaampanya ambali. A lion when it is chasing an animal does not go straight for it, but goes in an indirect way to the side.
slap, rt. -ampa, Naakamutukila, walo nkokumwaampasyila. = When he insulted her, she slapped him severely.

slp with hand several times, Mutinta wamwaampaula tubayi mwana naasuba abulo. = Mutinta slapped the child several times when it urinated on the bed. (1.-ampaulwa, 2.-ampaude, 3.-ampauzya, 4.-ampaulila, 5.-ampaulilalyo, 6.-ampaulisya, 7.-ampaula-ampaula, 8.-ampaulana)
be preserved, rt. -ampa, Bantu bakali kulya buyo zilyo zyaampidwe anyama njumu. = The people were only eating preserved food with dried meat.
nickname, Beenzinyina bakalimwaampikizizye amazina manjaanji nkaambo kamilimo yakwe yabumpelenge. = His friends nicknamed him with many bad names because of his deeds of deceit. Also: -antikizya
slap (once), Ndamwaampula lubayi mwana. = I have given the child a slap. (1.-ampulwa, 2.-ampulide, 3.-ampuzya, 4.-ampulila, 5.-ampulilalyo, 6.-ampulisya, 7.-ampula-ampula, 8.-ampulana)

disappear gradually as a cloud, dry up, Yaamuka mvwula, mweende kumuunda. = When the rain stops, you can go to the field. (The rain has stopped, go to the field.) (2.-amukide, 3.-amusya, 4.-amukila, 5.-amukilalyo, 6.-amukisya, 7.-amuka-amuka)
had ceased, Imvwula yaamukide kale nindasika. = The rain had already stopped when I arrived. Also: -timuka, -tamuka, -tamuna.

tell a story, Mucembele ulaana zyaano zibotu. = The old lady tells good stories. Lyoonse kumangolezya nobamana kulalila, bapati balaana akutalika kabati, "Mbokaaninga", abalo bana balavwiila balati "Galangati". = Always in the even ing when they had finished the evening meal, the elders tell stories and begin by saying "Mbukaaninga' and the children answer, "Galangati". (1.-anwa, 2.-anide, 4.-anina, 5.-aninalyo, 6.-anisya, 7.-ana-ana)

waver from one point to another in speaking, Koleka kwaanaika mukwaamba kwako nkaambo bantu tabakwe kuzyiba masimpe. = Stop speaking in an ambivalent manner because people will not know the truth.
  • throw about here and there, Musankwa wakalikwaanaika mali akwe oonse naakali kubeleka. = The boy was wasting all his money when he was employed.

strike by lightning, Imvwula yakaanda bantu bobile jilo. = The rain, (i.e. the lightning), struck two people yesterday.
  • freeze, Mpeyo yabaanda bana masiku nkaambo tabajisi mapayi. = The cold froze the children at night because they had no blankets. (1.-andwa, 2.-andide, 3.-andya, 6.-andisya, 7.-anda-anda)
  • notch, as a cow's ear to identify the owner, Bantu balaanda nombe mumatwi. = People notch cattle on the ears.
  • accuse vehemently, Mwiiyi wakaile kumwaanda buya sicikolo akumuuma katakwe kaambo. = The teacher vehemently accused the pupil and beat him without reason.

separate, Bantu bakaandaana ciindi nobakamana kumvwana. = The people separated when they had understood one another. (1.-andaanizigwa, 2.-andeenye, 3.-andaanya, 4.-andaanina, 5.-andaaninalyo, 6.-andaanisya, 7.-andaana-andaana.)
be separated, Minzi yobile eyi yakaandaanizigwa amunyinza. = These two villages were separated by a boundary.

separate, Mucembele wakabaandaanya bana naakabona nkobaIwana lyoonse. The old woman separated the childen when she saw how they were always fighting. (1.-andaanizigwa, 2.-andaanide, 3.-andaanizizya, 4.-andaanzizya, 5.-andaanzizyalyo, 6.-andaanisya, 7.-andaanya-aandaanya) Also: -andanya, -pambulana.
become late in the evening, Atukoone, bwaandalala busiku. = Let us sleep, it is getting late in the night.
work without help, Lyoonse Mutinta yakali kumwaandamina milimo. Mutinta was always left to do all the work without help.
separate, Nzila zilaandana atala amulundu. The roads separate at the top of the hill.
diverge, Mali ndaajana anzila mpozyaandanina. = I found money where the paths diverge. Ukasike aalya andanina nzila. = Go straight there to where the paths diverge. Also: -palana nzila.
divide into parts, separate Kamubaandanya bana balacisana. = Separate the children, they will hurt one another. Kuvwiya ncibi nkaambo caandaanya bantu. = Gossiping is bad because it divides people.

be split up, e.g Inanda yangu yaandauka, bulongo tiibwakajatana kabotu. My house cracked because the clay did not stick together (i.e. It was not well mixed.) Citende cakaandauka nicakaloka kuzwa amutwe. = The pumpkin split apart when it fell from the head. Milomo yabo yakaandauka akuyuma nta akaambo kampeyo. Their lips were chapped and dry because of the cold. Also: -pandauka.
broken in pieces, Tubeela twacitende twakali kwaandaukila ansi. Pieces of the pumpkin were broken up on the ground.

beat with repeated blows, chop up, grind, Nkuni bazyaandaula kale. = They have already chopped up the firewood. Kamwaandaula mapopwe kuti abe masembe. = Grind the maize into smaller particles. Bakamwaandaula mbayi nzyatanabwene kuzwa naakazyalwa. = They hammered him with blows which he had never seen since he was born. (1.-andaulwa, 2.-andawide, 3.-andauzya, 4.-andaulila, 5.-andaulilalyo, 6.-andaulisya, 7.-andaula-andaula, 8.-andaulilana) Also: -pandaula.
crack, Miindi yangu yatalika kwaandauzya ibee ncimbwali caata mumubundu. The calves of my legs were cracking like a sweet-potatoe in an overcrowded mound.
be diverse, rt. -andana, Misyobo yabantu ilaandeene. = The tribes of people are diverse. Mapopwe aya alaandeene This maize is of different varieties.
be cracked, Munkuli wakaanduka naakautula ansi. The gourd cracked when she put it down on the ground. Also: -kwamuka, -panduka.

crack, split, open up, operate on, tear as a cloth, Mwana wacaandula cibiya. The child cracked the pot. Basilisi bakamwaandula mwana wakali kuciswa. = The doctors operated on the child who was sick. {wakaandula nkanya = the child who opened the womb. (i.e. the first-born) } (1.-andulwa, 2.-andukide, 3.-andusya, 4.andukila, 5.-andukilalyo, 6.-andukisya, 7.-andula-andula.)
  • demarcate by opening a furrow, open a path through high grass, Bana, kamwaandula bulimo busyoonto. = Children, make a furrow to demarcate a small section to be ploughed. Wakanyandwa kapati kubona mpwitamamina iandula mabanda kuya kuyanda musamu warjombe. = He was very surprised to see a nose-dripping youngster opening a way through the plains going in search of a charm to increase cattle.
pass through the middle, Jolezya wakaandulula akati kamuunda wangu. Jolezya passed through the middle of my field. (1.-andululwa, 2.-andulukide)

be struck by lightning, rt. anda, Cisamu cakaandwa mvwula jilo. = The tree was struck by lightning yesterday.
  • be frozen, Mabbanana akaandwa mpeyo. The bananas were frozen with the cold.

• tie, arrest, Jolezya bakamwaanga naakabba mucintoolo. = They arrested Jolezya when he stole in a shop. Kamwaanga mubwa, atalumi bantu. = Tie up the dog so that it does not bite people. Kamwaanga bwizu mumisunta kutegwa ibwezegwe kabotu. = Tie the grass in bundles so that they can be carried easily. Mpola yausyi ipegwa kumwana, lyoonse ilasubila alimwi yaangwa kukuboko kwalulyo. The bracelet given to the baby by the father is always red and it is tied on the right arm. (1.-angwa, 2.-angide, 3-anzya, 4.-angila, 5.-angilalyo, 6.-angisya, 7.-anga-anga, 8.-angilana.)

cikoto = tie a knot
  • freeze, thicken, curdle, solidify, Mukupa inga ulaanga wabikkwa mutontola. Milk gets frozen when put in a cold place (i.e. a fridge). Kuti musinza wanyama yamafwuta watontola, ulaanga. = If soup of fatty meat cools, it thickens. (kulyaanga makoto or kulyaanga masuma = to coagulate into lumps.)
  • tie the spirit, Buzuba bwakwaangwa cifwuwa, buzuba bwakumena muzi mo nobwakali kusika, kwakali kusalwa mulombwana munkutwe, musazinyina asikwaazwa. When the day arrived for tying the bone, the day for swallowing the spirit, a young man was picked, a relative of the dead man.
fly high, Makumbi alaangama mujulu. = The clouds are moving high in the sky. (1.-angamikwa, 2.-angeme, 3.-angamya, 4.-angamika, 5.-angamikilalyo, 7.-angama-angama)
be hanging, hovering, rt. angama, Sikakonze ulaangeme mujulu kweena twana twankuku. = The hawk is hanging aloft, eyeing the chickens.

be expansive, as the chest, Akaambo kakubeleka kapati, camba ca Chimuka caangamana. = Because of working hard Chimuka's chest expanded. (i.e. chest protrudes and back hollows.) Also: -balala.
  • stand in awe, Wakaangamana akulanga mukugambwa. He stood in awe and looked in amazement. Also: -ankamana
be expanded, rt. -angamana, Camba cako cilaangamene. = Your chest is expansive.

• tie one another, rt. -anga, Bana, cilatondwa kwaangana loozi munsingo nomusobana cakuvwolekana. = Children, it is taboo to tie one another by the neck when playing the game of yoking one another (like cattle).
  • congeal as blood, coagulate, rt. -anga, Minwe yangu yaangana nkaambo bulowa tabweendi kabotu. Ndabaa cinywe. My fingers have become stiff because the blood is not flowing. I am numb.
  • be tongue-tied, Nindakali kubetekwa, mulaka wakaangana, aboobo tiindakakanana kabotu pe. When I was being tried I was tongue-tied, and so I did not speak well.
  • become immobile, as with fear, *Babbi nobakadonkola nanda ndakaangana, tiindakakonzya kucita cintu.* = When the thieves broke into the house I was frozen with fear, I was unable to do anything.

be tongue-tied, stammer, *Ndakaile kwaangatila nindakali kuyanda kwaamba cimwi cintu mumuswaangano.* = I was tongue-tied when I wanted to say something at the meeting. (1.-angatilwa, 2.-angatide, 3.-angatizya, 4.-angatilila, 5.-angatililalyo, 6.-angatisya, 8.-angatilana) Also: -kankatila, -babayisyas, -yayausya, -uusya, -bebeezya.
  • refuse to move, stick to one position, *Mukaintu wangu waangatila kwabo, tayandi kuboola kumunzi wangu.* = My wife persists in staying at her parents home, she does not want to come to my home. Also: -jatilila, -kakatila, -zyazyatila.
be mentally and physically inactive, rt.-angana, *Ulaangene.* = He is inactive in mind and body.
tied, knit, *Ooyu munene naambaula boobo, kumeso kwakwe wakaangide tunkusa.* = When the old man talked like that, his face was lined with furrows.
be tied, rt. -anga, *Moomba naakabba nombe yamunene, wakalaangidwe.* = Moomba was arrested when he stole the cow of the old man.

take by force, appropriate, *Wakayaangila nombe itali yakwe.* = He took a cow which was not his own. Also: -taminina.
  • be caught, be stuck in, *Cisani cawuuka muwo caangila mucisamu.* = The cloth that has been blown away by the wind is caught in the tree. *Kayuni nkindauma amalekani kaangila amutabi wacisamu.* = The bird, which I hit with a catapult, is caught on the branch of a tree. (2.-angilwa)
  • hold on illegally, *Misozi wayaangila nanda, wakaka kuzwa nasika ulaayo.* = Misozi held on to the house, she refused to move even after the owner had arrived. Also: -zyazyatila, -anyina.
  • tie for, rt. -anga, *Kamundaangila bwizu kutegwa ndibubweze kabotu.* = Tie the grass for me so that I can carry it easily.

tie on to, connect, rt. -anga, *Masowe wakaambila mwanaakwe usuba abulo kuti, "Bumwi buzuba uyakucibona nkaambo ndiyakukwaangilila nciinga cula mucibuno."* = Masowe told his child who had urinated on the bed, "One day you will get it because I will tie a horrible frog to your waist." (1.-angililwa, 2.-angilidwe, 3.-anzya)

drop down suddenly, *Mutinta mbwaasikila buyo kuzwa ku Lusaka, waide kwaanguka akufwa.* = As soon as Mutinta arrived from Lusaka, s/he collapsed and died. *Naakatijaana kaindi kalamfwu, wakaile kwaanguka wafwa akaambo kakukatala.* = When he had been running for a long time, he just dropped and died because of exhaustion. *Musankwa wakali kucela matobo wakaanguka kuzwa mumutobo akulicisa.* = The boy who was gathering matobo fruit, fell down out of the tree and hurt himself. *Muyuni wakaanguka kuzwa muciteente.* = The big bird fell down from the nest. *Bbaasi ndeelyo lyaanguka kuzwa kumusanza.* = There is the bus dropping in from the south. Also: -ngenyuka

take down *Kwaangula cisaka canyemu cilaa ciluli cananda.* = Take down the sack of groundnuts which is on the roof of the house. (1.-angulwa, 2.-angwide, 3.-anguzya, 4.-angwida, ors, -anguda, 5.-angwidalyo, 6.-angulisya, 7-angula-angula.) Also: -anzula
  • start a song Kwaangula kabotu ciimbo nocitiibote. = Lead the song properly and it will go well. Also: -tunga, -taanguna

be free, be released, rt. anga, Lino ndaanguluka nkaambo mu-landu wangu ndaubbadela. = I am free now because I paid for my crime.
  • become loose, Cileye cankuni caanguluka nindali kutija mubwa. = The bundle of firewood became loose when I was running away from a dog.

free, release, untie, rt. anga Munene bakamwaangulula muntolongo. = They let the old man free from prison. Kamuzyaangulula nkuni zyaleta bacembele kutegwa tujisye. = Untie the bundle of firewood which the old woman brought so that we use it for cooking. (1.-angululwa, -2.-angulwide, 3.-anguluzya, 4.-anguluda, 5.-anguludalyo, 6.-angululisya, 7.-angulula-angulula, 8.-angululidana)
  • perform ritual of receiving a member of the family back home, Kaindi mulombwana naakali kupiluka kuzwa kumbeleku, usyi nguwakali kwaangulula mukuli. = Long ago when a boy returned from work, his father would `untie the luggage.' (This was a custom of the past whereby a son when returning from work in a distant place would bring back a box full of goods and offer it to the father. When the father opened the box he was said to -angulula mukuli.)
give birth, Nakayila waangunuka masiku akuleta mwana musankwa. = Nakayila gave birth at night and brought forth a boy child. Also: -tumbuka, -yoboloka.

undo, rt. -anga, Kamumwaangununa lutambo musune akacele kabotu. = Undo the rope with which the ox is tied so that it can graze properly.
  • a ritual which a girl must undergo who has been taken unlawfully in marriage, Mutinta wakaangululwa kale, kwacaala buyo kukwelwa. = Mutinta was already returned to her parent's home, what. remains was to carry out the correct ritual practice. (i.e. by 'pulling' her away from her parent's home to the boy's village.) (1.-angununwa, 3.-angunuzya, 4.-angunwida, 5.-angunwidalyo, 6.-angununisya, 7.-angununa-angununa, 8.-angunwidana,)
untie for someone, Kolindila nencikwaangunwida mukuli wako. = Wait while I untie your load.

celebrate to give good luck to someone who has achieved something out of the ordinary, Bina Chibbamu wakaleta kabiya mwakali mombo kuti Sicibende aanquzule. = Bina Chibbamu brought a dish in which was a cooked dove so that the ritual to honour Sicibende could be carried out.

be tied or imprisoned, rt. anga, Ooyu musankwa ulaangwaangwa nkaambo kakutaleka kubba. = This boy is being continually imprisoned for persisting in stealing. (1.-angidwe, 2.-angizigwa, 4.-angilwa, 5.-angilwalyo, 6.-angisya)
  • be quickly tied, Kowangwa-angwa masusu aako tweende, twabinda. = Tie up your hair quickly so that we go, we are in a hurry.
lose the voice, Cazimina camwaanga jwi ncaaleka kukanana munene. = It is not known what blocked the voice which made the old man stop talking.

tell a story to someone, rt. ana, Njanda kumwaanina caano casulwe anondo. = I want to tell you a story of the hare and the tortoise. Atweende kuli baneene, ndiza balatwaanina twaano. = Let us go to grandmother perhaps she will tell us stories.
  • turn away from, Chilala naakakomena wakabaanina bakaapanyina akubasiya balapenga. = When Chilala grew up she abandoned his grandmother and left her to suffer. Ndabwaanina bukoko. = I have turned away from beer. Kunyina muntu uyelede kwaanina cibbadela. = No one should turn away from the hospital.
begin, Oyu mwana waanka kale kulila. = This child has already begun to cry. Also: -talika, -kanka.

falter in action, Koleka kwaanka-anka kujata, kosala biyo comwe cintu. Stop hesitating about what you should take, just chose one thing. Nibaandaambila kusala cibaki muli zyaali mubbokesi, ndakatalika kwiile kwaanka-anka. = When I was asked to choose a shirt from among the ones which were in the box, I started fumbling undecidedly.

be moved, be afraid, disturbed, Bana baankamana nibamvwa kulila kwabantu. The children were afraid when they heard the wailing of the people. Umwi mukaintu naakasika kumuunda wakaankamana naakajana kuti kuli bamubbida. = When a certain woman reached the field, she was startled to find that there were people who had stolen from her.

perplex, surprise, amaze, Majwi aakandaambila mwana akandaankamika. = The words which the child said to me surprised me. Ciindi cabwiinga bwakaindi kwakali kwiimba akuzyana kwaankamika alimwi kwaandeene. = During a marriage of long ago there was an amazing variety of singing and dancing.

evade by prevarication, 'beat about the bush' Kwaamba cacigaminina, koleka kwaantaika kutegwa bapati bakugwasye. Speak directly, stop beating about the bush, so that the elders can help you. Also: -tamauka, -anaika.

call one by nickname, Bakandaantikizya zina lya Chiyobeka nkaambo kakukananisya. = They nicknamed me Chiyobeka because of being talkative. Izina muntu oyo ndibaamwaantikizya ategwa ngu Saatani nkaambo wakali kucenga bantu. The name by which they nicknamed that man is Satan because he deceived people. (1.-antikizigwa, 2.-antikizidwe, 3.- antikizizya, 6-antikizisya, 8.-antikizyanya.) Also: -anzikizya, -ulikizya, -zalikizya.
obstruct, Wakamwaantila mweenzinyina cakuti taakali kukonzya kubona cakali kumpela lyakwe. = He blocked his friend in such a way that he could not see what was before him. Also: -sinkilila

be or become wise, Miyoba wakaanuka akaambo kamapenzi. = Miyoba became wise through the experience of sufferings.
  • recall, Ndakaanuka lufwu Iwabataata. I recalled the death of my father. Also: -yeeya, -ibaluka.
  • become sexually immoral, Musimbi wakalomenye wakaanuka naakeenda a musankwa mupati. The girl who was upright became sexually immoral when she went about with an older man.

change behaviour from good to bad, Ooyu mwana ncamwaanuna mmapenzi aakufwidwa bausyi abanyina. = What makes this child immoral is the sufferings of losing her/his father and mother. (1.-anunwa, 2.-anunide, 3.-anusya, 8.-anunisyanya)
give good advice, rt. -anuka, Mudaala wakaanusya mwana wakwe amajwi mabotu. = The old man instructed his child with wise words. Also: -cenjeżya
take illegally, Chigabba wakayaanyina mpongo iitali yakwe. Chigabba took a goat unjustly which was not his. Also: -taminina. =

compose a song, Mweemba wakaanza ciimbo cibandauka nombe zyakwe. = Mweemba composed a song praising his cattle. Also: -panga. (1.-anzwa, 2.-anzide, 3.-anzizya, 4.-anzila, 5.-anzilalyo, 6.-anzikizya, 7.-anzaanza.)
  • initiate, Chimuka wakaanza nzila iikosola kuya kumantoolo. = Chimuka opened a path cutting across to the stores. Muntu wakaanza kupaila mizimo wakalini? = Who was the first person to begin offering sacrifice to the spirits?
  • provoke, Sibukoko wakaanza bana mbaakajana beembela nombe. = The drunkard provoked the children whom he found herding cattle. Also: -soka, -talika
spread out to dry in the sun Kozyaanzala nswa kutegwa ziyume. = Spread out the flying termites in the sun so that they dry out. Also: -yanzala.
get stuck between, Nkaaka kasanga ulidokonozye nyama yakuanzamina mumenyo. = Here is a piece of grass for you to use to pick pieces of meat stuck between your teeth. Also: -patila
have particles stuck between the teeth, rt. -anzamina, Waanzaminwa makwaa mangamwe ngaalikulya. = He got particles of boiled maize which he was eating stuck between his teeth.
fall heavily Ula-anzamuka kuzwa mucisamu kuti kota-jatisyi. = You will fall off the tree if you do not hold on tightly. Wakaanzamuka kulila. = She cried painfully. Also: -anzuka, -anguka.

address another in a wrong way, Wakamwaanzamukila kuti ngu Chula kakuli walo ngu Mutinta. = H/She called him/her Chula, while his/her real name is Mutinta. Mainza wakandaanzamukila kunditukila akati kabapatima. = Mainza insulted me by addressing me in a wrong way before my fellow elders. (1.-anzamukilwa, 2.-anzamukide, 5.-anzamukilalyo, 6.-anzamukisya, 8.-anzamukilana) Also: -onzomokela, -unzumukila.

slap with palm of hand Wamwaanzamuna lubayi mwana. = She slapped the child. (1.-anzamunwa, 2.-anzamwide, 3.-anzamusya, 4.-anzamwida, 5.-anzamwidalyo, 6.-anzamunisya, 7.-anzamuna-anzamuna, 8.-anzamunana.) Also: -kwapa, -zenzemas, -zenzemuna, kukamba.

separate, Cheelo a Mweemba bakaanzana. = Cheelo and Mweemba separated. Bubala a Chimuka bakaanzana nibakamana kulya musalo. = Bubala and Chimuka parted company after the conversation. Also: -andana. (2.-anzanide, 3.-anzanisya, 4.-anzanina, 5.-anzaninalyo, 6.-anzanisya)
struggle, Musimbi bakamwaanzanganya akumutizya natayandi. They struggled with the girl and dragged her away against her will. Also: -azanganya (1-anzanganizigwa, 2.-anzanganizidwe)
separate, Banyina bakabaanzanya bana babo kuzwa kubana babamwi bantu. = The mother separated her children from other people's children. (1.-anzanganyizigwa, 2.-anzanganizidwe) Also: -andanya, -anzana

beat, slap, Noowunka matwi oonse asinka nkobali kukwaanzaula mbayi. When you went, both ears were blocked where they were slapping you about. (1.-anzaulwa, 2.-anzauzya, 3.-anzaulisya, 4.-anzaulila, 5.-anzaulilalyo, 6.-anzaulisya, 7.-anzaula-anzaula, 8.-anzaulana)

hang up, put on shelf, load up, Kamwaanzika zisani amulenga. = Hang the clothes on the line. Kubwaanda bwananda yamunanga kwakaanzikidwe zintu zinji mbuli zifwuwa amitwe yabantu bakafwa. = On the wall of the witchdoctor's house were hanging many things such as the bones and skulls of dead people. Also: -gobeka (1.-anzikwa, 2.-anzikide, 3.-anzikizya, 4.-anzikila, 5.-anzikilalyo, 6.-anzikisya, 7.-anzika-anzika, 8.-anzikilana.)
  • install a spirit in home, Muzimo bakauwaanzika kubwaanda. = They installed the spirit of the dead in the wall. (This is a custom whereby if a dead person had a disease, his/her spirit is not transferred to another living person, but is lodged temporarily in the wall of a house.)

hang something for someone, Mwamana kwaanzika zisani zyanu, kamundaanzikizizya jansi lyangu. = When you are finished hanging your clothes, also hang my coat for me. (1.-anzikizilwa, 2.-anzikizizya, 4.-anzikizila, 5.-anzikizilalyo, 6.-anzikizisya, 7.-anzikizizya-anzikizizya, 8.-anzikilana.)

nickname, invent a story, Baneene bakandaanzikizya zina lyamuntu utali musazima. = My grandmother nicknamed me with the name of a person who was not my relative. Mwami wesu wakabaanzikizya kuti "Ibana bakuzuma mvwula". = Our Lord nicknamed them "the children of thunder." (1.-anzikizigwa, 2.-anzikizidwe, 8.-anzikizyanya Also: -antikizya, -zalikizya.
be nicknamed, Izina eelyo ndyakwaanzikizigwa. = That name is of being nicknamed.
give a new name, rt. -anza, Bakamwaanzilila zina lya Chilala. = They gave him/her the new name of Chilala. Also: -ulikizya (rt. -ulika)
wake up with a fright, Naakaanzimuka wakayoowa kapati. = After waking from a nightmare s/he was very frightened. Also: -bbatamuka,

die suddenly, Waile kwaanzuka. = S/He just died suddenly. Also: -anguka.
  • fall from a height, Bbodela lyakapwaika nilyakaanzuka kuzwa atebule. = The bottle was smashed when it fell down from the table.
take down from a high place, Mutinta waanzula ndongwe kuzwa mucisanza. = Mutinta is taking down the groundnuts from the platform. (1.-anzulwa, 2.-anzulide, 3.-anzulizya, 8.-anzulilana)

be warmed up, Bana bakafwide mpeyo bakaanzuluka nibakayota mulilo. = The children who had been cold were warmed up when they sat beside the fire. Zuba lyapasula, banyama azikalaba ansi zilaanzulukwa. = When the sun rises the animals and crawling things on the earth are warmed up.

recompose, rt. -anza, Ciimbo ncookaanza tacili kabotu, weelede kucaanzulula. = The song which you composed is not good, you should recompose it. (-anzululwa)
  • melt a solid to liquid, Kwaanzulula meenda angide, nkwaabikka azuba. = To melt ice is to put it in the sun. cf. -zinzula.
  • invigorate, Zuba lyapasula, banyama azikalaba ansi zilaanzulukwa. = When the sun rises the animals and things which crawl on the earth are invigorated.

greet, Kamubaanzya nomusika kwa Kawaile. = Greet them when you reach Kawaile. Ndabaanzya bakuli ba Kawaile. = I greet the people of Kawaile. Give a belated greeting = -anzya mutompo (1.-anzigwa, 2.-anzyide, 3.-anzisya, 4.-anzila, 5.-anzilalyo, 6.-anzisya.)
  • cause to be arrested, rt. -anga, Ndakamwaanzya kumasilikani kutegwa mpumune kubbidwa. = I had him arrested by the police so that I might have a break from being robbed.
  • tie with, rt. -anga, Basimbi bakaanzya loozi luyumu nibakali kutebba nkuni. When the girls were gathering firewood they tied it up with strong fibres.

bind securely with, rt. -anga, Kamwaanzya-anzya loozi lubotu misunta yabwizu. = Bind the bundles of grass securely with good fibres.
  • greet quickly, Kamwaanzya-anzya bantu tweende. Greet the people quickly so that we can go.

be divided in groups, Mikowa yoonse yakaapaulwa mumanyika-manyika mbubona bwakacimbaulwa meenda anyika. All the races were divided into different lands just as the water and the land were partitioned. (1.-apaulwa, 2.-apaulide, 8.-apaulana)
divide, Ciindi cakasika mpuuwaapawida muwo wamainza acilimo. = The time came when the wind divides the rainy and the dry season.
be given a share of, Bantu bakatalika kwaapawidwa pobwe. = The people began to be given a share (of the food) of the feast.

dish out, take out meal from mortar, Koapula nsima yabasankwa. = Dish out the nsima for the men. Ucimana kujika, nkujula akwaapula munkwandi. = When you finish cooking, take it off the fire and put it in a wooden dish. (1.-apulwa, 2.-apwidwe, 3.-apuzya, 4.-apwida, 5.-apwidalyo, 6.-apulisya, 7.-apula-apula, 8.-apwidana.)

share out, Kuti bayanda kujaya bujwejwe, tuconco atutiiti, basala cilawo aasowelwa busenga ampobakwaapwidwa musozya. = If they want to kill small birds, (bujwejwe, tuconco, tutiiti), they choose a place where bran has been thrown out or samp has been shared out.

open mouth widely, Utani kwiile kwaasama, ulanjilwa nzinini mukanwa! = Don't just open your mouth widely, it will be filled with flies! (1.-asamikwa, 2.-aseme, 3.-asamuzya, 4.-asamukila, 5.-asamikilalyo, 6.-asamisya, 7.-asama-asama, 8.-asamikana) Also: -lakana, -lakamas, -asamuka open mouth widely, yawn, Mwatalika kale kwaasamuka kakucili mangolezya! = You have already started yawning while it is so early in the evening! Nibakanjila munanda, bakajana mulwazi wiile kwaasamuka akufwekemba kapati. = When they entered the house, they found the patient opening his mouth widely and panting. Bana bakatalika kusinsimuka, kwaasamuka akulyoolola. The children began to wake up, yawn and stretch themselves. (1.-asamunwa, 2.-aseme, 3.-asamuzya, 4.-asamukila, 5.-asamukilalyo, 6.-asamukisya, 7.-asamuka-asamuka)
cause the mouth to open, Kamumwaasamuna mubwa anywisigwe musamu. = Open the dog's mouth so that it can be given the medicine to drink.
have mouth wide open, rt. asama, Banyina bakasyaala baaseme buyo. His mother was left just openmouthed.
be pushed aside, rt. -asya, Basicikolo baniini baasigwa mucimbayambaya ciindi lyaboola bapati-pati. = The smaller pupils were displaced when the bigger boys came into the lorry.

displace, push aside, take up more space, rt. -ata, Nindakali kuyota mulilo, mweenzuma wakandaasya mpindakakkede. = When I was warming myself at the fire, my friend pushed me aside from the place where I was sitting. (1.-asigwa, 2.-asyide.)
  • evict, Amubone nobantu bangu, aaba bana Sialyabbubba batwaasya, ino tucite buti? = Look my people, these people of Sialyabbubba are pushing us out, now what should we do?

be pushed together, rt. -ata Bantu baasyanya mumootokala. = The people are squeezed together in the vehicle. Ngoma noyakalila bakabona nkwilimba zyadilimuka kwaasyanya kuzwa munanda. = When the drum sounded, they saw the pidgeons scattering, piling together to get out of the house. Also: -syankana.

be too large to fit, Muzovwu ulaata amulyango warnanda. = The elephant is too large to pass through the door. Joni ulineneede, ulaata mucibaki eeci. = Joni is fat, he cannot fit into this shirt. Bantu nibakaata munanda, bamwi bakoona anze. = When the people were packed in the house, some slept outside. Mapopwe aata mubutala. = All the maize cobs are too many for the maize-bin to hold. (1.-atwa, 2.-atide, 3.-atizya, 4.-atila, 5.-atilalyo, 6.-atisya, 7.-ataata.)
be overcome with emotion, Nenjeeya Elizabeth inga ndatelaika, camba caatikila. = When I remember Elizabeth I ponder, my heart overflows. (1.-atikilwa)

squeeze, Kosola kwaatikizya kusama mabbusu. = Try to squeeze yourself into this pair of shoes. Kolyaatikizya buyo kunjila mumoota, weenda uleela. = Squeeze yourself into the car, when it starts to move you will find enough room for yourself. (1.-atikizigwa, 2.-atikide, 3.-atikizya, 4.-atikizyila)

press on top of, or against, one another, Bantu ncobasondoka biyo inga mizeezo yavwulisya yaatikizyanya mucamba. = That is why people just go mad perhaps thoughts become too many and pile up in the heart.

stick, as in a gap, rt. -ata, Impopwe yaatila mumpemo yamwana. = The maize grain has got stuck in the child's nostril. Also: -patila.
  • claim something to be yours, Wawaatila mutiba uutali wako. = You have claimed a plate which is not yours.

leave due to unfavourable circumstances, Wakaatuka akaambo kalukomo. = She had to leave because of being ill-treated. Mukaintu wa Munene wakaatuka buzumi nibwakamuyumina. = The wife of Munene had to leave when life became too hard for her. Banyama boonse bakaatuka akaambo kabantu bavwuzyanya mucisi. = All the animals left because people multiplied in the territory. Mbanji banalumi a basankwa bakali kwiide koona musyokwe mazubaayo nkaambo muminzi bakali kwaatuka kuumwa. = In those (colonial) days many young men and boys were just sleeping in the bush because in the villages they were leaving because of been beaten. (1.-atulwa, 2.-atukide, 3.-atusya)
leave, Koose kusanduka kuli namalelo cakalaalide, nanda mpati wakaliyaatukide. = All alternative visitng of the head wife was put aside, the main house was left out.

remove someone by force, Bakamwaatula atongo lyabausyi. = They forced him out of his father's original home. Wakali kuyoowa kuti balamwaatula amulimo akaambo kaluzyibo ndobakajisi. = He was afraid that they would remove him from the job because of the information which they had.

cause to remove, rt. -atula, Wakali makoto waciwena cakunga kwaanyina ciwena umbi wakali kukonzya kumwaatusya abwina oobu kuti anjile pe. = It was a brute of a crocodile which made it impossible for any other crocodile to push it aside from the entrance of the hole in order to enter.
cause to be too much, rt. -ata, Bunjaka bwakali amunzi wakwe bwakamwaatya. The bikkering which was going on in his village was too much for him.

grow or become bigger in size, Ibowa mbwindakabona jilo bwakacili buniini, sunu twajana bwaaya. = The mushroom which I saw yesterday was still small, today we found it has grown in size. Bulwazi mbwaali kusisa, bwaaya. = The disease which he was hiding has increased (so that it can be no longer concealed). Ida ndyaali kusisa, lyaaya. = The pregnancy which she was concealing has become too big to hide.

make grow or increase, rt. aya, Wali kuyeeya kuti kubba ncibotu, pesi naajatwa camwaayila, wapya, wasubuka. He thought it was good to steal, but when he was caught it added to his problems, he was punished, he repented.
  • be unveiled, be exposed, rt. -aya, Ooyu musimbi lyamwaayila ida ndyaali kusisa. The pregnancy which this girl was concealing has become visible.

spread out with flat of hands, spread out manure, Mutinta, kwaazala mapopwe aayo ayume. = Mutinta spread that maize with your hands so that it dries. (1.-azalwa, 2.-azalide, 3.-azalizya, 4.-azalila, 6.-azalisya) Also: -yanga-yanga, -anzala, -yanzala.
talk nonsense, Munene taakoona akoona pe, wakali kwiide kwaazamuka akulabalika. = He was just talking nonsense and raving.

be fully involved in doing something or dealing with something, focus on, concentrate on, Muvwimi naakajaya munyama, wakalikwaazanga nya kutenda nyama alikke. When the hunter killed an animal, he was fully occupied as he cut it up alone. Mulipenzyezya nzi kwaazanganya cintu cisondokede. = Why do you trouble yourself so much in focusing on what is mad. Babbi nobakamana kumwaazanganya boobu munene, bakamusiya. When the thieves had finished dealing wih the old man in this way, they left him.
be fully taken up with, Mulipenzyezya nzi kwaazankanya cintu cisondokede? = Why are you troubling yourself by being involved with a mad thing?

cut meat in pieces, Kwaazaula nyama muzipaanzi-paanzi. = Cut the meat into pieces. Njakumwaazaula zenimutendu, muswi wamu Luvwubu. = I will tear apart the shark, the big fish of the sea. Also: -tendaula, -fwanzaula. (1.-azaulwa, 2.-azaulide, 3.-azauluzya, 4.-azaulila, 5.-azaulilayo, 6.-azaulisya, 8.-azaulana)

chop up meat in pieces, Kamwaazuula nyama mwamana mupe bantu balimumunzi. = Cut up the meat and when you are finished give it to the people who are in the village. Also: -azaula
  • give profusely, extravagantly, plentifully, Banyinakulu bakaazuula kupa nyemu kumuzyukulu wabo. = The old lady gave plenty of groundnuts to her grandchild.

become, be, Ninguzu zya Leza zindipede kuba waano. It is the powers of God which permit me to be here. Ncibi kuba mubaya. It is bad to be a careless person. Ndaakukomena ndiya kuba dokotela. When I grow up I will become a doctor. (1.-bwa or -begwa, 2.-bede, 3.-bezya, 4.-beda, 5.-bedalyo, 6.-besya, 7.-baaba.)

be with, have, obtain, Ndakaba amunyono. = I had envious feelings. Ndakaba amwana niyakamana myaka yosanwe. = I had a child after five years. Ndakaba amali manji nindakabeleka mubbanga. = I obtained a lot of money when I worked in the bank. Mapopwe okwesu ayanda kuba angalaala. = Our maize is about to tassel.
  • (be talkative in a bad way disturbing peace, be quarrelsome), baa kumulomo, Musimbi wakwatwa tayelede kubaa kumulomo. = A young married girl should not talk in an improper way.
prepare oneself in haste, get ready quickly, Kamulibaakanya natanasika uumulonda. = Get yourself ready quickly before the one who is coming to fetch you arrives. Also: -bambila-bambila, -pakanya.
surpass, Nguni mucembelenyina muno mucisi umubaala? = What other old lady friend of hers in this land can surpass her?

spread out wings, glide, Nkwilimba ilabaama kuuluka. = The pidgeon glides in flight. Mumajeleele mwenjakubaama mbuli kamembya. = From the cliffs I will glide like a swallow. Also: -peleemba. (2.-baamide, 3.-baamisya, 4.-baamina, 5.-baaminalyo, 7.-baama-baama)

be like, seem, Jolezya, wiile kuba anga tayandi kulya, pesi ulayanda. = Jolezya, he just seems not to want to eat, but he does. Nemwaambila lino kulaba anga nkubeja. = When I tell you now it will seem like lying.
be better than, Kojisi koombe nokaceya kubaazya kunyina. = It is better to have a calf no matter how small than to have nothing.

sharp to taste or touch, Cilababa awa akandiluma nzuki. = It is itching here where the bee stung me. Mpilibili ilababa. = Pepper is hot to taste. Nibakatalika kulya bamvwa buyo nkoci baba-baba cisyu. = When they began to eat they felt the sharp taste of the relish. (1.-babwa, 2.-babide, 3.-babya, 4.-babila, 5-babilalyo, 6.-babisya, 7.-baba-baba, 8.-babizyanya.)
walk unsteadily with discomfort, Nkaambo nzi ncobabaila buya kweenda mbuli muntu uciswa cinowe? = Why do you walk like someone suffering from corns? Also: -mamaila.

jump about, flap about, Kayuni kalababalika mumitabi yamusamu. = The bird is jumping about in the branches of the tree. Mintengwe ulababalika kuvwuna mwana wakwe. = The swift is flapping about to save its young. Also: - babama.
stammer, Ulya musimbi ulababalisya naambaula. = That girl stammers when she speaks. Also: -bbabbalisya.

flap, flutter wings, Nkwilimba ilababama yabona noole mucaanda. = The pidgeon flaps about when it sees a wild-cat in the hut. Mutinta ubabama buya anyema. = Mutinta flaps about when s/he is angry. Bana nobasobana, balababama mbuli bayuni. = The children when playing are flapping their arms like birds. Also: -baka-baka.
protrude, Camba cakwe wakali kucidikimuna akubabamuka mbuli muyuni uyanda kuuluka kuzwa mumeenda. = His chest was shaking and protruding like a bird which is about to take off from the water.
develop physically, Ulya mwana uyakubabana akukomena. = That child will develop well when it grows up. Also: -fwutumuka, -fwunga.
wither, as skin, Ooyu muntu wakababankana makanda akwe, tacinoneezyi. = This person's skin has withered up, it is not pleasant. Also: -ungana.

be peeled off, Cilonda cakwe cakababanuka nicakabikkwa musamu. = His scab peeled off when medicine was applied. Also: -bbabbanuka. (2.-babanukide, 3.-babanusya, 4.-babanukila, 5.-babanukilalyo, 6.-babanukisya, 7.-babanuka-babanuka.)

scratch or peel off, Bakababanuna bulongo bwakaindi nibakayanda kubikka bupya. = They peeled off the old plaster when they wanted to put new plaster. Also: -bbabbanuna. (1.-babanunwa, 2.-babanukide, 3.-babanusya, 4.-babanwida, 5.-babanwidalyo, 6.-babanunisya, 7.-babanuna-babanuna)
gallop, Eeli bbiza lilababata kutali kusobana. = This horse really gallops. Also: -bbabbata.
unglue, Babatula mapepa ali kubwaanda. = Unglue the papers from the wall. Also: -bbabbatula,-bbabbanuna, -namatula, -bbatulula. (1.-babatulwa)

jump in short movements, as fighting cocks, Mukombwe wakababauka niwakapya mulilo = The cock flew in short flights when it was burnt.
  • jump continuously when in pain, Cheelo wababauka kapati naalyata sizi lyamulilo. = Cheelo hopped about when she stepped on an ember. Mudaala wakababauka naakalumwa nsilibi. = The old man jumped about when he was bitten by red ants.

speak indistinctly, Wakali kwiide kubabausya kwaambaula mumuswaangano. = He was just incoherent at the meeting.
  • make jump in pain, Cheelo lyakamubabausya sizi lyamulilo ndyaakalyata. = The hot ember which Cheelo stepped on caused her to jump about in pain.

prepare before burning charcoal, i.e. pile up wood, cover mound with clay, Wakababila masamu aakwe mukubamba malasya. = He prepared his wood for making charcoal. Also: -bubila.
  • look after house, Sena tatukonzyi kujana mukaintu ukonzya kubabila maanda esu kwansondo yomwe? = Can we not find a woman to look after our houses for one week? (1.-babilwa, 2.-babilide, 3.-babilisya)

be startled, Ndakazikubabuka nibakazikunjila bayi. = I was startled when the teacher came in. Kayuni kababuka nikabona sikakonze. = The little bird was startled when it saw the hawk.
  • jump back out of danger, Bakazyuuma ndeye zyamyuumba akubabuka antobo. = They clashed the bundles of spears together and jumped back with their shields to avoid the charge.
  • fly in short flights as cocks when fighting. Also: -babauka

scare away, Kobabula muyuni ooyo auluke. = Frighten that bird so that it flies away. (1.-babulwa, 2.-babukide)
  • burn away, Mutamuki kubabula munsaa butala nkaambo bwizu bwaakuyuma buyakupya butala. = Don't delay in burning away the grass beside the granary because when the grass dries it will burn it. Also: -babwida.
detach plaster, Basilisi balacibabununa cipulasita kukwaanza kwakwe. = The doctors will remove the plaster from her hand. Also: -bbabbununa, (1.-babununwa, 2.-babunwide, 3.-babununzya)

be itchy, Ndababwa mpese mubili oonse. = I am itching because of the wild velvet-bean pod all over the body. Ndababwa mubili oonse nkaambo tiindakasamba jilo. = The whole body is itching because I did not bathe yesterday.

make a firebreak by burning, Kamubabwida mbewu kutegwa itapyi. = Make a firebreak around the garden so that it does not catch fire. Webo ono mulimo wako nkulibabwida nkaambo ndilizi kuti basankwa bamwi bayakuboola kukutizya. = Your work now is to build a fire-break around yourself (i.e. protect yourself) because I know some men will come to run away with you.

open wide space to find something. Nibaabadula mani, bakiibona mitiba yakasisidwe. = When they pushed the grass aside, they saw the plates which were hidden. (1.-badulwa, 2.-badwide, 3.-baduzya, 4.-badwida, 5.-badulilalyo, 6.-badulisya, 7.-badula-badula) cf. -bandula, -batula.
  • whip, Mwana ncalila bamubadula bacembele. = The child is crying because the old woman has whipped him.

catch a thing in flight, as a ball, Cheelo ulabaka kabotu mabbola. = Cheelo is good at catching balls in the air. (1.-bakwa, 2.-bakide, 4.-bakila, 5.-bakilalyo, 6.-bakisya, 7.-baka-baka, 8.-bakana) Also: -kwaba.

flap, Kayuni kakali kubaka-baka nikakali kuuluka. = The bird was flapping its wings when it was flying. Also: -babama, -bakama,
  • have burning taste, Mpilibili ilabaka-baka mukanwa = Pepper has a burning taste in the mouth. Also: -yaka-yaka.

flap wings in flight, Sikwaze walikubakama awa naainda atala ananda. The fish-eagle flapped it's wings as it passed thre over the house. Naali kulailila muntu kwakugama kabelesya maanza walikubee ubakama buya. = When he was giving directions to someone using his hands he seemed as though he was just flapping about. Also: -babama. (2.-bakamide, 3.-bakamisya, 4.-bakamina, 5.-bakaminalyo, 6.-bakamisya, 7.-bakamabakama)
throw and catch, Basimbi nibali kusobana bbola bali kubakila. = When the girls were playing netball, they were throwing and catching the ball.

shine, Izuba lilabala. = The sun is shining. (1.-balwa, 2.-balide, 3.-balisya, 4.-balila, 5.-balilalyo, 6.-balisya, 7.-bala-bala, 8.-balilana.)
  • read, study, Nobana kucikolo nkomuya oko kamulomya kubala. = Children, you should study hard at the school where you are going.
  • count, estimate, value, Choolwe, kobala mali ngomwajana sunu. = ChooIwe, count all the money you have collected today. Batonga mbantu bayandisya nombe, muntu utakwe nombe tabamubali pe. = The Batonga are a people who love cattle, they do not value a person who does not have cattle.
take turns, Moonga a Mweemba bakali kubalaana kweembela mpongo. = Moonga and Mweemba were taking turns in herding the goats. Also: -balana.
be big in size, Muntu ulya kabotu ulabalabana. = The person who eats well has a large body.
be large in shape, rt. balabana, Ooyu musankwa ulibalabenye. This boy is massively built.
be expansive, as the chest, Camba ca Chimuka cabalala. = Chimuka's chest is expansive. Also: -angamana
shine, Bamacembele bakalijisi mitwe ibalama yananikwa mafwuta ciindi nobaya kumadilwe. = The old women had shining heads smeared with oil when they were going to funerals.
take turns, as in herding, Babalana buya kweembela nombe. = They just take turns in herding the cattle. Also: -balaana, -dwilana, -cita malizi.

be transparent, Tacili cibotu kusama cisani cibalangala. = It is not good to wear a transparent dress. Mabwe amwi akali kuņaima akubalangala mbuli cimbonimboni. = Some stones were shining and transparent as a mirror. (i.e. crystals) Also: -bangalala, -bangala.

touch things superficially or temporarily when using them, move from one place to another, Mutinta ubala uka minzi kukkala akaambo kabubbi bwakwe. Mutinta lives temporarily in villages, moving from one to another because of her habit of stealing. (1.-balaukwa, 2.-balaukide)

beat repeatedly, Munene wamubalaula kasako musankwa uutamwi. = The old man beat the disobedient boy repeatedly with a stick. (1.-balaulwa, 2.-balaude, 4.-balaulila, 5.-balaulilalyo, 6.-balaulisya, 7.-balaulabalaula, 8.-balaulana.)
  • go around counting, Joojo ubalaula nombe muziba zyabantu bambi. = Joojo goes around counting the cattle in the kraals of other people.
  • spell as a word, Ncibotu kwiiya kubalaula majwi mu Chitonga. = It is good to learn how to spell words in Chitonga.

be countable. rt. -bala, Inombe zyokwa Joojo zilabalika nkaambo nzisyoonto. = Joojo's cattle are countable because they are few. (2.-balikide, 3.-balisya, 4.-balikila, 5.-balikilalyo, 6.-balikisya, 7.-balika-balika, 8.-balikana.)
  • run, Bamadaala balabalika abalo kuti bayanda. = Old men can also run if they want to.

run after, rt. -balika, Komubalikila natanasakana umujosye. = Run after him before he goes far and get him to come back. Musimbi naakacaala kaimvwi kumbali amunzi, babwa bamumunzi bakabalikila kuli nguwe. = When the girl remained standing near the village, the dogs of the village ran towards her.
  • run for, Ndamubalikila nkaambo uciswa kuulu. = I shall run for him because he has a bad leg.
take turns or shifts, Tweelede kubalilana buya mazuba akweembela. We should take turns during the days of herding. Also: -dwiilana

read loudly, rt. -bala, Kobalisya kutegwa boonse bamvwe. = Read loudly so that all can hear.
  • read intensely, Kuti *kobalisya* ziiyo uyakuzwidilila. If you study the lessons earnestly, you will pass.
  • make to run, Bakaabalisya kapati macinga akufwambaana kusika nkobakali kuya. They made the bicycles run fast and quickly arrived where they were going. Yamubalisya nombe naatiijate kana kayo. The cow made him run when he was about to catch it's calf.
  • feed with, Kaindi bami bakali kubalisya anzoka bazike. Long ago the chiefs used to feed the slaves with snakes.

send to take one's turn, Moonde wakabalizya Joni kuya kunyona nombe. Moonde sent John to take his turn in bringing back the cattle. (1.-balizigwa, 2.-balizyide, 4.-balizyila, 5.-balizyilalyo, 8.-balizyanya)
argue about whose turn it is to herd, Mainza a Cheelo balabalizyanya kunyona nombe. = Mainza and Cheelo are arguing about whose turn it is to bring back the cattle.

re-read, rt. -bala, Ncibotu kubalulula ciiyo catamvwugwa kabotu. = It is good to re-read a lesson which has not been well understood. (1-balululwa, 2.-balulwide, 3.-balulizya, 4.-balulwidila, 5.-balulwidilalyo, 6.balululisya)

take care of, Baacisya bandibamba kabotu. My uncle takes good care of me. (1.-bambwa, 2.-bambide, 3.-bambya, 4.-bambila, 5.-bambilalyo, 6.-bambisya, 7.-bamba-bamba, 8.-bambilana.)
  • mend, Kofwambaana kubamba ncinga, njanda kweenda. = Hurry up and mend the bicycle, I want to go.
  • make, Bana balabamba basune babulongo. = The children are making clay oxen.

go along an edge, Katuyaa kubambalika mulonga, tuyakusika. = Let us go along the edge of the river, we will reach the place. (1.-bambalikwa, 2.-bambalikide, 3.-bambalisya, 4.-bambalikila, 5.-bambalikilalyo, 6.-bambalikisya, 7.-bambalika-bambalika)
  • be evasive, Nobetekwa, ncibi kubambalika kwaamba. = When you are being tried, it is bad to be evasive. Utabi nobambalika, kwaamba kaambo keni. = Don't be evasive, state the true fact.

look after one another, Kukkala antoomwe kuyandika kubambana buya. = To stay together you need to take care of each other. (1.-bambanwa, 2.-bambanide, 4.-bambanina, 5.-bambaninalyo, 6.-bambanisya, 7.-bambana-bambana)
  • stay next to each other, Twabambana kukkala a Mainza. = I and Mainza live next to one another.
place side by side, Mwanaangu ndiyakumubambanya kukkala a mwana wa Joni mumusunko. = I will make my child sit next to John's child during the examination.

move in a wide line, Tacili cibotu kubambasana kweenda mumugwagwa mwiinda myootokala. = It is not good to walk in a wide line on a road where vehicles pass. (-bambasene)
  • walk majestically = -bambasana kweenda.
be flattened, rt. bambasana, Nibakamana kuzikka mwana muvwanda, cuumbwe bakacisiya cilibambasene. = When they had buried the infant, they left the grave flattened.

be rubbed off, as bits of skin, peel off, crack as skin, Mutabelesyi basune ciindi camuyoba nkaambo inga babambauka antunda. = Do not use the oxen during continous rain because the skin on the hump may be rubbed off. (2.-bambaukide, 3.-bambausya, 4.-bambaukila, 6.-bambaukisya.)
be stripped off, as skin, Ulibambaukide amubili akaambo kakuumwa. = The skin on his body is stripped off because of being beaten.

live beside one another, rt. -bambana, Sulwe a suntwe bakalibambene mukukkala kwabo. = The hare and the hyena were living close to each other.
  • continually look after one another, Mutinta a Mainza bakali kubambene nibakali kukkala antoomwe. Mutinta and Mainza always looked after one another when they lived together.
perform efficiently, Mucembele naakajoka kumuunda, wakajana milimo yabambikana amunzi wakwe. = When the old woman returned from the fields, she found all the jobs of her village had been done well.

prepare, Bakafwambaana kulibambila kutegwa batalike Iweendo Iwabo. They hurried up to prepare themselves so that they might begin their journey. (1.-bambilwa, 2.-bambilide, 5.-bambilalyo, 7.-bambila-bambila, 8.-bambilana)
  • make for someone, Mangamwe nguwakandibambila keembe. = Mangamwe was the one who made an axe for me.
abrade the skin (one spot), Wabambuka amubili naaumwa cimboko. = The skin was scraped off his body when he was beaten. Also: -bambauka, -bbatuka.

bruise, split open, Nyeele impya *ibambula mulomo*. = A new musical horn bruises the lips. (a proverb) Naakaumwa cimboko amubili cakamubambula. When he was beaten with a sjambok it split open his skin. (1.-bambulwa, 3.-babuzya, 6.-bambulisya, 8.-bambulana)

re-do, Basankwa bakaboola ijilo *kubambulula* mugwagwa. = The men came yesterday to repair the road.
  • restore, as a thing out of joint, Mwana naakafwuyuka, basilisi bakacibambulula cifwuwa cakwe. = When the child had his bone dislocated, the bone-setter put it back in place. (1.-bambululwa, 2.-bambulwide, 3.-bambuluzya, 4.-bambulwida, 5.-bambulwidalyo, 6.-bambululisya, 8.-bambululana)
be bruised, Wakabambuuka naakaloka ansi kuzwa mucisamu. = He was bruised when he fell off the tree. (2.-bambuukide, 3.-bambuuzya, 4.-bambuukila, 5.-bambuukilalyo, 6.-bambuukisya)
bruise, Wakamubambuula mubili oonse naakamuuma amuluso. = He bruised his body all over when he beat him with a flexible stick. (1.-bambuulwa, 8.-bambuulana) Also: -cuzula, -guluntana.

make with, rt. -bamba, Wakali *kubambya* zitina abulongo busubila. = He was using red soil to make bricks.
  • cause to mend, Bataata bayakukubambya ncinga yakatyoka jilo. = My father is going to get the bike repaired which broke yesterday.
hobble, Munene ubampa buya kweenda. = The old man hobbles as he walks. Also: -bbampa, -dyabatila, -dyabila, -sunkuta.

stitch on a patch. Kobampika kabotu cigamba. Stitch on the patch properly. Also: -bbampika, -lamatika, -gambika. (1.-bampikwa, 2.-bampikide, 3.-bampizya, 4.-bampikila, 5.-bampikilalyo, 7.-bampika-bampika, 8.-bampikilana)
hobble, walk with a limp, Mudaala *ulabampila* kweenda. = The old man hobbles along as he walks. Also: -bbampila, -sunkuta, kangaila.

hide by crouching down, Wakabandama mumani kuyoowa kuumwa. He hid and crouched in the grass fearing to be beaten.
  • lie flat or face downwards, Kobandama kutegwa ndibone cilonda cili kusyule. Lie face downwards so that I see the wound which is behind. Syaadolo wakali *kubandama* abwaanda. = The lizard was lying flat on the wall. (2.-bandamide, -3.-bandamika, 4.-bandamikila, 6.-bandamisya, 7.-bandama-badama) Also: -bbandama.

make lay down on stomach, Wakamubandamika mwana kuti amunanike mafwuta. = She made the child lie on its stomach so that she could rub it with oil. (1.-bandamikwa, 2.-bandamikide, 3.-bandamisya, 4.-bandamikila, 6.-bandamikisya, 7.-bandamikabandamika) Also: -bbandamika.
stretch out on stomach, Twakasika acikasaalizi, aalya

batombela kuyotela. = We arrived at about 8.00 hrs., the time when the lizards stretch themselves out on their stomachs warming themselves.
  • bend down to, Cilatondwa kubandamina kubantu omuntu osamide cifwaafwi. It is taboo to bend down in front of people, when you are wearing a short dress. Also: -bbandamina, -dingamina.

call out, as the name of the dead, *Naakali kweema, wakali kubandauka bamukowa wakwe.* = When she was singing a lament, she was calling out the names of her clan. *Naakali kulila mwanaakwe, wakamubandauka mazina oonse.* = When he was mourning his child, he mentioned all his/her names. (1.-bandaukwa, 2.-bandaukide, 3.-bandausya, 4.-bandaukila, 5.-bandaulilalyo, 6.-bandaukisya, 8.-bandaukana.)
  • mention, *Wakabandauka zintu zilaa lubuwa Iwakwe zyoonse naakali kujana cikwelete kubbanga.* = He mentioned the list of all his belongings (collateral) when he was getting a loan from the bank.

smear, *Cisyu cakaceya, toonse twakali kubandauzya buyo.* = The relish was insufficient, we all were just smearing it on the food. Also: -kukwaangulula.
  • run quickly, *Mulombwana wakalubikka luno luyumu nta. Wakalubandauzya kutegwa jule atamukoswedi nzila.* = The boy ran very quickly. He ran fast so that the secretary bird would not cross the path before him.

discuss, chat, *Bakubusi balayanda kubandika zyamabbola.* = Youths like talking about football. (1.-bandikwa, 2.-bandikide, 3.-bandisya, 4.-bandikila, 5.-bandikilalyo, 6.-bandikisya, 7.-bandika-bandika, 8.-bandizyanya.)
be renamed, *Bazike bakabandilwa kubbandilo lyabasimalelo babo.* = Slaves were renamed with the clan name of their owners.

converse with, *Musankwa uyanda kukwata uyandisya kubandisya musimbi ngwaasala.* = A boy who wishes to marry likes to converse with the girl he has chosen. *Komubandisya mweenzu walendelelwa.* = Talk with the visitor as he is lonely.
talk to one another, *Kuzwa waawo kunyina anibakabandisyanya.* = From there they did not talk to one another.

open a space in grass, *Kamubandula bwizu tubone kayuni kayuba.* = Open a space in the grass so that we see the bird which is hiding. (1.-bandulwa, 2.-bandwide, 3.-bandulisya, 4.-bandwida, 5.-bandwidalyo, 6.-bandulisya, 7.-bandula-bandula) Also: -yandula, -badula, -batula.
knock out teeth as a tribal custom, *Mapulanga wakalicizyi kubanga basimbi.* = Mapulanga knew how to knock out the upper teeth of girls. Also: -manyuna.

be hot to the taste, *Cisyu eeci cilabanga-banga nkucabikkwa mpilibili.* = This relish is hot because pepper was put on it. Also: -yaka-yaka, -nyenga-nyenga
  • taste better, *Mundyoli ulabanga-banga kwiinda Iwidi.* = A relish of dried pumpkin leaves mixed with groundnut mash is tastier than *Iwidi* wild roots.
  • make a grinding stone rough so that it grinds well, e.g *Kobanga-banga ziyo kutegwa uziye kabotu.* = Make the grinding stone rough so that you grind properly.
be transparent (become empty), *Mubutala bwabacembele mwabangala nkaambo mapopwe akamana.* = You can see through the maize granary of the old woman because the maize is finished.
be transparent, as gauze, *Cisani eeci cilabangalala.* = This dress is transparent. Also: -bangala, -balangala.

tie poles of hut, bind a hut with wattles, (of the roof = -anga) *Oobu butala buyandika kubangilwa.* = This maize bin needs to be tied with wattles. *Bamakwe bakamwiita musankwa kuti azikubagwasye kubangila butala.* = The in-laws called the boy to help them to bind the maize-bin with wattles.

roll the eyes about, *Mwamubona mbwabangula kulanga mbuli kuti wazyingwa.* = See the way she is rolling the eyes about as if she is confused. Also: -ilinganya
  • pull out jiggers from flesh, *Bakamubangula tuuka.* = They pulled out the insects from his flesh. Also: -songola.
  • give medicine to dog to make him fierce, *Aaba babwa uulaabo wakababangula.* = The owner of these dogs gave them medicine to make them fierce. (*lubangu* = medicine that makes dogs fierce)

have teeth knocked out according to tribal custom of the past, *Batonga kaindi bakali kubangwa kutegwa kabazyibana.* = Long ago the Batonga used to have the teeth knocked out so that they could identify one another. *Kaindi basimbi abasankwa bakali kubangwa meno aakutala ali cisambomwi.* = Long ago, girls and boys had their six front upper teeth extracted.

make indentations on the grinding stone used by the hand, *Kuti mućembele waziya maila ciindi cilamfwu, ziyo lilafwumpa, aboobo iziyo lyeelede kubangwa-bangwa.* = If an old woman grinds for a long time the grinding stone becomes blunt, and smooth and therefore it must be chipped to make it rough.

supervise, *Basyaacibula bobile taakwe wakali kubanjimela, bakali kulyeendelezya beni mumilimo yabo.* = The two inexperience workers had no one to supervise them, they were managing the works themselves.

slap repeatedly, *Ncibi kuti bayi kababantaula bana.* = It is bad for a teacher to slap pupils continually. Also: -bbantaula, -uula.
  • beat oneself with hands when excited, *Bacembele bakali kulibantaula acamba nibakamvwa kuti muzyukulu wabo wafwa.* = The old woman was beating herself on the chest when she heard of the death of her grandchild. *Sicikolo naakatambula lugwalo lulaa mali wakali kulibantaula acamba.* = When the pupil received the letter with the money s/he beat his/her chest with joy. Also: -bbantaula, lyaampaula
stick, *Kobantika bulongo aawo mpocizwisya.* = Stick the clay there where it is leaking. Also: -bbatika

uncover what is under one's hand, *Mudaala wakabanuna janza lyakwe kuti bana babone ncaakasiside.* = The old man uncovered what was under his hand so that the children could see what he had hidden. Also: -bbanuna
  • open the eyes, *Uuciswa ucibanuna meso.* = The patient is still opening her/his eyes. Also: -bbanuna.
  • open the mouth (idiomatic usage), initiate negotiations, *Bakandiitila mali manji aacibanuna mulomo kwakakwata mwana angu.* = They demanded much money from me to open the marriage negotiations where my son married. *Kamundipa mali aacibanuna mulomo wamunanga.* = Give me the money to open the mouth of the witchdoctor. (i.e. to start the process of divination.) Also: -bbanuna

extract, as grain from bin, *Swebo kwesu mapopwe tucibanza buya kuzwa mubutala.* = At our home we are still taking maize from the maize-bin. (i.e. We have not started buying it). *Mukaintu wakabanza mbuto.* = The woman took out seeds from the grain bin. *Mubbi wakalangaula mubutala, wajana kuli saka lyabusu. Katamwayi aciindi wakatalika kubeleka kubanza cilyo ca bantu. = The thief glanced around, he found a bag of maize-flour. Without wasting time he began to work taking out the people's food.
  • open up, as a termite-hill, Kuti cuulu cabanza inga inswa zilibambila kuzwa anze. = If the termite-hill splits up into many openings it means the termites are about to come out.

light, as a pipe for smoking, Banene bakali kubanzaana mfwuko akuluula mbuli mbobakiileya nkondo ya Makobbokobbo. = The old men were lighting their pipes and relating how they used to avoid the Makobbokobbo war.

increase heat, Kaindi babelesi bamunjanji bakali kubasela citima kutegwa ceendesye. = Long ago the railway workers would increase the fire in the train (by adding more coal) so that it would go faster. Also: -basila.

increase heat, Kamubasila mulilo afwambaane kubizwa mangamwe. = Stoke the fire so that the stew is quickly cooked. Kaindi bantu bakali kubasila citima kutegwa cilundukisye kwiinda mukubikka malasha manji. = Long ago the people used to add more coal to the locomotive to make it go faster. Also: - basela.

be quiet as water, Konga kobatama ayebo, watukatazya kwaambila. = Would you be quiet, your talking tires us. Iguwo nilyakamana, meenda akabatama. = When the gale died down, the water became quiet. Also: -leengula, -leenza, -liinza.
settle down, Nitwakamwaambila wakabatamana mbuli bubwebubwe bwakkalila kunsi aameenda. = After speaking to him he became quiet as small stones that settle beneath the water.
make quiet, rt. -batama, Ndakanyandwa kapati mbundakaci konzya kuubatamika moyo wangu. = I was very surprised by the way in which I was able to quieten my heart.
hurry, Kamunga kamubatauka kweenda! = Would you hurry up! Also: -bbatauka, -nyangauka, -bindaana.
skim off, as cream from milk, Bataata bakali kubataula mafwuta amabisi. = My father was skimming off the cream from the sour milk. Also: -pepaula, -ibulula.
be in quiet state, rt. -batama, Cisi eci cakalibateme, cakali cibotu kwiinda mazuba ano. = This country was quiet, it was better than nowadays.

remove, Kamubatula nyanzabili ameenda tuyanda kunywa. = Remove the scum from the water we want to drink. Kamubatula mafwuta amukupa. = Remove the cream from the milk.
  • make an opening in a bin or a box, Kobatula cingungulu tubone zili mukati. = Open the bin so that we see what it contains. Also: -bbatula
  • detach plaster, Bana bakabubatula bulongo munanda iijikila ansi. = The children pulled the plaster off the kitchen wall on to the ground. Also: -bbatula.
  • peel off, as a scab, Batula cilonda cako kutegwa busina buzwe. = Remove the scab from your wound so that the pus comes out. Also: -bbatula
become blind, Munene Chooka wakabaya mwakali. = The old man Chooka became blind last year. (2.-bayide, 3.-bayizya, 4.-bayila, 5.-bayilalyo, -6.-bayisya, 7.-baya-baya.) Also: -ofwaala.

defecate, Batumbu basiya mwana wabayaala abulo. = The mother left the child who soiled the bed. Also: -ambuka
  • be careless, soil something, Nindanyamuka ndabayaala nkaambo kasuko kanjila muli cakulya. = When I stood up I was careless because the dust entered the food. Also: -yambaala.

defecate on, *Mwana wabayaalila abulo.* = The child soiled the bed. Wakatalika kuzyangama kayoowa kumwi kuti ndiza inga ulalibayaalila. = He began to tremble while fearing that he might defecate.
  • be careless about something, Kocenjela kupopa musune, ulaluma kuti wamubayaalila. Be careful with the ox, it attacks if you handle it carelessly.
run away from danger, Mwanaa ba Suntwe wakalubayaula lubilo kuya kwa Malinki. Mr. Suntwe's child ran off as fast as he could going to Malinki.
be bruised, Wakajalula meso, ciindi eci akalibayukide. = He opened his eyes, at that time they were still bruised.

steal, Bana bamazuba ano balayanda kubba kapati. = The children of nowadays like to steal a lot. Ooyu musimbi ubba buya kulanga musankwa wakwe. This girl is stealing a look at her boy-friend. (1.-bbigwa, 2.-bbide, 3.-bbizya, 4.-bbida, 5.-bbidalyo, 6.-bbisya, 7.-bbaabba.)

fail to germinate, as in growth of seedlings, Nsangu mbundakali kuzisyanga zyakabbaamina. = The seedlings which I planted have failed to germinate. Also: -mbobomena.
