put, Kamubikka cimbwali eeci mumasizi kutegwa ciyokwe tulye. = Put this sweet potato in the embers so that it is roasted for us to eat. (1.-bikkwa, 2.-bikkide, 3.-bikkizya, 4.-bikkila, 5.-bikkilalyo, 6.-bikkisya, 7.-bikka-bikka.)

look forward to acquiring something good, Ndali kulibikka-bikka kuti sunu ndavwola mali manji, ani pe. I had hoped that I would be paid much money today, but it was not so. Boonse banamusimbi abanamusankwa bakalibikka-bbika cakukondwa kuti balabaa muzyukulu muciindi cisyoonto biyo. Both the parents of the girl and the parents of the boy look forward happily to having a grandchild in a short time. Also: -peekezya, -leelezya. (1.-bikkwa-bikkwa)
  • quickly put, Kobikka-bikka zisani zyako munanda tweende. Quickly put your clothes in the house so that we go.
form as tubers in the ground, Cimbwali cangu cilibikkide. = My sweet-potatoe has grown very well. (1.-bikkidwe)
place for, Nkuku yangu ndakaibikkila mayi aankanga jilo. = I put the eggs of a guinea-fowl with my hen yesterday. (1.bikkilwa, 2.-bikkilide)

seek revenge, Baya basankwa mbitwakauma, bakatubikkilila. Those boys whom we beat, are seeking revenge on us. Chuumangoma tanaakacizyi kubikkilila. Chuumangoma was not interested in taking revenge. (1.bikkililwa, 2.-bikkilide)
  • save up, rt. -bikka, Ndatalika kubikkilila mali kutegwa aakuvwula nkaule payi. = I shall start saving money so that when it becomes enough I buy a blanket.
put along with, rt. -bikka, Ndabikkilizya mayi ankanga muli mayi ankuku. = I have mixed eggs of a guinea fowl with eggs of a chicken. Also: -sanganya. (1.-bikkilizyigwa, 2.-bikkilizyide)

show signs of oncoming downpour, Imvwula eeyi ilabikuka kutondezya kuti ilaba mpati yawa. = This (on-coming) rain is building up clouds showing that it will pour heavily. Also: -biluluka. ( Makumbi alabiluluka.)

toss or poke as a bull does, Mucende wajombe wakali kubikula cuulu akubingila. The bull was poking the anthill with its horns and bellowing. Also: -bbikula. (1.-bikulwa, 2.-bikulide, 3.-bikusya, 4.-bikwida, 6.-bikulisya. 8. -bikulana)
  • raise with a lever, Ibbwe eli ndilemu kapati, aboobo liyandika kubikula acisamu ciyumu. = This stone is extremly heavy and so it should be levered with a strong pole. Also: -bbikula.

boil, Meenda abila, ubikke busu kutegwa ujike nsima. = When the water is boiled, put in the maize flour so that you cook nsima. (2.-bilide, 3.-bilizya, 4.-bilila, 6.-bilisya, 7.-bila-bila.) Also: -bodoma, -mbodoma
  • ferment, Bukoko bulabila munongo. The beer is fermenting in the clay pot. Also: -cocoma.
  • become angry, *Moyo wangu wabila nindabona wakabba nombe zyangu.* = My heart was boiling when I saw who had stolen my cattle.

desire, *Ncibotu kubilamina mulimo lyoonse.* = It is good to wish to work always. *Wacibilamina cakulya akaambo kakuti kwamazuba obilo aayinda taakali kulya.* = She longs for food because she has not eaten for the past two days. (1-bilaminwa, 2.-bilamide, 3.-bilamisya, 4.bilaminina.)

roll the eyes in pain, *Meso akwe akali kubilauka nkaambo wakali mumaciswe.* = His eyes were rolling because he was in pain. Also: -vwundula, -bangula (2.-bilaukide, 3.-bilausya, 4.-bilaukila, 6.-bilaukisya.)
roll the eyes about, *Nkaambonzi ncobilaula meso mbuli kuti watingwa cimbwali?* = Why do you roll your eyes as if you have been choked by a sweet-potato? (1.-bilaulwa, 2.-bilaude, 3.-bilausya)

sound energetically, as a drum, *Ngoma yakali kubilibinta nibakali kunywa bukoko kwa Haajilo.* = The drum was throbbing energetically when they were drinking beer at Haajilo's village. (1.-bilibintwa, 2.-bilibintide, 3.-bilibintya, 4.-bilibintila, 6.-bilibintisya.)
sound at, reverberate, *Ino ngoma ibilibintila kuli?* = Now where is the drum throbbing?

be a cause of worry, *Cilabilika kapati kutazwidilila mumusunko wamamanino.* = It is very worrying to fail the final examination. *Misunko ipa kulibilika yasika afwiifwi kuti koli tookalibambila.* = When exams draw near they cause you to become worried if you have not prepared yourself. *Walibilika musimbi naamvwa kuti ulatizigwa sunu.* = The girl worried herself a lot to-day when she heard that she was to be taken away to live with someone. (1.-bilikwa, 2.-bilikide, 3.-bilisya, 4.-bilikila, 6.-bilikisya, 8.-bilikana.)
cause to worry, *Kuli cimulibilisya.* = He is worried about something.
be afraid of one another, as in a competition, rt. -bilika, *Basinkondonyina babonana, balabilikana.* = When adversaries see one another, there is tension between them. (2.-bilikenye)

be angry, *Bataata bakabilila nibakamvwa kuti njanda kukwata.* = My father became angry when he heard that I wanted to marry. (2.bilide, 3.-bilizya, 4.-bililila, 6. -bililisya, 8.-bilizyanya.) Also: -nyema, -kalala.
  • boil in, rt. -bila, *Nyama yali kubilila mucibiya.* = The meat was boiling in the pot.

cling to something, be possessive, be fully occupied with, *Mupati wangu ulamubililizya namutendele uutali wakwe.* = My elder brother clings to the bicycle which is not his. *Mulombe wakali kulibililizya kuya kubonana anjabi yakwe.* = The boy was fully occupied with the thought of he and his girl friend seeing one another.
  • become angry, *Inzuki zilabililizya kuti wasika munsi-munsi adola lyabuci bwazyo.* = Bees are stirred up if one approaches near their honey combs. (1.-bililizyigwa, 2.-bililizyide, 4.-bililizyila, 8.-bililizyanya.)
run fast, *Yakabilima citaambiki ncinga naakali kutija kuumwa Michelo.* = The bicycle ran very fast when Michelo was fleeing from being beaten. (2.-bilimide, 3.-bilimya, 6.-bilimisya)
cause to run fast on wheels, *Naakali kutija kuumwa, Mutinta wakaibilimya ncinga citaambiki.* = When he was running away from being beaten, Mutinta made the bicycle run at remarkable speed.

work intensively without a break, Cimupa kubilingana amulimo akutapumuna nkulibilika mupati wamilimo. = The reason why she works so intensively and without a break is that she fears the boss. Bantu boonse bakabilingana kuti bamubone musololi. All the people were so worked up to see the leader. Also: -bbilingana, -gwilingana, -gwitinganas, -syibingana. (2.-bilingenye. 3.-bilinganya, 4.-bilinganina, 6.-bilinganisya)

make angry, irritate, rt. bilila, Ndamubilizya munene nindatyola nkoli yakwe. I annoyed the old man when I broke his stick. (1.-bilizyigwa, 2.-bilizyide, 8.-bilizyanya.)
  • make boil, rt. bila, Twakaabilizya meenda nitwakasikka nkuni zinji. = We made the water boil when we added more firewood.
argue violently, Bakabilizyama nibakaimpana mumizeezo. They argued violently when they differed in opinions. Also: -bilizyanya, -kakazyanyas, -nyemezyanya. =
argue violently together, annoy one another, Basimbi bobilo bakabilizyanya nibakali kukanana makani abasankwa. Two girls were annoying one another when they were talking about boys. Also: -bilizyama.

move to and fro, Makumbi aleka kubiluluka kulaboola mvwula mpati. When the clouds stop moving there will be a great downfall. nombe zilaleka kubiluluka zyajana bwizu bubotu. = The cattle stop moving from one place to another when they find good grass. (1.-bilulukwa, 2.-bilulukide, 3.-bilulusya, 4.-bilulukila, 6.-bilulukisya.)

roll eyes, Kobiluula meso kutegwa nkufwule kabotu. = Move your eyes around so that I blow out what is inside. Mutinta waabiluula meso banyina nibamuulila cisani cipya. Mutinta rolled her eyes in joy when her mother bought her a new dress. cf. -bilaula. (1.-biluulwa, 2.-biluulide, 3.-biluusya, 4.-biluukila, 6. -biluulisya.)

quiver, shake, Naakaciswa ntuntumaanzi, wakali kwiile kubimba. = When s/he was sick with malaria, s/he was just shivering. cf. -tenkaana, -kankama, -zyangama. (2.-bimbide, 3.-bimbya, 4.-bimbila, 6.-bimbisya, 7.-bimba-bimba)
be in a hurry, Ndabinda, ndizoolya ndajoka. I am in a rush, I will eat when I return. (2.-bindide, 3.-binzya, 4.-bindila, 6.-bindisya.)

be fast, as when walking, rt. -binda, Kobindaana kweenda, balatusiya bantu. Hurry up, people will leave us behind. Also: -batauka, -bbataukas, -nyangauka. -bindaanide, (3.-bindaanya, 4.-bindaanina, 6.-bindaanisya.)
be in a hurry to do something, Tumvwe ncobindaanina boobu kuti ukwatwe, Chaalama. Chaalama, tell us why you are in such a rush to get married. (1.-bindaaninwa, 2.-bindaanide, 3.-bindaainzya.)

give presents, like rings or beads with hopes of marrying later, Kaindi bakali kubindika basimbi bakukwata. In the past they used to give presents to girls, hoping to marry them. (1.-bindikwa, 2.-bindikide, 4.-bindikila, 8.-bindikana.) Also: -kalila
  • make negotiations concerning a young girl for future marriage, Musimbi ngwindakabindika, mmubotu kapati. The girl whom I have arranged a marriage with for the future is very beautiful. Lyansiku kwakali cilengwa cakuti muntu wakwata antela wabindika musimbi, bamakwaakwe bakali kumwiita kuti ababelekele. Long ago there was a custom that when a boy wanted to marry or intended to marry a girl, the in-laws would call him to work for them. Also: - lindilila.
drive an animal, Kamubinga nombe, zikanywe meenda. = Drive the cattle so that they drink water. (1.-bingwa, 2.-bingide, 3.-binzya, 4.-bingila, 6.-bingisya, 8.-bingana.)
chase one another, Twakabingana nokuba kuti wakandisiya. = We were chasing one another though I could not catch up with him.

tuck cloth between one's legs when sitting down, Kamumubingila mwana nkaambo ulamubisya ambuka. = Tuck the cloth between the child's legs because he will soil you when he defecates. Also: -bbangila. (1.-bingilwa, 2. -bingilide, 3. -bingizya, 4.-bingilila, 6.-bingilisya, 8.-bingilana.)
  • roar continually, as ox or bull, Mucende wabasibbuku ulabingila kapati. = The bull of the headman roars repeatedly.
  • drive cattle for someone, Kondibingila boombe bangu kutegwa batasangani amanyina. = Drive the calves for me so that they do not meet the cows.
lead a song, Mukaintu uwakali kubingula wakali simaimbo winiwini. = The woman who was leading the song was a real singer. Also: -angula. (1.-bingulwa, 2.-bingulide.)

cause to hurry, rt. -binda, Basankwa bakazibinzya mpongo nkaambo mvwula yakalaa fwiifwi. = The boys made the goats move quickly because the rains were near. (1.-binzyigwa, 2.-binzyide, 3.-binzyaanya, 6.-binzyisya, 7.-binzya-binzya, 8.-binzyanya) Also: -fwuusya (rt. -fwuuta.)
  • help someone to drive cattle, Basankwa bobilo mbabakandibinzya mpongo kutola ku Monze. = There were two boys who helped me to drive the goats to Monze.
  • drive with, Kobweza mukkwilo wakubinzya nombe. = Take a whip with you for driving the cattle.

be made bad, rt. -bija, Mwanaangu wakabisigwa naakatalika kweenda abantu babi. = My child was made bad when he started moving around with evil people. (2.-biside, 3.-bisya, 4.-bisila, 5.-bisizyalyo, 7.-bisya-bisya, 8.-bisilana.)
make bad for, do harm to, rt. bija, Buumi bwamudolopo bwandibisizya bana. = City life has brought a lot of harm to my children. (8.-bisizyanya)
spoil, harm, make dirty, Mwana wacibisya kale cisani cakwe naali kukalaba. = The child has already dirtied her clothes when she was crawling. (1.-bisyigwa, 2.-bisyide, 8.-bisizyanya.)
be ripe, be cooked, Mapopwe abizwa kamwaajula. = The maize is cooked, take it off the fire. (2.-bizwide, 3.-bizwisya, 4.-bizwila, 6.-bizwisya, 7.-bizwa-bizwa.)
become ripe or cooked at a given time, Mucoolwe bakajana cakulya mpucakali kubizwila. = Luckily enough they found the food was ready.

roar, as an animal, Mucende ooyu kuti waboba kuno inga ulalimvwinsya kwa Haamapande. = If this bull bellows here, it is heard at Haamapande. Also: - vwuta.
  • throb deeply, as a drum, Ngoma yabukali yakalila, abalo banamalwa bakaboba. = The war drum was booming and the friction drums were throbbing. (2.-bobede, 3.-bobya, 4.-bobela. 6.-bobesya, 7.-boba-boba.)
  • collapse, as a roof or grave, Lululi Iwakali kuyanda kuboba, pesi cisamu eeci citegwa 'musemu' cakali kulujata kutegwa lutabobi. = The big roof was about to collapse but this center pole called musemu was supporting it so that it did not fall. Bataata babambulula cuumbwe cakaboba. = My father is repairing the grave which fell in.
  • heap, Zyoonse zintu nzyobelesya *kamuziboba kabotu.* = Heap together all the things you use.

swagger, parade in proud fashion, Wiide kubobaila kweenda akati kabeenzinyina mbuli kuti mbabavwubi. = He swaggers among his friends as though they are rich ones. Also: -bombomana, -bombaila. (2.-bobailide, 3.-bobaizya, 4. -bobailila, 6.-bobailisya)
collapse inwards, rt. -boba, Ciluli cananda yangu cakabobela mukati niyakawa mvwula mpati. = The roof of my house collapsed inwards when heavy rain fell. Also: -dilikila. (2.-bobede, 3.-bobya)

pierce, Bakamubobola sumo bana Munyumbwe syuumbwa. = The people of Munyumbwe pierced a lion. Also: -bbwalula, -bbobola, -bbwankula. (1.-bobolwa, 2.-bobwede, 3.-bobozya, 4.-bobolela, 6.-bobolesya, 8. -bobolana.)
  • challenge, Musankwa wakali kubobola kuti umwi amulwane. = The boy was offering a challenge for someone to fight him.
be deep sounding, Meenda inga abila, alaboboma mbuli ku Musiotunya. = When the water boils, it sounds like the Victoria Falls. Also: -bbobboma (2.-bobomede, 3.-bobomya, 4.-bobomena, 6.-bobomesya.)
cause to groan in pain, Kamufwambaana kuleta masumo tumubobye cina nombe. Quickly bring the spears so that we make him bellow in the way a cow does (2.-bobede, 4.-bobela, 6.-bobesya.)
boil, Zitende zilabodoma acikko. = The pumpkins are boiling on the fire. Also: -bbodoma, -bila. (2.-bodomede, 3.-bodomya, 4.-bodomena, 6.-bodomesya.)
bend immodestly, Ncibi kuboqola boobo akati kabantu. = It is indecent to bend immodestly like that in public. Also: -bongola, -dingama. (4.-bogweda, 6.-bogolesya, 8. -bogwedana.)

rot, Nyama ilafwambaana kubola kuti yamuka kusamwa. = The meat will quickly rot if you delay in cutting it up into strips and hanging it up. Tabakosoli kuulu ccita kuti kwabola. = They will not cut off the leg unless it is rotting. (2.-bolede, 3.-bozya, 4.-bolela, 6.-bolesya, 7.-bola-bola.)
span, Kamuboleka basune tukalime. = Span the oxen so that we can go and plough. Also: -vwoleka, -sungas, -bopa, -popa. (1.-bolekwa, 2.-bolekede, 3. -bolesya, 4.-bolekela)

rot at or in, rt. -bola, Tiibakali kuubelesya mugodi akaambo kakuti kwaanyikide mubwa mukati alimwi wakabolela mumo. = They were not using the well because a dog had drowned in it and was rotting away in it. (2.-bolede, 3.-bozya, 6.-bolesya, 7.-bola-bola)

become swollen, Cinkwele ulabolomana munsingo nalila. = The parrot becomes swollen at the neck when it is calling. Mwana wabolomana nkwaciswa cimbolomu. = The child is swollen due to suffering from mumps. (2.-bolomenye, 3.-bolomeka, 4.-bolomanina, 6.-bolomanisya.)
  • swell, Mwami naakanyema wakabolomana mbuli nkombola yanyema. When the chief got angry he was swelling up like a cobra when it is provoked. Also: -kolomana. =

be in a swollen state, Bantu nibakasika bakajana kuboko kwa Chimbwali kulibolomene kuzimba akaambo kameno ngaakalumidwe kumwinakwe jilo. = When the people arrived they found the arm of Chimbwali was swollen because of the teeth with which he was bitten by his wife the day before.

prepare or train for a particular purpose or activity; groom, Kobolosola mweenzinyoko kutegwa akabe muleli wacisi awalo. = Prepare your friend so that he also becomes a leader of the country. (1.-bolosolwa)

be calm, meek, soft, Mutinta wakabomba nindakamana kumwaambila, wakaleka kuuma mweenzinyina. = Mutinta became calm when I talked to her, she stopped beating her friend. Bomba, ulye malelo. = Be submissive so that you make progress. (1. -bombezegwa, 2. -bombede, 3.-bombya, 4.-bombela, 5.-bombelalyo, 6.-bombesya)
  • become soft, Sena zikutu zyabomba kabotu? = Have the skins become soft enough? Cikutu ncindakanyika mumeenda cakabomba. The skin which I soaked in water has become soft. Imvwula yawa, nyika njumu ilabomba. When the rain falls, the hard earth becomes soft. Izuba nilyakabomba-bomba, bakaunka kuya kuyobolola nombe. When the sun became weak they went to gather in the cattle.
  • be thankful, Ukabaambile bacembele kuti ndakabomba kucipego ncibakandipa. Please tell the old lady that I am thankful for the gift which she gave me. Also: -lumba.

make soft, rt. -bomba, Kamwiibombeka milomo yamulwazi atufwuta kutegwa ileke kupandauka. = Soften the lips of the patient with oil so that they stop cracking. Imbooma yamana kumujaya timba, ilamubombeka mate akumumena. After a python has killed a small antelope, it softens it with spittle and swallows it. (1.-bombeka, 2.-bombekwa, 3.-bombekede, 4.-bombesya, 5.-bombekela, 6.-bombekesya, 8.-bombekana.)
  • allay the thirst, Kuti kondipa meenda, ndilabombeka amoyo. = If you give me water, my throat will be relieved.

whisper, speak with low voice, Kwaamba mubombelela. = Speak in a whisper. Kwaambaula camubombelela batatumvwi bantu. = My friend let us talk softly so that people do not hear us. (used as an adverb, Kamwaambaula moombelela.) (1.-bombelelwa, 2.-bombelede, 3.-bombelesya, 4.-bombelelela, 8.-bombelelana.)

assuage, mitigate, cool down, rt. bomba, Zilacitika zintu eezi, kobombesya buyo moyo. = Just cool down that's the way things happen. (1.-bombesyegwa, 2.-bombesyede, 3.-bombya, 4.-bombesegwa, 8. -bombesyanya.) Also: -kkazika moyo

fall to ruins, disintegrate, dissolve, Citina citanaumpwa cilabomboka kuti caugwa mvwula. = A brick which is not burnt will disintegrate if the rain falls on it. Also: -yaaya. (2.-bombokede, 3.-bombya, 4.-bombokela, 6.-bomboka-bomboka)

beat, as clothes heaped together, soften, cause something to disintegrate, Kamubombola civwuma eeci kutegwa caandane tulye kabotu. = Beat this coconut so that it breaks up and we can eat it easily. (1.-bombolwa, 2.-bombolede, 3.-bombozya)
  • be lazy in posture, Musankwa wabombola kukkala nkaambo wakalya kapati. The boy sat lazily because he had eaten much.

dissolve, crumble, Cibiya citasumikidwe cabomboloka nicaugwa mvwula. = The pot which is not yet fired dissolved when the rain fell on it. (2.-bombolokede, 4.-bombolokela, 6.-bombolokesya)
  • soften in behaviour, Haanjabu wakalaa nkazi naakacili mwana, pesi sunu wakabomboloka. = Haanjabu was stubbourn when he was a child but today he has mellowed.

make oneself comfortable, be very still, Ndakabombomana kukkala cakuliiba kakunyina ncebula. = I was living in comfort freely without lacking anything. (2.-bombomene)
  • act in a pompous or arrogant manner, Ulaliyanda ncabombomana bobuya kukkala. = He is full of himself that is why he sits pompously like that.
live with one's neighbours, Muvwubi mubi watubombomanina. The bad rich person was living with us. Also: -tintimana

severely beat repeatedly, Bamubomboola bbwe. = They have hammered him with a stone. Kanene wakamubomboola kasako Cheelo akumusiila zicisa mumutwe = Kanene severely and repeatedly beat Cheelo with a stick and left him with head wounds. (1.-bomboolwa, 2. bomboolede, 3.-bomboozya, 4.-bomboolela, 6.-bomboolesya, 8.-bomboolana.)

be soft as jelly, Wakasintama alimwi akumujatauka, wajana mubili ucikasaala pele nguzu kunyina, ubombotoka buyo kumwaalamuna. = He bent down and touched him, he found the body was still warm but had no power, he was so soft when he tried to turn him over. (2.-bombotokede.)

train as ox, tame, Basune bajongosi beelede kubombya kutegwa balime kabotu. Young oxen need to be tamed so that they plough well. Also: -tambisya. (3.-bombesya)
  • show respect to another, Bamakaintu balalibombya kubaalumi babo. = Women respect their husbands. Also: - bonzya.
kick, Wakamubompa cibbaka kumatako. = He kicked him on the buttocks. Also: -bbompa. (1.-bompwa, 2.-bompede, 3.-bompizya, 4.-bompela, 6.-bompensya, 8.-bompana.)
be drained, Meenda oonse akabompoka mucikala. = All the water was drained from the well. (2.-bompokede.)
drain, Wakabompola meenda oonse mumukala. = He drained all the water from the well. Also: -kupa.
see, Ndamubona naayinda sunu. = I saw her when she passed by today. (1.-bonwa, 2.-bonede, 3.-bonezya or -bonya, 4.-bonena, 5.-bonenalyo, 6.-bonesya, 7.-bona-bona, 8.-bonana.)
be admired, Mebo ndabonekelwa abasankwa banji kucikolo. = I am admired by many boys at school. (2.-bonekedwe)

discover, Ndakabonena kayuni mpokakumba mucisamu. = I spied a little bird where it was sitting on its eggs in a tree. Also: -enena.
  • see something for somebody, Ndakubonena nombe zyako kumalundu. = I have seen your cattle among the hills.
see clearly, Bapati balaamba kuti munyati tabonesyi pe. = The elders say that a buffalo does not see very well. (2.-bonesyede, 8.-bonesyanya)

bend down from the waist protruding one's bottom, Leka kubongola mbuli muntu uciswa cibongozi. = Stop bending down like someone suffering from a disease of the anus. Also: -bogola. (2.-bongwede, 3.-bongozya, 6.-bongolesya, 8.-bongwedana.)
see again after temporary blindness, rt. -bona, Kabaide kale, wakazikubonununa alimwi. = Having been blind s/he began to see again.

make one experience, rt. bona, Kutamvwa kulaigwa cibonya mapenzi. To refuse to take advice causes you to experience problems.
  • see with, Magilazi alandibonya kabotu. = Spectacles help me to see well.
  • be seen, Mbeba yakanjila mubwina yakaleka kulibonya. The rat which entered the hole was no longer to be seen.

disintegrate, melt, Cibiya, ncibakabumba jilo baneene, cabonzoka nkaambo bana bacitila meenda. = The pot which my grandmother moulded yesterday has disintegrated because the children poured water on it. Masuku aabizwa ciindi cilamfwu alabonzoka. = Masuku fruits which have ripened for a long time fall apart. (2.-bonzokede, 3. -bonzosya, 4.-bonzokela.)

humble oneself, Kulibonzya kubapati ncibotu. = It is good to humble oneself before the elders. Also: -bombya.
  • cause to rot, rt. -bola, Imvwunyu zibonzya nyama. = Maggots rot the meat. Also: -bozya.
  • quench thirst, Mukaintu wakafwambaana kuleta muleu wacibwantu kuti mulumi alibonzye amoyo. = The wife quickly brought a pot of sweet-beer so that her husband could quench his thirst.
  • soften, Also: -bombya, -toba, -tobeka.
come, Koboola kuno ndaye, mebo njanda kweenda. = Come here so that I say good-bye, as I want to go. (2.-boolede, 6.-boolesya.)
have come, have arrived, rt.. boola, Awalo Joni wakaliboolede kumuswaangano wakainda. John also came to the last meeting. Also: -zide (rt. -za); (1. -booledwe).
come along, Joni awalo wakaboolela kucikolo. John has also come along to school.
cry readily as a child, Ooyu mwana uboomona buya kulila. = This child cries easily. Also: -bboomona. (2.-boomwede, 3.-boomozya, 4.-boomonena, 6.-boomonesya.)

separate calves from cows for milking at midday, Kuti mweemvwe wavwula, beembela balaboosya boombe kunombe. If there is plenty of fresh grass, the herders separate the cows from their calves. (1.-boosyegwa, 2.-boosyede)

bring back, rt. -boola, Ndafwambaana kuciboozya cibaki cako. = I will be quick to bring back your shirt. Ciindi casikati bakali kuziboozya kukukama. At midday they were bringing the cows back to be milked. Wauboozya moyo. The heart was brought back to life. Also: -josya, -pilusya. (1.-boozyegwa, 2.-boozyede, 3.-boozya, 4.-boozyanya.)
  • reinstate, Mwiiyi wakatandidwe bakamuboozya amulimo wakwe. = They reinstated the teacher who had been sent away.

yoke oxen, Nobasankwa, mufwume kubopa, tuya kulima juunza. = You boys, wake up early to span the oxen, we are going to plough tomorrow. (1.-bopwa, 2.-bopede, 3.-bopya, 4.-bopela, 5.-bopelalyo, 6.-bopesya, 7.-bopa-bopa, 8.-bopekana) Also: -vwoleka, -sunga, -popa.

make good, beautify, tidy up, rt.-bota, Kamubosya awa nkaambo beenzu mpobatiizookkale. = Clean up this place because it is where the visitors will sit. Also: -salazya. (1.-bosyegwa, 2.-bosyede, 3.-bosya, 4.-bosyezya, 5.-bosyezyalyo, 7.-bosyabosya, 8.-bosyanya.)
  • be sharp, Bakacikwenga cipanga kusikila cakabosya. = They sharpened the knife until it became sharp.

be kind, good, beautiful, sweet, Ooyu mwana wakabota naakasama zisani zipya. = This child was beautiful when she wore new clothes. Cilainda kubota kweembelela mutulonga nkaambo momuli bwizu bubotu. = It is better to graze the cattle among the little streams because that is where there is good grass. (2.-botede, 3.-botya, 4.-botela, 5.-botelalyo, 6.-botesya, 7.-bota-bota.)
please, gladden, Cakababotela bamayi cizyano cabamacembele ku Chiyobola. = The dance of the old women pleased the teachers at Chiyobola. (2.-botelwa, 3.-boteledwe, 5.-botelalyo, 6.-botelana.)
make nice, Kamubotya awo mwami mpazyookkala. = Make that place nice where the chief will sit.

begin to ripen, Incenje a nundu zyakatalika kale kubozeka. = The incenje and nundu fruits have begun to ripen. Also: -bozyeka. (1.-bozekwa, 2.-bozekede, 6.-bozekesya.)
  • cause to rot, rt. -bola Mudumu ulafwambaana kubozeka ndongwe. = Dampness makes the groundnuts rot easily.
cause to rot, rt. -bola, Filiji lyakaleka kubeleka akubozya nyama yakali mukati. = The fridge stopped working and rotted the meat which was inside. (1.-bozyegwe, 2.-bozyede, 4.-bozyezya)

flower, bloom, ripen, Mafwuleenke atalika kale kubozyeka. = The oranges have already started to ripen. Also: -bozeka. (2.-bozyekede)
  • cause to rot, rt. -bola, Izuba nolibala kapati, lilafwambaana kubozyeka nyama. = When the sun shines a lot, it quickly rots the meat. Also: -bozeka.
heap, Wakabubila masamu kutegwa abambe malasya. = He heaped up the wood so that he could make charcoal. Also: -bbubila, -babila. (1.-bubilwa, 2.-bubilide, 3.-bubizya)

wake up, rise, Kamubuka, bwaca, tuye kumuunda. = Rise, it has dawned, let us go to the field. Nibakali kunywa bukoko, yakabuka nkondo mpati. = When they were drinking beer, a great fight broke out. (2.-bukide, 3.-busya, 4.-bukila, 5.-bukilalyo, 6.-bukisya, 7.-buka-buka, 8.-bukilana.)
  • develop, Sunu cisi catalika kubuka, cilijisi zikolo zibotu. = These days the area is developing, it has good schools.
  • change behaviour, Muntu walikuseka, wabuka kulila nibafwa banyina. = The person who was laughing, changed to weep when his/her mother died.
  • take back what was given, also - bukila Wakandibuka mali ngaakandipede. = He took back the money which he had given me.
break a contract by returning a gift, e.g Musankwa a musimbi babukana zipego nzibakali kupana. = The boy and the girl returned the gifts which they had given to one another.

nurse into sleep, fondle, Mwana wakatalika koona, banyina nibakamubukata. = The child began to sleep, when the mother nursed it. Also: -butika, -fwukata. (1.-bukatwa, 2.-bukatide, 7.-bukata-bukata, 8.-bukatana.)

rise, rt. -buka, Basicikolo bakabukila antoomwe ciindi camafwumofwumo. = The schoolboys rose up together in the morning. Tubambo twakali kulibonya mbuli muntu mulwazi uutabukili bulo uciswa kakweekwe. = The ribs were seen like a sick person suffering from tuberculosis who is bed-ridden. Mpampawaawo akabukila lumamba lupati. = It is at that time that a great fight arose. Mpoona bakamutola kucibbadela nkwaakaakubukila. = Thereupon they took her to hospital where she regained consciousness. Nkondo yabukila uuvwuna. = The war rose up against the peacemaker. (1.-bukilwa, 2.-bukide, 3.-bukizya, 5.-bukilalyo, 8.-bukilana.)
  • take back what was given, Mainza wakaabukila mali ngaakapede Joni. = Mainza took back the money which he had given to John.
be in conflict with one another, Bantu baya bakalimvwene babukilana. Those people who were friends are fighting with one another.

recall a topic, revert to a question to make it clear, Munene wakali kubukulusya twaambo twakaindi kutegwa alungilwe kabotu. = The old man was recalling the past events so that he (himself) would be paid a just fine. (1.-bukulusyigwa, 2.-bukulusyide, 8.-bukulusyanya)
  • renovate, Wakatalika kubukulusya munzi. = He began to restore the village.

counsel, instruct, to teach wisdom, Kamuboola nomanene, kamutubula maanu. Come old men and enlighten us. Tulabuzya bamatatakulu a bamamakulu kuti batubule twaambo twakaindi. We are asking our grandfathers and grandmothers to instruct us in matters of the past. (1.-bulwa, 2.-bulide, 8. -bulana)
  • lack, be without, Nkubula maano cipa kuti muntu kacita zitayandiki. = It is lack of wisdom which leads a person to do things which are not necessary. Mapenzi akwe mapati akali aakubula matwi. = Her great problems was due to her deafness. Akati kabantu lyoonse takubuli batamvwi, batateeleli, batyola milawo alimwi batayoowi zitondwa. = Among people there are never lacking those who do not listen, who do not obey, who break laws and who do not fear to do what is forbidden. Mulibulizizye mukuyeeya kwanu. = You are seriously lacking in your thinking.
communicate with one another, Kubulana twaambo tugwasya ncibotu. = To share helpful ideas is good.

many people, Inkanga tiizyalili abuleya. The guinea fowl does not give birth where there are many. Cilatondwa kulikwatilila, mukaintu ngwabuleya. It is taboo to marry just for yourself, the woman belongs to many.

be not available, rt. -bula, Mutinta wabulika buyo mali masyoonto naawunka ku Monze. = Mutinta would have gone to Monze only that she was short of a little money.
  • be reliable, Ooyu muntu ulabulika nkaambo ulasisa maseseke. = This man is reliable because he keeps secrets. Also: -ambilika.
  • lack, be without, Mpongo zilabulika bwizu mulukoka. The goats were without grass among the umbrella thorn trees.

be deprived of, rt. -bula, Bantu babulila nsima. = The people have not enough nsima. Nibakali kuweza bakali kunga kuti umwi wabulila, balamulolezya. = When they were hunting they used to share the meat with the one who had not made a kill.
  • tell, advise, Wamubulila nzi kozyi kuti aaya mmaseseke? = Why did you tell him when you knew that these matters are confidential?

cause to be without, deprive, Aaba bana batubulizya zilyo. = These children have deprived us of food. Ndakabulizya mali ncindatakacuula cisani eeci. = I had not enough money, that is why I did not buy this garment.
jabber, Wakalota kuti waswaanganya bantu banji ibakali kwiide kubulubuzya kukanana. He dreamed he met with many people who were just jabbering. Also: -bwelebwezya

lose power, as medicine, Ooyu musamu wakabuluka. = This medicine is out of date.
  • become old or faded, as clothes, Buluke bwa Mainza bwabuluka kale. = The trousers of Mainza have aready faded. Also: -bbuluka, -jujuka.
  • die out as a custom, Cilengwa cakubangwa cakabuluka. = The custom of knocking out the teeth has died out. Lwiindi nolwakali kucitwa, mvwula yakalikuboola, kuleka mazuba ano zintu zyoonse nizyabuluka. = When the *Iwiindi* ritual was performed, the rain was coming, not like nowadays when all things have lost their power.
  • be barren as a field, Ooyu muunda wakabuluka. = This field was barren.
  • fade, as an emotion, Luyando Iwa Joni a Jeni Iwabuluka kuzyila cindi nobakakkede antoomwe munanda. = The love of John and Jenny has grown weak since the time they lived together in their home. (2.-bulukide, 3.-bulukisya, 4.-bulukila.)

make a disturbing noise, mutter, Eeci ncomunga mwali kubulukusya kukanana cinyonganya bantu babala. = This tendency of muttering disturbs the people who are studying. Also: -vwulukuta, -fwefwenezya. (1.-bulukusyigwa, 2.-bulukusyide, 8. -bulukusyanya.)

exhaust, as weeds do to a field, Isyokwe lyakabulula busani mumuunda. = The weeds exhausted the fertility of the soil. (1.-bululwa, 2.-bulukide, 3.-bulusya, 4.-bulukila, 5.-bulukilalyo, 6.-bululisya, 8.-bululana.)
  • spit out, Ndacibulula cakulya akaambo kakulula. = I spit the food out because of being bitter. Naakamvwa boobo wakatalika kulya mulilo masizi ula bulula. = When he heard this he began to eat fire and spit out the embers. (i.e. He was extremely annoyed.) Also: -swa.

run away in panic, stampede, Wakabulumuka kutija naakajanwa a mukamuntu. = He ran away in panic when he was found with another's wife. Nabulwe wabulumuka naabona babwa. = The iguana ran away in panic when it saw the dogs. Also: -lilimuka (2.-bulumukide, 3.-bulumusya, 4.-bulumukila, 6.-bulumukisya.)

roll about, Ncebulungana boobu mmutwe ucisa = It is the head which is paining which makes me roll about. Bacembele bakaliwaala ansi balabulungana. = The old woman threw herself on the ground rolling about. (a demonstration of gratitude) Also: -bbulungana, -syolomba, -culumba. (2.-bulungenye, 3.-bulunganya, 4. -bulunganina, 5. -bulunganinalyo)
  • become smooth and round, Twakajana haafwumbula katonta bufwumba mane limwi bwabulungana. = We found the black beetle pushing the cow-dung until it finally became smooth and round.

make smooth and round, Basankwa babulunganya bulongo kubamba mabwe aamalekani. = The boys made the clay smooth and round to make stones for the catapults.
  • roll as to make someone dirty, Naakamana kusamba, mwana wakalibulunganya mumavwu. = When the child had finished washing, it rolled about in the soil. Also: -bbulunganya.
be bursting, Masaya akwe akalibulungeme kuneneya. = His cheeks were bursting with fatness.
be round, Masaya akwe akalibulungene kuneneya. = His cheeks were fat and round. Mboibede nyika, ilibulungene. = That is how the world is, it is round.

impoverish, extract the power, annul, rt. -buluka, Munanga wakabulusya musamu wamulozi. = The witchdoctor neutralized the medicine of the witch. Also: -bbulusya. (1.-bulusyigwa, 2.-bulusyide, 4.-bulusyizya, 8.-bulusyanya.)
roll about on the ground, Bana balabuluukana kusobana. = The children are rolling about on the ground as they play. Also: -bbulungana. (4.-buluukanina.)
be instructed, rt. -bula, Bantu banji bakali kuunka kuli bina Muumbule kukubulwa maanu. = Many people were going to the mother of Muumbule to be instructed. (8.-bulana.)

mould, make a cake of, plaster, make pottery, Kubumba zibiya kuyandika kuti kakuli uukuyiisya. = You need someone to teach you how to make clay pots. Nobasimbi mujatisye mulimo wakubumba, unununa banakazi banji mucisi ca Batonga. = Girls, continue with pottery work, it has sustained many women in Tongaland. (1.-bumbwa, 2.-bumbide, 3.-bumbya, 4.-bumbila, 5.-bumbilalyo, 6.-bumbisya, 7.-bumba-bumba, 8.-bumbilana)
  • eat as termites, Cuulu cibumba mapopwe angu mumuunda. Termites are eating my maize in the field.

be quick in mould- ing, Kamubumba-bumba zibiya eezyo kutegwa zyuulwe kufwambaana. = Make those clay pots quickly so that people buy them soon.
  • comfort a distressed person, Ka- mumubumba-bumba mucaala kutegwa atani kuyeeyi bakafwa. Console the orphan so that s/he does not think about the dead. Also: -umbulizya
  • pout, Mwana ulaa mambeke ula- bumba-bumba malomo nokunyina a mbwaaba. A spoilt child pouts for no reason. Also: -bbebbenyana, -bbebbula, -debbula, -piinyika, -pipinyana.
hang as a swarm, Ndajana nzuki zilibumbilide acisamu. = I found a swarm of bees hanging from a tree.

swarm over, hang as swarm, bees clustering around the queen bee, Bunyenyene bwabumbilila cinkwa. The black ants have swarmed over the bread. Mwana naakainda mpozyakabede inzuki, zyakamubumbilila akutalika kumuluma. When the child passed near the bee-hive, the bees swarmed around him and began to sting him. Bakali kubumbilila mulilo. They were crowding around the fire. Also: -milila. (1.-bumbililwa, 2.-bumbilide, 3.-bumbilizya, 4.-bumbilila, 5.-bumbililalyo, 6.-bumbilisya, 8.-bumbililana.)
  • mould carefully, rt. bumba, Bacembele bakafwambaana kucibumbilila cibiya nicakatiikomoke. The old woman was quick to mould the pot when it was about to crack.

peel off, wear away, Eeli bbwe lilabumbuluka notulicumbya. This stone wears away when we use it for scrubing ourselves. Also: -seuluka, -buuluka.
  • roll about on ground, Kana kalabumbuluka muvwu nokasobana. = The little child rolls around in the dust when playing. Also: -bbulungana. (1.-bumbulukwa, 2.-bumbulukide, 3.-bumbuluzya, 4.-bumbulukila.)
shell as mealies, Kamwaabumbulula mapopwe aaya. Shell these maize cobs. Also: -buulula, -umbulula, -senkemuna. (1.-bumbululwa, 2.-bumbulukide, 3.-bumbulusya, 4.-bumbulwida.)
roll on ground, Wakoona ansi kalibumbulusya kulumba makwe akwe. = He rolled on the ground thanking his in-laws. (2.-bumbulusyide.)

be round and smooth, Kamucikakwizinga kabwe kakukwiizya tombwe nkaambo takanabumbusana. = Continue to rub the little stone for grinding tobacco because it is not yet round and smooth enough. Miindi yamusimbi ooyu yakalituntumene a kubumbusana kabotu. = The calves of this girl were shapely and well rounded and smooth. Also: -bulungana, -umbusana. (2.-bumbusene, 3.-bumbusanya, 4.-bumbusanina.)
be in a smooth, round state, Kabwe kakukwiizya tombwe kalibumbusene. = The small stone for crushing tobacco is smooth and round..

mould with, rt. -bumba, Bumwi bulongo mbwakubumbya nongo ambede. = Some clay is for making big pots and drinking mugs. (1.-bumbisigwa, 2.-bumbisyidwe, 3.-bumbya.)
  • cause to be eaten by termites, Mwana wakacibumbya cisani naakacisiya anze. = The child caused the garment to be eaten by termites when she left it outside.
insult, Koleka kubumina, cilatondwa. = Stop insulting, it is taboo. Also: -tukila, -tukana. (1.-buminwa, 2.-buminide.)

be long dead, become worn or inedible, Eeyi nyama yankuku yakabunda kale, ilaa nkubi. = This chicken meat is already inedible, it is mouldy. Dilwe talibundi. (or Sidilwe tabundi) = A funeral never dies. (i.e. no matter how long ago the funeral has taken place you can always go and offer your condolences.) Also: -vwunda. (2.-bundide, 3.-bundya, 4.-bundila, 5.-bundilalyo, 6.-bundisya, 7.-bundabunda.)

fade as colours, become unclear, Mubala wamulembo oyu wabunda-bunda. = The colour of this cloth has faded. Meso akwe akali kubunda-bunda mumudima. = His eyes could not see clearly in the dark. Also: -zimaana

stay in one place for a long time, Twakabundaya kudilwe lyamwami nkaambo lyakatola mazuba manji. = We spent a long time at the funeral of the chief because it took many days. Also: -bungula, -bunduka.

be in a corrupt or faded state, rt. -bunda, Nyemu eezi zilibundide. = These groundnuts are rotten. Sunu mukondo ngwaakasiya mpouli, nokuba kuti ulibundide-bundide. = Today the track which he left is there, even though it has faded.

prolong stay in a place, Ba Choombe babunduka mu Chikuni. = Mr. Choombe has overstayed in Chikuni. Ndali kubunduka, ndali kubunduka, tababooli. = I waited and waited, but he does not come. (1.-bundukwa, 2.-bundukide, 3.-bundusya, 4.-bundukila, 6.-bundukisya.) Also: -bbunduka, -punduka, -juluka.
  • become worn out, Eeci citeenge cakabunduka. = This citeenge material is worn out. Also: -buluka, -jujuka.
overstay or stay for no reason, Basa atupiluke kuminzi yesu, twabundulala kuno. = Friends let us return home, we have prolonged our stay here.

die down, Mulilo acikko nowakabundulata, ntunga zyakaya kuli nguwe akumusipa bulowa. = When the fire in the fireplace died down, the insects came to him and sucked his blood. (2.-bundulete, 3.-bundulatya, 4.-bundulalila.)
shrink back before starting to run, Wakabunduluka naakatiilun duke. = He shrank backwards when he was about to run.

gather, as maize stalks, Balimi banji balabunga makuba mumyuunda yabo kumwaka. = Many farmers collect the maize stalks in their fields during the last part of the dry season. Inkasaalo yakamweenda mbuli kuti ulabunga. = He is sweating as if he is gathering maize-stalks in a field. (1.-bungwa, 2.-bungide, 3.-bunzya, 4.-bungila, 5.-bungilalyo, 6.-bungisya, 7.-bunga-bunga.)

gather, Kamubunga-bunga makuba ayo tulibambile kulima. = Gather up the maize stalks so that we prepare ourselves for ploughing. Bantu bakalibunga-bunga kutegwa baunke anto-omwe kuya kukwaanzya mwami mupya. = The people gathered so that they could go together to greet the new chief.

congregate, assemble, come together, Bantu bakabungana lyadilwe. = People gathered at the time of a funeral. (1.-bunganwa, -bunganide, 3.-bunganya, 4.-bunganina, 5.-bunganinalyo, 6.-bunganisya, 7.-bungana-bungana.)
gather around, Ino tuya kubunganina kuli juunza? = Where shall we assemble tomorrow?

gather people or animals together, Ndakabunganya bamacembele kuti bandiyiisye. = I gathered the old women for them to teach me. Wakabunganya basune kuti babopwe. = He brought the oxen together to be yoked.

wait as one lost, Ndiswe twalumba nkomwatusisya ananda, nikwali kunga tulabungaula acitisyini. = It is we who are thankful because you have brought us home, if not we were going to anxiously wait at the station. Also: -bungula (2.-bungaulide, 3.-bunga-uzya, 4.-bungaulila, 6.-bungaulisya)

heap together, Kamubungika makuba kutegwa aumpwe. = Gather the maize stalks so that they be burnt. Also: -lundika, -kunga-kunga. (1.-bungikwa, 2.-bungikide, 3.-bungizya, 4.-bungikila, 6.-bungikisya, 7.-bungika-bungika, 8.-bungikana.)
become impatient, Twakabungula kumulindila, walo kunyina naakasika. = We were impatient waiting for him, and he never came. (2.-bungulide, 4.-bungulila.) Also: -bundaya, -bungaula.

remain alone, Boonse basaama bakamana kufwa, ndime ecibungulala. = All my contemporaries have died, it is I who still remain alone. Ndasiigwa njide kubungulala ananda endikke kubee ndime mulonda ulonda caanda cakwe. = I am just left remaining alone at the house as if I am the watchman who guards his shack.
  • sitting with nothing to do, Wakajana milwi-milwi yabantu ilabungulala balindilizya kusika kwacitima. = He found crowds of people sitting waiting for the arrival of the train. Also: -bungaula
be smooth, Naakamana kumunanika mafwuta mwana, cikanda cakwe cakabungusana. = When she had smeared oil on the child, its skin began to become smooth. Also: -bumbusana (2.-bungusene, 3.-bungusanya.)
be in a smooth condition, Mubili wakwe ulibungusene. = His body is very smooth.
rebel, defy, Ooyu mwana wakababungwida bazyali bakwe, wabazangila. = This child has defied its parents, it has rebelled on them. Also: -bbungwida. (1.-bungwidwa, 2.-bungwide.)

throw down, Mwana wacibunta cinkwa mumamvwu. = The child has thrown the bread down in the soil. Nowakasika mutumba wamufwu, bamacembele bakalibunta muvwu. = When the body of the dead person arrived, the old women threw themselves down in the dust. Also: -bbunta, kulivwikkila. (1.-buntwa, 2.-buntide, 3.-buntya, 4.-buntila, 5.-buntilalyo, 6.-buntisya, 7.-bunta-bunta, 8.-buntana.)
be extremely sorry, Ndakaile kubuntama nindakamvwa kuti wakafwa. I was just so sad when I heard she had died. Also: -lembukilwa (2.-buntamide, 3.-buntamisya.)

be competent in handling many jobs, Uulya kuti wamutwala inga nabuntauka munanda ayebo wamvwa nanda yalemenena. If you marry that one, you will feel that the house is honoured the way she carries out so many tasks so efficiently. .(2.-buntaukide, 3.-buntausya, 4.-buntaukila, 5.-buntaukilalyo, 6.-buntaukisya.)
reveal, Kubununa bulale bwamuntu tacili cibotu pe. = To reveal the adultery of another person is not good. Also: -bbutula, -bbununa. (1.-bununwa, 2.-bunwide, 3.-bunusya, 4.-bununina, 8.-bununana.)
wake up for, rt. -buka, Kamundibusizya mwana, anyonke. Wake the child up for me, so that it sucks. (2.-busizye, 3.-busya, 4.-busyila)

waken, rouse, Kamumubusya alye. Wake him so that he can eat. Ngoma nizyakalila kabotu, zyakabusya masabe aamucembele. When the drums were well played, they caused the old woman to be aroused by the masabe spirits. (1.-busyigwa, 2.-busyizye, 4.-busyizya.)

pick out for enforced service, (in colonial days) Bamasinja bakali kubuta bantu akubatola kucibbalo. The messengers would pick out men for enforced labour. Also: -jata cibbalo. (1.-butwa, 2.-butide, 3.-butya, 4.-butila, 5.-butilalyo, 6.-butisya, 8.-butana.)
move about actively, Mukaintu muyumu ulabutauka ciindi coonse, takkali buyo. An industrious woman is active all the time, she does not just sit. (2.-butaukide, 3.-butausya) Also: -kutauka, -buntauka.

lull to sleep, Kamumubutika mwana ajanike woona twayanda kweenda. Put the child to sleep so that it is sleeping when we want to go. (1.-butikwa, 2.-butikide, 4.-butikila, 5.-butikilalyo) Also: - vwululatika.

pack, Ndakatuma basankwa bobilo kubutila bwizu acibalu munsi ananda kutegwa muwo ukwabililwe.= I sent two boys to pack grass into the windbreak near the house so that there would be protection from the wind. (1.-butilwa, 2.-butilide, 3.-butisya, 4.-butukila, 5.-butukilalyo, 6.butukisya.)
put things together, pile up as stones, Mwaalumi mulyato ubutitika bamakaintu banji mulukwato. A greedy man gathers up many wives. Also: -lundika

gain weight, Mazuba ainda Kachesa wakalifwulukide, mazubaano wabutuka. In past days Kachesa had become thin, but these days he has improved in weight. Aaka kana nikakazyalwa kakali kaniini, mazubaano kabutuka. = This baby was small when it was born, nowadays it has gained weight.

squat, Wakasintama ansi kulangisisya kanyama mpokakabutumene nkokapwatula meso mbuli kuti ninsozi yaceyo. He bent down looking carefully at the small animal squatting, rolling its eyes like a grass-hopper in a time of plenty. (2.-butumene, 3.-butumisya, 4.-butumanina)

jump up and down, Nzweluuke wakamunika, wakabona siko swe ulabutuuka. = Nzweluuke lit up the place and found the rat jumping up and down. Also: -mantauka, -sotooka. (3.-butuusya, 4.-butuukila, 6.-butuukisya)

take away something from, as a handful of grain, as from a big bag with both hands, subtract, Kobuula busu mujanza. = Take out a handful of meal. Cakulya ameenda kwakali kubuula vwu. = The food and the water were to be taken as much as you wanted. Poonda abananyina bakatubuula tunyemu twakasyaala akutalika kukwanga. = Poonda and his friends took some groundnuts that remained and began to eat them raw. (1.-buulwa, 2.-bwiide/-buulide, 3.-buuzya, 4.-bwiida, 5.-bwiidalyo, 8.-bwiidana.)

raise one's eyes looking upwards, Twajana mucembele wiide kubuulala kulanga mujulu kuti abone ndeke. = We found the old woman just looking up so that she would see the plane. Also: -bbuulala. (2.-buulalide, 3.-buulazya, 4.-buulalila.)

be shelled, crumble, Aaya mapopwe abuuluka kabotu. = This maize shells well. (2.-buulukide, 3.-buuluzya, 4.-buulukila.)
  • fall, as heavy rain, Ijilo mvwula yakabuuluka. = Yesterday the rains were heavy. Also: -cobola, -lyobola.

shell as mealies, Kamwaabuulula mapopwe tubone masaka atiivwule. = Shell the maize so that we see how many bags will be filled. Kamuleta mitiba mubanze mapopwe akabuululwa kale. = Bring dishes and take out the maize that has aleady been shelled. (1.-buululwa, 2.-buulwide, 3.-buuluzya, 4.-buulwida, 8.-buulwidana.) Also: -bumbulula, -umbulula, -senkemuna.

shell mealies by using something, Bamacembele bakali kubuuluzya zinkonti kutegwa bafwambaane kumanizya. = The old women were using empty maize cobs to shell so that they would quickly finish. Also: -umbuluzya. (1.-buuluzyigwa, 2.-buuluzyide, 3.-buuluzya, 4.-buulwida, 8. -buulwidana.)

become white with dust, Mumwezi wa Kkunkumuna-masamu bamakaintu balabuumuna kapati nkaambo kalusuko. = In the month of July the women become white with the dust. Also: -tubuluka. (2.-buumwide, 3.-buumuzya)

rub with hands, Ndakalibuwa ankumo nindakatalika Iweendo Iwangu. = I was rubbing myself on the forehead when I started my journey (i.e. traditional sign invoking good fortune). Toonse ano tuyakutalika kulibuwa kumakosi notuyeeya zyakaindi akuti, "Iiyi, mmasimpe alya akali mazuba nsini." We here will begin to rub the back of our necks when we think of past things and say, "Yes indeed they were different days." Ulibuwa-buwa kumutwe ulasekaseka ulanga kumweenzinyina. = He rubbed his head laughing looking at his friend. (1.-buugwa, 2.-buwide, 3.-buusya, 4.-buwila, 5.-buwilalyo, 6.-buwisya, 7.-buwa-buwa, 8.-buwana.)
  • lying about, as cattle under a tree resting, Ezi nombe ncoziile kubuwa mucimvwule nkokuti zyakkuta. = The reason why these cattle are just lying about in the shade is that they are satisfied.

rub in. well, Kamumubuwa-buwa amusamu Changu kutegwa ayumye. = Rub Changu well with the medicine so that he recovers. Muntu naafwa bamacembele inga balamubuwa-buwa akumoonda nkoye. = When a person is dying the elderly women rub the body with their hands and close the eyes.

rub one another, Kamubuwana amafwuta muzibaka momutalisiki. = Rub each other with oil in places where you cannot reach yourself. Basankwa ba buwana musamu kumeso. = The boys are rubbing each other with medicine on the faces.
nsima eat nsima without relish, Twakaibuya nsima nkaambo twakabula cisyu. We ate the nsima by itself because we had no relish. Also: -ganka nsima.
be tired of waiting, Bantu bakabuyala musololi naakamuka kusika amuswaangano. The people became tired of waiting when the leader was late for the meeting. Also: -bundaya.

rub with a little oil, Kamubuyausya buya mafwuta kutegwa muvwulile nyoonse. Rub in just a little oil so that there is enough for all of you. Also: -nanika, -zila-zila. (1.-buyausyigwa, 2.-buyausyide, 3.-buyausisya, 8.-buyausyanya)

lick, as sugar on hand, Utalimani kulibuyila ccuka, tubikke mucibwantu. = Do not lick all the sugar, we want to put it in the sweet beer. Also: -bwiila, -mwankila. (1.-buyilwa, 2.-bwiide, 3.-buyizya)
  • scoop up, Amumubweze mwana aleke kubuyila museenga. = Take up that child so that it stops scooping up the sand. (into the mouth)

inquire intensively, rt. buzya, Kutegwa uzyibe kuti cintu cilayandika nkubuzisisya. = You need to inquire carefully to know what is needed. Kamubabuzisisya bana kutegwa bamutondezye nzila mfwiifwi. Question the children carefully so that they show you the shortcut. (1.-buzizyigwa, 8.-buzisisyanya.)
inquire for someone, rt. buzya, Ndakafwambaana kumubuzizya zina lyamuntu wakamuuma mwanaakwe. I quickly inquired for him the name of the person who beat his child. (8.-buzizyanya.)

question, inform, advise, counsel, rt. -bula, Komubuzya nkwaazyila. Ask him where he has come from. (1.-buzyigwa, 2.-buzyide, 4.-buzyizya, 5.-buzyizyalyo, 6.-buzisya, 7.-buzyabuzya, 8.-buzyanya.)
  • (idiomatic use) Wamvwa nzala yamubuzya mukowa. She felt the hunger so much that it caused her to seek out and get to know her relatives. {A proverb says, Nzala itondezya (izyibya) mukowa. = Hunger makes one know the clan.}
  • cause to lose, rt. -bula, Mizeezo yakuvwuba yamukatazya, yamubuzya nonzi, yamubuzya maanu. Thoughts of possessing wealth trouble him, they deprive him of sleep, they take away his wisdom.

consult together, Mwalikkede kamubuzyanya mibuzyo mibotu. You were seated asking each other good questions. Twali kulibuzyanya mbotunga tuleenda kuya ku Lusaka. = We were conferring together as to how we should go to Lusaka.

come to surface, bubble at surface (as live fish) Inswi zilabwa kapati kuti kwaba kumazuba. The fish come to the surface when it is evening. (2.-bwide, 3.-bwizya, 4.-bwida or bwizyila)
  • babble, blurt out, Wakali kwiile kubwa, kunyina ncaakali kukanana. = He was just babbling, he said nothing. Umwi mwana wakaile kubwa kwaamba cintu ncaatakali kuyanda Mainza. = One child was just carelessly talking about something which Mainza did not want to be disclosed. Akaambo kakwiile kubwa kufwumbwa caboola kumoyo, Mainza wakabula mweenzinyina. Because of just blurting out anything which came to her heart, Mainza had no friend.
  • pulsate, Taakwe akasinga nokaceya kakali kulimvwinsya kubwa. = There was not even a small vein that was pulsating.

hop, jump down from a vehicle, Kobwaantuka kuzwa mucimbayambaya, tonacembaala. = Hop down from the vehicle, you are not yet old. Also: -bbwaantuka, -dwaantuka, -sotoka. (1.-bwaantukwa, 2.-bwaantukide, 3.-bwaantusya, 4.-bwaantukila, 6.-bwaantukisya, 7.-bwaantukabwaantuka, 8.-bwaantukana)
waddle, Jumbe wakali kubwabwaila biya kweenda nkaambo wakakkutila lyo. = Jumbe was just waddling along because he was completely full. (4.-bwabwailila.)
shiver, Mubili ulabwakama. The body is shivering. Also:
-tuntuma, -zyangama, -zuzuma.

come to surface like fish, Inswi zyalikubwalula notwainda. = The fish was coming to the surface when we passed by. Also: -bwa (1.-bwalulwa, 2.bwalwide, 3.-bwalusya, 4.bwalwida, 8.-bwalulana.)
  • bore a hole, pierce, Inombe yokwesu bakaibwalula sumo. = They pierced our cow with a spear. Also: -bbwalula
pound corn, Kamubwamuna maila kuti bube busu. = Pound the corn so that it becomes powder. Also: -dibula (1.-bwamunwa)
lie flat, Wakabwandalala kuyuba mubwizu. = He lay flat, hiding in the grass. (2.-bwandalete.) Also: -vwantabala,-landabala, -bwandalata.

run with short steps, Bina Mainza nkubaneneya kulunduka baile kubwanka. The mother of Mainza as she is so fat, when she runs she trots. Cibize ulabwanka amwana akwe atala. Ndiziyo ankando. (a riddle) = The zebra runs off with its young on top. It is a grinding stone and a grinder. (4.-bwankila, 7.-bwanka-bwanka.)
waddle, Kuneneya kwalo, Mutinta wiile kubwankabwanka kulunduka. Because of being fat, Mutinta waddles along when she is running.
stab with spear, Choonga wakamubwankula sumo mubbi. = Choonga stabbed the thief with a spear.
crouch down on, Nibakali kusobana bakali kubwata maulu aabo. = When they were playing they crouched down on their feet.
become watery, Eeci cimbwali cakabwaya, ncocitanoni. = This sweet-potato has become watery, that is why it is not tasty. Also: -pulumba. (2.-bwaide, 3.-bwaizya, 4.-bwayila, 5.-bwayilalyo)
open eyes wide, Kobwazula meso aako notiibone nyeleti. = Open your eyes wide, that is when you will see the needle. Also: -pwatula. (1.-bwazulwa, 2.bwazwide, 3.-bwazulizya, 8.-bwazulana.)
return, go back, Beenzu bakatulaya kale kubweeda nkobakazyilide. = The visitors already bade farewell on returning to where they had come from. Also: -joka, -piluka, -jokela. (4.-bweedela)
return, Cakatola mawoola manji-manji kuti abweede kubuzumi bwini-bwini. = It took many hours for him to return to real life.
give back, Kobweedezya nkomeki nkooyijana. Take the cup back to where you found it. Also: -jokezya, -pilusya. (1.-bweedezyegwa, 8.-bweedezyanya)
return, (Ila) Nokwakaba kumazuba Dwaantwa wakalaya wakabweela kwakwe. When it was evening Dwaantwa said goodbye and returned home. Also: -bweeda.

look for a quarrel, complain, Ulaciyanda cakubweka lyoonse, akaa mbo kaako bantu tabamuyandi pe. = She is always complaining, that is why people do not like her. Muntu ubweka caamba kuti ulaa kumulomo. Ngonguyooyo unga wati akanane-kanane buti, kunyina muntu unga wamuteketela. = A person who complains is said to be full of useless talk. This is the kind of person that no matter how s/he talks no one listens to him/her. (1.-bwekelwa, 2.-bwekede, 4.-bwekela, 6.-bwekesya, 7.-bweka-bweka, 8.-bwekelana) Also: -bwenta.

go about from one place to another, Webo wiile *kubwelauka* kweenda akooku-akooku akaambo kakutalilemeka kwako. = You are just wandering about here and there because you have no respect for yourself. (2.-bwelaukide, 3.-bwelausya, 4.-bwelaukila.)
babble, Koleka

kuti bapati kabaamba. = Do not be babbling when the elders are speaking. Balaambaula notutazimvwi nzyobaambaula. Babaanga baide *kubwele-* *bwezya*. = They speak when we do not understand what they are saying. They seem to be just babbling. Also: -bebeezya, -vwelenganya.

be alarmed, Bazyali nibakamvwa kuti mwanaabo wakatizya musimbi, bakaile *kubwelemana*. = When the parents heard that their child had taken a girl for marriage illegally, they were alarmed. (4.-bwelemanina.)

become watery or too soft as porridge, Cibwantu *cabweluka* kale, utabikki umbi munkoyo. = The sweet beer is already watery, don't add any more roots. (2.-bwelukide, 3.-bwelusya, 4.-bwelukila, 6.-bwelukisya.)
make porridge light, Kofwambaana *kubwelula* ceele kutegwa tulye. = Be quick to make light porridge so that we can eat.

fuss about something missing, Mucembele *wakabwembauka* naakasowa mali. = The old lady fussed about when she lost her money. Also: -embauka. (1.-bwembaukwa, 2.-bwembaukide, 3.-bwembauzya, 4.-bwembaukila, 6.-bwembaukisya, 8.-bwembaukana.)
tremble in fear, Bantu bakatalika *kubwembweleka* kuyoowa nibakabona basinkondonyina. = The people began to tremble in fear when they saw their enemies. (2.-bwembwelekede, 3.-bwembwelesya)
rant, *Kubwem-*
akupozomoka mbuli muntu ulaa ncinko kunyina ncocitiindijanye pe. = To rant and rave like a mad person does nothing to help me find a solution.

be able or be in a position to see, Ndalimubwene naakkede kumbele ankamu yabasimbi. = I had seen him when he was sitting in front of the group of girls.
  • have experience, rt. -bona, Ulici*bwene kubeza*. = He knows how to carve. Also: -zyi. (1.-bwenwe)

dip into gravy, use relish, Ijilo *twakabwenga* cisyu cinono. = Yesterday we dipped into a tasty relish. Nikwabula cisyu, *twabwenga* koondoonde. = When we had no relish, we dipped into fried pounded groundnuts. *Kubwenga* nyabo akusama masaili, twakaakucimvwa. = We got tired of having beans for relish and wearing prison uniform. Ngooyu musinza, kwabula buyo *babwenga*. = There is the gravy, all it needs is for them to dip into it. (1.-bwengwa, 2.-bwengede, 3.-bwenzya, 4.-bwengela, 7.-bwenga-bwenga.) Also: -sunsa, -jompeka.

re-dip in the relish which is insufficient, rt. -bwenga, Tiitwakakkuta nkaambo tusyu twakali twakubwe ngulula. = We were not satisfied because we were re-dipping into the inadequate relish. (1.-bwengululwa, 2.-bwengulwide, 3.-bwenguluzya.) Also: -bandauzya, -kwangulula.

quarrel, Ijilo baama abataata bakali kubwensyanya masiku. = Last night my mother and father were quarreling. Mainza wakaujata moyo limwi baakusika kumunzi kabotu-kabotu kakunyina kubwesyanya munzila. = Mainza controlled his heart until they arrived home nicely without quarreling on the way. Also: -bwentelana

complain, protest, Bataata bakabwenta kapati Joni naakasowa nombe. My father was complaining a lot when John lost the cows. Mukaintu wakalaa cindongwe wakabwenta naakajana ndongwe zyakwe zyamana kubbigwa. = The woman who had a groundnut plot complained when she found her groundnuts had been stolen. (1.-bwentelwa, 2.-bwentede, 3.-bwentya, /-bwentezya, 4.-bwentela, 5.-bwentelalyo, 6.-bwentesya, 8.-bwentelana.)
quarrel, Chiimba a mukaintu wakwe bakali kubwentelana jilo masiku nkaambo bakalikoledwe. = Chiimba and his wife were quarreling yesterday because they were drunk. Also: -bwensyanya.

have or had seen, rt. -bona, Oyu muntu wakeenda musinzo mulamfwu kusikila limwi wasika nkwaakabwenyi kuti kuli mbeba zinji. = This man went a long distance until finally he reached were he had seen there were many rodents.

be lecherous, have excessive sexual desire, Naakakkede akati kabasimbi, wakali kwiide kubwenyuka. When he was seated among the girls, he was filled with lust. (2.-bwenyukide, 3.-bwenyuzya, 4.-bwenyukila, 6.-bwenyukisya.)
  • be startled, Ndakabwenyuka nindakamvwa muntu undijata kusyule. = I was startled when someone caught me from behind. Also: -bbwenyuka.
dip nsima into something, rt. -bwenga, Ino wali kubwenzya cisyu nzi? What relish were you dipping into? (Ila) Also: -lisya, -sunsa.

quarrel, Mwaalumi wakaujata moyo limwi baakusika amukaintu wakwe kumunzi kakunyina kubwesyanya munzila. The husband controlled his heart without quarreling with his wife until they arrived home. Also: -bwensyanya, -bwentelana.

take hold of, carry, Kamubweza nkuni eezi muzibikkile aambi. = You carry these pieces of firewood and put them in another place. (1.-bwezegwa, 2.-bwezede, 3.-bwezezya, 4.-bwezela, 5. -bwezelalyo, 6.-bwezesya, 7.-bweza-bweza, 8.-bwezana.)
  • set out on a journey, Kuti wabweza Iweendo lulamfwu, uleelede kubweza acakulya. If you go on a long journey, you should take food.
  • take registration card, Mutinta wakakkala mazuba otatwe kumunzi, buzuba bwane wakacibweza camutwe. = Mutinta stayed for three days at the village, on the third day she picked up her registration card.

pick up, rt. -bweza, Ndabwezela mali munzila. Luckily I picked up money on the path. (1.-bwezelwa, 2.-bwezelede, 8.-bwezelana.) Also: -gomena.
  • carry or take for, Kamundibwezela cisuwo eeci ndiyakucijana kumunzi wanu. = Carry this basket for me, I will find it at your village. Nobakalomba kuti bababwezele mulwazi, bakazumina. = When they asked to take the patient for them, they agreed.
gather up, Wakabwezelela mabwe manji akwaanga mumulembo ngwaakasamide. = He gathered up many stones and tied them up in a cloth which he was wearing. (1.-bwezelelwa, 2.-bwezelede.)
lick up or from hands, Aaba bana bali kubwiila ccuka. = These children were licking the sugar up. (1.-bwiilwa, 2.-bwiilide, 3.-bwiizya, 4.-bwiilila.) Also: -buyila

go off quickly, Bantu nobakamulangisya kapati, cakamucima limwi walo wakanyamuka makoto ngooyu nkubwindaila waunka kwakwe. = When the people stared at him it annoyed him, then suddenly there the fellow is, rushing off back home.
rush off, Sena munyati takuli kubwindima kutija. = Did not the buffalo rush away at high speed. (2.-bwindimide, 4.-bwindimanina.)
rush, Haaluno wakalubwindimuna lubilo kutozya kunselelo kwa Chijanwa kuya kumunzi. = Haaluno rushed home to Chijanwa.

sow, Ndakabyala nsangu zyacisyu eeci ncobati 'namajindi'. = I sowed the seeds of this vegetable plant which they call namajindi. Also: -syanga (1.-byalwa, 2.-byalide, 3.-byalizya, 4.-byalila, 5.-byalilalyo, 6. -byalisya, 7.-byala-byala, 8.-byalilana.)
belch, Ndali kwiile kubyola mayi ngindakalikulya masiku. = I was just belching the gases of the eggs I had eaten at night. Also: -bbya (1.-byolwa, 2.-byolide.)

snare, catch in noose or net, Bana baca inziba yomwe akaiba komwe mutooye twabo. = The children caught one dove and a small dove in their traps. Bana baca kasulwe a mbeba. = The children trapped a rabbit and a rat. Wakaca bayuni a banyama mutukole twakwe amu makole aakwe. = He caught birds and animals in small traps and big traps. Also: -teya (1.-cegwa, 2.-cede, 3,-cezya, 4.-ceda) Some kinds of traps: *Mulindi* = a deep hole or pit narrowing towards the bottom to trap big game. *Inkona* = very big pit to trap several head of game. *Kabulindi* = a small hole concealing noose to catch every variety of game, even elands. (Also: *ikole*.) The strong rope used is called *kakole*. The smaller ones are

or *tooze*. The noose itself is called *bufwizu*. The bent pole or stick acting as a spring is called *mweeto* or *mulapu*. The little bit of string which holds very part in place is called *intanyo* or *munano*. *Idiba*, *pl. maliba* = a fall-trap with a flat stone to catch rats, birds etc. It has five parts: *kakole* = a string; *mweeto* = the top stick tied to the string (also *mulapu*); *inkwabyo* = a peg (also *inkanka* ); *intanyo-ntanyo* = a very small stick tied to the string below; *syaanano* = a longer stick which when trodden on by the prey, releases the flat stone. (Also: *munano*, *intando*) *Kantembo* = a small hole with a pad of grass at the mouth, bait at the bottom, and a noose laid horizontally to catch carniverous quadrupeds. (Also: *imbobo*) *Bukukulika* = a noose set vertically in the runs of birds to catch them by the neck. (Also: *bukuki, bukulila*) *Kooye kakaanda* = a small construction or tiny hut with a noose laid on little sticks to entangle the neck of guinea-fowls and other birds.

(*moono, kalabwi*) = a fish trap. The trap-door inside of the fish trap is called *buvwazi* (*bunjililo*) *Kaanda* = a big trap with two compartments one for a small animal used as bait, the other for the large animal to be caught, like a leopard. When a trap falls it is said to -lebuka, or -lesuka.
  • dawn, Kwaca kale, tuye kumilimo. = It has already dawned, let us go to work. (1.-cedwa, 2.-cede, 3.-cesya, 4.-ceda, 5.-cedalyo, 6.-cesya, 7.-caaca.)
remain behind, Kocaala musankwa, tulakujana awa. = Remain behind young man, we will find you here. (2.-ceede, 3.-caalizya, 4.-caalila, 5.-caalilalyo, 6.-caalisya, 7.-caala-caala, 8.-caazyanya.)
become last, rt. -caala, Webo weelede kucaalizya nkaambo nduwe mmusyoonto. = You should come last because you are the youngest. (1. -caalizyigwa, 2.-caalizyide, 3.-caalizya, 8. -caalizyanya.)
remain with, rt. -caala, Okuno ndacaazya makkwacca osanwe. = Here I remain with five kwacha. (2. -caazyide.)
remain with one another, rt. -caala, Tumane twacaazyanya kulangana limwi twatalika kulila. = When we were finished we remained with each other looking at one another until we began to cry.

sizzle, Nyama yamafwuta ilacacama mucibiya. = The fatty meat is sizzling in the pot. Cacacama cisyu cili acikko. The relish which is on the fire is sizzling. (2.-cacamide, 3.-cacamya, 4.-cacamina, 6.-cacamisya.)
  • shake with emotion, Musankwa ooyu ulacacama kapati kuti wanyema, taswiilili muntu pe. This man becomes very worked up when he is angry, he does not listen to anyone at all. Bakamvwa babwa nkobacacama kukuwa anze. = They heard the dogs how they were in a frenzy barking outside.
rattle, shake, Kayuwa kangu kalacakama kabotu. My rattle is rattling well. (2.-cakamide, 3.-cakamya, 4.-cakamina, 6.-cakamisya.)

spit between teeth, Inzoka ilacanca mate mumeso aabantu. = The snake sprays spittle on people's eyes. (1.-cancwa, 2.-cancide, 3. -cancizya, 4.-cancila, 6.-cancisya, 8. -cancana. Also: -swa.
  • have breakfast, (idiom) Ijilo ndakoona anzala, ndilayanda kucanca mate. = Yesterday I slept without eating, I would like to have breakfast. (recharge my spittle)
avoid, abstain from, Nchimunya, kocancamvwa kuyanda basimbi, kuli malwazi. = Nchimunya, avoid loving girls, there are diseases. Also: -yozya.

beat with a flexible stick, Ncibi kucancaula mwana akaluso. = It is bad to beat a child with a flexible stick. Also: -cwankaula, -sansaula. (1.-cancaulwa, 2.-cancaulide, 3.-cancauzya, 4.-cancawida, 6.-cancaulisya, 8.-cancaulana.)

adapt, change, Ucizumina muzicelo zyamuminzi, alimwi nkooku akucangamuka tonacangamuka. = You still believe in the medicines of the villages, again as regards making adaptation you have not yet adapted.

grill meat or fish on fire, toast bread, Kamuzicanjika nswi amasizi aamulilo kutegwa zifwambaane kubizwa. = Grill the fish on the embers of the fire so that it quickly becomes cooked. (1.-canjikwa, 2.-canjikide, 3. -canjikila)
act or do politely or slowly, Nabwiinga ulacankaila kulya nokuba kuti ulaa nzala. The bride eats slowly even when she is hungry. Also: -lelema

esaula, -emaika, -emeeka.
  • walk majestically, Bamwi bavwubi bacankaila buya kweenda. Some rich people walk majestically. Also: -jankaila
eat slowly, Kabwa kaniini kaile kucankwinya kulya. = The little puppy is just slowly eating. Also: -cankaila, -nozya-nozya.

find out the medicines the witch is using, Bamucape balayandisya kucapa balozi. = The diviners like to find out what medicines the witches are using. Ooyu muŋanga ulicizi kucapa. = This witch-doctor knows how to divine. (1.-capwa, 2.-capide, 3.-capya, 4.-capila, 5.-capilalyo, 6.-capisya, 7.-capa-cара, 8.-capana.)
  • despise, Kapapa ulayandisya kucapa beenzinyina. Kapapa likes to despise his companions. Also: -sampaula
  • wash clothes, Tuyakucapa zisani juunza. We will wash the clothes tomorrow. Also: -sanzya.

walk as one recovering from illness, Kaluma wakalicisidwe kapati, aano mazuba ulasola kucataila kweenda. = Kaluma was very sick, but nowadays he tries to walk as he recovers. Also: -cotaila, -condaila. (4.-catailila.)
steep, Kofwambaana kuzicavwamika zisani, wamana uziyanike. = Quickly steep the clothes, when finished hang them out to dry. Also: -cawamika. (1.-cavwamikwa, 2.-cavwamikide)

wade in water, Musune mucembele waalilwa kucavwaila mu-тееnda. = The old ox is unable to wade in the water. Cheelo cakamwaalila kuyamba mumeenda jilo, wakali kwiile kucavwaila. = Cheelo was unable to swim yesterday, he was just wading. (2.-cavwailide, 4.-cavwailila.)
soak in liquid, Kocavwika zisani mumeenda akasaala. = Soak the clothes in warm water. (1.-cavwikwa, 2.-cavwikide, 4.-cavwikila.) Also: -nyika, -ccavwika
steep, soak quickly and withdraw at once, Cawamika cisani eeci mumeenda asalala. = Steep this cloth in clean water. Also: -cavwamika (1.-cawamikwa, 2.-cawamikide.)
steep, Baama bacawika zisani zibali kusanzya. Mother is steeping the clothes which she was washing. (1.-cawikwa, 2.-cawikide, 4.-cavwikila, 8.-cawikilana.) Also: -cawamika

steep, Kocawila kabotu mumeenda ulazikonga nswi. = Wash the clothes carefully in the water you will scare the fish away. (1.-cawilwa, 2.-cawilide, 4.-cawilila.)
  • wade in water Also: -cavwaila
cause to drive, Mweelede kubeleka kakwiina akapitawu kumuccaccizya. = You ought to work without a foreman to drive you. Also: -binga

drive yoked oxen, Kofwambaana kuccaila basune kutegwa bulimo bumane. = Be quick in driving the oxen so that the plot is finished. (1.-ccailwa, 2.-ccailide, 3.-ccaizya, 4.-ccailila, 6.-ccailisya, 8.-ccaililana.)
drive oxen for, Kondiccailila basune aaba beendesye. = Drive these oxen for me so that they move fast.
become active, Musankwa wakasima akuccampuka kubuumi buyumu. = The boy became mature and was active in a hard life. (2.-ccampukide, 4.-ccampukila.)
become sharp or mature in mind, Ooyu mwana wakaccangamuka. This child has become sharp in mind.

be worked up, Ibantu banji mbubakakatede kale kuswiilila twaambo twiindene-indene, aka kaambo kakabaccangamuna. Many people as they were already tired listening to the differnt cases, this case really worked them up.
steep, Koccavwika zisani mumeenda akasaala. = Steep the clothes in warm water. Also: -njavwika (1.-ccavwikwa, 2.-ccavwikide.)

drink quickly, Musankwa wakagusya tupepa alimwi tobile twa-kaccasu, kamwi wamupa musimbi, kamwi wakakaccaya musankwa cakufwambaana. The boy took out two packets of kaccasu alchohol, one he gave to the girl the other he drank quickly. (1.-ccayigwa, 2.-ccayide, 3.-ccaizya, 4.-ccayila.)
become effective, Cizimba cabo sunu caimpya, cabbuluka, tiicaccekula. = Their magic power has missed its target, it has lost its power, it has become ineffective.

delay, cause to be late, Bamuccelesya kuya kucikolo mbacembele. = It is the old woman who caused him to be late going to school. Also: -musya (rt. -muka), -munsya, -vwolopezya. (1.-ccelesyegwa, 2.-cceledwe, 4.-ccelesyela, 5.-ccelesyelalyo, 6.-ccelesyanya.)
be late, Ndaccelwa kucikolo sunu. = I was late for school today. (1.-ccelwa, 2.-cceledwe, 3.-ccelezya, 4.-ccelelwa, 5.-ccelelalyo, 6.-ccelesya, 7.-ccelwa-ccelwa.) Also: -muka.

crackle, hiss, Cisasa wakandicceemena nindakamulyata. = The puff-adder hissed at me when I trod on it. Ndalyata kamucceemena. Mmakweelele. (a riddle) = I have stepped on it, it hisses. It is dried maize leaves. (2.-ccemene.) Also: -cceemuna, - fwoomena.
crackle, hiss, Mitabi ilacceemuna mumulilo. are hissing in the fire. The branches (2.-cceemwide, 3.-cceemuzya, 4.-cceemunina)

hiss at, Ndayoowa naandicceemwida cisasa. I was afraid when the puff-adder hissed at me. Also: -cceemena *ccija run away from, Ino muccija nzi nywebo? = From what are you running away? Also: -tija. (1.-ccijigwa, 2.-ccijide, 3.-ccijisya, 4.-ccijila, 8.-ccijana)

run, go in a group, Bana balaccijaana kuya kucikolo. = The children are running to school. Also: -tijaana, -lunduka, -balika. (1.-ccijaanwa, 2.-ccijaanide, 3.-ccijaanya, 4.-ccijaanina, 4.-ccijaaninalyo.)
run away from one another, Basincinko balaccijana. = Mad people run away from each other. Also: - tijana. (2.-ccijanide, 3.-ccijisya, 4.-ccijaanina, 5.-ccijaaninalyo.)
run away with great speed, Kamuccijisya buya kutegwa batamweenzyi babwa basondokede. = Run fast so that the rabid dogs don't catch up with you. Also: -tijisya.
help someone to flee, Ndakali kuccijizya mwana musimbi.ngobakali kuyanda kuuma. = I was helping the young girl to flee from those who wanted to beat her.

follow, tuya kusika nkotuya. will reach where we are going. (1.-ccililwa, 2.-ccilide, 3.-ccilizya, 4.-ccililila, 5.-ccilililalyo, 6.-ccililisya, 7.-ccilila-ccilila, 8.-ccililana.) Also: -tijizya. Kamundiccilila buyo, Just follow me, we

follow along after, Bakaccilizya matende abulowa bwakali kusweka kuzwa kumusune munzila kuzwa kwa Chibbwalu. = They followed out the hoof-prints and the blood which was dropping from the ox along the path coming from Chibbwalu's village.

iron, Kamuccisa zisani eezi kutegwa zibote. = Iron these clothes so that they look nice. (1.-cciswa, 2.-cciside, 3.-ccisya,/-ccisizya, 4.-ccisila, 5.-ccisilalyo, 6.-ccisisya, 7.-ccisa-ccisa, 8.-ccisilana.)
  • brand, *Kamuccisa* ŋombe zyanu ansimbi kutegwa zyaando kazilibonya. = Mark your cattle with a branding iron so that the brand-marks can be clearly seen. Also: -umpa.
  • dance with all one's might, *Kuti baccisa baccisisya inga kulunda kasuko.* = If they dance with all their might they kick up the dust.
go away from home for an indefinite time, Bantu aaba bakaakuccona. = These people disappeared for a long time from home. (2.-cconede, 3.-cconezya, 4.-cconena, 5.-cconenalyo, 6.-cconesya)
peddle, Mutinta ulayiisya kuccovwa ncinga. = Mutinta teaches to ride a bicycle. (1.-ccovwegwa, 2.-ccovwede, 3.-ccovwezya, 4. -ccovwela, 6.-ccovwesya, 8.-ccovwana)

pass along, Tuzikwaambaula akale mazuba mbwaayabuccovwana mbotweelede kuzyeenzya zintu. = We will talk later on as the days pass as to how we should direct affairs. (1.-ccovwegwa, 2.-ccovwede, 3.-ccovwezya, 4.-ccovwela, 6.-ccovwesya, 8.-ccovwana.)
  • peddle in turns, Basankwa bali kuccovwana ancinga. = The boys were peddling in turns on the bicycle.
pass, as time, Eeci ciindi alo mazuba akaliccovene kale kuzwa lyakafwa batumbu bakwe. = At that time the days were passing by since his wife died.

preach, Bakali kuccumaila ijilo bakaamba kabotu. = The one who was preaching yesterday spoke well. Also: -kambauka. (1.-ccumailwa, 2.-ccumailide, 3.-ccumaizya, 4.-ccumailila, 6.-ccumailisya, 8.-ccumailana.)
  • give advice, Ooyu musankwa natamvwi, ijilo wakaccumaililwa. = However heedless this boy is, he was lectured yesterday.
run quickly, Musimbi wakaccwelemuka kuya kunselelo. = The girl ran quickly in descending. Also: -lunduka. (2.-ccwelemukide, 4.-ccwelemukila.)

turn around to look at, *Kamuceba kuno mubone ncecita.* = Turn round here and look at what I am doing (1.-cebwa, 2.-cebede, 3.-cebya, 4.-cebela, 5.-cebelalyo, 6.-cebesya, 7.-ceba-ceba, 8.-cebana.)
  • look back, *Ncibotu kuceba munsi kotanaya kumbele muli ncocita.* = It is good to reflect on the past before you proceed in what you are doing.
  • turn to help, *Kamubaceba bamukabafwu mukuyiisya bana.* = Help the widows in educating the children.

glance sideways, look around constantly, Bakali kwiile kucebauka kuyoowa kubonwa. = They were looking around fearing that they would be seen. (1.-cebaukwa, 2.-cebaukide, 3.-cebausya, 4.-cebaukila, 5.-cebaukisya, 8.-cebaukana.)
take a look at, *Kamucebuka, mubone cicitika.* = Take a look, see what is happening. (2.-cebukide, 8.-cebukana)
look around continually, *Ani ucebuuka kuti ubone ni?* = Whom do you hope to see by looking around continually? (2.-cebuukide, 8.-cebuukana.) Also: -cebauka.

be in anguish or distress, Mwana ncacecebbana kumeso nkaambo bamujosya banyina naatiibaccilile. = The reason why the child has a distressed face is because the mother made him go back when he was about to follow her. (2.-cecebbene, 3.-cecebbanya, 4.-cecebbanina) Also: -cecembana, -kolobbana.

be ready and prepared to do something, Twakaunka ooko kwakali muswaangano akujana nobaceceeka ku *talika.* = We went there where the meeting was and found that they were prepared to start. (1.-ceceekwa, 2.-ceceekede.)
be in anguish, Mukaintu utumbuka ulacecembana nkocicisa. = The woman who is giving birth is in anguish where it pains. (2.-cecembene, 3.-cecembeka, 4.-cecembanina.)

gnaw, nibble at, Kabeba kalacecetula kulya nyama. The mouse is gnawing the meat. Basikoswe bakakkala munanda kabacecetula mbuto. = The rats lived in the house nibbling at the seeds. (1.-cecetulwa, 2.-cecetwide, 3.-cecetwida, 8.-cecetulana.)
dawn for, rt. *-ca,* Bwamuceda munzila kaenda kuya ku Lusaka. = Dawn broke for him on the way as he was going to Lusaka. (1.-cedwa, 2.-cede, 4.-cedela)

has dawned, rt. *-ca,* Bwacede kale naasika. = It had already dawned when he arrived. (1.-cedwa, 2.-cede, 3.-cedya, 4.-cedela.)
  • be caught in trap, rt. *-ca,* Musankwa wacede kakololo ino bamubba. = The boy trapped a hartebeeste now thye have stolen it from him.
be late, rt. -ceelwa, Wacedwa kusika kuno. = She was late in arriving here. Also: -ccelwa, -muka.

remain, rt. -caala, Kwakaliceede mazuba masyoonto buyo kuti zikolo zijalwe. There remained only a few days for the schools to close. Nangoma wakaceede buyo ciindi cisyoonto kuti avwundikwe. Only a short time remained before Nangoma would be initiated.
close slightly, Koceeka cijazyo, kwanjila muzyansende munanda. = Close the door slightly, the humid wind is entering the house. Also: -ceyeka.
be partly closed leaving it ajar, Kwaceekwa kumulyango. = The door has been left ajar.

be insufficient for, rt. -ceya Mwandiceela bana, nsyekonzyi kulwana andinywe. = You are too young for me, children, I cannot fight with you. Andiceela mali, ncindataunka ku Lusaka. = The money was insufficient for me, that is why I did not go to Lusaka. Kwabula nkonditijila, nyika yandiceela. = There is nowhere I can flee to, the earth is too small for me. Ciindi cakatuceela. = The time was insufficient for us. (2. -ceede.)
creak, squeak, Naakali kweenda mabbusu aakwe akali kuceema. = When he was walking his shoes were squeaking. Also: -cwema. (2.-ceemede, 3.-ceemezya)
lessen, diminish, rt. -ceya, Ooyu mwana waceesya, takonzyi kuunka ku Lusaka alikke. This child is too small, she cannot go to Lusaka alone.
be caught, rt. -ca, Wacegwa mukooye kwale. = A partridge was caught in a snare. (2.-cegede, 3.-cezya)
saw, Kamuceka-ceka acipeni. Saw with a knife. Sulwe wakalipa cipanga akuliceka-ceka, mpoona wakazaya. The hare took a knife and sawed himself up, thereupon he died. Also: -tenda.

decorate, make a design on, e.g Taata naakamana kufwala cuuno, wakacicekaula kutegwa cibote. = When my father had finished carving a stool, he decorated it so that it would be beautiful. Also: -zekaula, -nyekaula, -nyenyembas, -zeleemba. (1.-cekaulwa, 2.-cekawide, 3.-cekauzya, 4.-cekaulila, 8.-cekaulana.)
  • make incisions, tattoe, Kamumucekaula nsimbo mulwazi apone. = Make incisions so that the patient gets well.
be decorated, Cisani cako cilicekawidwe kabotu. = Your dress is beautifully decorated.

twitter or chirp, as a bird, Wakabamvwa kale bamintengwe abuyuni boonse mbobacekwezyana kusekelela zuba lyaboola kubucedo. = He already heard the swifts and all the flocks of birds chirping, rejoicing as the sun came up at dawn.

collect fruit or vegetables, Kamucela cisyu mumbewu mujike. = Gather relish from the garden so that you cook. (1.-celwa, 2.-celede, 3.-cezya, 4.-celela, 5.-celelalyo, 6. -celesya, 7.-cela-cela, 8.-celelana.)
  • graze, Kucela koonse musune oyu tanaakali kusakana. = This ox did not wander far away in grazing.
  • weaken further, Waakumujana buti mulwazi mucibbadela? Ma! Cilacela, talangilwi kupona. = How did you find the patient at the hospital? He is weakening further. He is not expected to recover.

strain, as salt from ashes, Kamuceleka musika tubikke mucinkomba. = Strain off the ashes to make soda so that we cook okra. (1.-celekwa, 2.-celekede, 3.-celesya, 4.-celekela, 6.-celekesya, 8.-celekanina.
  • Strain as through a sieve, -sefwa.

share tobacco, Suntwe a Syaanasulwe bakapangana bulongwe nibakamana kucelekana tombwe. = The hyena and the hare made a bond of friendship after sharing tobacco with one another. Also: -fwezyanya tombwe. (1.-celekanwa, 2.-celekanide, 3.-celekanizya, 4.-celekanina)
strain off, rt. -celeka, Mukaintu wakali kucelekezya musika wamuteezi. = The woman was straining off soda liquid from ashes.
answer in an angry tone, Mwana wakacelemuka naakaitwa ku beleka mumbewu. = The child answered in an angry tone when asked to work in the garden. Also: syoleka.

become red, as eyes, Mudaala ooyu Choonya mbwaakabonena buyo basilumamba a bamasilikani kwiima amulyango, wakaapwatula meso akwe aakacelengene kusalala mbuli kuti wabona zyeelo. = This old man, Choonya, as soon as he saw the soldiers and police standing at the entrance, he opened his eyes widely which were red as if he had seen ghosts.
