delay, Candicelesya kusika kumuswaangano nkumuka kujika cakulya. = What delayed me arriving at the meeting was been late to cook. (1.-celesyegwa, 2.-celesyede, 3.-celesya, 4.-celesyela, 8.-celesyanya.)
be delayed Bamakaintu bakacelezeka mumilimo yabo yoonse. = The women were delayed in all their works. (1.-celesyegwa, 2.-celezede, 3.-celesya, 4.-celesyela, 8.-celezekana.)
leave something behind, Syaala mwanaa kwale mukooze, bakucelezya basongo. = The young partridge is left in the snare, it is the clever ones who have left it there.
be delayed, Ndali kuyanda kufwambaana kusika kumunzi, pesi musilisi wandicelezyeka. = I wanted to reach home quickly, but I was delayed by the doctor. Also: -celezeka, -celesya.
flare up, as in temper, Moyo wangu wakaceluka naakanditukila mwana. = My heart flared up when the child insulted me. (1.-celukwa, 2.-celukide, 3.-celusya, 6.-celukisya, 8.-celukana.)
rouse anger, rt. -celuka, Cicelusya moyo nkutukilwa kumwana muniini. = What makes the heart flare up is being insulted by a child. Also: -nyemya.
screech, Mwana wakacema nibakali kuyanda kumuuma badaala. = The child screeched when the old man wanted to beat it.
grow old, Ooyu muka-intu wacembaala. = This woman has grown old. (2.-cembeede, 3.-cembaazya, 4.-cembalila, 5.-cembalilayo, 6.-cembaalisya.)
be old, rt. -cembaala, Kwategwa wakalicembede cakuti wakali kweenzya kafwunko. = It was said that she was so old that she was walking with a stick. Also: -cembeede

look in an indirect way, Banabwiinga bakali kwiide kucembula kulanga mali bantu ngubakali kubabikkila. = The newly weds were looking out of the corner of their eyes at the money which the people were contributing. Kulanga kwakali kucembulwa buyo mbuli kuti kuli uulindila mweenzu. = His look was like a sideways glance like one awaiting a visitor. (2.-cembwide, 3.-cembuzya, 4.-cembwida, 8.-cembwidana.)

joke, Mwaasyoma makani aamba musilisi, mebo ndali kuti ucena buyo. = So you believe what the doctor says, I myself thought he was just joking. (1.-cenwa, 2.-cenede, 3.-cenezya, 4.-cenena, 6.-cenesya) Also: -sobana.

moving towards, Musankwa wakali kuzyana kumwi ucenceleka musimbi mbuli bamoomu. = The boy was dancing while moving close to the girl. Mbwaakaamba obo Naceta ciindi eeco, kacenceleka kunjila mubbaasi. = That is how Naceta spoke at that time when she was moving to get into the bus. (1.-cencelekwa, 2.-cencelekede, 3.-cencelesya, 4.-cencelekela, 6.-cencelekesya, 8.-cencelekana.) + stagger Also: -tenteleka, -jajalika.

stand motionless in awe, Bamacembele bakaile kucencemana nibakamvwa kuti mudaala walisina. = The old women just stood still when they heard that the old man had committed suicide. Mainza wakaide kucencemana mbuli muntu wajatwa bulale. = Mainza remained paralyzed like a man caught in adultery. Also: -gambwa, -nyandwa, kankamana, -ankamana. (2.-cencemanide, 3.-cencemesya, 4.-cencemanina, 6.-cencemanizya.)

cheat, deceive, Musankwa ulya wakacenga basimbi banji. = That boy cheated many girls. (1.-cengwa, 2.-cengede, 3.-cengezya, 4.-cengela, 5.-cengelalyo, 6.-cengesya, 7.-cenga-cenga, 8.-cengana.) Also: . -unina, -bejela, -guba.

not to be upright, be in unstable equilibrium, Eeyi nongo tai-kkali kabotu, ilacengama. = This earthen pot is not sitting upright, it is leaning to one side. (1.-cengamikwa, 2.-cengeme, 3.-cengamisya, 4.-cengamina, 5.-cengaminalyo, 6.-cengaminisya.) cf. -cenemana, -pesyama, -sendama. + be already declined, as the sun, Tatukasiki kabotu nkotuya nkaambo izuba lyacengama kale. = We will not easily reach where we are going because the sun has already gone down. Also: -leyama.

slant sideways, Nongo yabukoko baicengamika bana, ncobwatika bukoko. = The children pushed the pot of beer tilting it sideways, that is why the beer spilt. Also: -sendeka, -zendamika. (1.-cengamikwa, 2.-cengamikide, 3.-cengamisya, 4.-cengamikila, 6.-cengamikisya, 8. -cengamikana.)

pretend, hide the truth, deceive, Sulwe wakalicengeezya ku-ciswa nobakamujata kubba. = The hare pretended to be sick when they caught him stealing. Ooyu musilisi mulimo wakwe wakaluuzyi kutacengeezya. = This doctor truly knew his job without deceiving. Cilamugwasya nzi kuti kamulicengeezya kubona pesi kakuli muli boofu? = What use is it if you pretend that you can see while you are blind. Also: -cenjeezya. (1.-cengeezyegwa, 2.-cengeezyezye, 4.-cengeezyezya, 8.-cengeezyanya.)

turn around, Kamucenguluka nyoonse mulange kumbo. = All of you turn around so that you look to the west. Also: -nyenguluka, -zyuuluka. (1.-cengulukwa, 2.-cengulukide, 3.-cenguluzya, 4.-cengulukila, 6.-cengulukisya, 8.-cengulukana.)
turn around towards, rt. cenguluka, Wakamucengulukila kuti amvwe ncaakali kwaamba. = He turned around towards her to hear what she was saying.

turn someone around, Kamumucengulula mulwazi alange kumbo. = Turn the patient around to face the west. Kamucengulula nongo yameenda kutegwa ikkale kabotu. = Turn the pot of water around so that it sits well. (1.-cengululwa, 2.-cengulwide, 3.-cengulusya, 4.-cengululila, 6.-cengululisya, 8.-cengululana.)

take care, Kamucenjela babwa batamulumi ooko. = Mind the dogs so that they don't bite you over there. (1.-cenjelwa, 2.-cenjede, 3.-cenjezya, 4.-cenjelela, 5.-cenjelelalyo, 6.-cenjelesya, 7.-cenjela-cenjela, 8.-cenjelelana.)

pretend, Wakalicenjeezya kuciswa kutegwa atabeleki. = He pretended to be sick so that he would not have to work. Also: -cengeezya. (1.-cengeezyegwa, 2.-cenjeezyede, 3.-cenjeezyesya, 4.-cengeezyezya 8.-cengeezyanya.)

caution, warn, Twakabacenjezya bubi bwasyuumbwa. = We warned them of the danger of the lion. Also: -bula maanu, -syangila. (1.-cenjezyegwa, 2.-cenjezyede, 4.-cenjezyezya, 6.-cenjezyesya, 8.-cenjezyanya.)

admire, Aba basimbi bamuka kucikolo akaambo kakulicenka mucimboni-mboni. = These girls are late for school because they were admiring themselves in a mirror. Chilyabanyama wakali kulombozya akucenka mootokala wamweenzinyina. = Chilyabanyama was looking with approval and admiring the motorcar of his friend. Also: -eba (1.-cenkwa, 2.-cenkede, 3.-cenkezya, 4.-cenkela, 6.-cenkesya, 8.-cenkana)

be astonished, Ciwena wakali kuuma kankobela naakadunuka kumunzi. Bantu bamumunzi bakacenkama, cenkaa! = The crocodile was playing a hand-piano when he appeared at the village. The villagers were astonished. cf.-cencemana. (1.-cenkamwa, 2.-cenkene.)

face one another, Basankwa aba bakaima anze aopesi lyabayi bapati kabacenkana abee mbakombwe bakatala kulwana. = These boys stood outside the office of the head teacher facing one an other like cocks tired of fighting. (1.-cenkanwa, 2.-cenkeme.)
  • admire one another, Twakali kwiile kucenkana akutembaulana amwinangu. Me and my wife were just admiring and praising one another.
be admired, rt. -cenka, Mwanaakwe wakali kuyandwa kapati, lyoonse wakali kwiide kucenkwa akulangwa naseka-seka. Her child was greatly loved, it was always admired and looked at when it smiled. =

arouse to action, cause to act, Naakandifwubaazya mwana, ndakamuuma nkaambo wakacesa moyo. When the child made a fool of me, I beat him because he aroused my heart. (1.-ceswa, 2.-cesede, 3.-cesezya, 4.-cesela, 6.-cesesya, 8.-cesezyanya.)
  • cut, e.g Bamakaintu bacesa bwizu mumusena. = The women are cutting the grass in the vlei. Also: -jwa bwizu.

cause to lessen, rt. -cesya, Ooyu mudaala wakajisi bazyukulu banji, pesi eeci tiicakali kukonzya kumucesezya mapenzi akwe. = This old man had many grandchildren, but this could not lessen his problems.

anger, annoy, rt. -cesa, Busiikka bucesuzya myoyo yabaabo babulya. = Busiikka fruit causes the heart to be easily irritated by those who eat it. Makani aaya akali kucesuzya moyo wamukaintu wakwe. = This news irritated his wife. (1.-cesuzyigwa, 2.-cesuzyizye, 3.-cesuzya, 4.-cesuzyizya, 6.-cesuzyisya, 8.-cesuzyanya.)
  • cut with, rt. -cesa, Isikela ndelicesuzya bwizu. = The sickle is for cutting the grass with.

lessen, rt. -ceya, Kamucesya meenda mumupika wansima. = Take off some of the water from the pot of nsima.
  • cause to dawn, rt. -ca, Wabucesya (morning greeting) = It has dawned for you. Ngoma yabucesya ilalila. = The drum has been sounding until dawn. Boonse bakamubona baali kuyeeya kuti takwe kubucesya pe. = All who saw him did not think that he would still be alive at dawn. (1.-cesyegwa, 2.-cesyede, 8.-cesyansya.)

become poor, Ooyu muntu wakali muvwubi pesi sunu wakacetaala. = This person has been rich all along, but nowadays he has become poor. (1-cetaalwa, 2.-cetaalide, 3.-cetaazya, 4.-cetaalila, 6.-cetaalisya, 8.-cetaazyanya.)

make poor, rt. -cetaala, Bana balacetaazika nobayanda mali aakucikolo. = Children make one poor when they want money for school. (1.-cetaazikwa, 2.-ceteede, 3.-cetaazika, 4.-cetaazikila, 6.cetaazikisya, V - 84 8.-cetaazikana.) Also: -cetaazya.
make poor, Butolo bulacetaazya. = Laziness brings poverty. cf. -cetaazika. (1.-cetaazyigwa, 2.-cetaazyide, 4.-cetaazyizya, 6.-cetaazyisya, 8.-cetaazyanya)

be scarce, be few, insufficient, Bantu baceya baboola kumuswaangano sunu. = The people are few who have come to the meeting today. (1.-ceyegwa, 2.-ceede, 3.-cesya, 4.-ceyela, 5.-ceyelalyo, 6.-ceesya, 7.-ceya-ceya.)
  • be too narrow, Aawa mulonga waceya nkaambo nkomwe yamulonga ilifwuundene. = The river is narrow here because the banks are close to one another.

leave door ajar, close door a bit, Kamuceyeka cijazyo wavwulisya muwo. = Close the door a bit, the wind is too strong. (1.-ceyekwa, 2.-ceyekede, 3.-ceyekezya, 4.-ceyekela, 8.-ceyekelana) Also: -ceeka.

cause cattle to graze, rt. cela, Mbaani bayakukucezya nombe juunza? = Who are going to bring the cattle out to graze tomorrow? Mweembezi mubotu ulacezya mbelele zyakwe mumweemvwe mubotu. = The good shepherd grazes his sheep on good fresh grass. (1.-cezyegwa, 2.-cezyede, 4.-cezyezya)
  • be delayed, Moonde waakucezya ku Lusaka asunu taningapiluka. = Moonde was delayed at Lusaka and even today has not yet returned. Mwaalumi uutaningatela, uyoocezya muntolongo. = The man who has not paid tax, will be kept in prison.

take to a place to graze, rt. cela, Mweembezi wakali kucezyezya nombe zyakwe musinzo mulamfwu kuzwa kumunzi. = The herd boy made a long journey from the village to take the cattle to a place to graze. (2.-cezyezyede.)

dance happily, Kunkolola kwa Diintingwe bantu bakacibinta kusikila limwi bwakaca tubulu. = During the initiation ceremony at Diintingwe's, the people danced happily until dawn. (1.-cibintwa, 2.-cibintide, 3.-cibintizya, 4.-cibintila, 6. -cibintisya, 8.-cibintilana.)
  • dance as a witch, Mainza wakajanika ulacibinta amulyango wananda ya Simuunza ciindi camasiku. = Mainza was found dancing (as a witch) at Simuunza's door during the night.

be placed crosswise, Zisamu nzibakabikka acaanda campongo zyakaciinkana. = The poles which they placed at the entrance of the goat's hut were placed crosswise. Also: -ingana. (1.-ciinkanwa, 2.-ciinkene, 3.-ciinkanya, 4.-ciinkanina, 6.-ciinkanisya.)
  • be all about, Yaciinkana mvwula. = It is raining all about.
place across, Kamuciinkanya micinjili amulyango waciba canombe. = Put those smaller poles across the entrance of the kraal. (1.-ciinkanizigwa, 2.-ciinkenye, 4.-ciinkanyizyizya, 6.-ciinkanisya)

be placed across as a boundary, rt. -ciinkana, Muunda wa Kaumba ncowakali mufwaafwi nkuti kumalomoneno nkuwakali kujwe kwakali cilundu cipati cakaciinkene. = The reason why the field of Kaumba was small was because of the boundary which was a big hill blocking the eastern side.
cause to make an effort, Bayi bakamucikika mwana kuti akabone banyina. = The teacher persuaded the child to see her mother. (8.-cikikana.)

wait to eat together with, Bana bakalaigwa kuti kabacila antoomwe. = The children were advised to wait so that they could eat together.
  • look forward to having a wife, Naakakubuka, wakacila musimbi. = When he was of age, he looked forward to having a wife.
  • put on weight, Kuswaya bavwubi nkubotu inga waakucila. = To visit the rich is good because one builds up ones weight. Also: -neneya.

discourage, Bakamucilaika jilo naakali kuyanda kuya muIweendo. = They discouraged him yesterday when he wanted to go on a journey. (1.-cilaikwa, 2.-cilaikide, 3.-cilaizya, 4.-cilaikana.) Also: -tyungilila.
  • pack all one's belongings, Naakapola, wakacilaika azintu zyakwe zyoonse. = When he moved his residence, he took all his belongings with him. Also: -kulaika.
strain, as salt from ashes, Kamucilika musika tujike muteezi. = Strain off the ashes for soda so that we can cook okra. (1.-cilikwa, 2.-cilikide, 3.-cilizya.) Also: -celeka.

be hateful to, Uulya muntu ulandicima nkaambo ulabba. That person is hateful to me because he steals. (1.-cimwa, 2.-cimide, 3.-cimya, 4.-cimanina, 6.-cimisya, 7.-cima-cima, 8.-cimana.)
  • be fed up with, become distasteful to, Basicikolo cakabacima kulisya kkabicci mazuba oonse. = The pupils were fed up of eating cabbage every day.
be enemies with, Twakacimana a Mutinta mazuba akainda. = For the past few days Mutinta and myself were enemies.
be hateful to one another, Katucimanwa buyo nkaambo kulubizyanya inga cilaindilila. = Let us just be enemies because mutual trangressions may well increase.

float, Ooyu mwana ulacimbama atalaa meenda citondezya kuti wanyikila. = This child is floating on top of the water showing that she has drowned. Also: -ibauka, -impauka. (2.-cimbamide, 3.-cimbamya, 4.-cimbamina)

divide, partition, Kucimbaula muunda cilakatazya nkaambo aumwi tayandi kunyengelelwa. = Dividing up a field is difficult because neither one wants to have it taken from him. Ncibotu kucimbaula nanda kuti kube mazyuli. = It is good to partition a house so that there are bedrooms. (1.-cimbwaulwa, 2.-cimbawide, 3.-cimbauzya, 4.-cimbawida, 8.- cimbawidana.) Also: -cimbula.

make a division, divide into two parts, Kocimbula muunda kutegwa usyange zisyango zyobilo. = Partition the field so that you can sow two different types of crops. Also: -cimbaula. (1.-cimbulwa, 2.-cimbwide, 3.-cimbuzya, 4.-cimbwida, 8.-cimbwidana.)
divide between one another, rt. cimbula, Katucimbwidana biyo minyinza mumuunda. = Let us mark out, agreeing with one another, the boundaries of the field. (2.-cimbwidene)
be displeased, rt. -cima, Bakacimwa nibakapegwa muunda musyoonto. = They were resentful when they were given a small field. (2.-cimidwe)

change, (ety. Eng.), Sunu zintu zyakacinca. = Today things have changed. (1.-cincwa, 2.-cincide, 3.-cincizya, 4.-cincila, 5.-cincilalyo, 6.-cincisya, 7.-cinca-cinca, 8.-cincana.) Also: -sanduka.
  • exchange, (ety. Eng.), Bantu balayanda kucinca musune a mpwizyi. = People like exchanging an ox for a cow. Also: -sintana.
change at will, Zisani zyakwe musimbi oyu wakali kwiile kucincaanya. = This girl was changing her clothes at will. (1.-cincaanizigwas, -cincaanyide, 3.-cincaanyizya)

change places, swop, Kamucincana, webo uboole waano, oyu aunke kokuya nkoobede. = Change places so that you come here and she goes over there where you were. (1.-cincanwa, 2.-cincanide, 3.-cincanizya, 4.-cincanizyizya)
  • barter, exchange goods, Kamucincana mpongo amapopwe. = Exchange the maize for a goat. Also: -sintana.
stand still, Ino yawe ucincimana nzi mbuli wabona muntu ufwide? = Now why have you stood still as if you have seen a dead person?
cause to roar with laughter, Also: -gagamuna
exchange for, Bunji bwabo bakali kucincizya nombe angoma. = Many of them were exchanging cattle for musical drums. (1.-cincizyigwa, 2.-cincizyide.)
insert, Ino mootokala wa 'Benz' kutakatazya, mbwaakazikukacindwila kapikili wakatalika kulila mootokala. = The Mercedes was not a problem, as soon as he inserted a nail the engine started.

meet, Kamumucinga nkaambo ulasika sunu. = Meet him because he is coming today.
  • protect through treatment with traditional medicines, Bamuka Mutinta balicizyi kucinga bana bavwanda. = The wife of Mutinta knows how to protect infants with traditional medicines. (1.-cingwa, 2.-cingide, 3.-cingizya, 4.-cingila, 5.-cingilalyo, 6.-cingisya, 7.-cinga-cinga, 8. cingana.)

expect to meet someone at a certain place, Ndicingausya mweenzu uzyila ku Mazabuka. = I have come expecting to meet a visitor from Mazabuka. Cilakatazya kucingausya muntu ngotazyi naboola. = It is difficult to meet a person whom you don't know when she arrives. Also: -cingauzya. (1.-cingauzyigwa, 2.-cingausyide, 3.-cingauzya, 4.-cingauzyizya, 8. cingauzyanya.)
expect to meet a person at a certain place, Also: -cingausya.

ward off, *Kocingila* muwo akubikka bwizu. Ward off the wind by putting grass. (1.-cingilwa, 2.-cingilide, 3.-cingilizya, 4.-cingilizyizya, 8.-cingililana.)
  • surround, *Katucingila* mpongo kutegwa zyoonse zinjile mucaanda. Let us surround the goats so that they all enter the shelter. *Kamucingila* mbewu eeyi amamvwa. Surround this garden with thorns.

protect from, as from wind, disease, etc., *Cibalu ncakucingilila* luwo. The screen is for protecting against the wind. Sibbuku Kagele wakalilide misamu yakulicingilila. Headman Kagele had taken traditional medicines to protect himself. Atusole *kucingilila* banyama besu bamusyokwe. Let us protect our wild animals. (1.-cingililwa, 2.-cingilidwe, 3.-cigilizya, 4.-cingilizyizya, 8.-cingililana.)
partly close door, Kamu
citendele kutegwa muwo utanjili canguzu. Close the door partially so that the wind does not enter in a gust. (1.-cinjilwa, 2.-cinjilide, 3.-cinjizya.) cf. -ceeka.
bar the way, block, Kamu
kabwa katanjili mujikilwa. Block the puppy from entering the kitchen. Also: -cingilila, (1.-cinjililwa, 2.-cinjilide, 3.-cinjilizya, 4.-cinjililila, 8.-cinjililana)

dance the *cinande* dance, Basimbi bali *kucinka* kunkolola. The girls were dancing the *cinande* at the initiation ceremony. Nibakali kuzyana *cinande* bakali *kucinka* kabotu When they were dancing the *cinande* they were dancing well to the *cinande* beat. (2.-cinkide, 3.-cinkizya)
  • be sensitive, be diplomatic, *Kocinka* kwaambaula inga koya kwaamba citondwa. Be sensitive when speaking otherwise you might say something which is taboo.
be mad, Chipoowe waka
naakamana kufweba lubanje. Chipoowe went mad when he had smoked dagga. (2.-cinkukide, 3.-cinkusya, 4.-cinkukila, 6.-cinkukisya.) Also: -gauka, -sondoka
be in a mad state, Waakumana kuyeeya, uyakujana nse*cinkukide*. When you have finished thinking, you will find that I am not mad.

snatch, grab, Suntwe uciinda biyo amulyango wakabona moongola wacifwuwa camusana wamunene nkocituba, mpoona *nkucinkwabwida*. A hyena passsing by the doorway saw the spine-bone of the old man glistening, thereupon it snatched him.
overcharge, Akaambo kamulandu wakwe bakamucinsaikila akumuinkawida. Because of his crime, they overcharged and verbally abused him.
cause to meet, rt. -cinga, Ndime ndamucinzya bantu kutegwa bamunyamwide zyoola. I am the one who caused the people to meet him so that they could carry his luggage.

be worn out, *Moota* wakaindi wakacipa. The old car was worn out. (2.-cipide, 3.-cipya, 4.-cipila, 6.-cipisya)
  • be annuled Also: -buluka

demote, Ooyu muntu bakamucipulula kuzwa muopesi lipati kumuleta ansi kuli syoonto. They demoted this person from the main office and brought him to a lower one. (1.-cipululwa, 2.-cipulwide, 3.-cipuluzya, 8.-cipululana.)
  • reduce the price, Waicipulula nombe kutegwa ndicikonzye kuyuula. He reduced the price of the cow he was selling so that I could manage to buy it.
become cheap, Zyacipuluka ncobeni zintu kuno. Things have become cheap here indeed.

experience pain, be sore, Cilacisa akanduuma bayi kucikolo. = The spot is painful where the teacher beat me at school. Moyo wangu wakacisa nindakabbidwa mali. = My heart pained when money was stolen from me. (1.-ciswa, 2.-ciside, 3.-cisya, 4.-cisila, 5.-cisilalyo, 6.-cisisya, 7.-cisa-cisa, 8.-cisana)
cause to suffer, rt. -cisa, Majwi aamulongwaakwe akaindilila kumukopa akumucisizya moyo. The words of her friend disturbed her more and increased the pain in her heart. (1.-cisizyigwa, 4.-cisisyizya)

be sick, Waciswa nzi webo ncoungumana boobu? = What are you suffering from that makes you look so downcast? Musankwa wakaciswa mpandula mutwe. = The boy had a splitting headache. Also: -Iwala. (2.-cisidwe)
cause pain to, injure with, rt. cisa, Ngu Lwando wamucisya mwana naamuunsya. = It is Lwando who made the child sick when she made her fall. (1.-cisizyigwa, 2.-cisyide)
feign illness, Kolicisya-cisya kutegwa batakutizyi basankwa. = Pretend to be ill so that the boys do not take you away.

do, make, Kocita kabotu mulimo wako oyu kutegwa utatandwi. = Do this work of yours properly so that you don't get sacked. Nyota yakatucita mulimo. (idiomatic) = The thirst made work for us. (We worked to find water) (1.-citwa, 2.-citide, 3.-citya, 4.-citila, 5.-citilalyo, 6.-citisya, 7.-cita-cita, 8.-citana.)
happen, rt. -cita, e.g Cakacitika ncibakali kwaamba bantu. = What the people used to say happened. (2.-citikide, 3.-citizya, 4.-citila)
do for someone, rt. cita, Bakamucitila pobwe. They made a feast for him. (1.-citilwa, 2.-citikide, 3.-citizya, 4. -citila, 8.-citilana.

cause to take place, Nchimunya nguwakacicitisya buya, kakunyina uumbi. It was Nchimunya who made this happen, no one else.
  • do more, do with energy, Belita wakacitisya mulimo wakwe nkabela wakasumpulwa. = Belita excelled in doing her work and so she was promoted.
  • make something with, Wakacicitisya anzi cuuno eeci? Ndakacicitisya ambezyo. With what did you make that stool? I made it with an adze. Also: -bambya, -citizya.
pack a boat/canoe, Kamucizya bwato obo. = Pack that boat.

move as if stalking something, Ino uyandaula nzi ooko nkoile kucobaila anga uvwima kayuni? = Now what are you searching for over there where you move as if stalking something like one who hunts a little bird? (2.-cobailide, 3.-cobaizya, 4.-cobailila)
rain heavily, Kacobo-cobo kameenda nomuli kwa Moonze! = How heavily it is raining for you who are in Monze. (2.-cobwede)
rain heavily. Imvwula yakacobola ijilo kumazuba. = The rain fell heavily yesterday evening. Also: -lyobola. (2.-cobolede)

rattle as bangles, Inkaya zyakwe zyakacoca naakali kusanzya zisani. = Her bangles rattled as she washed the clothes. Also: -lizya, -cokola, -ngwelema
  • purge, Ooyu mwana wakali kucoca masiku oonse. This child had diarrhoea all night. Also: -cocomona, -soomona

fidget, move about here and there, Bana bacikolo tabeelede kucocoleka, mwiiyi nayiisya. = Pupils should not fidget, when the teacher is teaching. Mupati wamilimo wakali kwiile kucocoleka kunze aababelesi. = The manager was just moving about here and there behind the workers. Also: -cuculika

sizzle, Impende zilacocoma amulilo. = The bream fishes are sizzling on the fire. Bukoko bulacocoma kabotu. = The beer is fermenting well. Also: -bila, (2.-cocomede, 4.-cocomena)
  • crackle, Intobolo yamudinkilwa ilacocoma niiyanda kudubuka. = The gun packed (with gunpowder) crackles as it is fired. Also: -concoma
  • talk too much, Munene ulaa bunjaka ulacocoma kubbila zuba. = The old man who is full of contention, rambles on until the sun sets.

purge continuously, Kuti mwana wagonkwa kacili muvwanda inga ulacocomona. = When the child is weaned (due to another pregnancy of the mother) when still an infant, it can have continuous diarrhoea. Also: -coca

rattle, Koteelela mayuwa nkwaacokola auma bamakaintu. = Listen to the rattles which the women are shaking. Citima cilacokola nicabikkwa malasa manji. The train makes noise when more coal is added. Also: -coca

rake out fire Koucokoma mulilo kutegwa uzime. = Rake out the fire so that it is extinguished. (1.-cokomwa, 2.-cokomwede, 3.-cokomezya, 4.-cokomwela) cf. -fwukuma, -cunda-cunda, -yokolola.
  • poke as in a burrow Also: -cokonsa, -sokosa
  • be painful, Cilacokoma kuti muntu wafwa. = It is painful if a person dies.

rake out with, hook, rt. cokoma, Mukaintu naakabona kuti kuleleenga buyo milembelela yabuci, wakabweza kasamu akutalika kucokomya cilembelela cabuci kuti ciloke ansi. = When a woman saw the combs of honey hanging down, she took a stick and started to hook a honey-comb so that it would fall down on the ground.

poke, irritate, Kamuleka kucokonsa nzoka iili mubwina nkaambo ilakonzya kumuluma. = Stop poking at the snake in the hole because it can bite you. Kaindi nibakali kujika muzuba, balamwe bakali kucokonsa mulilo kutegwa uzime. = Long ago when they were cooking the dish of muzuba, the in-laws used to poke the fire so that it would go out (refers to a custom connected with marriage by which the man is tested to see if he really wants the woman.) Tanaakali kuyanda kumucenga nkaambo inga camucisa kwiinda mbuli cakali kumucokonsa. = He did not want to deceive her because it would hurt her more than what had been irritating her before. (1.-cokonswa, 2.-cokonsede, 3.-cokonsezya, 4.-cokonsela, 8.-cokonsana) Also: -dyunga-dyunga.
make a rustling noise, as animal in grass, Kuli cicokonya mubwizu aalya. There is a rustling sound coming from the grass over there. (2.-cokonyede) Also: -sokonya, -sokosa, -fwoota.
divine, find out the cause of death or illness, Balombwana bakaunkide kukucokoozya bakali bone. = The boys who went to divine were four. (1.-cokoozyegwa, 2.-cokoozyede, 4.-cokoozyezya) Also: -sonda
insert, Wakaconcela tusyonga toonse mukatobolo kakwe. = He inserted all the bullets into his gun.
come out well, Icisyu ncobajika baama caconcoka. = The relish which my mother has cooked has come out well. (2.-concokede) Also: -nunsuka, -nontoka.
have normal relationships with others, Taakwe nobakali kwaambwiidana akuconcokana. They never talked to each other or were on easy terms with one another.
sizzle, Inyama yamafwuta ilaconcoma mucibiya. = The fatty meat is sizzling in the pot. Also: -cocoma. (2.-concomede, 3.-concomezya, 4.-concomena, 6.-concomesya.)

project, lift up head, as a cobra, Katwe kanzoka kakaconcomana atalaa bwizu. = The snake's head projected above the grass. Musana wamangoye ulaconcomana nalwana amubwa. = The back of a cat arches when it fights a dog. (2.-concomene, 3.-concomeka, 4.concomanina.) Also: -nongomana.
make erect, stand upright, arch, Kokaconcomeka buya kukabikka kantu aaka. Put that thing upright. (1.-concomekwa, 2.-concomekede, 3. -concomekela)

become flat-buttocked, Choombe wakalineneede mwakali, pesi sunu wakacondobala. = Choombe was fat last year but today he is flat-buttocked. (2.-condobalide, 3.-condobezya, 4.-condobalila) Also: -condola, -cotobala, -syelebala.
become flat-buttocked, Munene wakacondola akaambo kakuciswa. The old man became flat-buttocked because of illness. Also: -cotobala, condobala.
pour out a little, Kouconzola umwi mukupa, upe bana. = Pour out some milk so that you give it to the children. (1.-conzolwa) Also: -ungula, -pungula, -punula.

make noise, as rain pouring down, Imvwula ilacooma, katufwam baana kuya kumunzi tukayuse. = The rain is pouring down, let us hurry home to shelter. Imvwula yalikucooma masiku oonse. The rain was pouring down the whole night. (2.-coomede, 3.-coomya, 4.-coomena)
  • be about to boil, Meenda alacooma, ayanda kubila. = The water is warming up, it is about to boil.
purge, have diarrhoea, Mwana wakali kucoomona masiku oonse. = The child was purging all night. (1.-coomonwa, 2.-coomwede, 3.-coomozya, 4.-coomweda.)
cause to purge, Ino musamu nzi wakucoomozya? = What medicine is there for purging?

move with buttocks along the ground, Ooyu mwana ulacota azyila kucimbuzi lyoonse. = This child moves along on its buttocks when it has defecated to clean itself. (1.-cotwa, 2.-cotede, 3.-cotya, 4.-cotela, 8.-cotana.) Also: -cuta.

walk slowly, Twajana muIwazi ulacotaila kweenda naazwa mucibbadela. We found the patient walking slowly when she came out of the hospital. Jolezya wakaunka kuluba uyabucotaila. = Jolezya went to the kraal walking slowly. (2.-cotailide, 3.-cotaizya, 4.-cotailila) Also: -cataila.

become flat-buttocked, Mazubaano bantu banji bakacotobala akaambo kanzala. = Nowadays many people have become flat-buttocked because of the hunger. (2.-cotobede, 3.-cotobezya, 4.-cotobalila) Also: -condobala
be flat-buttocked, Ooyu muntu ulicotobele kumatako. = This one is flat-buttocked.

pedal, Ndalomba ncinga yako, ndiyanda kucovwa. I am asking for your bicycle, I want to ride it. Also: -ccovwa. (1.-covwegwa, 2.-covwede, 3.covwede, 4.-covwela, 6.-covwesya, 8.-covwana.)
  • shuffle cards, (gamble) Ndakajana bantu bacovwa njuka ciindi cakumazuba. = I found people playing cards in the evening.

produce bubbles, Makwa amububa alacovwola mbuli nsipa. = The bark of the mububa tree produces bubbles like soap. (2.-covwolede.)
  • be clogged with mucous, Meso amwana alacovwola. The child's eyes are clogged with mucous. Also: -kovwola.
stir to prodce bubbles, Kamucovwoola meenda kutegwa acovwooke. Stir up the water so that it produces bubbles. (1.-covwoolwa, 2.-covwoolede, 3.-covwoozya, 4.-covweeda.)
rub oneself, as in washing, Mutumbu wakaunka kuya kulicuba kusamba mukazyiba kokwa Kaangulika. = The suckling mother went to wash herself in the pool of Kaangulika. (1.-cubwa, 8.-cubana.)

be scraped, Muntenda yamumugwagwa mukaintu awalo wakacubbauka azisani zyakazapauka. = In the road accident the woman was also scraped and the clothes torn. (2.-cubbaukide, 3.-cubbauzya, 4.-cubbaukila, 8.-cubbaulana.)

scrape, Banyina nibakali kusanzya mwana wakalaa bweele, bakazicubbaula zicisa kutegwa buzwe busina. = When the mother was washing the child who had scabies, she scraped the sores so that the pus would come out. Mukaintu wakacubbauka azisani zyakazapauka. The woman got bruised and her clothes were torn. (1.-cubbaulwa, 2.-cubbaulide, 3.-cubbauzya, 4.-cubbaulila, 6.-cubbaulisya 8.-cubbaulana.)
be skinned, Mwana naawa kuzwa acilayi, wacubbuka ankumo. = When the child fell off the sledge, it was skinned on the forehead. (2.cubbukide, 3.-cubbuzya, 4.-cubbukila.) Also: -yabbuka, -yubbuka.

tear one's skin, Cisamu ncaakali kugonka nicakawa, cakamucubbula amwiindi. When the tree fell which he was cutting, it tore him on the calf of the leg. (1.-cubbulwa, 2.-cubbwide, 3.-cubbuzya, 4.-cubbwida, 8.-cubbulana.) Also: -cubula, -bbabbula.

continue tearing, Walicubbuula naali kulikwezya nkaambo bweele bwali kubaba. He continued to tear himself when he was scratching because the scabies were itching. (1.-cubbuulwa, 2.-cubbuulide, 3.-cubbuzya, 4.-cubbuulila, 8.-cubbuulana.)cubila disturb, pester, annoy, tease, play with, Koleka kucubila zyabantu. = Stop playing with people's belongings. Koleka kucubila nzuki, zilaluma. = Stop disturbing the bees, they sting. (1.-cubilwa, 2.-cubilide, 8.-cubilana.)
tear one's skin, scrape, Bakamucubula nobakali kulwana. = They tore his skin when they were fighting. (1.-cubulwa, 2.-cubulide, 3.-cubuzya, 8.-cubulana.) Also: -cubbula, -cumbulas, -yupula, -kwamuna.

become active, Webo ulacucauka kukkala. You sit in a restless way. Mbwaakatalika kwaamba obu munene kumwi kacucauka acuuno mbuli kuti cakali kupya akaambo kakunyema. = As he began to speak he was moving about in anger on the chair as if it was on fire. Nentacucauki nombe zyangu tazikwe kufwambaana kuvwula, alimwi milimo yangu minji iloona. If I do not do something my cattle will not increase quickly, and then many of my projects will be at a stand-still. Also: -yatauka, -jatauka. (2.-cucaukide, 3.-cucauzya, 4.-cucaukila.)
cause to take action, Oobu bulwazi bwakanswende bwakamu-cucausya cakuti wakafwambaana kuunka kukusilikwa. = This disease of gonorrhoea caused him to do something so that he quickly went to be healed.

make noise with feet, e.g Kuli muntu wali kucuculika ciindi camasiku. = There was someone making noise with the feet at night. Banyina mooye baka-unka oku akooko kabayaabucuculika ku-zyana nkabela kabasamide zisani zi-zapaukide. = The mother of the initiated girl moved here and there while shuffling her feet as she danced while wearing torn clothes. (2.-cuculikide, 3.-cuculisya, 4.-cuculikila.)
move around, shuffle around, Wakaleka kusakana kuma-koko pele buyo kucuculikila munsi-munsi amunzi wakwe. = He stopped going far away for beer gatherings but just moved around near his home.

sound when beer is fermenting, Ansanza yananda, mpiyakali kulubazu-bazu kwakali cibwantu munongo camulalansana icakali kucucuma. = At the south end of the house there was sweet-beer made from the mulalansana root which was bubbling in a clay pot. (2.-cucumide, 3.-cucumya, 4.- cucumina)
drag along, Bakamukwela Mutinta oku kumwi kajisi amwana-akwe bamucucumya kutola kumulonga. = They pulled Mutinta there while she had her baby on her back, dragging her along taking her to the river.
place beside, Ncibi ku-cucutizya maanda munsi amunzi wamwe-enzinyoko. = It is bad to place houses near your friend's home. Also: -jujutizya, -cumbilizya.
rub together, Uleelede ku-cuka zisani kutegwa zisalale. = You ought to rub the clothes together so that they become clean. (1.-cukwa, 2.-cukide, 3.-cukizya, 4.-cukila, 8.-cukana.)
shake, as water in mouth, churn, Kamucuka-cuka mukupa uvwelengane. = Shake the fresh milk to mix it with the sour milk.
churn, Kamwiicukaula nsuwa kusikila usase mukupa. = Shake the gourd until the milk becomes sour. (1.-cukaulwa, 8.-cukaulana.)
be worn out, Twacukuka nkaambo twatalika kaindi kubeleka. = We are worn out because we started to work long ago.

tire one another, Bana Choobe a bana Chipembele bakacukulana nobakali kusobana bbola muzuba. = The teams from Choobe and Chipembele ex-hausted one another when they were playing in the sun. (2.-cukulanide.)
shake, as old eggs, Kocukuma mayi, umvwe naa mmabi. = Shake the eggs to see if they are bad. (3.-cukumya)
slide along, Inzoka iculuba buya kweenda. = A snake slides along as it moves. (2.-culubide, 3.-culubya, 4.-culubila.)
cry sharply, Bala-culubwizya kulila amadilwe. = They cry sharply at the funerals. Also: -ulubwizya, -kwiila, -kwemba.

fall into, slip down into, Naakali kuselemuka akalundu, waka-culukila mucilindi. = When he was going down the hill, he fell into a ditch. (2.-culukide.) Also: -wida, -tyumpukila, -selemukila, -tezemukila, -golokela.
slide, Mwana waka-cululika kuzwa a cuulu naakali kusobana. = The child slipped down from the anthill when it was playing.

cause to accompany Bana koomusimbi nibakaswaangana a-bwii nga, *bakacululisya mwana uucibbalwa kuli banabwiinga.* = When the relatives of the girl met the wedding group, they caused the child who was still being carried on the back to accompany the wedding group.

roll in pain when sick, *Cicisa nicakacisa kapati, mulwazi wakali kuculumba masiku oonse.* = When the illness was paining intensely, the patient was twisting about the whole night. (2.-culumbide, 3.-culumbya, 4.-culumbila.)

rub, polish, rub one's feet against the ground, *Kamulicumba abbwe kutegwa musalale.* = Rub yourself with a stone so that you can be clean. (1.-cumbwa, 2.-cumbide, 3.-cumbya, 4.-cumbila, 5.-cumbilalyo, 6.-cumbisya, 7.-cumba-cumba, 8.-cumbana.) Also: -buwa, -kumba-kumba, kulisansa-muna, kulicuutizya.
  • irritate, *Mumoyo cakali kucumba kapati.* = He was worried in his heart.
scrub, *Kocumba-cumba cigamba cancinga cisalale.* = Scratch the patch of the bicycle tube well so that it is clean.
be rough as skin, *Mabbusu akali mabotu nokuba kuti kumbele akalicumbaukile akaambo kakubula mafwuta.* = The shoes were good even though in front they were rough from lack of polish.
offer, *Ncibotu kucumbikila mweenzu mutiba wamusozya.* = It is good to offer a visitor a plate of musozya. (1.-cumbikilwa, 8.-cumbilikana) Also: -somba.

push a thing towards a person for it to be taken away, *Kamucicumbikizya aceeci kutegwa zisalale antoomwe.* = Push this also over to her with that so that they can be washed together. (2.-cumbikizyide) Also: -sunda
  • force oneself through, *Koleka kulicumbikizya mubantu mbotazyi nkaambo balakubbida mali.* Stop forcing yourself through people whom you do not know because they will steal your money.
bruise, *Mwana naawa wacumbuka amwiindi.* = When the child fell it bruised itself on the calf. (1.-cumbukwa, 2.-cuumbukide, 3.-cumbuzya, 4.-cumbukila.)
bruise oneself against, rt. -cumbuka, *Mutinta wacumbukila mumugwagwa naawa.* = Mutinta bruised herself on the road when she fell. (2.-cumbukide, 3.-cumbuzya)
tear one's skin, *Cisamu camucumbula amwiindi.* = The wood tore his calf. (1.-cumbulwa, 2.-cumbulide, 3.-cumbya, 4.-cumbulila, 8.-cumbulana.) Also: -cubula.
clean with, rt. -cumba, *Wakabweza zintu zyakulicumbya mukanwa.* = She took the things for cleaning her mouth. (2.-cumbuzyide)

dip or push the end of something into something, *Munene naakakolwa, wakawa akucunca mulomo mumusenga.* = When the old man was drunk, he fell pushing his mouth into the sand. (1.-cuncwa, 2.-cuncide, 3.-cuncizya, 6.-cuncisya, 8.-cuncana.)
waddle, *Mutinta wakali kucuncuma kutijaana.* = Mutinta was waddling as she ran. (2.-cuncumide, 3.-cuncumya, 4.-cuncumina.)

take something heavy and move it to another place, *Nokwakabbuka bantu banji, mucembele waka-fwambaana kucuncumya cibiya camyuungu akuya kucisisa munanda.* = When many people appeared the old woman quickly moved the pot of pumpkins and hid it in the house. *Bamadaala balacuncumya nongo zyabukoko ciindi calwiindi.* = The old men carry heavy pots of beer during the Iwiindi ceremony. Also: -dumbya-dumbya, -dumbaizya.

push under, Mutinta, *kocunda-cunda cisisi acikko kutegwa cifwumo tuzikujisye.* = Mutinta, push the piece of burning wood under the ash (to put the fire out) so that we use it to cook tomorrow. (1.-cundwa-cundwa, 2.-cundide-cundide, 3.-cundya-cundya, 4.-cundila-cundila)
  • poke, provoke, Musankwa wali

caali musimbi, ncaamuuma bbwe. = The boy was deliberately pestering the girl, that is why she hit him with a stone. Lwiindi wakanyema nkwaakali *kucundwa-cundwa.* = Lwiindi was made angry when he was provoked. Also: -dyunga-dyunga, -sunda.
trot, Koyaabu

notiifwambaane kusika kuya. = Trot as you go so that you reach there quickly. Syaacaande wakacunka-cunka akubba-tauka munzila. = Syaacaande was trotting and hopping along the way. (2.-cunkide-cunkide) Also: -zeba-zeba, -cunta-cunta.
trot, Koyaabucuntacunta uyakusika kufwambaana. = Trot as you go so that you reach there quickly. Also: -cunka-cunka, -zeba-zeba.
go with short quick strides, *Kucuntila antaamu zifwaafwi-fwaafwi ncibotu kapati nkaambo inga tofwambaani kukatala.* = To go with short quick steps is good because you will not tire quickly.
cadse to push mouth into, rt. cunca, *Wacunzya mulomo ansi naawa, bulowa bwazwa kapati.* = When he fell he pushed his mouth into the ground, much blood flowed out.

move along on buttocks, *Mwana ulacuta amana kwaambuka.* = The child moves along on its buttocks when it has defecated (to clean itself). Ciindi lyakafwa mukaintu wakwe, Jolezya wakacutwa biyo, wakali kuyoowa kusalazigwa munzila yakuswaana amukaintu umbi akaambo kabulwazi bwasikalileke. = When his wife died Jolezya only had an exterior ritual cleansing, he feared to have the traditionally demanded ritual with another woman because of the disease of AIDS. (1.-cutwa, 2.-cutide, 3.-cutya, 4.-cutila, 6.-cutisya.) Also: -cota.
rub against, Kapongo kalalicuusya acisamu. = The goat is rubbing itself against a tree. Also: ku-li-guya (2.-cuusyide, 4.-cuusyila, 8.-cuusyanya.)
be bruised, Cheelo wakacuzuka agondo naakawa. = Cheelo got bruised on the knee when he fell. (2.-cuzukide, 3.-cuzuzya, 4.-cuzukila, 6.-cuzukisya.) Also: -cumbukwa.

bruise, Wakalicuzula nibakali kusobana abananyina. = She bruised herself when she was playing with her mates. Munyati nguuya, waakwiide kucuzula cisamu. = The buffalo, there he goes, he just bruised the tree. Also: -gululunta, -bambuula. (1.-cuzulwa, 2.-cuzulide, 3.-cuzuzya 4.-cuzukila, 8.-cuzulana.)
beat with a cane Also: -cancaula.

strike with a little stick, beat with cane to correct, Bamu*cwankaula mwana naalubizya.* = They caned the child when it made a mistake. (1.-cwankaulwa, 2.-cwankaulide, 3.-cwankauzya, 4.cwankaulila 6.-cwankaulisya, 8.-cwankaulana.) Also: -cancaula, -sansaula.
scream, Musimbi waka*cwema kulila naakabona nzoka.* = The girl screamed when she saw a snake. (2.-cwemede, -cwemya, -cwemela) Also: -cwemba, -kwemba, -kwiila.
squeal, Kangulube kacwemba nibakaluma babwa. = The piglet squealed when the dogs bit it. (2.-cwembede, 3.-cwembya, 4.-cwembela, 6.-cwembesya.) Also: -cwema.
fill with chirping, Bamintengwe bakali kwiile kucwencwezya zisaka zyoonse. = The swallows were just filling the woods with their chirping.

scream together, Bana balacwiizyanya munanda nobayoowa syaamankwamu. = The children scream together in the house when they fear the masked dancer. Ngulube zilacwiizyanya mucaanda. = The pigs are squealing together in the pig-sty. (3.-cwiizya, 4.-cwiizyila.)
sniffle, Nibakamuuma banyina, wakacwinta kulila. = When her mother beat her, she sniffled. (2.-cwintide, 3.-cwintya, 4.-cwintila.)
stand firm, Ulajana basankwa bazisama ngoma mucibuno, bamana aumwi wadaabala kwiima. = You find the boys wearing drums on the waist and after that standing firmly. Also: -daamana

Tuladaalika, kujujuka biyo zisani. = We are in good health, it is only the clothes which are wearing out. Baide kudaalika, kwaceya biyo nanda. = The are just in good health, only lacking a house. (4.-daalikila.)

stand firm as you pull, Musankwa wakadaamana kukwela musune ngwaakali kutambisya. = The boy was firmly pulling the ox which he was training. (2.-daamene, 3.-daamika, 4.-daamanina, 6.-daamanisya.)
  • become dilated or swollen, Kuulu kwangu kwatalika kudaamana. = My leg has begun to swell. Also: -ndaamana
  • show disrespect to elders, Ncibi kudaamana kumpela amwami. = It is bad to show disrespect (by standing instead of kneeling) before the chief.

be in swollen state, Ida lyakwe lilidaamene akaambo kakuzimbilwa. = His stomach is swollen from overeating.
  • show disrespect (by standing instead oof kneeling) to the elders, Ooyu mwana unyina mulemyo, ulajana waboola kwaamba kaambo ulaamba kumwi ulidaamene. = This child has no respect, when she comes to report something she says it while standing.
  • stand firm, Wakalidaamene naakali kukwela ngulube. = He stood firmly as he pulled the pig.

pull with strength, stand firm when pulling, Basune nobakwela cilema, inga baladaanyana. = When the oxen are pulling something heavy, they pull with strength. Basankwa bakadaanyana nibakali kukwelana. = The boys stood firm when they were pulling one another. (2.-daanyene, 3.-daanyika, 4.-daanyanina.) Also: -duunyana, dudunyana, -dadanyana.
  • persist, Ooyu musankwa uladaanyana kukazya nokuba kuti kaambo ulikazyi. = This boy persists in denying even though he knows the the truth of the matter.
  • stiff or swollen, as when dead, Musankwa ngobakauma jilo wadaanyana nkwali anze. = The boy they beat yesterday is lying stiff (i.e. dead) outside. Nibakasika bakajana ncobeni ulidaanyene. = When they arrived they found he was really dead.

persist, become entrenched, Mwami ooyu ulalidaanyika kulela nacembaala. = This chief holds on to power even when he is old. (1.-daanyikwa, 2.-daanyikide, 4.-daanyikila, 8.-daanyikana.)
  • tighten, Kamudaanyika luwaile kutegwa lutakobi-kobi. = Tighten the wire so that it is no longer slack.
  • cause death, kill, *Mweenzu bamudaanyika ibabbi.* = The thieves killed the visitor.
be rough, uncouth, or brusque in speech, *Kuvwiila wali kudabaila kubee tavwiili bapati.* = In answering she was just rough as if she was not answering the elders. Also: -dabaula.

walk with quick steps, *Uladabana kweenda akaambo kakubinda kapati.* = Because she was in such a rush, she walked with quick steps. (1.-dabanwa, 2.-dabanide, 3.-dabanya, 4.-dabanina.) Also: -dambila, -tabalika, -kansyaila.
  • dance for rain with quick steps, *Bamakaintu banji balayandisya kudabana nobakambila mvwula kumalende.* = Many women are very fond of dancing with quick steps when they pray for rain.

be unsteady, *Akaambo kakukolwa, kweenda wiile kudabankana.* = Because of being drunk, he walks unsteadily. (2.-dabankenye, 3.-dabankanya, 4.-dabankanina.)
  • be covered with mud, e.g *Zisani zyangu zyadabankana nindawa mumankanda.* = My clothes were covered with dirt when I fell in the mud. (*Kulidabankanya mumankandya* = to wallow in the mud.) Also: -dabbankana, -dadankana.

be inconsistent, change statements, *Naakali kubetekwa munkuta, wakali kwiile kudabanya kwaambaula.* = When he was being tried in court, he was just inconsistent in what he said. (1.-dabanwa, 2.-dabanide, 4.-dabanina.)
  • make dirty, *Mweemba wacidabanya cisani.* = Mweemba has dirtied her dress.

answer in a rough way, *Koleka kudabaula kwaamba.* = Stop answering rudely. (1.-dabaulwa, 2.-dabaulide, 3.-dabauzya, 4.-dabaulila, 8.-dabaulana.) Also: -dabaila.
  • speak to the point, *Ncibotu kudabaula kwaambaula, nkokufwiinsya kaambo.* = It is good to speak to the point, it shortens the discussion.
  • cut in many sections, *Kodabaula mawaile nombe ziinde.* = Cut the wires to let the cattle pass through.
be covered with mud, *Wali kutyani oyu naadabbankana boobu amankanda?* = What has this one been doing that he is so covered with mud? (2.-dabbankene, 3.-dabbankanya, 4.-dabbankanina.)

jump into water, *Wakadabbuka mumeenda dabbu!* = He jumped into the water (with a loud splash). (2.-dabbukide, 4.-dabbukila) Also: -bbwantuka.
  • talk openly so as to endanger oneself, *Wiile kudabbuka kwaamba kumbele a bapati.* = He talks in a way that can endanger himself before the elders. Also: -dabbwila

speak openly endangering onself, *Mubetesi nabalanga acabukali bacembele aaba, balo pele buyo kumweta-mweta bamana kudabbwila nzyobadabbwila eezyo.* = When the judge angrily looked at this old woman she was just smiling, having spoken openly about those matters endangering herself. i.e. by revealing things she should not reveal. (2.-dabbwide, 4.-dabbwida.)
be dressed with little clothing, *Boonse balidabide kuti basebenze anguzu.* = All were scantily dressed so that they could work energetically.
dress scantily, *Kusama mwana uulya wiile kudabila.* = That child dresses scantily. (2.-dabilide, 3.-dabbwida.)

take a short cut, *Ooku kwa Haamaleke nenzila yakali kwiindwa idabula noyenda amaulu kuya kwa Haanziba kujwe ku Nadongo.* Over there at Haa maleke there is a path which is used to take a short cut by foot going to Haanziba east to Nadongo.

undo, as a seam, Kocidabulula cikobela cangu eeci ncibakasumide. Undo this coat of mine which they had sewn. (1.-dabululwa, 2.-dabuIwide, 3.-dabuluzya, 4.-dabulwida.) Also: -zambulula, -zambununa, -dadamuna
unstitch, Nguni wakakuyiisya kudabununa cisani? = Who taught you to unstitch a cloth? (1.-dabununwa, 2.-dabunwide, 3.-dabunuzya) Also: -dadununa

be unsteady, as one drunk, Muntu naakolwa kapati uladadalika. = When a person is very drunk s/he walks unsteadily. Mucembele mulwazi wakadadalika akafwunko. The sick old woman was tottering along with a stick. (1.-dadalikwa, 2.-dadalikide, 3.-dadalisya, 4.-dadalikila.) Also: tenteleka, -daalika

be opened as a seam in cloth, be undone, Eeci cisani ciladadamuka mumoombe. = The hem of this dress is undone.
  • appear as veins, Watusabila yawe ayebo nomunga kwaakudadamuka kale nsinga kubwenta. You, whose veins stand out, are pestering us as you grumble bitterly. (2.-dadamukide, 3.-dadamukizya, 4.-dadamukila.) Also: -zambunuka, -dadanyana

unwind, unravel, undo, stretch, Kamucidadamuna mucakoombedwe cisani kutegwa cilampe. = Undo the seam of the cloth so that it is lengthened. (1.-dadamunwa, 2.-dadamwide, 3.-dadamwida.) Also: -dadununa.

become wrinkled, Waakucembaala, cikanda cako ciyaku talika kudadankana. = When you grow old your skin will become wrinkled. (2.-dadankene, 3.-dadankanya, 4.-dadankanina.)
  • become spoilt, be made dirty, Mubambi wamyoota uladadankana amafwuta mubili oonse. The mechanic is dirty with oil all over his body. Also: -dabankana

be wrinkled, Ooyu muntu ulidadankenye ankumo minya. = This man has a wrinkled brow.
  • be ugly, Ooyu muntu ulidadankenye akaambo kaminya iilaa nkumo. = This person is ugly because of the wrinkles on his forehead.
stretch as cloth or rubber, Kodadanuna mulembo oyu kutegwa tubone mbuulampa. Stretch out the cloth so that we see how long it is.

persevere energeticaly in action, Kamudadanyana kukwela cisamu nocilema kusikila cizwe. = Continue to pull the tree with strength no matter how heavy it is until it comes out. (2.-dadanyene, 3.-dadanyika, 4.-dadanyanina.) Also: -kakanyana, -duunyana, -dudunyana.
  • be adamant in what you have decided to do, Ooyu muntu taleki cintu ncaadadanyana kale. This person does not give up on something which he has already decided upon.
  • stand out, as a vein, Moonde naakanyema nsinga zyakadadanyana. = When Moonde was angry the veins stood out.
be in a protruded state, Nsinga yalidadanyene naali kulila mwana. A vein was protruding when the child was crying.

uproot, Kusya masamu munyika ipandwa muunda takuli kwakusobana pe. Inga nkusya ncobeni amiyanda yoonse nkwiidadaula. To dig up the trees from land that has been cleared for a field is not a game. It means to really dig, uprooting all the roots.
be uprooted, Yakadaduka miyanda yamusamu niwakaunga muwo. = The roots of the tree were uprooted when the wind blew. (1.-dadulwa, 2.-dadukide, 3.-daduzya, 4.-dadukila.)

lift up, Kodadula mweendo wako umwi mujulu. = Lift up one of your legs in the air. Munyati naakatiimudadule kumusana, Chakatazya wakaliwaala ansi. = When the buffalo was about to pick him up by the back, Chakatazya threw himself on the ground. (1.-dadulwa, 2.-dadulide or -dadwide, 3.-daduzya, 4.-dadwida, 8.-dadulana.) Also: -nyamuna, -dandula.
  • take off, as shoes, Kodadula mabbusu aako ukoone. Take off your shoes and sleep. Also: -samununa.
  • uproot, as potatoes, Kamwaadadula buyo magwili aayo mbwaalibonya kale. Uproot those potatoes as they are already visible. Kamuudadula muyanda wacisamu. Uproot the root of a tree. Kuti kojata nkolobeki abuyamba, iladadula mapopwe. If you hold the cultivator carelessly, it will uproot the maize. Also: -gagula.

unwind wire, Kamudadununa luwaile oolu kucisamu eeci. = Unwind that wire from the tree. (1.-dadununwa, 2.-dadunwide, 3.-dadununzya, 4.-dadunwida.) Also: -zambulula
  • undo, take out the stitches, Kamudadununa moombe wacisani eeci kutegwa cisumwe kabotu. Take out the stitches of the hem of the cloth so that you sew it properly. Also: -dabununa.
  • stretch, like rubber, Kamudadununa malekani aayo tubone mbwaalampa. = Stretch out those catapults so that we see how long they are. Also: -landamuna, -lozomona.
uproot with a tool, rt. dadula.
be stuck in mud, Cimbayambaya cakadakamina mumankandya. The vehicle was stuck in the mud. (2.-dakamide, 3.-dakamizya.) Also: -dankamina, -patila, -njomba.

do what you want, Nkooko nkakumvwe Iwabili kuti wamusankamina mulumyaako wadakaya mboyanda, uyakubona uli wankoli yakumakosi. = If I hear a second time that you have treated your husband with disrespect and behave as you wish, you will see I will come with a stick to beat you on the back of the neck.

protect an infant from the disease of luvwumwe, Baumpa nungwida antela cuuma amiyanda yamumbu akusila musizi Iwaba lusu luvwelenganizigwa mumafwuta, eelyo mwana ulananikwa aduntilo akumusana. Eeci nceciitwa kuti kudala muvwanda. They burn roots of nungwida or cuuma and those of mumbu, and grind the burnt roots into powder to mix it with the oil to anoint the baby on the top of the head and back. This is what is called 'protecting the infant'.
walk with quick steps, Bakali kudambila buya kweenda basankwa kakulunda kasuko. The boys walked with quick steps raising a lot of dust. Also: -dabana. (1.-dambilwa, 2.-dambilide.)
be saturated with, be mixed up with, Nyama ilidampankene amankandya. The meat is mixed with mud. Also: -dapankene.
be surprised, Makala takwe naakadamwa. Makala was not surprised. Also: -nyandwa, -gambwa.
be inconsistent in responding to the same question, Koamba kakunyina kudantaika. Speak without being inconsistent. (1.-dandaikwa, 2.-dandaikide, 3.-dandaisya.) Also: -dantaika

*speak abusively*, Mu- tinta wakaumwa akaambo kakudandaula kubandika kubasankwa. = Mutinta was beaten because of speaking abusively to the boys. (2.-dandawide, 4.-dandaulila, 7.-dandaula-dandaula, 8.-dandawidana.) Also: -bbodola.

*lift one leg in the air*, Koleka kudandula mweendo ulakkala bukwazi. = Stop lifting up your leg, your nakedness will be seen). cf. -pangula (1.-dandulwa, 2.-dandwide, 3.-dandusya, 4.-dandwida, 7.-dandula-dandula, 8.-dandulana.)
  • *speak pompously*, Uladandula ku- kanana nkaambo mmuvwubi. = He speaks pompously because he is rich. Also: -dandaula
*speak in a drunken fashion*, Udanganya buya kwaamba mbuli uukoledwe. = The way he speaks is as if he is drunk.

*be stuck in the mud*, Koombe kokwa Mainza kadankamina muntimba. = The calf of Mainza got stuck in the mud. (2.-dankamide, 3.-danka- mizya) Also: -patila, -dakamina, -ndondomena, -loba, -patila.
  • *stand when one should kneel to show respect to elders*, Uulya mwana ta- lomenye nkaambo udankamina bapati ka- kunyina kuyoowa. = That child is not polite because s/he stands instead of kneeling near the elders without fear.
*make muddy*, Ooyu mwana wadankanya zisani nzyasama ku- cikombelo. = This child has muddied the clothes she wears at church.
*walk at ease with oneself*, Wakali kudansaila kweenda. = He was walking in a relaxed manner. (1.-dansailwa, 2.-dansailide, 4.-dansailila.)
*stand motionless*, Ino yawe nomudansamana, toyandi kulya? = Now you who are standing motionless, don't you want to eat? (1.-dansamanwa, 2.-dansamene, 3.-dansamika, 4.-dansamina.)

*be inconsistent in explan- ation*, Wali kwiile kudantaika kwa- amba naali kubuzigwa mibuzyo kumu- silikani. = He was just being inconsistent when he was been asked questions by the policeman. (2.-dantaikide.) Also: -dandaika
*cut open*, Kamudanuna cibele carjombe nkaambo yafwundwa kale. = Cut open the udder of the cow because it has already been skinned. Also: -fwundula (1.-danunwa, 3.-danuzya, 4.-danwida.)

*change one's statements*, Wakatalika kudataika kwaamba naaka- zulwa mumulandu. = She began to be inconsistent as she spoke when she was being tried for a crime. (1.-dataikwa, 2.-dataikide.) Also: -dantaika, -dabanya, dabanya.

*fall off in big pieces or lumps*, Bakaintu bapya kapati, zi- kanda zyali kwiile kudebbauka. = The woman got burnt extensively, pieces of skin were just falling off. (1.-debbaukwa, 2.-debbaukide, 3.-debbauzya, 4.-debbaukila.)
*fall to one side* Cakade- bbuka cibeela cimwi cacisanza cama- popwe. = One part of the maize-bin fell down. (2.-debbukide, 3.-debbuzya, 4.-debbukila.)

*protrude lips (in disgust), pout*, Wakadebbula mulomo kuton- dezya kuti ncindakali kwaamba tiicaka- mukonda. = She pouted, showing that she was not pleased at what I was saying. (1.-debbulwa, 2.-debbwide, 3.-debbuzya, 4.-debbwida, 8.-debbulana.) Also: -bbebbula, -bbebbenyana.
*go without energy*, Bantu batolo tabayumi-yumi, badebbwaila buya kweenda. = Lazy people are not strong, they walk without energy. (2.-debbwailide, 3.-debbwaizya, 4.-debbwailila.)
tremble, be convulsed with contortions and twitchings, Naakaciswa kapati wakatalika kudedela. = When he became very sick he started trembling. (2.-dedelede.) Also: -bimba, -kankama.

plead with, Wakadedelela kuti bapati bacikolo bamupe cibaka camwana. = He earnestly pleaded with the headmaster for a place in school for his son. (2.-dedelede, 3.-dedelezya, 4.-dedelela, 8.-dedelelana.) Also: -kombelela

quiver Uladedema kukanana musyoonto wangu. = My young brother speaks with a hoarse voice. Mutinta wakavwuwa kumwi ijwi kalidedema. = Mutinta answered while her voice was shaking. (2.-dedemede, 3.-dedemya, 4.-dedemena) Also: -lendema

tickle, Batumbu bakamudekaanya mwanaabo kutegwa aseke. = The mother tickled the child so that it would laugh. (1.-dekaanyizyigwa, 2.-dekaanyide, 3.-dekaanyizya, 4.-dekaanyizyiza.) Also: -dekeenyas, -tekenya, -tegunya, -teguwa.
tickle, Mwana wakaseka kapati banyina nibakamudekeenya. = The child laughed very much when the mother tickled it. Also: -tekenya, nyiminya, -tekaanya, -dekaanya.
cause to laugh, Mankonono akalila pele cakazikwiile kudekenesya maunda-maunda abakubusi bakali kulangilizya 'sinema'. = He was snoring but it just made the crowds in the cinema laugh.

tell falsely, Batalika kudelaula bakaintu aaba kuti ndakamumisya mwanaabo. = This woman began to say falsely that I had impregnated her daughter. (1.-delaulwa, 2.-delwiide, 3.-delauzya, 4.-delaulila, 8.-delaulana.)
disregard, Bamaalumi bamwi balabadelela bamakaintu babo. = Some husbands disregard their wives. (1.-delelwa, 2.-delede, 3.-delezya, 4.-delelela, 8.-delelana.)
be torn, Cakadeluka cisani camwanaangu jilo. = The dress of my child got torn yesterday. (2.-delukide, 3.-deluzya, 4.-delukila.) Also: -zauka, -zapuka.

tear, Mupati wangu nguwakacidelula cisani camwana. = It is my elder sister who tore the child's dress. Mutani kwaabikki mabbuku munanda muli basikoswe, balaadelula. = Don't be putting books in a house where there are rats, they will tear them up. (1.-delulwa, 2.-delukide, 3.-delwida, 6.-delulisya, 8.-delulana.) Also: -zaula, -zapula
be torn in different places, Tacili cibotu kusama cisani cakadeluuka. = It is not good to wear a garment torn in different places. (2.-deluukide, 3.-deluukila.)
be torn in different parts, Cisani cilideluukide muzibeela zinjaanji. = The cloth is torn in many parts. Also: -ndeukide, -zapaukide.

tear in different parts, Kocideluula muzibeela-beela. = Tear it up in pieces. Basikoswe bakakkala munanda kabadeluula zisani amabbuku. = The rats remained in the house tearing up the clothes and the books. (1.-deluulwa, 2.-deluukide, 3.-deluuzya, 4.-delwiida, 8.-deluulana.) Also: -zapaula, -yawuula

lack energy or enthusiasm, be lazy, Wiile kudembaila kweenda nkaambo kakuneneya. = He walks without energy because he is very fat. Kuti V - 101 Moonga wakatala udembaila buya. = If Moonga is tired he just drags the feet. (2.-dembailide, 4.-dembailila.) Also: -debbwaila, -lembaila

die in large numbers, Bantu banji baladenauka akaambo kabuIwazi bwasikalileke. = Many people are dying in large numbers because of the disease of AIDS. (2.-denaukide, 3.-denauzya, 4.-denaukila, 6.-denaukisya.)
  • fall off continously, Cibiya ciladenauka kuti tacisibikwi kabotu. = The pot on the fire falls off continuously if it is not placed properly.

remove one by one, Kamudenauna mabwe ngomwatabide bulo. = Remove the stones with which you were supporting the bed. (1.-denaunwa, 2.-denaukide, 3.-denauzya, 4.-denaunina, 6.-denaunisya, 7. -denauna-denauna, 8.-denaunana.)
  • cause to fall in great numbers, Silubanje wakaadenauna masamu muciindi cisyoonto. = The dagga smoker cut down many trees in a very short time.
discourage, Bakamudendeekela mwana ncaatakali kuunka kubazyali bakwe. The reason why the child did not go to its parents is because they discouraged him.

carry on head without holding, Bamacembele bacicikonzya kudengenezya nongo. The old women still have the skill of carrying pots on the head without holding them with hands. (1.-dengenezyegwa, 2.-dengenezyede, 4.-dengenezyezya.) Also: -tengenezya
rock, as a canoe, Bwato nobweenda mumeenda buladengunuka. When the canoe is moving in the water it sways from side to side. Also: -tenguna

throw to the side, as a log from the shoulders, Kuti kodenketa coola, ulajaya zipwaika zili mukati. If you throw the luggage down you will destroy the breakable things inside. Bamaama bakali kwiide kulidenketa mizinga mukasuko. My mother was just throwing herself down on the ground in the dust. Wakaide kudenketa nkata yaloozi. = He just threw down the bundle of fibres. Also: - lenketa (1.-denketwa, 2.-denketide, 3.-denketya, 4.-denkete, 6.-denketesya, 8.-denketana)

prolong conversation, Mudaala wakali kudenta kwaciindi cilamfwu naakazyila kubukoko. The old man was talking for a long time when he came from the beer. (1.-dentwa, 2.-dentede, 3.-dentya, 4.-dentela, 6.-dentesya)

get detached, drop, as a falltrap, slip off, Cadenuka cikuni nitwali kuya ku Chisekese acilayi. A log slipped off the sledge as we were going to Chisekese. Cuuno nicakadenuka bacembele bakawida ansi. When the chair slipped the old woman fell to the ground. (2.-denukide, 3.-denuzya, 4.-denukila, 6.-denukisya)

release, as a trap or trigger, Naakabona kambaambi musyokwe wakaidenuna ntobolo akukajaya. When he saw the duiker in the forest he pulled the triger of the gun and killed it. (1.-denunwa, 2.-denwide, 3.-denuzya, 4.-denwida, 6.-denunisya, 8.-denunana.)
  • pull away, Ncibi kudenuna cuuno cacimbwalakasa kuti muntu kayanda kukkala. It is bad to pull away a stool if a person wants to sit on it. Also: -tesula, -gwenuna.
  • reject, rebel, Nokuba kuti bamwi baamba kuti 'muzike ulafwa amajwi mukanwa', bwasunu buyo ndacidenuna nkaambo naa caamba kulwana ndazumina. Even though some say that a slave dies with words in his mouth, today I refuse to accept it because if it means to fight I will.

dance without following the rhythm properly, dance without coordination, Aaba basimbi tabacizyi kuzyana, baile kudibana. = *These girls do not know how to dance, they are just shaking themselves without rhythm.* (1.-dibanwa, 2.-dibanide, 3.-dibanya, 4.-dibanina, 6.-dibanisya.)
  • walk out of step, Basicikolo bakali kwiide kudibana kweenda nibakali kufwoolwa. *The pupils were just out of step when they were marching.*

be disfigured, Ino mwana ooyu udibankana nzi kumeso? = *Why is this child so facially disfigured?* Wakadibankana kumeso nkaambo kakuciswa kwaciindi cilamfwu. = *He is facially disfigured because of the prolonged illness.*

strike with power, Mubbi nibakamujata bakamudibaula ankoli. *When they caught the thief, they beat him severely with knobkerries.* (1.-dibaulwa, 2.-dibaulide, 3.-dibauzya, 4.-dibawida, 6. -dibaulisya, 8.-dibaulana.) Also: -tibuula.

struggle to move quickly, Wakadibilika munene mbwacibwene kati afwambaane akabone cakali kukuugwa babwa. *The old man struggled to move thinking that he would be quick to see what was causing the dogs to bark.*
Also: -didinkana

be beaten or crushed into dust, meal or powder, Mapopwe akadibuka naakatugwa ciindi cilamfwu. = *The maize was crushed to powder when it was pounded for a long time.* Also: -tibuka. (2.-dibukide, 4.-dibukila, 6.-dibukisya)
  • become weak, Nkujana kasimbi kadibuka mumagondo, kuyoya kayoyela azilo. *It happened that the girl was weak at the knees, she was not able to breathe properly.*

pound, with thick end of pestle, Kamudibula mapopwe kutegwa azukile. *Pound the maize with the thick end of pestle until it is crushed.* (1.-dibulwa, 2.-dibulide, 3.-dibuzya, 4.-dibulila, 6.-dibulisya, 7.-dibulula, 8.-dibulana.)

repound, Wadibuka musozya, weelede kudibulula kutegwa ubote. *When you have pounded the maize into samp, repound it so that it is properly crushed.* (1.-dibululwa, 2.-dibulwide, 3.-dibuluzya, 4.-dibulwida.)
remain silent, Naakamvwa makani akankamanisya, wakadidibala buyo mpoona acuuno mpaakakkede. *When he heard this surprising news he just remained silent on the chair where he was sitting.*

dance in different directions, Bantu bakali kwiile kudidilika kuzyana akooku akooku nkaambo kakukkomana. *The people were just dancing in different directions here and there because of being so happy.* (2.-didilikide, 4.-didilikila, 6.-didilikisya)
  • move about without aim, Udidilika nzi aawa? Koya ukazinyone nombe. = *Why are you moving about pointlessly? Go and bring the cattle back.*

make a heavy sound, Imvwula iladidima kumbo. *There is heavy thunder in the west. Nokuli mudumu, citima cilalimvwisya kudidima. When it is humid, the train can be heard rumbling. Mucembele ulayoowa niididima ndeke kujulu. The old woman fears when the areoplane makes a loud noise in the sky.* (2.-didimide, 3.-didimya, 4.-didimina, 6.-didimisya, 7.-didimadidima) Also: -ndindima, -duduma.

thunder and lightning without rain, Sunu yali kudidimuna mvwula masiku oonse. There was = = thunder and lightning all night, but no rain. (1.-didimunwa, 2.-didimwide, 3.-didimuzya.)
  • drive away, Minsi yakumweka kwazuba iladikimuna musinze oonse. = The rays of the shining sun drives away the darkness.
be disfigured, Ooyu mudaala wakadidinkana kubusyu naakawa. The old man's face was disfigured when he fell. Also: -ilingana (2.-didinkenye, 3.-didinkanya, 4.-didinkanina, 6.-didinkanisya.)

deface, Meenda akadidinkanya cifwanikiso nicakaloka mucibulo. The water defaced the picture when it fell into the bucket. Masowe wacididinkanya cibiya cabotede kale. = Masowe defaced a beautifully moulded clay pot.

be free to do what is wrong, Ooyu mwana wadiikila kukkala nkaambo taakwe bananyina bamuuma. = This child is free to live in a bad way because there are no other children to beat him. Muno mumunzi tamudiikilwi nkaambo babwa mbakali = Here in this village you are not free to do wrong because the dogs are fierce. (1.-diikilwa, 2.-diikide, 3.-diikizya, 4.-diikilila)

not be upright, become curved, Moonga naakaumwa kumusana wakadiimana. When Moonga was beaten on the back it became bent. Ncinga niyakapwaya amusamu ivwili lyakadiimana. When the bicycle crashed into the tree the wheel was bent. Banyina bakalipengede kubona mwanaabo udiimana kweenda amunduumbwa wada, lijisi mwana uutakwe usyi. The mother was distressed to see her daughter crippled, walking with the burden of pregnancy, having a child without a father. (2.-diimenye, 3.-diimika, 4.-diimanina) Also: -dilimana.
be in a crooked state, Masomo oonse ngaakagonka Munene akalidiimene. All the poles which Munene cut were bent.
bend, Ncuubauba kudiimika cibulo nocicipya. It is easy to bend iron when it is still hot. (1.-diimikwa, 2.-diimikide, 4.-diimikila, 8.-diimikana.) Also: -ongomeka, -gogomeka.

pour out in a swarm, Kwakadiimuka buyo bususuli. = Only midges swarmed out. Nsima njobakadiimuka bakasika balo babwa biilya. = The dogs came and ate the nsima which they had poured out. Also: -dilimuka (2.-diimukide, 3.-diimusya, 4.-diimukila.)

bite and shake, as a dog Bakamudika babwa kutali kumusobanya. = The dogs bit and shook him severely. (1.-dikwa, 2.-dikide, 3.-dikizya, 4.-dikila, 5.-dikilalyo, 6.-dikisya, 7.-dika-dika, 8.-dikana)
  • amuse, Aya majwi amwi akali akudika. Some of these words are just meant to amuse.
shake out, Nomulimina kamwaadika-dika mani kutegwa ayume. = When you are weeding shake out the grass so that it becomes dry. Also: -dikinya, -didimuna, -dikimuna.

feel internal pain, Wakadikiminwa mucamba akaambo ka zyuumo. He suffered internal pains in the chest because of the blows.
  • become exhausted, Ndakadikiminwa jilo nkaambo ndakabwezede mukuli mulemu. = I was exhausted yesterday because I was carrying a heavy load.

cause internal injury, Nkoli nzibakalikumuumya zyakamudikimizya. The knobkerries with which they beat him damaged him internally. Wakalifwusa sumo lyamala lyakakayasa kanyama mumabambo lyakakadikimizya mpoona. = He threw a barbed spear, it pierced the animal in the ribs and then entered deep inside.
  • cause to become exhausted, Ndaci*dikimizya kucuuma.* = I caused it to be completely overcome in beating it. (1.-*dikimizyigwa*, 2.-*dikimizyide*, 4.*dikimizyizya*, 8.-*dikimizyanya*) cf. -*tikimizya*.

fall inwards, Kacitaninga*kubaa ciindi, cimbuzi cakadilika akuzuma cakuyoosya.* = In a short time the toilet fell inwards with a fearful crash. (2.-*dilikide*, 3.-*dilisya*, 4.-*dilisyizya*)
  • go backwards, *Kweenda koonse mubwato bakali kumvwa mbuli kuti badilika munsi.* = When they were going in the boat they felt as if they were going backwards.

scattered in a flock, *Tuyuni twakali kulya maila twakadilimuka nindakasiba mulosi.* = The birds which were eating the sorgum scattered when I whistled. (2.-*dilimukide*, 3.-*dilimusya*, 4.-*dilimusyizya*)
scatter to, *Awo mpozyakadilimukila nombe akali akalundu kakajisi loonde.* = There, to where the cattle scattered, was a hill with a thicket. (2.-*dilimukide*)

flap wings, shake oneself, shake out, cast off, *Kamudikimuna mapayi luzwe lusuko.* = Shake out the blankets to remove the dust. *Minsi yakumweka kwazuba iladikimuna musinze oonse.* = The rays of the shining sun cast off all the darkness. *Wakalidikimuna mbuli muyuni wazwa mumeenda.* = He shook himself like a bird coming from the water. Also: -*dikinya*, -*dika-dika*, -*vwukumuna* (1.-*dikimunwa*, 2.-*dikimunide*,/*-dikimwide*, 3.-*dikimunzya*, 4.-*dikimwida*, 5.-*dikimwidalyo*, 6.-*dikimunisya*, 7.-*dikimuna-dikimuna*, 8.-*dikimunana*.)

shake, *Nibakali kwiizya masiku, nanda yakadikinya akaambo* *kaguwo pati lyakalikuunga.* = When they were chatting at night, the house shook because of a great wind which was blowing. *Cheelo, kodikinya mapayi inga koya kulumwa kabanze.* = Cheelo, shake out the blankets or else you will be bitten by a scorpion. (1.-*dikinyizyigwa*, 2.-*dikinyide*) Also: -*dikimuna*, -*vwukumuna*s, -*bbukumuna*.
be shaken, *Mangoye wakalumwa amubwa, wakadikinywa kapati.* = The cat was attacked by the dog and was shaken a lot.

draw any liquid which is plentiful, *Bantu banji bakali kudikula cibwantu kunkolola.* = Many people were drawing plenty of the abundant sweet beer at the initiation. (1.-*dikulwa*, 2.-*dikwide*, 3.-*dikuzya*, 4.-*dikwida*)

fall inwards, collapse, *Inanda yakadilika kumbali lyakawa mvwula mpati.* = Part of the house fell in during the heavy rains. Also: -*kolomoka*. (2.-*dilikide*, 3.-*dilisya*, 4.-*dilikila*.)
  • cool one's temper, *Musankwa wakanyemede kapati, wakadilika naakalaigwa abapati.* = The boy who was very angry, cooled his temper when he was advised by the elders.
  • retreat, reverse, *Basune bakadilika nilyakapatila jamba.* = The oxen went backwards when the plough got stuck.
be in a collapsed state, *Aawo atongo kwakali nanda yomwe yatakadilikide.* = There among the ruins there was one house which had not collapsed.
collapse on, entomb, rt. -*dilika*, *Cuumbwe cabakaapa cakadilikila mukati.* = The grave of my grandmother collapsed inwards. Also: - *bobela*. (1.-*dilikilwa*, 2.-*dilikide*, 3.-*dilisya*)
clap as thunder, *Imvwula noizuma iladilima cakuyoosya kapati.* = When the rain thunders it claps in a very frightening way. Also: -ndindima, -zuma. (2.-dilimide, 3.-dilimya)
be bent, *Mutabi wakadilimana nikwakakkala muntu uneneede.* = The branch was bent when the fat man sat on it. (2.-dilimene) Also: -diimana
be in a crippled state, *Uulya mbwaakazyalwa ulidilimene.* = That person, since she was born, has been bent. Also: -diimene.

fly or run away together, *Mancwe adilimuka nindainda mujungusi acisamu.* = The flock of little birds scattered as I passed under the tree. *Twabona nombe zyaile kudilimuka zyoonse akuboba. Awo mpozyakadilimukila akali akalundu kakajisi loonde.* = We saw the cattle just all running away and mooing. At the place where they had run away from, there was a hill which had a clump of trees. (2.-dilimukide, 3.-dilimuzya, 4.-dilimukila)
  • fall on, *Chilipa naakali koola nanda, bwaanda bwakadilimuka akumutyola maulu.* = When Chilipa was demolishing the house, the wall fell and broke his legs. Also: -kolomoka, -oleka.
take down, dismantle, destroy, *Matongo naakapola, maanda akwe wakaadilimuna.* = When Matongo moved out, he knocked down his houses. (1.-dilimunwa, 2.-dilimwide, 3.-dilimuzya, 4.-dilimuzyizya.)

be dismantled, *Sikulanga maanda ayakwa wakaamba kuti yomwe yeelede kudilimunwa nkaambo taiyakidwe kabotu.* = The inspector said that one house ought to be taken down as it was not built well. (2.-dilimwidwe, 3.-dilimuzyigwa, 4.-dilimwidwa)
cause to go backwards, rt. dilika, *Kodilisya munsi moota.* = Reverse the vehicle. (1.-dilisyigwa, 2.-dilisyide, 4.-dilisyizya, 8.-dilisyanya.)

rumble, *Muzovwu naakainda munsi ananda yangu, nyika yakali kudima.* = When the elephant passed near my house, the earth rumbled. (1.-dimizyigwa, 2.-dimide, 3.-dimya, 4.-dimina) Also: -didima.
  • be sound asleep, *Ndali kwiide kudima koona, tiindabamvwa bali kubba mpongo masiku.* = I was sound asleep, I did not hear those who were stealing the goats at night. Also: -onenena.
  • burn fiercely, *Kaanda kamunene kadima kupya mulilo.* = The small house of the old man burnt fiercly.
grow dark, *Twakasika kwadimaana kale amunzi.* = We arrived home when it was already dark. (2.-dimeene, 3.-dimaanya, 4.-dimaanina)

press down on something, *Cicula ndakacidimba abbwe.* = I pressed down upon the frog with a stone. *Idiba lyakamudimba kakololo naakatiilye ipopwe.* = The fall-trap fell on the big rat when it was about to eat the maize cob. (1.-dimbwa, 2.-dimbide, 3.-dimbya, 4.-dimbila, 5.-dimbilalyo, 6.-dimbisya, 8.-dimbana.)
become concave, *Cuuno ncaakali kufwala cakadimpuka.* = The stool which he was carving became concave. (2.-dimpukide, 3.-dimpuzya, 4.-dimpukila, 8.-dimpukana.)
be concave, *Moononono wampemo wakalidimpukide kapati.* = The bridge of the nose was excessively concave. *Musana wasuntwe ulidimpukide.* = The back of the hyena is concave. Also: -dyaamene.
drop into, *Mukaintu wakadimpukizya cibulo mumugodi.* = The woman dropped the bucket into the well. (1.-dimpukizyigwa, 2.-dimpukizyide, 4.-dimpukizyizya, 8.-dimpukizyanya) Also: -dumpukizya.

take a spoonfull, *Mbwaakasikila wakaudimpula musozya nkaambo wakalaa nzala.* = As soon as he arrived he took a spoon full of samp because he was hungry. (1.-dimpulwa, 2.-dimpwide, 3.-dimpuzya, 4.-dimpwida, 5.-dimpwidalyo, 6.-dimpulisya.)
  • do something in an excessive manner, going deep, stress further, *Kumeso wakajisi masimbo-masimbo alimwi wakali kumuyasaula wakali kumudimpula buyo kuyasa.* On his face he had scars and the one who had made incisions had gone deep. *Nabulonga wakadimpula kwaamba.* = Nabulonga stressed what she said.
be astonished, *Nda-dimpwa nindamvwa lufwu Iwa Michelo.* = I was astonished when I heard of the death of Michelo. Also: -nyandwa

hold by the throat, strangle, choke, *Bakamujata akumudina akameneno ncaakafwa.* They caught him and strangled him by the throat, that is why he died. *Citolopo camudina musune ncatakweli kabotu.* = The strap is choking the ox, that is why it is not pulling well. cf. -sina. (1.-dinwa, 2.-dinide, 3.-dinizya, 4.-dinina, 5.-dininalyo, 6.-dinisya, 7.-dinadina, 8.-dinana)
  • press, as matter out of abcess, *Kodina cilonda buzwe busina.* = Press the sore to remove the pus. Also: -tyanka, -sina
  • close one eye when aiming, *Kodina liso kutegwa udubule kabotu kanyama.* = Close your eye when aiming so that you shoot the animal well.
  • kadina nio, *Bamisela yakwe boonse ciindi kabacili bakubusi waali kubakonzya kubaanga kadina nio.* = He was able to tie both hands in the hole of all his age-mates when they were boys. (This refers to a punishment practiced among herders where both hands were placed in a hole and the earth pounded around it so that the hands could not be pulled out.)
bounce, be springy, *Ndoona kabotu nkaambo ndalede abulo budindibuka.* I have slept well because I have been lying on a spring bed. (2.-dindibukide, 3.-dindibukizya, 4.-dindibukila) Also: -dundubuka.
bend up and down, *Bantu basya ndongwe baladingaama tunjitunji.* People who dig groundnuts bend up and down continuously. 2.-dingaamide, 3.-dingaamika, 4.-dingaamina)

bend down, crouch, *Wakadingama kuti abweze cisani kuti amusamike mwana.* He bent down to take a cloth to dress the child. *Wakadingama kuti anywe meenda mukalonga.* = He bent down to drink water in the stream. Also: -tingama. (1.-dingamikwa, 2.-dingeme, 3.-dingamya, 4.-dingamina.)

overturn, *Nibwakamana bukoko, bakazidingamika nongo zyoonse.* When the beer was finished, they overturned all the pots. Also: -gununa, -vwuntamika, -dingamuna. (1.-dingamikwa, 2.-dingamikide, 3.-dingamisya, 4.-dingamukila, 8.-dingamikana)
bend down towards, *Mmalweza kudingamina muntu acinswe.* = It is taboo to bend down towards a person while naked. (2.-dingaminide.)
bend down in cowardly fashion when fighting, *Tuladingaminana cababwa.* = We were bending down like cowardly dogs when fighting one another.

be overturned, *Nongo yabukoko niyadingamuka, boonse bukoko bwali mukati bwatika.* When the beer pot overturned, all the beer which was inside poured out. (1.-dingamukwa, 2.-dingamukide, 3.-dingamukila.)

overturn, *Ngulube yazidingamuna zitalo zyabukoko.* = The pig overturned the barrels of beer. Baci wubwe baladingamuna mato masyoonto. = The hippos overturn small boats. Also: -bbindamuna, -tingamuna, -vwuntamuna.

look with difficulty, rt. -dina, Nkaambo nzi ncodinikizya kulanga mbuli kuti uciswa meso. = Why are you looking with difficulty as if your eyes were sore? (1.-dinikizyigwa, 2.dinikizyide, 4.-dinikizyigwa) Also: -fwinyikizya (rt. -fwinya), -mwinikizya

beat hard, Sulwe wakabweza bbwe akudinka nondo. = The hare took a stone and hammered the tortoise. Sicikolo wakamudinka mfwaindi mweenzinyina. The pupil punched his friend. Walo Mubekwabekwa bakafwa kumudinka citako cantobolo. = They kept on beating Mubekwabekwa with the butt of the gun. (1.-dinkwa, 2.-dinkide, 3.-dinkizya, 4.-dinkila, 5.-dinkilalyo, 6.-dinkisya, 7.-dinka-dinka, 8.-dinkana.)

level by beating down, pound, Kamubudinka-dinka bulimo bweelane = Level off that plot of land so that it is even. Sicuuno tayelede kudinkadinka atebule nasololela muswaangano. = The chairperson should not pound the table when leading the meeting.

strike, rt. -dinka. Bakamudinkaula beenzinyina kusikila bamucisa. = His friends beat him up until they hurt him. (1.-dinkaulwa, 2.-dinkwide, 3.-dinkaulizya, 4.-dinkawida, 6.-dinkaulisya, 8.-dinkaulana)

beat hard, Bantu bakadinkawida mwana wakatukila mudaala. People beat the boy for insulting the old man. (1.-dinkawidwa, 8.-dinkawidana)
  • talk abusively to, Ndakamudinkawida kumwaambawida naakanditamikizya kubba bukoko. = I talked abusively to him when he accused me of stealing beer.
be stamped, as a floor, polish with broken bottles, Cibuye cakalidinkidwe. The floor had been stamped.
stamp down, Bakaintu badinkila nanda. The women are stamping down the floor of the house. (1.-dinkilwa, 2.-dinkidwe, 3.-dinkizya, 4.-dinkilila, 5.-dinkilana, 6.-dinkilisya, 7.-dinkila-dinkila.)
ntobola yamudinkilwa = a muzzel gun.

beat, Wandidinkula andelo. You have beaten me on the back. (1.-dinkulwa, 2.-dinkulide, 3.-dinkuzya, 4.-dinkulila, 5.-dinkulilalyo, 6.-dinkulisya, 7.-dinkula-dinkula, 8.-dinkulana)
  • speak in a rough way, Nindakaunkide kukubuzya waakutalika kudinkula kukanana. = When I went to ask you, you began to speak in a rough way.
beat each other, rt. -dinka, Basankwa bakali kulwana bakadinkulana kusikila limwi balekana. = The boys just beat one another until they left off. (2.-dinkulene, 3.-dinkulanya, 4.-dinkulanina)
be beaten, Musune uukaka kweenda kabotu wakali kudinkuIwa cisamu. = The ox which refused to move properly was beaten with a stick. (2.-dinkudwe, 4.-dinkwidwa.)

stamp, make impression, make tattoe, Mobalikulyata balikuyaabudinta mano. They left some footprints where they stepped. Koludinta lugwalo natiikazumine kundisilika musilisi. Stamp the letter and then the doctor can agree to treat me. Umwi wakadintidwe syuumbwa kukwaanza kwalulyo. = One was tattooed with a lion on his right hand. (1.-dintwa, 2.-dintide, 3.-dintya, 4.-dintila, 5.-dintilalyo, 6.-dintisya, 7.-dinta-dinta, 8.-dintana.)
be bent, Ooyu conco wiile kudivwuka nkaambo wakabambwa alubulo luteteete. This spoon bends easily because it was made of a soft metal. (2.-divwukide, 4.-divwukila.)

be weak, Mubili wamwana uladizyauka citondezya kuti ucisidwe kapati. The body of the child is weak showing that it is very sick. (2.-dizyaukide, 3.-dizyaukizya, 4.-dizyaukila) Also: -tesyauka, -benzauka.
be filled with dirt, Zisani zyamunene zyakadobela tombe The clothes of the old man were clogged with dirt. (2.-dobede, 3.-dobezya, 4.-dobelela, 5.-dobelelalyo.) Also: -fwuba, -dombela.
be untidy, Njanda kukukula munanda yangu nkaambo nseyandi kuti yatalika kudobenkana. I want to sweep my house because I do not want it to become untidy. (2.-dobenkene, 3.-dobenkanya, 4.-dobenkanina)
