look upwards, Kogwalala tubone nsingo yako mboisalala. = Look upwards so that we see how clean your neck is. Also: -gwaalala, -nuka, -lungumana. (2.-gwalalide, 3.-gwalalizya, 4.-gwalalila, 5.-gwalalilayo, 6.-gwalalisya, 7.-gwalalagwalala, 8.-gwalalana.)

open as a big space, Kogwalamuna kujula mulyango bainde bantu. Open the door wide so that people can pass. (1.-gwalamunwa, 2.-gwalamwide, 3.-gwalamuzya, 4.-gwalamwida, 5.-gwalamwidalyo, 6.-gwalamunisya, 7.-gwalamuna-gwalamuna, 8.-gwalamunana) Also: -gwaamuna

dig up medicines for some-one, Munene wakamugwala wida Makala ziyanda-yanda mbuli mbwaakali ku-yanda. The old man dug the medicines for Makala as he wanted. (1.-gwalawidwa, 2.-gwalawide, 3.-gwalawizya, 4.-gwalawidila, 5.-gwalawidilalyo, 6.-gwalawisya, 7.-gwalawida-gwalawida, 8.-gwalawidana.) Also: -syida.

struggle, Wakajana mwana ulagwalaya mulungu. = She found the baby struggling among the pumpkin leaves. Ino mulota nzi ncomunga mulagwalaya masiku oonse? = What are you dreaming about that makes you toss about all night. Watalika kugwalaya meso kaajalidwe mbuli muntu wafwa maafwa. = He began to roll his closed eyes like one who had an attack of epilepsy. (2.-gwalayide, 3.-gwalaizya, 4.-gwalayila, 5.-gwalayilalyo, 6.-gwalaikisya, 7.-gwalaya-gwalaya.)

gulp, Mutinta wakagwalika-gwalika kunywa cibwantu. = Mutinta was gulping down the sweet beer. ('gwalya' = the sound made when gulping something down) (1.-gwalikwa-gwalikwa, 2.-gwalikidegwalikide, 3.-gwalikizya-gwalikizya, 4.-gwalikila-gwalikila, 5.-gwalikilalyogwalikilalyo, 6.-gwalikisya-gwalikisya, 7.-gwalika-gwalika)

light a match, Kamugwalula kancisi komwe. = Strike one match stick. Also: -kkwenyuna. (1.-gwalulwa, 2.-gwalwide, 3.-gwaluzya, 4.-gwalwida, 5.-gwalwidalyo, 6.-gwalulisya, 7.-gwalula-gwalula, 8.-gwalulana.)
scrape, Nindakasika ndakajana mwaalumi ugwama-gwama kasamu. = When I arrived I found the man scraping a stick.
slap and kick, Bakugwamaune mbayi azikatulo mutusolo kuyanda tuli twalo. = They will slap and kick you with sandals because they want money.

hold on to firmly, Sicinsuungwe naakanditanda, ndakasotoka a kugwambatila kumutabi wamusamu. = When the mad dog chased me, I jumped and clung to the branch of a tree. Mutinta mumapenzaakwe wakabagwambatila banyina. = Mutinta in her sufferings held on firmly to her mother. Busololi nkugwambatila kujata. Leadership must be held on to firmly. (1.-gwabatilwa, 2.-gwambatide, 3.-gwambatizya, 4.-gwambatilila, 5.-gwambatililayo, 6.-gwambatilisya, 7.-gwambatila-gwambatila, 8.-gwambatilana.) Also: -ombetela.

be useless, lie idle, be helpless, be too small, Cigabba cinyina mulimo, ciile kugwangalika. = This tin has no function, it is too small. Munene uupengede ugwangalika buyo abulo unyina ipayi. = The suffering old man lies helpless on the bed without a blanket. (2.-gwangalikide, 3.-gwangalisya, 4.-gwangalikila, 5.-gwangalikilalyo, 6.-gwangalikisya, 7.gwangalikagwangalika)

quarrel, Mulagwangana kubwentelana mbumwali kutalika. = You have been quarreling and giving out to one another since you started. Also: -kwangana, zwangana, -bwensyanya, -kwankwana. (1.-gwanganwa, 2.-gwanganide, 3.-gwanganya, 4.-gwanganina, 5.-gwanganinalyo, 6.-gwanganisya, 7.-gwangana-gwangana.) =

open widely more than usual, Mwana naakaciswa syini ciindi cilamfwu mpemo zyakagwanguka. When the child was suffering from a cold for a long time the nostrils widened abnormally. (2.-gwankukide, 3.-gwanguzya, 4.-gwangukila, 5.-gwangukilalyo, 6.-gwangukisya, 7.-gwanguka-gwanguka.)
be extensive, Cisi cokwanu cigwangwamukide kapati. = Your land is very extensive.
argue Also: -gwangana, -tengausyanya
help in doing something, rt. gwasya, Kamumugwasilila munene acikonzye kweenda. Help the old man so that he is able to walk. (1.-gwasililwa)

help, Kamumugwasya mwana cakulembya zyakucikolo. = Help the child with something to write his homework. (1.-gwasyigwa, 2.-gwasyide, 3.-gwasyizya, 4.-gwasyililila 5.gwasyililalyo, 6.gwasyisyisya, 7.-gwasya-gwasya, 8.-gwasyanya) Also: -yovwa.

pound the ground with footsteps, stamp the feet, Naali kugwataila kweenda, nyika yalikudima-dima. = When he was coming pounding along, the earth was reverberating. (1.-gwatailwa, 2.-gwatailide, 3.-gwataizya, 4.-gwatailila, 5.-gwataililalyo, 6.-gwatailisya, 7.-gwataila-gwataila) Also: -gantaila, -jintaila

be unsteady Wakatalika kubala cakugwatangana. = He began to read unsteadily. (1.-gwatanganwa, 2.-gwatanganide, 3.-gwatanganya, 4.-gwatanganina, 5.-gwatanganinalyo, 6.-gwatanganisya, 7.gwatangana-gwatangana.)

be slack, become weak, Naamvwa kuti banyina bafwa, waile kugweba-gweba. When he learnt of his mother's death, he became weak. Also: -teba-teba, -kweba-kweba. (1.-gwebwa-gwabwa, 2.-gwebide-gwebide 3.-gwebya-gwebya, 4.-gwebela-gwebela, 5.-gwebelalyo-gwebelalyo, 6.-gwebesyagwebesya.)
  • cut bushes, Kamugweba-gweba zitewo mpotuyanda kusyanga ndongwe. = Cut the bushes where we want to plant groundnuts. Also: -gwetaula.

fold up, Kokagwedula kapepa ako, tutumine Mutinta. = Fold up that paper so that we send it to Mutinta. (1.-gwedulwa, 2.-gwedulide, 3.-gweduzya, 4.-gwedwida, 5.-gwegwidalyo, 6.-gwedulisya, 7.-gwedula-gwedula, 8.-gwedulana.) Also: -vwunga.

be clear, Kwagweemuka kujwe kwasizizye mvwula. = The east which was darkened by rain is now clear. Mizeezo yagweemuka, naalibonya mwana wasowekede. = My thoughts became clear, when the child who was lost was found. Oonse sikunku wakasinkide mumalundu wakagweemuka koonse kwatalika kulibonya. = All the mist which had blocked the hills cleared away and everywhere became visible. (2.-gweemukide, 3.-gweemuzya, 4.-gweemukila, 5.-gweemukilalyo, 6.-gweemukisya, 7.-gweemuka-gweemuka, 8.-gweemunana.)
  • open wide, Mulyango wakujulu wakagweemuka. The gate of heaven was opened wide.

be active in causing disturbance, Bamwi bantu balagweqwetela mutwaambo tutayi koomoonga. = Some people are caught up in discussing things which are of no importance. Mainza ndamucitila cicisizya moyo, pesi taagwegwetela. I did something that hurt Mainza, but she did not mind. Also: -gwagwatila. (gwegwetela is also used as a noun, kumucitila gwegwetela) (1.-gwegwetelwa, 2.-gwegwetede, 3.-gwegwetezya, 4.-gwegwetela, 5.-gwegwetelalyo, 6.-gwegwetelesya, 7.-gwegwetela-gwegwetela, 8.-gwegwetelana.)
persist Also: -gwagwatila. (1.-gwegwetilwa, 2.-gwegwetilide, 3.-gwegwetilizya, 4.-gwegwetilila, 5.-gwegwetililalyo, 6.-gwegwetililisya, 7.-gwegwetila-gwegwetila, 8.-gwegwetilana)

dislocate, Ndagwejuka mukasolo nindali kusotoka. = I dislocated my hip when I was jumping. Cuuno cakkede mudaala cagwejuka mweendo, = The leg of the chair on which the old man was sitting was out of position. (2.-gwejukide, 3.-gwejuzya, 4.-gwejukilagwejukila, 5.-gwajukilalyo, 6.-gwejukisya, 7.-gwejuka-gwejuka, 8.-gwejukana.)

draw, drag, Kamugwela looye luyume tusyange kabotu. = Pull the rope so that it becomes taut for us to plant well. (1.-gwelwa, 2.-gwelede, 3.-gwelezya, 4.-gwelela, 5.-gwelelalyo, 6.-gwelesya, 7.-gwela-gwela, 8.-gwelana.) Also: -kwela.

have severe stomach upset, Ndakamvwa mwida mwiile kugwelauka njanda kunetuka. I felt my stomach churning, I was about to faint. (1.-gwelaukwa, 2.-gwelauikide, 3.-gwelauzya, 4.-gwelaukila, 5.-gwelaukilalyo, 6.-gwelaukisya, 7.-gwelauka-gwelauka) Also: pituka

strike objects one against the other, Mbeba zyali kugwelenganya mitiba masiku. = The mice were making noise with the dishes at night. Also: -golonganya, -gwetenganyas, -gulunganya. (1.-gwelenganyizigwa, 2.-gwelengenye, 4.-gwelenganyizyizya, 5.-gwelenganyizyizyalyo, 7.-gwelenganyagwelenganya)

be immodest, Muntu utalomene ulagwenauka kweenda. = A person who is not honourable goes about in an immodest way. (1.-gwenaukwa, 2.-wenaukide, 3.-gwenauzya, 4.-gwenaukila, 5.-gwenaukilalyo, 6.-gwenaukisya, 7.-gwenuaka-gwenauka.)

refuse by shaking the head, Nindaamubuzya kuti sena nduwe wabba, wakagwenaula buyo mutwe. = When I asked him are you the one who has stolen, he just shook his head. (1.-gwenaulwa, 2.-gwenaulide, 3.-gwenauzya, 4.-gwenaulila, 5.-gwenaulilalyo, 6.-gwenaulisya, 7.-gwenaula-gwenaula.) Also: -pungunya mutwe.

fit loosely, Maulu aamwana agwengela mumabbusu. = The feet of the child fit too loosely into the shoes. (1.-gwengelwa, 2.-gwengede, 3.-gwengezya, 4.-gwengelela, 5.-gwengelelalyo, 6.-gwengelesya, 7.-gwengelagwengela)
become bright, Yalikuwa kapati mvwula kuzwa buseeni, ino kwagwenuka. = The rain was falling heavily from the morning, but now it has become bright. Also: -gweenuka, gweemuka

strike a match-stick, Gwenuna mancisi kulibonye nkaambo kwasiya. = Strike a match-stick so that it becomes bright because it is dark. (1.gwenunwa, 2.-gwenwide, 3.-gwenuzya, 4.-gwenwida, 5.-gwenwidalyo, 6.-gwenunisya, 7.-gwenuna-gwenuna, 8.-gwenunana) Also: -kkwenyuna
  • remove support, Mootokala wakawa ciindi bana nobakagwenuna mabwe ngowaatabidwe. = The vehicle fell down when the children removed the stones which were supporting it. Also: -denuna.

dismantle, as a camp bed, Bagwetaula bulo mbutwalede sunu. = They have dismantled the bed on which we slept today. Also: -sekaula, -talamuna (1.-gwetaulwa, 2.-gwetawide, 3.-gwetauzya, 4.-gwetawida, 5.-gwetqwidalyo, 6.-gwetaulisya, 7.-gwetaula-gwetaula, 8.-gwetaulana.)
  • cut bushes, Basankwa bakatugwetaula tusamu twakali munsaa muu nda. = The boys cut down the bushes which were near the field.

make to shake, Izina lyakwe lya Magwete bakamuulika akaambo kazifuwa nzyaakali kugwetemya mucibuno cakwe. = They named him with the name of Magwete because of the bones which he was rattling on his waist. (2.-gwetemide, 4.-gwetemina, 5.-gweteminalyo, 6-gwetemisya, 7.-gwetemagwetema)

create a rumpus, make noise, disturb, Babwa bangu bakali kugwetenganya zibiya nkaambo tiindakabasanina jilo. = The dogs were making noise with the pots because I did not feed them yesterday. (1.-gwetenganizigwa, 2.-gwetengaizide, 4.-gwetenganizyizya, 7.-gwetenganya-gwetenganya, 8.-gwetenganyizyanya.) Also: -gulunganya.
open up, as the sky, Kujulu kwagwetuka. = The sky is clear. (2.-gwetukide, 3.-gwetuzya, 4.-gwetukila, 5.-gwetukilalyo, 6.-gwetukisya, 7.-gwetuka-gwetuka)

strike a match, Kamuqwetula kancisi kusalale. = Strike a match-stick so that there is light. (1.-gwetulwa, 2.-gwetwide, 3.-gwetuzya, 4.-gwetwida, 5.-gwetwidalyo, 6.-gwetulisya, 7.-gwetula-gwetula, 8.-gwetwidana) Also: -gwalula, -gwenuna, -kkwenuna.
  • clear a space, Kamugwetula awa mpotuyanda kubamba mugwagwa. Clear this space where we want to make a road. =

scream as from pain or fear, Munene ulagwiila nkaambo ulaciswa. = The old man is screaming in pain because he is sick. (1.-gwiilwa, 2.-gwiilide, 3.-gwiizya, 4.-gwiilila, 5.-gwiililalyo, 6.-gwiilisya, 7.-gwiila-gwiila) Also: -kwiila

work without rest, Mainza wakali kugwilingana kuzwa ciindi cacifwumofwumo kusikila kumazuba. = Mainza was working furiously from morning until evening. (1.-gwilinganwa, 2.-gwilinganide, 3.-gwilinganina, 5.-gwilinganinalyo, 6.-gwilinganisya, 7.-gwilingana-gwilingana) Also: -bilingana, -gwitingana.

give an electric shock, Cigwinya tatyankwi amaanza. *Ulagwinta!* Inkwazi iluma baswi batagwinti, baswi batakwe meno ayasa. = The fish called cigwinya is not to be pressed. It gives a shock. The fish-eagle snatches fish that do not give a shock, fish that do not have teeth which pierce. (1.-gwintwa, 2. -gwintide, 3.-gintya, 4.-gwintila, 5.-gwintilalyo, 6.-gwintisya, 7.-gwinta-gwinta, 8.-gwintana)
  • release arrow from bow, Muvwimi wabayuni wakamuka kugwinta kata. = The hunter of birds was slow to release the arrow. Also: -kwinta.
swindle, Babbi baagwinya mali aangu. = The thieves have swindled me of my money. (1.-gwinyigwa, 2.-gwinyide, 3.-gwinyizya, 4.-gwinyina, 5.-gwinyinalyo, 6.-gwinyisya, 7.-gwinyagwinya, 8.-gwinyana)

take out, Kamugwisya nombe muluba zikacele. = Take the cattle out of the kraal so that they graze. (1.-gwisyigwa, 2.-gwisyide, 3.-gwisyizya, 4.-gwisyila, 5.-gwisyilalyo, 6.-gwisyisya, 7.-gwisya-gwisya, 8.-gwisyanya) Also: -gusya, -zwisya.

be in a confused state, rt. gwitila, Ncintu ciyumu kugusya gubilizi ligwitide mumitwe yabantu. = It is difficult to remove a blurred vision which confuses the minds of people. (1.-gwitizyigwa, 3.-gwitizya, 4.-gwitizyizya, 5.-gwitizyizyalyo, 6.-gwitilisya, 7. -gwitila-gwitila)

be uncontrolled in action, Basimbi bakali kugwitikizya kulila mbuli basidilwe balindila mutunta kuti usike kunamaumbwe. = The girls were crying hysterically like mourners waiting for a dead person to arrive at the graveyard. (1.-gwitikizyigwa, 2.-gwitikizyizye, 4.-gwitikizyizya, 5.-gwitikizyizyalyo, 6.-gwitikizyisya, 7.-gwitikizya-gwitikizya, 8.-gwitikizyanya.)

be in a turmoil, Kwagwitila munanda akaambo kakuyobeka kwabana. = The house is disturbed within because of the din of the children shouting. Nibakasika kudilwe, munzi woonse wakagwitila. = When they reached the funeral, the whole village went into turmoil. Wakamvwa kugwitila a magwagwaagwa akali munanda. He heard the uproar and the laughter in the house. (2.-gwitide, 3.-gwitizya, 4.-gwitizyizya 5.-gwitililalyo, 6.-gwitilisya, 7.-gwitilagwitila)
  • stench, Munanda mwagwitila nkwaabola muntu ufwide. = There is a stench in the house because of the decomposing of a dead body.
  • be filled, as to suffocate, Murnanda kwagwitila busi. = The house is filled with suffocating smoke.

cause noise, disturbance or conflict, rt. -gwitila, Bana bayoba bagwitilizya nanda yoonse. = The children who are shouting have filled the whole house with noise. Kufwumbwa mpaakkala, aawo ulamvwa wagwitizya kale abeenzinyina. = Wherever she stays, there you hear she is already in conflict with her friends.

be busy, be distressed, *Ndagwitingana* nkaambo ndamvwa kuti Muleya walicisa. = I was distressed because I heard that Muleya hurt himself. Nenciswa boobu, Mwiinga nguugwintingana kuyandaula misamu. = When I am sick like this, it is Mwiinga who is running around looking for medicines. Bakatalika

lufwu. = They began to be entirely caught up with the matter of the death. (1.-gwitinganwa, 2.-gwitinganide, 3.-gwitinganya, 4.-gwitinganina, 5.-gwitinganinalyo, 6.-gwitinganisya, 7.gwitingana-gwitingana, 8.-gwitinganinana) Also: -gubingana.
make busy, Banyina bakatalika kumugwitinganya mwanaabo kubabelekela mulimo wakujika. = The mother began to make her daughter busy in working for her in cooking.

upset, affect, disturb, Mwana wania wagwitizya nanda yoonse. = The child who defecated filled the whole house with a bad smell. Inombe zyazwa kukucela, munzi oonse zyaugwitizya nkozililila boombe. When the cows come back from grazing, the whole village is disturbed with their crying for the calves. Kufwumbwa mpaakkala ulamvwa wagwitizya kale abeenzinyina. = Wherever he sits you hear that he is already troubling his friends. (1.-gwitizyigwa, 2.-gwitizyide, 3.-gwitizya, 4.-gwitizyizya, 5.-gwitizyizyalyo, 6.-gwitilisya, 7.-gwitizya-gwitizya, 8.-gwitizyanya.)
grind, Kamugwiya tombwe kutegwa tufwebe. Grind the tobacco so that we snuff. (1.-gwiyigwa, 2.-gwiyide, 3.-gwizya, 4.-gwiyila, 5.-gwiyilalyo, 6.-gwiisya, 7.-gwiya-gwiya, 8.-gwiilana.) Also: -kwiya.
rake, (ety. English) Twajana basankwa bobile balahala mumbewu. We fund two boys raking in the garden.

feel free, Ndaliiba buya kubeleka mumuunda nkaambo kakuti kunyina ziluma naa ziyoosya. = I felt free working in the field because there is nothing which bites or causes fear. (1.-ibwa, 2.-ibide, 3.-ibizya, 4.-ibilila, 5.-ibililalyo, 7.-iba-iba)

fill up, Ndabona misozi yaiba-iba mumesaakwe. = I saw the tears filling his eyes. Weesyemuka akweesyemuka, ilimwi kwakaide kumwiiba-iba misozi mumeso. He sneezed and sneezed until the tears just filled his eyes. (1.-ibwa-ibwa, 2.-ibide-ibide, 3.-ibizyaibizya, 4.-ibila-ibila, 5.-ibilalyo -ibilalyo, 7.-iba-iba)
  • float on, Ikauka kaali kwiiba-iba atalaa meenda. The insect was floating on top of the water.

remember, recollect, Ndakazikwiibaluka anga baunka kale bayi, ncindakali kuyanda kubuzya. After the teacher had already gone, I remembered the thing which I wanted to ask. Watalika kwiibaluka akuliseka kuti ninonzi nzi zyakandeeta okuno. He remembered and laughed at himself saying what dream brought me here. (1.-ibalukwa, 2.-ibalukide, 3.-ibalusya, 4.-ibalukila, 5.-ibalukilalyo, 6.-ibalukisya, 7.-ibalukaibaluka, 8.-ibalukana) Also: -ibuluka
be reminded, Kuti muntu kafwambaana kuluba uleelede kwiibalulwa. If a person is quick to forget, he should be reminded. (2.-ibalwide, 7.-ibalulana) Also: -lubulwa.
rt. ibaluka, remind, cause to remember, rt. -ibaluka, Baama, kamubaibalusya bana baye kucikolo. = Mother, remind the children to go to school.

float, Inyabo nizyanyikwa mumeenda, zyakabola zyaibama. = When beans are steeped in water, the ones which have rotted, float to the surface. (2.-ibamide, 3.-ibamya, 4.-ibamina, 5.-ibaminalyo, 6.-ibamisya, 7.-ibamaibama) Also: -ibuka, -kapama.

float, Inswi yafwa inga yiile kwiibauka atalaa meenda. = The dead fish just floats on the water. (1.-ibaulwa, 2.-ibaukide, 3.-ibausya, 4.-ibaukila, 5.-ibaukilalyo, 6.-ibaukisya, 7.-ibauka-ibauka) Also: -cimbama,-impauka

float on surface, rt. -ibama, Niyakamana kuwa mvwula yakutaanguna, matu mayumu akaliibeme atalaa meenda. = When the first rains had fallen, the dry leaves were floating on the water. (2.-ibemede, 3.-ibemya, 4.-ibemena, 5.-ibemenalyo, 6.-ibemesya, 7.-ibemeibeme)

be pleased, Haamasumo wakaibililwa musobano wabbola, ncaakamuka kupiluka. Haamasumo was delighted with the football game, that is why he was late in returning. (1.-ibilizigwa, 2.-ibilidwe, 3.-ibilizya, 4.-ibililwa, 5.-ibililwalyo, 7.-ibililwa-ibililwa)
be pleased, Beenzuma baya baibilizigwa buyo kweebelezya kabwa nkokasotooka akunyiŋinya mucila. = My friends over there are delighted watching the puppy as he jumps and wags his tail.

be pleasing, Caibilizya cisobano, ncitwamukila kuboola kumunzi. = The play was pleasing, that is why we were late in coming home. Myaambo ya Chipwetenge yakamwiibilizya Dyabbula. = The saying of Chipwetenge stimulated Dyabbula.

come to the surface, as dead fish, Niyafwa nswi yakaibuka kumane twaibona akwiibweza. When the fish died it came to the surface and then we saw it and took it. Ukonzya kukondoola meenda kwiibusya citaka muzyiba mocilimo, pesi mocitamo tacikonzyi kwiibuka. = You can stir up the water to bring fish to the surface when they are there, but if they are not there they cannot come to the surface. Also: ibama. (2.-ibukide, 3.-ibuzya, 4.-ibukila, 5.-ibukilalyo, 6.-ibukisya, 7.-ibuka-ibuka)
  • gather as thick clouds, Kujulu kwakatalika kwiibuka makumbi aakasizya ansi mbuli mudima. The sky became covered with thick clouds which blackened the earth into darkness.

skim, collect what is floating, remove from surface, Twayiibula nswi nitwaibona. = We collected the floating fish when we saw it. Bantu bamwi balapukila musamu ukola nswi mumeenda. Inswi zilaibuka atala ameenda, balaziibula. = Some people rub leaves in their hands over the water which poisons the fish. The fish float on top of the water and they collect them. Bakaibula buyo bamunkwaze a magukusu, tunyenyene bakatuleka. = She removed the crikets and the cockroaches, she left the little black ants. (1.-ibulwa, 2.-ibulwide, 3.-ibuzya, 4.-ibulwida, 5.-ibulwidalyo, 6.-ibulisya, 7.-ibula-ibula) Also: -yibula.
  • raise part of face to show disapproval, Bacembele bakali kwiile kwiibula keebo kabo kulanga bantu bakalundene mbuli nombe zilwana. The old lady was just raising her jaw looking at the crowd of people who were rushing together like cows fighting.

recall, remember, Ndakaibuluka kuti kuli ncibakanditumide ku Monze. I remembered that there was something for which they had sent me to Monze. (1.-ibulukwa, 2.-ibulukide, 3.-ibuluzya, 4.-ibulukila, 5.-ibulukilalyo, 6.-ibulukisya, 7.-ibuluka-ibuluka, 8.-ibulukana) Also: -ibaluka.
  • float on surface, Busenga bulaibuluka atalaa meenda. The dregs are floating on top of the water. Also: -ibauka.

skim off, Buumba wakaibulula maumba kabotu-kabotu. = Buumba skimmed off the butter carefully. (1.-ibululwa, 2.-ibulwide, 3.-ibuluzya, 4.-ibulwida, 5.-ibulwaidalyo, 6.-ibulukisya, 7.-ibulula-ibulula) Also: -bataula, -pepaula, -yibulula.
be skimmed off, Maumba akali kwiibululwa kabotu-kabotu. = The butter from the sour milk was skimmed off carefully.

cause to remember, Wakabaibulusya muzeezo ngwaakaba-ambide kale. = He caused them to remember the idea which he had already told them. (1.-ibulusyigwa, 2.-ibulusyide, 4.-ibulusyizya, 5.-ibulusyizyalyo, 6.-ibulusyisya, 7.-ibulusya-ibulusya, 8.-ibulusyanya.) Also: -ibalusya.
  • remove from surface with something, Kobelesya nsefwa kwiibulusya masenga-senga aibuka mucibwantu. = Use a sieve to remove the material which is floating on top of the sweet beer. Also: -ibuluzya.
skim off with, Twakabelesya conco wacisamu kwiibuluzya mafwuta. = We used a wooden spoon to skim off the fat. (1.-ibuluzyigwa, 2.-ibuluzyizye, 4.-ibuluzyizya, 5.-ibuluzyizyalyo) Also: -ibulusya.

cause to come to surface, rt. -ibuka, Kukondoola meenda nkwi-ibusya citaka muzyiba mocilimo pesi mocitamo tacikonzyi kwiibuka. = To stir the water causes the fish to come to the surface when they are there, but when they are not there they cannot rise up. (1.-ibusyigwa, 2.-ibusyide, 3.-ibusyizya)

be burnt, Caida cisyu nitwali muciba katukanana. = The relish got burnt when we were in the kraal talking. (1.-idwa, 2.-idide, 3.-idya or idizya, 4.-idila, 5.-idilalyo, 6.-idisya, 7.-ida-ida, 8.-idilana) Also: -lungula.
  • water plants, irrigate, Nitwali kwiida, meenda azikumana. = When we were watering, the water got finished.
  • assist in pounding, Kamumwiida musozya mwana nkaambo ulaciswa. = Help the child in pounding the samp because she is sick.

pound together in mortar, rt. -ida, Twali kwiidana buya kutwa musozya. = We were pounding the samp together. (1.-idanwa, 2.-idanide, 3.-idanizya, 4.-idanina 5.-indainalyo, 6.-idanisya, 7.-idana-idana, 8.-idana)

be learned, Dwaantwa wakali-ide kasyoonto buyo nkaambo wakali kukonzya kubala akulilembela manwadi. = Dwaantwa was a just a little learned because he was able to read and write letters by himself. (1.-idwe)

irrigate for, rt. -ida, Citwiidila zisyango ciindi camainza nimvwula. = It is the rain which waters the crops during the rainy season. (1.-idilwa, 2.-idilide, 3.-idilizya, 4.-idililwa, 5.-idilalyo, 6.-idilisya, 7.-idila-idila, 8.-idana)

cause to burn, rt. -ida, Waciidizya cisyu naali kujika masikati. = The relish got burnt when she was cooking at midday.
  • water with, Ndali kwiidizya cigabba cisyoonto mumbewu. = I was watering with a small tin in the garden.
be told to, rt. -iya, Twa-ambo toonse twakali kucitika kaindi twakali kuyiiqwa amizyalano itobela. = All happenings which occurred in the past were related to the generations that followed.
be understandable, rt. -iya, Aaka kaambo kalaiika nkaambo ndakakamvwa nikakali kwaambwa. = This matter is undersandable because I followed it when it was being explained.

tell, relate, Mwanaangu wamuka kundiyiila kaambo nkaakacita jilo. = My child was slow to tell me what he did yesterday. Also: -yiila. (1.-iilwa, 2.-iide, 3.-iizya, 4.-iilila, 5.-iilalyo, 6.-iilisya, 7.-iila-iila, 8.-iilana)
  • remain after others have gone, *Ndakajisi basune banji, sunu kwakayiila bobilo.* = I had many oxen, today there remains two.
study hard, rt. *-iya,* *Kamuyiisisya mucikolo kutegwa mukazwidilile.* = Study hard in school so that you pass your exams. (1.-iisisyigwa, 2.-iisisyide, 4.-iisisyizya, 5.-iisisyalyo, 8.-iisisyanya)

cause to learn, teach, rt. *-iya,* *Ndakamuyiisya kulemba lugwalo mu Chikuwa.* = I taught him how to write a letter in English. (1.-iisyigwa, 2.-iisyide, 3.-iisyizya, 4.-iisyila, 5.-iisyilalyo, 6.-iisyisya, 7.-iisya-iisya, 8.-iisyanya.)

be left, *Nindakatiiwambe kaambo wakandikasya, ndakayiizya kuyeeyela mumoyo.* = When I was about to say something he stopped me, so I was just left reflecting about it in my heart. (1.-iizyigwa, 7.-iizya-iizya, 8.-iizyanya)
  • limit, end, *Kulima kamuyiizya waawa, ooku mutasiki.* = When ploughing just end here, do not reach over there.

relate, tell to another, instruct, rt. *-iya,* *Wakatalika kundiila mbwaakapenga.* = He began to tell me how he had suffered. *Munene ooyo wakali kuila bana bakwe ciindi camangolezya kwamana kulalila.* = That old man was instructing his children in the evening after supper. (1.-ilwa, 2.-ilide, 5.-ilalyo, 6.-ilisya, 7.-ila-ila, 8.-ilana)
  • affect, *Obu bulwazi bwako tiibwaila ali nduwe pe, banji bantu bamucisi omuno balabuciswa.* = This your disease does not only affect you, many people here in the country are suffering from it.

sleep without eating food, *Mazuba anzala bantu banji balailala.* = During the days of hunger many people sleep without food. *Mulumi wailala akaambo kabubaya bwangu.* = My husband slept without food because of my carelessness. *Cimwi ciindi muntu wakali kufwa masiku nkaambo kakwiilala lyoonse.* = Sometimes someone would die at night because of always going to bed without eating. (1.-ilalwa, 2.-ilalide, 4.-ilalila, 5.-ilalilalyo)

rise in mass, *Alange kujulu atala lyakwe, wakajana kwailamuka ambi makumbi.* = When he looked above himself, he found more clouds piling up. (1.-ilamukwa, 2.-ilamukide, 3.-ilamusya, 4.-ilamukila, 5.-ilamukilalyo, 6.-ilamukisya, 7.-ilamuka-ilamuka) Also: *-insamuka*

be scattered, *Makumbi akali kwiilauka kujwe akumbo cakunga mwezi wakacaala antangalala.* = The clouds were being scattered to the east and west so that the moon remained visible. (1.-ilaukwa, 2.-ilaukide, 3.-ilausya, 4.-ilaukila, 5.-ilaukilalyo, 6.-ilaukisya, 7.-ilauka-ilauka)

cause to sleep without food, rt. *-ilala,* *Mubwa naakabutya busu, wakabailazya bana bangu.* = When the dog spilt the mealie-meal, it caused my children to sleep without food. (1.-ilazyigwa, 2.-ilazyide, 4.-ilazyizya, 5.-ilazyizyalyo, 6.-ilazyizyizya, 7.-ilazya-ilazya, 8.-ilazyanya)
just, *Ndaile kucaala endikke mbubaunka kumuunda boonse.* = I just remained alone since they all have gone to the field. (2.-ide)

heap more things on, *Ndiyanda kwiilika zisani sunu nkaambo kuli mpeyo.* = I want to pile on the clothes today because it is cold. *Makani ngomukanana akumusempuzya mwananyokwe mwiilika makondo aambi atala ankondo eeyi yamusikila ciindi cino.* = The matter you talk about of the mocking of your friend adds more problems on top of the problem which has already affected him. (1.-ilikwa, 2.-ilikide, 3.-ilisya, 4.-ilikila 5.-ilikilalyo, 6.-ilikisya, 7.-ilika-ilika, 8.-ilikana)
  • be physically developed, put on weight, fully grown, Mwanaangu musimbi wakailika. = My daughter is putting on weight.
  • put additional charge, Mulandu ulungwa nombe zyone, bamakwaangu bailika imbi zyaba zyosanwe. = My in-laws added another cow to the fine of four cows to make it five.
be on top of another, Insilibi zilailikana nozeenda. = Soldier ants walk on top of one another when they move.

add something extra to, Kuli ncitwakapangene nitwakakkede muswaangano, ndakailikila cimbi. = I added something further to what we had agreed upon at the meeting. Kamumwiilikila ambi mapopwe musimbi mupati abweze. = Add some more maize for the big girl to carry. (1.-ilikilwa, 2.-ilikide, 3.-ilikizya, 4.-ilikila, 5.-ilikilalyo, 6.-ilikisya, 7.-ilikila-ilikila, 8.-ilikana)

put on extra clothes, Ooyu mwana ulaciyanda kwiilikizya zikobela nokunyina mpeyo. = This child likes to pile on extra clothes even when the cold is not there. Also: -yilikizya.
  • practice usury, Ncibi cakwiilikizya mali ngaatakakweleta. = It is bad to demand extra money on what has been borrowed.

move about, Bantu banji balikwiilingana mucibbadela. = Many people were moving about in the hospital. Mubbi wakailingana mbuli muntu ulomene. = The thief was moving around like an honest person. Wakajana kuti kumbo nkokwakali kwiilingana makumbi. = He found that it was to the west that the clouds were on the move. Waka-ilingana mutwanga kuyandaula zyakulya zyaandeene-andeene. = The servant moved around looking for different types of food. Nobwakaca ansi kucisiya-siya bantu bakailingana amasumo, tweembe azimwi buyo zilwanyo zyaandene-andeene. = When it was dawn but still dark people were moving around with spears and axes and other weapons of different kinds. (1.-ilingana, 2.-ilinganide, 3.-ilinganya, 4.-ilinganina, 5. -ilinganinalyo, 6.-ilinganisya, 7.-ilingana-ilingana)
be in a twisted state, rt. -ilingana, Nindamulanga kumeso wakaliilingene nkaambo wakaliyoowede. When I looked at his face he grimaced because he was afraid. =
roll the eyes, Sibbuku naakanyema, wakailinganya meso nkabela bantu bakayoowa. = When the headman was angry, he rolled his eyes and so the people were afraid. Also: -bangula.

increase, as a swelling Kuulu kwangu kwailinkana. = My leg has become more swollen. (1.-ilinkanwa, 2.-ilinkanide, 3.-ilinkanya, 4.-ilinkanina, 5.-ilinkaninalyo, 6.-ilinkanisya, 7.-ilinkanailinkana)
  • travel about, Toboneki kukkalikila nkaambo wiile kwiilinkana. = You do not seem to be settled, because you are just travelling about. Choombe ulailinkana nkaambo nombe zyakwe zyakabbigwa nsondo yakamana. Choombe travels about because his cattle were stolen last week. Also: -ilingana.

come up, Ijamba lyakailuka nilyakasika anyika njumu. = The plough came up when it reached hard ground. Also: - eluka. (1.-ilukwa, 2.-ilukide, 3.-ilusya, 4.-ilukila, 5.-ilukilalyo, 6.-ilukisya, 7.-iluka-iluka)
  • be in process of healing, Cilonda cangu cailuka. = My wound is healing. Also: -yiluka

raise up, Ilula jamba kutegwa basune baubaubilwe. = Raise the plough up so that it will be easy for the oxen. (1.-ilulwa, 2.-ilukide, 3.-ilusya, 4.-ilulila, 5.-ilulilalyo, 6.-ilulisya, 7.-ilula-ilula)

skim off, remove top part, Kamwiilulula nzinini mumukupa. = Skim off the flies from the milk. Kamwiilulula zintu zimwi mumootokala nkaambo walemenwa kapati. Take off some things from the vehicle because the weight is too heavy. Also: -inyuna
  • clip hair, Baama bakandiilulula masusu. My mother clipped my hair.

stop, Basune balaima nicapatila cilayi. = The oxen stop when the sledge gets stuck. (1.-imwa, 2.-imide, 3.-imya or-imikizya, 4.-imina, 5.-iminalyo, 6-iminsya, 7.-ima-ima, 8.-imana.)
  • refuse to give to, Wandiima cakuIya Moonga. Moonga has refused me food.
  • stand, Koima kumbele abasune baleke kweenda. Stand in front of the oxen so that they stop moving.
  • be pregnant, Sena muka Chiika waima sunu? Is the wife of Chiika pregnant? Kuzwa ciindi naakakwatwa asunu tanaima. From the time she was married she has not become pregnant.
  • grow well as maize in good soil, Oomu mumuunda mapopwe alaima kabotu. In this field the maize grows well.
  • punctuate with full-stop, Ubikke twakwiima, twakubuzya, twakugambwa, tukoto atweengo twakuyoyela, alimwi atwamajwi aatonkomene. = Insert fullstops,question-marks, exclamation marks, commas and colons for breathing, and quote-marks for direct speech. (Utabikki tuputizyo otu. Don't put these inverted commas.)
linger, hesitate, Kamuleka kwiima-ima nkaambo izuba lilaafwiifwi kubbila. Don't dilly-dally because the sun is near to setting. Also: -kokobela, -nonelela.

sing, Kamwiimba kutegwa bauma bbola bakulwaile. = Sing so that the footballers will be encouraged. (1.-imbwa, 2.-imbide, 3.-imbya, 4.-imbila, 5.-imbilalyo, 6.-imbisya, 7.-imba-imba, 8.-imbana.)
  • become stained or soiled, Cisani cituba cakaimba nkocitasanzigwi kwaciindi cilamfwu. = The white cloth was stained as it had not been washed for a long time.
  • rush matters, Tiibakali kuyanda kuciimba alubilo. She did not want to rush matters.
be sung easily, Eeci ciimbo cilaimbika nkaambo cilanjilana kabotu a muyuwa. This song can be sung easily because it fits in with the rhythm of the rattle.

be sung for, rt. -imba, Wakaimbilwa ziimbo zibotu muleli wacisi naakaliko ku Chikuni. Nice songs were sung for the president when he was at Chikuni. (2.-imbide, 3.-imbya, 4.-imbila, 5.-imbilalyo, 6.-imbisya, 7.-imbilwa-imbilwa, 8.-imba-imba)
  • be left alone, be lonely, Ndaimbilwa mucisi muno. = I am left alone in this world. Mudaala naakaimbilwa wakaita mwana Syaampeyo kuti bazikusobane limwi cisolo. When the old man was left alone he called the child Syaampeyo so that they would play a game of cisolo together. Also: -tontwedwa
leave one in solitude, Also: -lendelezya, -tontozya.

look with resentment, Uide kwiimbula meso akaambo kakunyema. = He just has a look of resentment on his face because of being angry. (1.-imbulwa, 2.-imbwide, 3.-imbuzya, 4.-imbwida, 5.-imbwidalyo, 6.-imbulisya, 7.-imbulaimbula, 8.-imbwidana)

repeat singing, rt. imba, Basicikolo bakaciimbulula ciimbo ziindi zinji nkaambo cakakonda bantu banji. = The pupils repeated the song many times because it pleased many people. (1.-*imbululwa*, 2.-*imbulwide*, 3.-*imbulu-zya*, 4.-*imbulwida*, 5.-*imbulwidalyo*, 6.-*imbululisya*, 7. *imbulula-imbulula*, 8.-*imbulwidana*)

be sung about, *Mutinta wakali mubotu cini-cini cakuti mbabasimbi bakategwa wiimbwa meenda kubota*. = Muntinta was truly beautiful and was one of those girls whom you would say the water sung her praises.

stop, *Kamumwiimika muntu ooyo, kuli nceyanda kwaamba anguwe*. = Stop that person, there is something I want to discuss with him. *Sibbuku kaambo wakakaimika akubaambila kuti kaya kubetekwa bwaakuca cifwumo-fwumo*. = The headman stopped the trial and told them that it would be judged at dawn in the morning. (1.-*imikwa*, 2.-*imikide*, 3.-*imikizya*, 4.-*imikizyizya*, 5.-*imikizyizyalyo*, 6.-*imikizyisya*, 7.-*imika-imika*, 8.-*imikizyanya*.)
  • show signs, *Kamutola mpongo kumunzi, imvwula yaimika*. = Take the goats home, the rain threatens. *Ooyu muunda ulaimika mapopwe kabotu*. = This field show signs of a good growth of maize.
  • make stand up, *Mwiiyi wakabaimika bana kumbele a Mwami Moonze*. = The teacher made the children stand up in front of Chief Monze.
  • *Kuzyala mwana nkwiimika*. = To give birth to a child is to be able to make it grow.
  • start, as a dance, *Nitwakasika ku Makamba twakajana makkwaya baayimika kale basimbi balazyana*. = When we arrived at Makamba we found that they had already started the makkwaya dance and the girls were dancing.

arise and stand, *Kamwiimikila twaanzye mwami wacuundu*. = Stand up so that we greet our chief. *Kamwiimikila, twiimbe Iwiimbo lwacisi*. = Stand, let us sing the national anthem. *Kamwiimikila mpoona awo*. = Stand right there. (1.-*imikilwa*, 2.-*imikilide*, 3.-*imikizya*, 4.-*imikilila*, 5.-*imikillilalyo*, 6.-*imikilisya*, 7.-*imikila-imikila*)

umbi* replace one by another, as a deceased wife by her sister, or a cow by another one, *Mwami naakafwa bakaimikizya umbi kufwambaana kutegwa alele cisi*. When the chief died they quickly replaced him with another to rule the country.
stand facing one another, *Bakaimikizyanya kuti balwane basankwa*. The boys stood facing one another so that they fight.

stood on, rt., *Umwi muntu naakanyema wakaimina atalaa cuulu akutukila matusi mabi*. = One man when he was angry stood on top of an ant-hill and cursed with bad insults. (1.-*imwa*, 2.-*imidwe*, 3.-*imya*, 4.-*iminwa*, 5.-*iminwalyo*)

stand for, represent, *Ndali kwiiminina mwana kucikolo mumu-swaangano wabazyali*. = I was representing a pupil at the school at a PTA meeting. *Bafwide balatwiiminina kuli Leza notumulomba kuti atupe mvwula*. = The dead represent us before God when we ask Him to give us rain. *Manyika amwi aayakutumina baayiminina ngaaya: Malawi, Zimbabwe, a Zambia. Kaunda nguuya-kwiiminina cisi cesu*. = Some of the countries who will send representatives are these: Malawi, Zimbabwe and Zambia. Kaunda will represent our country. (1.-*imininwa*, 2.-*iminide*, 3.-*iminizya*, 4.-*imininina*, 5.-*iminininalyo*, 6.-*imininisya*, 7.-*iminina-iminina*, 8.-*imininana*)
  • support, protect, Basazinyina bakamwiiminina Chimbwali mumapenzi akwe oonse. Relatives supported Chimbwali in all his troubles. Nikwatakaba kwiiminina kwa Leza, nikwaali kunga ulya mukaintu walicisa calufwu. If it wasn't for the protection of God, that woman would have fatally harmed herself.
  • act as sponsor in Christian ritual, Ncibotu kukkala munsi amuntu ngookaiminina mukupapatiswa. It is good to live near the person for whom you are acting as sponsor for baptism.
  • stand by or over, Mvwundyanga wakalota kuti syaazyana wajalula mulyango, wanjila kugobelo, wamwiiminina abulo. Mvwundyanga dreamt that the witch-dancer opened the door, entered the male quarters and stood over him by the bed (with evil intent).

make stand, Nobasimbi kamwiimizya basune bavwoleke kabotu basankwa. Girls, make the oxen stand so that the boys yoke them. (1.-imizyigwa, 2.-imide, 4.-imizyizya, 5.-imizyizyalyo, 6.-imikizyisya, 7.-imizyaimizya, 8.-imizyanya) Also: -imika.
miss, Bamasilikani bakamwiimpa buyo asyoonto. = The police missed him narrowly. (1.-impwa, 2.-impide, 3.-impya, 4.-impizyizya, 5.-impizyizyalyo, 6.-impisya, 7.-impa-impa, 8.-impana.)

pass without meeting, Twaimpana tiitwabonana nkaambo kanzila ziindene nzitwaletezya. = When we passed one another, we did not see one another because we had taken different paths. Kuzwa ceeco ciindi magwalo akali kwiimpana nkanzele-kanzele kusikila twaka-maninzya cikolo. From that time our letters were posted one after another until we finished school. (1.-impanwa, 2.-impanide, 3.-impanya, 4.impanina, 5.-impaninalyo, 6.-impanisya, 7.-impana-impana, 8.-impana)
  • disagree, Bakwetene bamwi balavwula kwiimpana munanda. Some married people frequently disagree with each other.
  • pass one another when going in different directions, Mutinta a Masowe baimpana mukalonga. = Mutinta and Masowe passed one another in the river when going in opposite directions.

reversing in opposite directions, Bataata nibakali kuyaka cisanza bakali kuziimpanya zisamu. = When my father was building a platfom he was reversing the poles in opposite directions. Also: -pimpanya.

float, Inswi ziile kwiimpauka atalaa meenda nkaambo zyakolwa ntimba. The fish are just floating on top of the water because they have been choked with mud. (1.-impaukwa, 2.-impaukide, 3.-impauzya, 4.-impaukila, 5.-impaukilalyo, 6.-impaukisya, 7.-impauka-impauka, 8.-impausyanya) Also: -ibauka, -cimbama.

lie down with head where feet ought to be, Wakaimpinikwa mukamufwu naakalazikwa amutumba wamulumi. The wife of the deceased was made to lie down with head at the feet of the corpse of her husband. (1.-impinikwa, 2.-impinikide, 3.-impinikizya, 4.-impinikizyizya, 5.-impinikizyizyalyo, 6.-impinikizyisya, 7.-impinikwaimpinikwa, 8.-impinikizyanya) Also: -pimpanya, -impanya.

wander around, Mutinta wali kwiimpita mudolopo. Mutinta was wandering around the city. (1.-impitwa, 2.-impitide, 3.-impitya, 4.-impitila, 5.-impitilalyo, 6.-impitisya, 7.-impitaimpita) Also: -ingaila, -empeta.
wandering about, Tandiyandi bantu baile kwiimpitika mumunzi wangu. = I do not want people just wandering around my village.

float about, Mitumba yabantu bafwide yakali kwiimpuuka muIwizi Iwa Kaliba. The corpses of dead people were floating about on Kariba lake. (1.-impuukwa, 2.-impuukide, 3.-impuusya, 4.-impuukila, 5.-impuukilalyo, 6.-impuukisya, 7.-impuuka-impuuka, 8.-impuukisyanya) Also: -impauka.

miss, make a mistake, Ndakaimpya buyo asyoonto kuti ndimubone mpaakayubide. I just barely missed seeing where she was hiding. Ndakaimpya buyo asyoonto kuti ndilanduke kuya mubbuku lyakkumi. = I only barely missed, by a few marks, from passing into Grade 10. Nindakali kubetekwa, ndakakaimpya kaambo. = When I was being tried, I missed the point. Kazyalanzubo wakali kwiimpya mumicito yakwe, pesi wakali mulome uusitikide. = Kazyalanzubo made mistakes in his actions, but he was honourable and just. (1.-impwa, 2.-impide, 4.-impizyizya, 5.-impizyizyalyo, 6.-impisya, 7.-impyaimpya, 8.-impana)
miss, Ndakamwiimpyizyide buti?. = How could I have missed her.

be in a standing position, rt. ima, Ndakajana bana bobilo baliimvwi mucimvwule. = I found two childen standing in the shade. Ntakakuboni kabili kamwiimvwi amusankwa ulya. = Let me not see you a second time standing with that boy. (1.-imwa, 2.-imide, 3.-imya, 4.-imina, 5.-iminalyo, 6.-imisya, 7.- imaima, 8.-imikizyanya)
  • stand with, Mwaimvwi ani? = Who were you standing with? (Idiomatic use: What relish are you using for the evening meal?)
  • be upright, Kazyalanzubo wakali muntu ulomenye uwakaimvwi nci kumuntu oonse. Kazyalanzubo was an honest person who was honest with every person.
delay, rt. -ima, Mwiiyi wakabaimya nsima basicikolo naakamuka kubaleka. Because the teacher cause the pupils to miss the food when he delayed them.

be tasty, be sweet, Nkukkisi zyakandipa mweenzuma zilaina. = The biscuits which my friend gave me were sweet. (2.-inide, 3.-inizya, 4.-inina, 5.-ininalyo, 6.-inisya, 7.-ina-ina) Also: -nona.
  • become healthy, recover weight, Munene wakakokede kapati akaambo kakuciswa, sunu waina akaambo kakulya kabotu. The old man who was thin due to illness, nowadays he has put on weight because of eating well.

ever be, ever do, (auxiliary verb -ina-), Tiindakainaibona mvwula ilaba bobuya. I had never seen the rain producing such lightning. Nokuba kuti kunyina ngucakainalwanide limwi, kuti walanga biyo majindi amaboko, inga walibonena ayebo kuti muntu oyu ulijisi nguzu zitaambiki. = Even though he had never fought, if you looked at the calves of his legs and his arms, you yourself could see that this man had indescribable energy.

move immodestly, Ulainauka mubantu mbuli muntu wasondoka. = She moves immodestly among the people like a mad one. Also: -inyauka. (1.-inaukwa, 2.-inaukide, 3.-inausya, 4.-inaukila, 5.-inaukilalyo, 6.-inaukisya, 7.-inauka-inauka, 8.-inaukizyanya)

pass, Nibakasunkidwe bana kucikolo, mwana angu bakamwiinda. = When the children were examined at school, they surpassed my child. Kamwiinda buyo, tabakwe kumuluma babwa. = Just pass through, the dogs will not bite you. (1.-indwa, 2.-indide, 3.-indya, 4.-indila, 5.-indilalyo, 6.-indisya, 7.-indainda, 8.-indana) Also: -yinda.
  • *bewitch*, Ooyu mwana baka-mwi

buya, ambweni ncazilaika boobu. = They just bewitched this child, perhaps that is why he looks stupid.
  • *die*, Bwane kubucedo wakainda. = On Friday morning he died..

*pass one another*, rt. -inda, Twakali kuya *kwiindana* awakali kumbele lyangu nindakali kuya ku Monze. = I and the one in front of me, were passing one another on the way to Monze.
  • *compete*, Bamakaintu balayanda
kusama. Women like to compete in how they dress.

*go to many places and people looking for treatment*, Bausyi bakaindauka munji ncaakapona. = His father went to many places looking for medicines that is why he became well. Nobakamana *kwiindauka* alimwi akupegwa micelo, bakaambilwa kuti kabatanooya *bwiinda* muminzi yabantu alimwi kabaya bulala musyokwe. When they had searched many places and had received medicines, they were told that they should not pass through villages of other people and that they should sleep in the bush on the way. Also: -syindauka.
  • *pass repeatedly in the same place*, rt. inda, Bana bakabalesya *kwiindauka* aakakkede bapati. They stopped the children from passing repeatedly where the elders were sitting.
*be subjected repeatedly to a charm*, Mulwazi *wakaindaukwa* ciindi cilamfwu ncaakapona. = The patient was given many different types of medicine that is why he recovered.

*be different, unequal*, rt. indana, Tobasankwa *tuliindene* abasimbi. = We boys are different from girls. Zina lyanguli *ciliindenye* alyaakalo. = The clan name is different from the public name. (3.-idanya, 4.-indanina, 5.-indaninalyo, 6.-idanisya, 7.-indene-indene)

*have passed by*, rt. -inda, Ono zuba lyakaindide kale acilangankumo, lyakali kuyanda kusika mpolilomba moombe. Now the sun had already passed over at midday, and was about to set. (1.-indidwe, 7.-indide-indide)
*passable, penetrable, crossable*, rt. -inda, Inzila eeyi *ilaindika* kuya kumuunda. This path to the field is passable. (1.-indikwa, 2.-indikide)

*pass on before*, rt. -inda, Kakamwiindila kusika kana kakwe. = His child arrived before him/her. Also: -beelela. (1.-indilwa, 2.-indilide, 3.-indilizya, 4.-indililila, 5.-indilililalyo, 6.-indilisya, 7.-indila-indila, 8.-indilana)
*compete*, Twali kwi
buya kuya kusika kumuunda. = We were competing as to who would reach the field first.

*pass by*, Waindilila kunanda akaambo kakulubila. She passed by the house because by mistake. (1.-indililwa, 2.-indilide, 3.-indilizya, 4.-indililila, 5.-indilililalyo, 6.-indilsya, 7.-indilila-indilila, 8. -indililana)
  • *increase*, Ooyu mulwazi caindilila kucisa sunu. This patient is suffering more today.
*be in the process of passing by*, Tandikkali, ndili mweenzu wiindilide. I am not staying, I am a visitor just passing by...

*be excessive, exaggerate*, Ulabwiindilizya busongo, ncobamwa amba bumpelenge. He is just too clever, that is why they say he is crooked. Joni ulaindilizya kunywa bukoko ncobumukola kufwambaana. = Joni drinks beer to excess that is why he gets drunk easily.
  • *give birth to still-born child*, Muka Chimuka wakaindilizya jilo, mwana wakali musankwa. = The wife of Chimuka gave birth to a still-born baby yesterday. The child was a boy.
  • pass through with something, Mutinta wakabwiindilizya bwizu, taakabusiya pe. = Mutinta passed through with the bundles of grass, he did not leave any behind.
be surpassed, Muunga wakaindilwa kukwata kumuce wakwe. = Muunga was left behind by his young brother as regards getting married. Also: -beelezegwa.

run from place to place, Wakaindingana kuyandaula mali nibaka-zwidilila bana bakwe mumisunko. = He ran from place to place looking for money when his children passed the exams. (1.-indinganwa, 2.-indigene, 3.-indinganya, 4.-indinganina, 5.-indinganinalyo, 6.-indinganusya, 7.-indingana-indingana, 8.-indinganana)
increase, rt. -inda, Wa-indizya kulunduka. = She increased speed in running. (1.-indwa, 2.-indide, 3.-indya, 4.-indila, 5.-indilalyo, 6.-indisya, 7.-indizya-indizya, 8.-indizyanya.) Also: -yindizya.

repeat, Kamuciindulula ciimbo eeci, candikonda kapati. = Repeat singing this song, it delights me. Kamwi-indulula kwaamba kaambo aaka, tiindamvwa kabotu. = Repeat this sentence, I did not understand it well. (1.-indululwa, 2.-indulwide, 3.-induluzya, 4.-indulwida, 5.-indulwidalyo, 6.-indululisya, 7.-indulula-indulula, 8.-indululana)

be passed over, be ommitted, rt. -inda, Ndakaindwa mbuli kuti tandizyibidwe anguwe. = I was passed over as if I am not known by him/her. Bamwi bana tabayandi kwiindwa mucikolo. = Some children do not want to be surpassed in class. (2.-indidwe)

stick in throat, Kamvwa kanswi kakandiinga amoyo = The bone of a fish stuck in my throat. Also: -tinga. (1.-ingwa, 2.-ingide, 3.-ingizya, 4.-ingila, 5.-ingilalyo, 6.-ingisya, 7.-inga-inga, 8.-ingana)
  • place across to bar entry or exit, Koinga cisamu amulyango wacaanda cangulube kutegwa zitazwi. Put a bar across the entrance of the pig sty so that they don't go out. Naakacimvwa kuteelela kaambo komwe, Mainza wakayeeya kuti nkubotu kuti amwiinge kumulomo mweenzinyina. When he got tired of listening to the one topic, Mainza thought it would be good to block the mouth of his friend. Also: -pinga.
  • throw at an object in motion, Kwale naakauluka ndakamwiinga nkoli akumu-uma. = When the partridge flew, I threw a stick and struck it.
  • insert a stick or bone, Kamumwiinga cisamu moombe mumpemo kutegwa afwambaane kuleka kunyonka. = Insert a stick in the nose of the calf so that it quickly stops sucking.
  • cross arms on head, Bantu nobalila baliinga maboko amutwe kutondezya kuusa. When people lament they cross their arms on their heads showing sorrow.
  • disturb, Bwandiinga busiku. = The night disturbs me.
  • go across in front of, Mukutobela banyama bakabainga kuzwa kulubazu kwakali kutozya muwo. In following the animals they went across in front of them in the direction in which the wind was blowing.

wander about confused or lost, Wiide kwiingaila kwabula kwakukkala. = He is just wandering about with no place to live. (1.-ingailwa, 2.-ingailide, 3.-ingaizya, 4.-ingailila, 5.-ingaililalyo, 6.-ingailisya, 7.-ingaila-ingaila) Also: -impita, -ungulika, -ingayila.
move about with, Koonse nkoolanga aumwi wakali kwiingaizya buyo zituli zyanyama mumaanza. = Wherever you looked everyone was just going about with pieces of meat in their hands.

go across, Ndayoowa nindabona inzoka *yaingana* mumugwagwa. = I was afraid when I saw a snake going across the road. Isamu lyakaimvwi munsi akalonga lyakawa lyaingana atala akalonga. = The big tree which was standing beside the stream fell across the stream. (1.-inganwa, 2.-ingenye, 3.-inganya, 4.-inganina, 5.-inganinalyo, 6.-inganisya, 7.-ingana-ingana, 8.-inganyizyanya)
  • go around, Eeci *ncoingana* abamuka bantu ulaliletela mapenzi. = You will bring yourself problems through this habit you have of going around with other people's wives.

disturb, Ncibi kumwiinganina mwana, ulasobana. = It is bad to disturb the child, it is playing. Kuti koinganina nzoka, ilakuluma. If you disturb the snake, it will bite you. (1.-inganinwa, 2.-inganide)
  • interrupt rudely, Ncili ono aawa *ciinganinwa*? Sena mbwaatabuzigwa nguwe? = What kind of interruption is this? Is it because she was not the one who was asked?

put one thing across another, Mukaintu wangu wandiinganya akaambo kakuyanda kapati zyuulwa-ulwa. = My wife has upset my plans because of her addiction for buying things. (1.-inganyizyigwa, 2.-ingenye, 4.-inganizyizya, 5.-inganizyizyalyo 6.-inganyizyisya, 7.-inganya-inganya)

be totally committed, Ulaingasila kuya kucibbadela. = He is utterly determined to go to hospital. Mebo ndi-ingasila buyo kuya kukulya. = For myself I have just concentrated on going to eat. Also: -yingasila. (1.-ingasilwa, 2.-ingasilide, 3.-ingasizya, 4.-ingasilila, 5.-ingasililalyo, 6.-ingasilisya, 7.-ingasila-ingasila, 8.-ingasilana)

use to support, Kondipa nkoli eeyo ndayanda kwiingatizya mukuli ngweyumwide. = Give me that walking stick so that I use it to help me support the load I am carrying. (*kuliingatizya* = support a load on the shoulders by using a stick as lever.) (1.-ingatizyigwa,2.-ingatizyide, 4.-ingatizyizya, 5.-ingatizyizyalyo, 6.-ingatizyisya, 7.-ingatizya-ingatizya, 8.-ingatizyanya)

wander aimlessly, Mbanji bantu baingauka kuyandaula cakulya ciindi canzala. = There are many people who wander about looking for food during a time of famine. (1.-ingaukwa, 2.-ingaukide 3.-ingauzya, 4.-ingaukila, 5.-ingaukilalyo, 6.-ingaukisya, 7.-ingauka-ingauka) Also: -inguuka.

wander about, Sunu uide kuingayila, tanabona mulimo umbi. = Today he is just wandering about, he has not found alternative work. (1.-ingayilwa, 2.-ingayilide, 3.-ingayizya, 4.-ingayilila, 5.-ingayililalyo, 6.-ingayilisya, 7.-ingayilaingayila) Also: -ingaila

be busy, Bantu bakaingene buyo kuunka kumiswaangano nkobakali kuvwola zintu. = The people were just busy going to meetings where they were given hand-outs. (3.-inganya, 4.-inganina, 5.-inganinalyo, 6.-inganisya, 7.-ingana-ingana)
  • be promiscuous, Wakalijisi kanswende alo tacinyandyi nkaambo wakaliingene kubasankwa naakacili ku Lusaka. = She had a sexual infection and it was not suprising as she was quite promiscuous when he was in Lusaka.
cross Nguwena Bbandama nguwakaingenye zisamu zyobilo. = The same Bbandama crossed two sticks.

have arms crossed over head as sign of sorrow or pain, rt. -inga, Wakabona Milimo ulazemba kumwi uliingide amutwe. = He saw Milimo going up and down in grief while clasping his hands over his head. (1.-ingidwe, 3.-ingizya, 4.-ingililila, 5.-ingililayo, 6.-ingilisya)

block for, rt, -inga, Kondiingila cisamu ciyumu amulyango waciba canombe. = Block for me the entrance of the cattle krall with a strong pole. (1.-ingilwa, 2.-ingilide, 3.-ingizya, 4.-ingilila, 5.-ingililalyo, 6.-ingilisya)

block, as a escaping animal, cut off, Musune naakali kutija, musankwa wakafwambaana kumwiingilila. = When the ox was running away, the boy quickly ran ahead of it to block it. Ime ndakati, "Wakali kukwaanzya.........." Kalo kakandiingilila nsetanaakumanizya ategwa, "Ni?" = "You were being greeted by................." But she cut me off before I could finish, saying, "Who?" (1.-ingililwa, 2.-ingilide, 3.-ingilizya, 4.-ingililila, 5.-ingililayo, 6. -ingilizya)
be blocked, rt. -inga, e.g Musune wakakaka kwiingililwa. = The ox refused to be blocked. Also: -ingilwa.

be blocked, rt. -inga, Ndakaingilwa abantu bakalikuyanda kundijaya ncindatakasika nkwindakali kuya. = I was blocked by people who wanted to kill me, that is why I did not reach my destination. Also: -ingililwa.
  • be left alone, Ndaingilwa. = I am left alone. Also: -lendelelwa

cause to block, rt. -inga, Sinkondoma wakandiingizya bantu bajaya kutegwa nditakasiki nkwindakali kuya. = My enemy organized killers to block me so that I would not reach where I was going.
  • block with, rt. -inga, Ndakaingizya munsi acijazyo kutegwa citajaluki. = I blocked the door with the pestle so that it would not open.
  • leave one alone, Utanikundiingizyi. = Never leave me alone.

reply, Ndakali kulemba magwalo manji-manji, walo tainguli akwiingula. = I was writing very many letters, but she did not reply at all. Ndime, ngoingula boobo, ndeuso! = I, the one you answer in this manner, am your father! (1.-ingulwa, 2.-ingwide, 3.-inguzya, 4.-ingwida, 5.-ingwidalyo, 6.-ingulisya, 7.-ingula-ingula, 8.-ingulana)
  • respond to a song, Mwaanguzi naakali kwaangula ziimbo, twakali kufwambaana kumwiinqula. = When the song-leader was initiating the songs we were quick to respond.

wander as one lost, Muntu ugaukide ulainguuka mudolopo. = The mad person was wandering around the city. (1.-inguukwa, 2.-inguukide, 3.-inguuzya, 4.-inguukila, 5.-inguukilalyo, 6.-inguukisya, 7.-inguuka-inguuka) Also: -ingauka.

be in trouble, Ndakaingwa mapenzi manji kapati cakuti akulya koonse cakalikuyanda kundaalila. = I was plagued with many sufferings so that I almost gave up eating any food. (2.-ingide, 3.-ingizya, 4.-ingila, 5.-ingilalyo, 6.-ingilisya, 7.-ingwa-ingwa)
  • lodge in, stick in, Mwana waingwa kafwuwa kanswi akameneno. = A little fish bone stuck in the child's throat.

be interesting, delightful, rt. ina, Ncobeni uulya munene kutakatala kukanana, pesi nzyaamba zilaininizya. = Truly that old man does not tire talking, but what he says is very stimulating. Izuba lyakali kubala cakwiinininzya. = The sun was shining pleasantly. (1.-ininizyigwa, 2.-ininizyide, 4.-ininizyila, 5.-ininizyilalyo, 6.-ininizyisya, 7.-ininizya-ininizya, 8.-ininizyanya)
be pleased with, Mutinta wakali kwiininwa twaambo twamusyobo oyu. Mutinta was pleased with topics like this. Also: -nonenwa, -botelwa

go away, Ambeyo ndayanda kwiinka anywebo kukuzyana ciņande. = I also want to go with you and dance the ciņande. (1.-inkwa, 2.-inkide, 3.-inkizya, 4.-inkila, 5.-inkilalyo, 6.-inkisya, 7.-inkainka) Also: -unka.
drown, Wakainkila mukalonga ka Magoye. She drowned in the river Magoye. (2.-inkilide, 3.-inkizya, 4.-inkilila, 5.-inkililalyo, 6.-inkilisya, 7.-inkila-inkila, 8.-inkilana)

rising together, Makumbi manji akali kwiinsamuka kuzwa kujwe. Many clouds were rising together coming from the east. Nitwaka-tanta amulundu wa Kazyalila twakabona kwainsamuka ambi malundu kujwe. = When we climbed Kazyalila hill we saw other hills rising from the east. (2.-insamukide, 3.-insamuzya, 4.-insamukila, 5.-insamukilalyo, 6.-insamukisya, 7.-insamuka-insamuka) Also: -intamuka.

moving up and down, passing by, Wakalibabwene bantu nkobakali kwiinsauka mumugwagwa wakali munsimunsi ananda yakwe mudolopo. = He saw people passing by on the road beside his house in the city. Bantu bakali kwiinsauka biyo kuzyana nanda yoonse. = The people were just moving around the whole room as they danced. Naakoongolola munene, bantu bakali kwiinsauka mumazila bakaima boonse cakunyandwa. = When the old man shouted, the people who were passing by in the streets stopped in surprise. (1.-insaukwa, 2.-insaukide, 3.-insauzya, 4.-insaukila, 5.-insaukilalyo, 6.-indaukisya, 7.-insauka-insauka)

cause to be taken away or to disappear, Tokonzyi kutola baama batubya susu mutala amulonga, uyoobainsya mulonga. You cannot take my white-haired mother across to the other side of the river, you will cause the river to take her away. (1.-insyigwa, 2.-insyizye, 4.-insyizyizya, 5.-insyizyizyalyo, 6.-insyisya, 7.-insya-insya, 8.-insyanya.) Also: -unkizya.

appear, as of many things, Nitwakasika atalaa kalundu kafwiifwi, twakabona yaintamuka imbi milundu kumbele. = When we reached the top of the little hill, we saw other hills appearing ahead. Bwaintamuka kumeso akwe buzumi bwakwe bwakainda. = His life of the past appeared before his eyes. Also: -insamuka. (1.-intamukwa, 2.-intamukide, 3.-intamuzya, 4.-intamukila, 5.-intamukilalyo, 6.-intamukisya, 7.-intamuka-intamuka, 8.-intamukana)
  • look up, Kointamuka mooye, tukubone kabotu kumeso. = Girl, look up so that we see you clearly in the face.

look up, Wakasintama akulanga mutunta wamweenzinyina. Mbwaakaintamukila buyo aawo, wakatalika kutijaana kutozya kumunzi. = He looked down at the corpse of his friend. As soon as he looked up he began to run towards his home.

cause to turn one's face upwards, Kamumwiintamuna tumubone kubusyu mbwabede. Turn the face upwards so that we see how her face is. (1.-intamunwa, 2.-intamwide, 3.-intamuzya, 4.-intamwida, 5.-intamwidalyo, 6.-intamunisya, 7.-intamuna-intamuna, 8.-intamunana) Al;so -sintamuna

give into sexual craving, rt. intila, Twakali kubabona aswebo basankwa abasimbi bakaintide mazuba ngutwakakomena, tiibakajisi mibili mibotu. = We ourselves saw boys and girls who were carried away with lust when we were growing up, they did not have healthy bodies. (1.-intidwe, 3.-intizya, 4.-intilila, 5.-intililalyo, 6.-intilisya, 7.-intilaintila, 8.-intizyanya)

be startled, confused, *Ndaintila nindabona bantu banji kabazyaa kulunduka kuli ndime.* = I was alarmed when I saw many people running towards me. *Ndaintila nindabona nombe zinji, kumamanino ndaile kuula ifwulukide.* = I was confused when I saw many cattle, as a result I just bought a thin one.
  • be spoilt, *Bana baintila akaambo kabukoko mbobaulisyila munsi-munsi amunzi.* = The children are ruined because of the beer they are selling near the village.
  • be careful and slow, be cautious, *Syuumbwa nombe uziluma ciindi mucende naona, kuti mucende kalanga, taintili kukuvwampila kanamani.* = The lion attacks the cattle when the bull is asleep, if the bull is awake, he is cautious in attacking the grazing animal.
  • have sexual desire for, *Kuti waintila kubasimbi, ulaciswa bulwazi bwasikalileke.* = If you play around sexually with girls, you will become sick of HIV/AIDS.

excite, cause to be startled or confused, worry, rt. -intila, *Babbi bandiintizya nibatalika kundizwanganya.* = The thieves alarmed me when they started quarreling with me.
  • cause to be spoilt, *Bukoko mbobwabaintizya bana aba.* = Beer is what has spoiled these children.

eat plentifully, *Twakaumuna kwakaindi katwiile kwiinyauna makusu ansima.* = We were quiet for a while just eating plenty of nsima. (1.-inyaunwa, 2.-inyaunide, 3.-inyaunzya, 4.-inyaunizyila, 5.-inyaunizyilalyo, 6.-inyaunisya, 7.-inyauna-inyauna)

show immoral behaviour, *Musimbi utalomenye ulainyauka akati kabasankwa.* A disrespectful girl be-haves immoraly among men. (1.-inyaukwa, 2.-inyaukide, 3.-inyauzya, 4.-inyaukila, 5.-inyaukilalyo, 6.-inyaukisya, 7.-inyauka-inyauka, 8.-inyaukilana) Also: -inauka.

spring, as trap, *Mweeto wakainyuka inziba niyakacegwa.* The trapping-stick sprung up when the dove was caught. (1.-inyukwa, 2,-inyukide, 3.-inyuzya, 4.-inyukila, 5.-inyukilalyo, 6.-inyukisya, 7.-inyuka-inyuka, 8.-inyukilana) Also: -lebuka.
  • lift vigourously, *Musankwa naakanyema wakainyuka akuyumuna ibbwe pati.* When the boy became angry he lifted the big stone with strength. Also: -enyuka.

lift up, help one to lift a load on head, adjust someone's load, lift a big stone on its side, *Wakainyuna maanza kuuma mweenzinyina amunsi ngwaakajisi.* She lifted up the pestle which she had in her hands to beat her friend. (1.-inyunwa, 2.-inyunide, 3.-inyunizya, 4.-inyunina, 5.-inyuninalyo, 6.-inyunisya, 7.-inyuna-inyuna, 8.-inyunana)

reflect quietly on deep matters, *Ndamujana alya wali kuliinza zyakaambwa jilo amabeta.* I found him there quietly recalling what had been said at the court. *Bakaintu bamwi bakaswena munsimunsi lyakwe Mutinta, baliinza boonse zii kwaciindi cili mbocibede kuti bateelele majwi ngataambe.* = Some women drew near to Mutinta, quietly awaiting for a while so that they would hear what words she would say. (1.-inzwa, 2.-inzide, 3.-inzilizya, 4.-inzilila, 5.-inzililalyo, 6.-inzisya, 7.-inza-inza, 8.-inzana)
  • be in a quiet state, can be used in a greeting, *"Balainza nkumwazyila."* "Balainza." = "Are they at peace where you came from?" "They are at peace."
be in a calm state, rt. -inza, Uliliinzide ino mbwaamana kukandaulwa. = She is in a calm state after having been beaten.
be at rest, Meso akwe akali *kwiinzikide*. = His eyes were untroubled. (1.-inzikidwe)
be quite, as water, Waile
mbuli meenda abatama amusika. = She is as quiet as water which has been strained from ashes. Also: -zinzibala, -zinzimana.

check, inspect, *Kamuciinzila* cisyu mumbewu naa cili kabotu. = Inspect the vegetables in the garden to see if they are good. (1.-inzilwa, 2.-inzilide, 3.-inzilizya 4.-inzilizyizya, 5.-inzilizyizyalyo, 6.-inzilisya, 7.-inzila-inzila, 8.-inzilana) Also: -yunzila, -lingula.

miss taking something, Kainzya kujata kayuni nkaanga noole. = The wild cat missed catching the little bird. (1.-inzyigwa, 2.-inzyide, 3.-inzyisya, 4.-inzyila, 5.-inzyilalyo, 6.-inzyisya, 7.-inzya-inzya, 8.-inzyanya)
  • cause to pass, *Ino mbaani bainzya nombe masiku?* = Who were driving the cattle through at night? *Mbwaayumukila biyo nkuliinzya-inzya munsaa cibiya kutegwa cisani catombe cinjile muli cakulya.* = As he just got up he made himself pass beside the pot on purpose so that his dirty garment entered into the food.
  • finish off, *Atuciinzye-inzye cimane.* = Let us finish it off so that it is ended.
  • sleep once with a woman after her husband's death; abuse wife in lending her to sleep with another man, *Ncibi kumwiinzyanya mukaintu wako.* = It is bad to lend your wife to another man.
call, *Kamumwiita aboole kuno.* = Call him so that he comes here. V - 208 (1.-itwa, 2.-itide, 3.-itya, 4.-itila, 5.-itilalyo, 6.-itisya, 7.-ita-ita, 8.-itana)
call, rt. -ita, Ngu Maliko wandiitide. = It was Maliko who called me.
easy to call, rt. -ita, Izina lyamudaala lilaitika. = It is easy to say the name of that old man (2.-itikide)
call for, Kamufwambaana kundiitila musilisi. = Be quick to call the doctor for me. (1.-itilwa, 2.-itilide, 3.-itilizya, 4.-itilila, 5.-itililalyo, 6.-itilisya, 7.-itila-itila, 8.-itilana)
call by name, Mebo zina lyangu ndime Mutinta, pesi bana bakali kundiitizya lya Chikuwa lya Kkosimasi. = My name is Mutinta, but the children were calling me by the English name Cosmas.

learn, be educated, Ncibotu kwiiya musyobo wabantu mboswaya mucisi. = It is good to learn the language of the people whose country you visit. Ooyu musankwa uyeeya kuti tobazyali taku ncotuzyi nkaambo tiitwakaiya kucikolo. = This boy thinks that we parents know nothing because we did not learn at school. (1.-isyigwa, 2.-iide/-iyiide, 3.-iisya, /-yiisya, 4.-iyiila, 5.-iyiilalyo, 6.-iyiisya, 7.-iya-iya, 8-iyana.)
  • imitate, learn from, Iya sikwaze. = Learn from the fish-eagle.
  • tell, relate, "Mapenzaangu nsekonzyi kwaaiya oonse." = "I cannot relate all my sufferings."
tell to, Ndakavwiila ndakati, "Mapenzi nzi ngomwakapenga nobacembele, amutuiyile?" = I answered saying, "What pains did you suffer from, old lady, tell us about them." (1.-iyilwa)

pass the time chatting, chat after supper, Sunu twamuka koona nkaambo twali kukwiizya. = Today we went to sleep late because we were chatting. (1.-izyigwa, 2.-izyide, 3.-izyizya, 4.-izyila, 5.-izyilalyo, 6.-izyisya, 7.-izya-izya, 8.-izyana.)
ooze as fat from meat when being roasted, *Nyama ilajajama acikko.* = The meat is oozing fat on the fire place. Also: -cacama.

raise a heavy thing, jack up, *Kujakula cintu cilemu nkunyamwida antoomwe.* = To raise a heavy thing is to lift it together. (1.-jakulwa, 2.-jakwide, 3.-jakuzya, 4.-jakwida, 5.-jakwidalyo, 6.-jakulisya, 7.-jakula-jakula, 8.-jakulana) Also: -nyamuna, -dadula.

close, *Kamujala kumulyango batanjili babwa munanda.* = Close the door so that the dogs do not enter the house. (1.-jalwa, 2.-jalide or -jede, 3.-jazya or jalizya, 4.-jalila, 5.-jalilalyo, 6.-jalisya, 7.-jala-jala, 8.-jalilana.)

lock in, confine, shut in, block, *Basankwa bajalila nombe muciba.* = The boys locked the cattle into the kraal. *Kamubajalila babwa, balaluma bantu ba-tiiboole.* = Lock in the dogs, they will attack the people who will be coming. (1.-jalilwa, 2.-jalide, 3.-jalizya, 4.-jalilila, 5.-jalililalyo, 6.-jalilisya, 7.-jalila-jalila, 8.-jalililana)

open, *Bacembele bakajalula mulyango kuti munene anjile.* = The old woman opened the door for the old man to enter. (1.-jalulwa, 2.-jaludwe, 3.-jaluzya, 4.-jalwida, 5.-jalwidalyo, 6.-jalulisya, 7.-jalula-jalula, 8.-jalwidana.) Also: -jula, -yula.

open for, rt. -jalula, *Bakamujalwida, bakamuleka, wakaunka kucisi cakwe ulaangulukide.* = They released him, they let him go, he went to his country having been freed. *Undijalwide kagabba aka, njanda kulya nswi.* = Open this tin for me, I want to eat fish. *Mweenzu naakakonkomona, Muntinta nguwakaunka kumujalwida.* = When the visitor knocked on the door, it was Mutinta who went to open it for her.

find, *Ndakamujana mwana ngwindakali kuyandaula.* = I found the child for whom I was searching. *Bazyali baleelede kujana mali manji aabasicikolo.* = Parents have to find a lot of money for school children. (1.-janwa, 2.-janide, 3.-janizya / -janya, 4.-janina, 5.-janinalyo, 6.-janisya, -7.-jana-jana, 8.-janana)

stamp hard maize, *Ndakajana bamacembele bajanda mapopwe.* = I found old women stamping the maize. (1.-jandwa, 2.-jandide, 3.-jandizya, 4.-jandila, 5.-jandilalyo, 6.-jandisya, 7.-janda-janda, 8.-jandana) Also: -ganda. tramp, *Mbutwabula moota wakutanta, katujanda buyo amaulu tuya kusika naaba masiku.* = Since we have no vehicle to get into, let us just tramp along even though we reach at night. Also -ganta

be found, rt. -jana, *Ndakajanika kumunzi lyakasika beenzu kumuunda.* = I was found at home when the visitors arrived at the field. *Ankolola kwakajanika mali manji kapati.* = A great amount of money was found at the initiation ceremony. (1.-janikwa, 2.-janikide, 3.-janisya, 4.-janina, 5.-janinalyo, 6.-janikisya, 7.-janika-janika, 8.-janikizyanya)

find one in the act of, rt. -jana, *Ndamujanikizya katukila bacembele.* = I found him insulting the old lady. (1.-janikizyigwa, 2.-janikizyizye, 3.-janikisyisya, 4.-janikizyizya, 5.-janikizyizyalyo, 7.-janikizya-janikizya, 8.-janikizyanya)
find one another out, rt. -jana, *Basankwa bakajanikizyanya ibasyabide musimbi omwe.* = The boys discovered each other at the same place as lovers of the same girl.

walk majestically, *Twajana basankwa bobile baile kujankaila kweenda mbuli kuti mbavwubi.* = We found two boys walking majestically as if they were rich people. (1.-jankailwa, 2.-jankailide, 3.-jankaizya, 4.-jankailila, 5.-jankaililalyo, 6.-jankailisya, 7.-jankailajankaila) Also: -cankaila.

stand erect, Kwajankamana tukolo kubee mBadenda. = The small breasts were standing erect as if she was of the Badenda clan. Mudaala naakamubuzya musimbi wakaile kujankamana, mulomo mbuwali kwaasama, maanza mbwaali kukwazamikwa mumabalibali. When the old man asked the girl, she stood erect, her mouth open, her hands spread wide at her sides. (1.-jankamanwa, 2.-jankamenye, 3.-jankamika, 4.-jankamanina, 5.-jankamaninalyo, 6.-jankamanisya, 7.-jankamana-jankamana, 8.-jankamaninana)

hold, catch, arrest, Kamumujata mumulete kuno abuzigwe ncatija. = Catch him and bring him here so that he can be asked why he is running away. Mubbi bakamujata jilo. = They arrested the thief yesterday. Nibakamvwa makani aaya, balombwana boonse bakalijata buyo kumulomo. = When they heard this news all the men just caught themselves on the mouth. (i.e. they were rendered silent with the shock.) (1.-jatwa, 2.-jisi, 3.-jatizya or -jatya, 4.-jatila, 5.-jatilalyo, 6.-jatisya, 7.-jata-jata, 8.-jatana.)
  • be busy, Ndajata bubi. = I am busy. Also: -pakasya.
  • control oneself, Kulijata kwaambaula cicesya bunjaka. = Controlling speech avoids squabbling.
  • abuse a child sexually, Ooyo wakajata mwana wakabikkwa muntolongo. = That one who abused a child was put in prison. Also: -sampa
hold or grasp one another, Ijilo bantu banji bakajatana mumaanza kutondezya luumuno mucikombelo. Yesterday many people shook hands with one another as a sign of peace in the church.

catch, hold or feel continually, rt. -jata, Koleka kujatauka mubwa, ulakuluma. Stop catching the dog repeatedly, it will bite you. Mulozi wakali kujatauka bana masiku. The witch was touching the children at night. Kujatauka ulakonzya kundijatauka pesi makani ankwela nseyandi akaniini pe. = You can hold me alright but as regards sex I do not want anything to do with it. (1.-jataukwa, 2.-jataukide, 3.-jataukizya, 4.-jataukila, 5.-jataukilalyo, 6.-jataukisya, 7.-jatauka-jatauka, 8.-jataukana) Also: -ampaampa, -yayaanga.

be caught up in some activity, Banyina bakali kujatikene kuzela. His mother was occupied in basket-fishing. (1.-jatikanwa, 3.-jatikanya, 4.-jatikanina, 5.-jatikaninalyo, 6.-jatikisya, 7.-jatikana-jatikana)

concern, involve, rt. -jata, Bakaintu nobakabona kuti makani taabajatikizyi, bakazwa anze. When the women saw that the discussion did not concern them, they went outside. (1.-jatikizyigwa, 2.-jatikizyizye, 4.-jatikizyizya, 5.-jatikizyizyalyo, 6.-jatikizyisya, 7.-jatikizya-jatikizya, 8.-jatikizyanya)
  • change of action while doing something else, "Boola muopesi lyangu tuvwiye," wakaamba mudaala oyu kumwi kajatikizya akujokela. = "Come to my office so that we talk privately", said the old man while turning back to the office.

reach climax, Cizyano cajatila kubucedo lyabuka bamacembele. = The dance reached its climax at dawn, the time when the old women got up and joined it. (1.-jatilwa, 2.-jatilide, 3.-jatilizya, 4.-jatililila, 5.-jatilililalyo, 6.-jatililisya, 7. -jatilila-jatilila, 8. jatililana)
  • forgive, Kondijatila, tiindacita caali. = Forgive me, I did not do it deliberately.
  • keep for, hold for, Komujatila mali mwana ataasowi. = Keep the money for the child so that he does not lose it.

become attached to, rt. -jata, Kakkoma wajatilila mudolopo, kumunzi takuyandi pe. = Kakkoma has got attached to the city, he doesn't like village life.
  • hold on to firmly, Mwana kajatilila acuuno canamutendele kutegwa atawi. = Let the child hold on firmly to the saddle of the bicycle so that s/he does not fall off. Also: -siminina.
  • cling to, Buci bulajatilila kuminwe. = Honey sticks to the fingers. Also: -lamatila.
  • stand in the place of, Ba Muuka bajatilila buyo cibaka cabapati bacikolo bali kukulyookezya. = Mr. Muuka is just acting for the head of the school who is on leave.

hold tightly, rt. jata, Kamumujatisya mulwazi atawi. = Hold the patient firmly so that s/he does not fall. (1.-jatwa, 2.-jatide, 3.-jatizya, 4.-jatila, 5.-jatilalyo, 6.-jatisya, 7. -jata-jata, 8.-jatana)

kill, Musamu ukola wakajaya banyama banji. = The toxic medicine killed many animals. (1.-jayigwa, 2.-jayide, 3.-jazya or -jayizya, 4.-jayila, 5.-jayilalyo, 6.-jayisya, 7.-jaya-jaya, 8. -jayana.)
  • break, Kujaya nsuwa mbuteezi. = To break a milk-gourd is an accident.
be in a state of being killed or finished or devastated, Nzala yakalimujayide. The hunger was killing him. (1.-jayidwe, 3. -jayizya)

cause to kill, rt. -jaya, Milandu yesu njiyakajazya Jesu. = It is our sins which caused Jesus to die.
  • use to close, Bantu bakaindi bakali kujazya zitendele zyamakuba. = The people of long ago were closing their entrances with doors made of maize stalks.
keep in a state of being closed, rt. jala, Kojede kumulyango kusikila buce. Keep the door closed until the dawn. (1.-jalwa, 3.-jazya, 4.-jalila, 5.-jalilayo, 6.-jalisya, 7.-jala-jala, 8. -jalilana.)

shake the voice, Ulajejema kwiimba mweenzuma ncatalimvwisyi kabotu. = My friend shakes the voice when s/he sings, that is why s/he is not heard clearly. Also: -dedema. (1.-jejemwa, 2.-jejemede, 3.-jejemya, 4.-jejemena, 5.-jejemenalyo, 6.-jejemesya, 7.-jejema-jejema, 8.-jejemenana)
  • rattle, Kojala kabotu cijazyo camoota kutegwa cileke kujejema. = Close the door of the car properly so that it stops rattling. Also: -njenjema.

become detached, Kamubbabbulula zikanda zyajejemuka. = Peel off the skin which is hanging loosely. (1.-jejemukwa, 2.-jejemukide, 3.-jejemuzya, 4.-jejemukila, 5.-jejemukilalyo, 6.-jejemukisya 7.-jejemuka-jejemuka, 8. -jejemukana)

pretend to give, tantalize, Mukaintu mubi wakajeemunzya bana ndongwe nzyatakwe kubapa. The evil woman tantalized the children with groundnuts which she did not give them. (1.-jeemunzyigwa, 2.-jeemunzyizye, 4.-jeemunzyizya, 5.-jeemunzyizyalyo, 6.-jeemunisya, 7.-jeemunzya-jeemunzya, 8.-jeemunzyanya) Also: -nyeemunzya.

play the children's game called Jemu ("Look at this nice thing but its not for you.") Mwana mubi ujemuzya beenzinyina zyakulya nzyatabapi. = A naughty child tantalizes her/his friends with food which s/he does not give them. (1.-jeemuzyigwa, 2.-jemuzyizye, 4.-jemuzyizya, 5.-jemusyizyalyo, 6.-jemunisya, 7-jemuzya-jemuzya, 8.-jemuzyanya)

found, rt. -jana, Nobakapiluka bakajene koombe kalede anze. = When they returned they found the calf lying outside the kraal. (1.-janwa, 2.-jene, 3.-janya, 4.-janina, 5.-janinalyo, 6.-janisya, 7.-jene-jene, 8.-janana)

be attended to continually, Cimwi cisyu taciyandi kujibilizigwa kwiidwa inga casubila. = Certain types of vegetables do not like to be watered frequently as they become red. (2.-jibilizidwe, 3.-jibilizya, 4.-jibilizizya, 5.-jibilizizyalyo, 6.-jibilizisya, 7.-jibilizyajibilizya, 8.-jibilizyanya)

become regular, Mbwaakali kuya mazuba eeci ciloto cakatalika kujibilizya kusikila wakatalika kulota kufwumbwa woona. = As the days passed this dream began to occur regularly until he began to dream about it whenever he slept. (1.-jibilizigwa)
be defeated in a contest, Chibila wajiizigwa mumuzundano wangoma. = Chibila was defeated in the drum competition. (3.-jiizya, 7. -jiizigwa-jiizigwa, 8.-jiizyana)
compete with one another, Wakalibambila kulijiizyana ngoma a sinkondonyina. = He prepared to compete with his enemy in a drum competition.

wrestle with one another, Basankwa bobilo bakali kujijilisyanya nibakakolwa bukoko. = The two men were fighting when they were drunk. (1.-jijilisyigwa, 2.-jijilisyenye, 4.-jijilisyanizyizya, (5.-jijilisyanizyizyalyo) Also: -gagalisyanya, -bbabbalisyanya.
cook, Kamujika nsima, bana bayanda koona. = Cook the nsima, the children want to sleep. (roast, fry, -kanga; cook variety of dishes

cook in water or heat cream or butter, -enga; be cooked, -bizwa; cook badly, -jika mafwasa, jika mavwunze) (1.-jikwa, 2.-jikide, 3.-jisya, 4.-jikila, 5.-jikilalyo, 6.-jikisya, 7.-jika-jika, 8.-jikana)
  • settle in a good manner, Sibbuku ulya ulicizyi kujika twaambo. = That headman knows how to settle matters. Also: -bamba.

be cooked with, rt. -jika, Basingoma nobakamana kulya, zipopwe a musozya wakajikilizigwa amusamu walumamba uutegwa mbala, bakaimikila. = When the drummers were finished eating corn and stew which had been cooked with the medicine for encouraging fighting, they stood up. (2.-jikilizide, 3.-jikilizya, 4.-jikilizizya 5.-jikilizizyalyo)

re-cook, Kamujikulula nsima yajilo. = Recook yesterday's nsima.
  • cook for a long time to free from poison, Kamumujikulula kapati syaa-muvwamba kutegwa busungu bumane. = Cook syaamuvwamba roots for a long time to free from poison. (1.-jikululwa, 2.-jikulwide, 3.-jikuluzya, 4.-jikulwida, 5.-jikulwidalyo, 6.-jikululisya, 7.-jikululajikulula, 8.-jikululana)

erect head, Munyati wakajilimana niyakalila ntobolo. = The buffalo stood with head erect when the gun was fired. Wajilimana unakuti musune wasondoka. = He raised his head as if he was a mad ox. (1.-jilimanwa, 2.-jilimenye, 3.-jilimika, 4.-jilimanina, 5.-jilimaninalyo, 6.-jilimanisya, 7.-jilimanajilimana)
  • walk with head erect in insolence, Musankwa uujilimana buya kweenda utondezya kutaloma. = The boy who just walks with his head in the air shows that he is not honourable.

insert, Kamujimika kasamu mpoyaandanina migwagwa. = Insert a stick where the roads part. Also: -jimpika, -simpika. (1.-jimikwa, 2.-jimikide, 3.-jimikizya, 4.-jimikizyizya, 5.-jimikizyizyalyo, 7.-jimika-jimika, 8.-jimikizyanya)

end, Lwiiyo Iwanu Iwa Chitonga luya kujimpa mwaka uboola. = Your Tonga studies will end next year. Buzumi buno bulajimpa muntu afwa. = This life comes to an end when a person dies. (1.-jimpwa, 2.-jimpide, 3.-jimpya, 4.-jimpila, 5.-jimpilalyo, 6.-jimpisya, 7. -jimpa-jimpa, 8.-jimpizyanya) Also: -simpa, -mana, -gola.
be inserted, Ezi nsengo zyakali kujimpidwe munsaa mulyango. = These charms were inserted beside the entrance.

put on, insert, Kamujimpika mpoto acikko. Put the pot on the fire. Basankwa bajimpika zisamu zyalubaya. The boys are putting up poles for a fence. (1.-jimpikwa, 2.-jimpikide, 3.-jimpya, 4.-jimpikizyizya, 5.-jimpikizyizyalyo) Also: -simpa, -sibika, -jimika.

end up at, rt. -jimpa, Boonse bana bakali amyaka ikankatutatu akujimpila kuli baabo ibakali amyaka kkumi akwiindilila kasyoonto, bakamwaika mulubuwa kusobana. All the children who were eight years old and ending up at those who were ten years and a little more, scattered into the courtyard playing. (1.-jimpwa, 2.-jimpide, 3.-jimpya, 4.-jimpila, 5.-jimpilalyo, 6.-jimpisya 7.-jimpila-jimpila, jimpizyanya.)

land as boat, come to shore, arrive at, Mulonga ulajinka mulwizi. = The river flows into a lake. (1.-jinkwa, 2.-jinkide, 3.-jinkizya, 4.-jinkizyizya, 5.-jinkizyizyalyo, 6.-jinkisya, 7.-jinka-jinka, 8.-jinkizyanya)
  • end, as a story, Kaano kako kalamuka kujinka. ending. Your story is slow in Also: -mana.
  • mature as a boy, Omuno mucisi ca Butonga kwakali cilengwa cabasikale cakuti ciindi cakooloka bana basimbi abaya batanakula antoomwe a basankwa batana-jinka bakali kuunka musyokwe mumbali amunzi kucita mantoombwa. = Here in Tongaland there was a custom of the ancestors that when the first crops were eaten, young girls and those who had not yet reached puberty together with boys who had not matured, would go into the bush near the village to prepare for adulthood. Also: -kubuka
be completed, rt. -jinka, Mibuzyo njaakajisi, imwi tiiyakali kuvwiilwa, imwi yakali kuvwiilwa citajinkide. = Some questions which he had were not answered, others were not fully answered.
end up, as a story, Kaano aawa mpokajinkila. That is where the little story ends. Yakamujinkila mizeezo. = He had no more thoughts. Also: -manina. (1.-jinkilwa)
suddenly stand still, Syaampeyo wakajinkimana kati abonesesye naa ncobeni nguusyi. = Syaampeyo stood still so that he could see clearly whether it was really his father.
thrust hard into the ground, Naakasika munsaa cisamu cipati, wakajinsika sumo ansi. = When he reached near a big tree, he thrust the spear hard into the ground.

push a part of something into ground and bury or cover, Bana bajinsila mweenzinyina akumusiya. = The children pushed the hand of their friend into a hole, buried it and left him there. (a punishment among herders when someone breaks the rules) (1.-jinsilwa, 2.-jinsilide, 3.-jinsilizya, 4.-jinsilizyizya, 5.-jinsilizyizyalyo, 8.-jinsilana) Also: -sindaila

push one another, rt. -jinsila, Ijilo bana bakali *kujinsilana* nobaali kusobana. = The children push (as a punishment) the hands of one another into the holes (and stamp the clay around) as they were playing. (a custom used long ago when herding cattle.)
