appeal, plead with someone, grovel, Balaa nkazi tabayandi kukombelela muntu. = Those who are stubbourn do not want to plead with anyone. Also: -dedelela. (1.-kombelelwa, 2.-kombelede, 3.-kombelezya, 4. -kombelela, 5.-kombelelalyo, 6.-kombelelelesya, 7. -kombelela-kombelela, 8.-kombelelana)

be persuaded, Ndakaka kukombelezegwa kucita ncetayandi. = I refuse to be persuaded to do something which I do not want. (2.-kombelezede, 3.-kombelezezya, 4.-kombelezyezya, 5.-kombelezyezyalyo, 6.-kombelelesya, 7.-kombelezegwakombelezegwa)

implore, beg, Eeci cilengwa cakukombelezya bantu taciyandiki. = This habit of pleading with people is not needed. Also: -sengelezya, -songelezya. (1.-kombelezyegwa, 2.-kombelezyede, 3.kombelezyesya, 4.-kombelezyezya, 5.-kombelezyezyalyo, 6.-kombelezyesya, 7.-kombelezya-kombelezya, 8.-kombelezyanya)

ladle out porridge, Kamukombola ceele mumutiba mulye. = Ladle out the porridge in a dish so that you eat. Also: -timpula. (1.-kombolwa, 2.-kombolede/kombwede 3.-kombozya, 4.-kombolela/-kombweda, 5.-kombolelalyo/-kombwedalyo, 6.-kombolesya, 7.-kombola-kombola, 8.-kombolana/kombwedana.)

ladle out a large helping, Ooyu mwana ulakombolesya ceele, ulabaima bananyina. = This child is taking too much porridge, he will prevent his friends from taking enough. (extensions are same as -kombola)

sit or lie lazily, Kuti kamukombomana kukkala, tamukonzyi kulemba kabotu pe. = If you sit lazily you won't write properly. Abuzuba ulakombomana mucimvwule butolo bwalo. = Every day you stretch out in the shade just in laziness. (1.-kombomanwa, 2.-kombomwede, 3.-kombomanya, 4.-kombomanina, 5.-kombomaninalyo, 6.-kombomanisya, 7.-kombomana-kombo-mana)

extract honey from a hive, *Basankwa bali kukomboola buci.* = The boys were extracting honey from the hive. (1.-komboolwa, 2.-komboolede, 3.-komboozya, 4.-kombweeda, 5.-kombweedalyo, 6.-komboolesya, 7.-komboola-komboola, 8.-komboolana)
  • take, leaving nothing, *Bana baci-komboola ceele kwabula acicaala.* = The children have taken all the porridge without leaving a thing.

let off, *Kamubakombosya babeleka nkaambo ciindi casika cakukotoka.* = Let the workers off because the time for knocking off has come. (1.-kombosyegwa, 2.-kombosyede, 3.-kombosyezya, 4.-kombosyela, 5.-kombosyelalyo, 6.-kombosyesya, 7.-kombosya-kombosya, 8.-kombosyanya)
ladle out with, rt. -kombola, *Twamuka kulya ceele nkaambo kwanyina cakukombozya.* = We were late in eating the porridge because there was nothing to ladle it out with.

humble oneself, rt. -komba, *Ndakalikombya buya nobaya kundipa ncindakali kuyanda.* = I had to humble myself for them to give me what I wanted. *Ndakabona waboola walikombya ategwa, "Ndacita cibi kapati kumvwa twabantu."* = I saw him coming humbling himself saying, "I did a very bad thing in listening to what people were saying." (1.-kombwa, 2.-kombede, 3.-kombya, 4.-kombelelela, 5.-kombelelelalyo, 6. -kombesya, 7.-kombya-kombya, 8.-kombelana)

grow, *Nobana bangu, ndabona kuti ino mwakomena mumaano.* = My children, I have seen that now you have grown in wisdom. (1.-komenwa, 2.-komenede, 3.-komezya, 4.-komenena, 5.-komenenalyo, 6.-komenesya, 7.-komena-komena.)
make to grow, rear, *Mwana nguwangu, ndakalikomezyezya.* = The child is mine, I reared her/him.

cause to grow, enlarge, *Kukomezya cisyu camuliwa cilakatazya.* = To grow rape is difficult. *Mwiiyi wakalijisi mwana musankwa ngwakakomezya.* = The teacher had a boy who he helped to grow up. (see extensions for -komena)

break off pieces and share with one another, *Bakali kukomodana twaambo.* = They were selecting topics to share with one another. (1.-komonwa, 2.-komwede, 3.-komozya, 4.-komodanina, 5.-komodaninalyo, 6.-komodanisya, 7.-komodana-komodana, 8.-komodana)

be split, *Cakomoka cuuno cacimbwalakasa mpucali alwaanzi.* = The stool was split where it had a crack. (1.-komokwa, 2. -komokede, 3.-komozya, 4.-komokela, 5. -komokelalyo, 6.-komokesya, 7.-komoka-komoka)

be broken up, *Cinkwa ncibaleta bana cakomooka.* = The bread which the childen brought was broken up. *Bulongo bulakomooka, bulayeemuka, bulaunka amulonga, bulatolwa aguwo.* = The clay is broken up, it dissolves, it goes with the river and is taken away by the wind. (1.-komookwa, 2.-komookede, 3.-komoozya, 4.-komookela, 5.-komookelalyo, 6.-komoðkesya, 7.-komooka-komooka) Also: -sunauka.

break up, *Kamukomona nsima mwaabane nyoonse.* = Break the nsima up and share it among yourselves. (1.-komonwa, 2.-komokede, 3.-komozya, 4.-komonena/komweda, 5.-komonenalyo-/komwedalyo, 6.-komonesya, 7.-komona-komona, 8.-komonana/komwedana) Also: -kompola.

continually break into pieces, *Mukaintu wakali kukomoona* zyeeya-zyeeya zyamyungu. = The woman was continually breaking off pieces of pumpkin. (1.-komoonwa, 2.-komoonede, 3.-komoozya, 4.-komoonena, 5.-komoonenalyo, 6.-komoonesya, 7.-komoona-komoona, 8.-komoonana)
blink, Wakagama buyo kukompaila meso mpaakakkede. = He began to blink his eyes where he was sitting.

droop as plants in drought, Malangazuba akali kukompama nkolibala zuba. The sunflowers were drooping when the sun was burning. (2.-kompamide, 3.-kompamya, 4.-kompamina, 5.-kompaminalyo, 6.-kompamisya, 7.-kompama-kompama) Also: -neta.

be broken, Ipopwe lyakakompoka nilyakaloka ansi. = The maize cob was completely broken when it fell on the ground. (1.-kompokwa, 2.-kompokede, 3.-kompozya, 4.-kompokela, 5.-kompokelalyo, 6.-kompokesya, 7.-kompoka-kompoka, 8.-kompokana)

break, Kokompola popwe twaabane. Break the maize cob so that we share it. Also: -komona, -tyola, -kanuka. (1.-kompolwa, 2.-kompolede, 3.-kompolezya/kompozya, 4.-kompozyezya, 6.-kompolesya, 7.-kompola-kompola, 8.-kompolana)
break, Bakamukompoola maulu. = They broke his legs. (1.-kompoolwa, 2.-kompoolede, 3.-kompoozya, 4.-kompweeda, 5.-kompweedalyo, 6.-kompoolesya, 7.-kompoola-kompoola, 8.-kompoolana)

be defeated, be overcome, rt. -koma, Mucende ookwesu wakakomwa kuli ookwanu. = Our bull was defeated by yours. (1.-komwa, 2.-komede, 3.-komya, 4.-komena, 5.-komenalyo, 6.-komesya, 7.-komwa-komwa,8.-komana)

share with, rt. -komona, *Kondikomweda cipaanzi camungu.* = Share with me a section of the pumpkin. (1.-komwedwa, 2.-komwede, 3.-komwedanizya, 4.-komwedanina, 5.-komwedaninalyo, 6.-komwedanisya, 7.-komwedakomweda, 8.-komwedana)

inherit, Eezi nombe bakazikona kuli baacisya. They inherited these cattle from my uncle. To Batonga tutalubi bwaabi mbotwakakona kuli bensiku besu. = We Tonga do not forget the habit of hospitality which we inherited from our ancestors. (1.-konwa, 2.-konede, 3.-konya, 4.-konela, 5.-konelalyo, 6.-konesya, 7.-kona-kona, 8.-konana / konizyanya.) Also: -bentaka.

contract nose and eyes, squint, Bantu bataboni kabotu, balakonama nobasola kulanga. = People who cannot see well, squint when they try to look. (1.-konamwa, 2.-konamide, 3.-konamizya, 4.-konamina, 5.-konaminalyo, 6.-konamisya, 7.-konama-konama)
pass down Buta obu mbwakukonana. This bow has been passed down from father to son. (1.-konanwa, 2.-konanide, 3.-konanizya, 4.-konanina, 5.-konaninalyo, 6.-konanisya, 7.-konana-konana)

delight, gladden, Cilakonda cicitika waawa. = What happens here is delightful. Cakandikonda kwiindilila nkujana bakunka kale mulilo. It made me exceedingly happy to find that they had already lit the fire. (1.-kondwa, 2.-kondede, 3.-kondya / -kondezya, 4.-kondela, 5.-kondelalyo, 6.-kondesya, 7.-konda-konda, 8.-kondana.)

be badly cooked, Basankwa bakaka kulya nsima nkaambo bajana yakondekana. = The boys refused to eat the nsima because they found it badly cooked. (2.-kondekanide, 3.-kondekanya, 4.-kondekanina, 5.-kondekaninalyo, 6.-kondekanisya, 7.-kondekana-kondekana) Also: -myala.

become pleasant, Cizyano cakakondela nobakasika basimbi. = The dance became pleasant when the girls arrived. (1.-kondelwa, 2.-kondelede, 3.-kondezya, 4.-kondezyezya, 5.-kondezyezyalyo, 6.-kondelesya, 7.-kondela-kondela, 8.-kondelana)

please, delight, Cinande ncizyano cikondelezya. = The cinande is a delightful dance. (1.-kondelezyegwa, 2.-kondelezyede, 3.-kondelezyesya, 4.-kondelezyezya, 5.-kondelezyezyalyo, 6.-kondelezyesya, 7.-kondelezya-kondelezya, 8.-kondelezyanya)

begin to be brewed, Bacembele bakondola bukoko. = The old woman has started brewing beer. (1.-kondolwa, 2.-kodwede, 3.-kondozya, 4.-kondweda, 5.-kodwedalyo, 6.-kondolesya, 7.-kondola-kondola, 8.-kondolana)

be turbid, muddy, thick, Meenda akondooka nibali kuzela mukalonga. = The water became muddy when they were fishing in the stream. Also: -vwundauka. (1.-kondookwa, 2.-kondookede, 3.-kondoozya, 4.-kondookela, 5.-kondookelalyo, 6.-kondookesya, 7.-kondooka-kondooka, 8.-kondookana)

be stirred up, rt. -kondooka. Meenda alikondookede, tatukonzyi kwaanywa. = The water has been muddied, we cannot drink it. (1.-kondookedwe, 3.-kondoozya, 4.-kondoozyezya, 5.-kondozyezyalyo, 6.-kondookesya, 7.-kondookedekondookede)

make muddy, stir up, Inombe zyakondoola meenda. cattle stir up the water. (1.-kondoolwa, 2.-kondoolede, 3.-kondoozya, 4.-kondoolela, 5.-kondoolelalyo, 6.-kondoolesya, 7.-kondoola-kondoola, 8.-kondoolana) Also: -fwundanya, -vwundanya.

be brewed at or for, rt. kondola, Cimwi ciindi basimbi bakali kukondola abukoko bwamantoombwa. Oobu bukoko bwakali kukondwedwa kumunzi. = Sometimes the girls were brewing beer of the 'mantoombwa. This beer was brewed at the village. Bukoko obu bwakondwedwa mizimo yabasikale. = This beer has been brewed for the ancestral spirits. (2.kodwede)

inherit wealth of the dead, rt. -kona, Ndakalikonena lubono lunji kuli baacisya nibakafwa. I inherited much wealth from my uncle when he died. (1.-konenwa, 2.-konede, 3.-konya, 4.-konena, 5.-konenalyo, 6.-konesya, 7.-konena-konena, 8.-konana) Also: -konya

frighten, Bandikonga beenzuma nindali kuya kunkolola masiku. = My friends frightened me when I was going to the initiation ceremony at night. (1.-kongwa, 2.-kongede, 3.-kongezya, 4.-kongela, 5.-kongelalyo, 6.-kongesya, 7.-konga-konga, 8.-kongana) Also: -kandusya, -kanga-kanga.

frighten with, rt. -konga, Bana kamuleka kubakongezya nkumba, mayongolo, abauka bamwi. = Don't be frightning the children with snails, centipedes and other insects. (1.-kongezyegwa, 2.-kongezyede, 3.-kongezya, 4.-kongezyezya, 5.-kongezyezyalyo, 6.-kongezyesya, 7.-kongezya-kongezya, 8.-kongezyanya)
be frightened, rt.-konga, Wakakongwa babwa ncaakatijila musankwa ulya. That boy was frightened by the dogs, that is why he ran away.

make sure, swear, Ndakonka, kasimpe nseli ndime ekaamba. = I swear, it wasn't me who said it. The (1.-konkwa, 2.-konkede, 3.-konkezya, 4.-konkela, 5.-konkelalyo, 6.-konkesya, 7.-konka-konka, 8.-konkelana) Also: -lumbizya, -sinizya.
  • sniff out, Kabwa kangu kalicizyi kukonka mukondo wakanyama. = My dog knows how to sniff out the track of an animal. Also: -numfwida.
  • invite, Bwasika buzuba bwabukoko bwa 'kaanzyo', mwaalumi ooyo sikwaanzigwa ulakonka, antela kutamba banamuzyaabo kuya kukusenga. = When the day of the 'beer for greeting' arrives that husband who is to be greeted invites his relatives to go to drink beer.

knock, Kamukonkaula amulyango mujaludwe. = Knock on the door and it will be opened for you. (1.-konkaulwa, 2.-konkaulide, 3.-konkauzya, 4.-konkaulila, 5.-konkaulilalyo, 6.-konkaulisya, 7.-konkaula-konkaula, 8.-konkaulana) Also: -konkomona.

be without energy, Ndakonkelwa nkaambo kakutalya kabotu. = I am without energy from not eating properly. Also: -gonkelwa, -ongedwe. (2.-konkelwe, 3.-konkezya, 4.-konkelelwa, 5.-konkelelwalyo)
  • be tracked down, rt. -konka, Tanaakonkelwa munyama waluma koombe akaambo kakuyoowa. = The beast which attacked the calf was not hunted down because of fear.

cause to swear, rt. konka, Kamumukonkezya mwana ooyo naa teesyi nguwakabba ncobeni. = Make that child swear to it if he is really not the one who stole. (1.-konkezyegwa)
  • cause weakness, Muteezi ulakonkezya kuulya abuzuba. = It makes one weak to eat okra every day. Also: -gonkezya.

curse, Bacembele bakamukonkobezya muzyukulu wabo naakabauma cisisi camulilo amutwe. = The old woman cursed her grandchild when she hit her on the head with an ember. Also: -singa. (1.-konkobezyegwa, 2.-konkobezyede, 4.-konkobezyezya, 5.-konkobezyezyalyo, 6.-konkobezyesya, 7.-konkobezya-konkobezya, 8.-konkobezyanya)

knock for someone, rt. konkomona, Komukonkokweda mwana bamujalwide bali munanda. = Knock for the child so that the people in the house may open for him. (1.-konkokwedwa, 2.-konkokwede, 3.-konkokwezya, 4.-konkokwedela, 5.-konkokwedalyo, 6.-konkokwedelesya, 7.-konkokweda-konkokweda, 8.-konkokwedelana) Also: -konkweeda.

propose marriage for another, Michelo nguwakakonkola makani alukwato Iwa Mutinta. = Michelo was the one who proposed for Mutinta's marriage. Also: -kokola (1.-konkolwa, 2.-konkolede, 3.-konkolezya, 4.-konkolela, 5.-konkolelalyo, 6.-konkolesya, 7.-konkola-konkola, 8.-konkolana)
  • hatch, Idada lyakakonkola jilo. = The duck hatched yesterday. Also: -konkona.
  • hit on the head with knuckle or stick, Bayi baamukonkola kasako mwana amutwe. The teacher hit the child with a stick on the head. Also: -konkola.

knock on door, Ndakajalula nindakamvwa ukonkolola. = I opened the door when I heard someone knocking. Also: - konkomona (1.-konkololwa, 2.-konkololede, 3.-konkololezya, 4.-konkolweda, 5.-konkolwedalyo, 6.-konkololesya, 7.-konkolola-konkolola, 8.-konkololana)

lift up head, as cobra, Yakonkomana nzoka eyi kuti ilume muntu. The snake raised its head to strike a person. (1.-konkomanwa, 2.-konkomanide, 3.-konkomeka, 4.-konkomanina, 5.-konkomaninalyo, 6.-konkomanisya, 7.-konkomana-konkomana)
  • be warped, Mweeto wakooye wakakonkomana kapati, ncikataca. = The stick, which acts as a spring in the falltrap, was warped, that is why it didn't fall. Also: -gogomana, -ongomana, -kokonyana

warp, be out of line, Koufwala kabotu mwiini, waukonkomeka. = Carve the handle properly, you have put it out of line. Mufwuzi wakakonkomeka keembe, ncokatagonki kabotu. = The black-smith made the axe out of line, that is why it does not cut properly.
be erect, be sticking out, Lwala lwako lulikonkomene. = Your finger nail is projecting. Nzweluuke wakabona nkata yanzoka amutwe ukonkomene. = Nzweluuke saw a snake coiled with the head erect.

knock, Weelede kukonkomona kotananjila munanda. = You ought to knock before you enter the house. Also: -konkaula. (1.-konkomonwa, 2.-konkomwede, 3.-konkomozya, 4.-konkomonena, 5.-konkomonenalyo, 6.-konkomonisya, 7.-konkomona-konkomona)
impress on the mind, counsel, Baiyi bali kukonkomwena Cheelo. = The teacher was counselling Cheelo. Also: -laya. (1.-konkomwenwa)
hatch, Nkuku yangu iyakukonkona mvwiki iboola. = My hen will hatch next week. (1.-konkonwa, 2.-konkonede, 3.-konkonya, 4.-konkonena, 5.-konkonenalyo, 6.-konkonesya, 7.-konkona-konkona)

droop as plants in drought, Matu a cisyu cangu akonkonyana akaambo kakupya zuba. = The leaves of my vegetables are dropping because of the sun's heat. Also: -kokonyana (1.-konkonyanwa, 2.-konkonyanide, 3.-konkonyeka, 4.-konkonyanina, 5.-konkonyaninalyo, 6.-konkonyanisya, 7.-konkonyana-konkonyana)
make to wither, Izuba libala kapati likonkonyeka mapopwe. = If the sun shines strongly it withers the maize. (see extensions for konkonyana)

knock or break off, Wakasika atanda lyamulilo akuyanga akukonkoola makala amulilo. = He arrived at the fireplace and stirred it up and broke off hot coals from a log. Also: -kunkaula. (1.-konkoolwa, 2.-konkoolede, 3.-konkoozya, 4.-konkoolela, 5.-konkoolelalyo, 6.-konkoolesya, 7.-konkoola-konkoola, 8.-konkoolana)
  • beat drum with a stick, Mwaaba wakali kukonkoola goma mpati. = Mwaaba was beating a big drum with a stick.

knock with Musimbi wakaboola kumulyango wananda yamucembele akukonkoozya akkoma akanteengezya kakwe. = A girl came to the entrance of the old woman and tapped the door with her little finger. (1.-konkoozyegwa, 2.-konkoozyede, 3.-konkoozya, 4.-konkoozyezya, 5.-konkoozyezyalyo, 6.-konkoozyesya, 7.-konkoozya-konkoozya, 8.-konkoozyanya)

walk slowly due to impediment, Munene ooyu wacembaala ncakonkoteka. = This old man is old that is why he is walking slowly. (1.-konkotekwa, 2.-konkotekede, 3.-konkotezya, 4.-konkotekela, 5.-konkotekelalyo, 6.-konkotekesya, 7.-konkoteka-konkoteka) Also: -gogoteka

lift up one leg and stand on the other alone, Nitwali kusobana ndacikonzya kukonya. = When we were playing I was able to lift up one leg while standing on the other. (1.-konyezyegwa, 2.-konyede, 3.-konya, 4.-konyezyezya, 5.-konyezyezyalyo, 6.-konyezyesya, 7.-konya-konya, 8.-konyezyanya)
  • wring out, Kamweenda mundigwasye *kukonya* payi. = Come and help me to wring out this blanket. Also: -*kanya*.
  • cause to inherit, Nibakafwa bataata *bakandikonya* nombe zyotatwe. = When my father died they gave me three cows as inheritance.

swagger when walking, Basokwe balikwiile *kukonyomba* munzila. = The monkeys were just swaggering along the path. (1.-konyombwa, 2.-konyombede, 3.-konyombya, 4.-konyombela, 5.-konyombelalyo, 6.-konyombesya, 7.-konyomba-konyomba)
be possible, rt. -*konzya*, Cilakonzeka kubamba bwato. = It is possible to mend the boat. (1.-kozekwa, 2.-konzekede)
be able to, Aaba bantu kunyina ancobakali *kulikonzezya*. = These people are never able to do anything for themselves.

can, be able, Sena ulakonzya kufwala bwato? = Are you able to carve a boat. (1.-konzyegwa, 2.-konzyede, 3.-konzyesya, 4.-konzyela/konzyezya, 5.-konzyelalyo/-konzyezyalyo, 6.-konzyesya, 7.-konzya-konzya, 8.-konzyanya)
  • overcome, defeat, *Bandikonzya* beenzuma balaa maano kuno kumunzi, moyo wangu bawaanga loozi. = My friends who are clever here in the village have defeated me, they have tied my heart with a fibre.

be hooked together, Syuumbwa wakaliyubide mukoonde koo*bene*. = The lion was hiding in an inter laced thicket. Kalobo kako *kakoobene* akolobo kangu. Your hook was hooked with mine. (1.-koobanwa, 2.-koobenye, 3.-koobanya, 4.-koobanina, 5.-koobaninalyo, 6.-koobanisya, 7.-koobbene-koobene, 8.-koobene)

pull off, strip, Kamukoola mapopwe mumuunda mupati. = Pull off cobs of maize in the big field. (1.-koolwa, 2.-koolede, 3.-koolezya/koozya, 4.-koolela, 5.-koolelalyo, 6.-koolesya, 7.-koola-koola, 8. -koolana.)
  • be allergic to certain foods, Ooyu mwana wakoola nyama yampongo ncaciswa kuti wailya. = This child is allergic to goat's meat that is why it becomes sick if it eats it. Sicibende wakapona pele takwe naakacili kwiilya nyama yampongo, wakaikoola. = Sicibende recovered but he did not continue to eat goat's meat, he was allergic to it.

stir, Nobasimbi, kamukopa cibwantu citasyilili. = Girls, stir the sweet beer so that it does not get burnt. (1.-kopwa, 2.-kopede, 3.-kopya, 4.-kopela, 5.-kopelalyo, 6.-kopesya, 7.-kopa-kopa, 8.-kopana) Also: -ponda, -puka
  • confuse, baffle, Bakaintu cakabakopa cakali kulya mapopwe kumuunda. = What was eating the maize confused the wife.

be busy, Tiindaunka kumuswaangano sunu nkaambo ndakopana. = I did not go to the meeting today because I am too busy. (1.-kopanwa, 2.-kopenye, 3.-kopanya, 4.-kopanina, 5.-kopaninalyo, 6.-kopanisya, 7.-kopana-kopana)
combine, Waka

meenda amungwimba. = He mixed up water and paraffin. (1.-kopanyizigwa and see extensions for kopana) Also: - vwelenganya.
  • disturb in doing something, Wazikopanya zintu yebo. = You have disturbed the things.

button, Kokopela nkopela, kulibonya da. = Button the button, your stomach is seen. (1.-kopelwa, 2.-kopelede, 3.-kopezya, 4.-kopelela, 5.-kopelelalyo, 6.-kopelesya, 7.-kopela-kopela, 8.-kopelana)
  • cook for, Inga kobuka kolikopela keele notanaunka kucikolo. You should be getting up to cook for yourself some porridge before you go to school.

be ugly or distorted, Timoti cakali cintu cifwiifwi, kumeso ciide kukopene, cisiya biya mbi. = Timothy was a short person, with an ugly face which was exceedingly black. (1.-kopenwe, 3.-kopanya, 4.-kopanina, 5.-kopaninalyo, 6.-kopanisya, 7.-kopene-kopene)

be busy, Bacembele bakopengana ncibataunka kumuunda. The old woman was busy that is why she did not go to the field. Also: -gwitingana (1.-kopenganwa, 2.-kopengenye, 3.-kopenganya, 4.-kopenganina, 5.-kopenganinalyo, 6.-kopenganisya, 7.-kopengana-kopengana)
  • speak incorrectly, Ndakopengana kupandulula makani nkaambo basilikani banduuma. I spoke incorrectly because the poice beat me.

mix up languages, Nakanana wiile kukopenganya misyobo nkwati wavwelanya ooyu ayooyu. = When he speaks he just blends the languages, mixing this one with that one. (1.-kopenganizigwa, 2.-kopenganizyide, 4.-kopenganina, 5.-kopenganinalyo, 6.-kopenganisya, 7.kopenganyakopenganya) Also: -wwelenganya, -golonganya
wipe, rub, Wakasinsimuka oku kumwi kalikopola kumeso. = He awoke while rubbing his eyes.

undo, as a belt, Kokopolola lutambo tubone cilonda ncowamba. Undo the belt so that we see the wound you are talking about. Also: -koponona. (1.-kopololwa, 2.-kopoIwede, 3.-kopolozya, 4.-kopolweda, 5.-kopolwedalyo, 6.-kopololesya, 7.-kopolola-kopolola, 8.-kopololana)

unfasten, Koponona nkopela tubone acamba naa ulasalala. = Undo the buttons so that we see whether your chest is clean. Also: -kopolola. (1.-kopononwa, 2.-koponwede, 3.-koponozya, 4.-koponweda, 5.-koponwedalyo, 6.-kopononesya, 7.-koponona-koponona, 8.-kopononana)

cut up into small pieces, Kokosaula butendutendu bwanyama. Cut up the strips of meat in small pieces. (1.-kosaulwa, 2.-kosaulide, 3.-kosauzya, 4.-kosaulila, 5.-kosauilalyo, 6.-kosaulisya, 7.-kosaula-kosaula, 8. kosaulana) Also: -kosoola.

die suddenly, Waile kukosoka kufwa. = She just died suddenly. Mulwazi wakosoka masiku. = The sick person suddenly died at night. (1.-kosokwa, 2.-kosokede, 3.-kosozya, 4.-kosokela, 5.-kosokelalyo, 6.-kosokesya, 7.-kosoka-kosoka, 8.-kosokana)
  • be cut, like a rope, Looye Iwakosoka nikakwela koombe. The rope snapped when the calf pulled.
  • be settled, Kaambo kakwe kakukwata kakakosoka kale. The negotiation concerning his marriage has already been settled.
cause to cut off, Wakakosokezya mizeezo yakwe nkabela wakaide kuvwiila cakufwambaana. = He cut off his thoughts and just answered quickly.

judge, settle a dispute, *Ndali kukosola kaambo kabana.* = I was settling a dispute among the children. (1.-kosolwa, 2.-kosokede/koswede, 3.-kosozya, 4.-kosweda/-kosoda/-kosolela, 5.-koswedalyo, 6.-kosolesya, 7.-kosolakosola, -kosolana.)
  • cut off, *Kokosola bunweba oobo ameno.* = Cut that thread with your teeth. *Nibakaijata nkuku, Maliya wakaikosola mukosi.* = When they caught the chicken, Mary cut its neck. Also: -gonka, -zutula.
  • shorten a discussion, *Kamukosola makani atazumanani kuya kumpela nkaambo ulubizide wabonwa kale.* = Shorten the discussion so that it does not continue because the one who has erred is already known.
  • cross a road, *Twaukosola mugwagwa uya ku Gwembe.* = We crossed the road going to Gwembe.
  • cough, *Ooyu mwana taoni kabotu ulakosola masiku oonse.* = This child does not sleep well, s/he coughs the whole night.

be prolific in bearing many children, *Ooyu mukaintu ulakosoola kuzyala.* = This woman bears many children. Also: -gonka bana. (1.-kosoolwa, 2.-kosoolede, 3.-kosoozya, 4.-kosweeda, 5.-kosweedalyo, 6.-kosoolesya, 7.-kosoola-kosoola, 8.-kosoolana)
  • break in many places, *Kamucikosoola cisamu eeci muzibeela-beela.* = Break that wood up into pieces. Also: -bbansaula, -dunsaula, -zutaula.
  • shorten, *Basicuuno baleelede kukosoola kukanana mumuswaangano.* = The chairperson should shorten the talk at the meeting. Also: -fwiimpya.

receive rain sometimes, *Wawidwa vwuma mumwaka wakono nkaambo mvwula ilakosozya kwako.* = You are lucky this year because it rains sometimes at your place. (1.-kosozyegwa, 2.-kosozyede, 4.-kosozyezya, 5.-kosozyezyalyo, 6.-kosozyesya, 7.-kosozya-kosozya, 8.-kosozyanya)
  • cut with, rt. -kosola, *Imbeba ibelesya meno kukosozya bwizu.* = The rat uses its teeth to cut the grass.
cross over, *Jule wakali kuyanda kumukosweda nzila.* = The secretary bird was about to cross his path. (an evil omen)
be absolved or freed from, *Ndakakkomana nindakakoswedwa kaambo.* = I was happy when I was freed from the matter.

make thin, rt. -koka, *Mizeezo yabana bakwe iyakutizya basimbi yamukosya.* = The plans of his children to take girls illegally caused him to become thin. *Buumi bwakulendelelwa mudolopo bwakamukosya.* = The lonely life of the city caused her to become thin. (1.-kosyegwa, 2.-kosyede, 4.-kosyela. 5.-kosyelalyo, 6.-kosyesya, 7.-kosyakosya, 8.-kosyanya)

bow one's head, *Wakotama mutwe ansi akufwa.* = He bowed his head and died. *Mubwa naakabona meenda wakamvwa nyota aboobo wakakotama kuti anywe.* = When the dog saw water it became thirsty and so bowed its head down to drink. (1.-kotamwa, 2.-kotamide, 3.-kotamika, 4.-kotamina, 5.-kotaminalyo, 6.-kotamisya, 7.-kotama-kotama, 8.-kotamikana)

bend forward, *Kokotamika mutwe.* = Bend your head. *Kokotamika mwana aleke kulungumana.* = Bend the child's head down so that s/he stops looking upwards. (1.-kotamikwa, 2.-kotamikide, 4.-kotamikila, 5.-kotamikilalyo, 6.-kotamikisya, 7.-kotamika-kotamika, 8.-kotamikana)

bow down before or into, *Tukotamina Leza* = We bow down to God. *Sincinko naakali kunywa meenda* wakakotamina munongo. = When the mad person was drinking water he bowed down into the water pot. (1.-kotaminwa, 2.-kotamide, 3.-kotamika, 4.-kotaminina, 5.-kotamininalyo, 6.-kotaminisya, 7.-kotamina-kotamina, 8.-kotaminana)

turn one's face upwards lift the head, Naabuka wakotamuka = When he woke he lifted up his head. (1.-kotamukwa, 2.-kotamukide, 3.-kotamusya, 4.-kotamukila, 5.-kotamukilalyo, 6.-kotamukisya, 7.-kotamuka-kotamuka, 8.-kotamukana)

lift up someone's head, *Komukotamuna* mutwe, waminwa mulwazi. = Lift up the patient's head, she is tired. (1.-kotamunwa, 2.-kotamunide, 3.-kotamusya, 4.-kotamunina, 5.-kotamuninalyo, 6.-kotamunisya, 7.-kotamuna-kotamuna, 8.-kotamunana)

become thin, Wakotela akaambo kakuciswa-ciswa. = He has become thin because of the sickness. (1.-kotelwa, 2.-kotede, 3.-kotezya, 4.-kotelela, 5.-kotelelalyo, 6.-kotelesya, 7.-kotela-kotela, 8.-kotezyanya)

make thin, Kulima cilili cangu nkokwakandikotezya. = Ploughing my plot has made me thin. Kuumwa akutukilwa akulya misozi abuzuba, kubula bana, kutakkuta, kubula maanda mabotu amandumba akasaala azisamo zibotu ali-mwi kunyonkwa, ntotwaambo tumwi tu-kotezya bakaintu muminzi yabo. = Being beaten and insulted and weeping miser-ably every day, having no children, eating less food, having no good houses and warm blankets or good clothes and breast-feeding, these are some of the reasons which make the women thin in the villages. (extensions same as -kotela with 8.-kotezyanya)

depart on conclusion of work, Mwafwambaana kukotoka sunu, basa. = You have been quick to knock off work today, friends. (1.-kotokwa, 2.-kotokede, 3.-kotosya, 4.-kotokela, 5.-kotokelalyo, 6.-kotokesya, 7.-kotoka-kotoka, 8.-kotokana)

send away from work, Batukotola kufwambaana sunu. = They sent us away from work early today. (1.-kotolwa, 2.-kotwede, 3.-kotosya, 4.-kotosyezya, 5.-kotosyezyalyo, 6.-kotolesya, 7.-kotola-kotola, 8.-kotolana)

fill up with mucous, suds, etc., Meso aamwana atalika ku-kovwola, = The eyes of the child have begun to fill up with mucous. Nsipa eyi ilafwambaana kukovwola. = This soap produces a lot of suds. Also: -covwola. (1.-kovwolwa, 2.-kovwede, 3.-kovwosya, 4.-kovwolela, 5.-kovwolelalyo, 6.-kovwolesya, 7.-kovwola-kovwola)

seem to be, Izuba lyakali-zwile, pesi kwakali kukoya anga talininga-zwa akaambo kasikunku wakasinkide nyi-ka yoonse. = The sun had come out, but it seemed as if it had not come out because of the mist which blotted out the whole world.

resemble, Mwana oyu ukozya ni? = Who does this child resemble? (1.-kozyegwa, 2.-kozyede, 3.-kozyezya, 4.-kozyela, 5.-kozyelalyo, 6.-kozyesya, 7.-kozya-kozya, 8.-kozyanya)
  • poison, Munanga wakabakozya musamu balwazi, ncibakafwa. = The witchdoctor poisoned the patients with medicine, that is why they died.

pretend, Ta-koledwe, ulikozya-kozya buya. = He is not drunk, he is only pretending.
  • cough, Umwi mubbi naakali kubba myuungu mumuunda taakandibwene pe. Naakamana kucela, ndakalikozya-kozya kutegwa azyibe kuti ndamujanikizya kaci bba. = A certain thief was stealing pumpkins in the field and did not see me. After she had finished gathering, I coughed on purpose so that she would know that I had found her stealing.
be alike, Aaba bobilo

kapati. = These two are very much alike. Ooyu *balakozyanya* amwana wangu wakaandula nkanya. = This one resembles my first born child. Naluntaambwe *wakalikozyanya* amatu anyanzabili kutegwa atabonwi. = The chameleon made itself like the green leaves so as not to be seen. (1.-konzyanyigwa | -konzyanyisyigwa, 2.-konzyene, | -konzyenye, 3.-konzyanisya, 4.-konzyanina, 5.-konzyaninalyo, 6.-konzyaninsya, 7.-konzyanya-kozyanya.)
  • make oneself resemble, Mubbi wakali kuyanda *kulikozyanya* amwana okwabo kutegwa atazyibwi kufwambaana. = The thief wanted to become like his relative so as not to be recognized quickly.
look alike, rt. -kozya, Aba bana *balikozyene* mbuli bamaanga. = These children resemble each other like twins.

look alike, rt. -kozya, Bana bamaanga *balikozyenye* kumeso. = Twins are facially alike. Maanda akali munsi-munsi amugwagwa oyo mudolopo akali kwiide *kukozyenye* mbuli kuti mmuntu omwe wakaayaka. = The houses which were beside one another on that road in the city were just the same as if it is one person who had built them.

be finished for one season, Masuku *alakuba* mumwezi wa Nalupale. = The masuku fruits are finished by the month of December. Munyengele ulasaanguna *kukuba*, gunga zilacaalila. Nozikuba azyalo, basimpongo balapenga. = The long grass is first to finish, the gunga grass remains. When that also finishes the goatherds suffer. Yoonse micelo yamusyokwe yakamana supu kulya, imwi yakali *kukuba*. = All the fruits of the bush had been eaten up, some had gone out of season.(1.-kubwa, 2.-kubide, 3.-kubya, 4.-kubila, 5.-kubilalyo, 6.-kubisya, 7.-kuba-kuba, 8.-kubana)
  • push, Kokuba ncinga yako mucimvwule nkaambo kulapya. = Push your bicycle under the shade as it is hot. Also: -kkuba, -tonka.
wash oneself quickly, Kamundilindila basa ndicilikuba-kuba mumaulu.= Wait for me my friends, I am still quickly washing my legs.

become mature, Musankwa *wakakubuka*. = The boy matured. Budima bwakali kuumwa mazuba afwa bantu amazuba ngobakali *kukubuka* basankwa. Bakali kuyanda nkuku zyakujaya zyakusekelela basankwa *bakubuka*. = The budima drums were beaten during the days of funerals and on the days when boys reached adolescence. They were looking for chickens to kill to celebrate the boys who had matured. (1.-kubukwa, 2.-kubukide, 3.-kubuzya, 4.-kubukila, 5.-kubukilalyo, 6.-kkubukisya, 7.-kubuka-kubuka) Also: -jinka.
come out of fixed position like nail or tooth, Eeyi mpikili yakuka kuzwa mpuyasyonkedwe. = This nail has come out of the position in which it was fixed. Mwana ooyu wakatalika kale ku
menyo. = This child's teeth have already started to fall out. Also: -lukuka. (1.-kukwa, 2.-kukide, 3.-kukuzya, 4.-kukila, 5.-kukilalyo, 6.-kukisya, 7.-kuka-kuka)

fall out, fall down, Keembe kangu kakukkuka kuzwa mumwiini. = My axe blade has come out of its handle. Niyakakukkuka nyenyezi jilo masiku, bantu boonse bakali kuzyana nkolola bakayoowa. = When a star dropped last night, all the people who were dancing at the initiation ceremony were afraid. (1.-kukkukwa, 2.-kukkukide, 3.-kukkuzya, 4.-kukkukila, 5.-kukkukilalyo, 6.-kukkukisya, 7.-kukkuka-kukkuka)

take out, as an axe blade from the handle, *Nguni wakakukkula keembe kangu, bana nywebo?* = You children, who took the blade out of my axe? (1.-kukkulwa, 2.-kukkwide, 3.-kukkuzya, 4.-kukkwida, 5.-kukkwidalyo, 6.-kukkulisya, 7.-kukkula-kukkula, 8.-kukkkulana)

writhe, flinch, bend down in fear, *Kana kankuku kakakukubala munsi acisamu sikakonze naakatiikalume.* = The chicken crouched down beside a tree when the jackal buzzard was about to snatch it. (2.-kukubede, 3.-kukubazya, 4.-kukubalila, 5.-kukubalilalyo, 6.-kukubalisya, 7.-kukubala-kukubala) Also: -kokobala.

be bruised, *Nokuba kuti wabelekesya buti canguzu limwi inga waakwiide kukubauka magwezyo, taku cijanika pe.* = No matter how hard you work even to be just bruised on the shoulders, there is no profit from it.

brush for, sweep for, rt. kukula, *Aaba bakaintu mbotubambene limwi balatuma bana babo kundikukuda mulubuwa.* = This woman who lives next door sends her children to sweep the courtyard for me. (1.-kukudwa, 2.-kukude, 4.-kukudila, 5.-kukudilalyo, 6.-kukudisya, 7.-kukudakukuda, 8.-kukudana) Also: kukwida
fall out as teeth Also: -kulumbuka

sweep, clear away, clean out, *Kuyandika kukukula alubuwa kusalale.* = It is necessary to sweep the courtyard so that it becomes clean. *Mucembele wakali kubaanina kumwaka bana naakali kukukula makuba mumuu-* nda wakwe. The old lady was telling stories in the dry season to the children in her field when she was clearing away the maize stalks. *Cisozi nicakaboola cakakukula mapopwe oonse akali kumuunda.* = When the locusts came they wiped out all the maize in the field. (1.-kukulwa, 2.-kukwide, 3.-kukuzya, 4.-kukwida, 5.-kukwidalyo, 6.-kukulisya, 7.-kukulakukula.)
slip, as from a load Also: -cululuka

be concluded, end, as funeral ritual, *Kalitanakukulwa dilwe, basimukowa bakakkala kuti bajane nzila yakatola mufwu.* = Before the funeral ritual was concluded, the relatives sat to find a way to know the cause of death. *Mulembwe bakamulila mazuba one, nkabela bakasala kuti obu Bwasanu cifwumofwumo lizookukulwe dilwe.* They mourned Mulembwe for four days, then they chose that on the fifth day in the morning the funeral should end.

slither, as sledge drawn by oxen, or to describe movement of snake, *Inzoka ikukuma buya kweenda.* = A snake slithers along as it moves. *Cilayi noceenda cilakukuma.* The sledge slithers along as it moves. (1.-kukumwa, 2.-kukumide, 3.-kukumya, 4.-kukumina, 5.-kukuminalyo, 6.-kukumisya, 7.-kukuma-kukuma)
  • crowd in, *Bana bankuku baali kukukuma munsi abanyina.* = The chicks were crowding in beside the mother.

sharpen, *Wakakukumuna panga lyakwe kuti abakosole mitwe.* He sharpened his blade so that he would cut off their heads. (1.-kukumunwa, 2.-kukumwide, 3.-kukumuzya, 4.-kukumwida, 5.-kukumwidalyo, 6.-kukumunisya, 7.- kukumuna-kukumuna)

gulp, Sincinko wakakukumwina cigabba camukupa cipati. = The mad person gulped down a big tin of milk. (1.-kukumwinwa, 2.-kukumwide, 3.-kukumwizya, 4.-kukumwida, 5.-kukumwidalyo, 6.-kukumwinisya, 7.-kukumwina-kukumwina) Also: -ngungumwina.

gnaw, Ino cilanona cifwuwa ncokukuta boobo? = Is the bone sweet that you gnaw it so? Also: -kukuzyula, lukuvwula. (1.-kukutwa, 2.-kukutide, 3.-kukutya, 4.-kukutila, 5.-kukutilalyo, 6.-kukutisya, 7.-kukutakukuta, 8.-kukutana)

gnaw, Kamukukuzyula nyama imanine kuzifwuwa. = Gnaw all the meat down to the bones. Mbocikukuzyula kubee ucita mulimo mupati. = It seems that you are doing a mighty job by the way you gnaw. (1.-kukuzyula, 2.-kukuzyulide, 3.-kukuzyuzya, 4.-kukuzyulila, 5.-kukuzyulilalyo, 6.-kukuzyulisya, 7.-kukuzyula-kukuzyula) Also: -lukuvwula
  • pare off, Kokukuzyula makwa amuyanda wamusamu ujike. = Pare the bark off the root of the tree and then cook it.

pay marriage installment, Amumvwe zintu ezi nzyobakalikukwa mbuli: meja abazovwu, maamba abunduwe (aabulumbu), inombe, impongo, alimwi ampande. = Note the things which they were paying in receiving a girl in marriage, like: elephants tusks, hoes, cattle and cowry shells. Ezi nombe tiizyaali zyakukwa peepe, zyakali buyo zyamulandu wakutizya mwanaamuntu. = These cows were not the marriage payment, they were just for the offence of running off illegally with someone's daughter. (1.-kukwedwa, 2.-kukwede, 3.-kukwazya, 4.-kukweda, 5.-kukwedalyo)

sweep for, rt. kukula, Sena mwandikukwida kabuwa? = Have you swept the little courtyard for me? Bamakaintu baunka kukukukwida mulwazi. The women went to sweep for the patient. (1.-kukwidwa, 2.-kukwidide, 3.-kukwidizya, 4.-kukwidila, 5.-kukwidilalyo, 6.-kukwidisya, 7.-kukwida-kukwida, 8.-kukwidana)

pull out of fixed position, Bamukula menyo nibali kulwana beenzinyina. They have knocked out his teeth when they were fighting. Kuli baaba batakwe mikowa bakali kukula buyo jamba akutila maanzi mumpako yamwiini akwaamba kuti, "Utakatubooleli." = For those without a clan they were detaching the head from the hoe-handle and pouring water into the hole of the handle saying (to the spirit), "Do not come back to us." (1.-kulwa, 2.-kulide, 3.-kuzya, 4.-kulila, 5.-kulilalyo, 6.-kulisya, 7.-kula-kula)
  • mature, Kakula kana kamutumbu lino. The child of the suckling mother has grown. Imvwula noiwa, syokwe azimena zyoonse zilakula. = When the rain falls the grass and all other seedlings grow. Also: -komena.
  • pluck unripe fruit, Bataata bakabauma bana nibakali kukula mango. = My father beat the children when they were plucking the unripe mangoes. Also: -onza, -kulumbula.

use hoe to clean yard, Bana bakula-kula lubuwa kuzinguluka nanda. The children are cleaning the yard around the house. (1.-kulwa-kulwa, 2.-kulide-kulide)
  • pluck quickly, rt. -kula, Kamukulakula mango nobatanaboola balaawo. = Quickly pluck the mangoes before the owners come.
  • rub beak against the ground, scratch Also: kwenga-kwenga

carry away, Bamuka Simalambo bakakulaika zintu zyabo zyoonse nobakaya kwabo. = The wife of Simalambo carried away all her possessions when she went back home. Wakulaika beembezi. = The shepherd has departed. (a phrase said when someone important, like a famous hunter, dies.)
  • become pregnant, Kasindi wakalizumenene kuzyala, nkaambo kunyina mukaintu unga waikkalilila nanda itabonwi bana, mpoona wakulaika kale alimwi. = Kasindi persevered in trying to have children, because no woman can sit in the house where children are not seen, thereupon she soon became pregnant again. (1.-kulaikwa, 2.-kulaikide, 3.-kulaisya, 4.-kulaikila, 5.-kulaikilalyo, 6.-kulaikisya, 7.-kulaika-kulaika) Also: -cilaika.

pass as years, Kukulauka myaka, tasiki kumunzi kwabo. = As the years pass, he does not come home. Banyama bakali kupona cakuliiba kakukulauka mazuba, nsondo, myezi amyaka kakunyina kuyoowa. = The animals were living in freedom as the days, weeks, months and years passed without fear. (1.-kulaukwa, 2.-kulaukide, 3.-kulaukizya, 4.-kulaukila, 5.-kulaukilalyo, 6.-kulaukisya, 7.-kulauka-kulauka)
  • occur in great numbers, Mwaka wantomba bantu bakakulauka kufwa. = In the year of smallpox the people died in large numbers.

pluck unripe fruits, rt. -kula, Bana bacikolo bakaakulaula mango oonse mumbewu yangu. The pupils plucked all the mangoes in my garden. (1.-kulaulwa, 2.-kulaulide, 3.-kulauzya, 4.-kulaulila, 5.-kulaulilalyo, 6.-kulaulisya, 7.-kulaula-kulaula)

put load on one's shoulder, Mwalikulika mukuli mupati, kakuli bantu banga bamugwasya nkobali. = You are lifting a big load yourself, while there are people present who might help you. Naakamana kugonka masamu, wakakulika zisamu zyakwe, alimwi keembe waka-pakata agwezyo. When he had finished cutting down trees, he put his wood on his shoulder and also put his axe on his shoulder. Musimbi wakalizyi kabotu kuti walipa mazwipu inga camukulika nciinga Chidaala akumutola nkucakali kuyanda. The girl knew that if she behaved foolishly, the horrid Chidaala would carry her on his shoulders and take her to where he wanted. (1.-kulikwa, 2.-kulikide, 3.-kulisya, 4.-kulikila, 5.-kulikilalyo, 6.-kulikisya, 7.-kulika-kulika, 8.-kulikana)
  • take on extra pain to free oneself from problem, Bamupa musamu wakulikulika kuti asoomone. = They have given him medicine however unpleasant to use to make him purge.

carry on one's shoulders, rt. kulika, Bakali kusola kumunyanga nyama njakulikide agwezyo. = They tried to take from him the meat which he was carrying on his shoulders. Wakasika akasaka kamapopwe ulikulikide alwezo. = He arrived with a sack of maize on his shoulder. Bausyi bakali kumutobela munyati kumwi kabakulikide ntobolo yabo aluwezo. His father was following the buffalo while carrying a gun on his shoulder.
give presents of cast-offs or second-hand things.
become bald, Mutwe wakakuluka. The head has become bald. (2.-kulukide, 3.-kuluzya, 4.-kulukila, 5.-kulukilalyo, 6.-kulukisya, 7.-kulukakuluka) Also: -lukuvwula
be permanently bald, rt. kuluka, Mutwe wasikube ulikulukide. = The head of the vulture is ever bald.
scratch, Inkuku yali kukulukuuta. = A chicken was scratching the ground. Also: -yanga-yanga.

shave off completely, Bamukulula mutwe woonse azwa masusu. = They shaved off all the hair from his head.
  • take out from mouth, Ino ayebo utani kuyeeyi kuti bbule mmunyama ukozyenye akabwa kako nkiinga Munziwabunjaka nkonga kaluma sulwe uwakulula mukanwa. = Now you do not think that the antbear is an animal like your little dog Munziwabunjaka, which when it catches a hare, you remove it from it's mouth. (1.-kululwa, 2.-kulwide, 3.kuluzya, 4.-kulwida, 5.-kulwidalyo, 6.-kululisya, 7.-kulula-kulula, 8.-kululana)

fall down, Mudaala watyoka kasolo naakululuka kuzwa aciluli cananda ncaali kuvwumba. = The old man broke his hip when he slipped down from the roof of the house which he was thatching. (2.-kululukide, 3.-kululuzya, 4.-kululukila, 5.-kululukilayo, 6.-kululukisya, 7.-kululuka-kululuka) Also: -kulumbuka.

fall out or down, Mango akulumbuka. The mangoes have fallen down. Kuti katutalondoli meno esu, ayakukulumbuka. If we don't take proper care of our teeth, they will fall out. Nindakaintamuka, kumeso misozi yakali kwiile kukulumbuka. When I looked up, the tears were flowing down from the eyes. (2.-kulumbukide, 3.-kulumbuzya, 4.-kulumbukila, 5.-kulumbukilalyo, 6.-kulumbukisya, 7.kulumbukakulumbuka) Also: -kululuka
  • pass by, Mazuba alimwi mvwiki zyakakulumbuka mulimo kautajaniki. = Days and weeks passed without finding work.

knock down as fruit from a tree, Kamukulumbula masuku mu vwundike. Knock down the masuku fruit and store them to ripen. Kana kaceta kakali kusobana mumubula akukulumbula makoto ambula. A small monkey was playing in a mubula tree and knocked off unripe mbula fruits. (1.-kulumbulwa, 2.-kulumbwide, 3.-kulumbuzya, 4.-kulumbwida, 5.-kulumbwidalyo, 6.-kulumbulisya, 7.-kulumbula-kulumbula, 8.-kulumbulana)

be worn out as clothes or shoes, Impato zyasikalumamba zyakakulumpala akaambo kakutanta malundu. The shoes of the soldier were worn out because of climbing the hills. Banyokokulu balaa bongo bwakakulumpala. Your grandparent has brains which are worn out. (2.-kulumpalide, 3.-kulumpazya, 4.-kulumpalila, 5.-kulumpalilalyo, 6.-kulumpalisya, 7.-kulumpala-kulumpala)
  • grow tall without bearing fruit, Mapopwe akakulumpala akaambo kamvwula yakawa kapati. The maize is growing tall without bearing fruit because the rain fell heavily previously.
confuse, Mubbi ooyu watukulumpanya. This thief has confused us.

rush off with pupose of doing something, e.g Mubwa wakakulumuka kujata sulwe. = The dog rushed off to catch the hare. Mukuyoowa babwa bakulumukila munanda akuya kunjila mujungusi aabulo. In fear the dogs rushed into the house and went under the bed (1.-kulumukwa, 2.-kulumukide, 3.-kulumusya, 4.-kulumukila, 5.-kulumukilalyo, 6.-kulumukisya, 7.-kulumuka-kulumka, 8.-kulumukana)

be disturbed, Kuli kakulunga mumoyo. There is something troubling the heart. (1.-kulungwa, 2.-kulungide, 3.-kulungizya, 4.-kulungila, 5.-kulungilalyo, 6.-kulungisya, 7.-kulungakulunga) Also: -gulunga, -fwulunga.

move at high speed, Incinga ilakulunta kumungenyu. = The bicycle is going at high speed down the slope. (1.-kuluntwa, 2.-kuluntide, 3.-kuluntya, 4.-kuluntila, 5.-kuluntilalyo, 6.-kuluntisya, 7.-kulunta-kulunta)

become old, as clothes, Zisani zyamucembele zyakakulupula, tazicisamiki. = The clothes of the old woman have become old, they are no longer wearable. Also: -jujuka, -kweta. (1.-kulupulwa, 2.-kulupulide, 3.-kulupuzya, 4.-kulupulila, 5.-kulupulilalyo, 6.-kulupulisya, 7.-kulupula-kulupula, 8.-kulupulana)
  • eat plentifully, Bantu bakali kulupula nyama unakuti tababikki mwida pe. = The people were eating plenty of meat as if they were not putting it in their stomachs.

continue plucking unripe fruit, Masuku oonse akali mumusamu bakaakuluula jilo. = Yesterday they plucked all the masuku fruits which were on the tree. Also: -kula-kula, -kulaula. (1.-kuluulwa, 2.-kuluulide, 3.-kuluuzya, 4.-kuluulila, 5.-kuluulilalyo, 6.-kuluulisya, 7.-kuluula-kuluula, 8.-kuluulana)

cause to be shaved, rt. kulula, Ndakamukuluzya mwanaangu mumutwe kutegwa aboneke kabotu. = I had my child's head shaved so that he could appear respectable. (1.-kuluzyigwa, 2.-kuluzyizye, 3.-kuluzya, 4.-kuluzyizya, 5.-kuluzyizyalyo, 6.-kuluzyisya, 7.-kuluzya-kuluzya, 8.-kuluzyanya)

commit oneself, follow in a determined way, Kuti kakuli ncayanda, wakali kukulwaila mane kucijana. = If there was something he wanted, he would pursue it until he found it. (1.-kulwaizyigwa, 2.-kulwaide, 3.-kulwaizya, 4.-kulwailila, 5.-kulwaililalyo, 6.-kulwailisya, 7.-kulwaila-kulwaila, 8.-kulwaizyanya)
encourage, Mwana kutegwa acite kabotu kucikolo, uleelede kumukulwaizya mumilimo yakwe. = For a child to do well at school, you ought to encourage him in his works. (extensions same as for -kulwaila)

brew beer, stir, Baama bakumba bukoko. My mother is brewing beer. Bana ba Nampeyo balakumba Iwiindi tobilo amwaka. Ino minzi ikumbila antoomwe ili yotatwe. The people of Nampeyo brew beer for the Iwiindi ritual twice a year. Now the villages that brew together are three. (1.-kumbwa, 2.-kumbide, 3.-kumbya, 4.-kumbila, 5.-kumbilalyo, 6.-kumbisya, 7.-kumbakumba, 8.-kumbana.)
  • clean teeth, scrub or rub, Kamulikumba menyo nobana kutegwa mutani kuciswi. Brush your teeth children so that you do not become sick. Bakajana balikumba menyo akasamu kamubula mumbalimbali anzila. = She found her cleaning her teeth beside the path with a stick of the mubula tree.
  • incubate, sit on eggs, Mbooma yakali kukumba mayi. The python was sitting on eggs.
free anything from dirt by polishing, scrubbing, filing etc. Kamukumba-kumba bana abo basalale. = Tidy up those children so that they are clean. (duplicate extensions for -kumba)
rub against another (like boughs of a tree), Mitabi yazisamu ilakumbana mpoiswaanganina. = The branches of the tree rub against one another where they touch.

embrace, Moonde naakazwidilila kucikolo, bausyi bakamukumbata calumwemwe. When Moonde passed his exams at school, his father embraced him happily. Mebo ndakakkala munsi lyakwe ndamukumbata akuboko kumwi. = I sat down beside her and embraced her with one arm. Also: -vwubata (1.-kumbatwa, 2.-kumbete, 3.-kumbatya, 4.-kumbatila, 5.-kumbatilalyo, 6.-kumbatisya, 7.-kumbata-kumbata, 8.-kumbatana)
  • fold the arms, Ulalikumbata akaambo kabuumba. = He is folding his arms because of loneliness.

embracing one another, rt. kumbata, Webo nekujana mbuli waawa mulikumbetene inga ndati mbubona obo mbucakalengwa. = When I find you there like this embracing one another I say, this is how it was created to be.

pray for something, ask for, beg, Ndikumbila Mwami kuti ndijane nceyanda. = I am praying to the Lord that I get what I want. Munzi wamuntu noubona takutegwa ulaleya kuti nkakumbile meenda amunzi ulya pe. = Even when you see the village of a person it does not mean that you can go in and ask for water at that village. Also: -lomba. (1.-kumbilwa, 2.-kumbide, 3.-kumbizya, 4.-kumbilila, 5.-kumbililalyo, 6.-kumbilisya, 7.-kumbila-kumbila, 8.-kumbilana)
  • brew beer in, rt. -kumba, Ndiyakukumbila mubbulo eli bukoko. = I shall be brewing beer in this drum.

be brushed clean, Inseke zyamusikili nozikumbuka zilategwa 'mombola'. = When the seeds of the musikili tree are brushed clean they are called mombola. Bakatalika kugela boya boonse bwakali kumucila limwi mucila wakakumbuka mbuli tuvwu lyabbanana. = They began to cut all the hair which was on the tail until the tail was as clean as banana leaves. (1.-kumbukwa, 2.-kumbulide, 3.-kumbuzya, 4.-kumbukila, 5.-kumbukilalyo, 6.-kumbukisya, 7.-kumbuka-kumbuka)

clean by rubbing, wash well, Micelo ikumbula meno abana. = Fruits clean the teeth of children. Basimbi balalikumbula mumulonga. = The girls are washing themselves thoroughly in the river. (1.-kumbulwa, 2.-kumbwide, 3.-kumbuzya, 4.-kumbulila, 5.-kumbulilalyo, 6.-kumbulisya
8.-kumbulana)

covet, desire greedily, Ndali kulikumbuzya kumusankwa ooyu. = I desired the wealth of this man for myself. Ndalikulikumbuzya lubono Iwamudaala ooyu. = I coveted the wealth of this old man. (1.-kumbuzyigwa, 2.-kumbuzyide, 4.-kumbuzyizya, 5.-kumbuzyizyalyo, 6.-kumbuzyisya, 7.-kumbuzya-kumbuzya, 8.-kumbuzyanya)

pluck, Bataata bakandituma kukumpala mango obilo. = My father sent me to pluck two mangoes. (1.-kumpalwa, 2.-kumpalide, 3.-kumpalizya, 4.-kumpalila, 5.-kumpalilalyo, 6.-kumpalisya 7.-kumpala-kumpala) Also: -kumpula.

detach, as leaves Kokumpaula kabotu matu aacisyu. = Pluck the leaves of relish properly. Kamuya bukumpaula zitende tutolele bana. = Go and pull out the pumpkins so that we take them to the children. (1.-kumpaulwa, 2.-kumpaulide, 3.-kumpauzya, 4.-kumpawida, 5.-kumpawidalyo, 6.-kumpaulisya, 7.-kumpaula-kumpaula, 8.-kumpaulana)

fall, as leaf or flower, Mungu wakumpuka ngobayandisya baama. = The pumpkin which my mother relishes has fallen off. (2.-kumpukide, 3.-kumpuzya, 4.-kumpukila, 5.-kumpukilalyo, 6.-kumpukisya, 7.-kumpukakumpuka)

pull down, pluck, Kokumpula itu lyamusekese utafwune. = Pluck a leaf of the musekese tree and chew it. Katukumpula mango obilo tukwange. = Let us pluck two mangoes and eat them raw. Also: -cela. (1.-kumpulwa, 2.-kumpwide, 3.-kumpuzya, 4.-kumpwida, 5.-kumpwidalyo, 6.-kumpulisya 7.-kumpula-kumpula)

unsheath, Wakakumuna panga kutegwa akosole mitwe yabasinkondonyina. = He drew his weapon so as to cut off the heads of his enemies. (1.-kumunwa, 2.-kumwide, 3.-kumuzya, 4.-kumwida, 5.-kumwidalyo, 6.-kumunisya, 7.-kumuna-kumuna, 8.-kumunana) Also: -fwumuna.

pour, Kamukuna meenda munywida nkuku, kutegwa zinywe. = Pour water into the hens trough for them to drink. Wakabweza saka lyamatu walikuna mumulonga. = He took a sack of leaves and poured it into the river. (1.-kunwa, 2.-kunide, 3.-kunizya, 4.-kunina, 5.-kuninalyo, 6.-kunisya, 7.-kuna-kuna)
  • be balanced, Kamucibikka ambi mapopwe nkaambo tacinakuna cikkelo. = Add more maize because the scales have not yet balanced. Also: -guna.
  • be disproportionate, not match, (in size, intelligence, ability etc.) Kuti mulombwana wakuna kumukaintu wakwe tacilangiki kabotu. = If a man is disproportionate to his wife in height it doesn't look well.

be at a slope or unbalanced, Itebule Iyakunama, talikkede kabotu. = The table is lop-sided, it does not sit properly. Also: -pesyama, -sendama (1.-kunamwa, 2.-kunamide, 3.-kunamya, 4.-kunamina, 5.-kunaminalyo, 6.-kunamisya, 7.-kunama-kunama)

tilt, Igande lyakakilwa kwiikunamika nongo. = The frog failed to tilt the clay pot. Naakakunamika nongo kwakatika bukoko busyoonto. = When he tilted the pot a little beer was spilt. (1.-kunamikwa, 2.-kunamakide, 3.-kunamika, 4.-kunamikila, 5.-kunamikilalyo, 6.-kunamikisya, 7.-kunamika-kunamika, 8.-kunamikana)

die in great numbers, Kwakabanjila ntomba. Bakakunauka akufwa. = They were infected with smallpox. They died in great numbers. (2.-kunaukide, 4.-kunaukila, 5.-kunaukilalyo, 6.-kunaukisya, 7.-kunauka-kunauka)
  • move up and down, as a boat, Bwato bwakali kukunauka mumayuwe. = The boat was going up and down on the waves.

fall out, as hair, Chilala naakaciswa kanswende, masusaakwe akakundyuuka. = When Chilala was sick with gonorrhoea, his hair fell out. (2.-kundyuukide, 3.-kundyuuzya, 4.-kunduukila, 5.-kundyuukilalyo, 6.-kundyuukisya, 7.-kundyuukakundyuuka) Also: -kuluka, -jundauka.

have no hair, rt. -kundyuuka, Muteyo lya Choonzwe mwa kali kukkala sikoswe mucembele waka kundyuukide boya. = In a thicket of Choonzwe an old female rat lived which had no hair. Also: -junduukide, -kulukides, -jundaukide.

gather up, Mbwaakabukila nkukunga mabwe, waunka kuti akaume Sautu. = As soon as he got up he gathered stones, he went to beat Sautu. (1.-kungwa, 2.-kungide, 3.-kungizya, 4.-kungila, 5.-kungilalyo, 6.-kungisya, 7.-kunga-kunga, 8.-kungilana)
gather many things together, Kamukunga-kunga makuba mumuunda aumpwe. = Gather up all the stalks in the field so that they be burnt. Also: -bungika.

make smooth, Chimbwali naakamana kufwala mwiini, waka ukunguba. = When Chimbwali had finished carving the handle, he smoothened it. Also: -kwenkweza, -kwiizinga, -kwizinga. (1.-kungubwa, 2.-kungubide, 3.-kungubya, 4.-kungubila, 5.-kungubilalyo, 6.-kungubisya, 7.-kunguba-kunguba)

lie down carelessly, without blankets Sele waile kukungubala anze. Sele was just sleeping outside without blankets. (1.-kungubalwa, 2.-kungubede, 3.-kungubika, 4.-kunubalila, 5.-kungubalilayo, 6.-kungubalisya, 7.-kungubala-kungubala)
be unsuitable, rt. -kuna, Uulya musankwa ulikunide kumukaintu wakwe. That man does not suit his wife, (in size, intelligence, age etc.)

enkindle, Kunka mulilo Mutinta tufwambaane kujika. = Mutinta, light the fire so that we quickly cook. (1.-kunkwa, 2.-kunkide, 3.-kunkizya, 4.-kunkila, 5.-kunkilalyo, 6.-kunkisya, 7.-kunka-kunka, 8.-kunkana.) Also: -kutula, -vwutula.
  • flow, Meenda alakunka mumbewu. = Water is flowing in the garden.

increase the fire by pushing wood together, Kamukunkanya mulilo uyake. = Push the wood together so that the fire lights. Wakakunkanya masisi akajisi mulilo. = He increased the fire on the embers which were burning. (1.-kunkanyizigwa, 2.-kunkanyizyide, 3.-kunkanyizyisya, 4.-kunkanyizyila, 5.-kunkanyizyilalyo, 6.-kunkanyizyisya, 7.-kunkanya-kunkanya)

break off, Munene wakatuma mwana kuya kukunkaula mulilo kutegwa afwebe. The old man sent a child to break off a piece from the fire so that he would smoke. Also: -konkoola. (1.-kunkaulwa, 2.-kunkawide, 3.-kunkauzya, 4.-kunkawida, 5.-kunkawidalyo, 6.-kunkaulisya, 7.-kunkaula-kunkaula, 8.-kunkaulana.

light fire for, rt. -kunka, Bamakaintu bali kukunkila munene mulilo. = The women were lighting a fire for the old man. (1.-kunkilwa, 2.-kunkilide, 3.-kunkilizya, 4.-kunkilila, 5.-kunkililalyo, 6.-kunkilisya, 7.-kunkila-kunkila, 8.-kunkilana)
light with, rt. kunka, Kwakali makwa ngobakali kukunkizya mulilo. = There were pieces of bark with which they were lighting the fire. (for extensions see -kunka)

break hard ground, scratch with a hoe, Ndali kukunkula mumuunda. = I was breaking the hard ground in the field (with a hoe). Boonse bakali kukunkula zindongwe zyabo amyuunda yabo. All were breaking up their groundnut patches and their fields. (1.-kunkulwa, 2.-kunkwide, 3.-kunkuzya, 4.-kunkwida, 5.-kunkwidalyo, 6.-kunkulisya, 7.-kunkula-kunkula)

roll along, Wali kukunkulika mbuli bbola lyamaulu nkaambo kakukolwa. He was rolling along like a football because of being drunk. Mainza wakakunkulisya ncili. Mainza rolled the mortar along. (2.-kunkulikide, 3.-kunkulisya, 4.-kunkulikila, 5.-kunkulikilalyo, 6.-kunkulikisya, 7.-kunkulika-kunkulika)

look downwards, Ncekunkumana, mutwe ulacisa. = The reason I am looking down is that my head is paining. Also: -sintama, -gogomana. (1.-kunkumanwa, 2.-kunkumanide, 3.-kunkumanika, 4.-kunkumanina, 5.-kunkumaninalyo, 6.-kunkumanisya. 7.-kunkumana-kunkumana)
  • be round shaped, Ooyu muntu, mutwe kukunkumana. Ubee ndibbola! = This person, the head is round. It is like a football!
  • rush to, Kunyina mulombwana naba mukaintu wakacaala mumunzi, boonse bakakunkumukila kucikolo. = Not a man or a woman remained at the village, all rushed to the school.

fall as leaves, Busimbi bukunkumuka mbuli malubaluba amusamu. Kuti malubaluba akunkumuka ansi, taakwe cikonzya kwaanamatika kumusamu. = Girlhood falls like leaves from a tree. If the leaves fall off, there is no one who is able to stick them back on the tree. (1.-kunkumukwa, 2.-kunkumukide, 3.-kunkumuzya, 4.-kunkumukila, 5.-kunkumukilalyo, 6.-kunkumukisya, 7.-kunkumuka-kunkumuka)
  • disperse quickly, e.g Bantu boonse bakakunkumuka kweenda mwabo-mwabo dilwe kalitanaakumana akaambo kamvwula mpati. = All the people dispersed and went to their homes before the funeral was finished, due to the heavy rain.

rush to, rt. -kunkumuka, Kunyina mulombwana naba mukaintu wakacaala mumunzi, boonse bakakunkumukila kucikolo. = Not a man or a woman remained at the village, all rushed to the school. Also: -mwaika. (1.-kunkumukilwa, 2.-kunkumukide, 3.- kunkumuzya, 4.-kunkumukila, 5.-kunkumukilalyo, 6.-kunkumukisya, 7.-kunkumukila-kunkumukila)

dust, beat off, make fall or shake off, Muwo munji nguukunkumuna matuvwu aamusamu mumwezi wa Kunkumuna-masamu. = A strong wind makes the leaves fall off trees during the month of July. Kacumbika ulakunkumuna mulanzyi. = Kacumbika is shaking off the termites. Muleya was beating a heap of clothes. = Muleya wakali kukunkumuna cilwi cazisani. Also: -bombola (1.-kunkumunwa, 2.-kunkumunide /-kunkumwide, 3.-kunkumuzya, 4.-kunkumunina, 5.-kunkumwidalyo, 6.-kunkumunisya, 7.-kunkumunakunkumuna, 8.-kunkumunana.)
  • strike with a stone, Utija nzi? Kasimpe tulakukunkumuna bbwe. = Why are you running away? Truly we will strike you with a stone.
  • wipe dust off, Siluyasila naakabona kuti kunyina naakapona mweenzinyina wakali kunkumuna kumatako. = When Siluyasila saw that his friend was not recovering he shook the dust off his bottom i.e. he gave up trying to help him.

wipe with, rt. -kunkumuna, Ndalikunkumuzya cisani kugwisya kasuko acimbonimboni. = I was wiping the mirror with a cloth to remove dust. (1.-kunkumunwa, 2.-kunkumwide, 3.-kunkumuzya, 4.-kunkumwida, 5.-kunkumwidalyo, 6.-kunkumunisya, 7.-kunkumuzya-kunkumuzya, 8.-kunkumunana)

pour for, rt. -kuna, Ndamukunina cibwantu cisyoonto awalo kuti alabile. I poured out a little sweet beer for him to taste. (1.-kuninwa, 2.-kunide, 3.-kunizya, 4.-kunwida, 5.kunwidalyo, 6.-kunisya, 7.-kunina-kunina, 8.-kuninana)

make fire with, rt. -kunka, Bana bakatola nkuni zyakukunsya mulilo kuti banyinakulu bayote. The children took the firewood for making a fire so that their grandmother would warm herself. (1.-kunsyigwa, 2.-kunsyide, 3.-kunsyizya, 5.-kunsyizyalyo, 6.-kunsyisya, 7.-kunsyakunsya)

remove hair after applying hot water. Twali kukunta ngulube yaankolola kunanda. We were removing the hair from the pig with hot water for the initiation ceremony at home. (1.-kuntwa, 2.-kuntide, 3.-kuntizya, 4.-kuntila, 5.-kuntilalyo, 6.-kuntisya, 7.-kunta-kunta, 8.-kuntana)
  • extract fibres of sisal, *Ndali kukunta mukusa wamukkwilo.* = I was extracting fibres of sisal for a whip.
  • pedal furiously, *Mapulanga a Twaambo aumwi yakunta ncinga kuya kwa Magabba.* = Both Mapulanga and Twaambo were each pedaling their bi-cycle furiously going to Magabba.

pluck, *Twakamuka ku-kuntaula mpakatwa ncaatakazyala kabotu madeede.* = We were late in plucking the shoots that is why they did not bear big tomatoes. (1.-kuntaulwa, 2.-kuntawide, 3.-kuntauzya, 4.-kuntawida, 5.-kuntawidalyo, 6.-kuntaulisya, 7.-kuntaula-kuntaula) cf. -numfwaula.

go quickly, *Mubwa wangu ulakuntuka.* = My dog runs at high speed. (2.-kuntukide, 3.-kuntuzya, 4.-kuntukila, 5.-kuntukilalyo, 6.-kuntukisya, 7.-kuntuka-kuntuka)
  • fall off, *Matu alakuntuka kuzwa kumisamu.* = The leaves fall off the trees.

pluck, *Kokuntula itu lyomwe* = Pluck one leaf. (1.-kuntulwa, 2.-kuntwide, 3.-kuntuzya, 4.-kuntwida, 5.-kuntwidalyo, 6.-kuntulisya, 7.-kuntula-kuntula)
  • increase speed, *Mooya wakai-kuntula ncinga kuya ku Monze.* = Mooya was making the bicycle go fast to Monze.

sit pondering, *Naakamana kubuka cifwumofwumo waka-kuntumana mukkoce kalindila mucem-bele.* = When he got up in the morning he sat pondering on the verandah waiting for the old woman. Also: -fwufwumana, -tungumana
  • stand with legs apart

capsize, upset, *Bwato bwakunuka mulwaanje.* = The boat cap-sized in the lake. (2.-kunukide, 3.-kunu-zya, 4.-kunukila, 5.-kunukilalyo, 6.-kunukisya, 7.-kunuka-kunuka)
  • be spilt, flow out, *Meenda ali munongo akunuka.* = The water which was in the clay pot has been spilt. *Inswi zyakunuka kuzwa mumoono.* = The fish have escaped from the basket.
  • break out, *Mucembele naakaamba makani asesya, toonse twakakunuka ku-seka.* = When the old woman had said amusing things, we all burst out laughing.
  • sleep soundly, *Bantu banji baka-kunuka koona akaambo kakukatala ka-pati.* = Many people slept soundly be-cause of great tiredness.

pour out, *Mubwa wakaakununa mabisi jilo.* = The dog spilt the sour milk yesterday. Also: -tila, -tya. (1.-kununwa, 2.-kunwide, 3.-kunuzya, 4.-kunwida, 5.-kunwidalyo, 6.-kununisya, 7.-kununa-kununa, 8.-kununana)
  • cut up, *Bakatalika kukununa nu-ngu.* = They began to cut up the por-cupine.
pour into/for, rt. -kuna, *Kamumukunwida mucigumbuli omu.* = Pour it for her into this container. *Ndau-kunwida mucibulo mukupa.* = I have poured milk into a bucket. (extensions same as for --kununa)

indent, as a rat does cheese, gnaw dry meat off a bone, bite off mealies from cob, e.g *Nociyuma cinyama walo wali kukunya.* = Even though the meat was tough he was gnawing it. *Uluujisi kukunya cifwuwa canyama mu-bwa.* = The dog is fully occupied in gnaw-ing the bone. *Musankwa wakali kukunya minyonje, amana waya ali limbi kusikila wakkuta.* = The boy was gnawing fresh green maize, when he had finished he went to another one until he was full. *Mubwa walikukunya cifwuwa campongo.* = The dog was chewing the bone of a goat. Also: -syuta, -kukuta. (1.-kunyigwa, 2.-kunyide, 3.-kunyizya, 4.-kunyina, 5.-kunyinalyo, 6.-kunyisya, 7.-kunya-kunya, 8.-kunyana)

bale out, scoop out, Twali kukupa meenda mabi kuzwa mucikala. = We were scooping out dirty water from a well. (-kupa mume = shake off the dew) (1.-kupwa, 2.-kupide, 3.-kupya, 4.-kupila, 5.-kupilalyo, 6.-kupisya, 7.-kupa-kupa) Also: -yuwa,-bompola.

overflow, as water from bucket, Meenda ngaayumwide ali kukupaika kuzwa mukanongo. = The water which she was carrying was flowing over from the pot. Meenda alakupaika akaambo kakuzula kapati. = The water is overflowing because it is too full. (2.-kupaikide, 3.-kupaizya, 4.-kupaikila, 5.-kupaikilalyo, 6.-kupaikisya, 7.-kupaika-kupaika)

scatter, as water, Bana balikukupaila meenda a cibuye cananda. = The children were spraying water over the floor of the house. Also: -kupiika. (1.-kupailwa, 2.-kupailide, 3.-kupaizya, 4.-kupailila, 5.-kupaililayo, 6.-kupailisya, 7.-kupaila-kupaila, 8.-kupailana)

splash water onto, Wakabona kuti wakalimukide kumilimo aboobo cakubindaana wakalikupa-kupa amubili nkabela naakamana wakasama akuyumuka. = He saw that he was late for work and so he hurriedly splashed water onto his body and then when done he dressed and set off. (extensions are a duplication of -kupa with addition of 8.-kupana-kupana)

drive away, as flies, (1.-kupaulwa, 2.-kupawide, 3.-kupauzya, 4.-kupawida, 5.-kupawidalyo, 6.-kupaulisya, 7.-kupaula-kupaula, 8.-kupaulana) Also: -kusaula, -vwupaula, -fwisaula
  • drive off evil spirits, Munanga ukupaula mulwazi. = The witchdoctor drives the evil spirits away from the patient.

drive off evil spirits with, rt. -kupaula, Munanga wakabweza mucila ngwaakali kukupauzya, akankuli antoomwe apepe lyanduba. = The witch-doctor took a tail which he uses to drive off evil spirits, and a gourd together with the feather of the scarlet touraco (a bird)

be scattered, as water, Meenda akali munongo akali kukupiika mwana naakali kweenda. = The water which was in the pot was flowing over when the child was walking. (2.-kupiikide, 3.-kupiizya, 4.-kupiikila, 5.-kupiikilalyo, 6.-kupiikisya, 7.-kupiika-kupiika, 8.-kupiikana) Also: -kupaika.

water with hands or dish, rt. -kupa, Kamukupila meenda mucisyu amaanza. = Water the vegetable with your hands. (1.-kupilwa, 2.-kupilide, 3.-kupizya, 4.-kupilila, 5.-kupililalyo, 6.-kupilisya, 7.-kupila-kupila, 8.-kupilana)

prosper, Michelo wakakupuka kwiinda mukuuzya cisyumani. = Michelo prospered by selling vegetables. "Muvwuba ccacca" mmuzeezo wiimvwi kapati anzila zyakuyanda kukupuka antela kuyanda kujana lubono lunji cakutalanganya anzila zinga zyabelesegwa mukubujana. = "Get rich quick" is a term which stands out clearly in relation to the manner of getting rich or of finding much wealth without examining the means which are used to find it. (1.-kupukwa, 2.-kupukide, 3.-kupusya, 4.-kupukila, 5.-kupukilalyo, 6.-kupukisya, 7.-kupuka-kupuka)

strip off, scratch off, Cisamu candikupula amwiindi = The tree scratched me on the calf of the leg. (1.-kupulwa, 2.-kupwide, 3.-kupusya, 4.-kupulila, 5.-kupulilalyo, 6.-kupulisya, 7.-kupula-kupula, 8.-kupulana)
  • make prosper, Cisyumani cakamukupula Michelo mwakali. = Vegetables made Michelo prosper last year.
  • wash face, Bana mbubakamana buyo kulikupula kumeso, bakatalika kweenda kucikolo. = As soon as the children had washed their faces, they went to school.

peel off, as skin, Naakaumpwa, mutwe wakwe wakakupuluka. = When he was burnt, the skin of his head peeled off. (1.-kupulukwa, 2.-kupulukide, 3.-kupuluzya, 4.-kupulukila, 5.-kupulukilalyo, 6.-kupulukisya, 7.-kupuluka-kupuluka)
blister, Kasamu nkakandikupulula amwiindi. = It was a piece of wood which blistered my leg. Also: -cubbuula, -cubbaula

mop up with, rt. -kupa, Ndali kukupya cikukuzyo kuzwisya meenda ali munanda. = I was getting rid of the water from the house with a mop. (1.-kupwa, 2.-kupide, 3.-kupya, 4.-kupila, 5.-kupilalyo, 6.-kupisya, 7.-kupya-kupya)

remove pieces of bark with a stick from the sisal leaf when it is crushed, Nitwakamana kupwayapwaya mukusa, twakatalika kukusa kutegwa makwa azwe. When we had finished crushing the leaf of the sisal, we began to remove the pieces of crushed bark (this is done with a slender stick by rubbing the crushed bark). (1.-kusigwa, 2.-kuside, 3.-kusizya, 4.-kusila, 5.-kusilalyo, 6.-kusisya, 7.-kusakusa) Also: -kunta

drive away, Kokusaula nzinini zizwe kusyule lyako. = Drive away the flies from your back. Also: -kupaula, -gusa. (1.-kusaulwa, 2.-kusaulide, 3.-kusauzya, 4.-kusaulila, 5.-kusaulilalyo, 6.-kusaulisya, 7.-kusaula-kusaula, 8.-kusaulana)

pull out, Basankwa a basimbi balicizyi kukusula tulobo nobaloba nswi. Boys and girls know how to pull out the hooks when fishing. Also: - kwisula. (1.-kusulwa, 2.-kuswide, 3.-kusuzya, 4.-kuswida, 5.-kuswidalyo, 6.-kusulisya, 7.-kusula-kusula)
be greedy in eating to the exclusion of others, Mwana ulaa nzala ulalikuta. The hungry child eats ravenously. (2.- kutide, 3. kutya, 4.- kutilila, 5.- kutililalyo, 6.- kutisya, 7.- kuta-kuta)

work earnestly, Ooyu musankwa ulakutauka kucita mulimo wakwe. This boy does his work earnestly. Mujiki wali kukutauka kujikila beenzu. = The cook was busily cooking for the visitors. Ino kayi mpaawa ono kwasiya kale. Ma! Cikutauke buyo cimane. = Now look how it has already become dark. Let the matter be worked out so that it finishes. Also: -butauka. (1.-kutaukwa, 2.-kutaukide, 3.-kutausya, 4.-kutaukila, 5.-kutaukilalyo, 6.-kutaukisya, 7.-kutauka-kutauka, 8.-kutaukana

work busily for, Ndali kukutaukila mulwazi ncindamuka kusika kumuswaangano. = I was busily working for the patient, that is why I was late for the meeting. Taku wakasika munsi-munsi ampobakali kukutaukila basankwa. = No one came near to where the men where working. (same extensions as for -kutauka)

clean, Tacili cuubauba kulikutaula andelo nkaambo kuboko takusiki kabotu. It is not easy to clean oneself behind the shoulders because the arm does not reach there easily. (1.-kutaulwa, 2.-kutaulide, 3.-kutauzya, 4.-kutaulila, 5.-kutaulilalyo, 6.-kutaulisya, 7.-kutaula-kutaula, 8.-kutaulana)

pack round, as grass round an unplastered hut, Kamucikutila caanda campongo. Pack the grass around the goats shelter. Zivwuka zyakali kuyasigwa tusamu akukutilwa abwizu. = The huts were build with sticks and covered with grass. cf. -butila, -fwukutila. (1.-kutilwa, 2.-kutilide, 3.-kutizya, 4.-kutilila, 5.-kutililalyo, 6.-kutilisya, 7.-kutila-kutila, 8.-kutilana)
See -kutulizya (1.-kutilizyigwa, 2.-kutilizyide, 4.-kutilizyizya, 5.-kutilizyizyalyo, 6.-kutilizyisya, 7.-kutilizya-kutilizya)

drive animals, Kolangisisya kubbazu lyakujwe, ulababona bazovwu balasika nkaambo ndaunka kubakutula kubbazu lyakujwe. = Look carefully to the eastern side, you will see the elephants arriving because I go to drive them from the east. Also: -binga (1.-kutulwa, 2.-kutulide, 3.-kutuzya, 4.-kutuzyizya, 5.-kutuzyizyalyo, 6.-kutuzyisya, 7.-kutula-kutula)
  • light a fire, Mufwambaane kukutula mulilo mwamana mukasaazye meenda. = Hurry up and light the fire and when you are finished heat the water. Also: -vwutula.

do one action after another, Batumbu nibakali kukukula munanda bakakutulizya amulilo kutegwa bajikile mwana ceele. = When the mother was sweeping the house she then lit the fire to cook porridge for the child. Also: -kutilizya. (see extensions for -kutula)

boil medicines in a pot, cover the patient with a blanket, put the pot under the blanket so that the patient breathes in the fumes, Bakatalika kumukutuzya musamu. = They began to fumigate the patient. Also: -umpilila, (kumujika)

drive an animal to or for rt. kutula Wakazikutwida kubbazu nkwaakasiide mweenzinyina. = He drove the animals to the place where he had left his friend. (1. -kutwidwa, 2.-kutwide, 3.-kutwizya, 5.-kutwidalyo, 6.-kutwidisya, 7.-kutwida-kutwida, 8.-kutwidana) Also: -binga.

be barked at, rt. -kuwa, Wakajana kuti bakuugwa kabwa mbakwe bakwe. = He found that the people who were being barked at by the little dog were his in-laws. (2.-kuwide, 3.-kuwizya, 4.-kuwila, 5.-kuwilalyo, 6.-kuwisya, 7.-kuugwa-kuugwa, 8.-kuwana)

start out on a journey in a crowd, Mainza a Michelo bakacaala balikkede acikuta eliya boonse nobakakuumuka kuya kunkolola. = Mainza and Michelo remained behind sitting at the grass-shelter at the time when all set off for the inititation celebration. (1.-kuumukwa, 2.-kuumukide, 3.-kuumuzya, 4.-kuumukila, 5.-kuumukilalyo, 6.-kuumukisya, 7.-kuumuka-kuumuka, 8.-kuumukana.

bark, as a dog, Babwa bajisi mikuwilo nsini nobakuwa munyama anobakuwa muntu. = Dogs have different barks when they bark at an animal and when they bark at a human being. (1.-kuugwa, 2.-kuwide, 3.-kuwizya, 4.-kuwila, 5.-kuwilalyo, 6.-kuwisya, 7.-kuwa-kuwa, 8.-kuwana)

deliver marriage security, Nobakamana kwaanzya bakatalika kukwa baabo bakali basikukwegwa. = When they had finished greeting they began to deliver the marriage security or insurance to the bride's representatives. (in the past this was looked upon as a consolidation or ratification of the marriage rather than a business payment as is often the case nowadays) (1.-kwegwa, 2.-kwete, 3.-kwasya, 4.-kwasyizya, 5.-kwasyizyalyo, 6.-kwasisya, 7.-kwa-kwa, 8.-kwana)

be spread wide, like horns of some oxen, be horizontal, Ulya musune nguwangu nobalombwana. Uuli mudaala? Ulya uusubila ukwaalele meja. = That ox is mine, young men. Where, old man? The red one with the horizontal horns. (Inombe ikwaalete = a cow with horns growing horizontally) Kamukomezya mulyango basune bokwa taata meja alikwaalele. = Extend the entrance for the oxen of my father whose horns are spread sideways. (1.-kwaalizyigwa, 3.-kwaalazya, 4.-kwaalila, 5.-kwaalilalyo, 6.-kwaalisya, 7.-kwaalele-kwaalele)

tear into pieces, Nguni wakwaamuna cisani camwana? = Who tore the child's dress into pieces. (1.-kwaamuwa, 2.-kwaamwide, 3.-kwaamuzya, 4.-kwaamwida, 5. -kamwidalyo, 6.-kwaamunisya, 7.-kwaamunakwaamuna, 8.-kwaamunana)
  • call insulting names, Bakaintu bafwuma kumukwaamuna mulumi wabo nkaambo wakalede kubukoko. = The woman set out early to upbraid her husband because he had slept at the beer party. Also: -tukila, -sampaula.

lift up and down, Bakajata tukolo twabo kumwi kabatukwaapula kati, "Ootu tukolo twangu ntwaakali kunyonka. "She caught her little breasts while lifting them up and down saying, "These little breasts are the ones which he was sucking". Also: -kwapula. Muleya was beating the corn up and down while winnowing. = Muleya wakalikukwaapula mapopwe naakali kupupulula. (1.-kwaapulwa, 2.-kwaapwide, 3.-kwaapuzya, 4.-kwaapwida, 5.-kwaapwidalyo, 6.-kwaapulisya, 7.-kwaapula-kwaapula, 8.- kwaapulana)
  • insult, Mukaintu naakakolwa bukoko, wakatalika kukwaapula mulumi wakwe akati kabuleya. When the woman was drunk with beer, she began to insult her husband in public.
  • winnow, Baama bakwaapula musozya kuti bajike. Mother is winnowing the samp so that she cooks. Also: -bbeeta, -pupulula, -vwanka.
winnow with, Bamwi baluka zisuwo zyakubikkila busu akukwaapuzya musozya. Some weave baskets for putting flour in and for winnowing samp.

grab, parry a blow, catch a thing being thrown, receive as by mouth as a dog does with food, Ndacikwaba amaanza cipeni ncaali kuyanda kundiyasya. I grabbed with my hands the knife with which he wanted to wound me. Bazyali bamusankwa bakasyaazya kulindila kukwaba nkoli kuzwa kubazyali bamusimbi ngwaakatizya mwana abo. = The parents of the boy remained waiting (to grab the stick) to receive the complaint of the parents of the girl whose daughter their son had taken illegally for marriage. Also: -baka. (1.-kwabwa, 2.-kwabide, 3.-kwabya 4.-kwabila, 5. -kwabilalyo, 6.-kwabisya, 7.-kwaba-kwaba, 8.-kwabana)

catch an object thrown between one another, Nobakamanizyanya kukwabana masumo aakumulomo, mutumbu wakabweeda kumulimo wakwe. = When they has finished catching piercing comments thrown at one another, the woman returned to work.

beat, as with sjambok or stick, Mubbi bamukwabbaula ciindi naali kuyanda kubba nkuku. = They whipped the thief when he was about to steal the chickens. Kazila wakabakwabbaula basimbi limwi balila mbuli tubwa. = Kazila whipped the girls until they cried like puppies. Also: -kwibbaula, -vwimbuula. (1.-kwabbaulwa, 2.-kwabbaulide, 3.-kwabbauzya, 4.-kwabbawida, 5.-kwabbawidalyo, 6.-kwabbaulisya, 7.-kwabbaula-kwabbaula, 8.-kwabbaulana)

beat, Wakakwabbuzya kana acisamu. = He beat the child with a stick. (1.-kwabbuzyigwa, 2.-kwabbuzyide, 3.-kwabbuzyizye, 4.-kwabbuzyizya, 5.-kwabbuzyizyalyo, 6.-kwabbuzyisya 7.-kwabbuzya-kwabbuzya, 8.-kwabbuzyanya)
hang as a towel on both sides of a beam, Maliya wakakwabika katambala kakwe amulenga. = Maria hung her handkerchief on the line.
be protected, Bazyali bakalizyi kuti mwanaabo wakalikwabilidwe. The parents knew that their child was protected.

protect, Kobikka bwizu kuzinguluka nanda kukwabilila muwo. = Put grass around the house to protect it from the wind. Also: -kobelela, -fwukutila. (1.-kwabililwa, 2.-kwabilide, 3.-kwabilizya 4.-kwabililila, 5.-kwabililalyo, 6.-kwabililisya, 7.-kwabilila-kwabilila, 8.-kwabililana)

respond, as in a song, Mwaanguzi naakaangula, bantu bakamuka kukwabula. When the leader started the song, the people were slow in responding. (1.-kwabulwa, 2.-kwabwide, 3.-kwabuzya, 4.-kwabulila, 5.-kwabulilalyo, 6.-kwabulisya, 7.-kwabula-kwabula, 8.-kwabulana)

ward off with, rt. -kwaba, Bakali kweenzya zisalu zitegwa ntobo, zyakukwabya masumo aabafwusa bantu. = They were going about with skins, which are called shields, to ward off the spears which people threw. Lwiiyo Iweelede kuba ntobo yakukwabya mapenzi eesu, talweelede kuba ntobo yakukwabya bazyali besu kuti batasiki munsi lyesu. = Education should become a shield to ward off our sufferings, it ought not become a shield to drive off our parents so that they cannot come near us. (1.-kwabwa, 2.-kwabide, 3.-kwabya, 4.-kwabila, 5.-kwabilalyo, 6.-kwabisya, 7.-kwaba-kwaba, 8.-kwabana)

regain power, Munene wakateelela kuti mubili wamusankwa wakatalika kukwaima mpoona. = The old man felt the body of the boy regain power right there. (1.-kwaimwa, 2.-kwaimide, 3.-kwaimizya, 4.-kwaimina, 5.-kwaiminalyo, 6.-kwaimisya, 7.-kwaima-kwaima)

open ears widely, Musimbi naakateelela kuya kutuminwa ku Sekondali ooku, wakakwakula matwi, wakazumina. = When the girl heard about being sent there to Secondary, she opened her ears, she agreed. (1.-kwakulwa, 2.-kwakwide, 3.-kwakwizya, 4.-kwakwizyizya, 5.-kwakwidalyo, 6.-kwakulisya, 7.-kwakula-kwakula.)
stick out, Matwi amwana oyu akakwakwabala mbuli kuti ngasulwe. The ears of this child are sticking out like that of a hare.

be spread out, Mulomo wakwe wakakwakwabuka mbuli mulomo wazenimutendu. = His mouth was as extensive as that of a shark. (1.-kwakwabukwa, 2.-kwakwabukide, 3.-kwakwabuzya, 4.-kwakwabwida, 5.-kwakwabwidalyo, 6.-kwakwabukisya, 7.-kwakwabuka-kwakwabuka.)

widen, enlarge, Mulimi wakakwakwabula muunda wamapopwe. The farmer widened his field of maize. (1.-kwakwabulwa, 2.-kwakwabwide, 3.-kwakwabuzya, 4.-kwakwabulila, 5.-kwakwabulilalyo, 6.-kwakwabulisya, 7.-kwakwabula-kwakwabula)

scratch about, Kana kankuku kalakwakwalika, kalapala, kalayanga. The chick scratches about, it digs the earth, it scrapes the surface. (2.-kwakwalikide, 3.-kwakwalisya, 4.-kwakwalikila, 5.-kwakwalikilalyo, 6.-kwakwalikisya, 7.-kwakwalikakwakwalika, 8.-kwakwalikana.)

struggle against one another, Mutinta a Masowe bakakwakwalisyanya akulwana kwaciindi cilamfwu. = Mutinta and Masowe were struggling and fighting with one another for a long time. (1.-kwakwalisyigwa, 2.-kwakwalisyide, 3.-kwakwalizya, 4.-kwakwalisyizya, 5.-kwakwalisyizyalyo, 6.-kwakwalisyisya, 7.-kwakwalisyanya)

be detached, Cisamu cakaandwa lulabo cakayuma akukwakwamuka makwa. = The tree which was hit by lightning dried up and the bark became detached. (1.-kwakwamukwa, 2.-kwakwamukide, 3.-kwakwamuzya, 4.-kwakwamukila, 5.-kwakwamukilalyo, 6.-kwakwamukisya, 7.-kwakwamukakwakwamuka.)

peel off as skin, slough as a snake, Mubuzuba bwasanu kasilikwa, mulwazi wakatalika kuli kwakwamuna. = On the fifth day of treatment, the patient began to feel his skin peeling off. Wakabona nzoka niyakali kulikwakwamuna. = He saw the snake as it was sloughing. (1.-kwakwamunwa, 2.-kwakwamwide, 3.-kwakwamuzya, 4.-kwakwamwida, 5.-kwakwamwidalyo, 6.-kwakwamunisya, 7.-kwakwamunakwakwamuna, 8.-kwakwamunana)
  • increase, Mandongwe wakakwakwamuna muunda wakwe wakali musyoonto. = Mandongwe enlarged his field which was small.
provoke, Utandikwali-kwali pe. = Do not provoke me. (1.-kwalwa, 2.-kwalide, 3.-kwalizya, 4.-kwalila, 5.kwalilalyo, 6.-kwalisya, 7.-kwala-kwala, 8.-kwalana) Also: -soka

scratch about, Kokkala mungazi, umwaye musenga kubbazu nkoocimvwida kukwalabanta. = Sit on the look-out platform and throw sand to the side where you hear anything scratching about. (1.-wakalabantwa, 2.-kwalabantide, 3.-kwalabantya. 4.-kwalabantila, 5.-kwalabantilalyo, 6.-kwalabantisya, 7.-kwalabanta-kwalabanta, 8.-kwalabantana) Also: -kwala-kwala.

scratch about here and there, Mbeba niyali kukwala-kwala a cijazyo, yamusinsimuna kufwambaana mwana. = When the mouse was scratching about at the door, it wakened the child quickly. Ooyu kwale mukukwalakwala akufwukula wakadonkola kasena abwina bwaciwena. = This partridge, with all its scratching about and uprooting, made an opening in the den of the crocodile. (duplicate -kwala as above for extensions) Also: -kwalabanta, -gwagwala.
quarrel with one another, Bakali kukkala amwaalumi wakwe kakunyina kukwalana-kwalana. = She was living with her husband without any quarreling.

dig or plough shallowly, Oyu munene ciindi niyakatanga mvwula, wakasola kulomba cipani mubasazinyina kuti awalo akakwalaule kaunda kasyoonto buyo. = When it began to rain, this old man tried to ask his relatives for a span of oxen so that he also could plough his little field however shallowly. (1.-kwalaulwa, 2.-kwalawide, 3.-kwalauzya, 4.-kwalawida, 5.-kwalawidalyo, 6.-kwalaulisya, 7.-kwalaula-kwalaula, 8.-kwalaulana)

clap while pounding, Bakaintu bakali kutwa akukwalika. = The women were clapping while pounding. (1.-kwalikwa, 2.-kwalikide, 3.-kwalizya, 4.-kwalikila, 5.-kwalikilalyo, 6.-kwalikisya, 7.-kwalika-kwalika, 8.-kwalikana)

remove seeds or bark as from a tree, Katukwama mpondo kutegwa tujane cakulya. = Let us remove mpondo seeds so that we get something to eat. Bakatalika kukwama zikwa zya muumba kuti babwezele buci. = They began to remove sections of bark from a muumba tree with which they could carry the honey. (1.-kwamwa, 2.-kwamide, 3.kwamya 4.-kwamina, 5.-kwaminalyo, 6.-kwamisya, 7.-kwama-kwama. 8.-kwamana)
