blaze, Mulilo wakali kwiile kunyefwuka aciluli cananda. = *The fire was just blazing on the roof of the house.* (1.-nyefwukwa, 2.-nyefwukide, 3.-nyefwusya, 4.-nyefwukila, 5.-nyefwukilalyo, 6.-nyefwukisya, 7.-nyefwukanyefwuka) Also: nyemfwuuma.
blaze Also: -nyefwuuma. (2.-nyefwumide, 3.-nyefwumya, 4.-nyefwumina, 5.-nyefwuminalyo, 6.-nyefwumisya, 7.-nyefwuma-nyefwuma)
blaze, Mulilo wakali kwiile kunyefwuuma mumakuba. = *The fire was just blazing among the maize stalks.*

be aglow or alight, Wanyeka kale mulilo. = *The fire is already alight. Ndapya! Ndanyeka! Kozya undizime.* = *I am burning! I am alight! Come and extinguish me.* Also: -yaka (2.-nyekede, 3.-nyesya, 4.-nyekela, 5.-nyekelalyo, 6.-nyekesya, 7.-nyeka-nyeka)

decorate with traditional designs, Bacembele nibakamana kubumba nongo, bakainyekaula kutegwa ibote. = When the old woman had finished moulding the pot she began to decorate it so that it would become beautiful. (1.-nyekaulwa, 2.-nyekawide, 3.-nyekauzya, 4.-nyekawida, 5.-nyekawidalyo, 6.-nyekaulisya, 7.-nyekaula-nyekaula, 8.-nyekaulana) Also: -nyenyemba, -cekaula, -zekaulas, -zeleemba.
chew Also: tafwuna

be angry, Wakanyema naakafwubaazigwa kukana kasyoonto. = He was angry when he was fooled by the little child. (1.-nyemenwa, 2.-nyemede, 3.-nyemya, 5.-nyemena, 5.-nyemenalyo, 6.-nyemesya, 7.-nyema-nyema, 8.-nyemezyanya)
  • be at an intensive stage, Mulimo wanyema, tuulekeki. = The work which has reached an intensive stage, cannot be stopped. Also: . -nyansya, -kalala.
be quick to anger, Kamufwambaana kumupa cakulya nkaambo ulanyema-nyema nafwide nzala. = Give him food quickly because he becomes annoyed when he becomes hungry.

be angry with, rt. -nyema, Wakakanyemena kana cakuti bantu baali kuti ulakauma. = She got angry with the child so much that the people thought she was going to beat it. Bapati bakabanyemena bana nibakayanda mali aabo. = The elders got annoyed with the children when they wanted their money. Koonse kwaamba boobu kwakali kubeja buyo, wakali kuyoowa kunyemenwa. = All the talking in this way was just lying, he feared people being angry with him. Also: -lemana, -kalalila.
make angry, also -nyemya.

blaze, Mulilo ulanyemfwuma mumulundu. = A fire is blazing on the hill. (1.-nyemfwumizyigwa, 2.-nyemfumide, 3.-nyemfwumya, 4.-nyemfwumina, 5.-nyemfwuminalyo, 6.-nyemfwumisya, 7.-nyemfwumanyemfwuma) Also: -nyefwuka.

chew ravenously, Syuumbwa unyemfwuta zifwuwa zyacibize. = A lion chews the bones of a zebra ravenously. (1.-nyemfwutwa, 2.-nyemfwutide, 3.-nyemfwutya, 4.-nyemfwutila, 5.-nyemfwutilalyo, 6.-nyemfwutisya, 7.-nyemfwuta-nyemfwuta, 8.-nyemfwutana) Also: -pulukuta.
be sour, like a lemon, Mukupa wasasa ulanyemuka. = When milk is sour it becomes acidic. Also: -sakamuka. (2.-nyemukide, 3.-nyemusya, 4.-nyemukila, 5.-nyemukilalyo, 6.-nyemukisya, 7.-nyemuka-nyemuka)

offer a thing to a person without intending to give it, as in the children's _nyemu_ game where they say, "Nyemu!" (Look at this nice thing, but it is not for you!), Ndamunyemuuzya nyemu nzindali kulya. = I tantalized her with groundnuts which I was eating. Tacigwasyi kunyemuuzya muntu acintu ncayanda ncobeni. = It is not helpful to tantalize a person with something which he really needs. (1.-nyemuuzyigwa, 2.-nyemuuzyide, 3.-nyemuuzyisya, 4.-nyemuuzyizya, 5.-nyemuuzyizyalyo, 6.-nyemuuzyisya, 7.-nyemuuzyanyeemuzya, 8.-nyemuuzyanya) Also: -nyeemuzya.
annoy, make angry, rt. nyema, Ino bakabanyemya bayi jilo mbaani? = Who angered the teacher yesterday? Ncibi kunyemya bantu. = It is bad to anger people. (1.-nyemezyegwa) Also: -nyemezya, -lalula.
mock, ridicule, Sena takuli, *nkokunyena oku?* = Is that not being selfish?

be fearful, *Ndanyenaala kweenda musyokwe mulila balavwu.* = I feel scared to go through the bush where lions are growling. *Inga tolimvwi kunyenaala kumilimo mibi mbuli bwayeeyi?* = Do you not feel afraid of evil deeds like these? (1.-nyenaalwa, 2.-nyenaalide, 3.-nyenaanzya, 4.-nyenaalila, 5.-nyenaalilalyo, 6.-nyenaalisya 7.-nyenaala-nyenaala, 8.-nyenaazyanya)

cause fearful emotions or anxiety, *Kweenda mumbali aamulonga uzwide, cilanyenaanzya.* = To go along beside a river in spate, produces fearful emotions. *Cilanyenaanzya kubona mwana kasobana atalaa mugodi.* = It causes anxiety to see a child playing on top of the well. *Malundu naanyenaanzya njakwaananalika.* = The mountains no matter how terrifying, I will step lighty across them. *Imvwula yakasibika cinyenaanzya kulubazu Iwakunyika.* = To the north there was the building up of rain which would make one anxious.

drop or open mouth in surprise, *Waile kunyenama naajaya nongo mooye.* = The girl just opened her mouth in shock when she broke the clay pot. *Wanyenama naalya cisyu cabikkwa mpilibili.* = He gasped when he ate the relish which had too much hot pepper. (1.-nyenamwa, 2.-nyeneme, 3.-nyenamya, 4.-nyenamina, 5.-nyenaminalyo, 6.-nyenamisya, 7.-nyenama-nyenama, 8.-nyenaminana)

act without control and without respect, *Musondosi wiile kunyenauka mubantu.* = The mad person is just acting without control or respect among the people. (1.-nyenaukwa, 2.-nyenaukide, 3.-nyenausya, 4.-nyenaukila, 5.-nyenaukilalyo 6.-nyenaukisya, 7.-nyenauka-nyenauka, 8.-nyenausyanya)

open mouth to show teeth, *Kiakupa ulanyenauna malomo kwaambila Dipiza zyoonse zyeelede kucitwa.* = Kiakupa is opening his mouth telling Dipiza everything that ought to be done. (1.-nyenaunwa, 2.-nyenawide, 3.-nyenausya, 4.-nyenaunina, 5.-nyenauninalyo, 6.-nyenaunisya, 7.-nyenauna-nyenauna, 8.-nyenainana)
stand around aimlessly, *Nsekwe ciindi cakunyenemaninwa akuyapawidwa madomo, mebo njanda cilyo.* = I have no time to stand round talking rubbish to you, I want food.

be hot or stinging, as pepper, *Mpilibili ilanyenga-nyenga mukanwa.* = Pepper is hot in the mouth. *Ndimvwide kabotu, pesi meso alikke ngaanyenga-nyenga.* = I feel well except for my eyes which are stinging. (2.-nyengede-nyengede, 3.-nyengezyanyengezya, 4.-nyengela-nyengela, 5.-nyengelalyo-nyengelalyo, 6.-nyengesyanyengesya, 7.-nyenga-nyenga - nyenga-nyenga)

deceive by coaxing, *Bamunyengelela mwana nibamuulila mabbusu afwambaana kufwa.* = They deceived the child when they bought him shoes which quickly wear out. (1.-nyengelelwa, 2.-nyengelede, 3.-nyengelezya, 4.-nyengelelela, 5.-nyengelelelelalyo, 6.-nyengelelesya, 7.-nyengelela-nyengelela, 8.-nyengelelana)

shine, glisten, *Balombwana aba bakajisi tubwe-tubwe tunyengema kabati mbaasimakwebo baulisya ma emalodi.* = These men had small shining precious stones saying they were traders who were selling emeralds.

look around by turning whole body, *Konyenguluka ulange* musule lyako ubone mubwa uukutobela. = Turn right around so that you look behind and see the dog following you. (1.-nyengulukwa, 2.-nyengulukide, 3.-nyenguluzya, 4.-nyengulukila, 5.-nyengulukilalyo, 6.-nyengulukisya, 7. *nyenguluka-nyenguluka*, 8. *nyenguluzyanya*) Also: -cenguluka.

look around all about, Simpongo ulanyenguula mumbali nanyona-nyona mbelele ampongo zyakwe. = The goatherd looks all about as he goes to bring back his sheep and goats. Also: - langaula. (1.-nyenguulwa, 2.-nyeguulide, 3.-nyenguuzya, 4.-nyenguulila, 5.-nyenguulilalyo, 6.-nyenguulisya, 7. *nyenguula-nyenguula*, 8. *nyenguulana*)

open out, as a shell or cotton ball, Makoto aabuluba anyenuka kale. The cotton balls are already opening out. (1.-nyenukwa, 2.-nyenukide, 3.-nyenusya, 4.-nyenukila, 5.-nyenukilalyo, 6.-nyenukisya, 7. *nyenuka-nyenuka*, 8. *nyenusyanya*) Also: -panduka.

bare teeth, Kasilili kalanyenuna menyo kukonga nzoka. = The red mongoose opens its mouth and shows its teeth to frighten a snake. (1.-nyenunwa, 2.-nyenwide, 3.-nyenusya, 4.-nyenwida, 5.-nyenwidalyo, 6.-nyenunisya, 7. *nyenuna-nyenuna*, 8. *nyenunana*) Also: -syitula menyo.

bare teeth in anger, e.g Syuumbwa wakatalika kunyenyauna milomo naakabona muvwimi ujisi ntobolo. = The lion began to bare its teeth when it saw the hunter with a gun. (1.-nyenyaunwa, 2.-nyenyawide, 3.-nyenyausya, 4.-nyenyawida, 5.-nyenyawidalyo, 6.-nyenyaunisya, 7. *nyenauna-nyenauna*, 8. *nyenyaunana*) Also: -nyetaula, -nyenuna, -nyenauna.

decorate by making lines with fire on a stick, e.g Kounyenyemba mwiini wajamba. Decorate the handle of the hoe. (1.-nyenyembwa, 2.-nyenyembede, 3.-nyenyembya, 4.-nyenyembela, 5.-nyenyembelalyo, 6.-nyenyembesya, 7. *nyenyembanyenyemba*, 8. *nyenyembana*) Also: -nyekaula, -cekaula, -zekaulas, -zeleemba.

rouse anger, Kaambo nkaamba ooyu kandinyesya moyo. What this one is talking about has inflamed my heart. *makani anyesya moyo* = inflammatory speech. Also: -celusya. (1.-nyesyegwa, 2.-nyesyede, 3.-nyesyesya, 4.-nyesyela, 5.-nyesyelalyo, 6.-nyesyesya, 7. *nyesya-nyesya*, 8. *nyesyanya*)
  • cause to light, Kamunyesya lambe musalale munanda. Light the lamp to make the house bright.

be short-tempered, Moyo wakwe wakali kufwambaana kunyetauka nkaambo bakali kumwiima cakulya bazyali bakwe. = His heart was quick to become angry because his parents were depriving him of food. Mudyaka wakali sikanyetu-nyetu cakuti bantu bakali kuti wakamitwa lyanzala myoyo yabantu neinyetauka. = Mudyaka was an irascible person so that people used to say he was conceived at a time of hunger when the hearts of people become annoyed easily. (1.-nyetaukwa, 2.-nyetaukide, 3.-nyetauzya, 4.-nyetaukila, 5.-nyetaukilalyo, 6.-nyetaukisya, 7. *nyetauka-nyetauka*, 8. *nyetausyanya*) Also: -nyema-nyema, -fwisuka kunyema.

be very hot and burning. Izuba lyanyetaula. The sun is scorching. (1.-nyetaulwa, 2.-nyetawide, 3.-nyetauzya, 4.-nyetawida, 5.-nyetawidalyo, 6.-nyetaulisya, 7. *nyetaula-nyetaula*, 8. *nyetaulana*) Also: -bilibinta
  • bare teeth in anger, Syuumbwa nayanda kuluma muntu ulanyetaula malomo akwe. = When a lion wants to attack a person it bares its teeth in anger. Also: -nyenauna, -nyetula.
  • open and close the mouth, Wakali kunyetaula mulomo wakwe kumwi kasekaseka. = He was opening and closing his mouth while he was smiling. Wandiyoosya syuumbwa naali kunyetaula malomo. = The lion terrified me when it was opening and closing its mouth.

bare the teeth, Mwaalumi mukali wali kunyetula menyo naayanda kulwana. = The fierce man was baring his teeth when he wanted to fight. (1.-nyetulwa, 2.-nyetwide, 3.-nyetwizya, 4.-nyetwida, 5.-nyetwidalyo, 6.-nyetulisya, 7.-nyetula-nyetula, 8.-nyetwidana) Also: -nyetaula.

become agitated, Nobakalangana kumeso, Mazuba wakanyiilwa, wakalimvwa bubi alimwi moyo wakwe wakazyulila bukali. = When they looked at one another in the face, Mazuba was agitated, he felt very angry and again his heart was filled with anger.

be aroused, Naakabona bazyana kalyaba, mubili wakwe wakanyiinya. When he saw them dancing the kalyaba, his body was aroused (to join in the dance). (1.-nyiinyizyigwa, 2.-nyiinyide, 3.-nyiinyizya, 4.-nyiizyisya; 5.-nyiizyizyalyo, 6.-nyiizyisya, 7.-nyiinyanyiinya, 8.-nyiinyizyanya) Also: -nyinya, -sakasa.
cause to arouse, Bakali kwiimba zyiimbo zinyiinyisya mubili. = They were singing songs which arouse the body.

steep, soak, dip, immerse, sink to bottom, Kamunyika masomo a nanda mumeenda. Soak the poles for the house in water. (1.-nyikwa, 2.-nyikide, 3.-nyisya, 4.-nyikila, 5.-nyikilalyo, 6.-nyikisya, 7.-nyika-nyika, 8.-nyikana) Also: -toba, -ccavwika.
  • prepare beer for the Iwiindi celebrations, e.g Bantu bamumunzi wa Chigunta bakanyika kale mapopwe aalwiindi. = The people of Chigunta have already prepared maize-grains for the Lwiindi festival.

drown, sink to bottom, Bazeli banswi bakanyikila mulwaanje bwato bwabo nibwakapindamuka. = The fishermen drowned in the lake when their boat overturned. (1.-nyikizyigwa, 2.-nyikilide, 3.-nyikizya, 4.-nyikilila, 5.-nyikililalyo, 6.-nyikililsya, 7.-nyikila-nyikila, 8.-nyikizyanya) Also: -nikila, -unkila, -inkila.

shake head, Wakasika mulomo wakamuyumya mate Mainza, mulomo wakamucita kuti anyikinye mutwe wakwe. There came a message which dried up Mainza's mouth, the news made him shake his head. (1.-nyikinyigwa, 2.-nyikinyide, 3.-nyikinyizya, 4.-nyikinyizya, 5.-nyikinyizyalyo, 6.-nyikinyisya, 7.-nyikinya-nyikinya, 8.-nyikinyizyanya)

drop something into, Mwana wakainyikizya mumugoti nkomeki. = The child has dropped the cup into a well. (1.-nyikizyigwa, 2.-nyikizyide, 3.-nyikizya, 4.-nyikizyizya, 5.-nyikizyizyalyo, 6.-nyikizyisya, 7.-nyikizya-nyikizya, 8.-nyikizyanya) Also: -dumpukizya, -golokezya, -tumpukizya.

take out of water or liquid, Cikutu cakubambya ngoma ncindakanyika mumeenda bayakucinyikula basankwa. = The boys will take the skin for making drums out of the water which I had put in. Komunyikula musune wanyikila mucikala. = Take the ox which has drowned out of the well. Bantu nobakaunka kumulonga kuya kunyikula, bakajana bana aabo kabafwide boonse. When the people went to the river to take = them out of the water, they found those children all dead. (1.-nyikulwa, 2.-nyikwide, 3.-nyikuzya, 4.-nyikwida, 5.-nyikwidalyo, 6.-nyikulisya, 7.-nyikula-nyikula, 8.-nyikulana)

tickle, Banyina nobakamunyiminya mwana, wakaseka cakubotelwa. = When the mother tickled the child, it laughed in delight. (1.-nyiminyigwa, 2.-nyiminyide, 3.-nyiminyizya, 4.-nyiminyizyizya, 5.-nyiminyizyizyalyo, 6.-nyiminyisya, 7.-nyiminya-nyiminya, 8.-nyiminyizyanya) Also: -dekeenya, -dekaanya, -tekaanya.

be excited, aroused, thrilled, Mubili *wanyinya* ndiyanda kulwana. = My body is aroused, I want to fight. (1.-nyinyizyigwa, 2.-nyinyide, 3.-nyinyizya, 4.-nyinyizyizya, 5.-nyinyizyizyalyo, 6.-nyinyizyisya, 7.-nyinya-nyinya, 8.-nyinyizyanya) Also: -nyiinya, -sakasa.

sob in pain, Mulwazi wali kunyinyita naali kuyanda kufwa. = The patient was sobbing in pain when he was about to die. (1.-nyinyitwa, 2.-nyinyitide, 3.-nyinyitya, 4.-nyinyitila, 5.-nyinyitilalyo, 6.-nyinyitisya, 7.-nyinyita-nyinyita.) Also: -tongela, -mimila.

wag, Basankwa bakali kweebelezya kabwa nkokasotooka akunyininya mucila. = The boys were watching the puppy how it jumped and waged its tail. (1.-nyininyizyigwa, 2.-nyininyide, 3.-nyininyizya, 4.-nyininyizyizya, 5.-nyininyizyizyalyo, 6.-nyininyisya, 7.-nyininya-nyininya) Also: -yuuna.

groan, roar with pain, Wali kwiile *kunyita* naamyongwa mukaintu wangu. = My wife screamed in agony when she was in labour. Ndakamvwa syuumbwa *wanyita* kunze aciba. = I heard the lion roaring beside the kraal. Wakaalabana ansi akupilingana kumwi

mbuli nombe izyala. = He rolled and twisted on the ground while he bellowed like a cow calfing. (1.-nyitwa, 2.-nyitide, 3.-nyitya, 4.-nyitila, 5.-nyitilalyo, 6.-nyitisya, 7.-nyita-nyita, 8.-nyitizyanya)

walk with the gait of a baboon, Sokwe naali kukosola mugwagwa wali kwiile *kunyokomba*. = When the monkey was crossing the road he was just swaggering along. (1.-nyokombwa, 2.-nyokombede, 3.-nyokombya, 4.-nyokombela, 5.-nyokombelalyo, 6.-nyokombesya, 7.-nyokomba-nyokomba) Also: -nanamba.
  • walk about with no purpose, wakali kwiide *kunyokomba* kakunyina kucita. = He was just wandering around aimlessly with nothing to do.
shave, cut hair or beard, Munene walikkede acimbwalakasa kali

malezu kunze ananda. = The old man was seated on a stool behind the house shaving himself. (1.-nyolwa, 2.-nyolede, 3.-nyozya, 4.-nyweeda, 5.-nyweedalyo, 6.-nyolesya 7.-nyola-nyola, 8.-nyolana) Also: -nyoola.

overcome, Basibbola besu bakabanyombola beenzinyina atugolo totatwe. = Our footballers beat their opponents by three goals. (1.-nyombolwa, 2.-nyombwede, 3.-nyombozya, 4.-nyombweda, 5.-nyombwedalyo, 6.-nyombolesya, 7.-nyombola-nyombola, 8.-nyombolana) Also: -zunda, -koma.

desire something which another person has and you cannot get, *Ndanyomenena* kubona bantu balya nyama. = I am overcome with envy when I see people eating meat. Nindakabona mbokubambidwe ananda yakwe, *ndakanyomenena* akuti kubota nikwali kwesu. = When I saw how his house was kept, I was envious saying if only it was ours. (1.-nyomenenwa, 2.-nyomenede, 3.-nyomenezya, 4.-nyomenena, 5.-nyomenenalyo, 6.-nyomenenesya, 7.-nyomenena-nyomenena, 8.-nyomenenanwa)
covet, *Ndakanyomenenwa* nindakabona bantu balya nyama. = I was envious when I saw people eating meat. Also: -dokelelwa, -menenwa

cause to envy, show something nice to another without the intention of giving, *Mweenzuma ijilo wakandinyomenezya* mukupa ngwaatakandipa akundipa pe. = My friend made me envious yesterday about the milk which he had no intention of giving me. *Inyama yamafwuta ilanyomenezya.* = Fat meat makes one envious. *Mwiza wakabanyomenezya basimbi bamwi naakasama bulungu bubotu munsingo.* = Mwiza made the other girls envious when she wore beautiful beads around her neck. Also: -nyeemuzya, -sombezya.

turn back, *Kamunyona nombe ziya, zilalya mapopwe aabantu.* = Turn back those cattle, they will eat people's maize. (1.-nyonwa, 2.-nyonede, 3.-nyonezya, 4.-nyonena, 5.-nyonenalyo, 6.-nyonesya, 7.-nyona-nyona, 8.-nyonana)
  • wring out, *Naakamana kusanzya zisani, taakazinyona kabotu kuti meenda azwe.* When she had finished washing the clothes, she did not wring them out well enough for the water to come out. Also: -kanya.
  • twist the tail, *Bamwi bantu nobatambisya basune balayanda kunyona mucila kuti musune woona.* = Some people when training oxen like to twist the tail if an ox lies down.
  • complete a job, Muntu omwe ukonzya kutola ciindi cilamfwu kunyona *mulimo umwi.* = One person can take long to complete a single job.

be possibe to be turned back, rt. -nyona, *nombe zilanyoneka nozi-kkuta.* Cattle can be turned back when they are satisfied. (1.-nyonekwa, 2.-nyonekede, 3.-nyonezya, 4.-nyonekanina, 5.-nyonekaninalyo, 6.-nyonekesya, 7.-nyoneka-nyoneka, 8.-nyonekaninana)

inclined to, *Muka Chimbwali lyoonse mumoyo wakali kunyonenezya kumulumaakwe kuti nguwakajaya mwana.* = The wife of Chimbwali always in her heart was inclined to think that it was her husband who had killed their son.

be confused, Bantu bakanyongana lyadilwe. People were confused during the funeral. *Mwida mulanyongana.* = In the stomach there is a disturbance. (1.-nyonganwa, 2.-nyongenye, 3.-nyonganya, 4.-nyonganina, 5.-nyonganinalyo, 6.-nyonganisya, 7.-nyongana-nyongana, 8.-nyonganizyanya)

cause confusion, *Bacembele bakafwambaana kujoka kudilwe nkaambo mwanaabo wakabanyonganya.* The old lady quickly returned from the funeral because her child was becoming difficult for her. (1.-nyonganyizyigwa, 2.-nyonganyizyide, 4.-nyonganyizyizya, 5.-nyonganyizyizyalyo,6.-nyonganyizyisya, 7.-nyonganyanyonganya, 8.-nyonganyizyanya) Also: -gubinkanya.

cut off, break, *Bamunyongola kanwe.* = They have cut off his finger. *Kamunyongola loozi Iwakuvwumbya nanda.* Cut fibres for thatching the house. *Akeembe aka nkakena, sunu nduunyongola mutwe wako.* With this very same axe I will chop off your head. (1.-nyongolwa, 2.-nyongwede, 3.-nyongozya, 4.-nyongweda, 5.-nyongwedalyo, 6.-nyongolesya, 7.-nyongola-nyongola, 8.-nyongolana) Also: -kosola

chop up, as wood, _Zisamu nzitwakausya ziyandika kunyongolola._ = The trees which we cut down need to be chopped up. _Basankwa bakali kukutema masamu akunyongolola zitanda kutegwa zikwelwe acikkocci zikabe nkuni mainza._ = The boys were cutting down trees and chopping them up into logs so that they could bring them in the scotchcart so that there would be firewood for the rainy season. (1.-nyongololwa, 2.-nyongolwede, 3.-nyongolozya, 4.-nyongolweda, 5.-nyongolwedalyo, 6.-nyongololesya, 7.-nyongolola-nyongolola, 8.-nyongololana)
be chopped up, _Nkuni zyakanyongololwa._ = The firewood was chopped up.

feel pangs, _Mukaintu utumbuka ulanyongosana._ = A woman who gives birth feels the pangs. (1.-nyongosanwa, 2.-nyongosene, 3.-nyongosanya, 4.-nyongosanina, 5.-nyongosaninalyo, 6.-nyongosanisya, 7.-nyongosana-nyongosana) Also: -myongosana.

suck the breast, _Mwana wakayeeya kunyonka kuli banyina._ = The baby wanted to suck from the mother. _Kuti mwana wakomena, uleelede kuleka kunyonka._ = If a child has grown, s/he ought to stop sucking. (1.-nyonkwa, 2.-nyonkede, 3.-nyonsya/-nyonkelezya, 4.-nyonkela, 5.-nyonkelalyo, 6.-nyonkesya, 7.-nyonka-nyonka, 8.-nyonkelana)

teach to suck, suckle someone else's child, feed baby from bottle, _Baama bakali kunga kana nkukanyonkelezya buya kubbodela kuti nobatayandi kunyonsya kunkolo._ = Mother used to feed a child with a feeding bottle when she didn't want to breast-feed. _Simpongo ulanyonkelezya twana twambelele twakafwidwa nyina._ = A goatherd is suckling lambs whose mother has died. Also: -nonkelezya, -nyonkolezya, -nonselezya.

help to suck, e.g Ko_nyonkolezya koombe kazyalwa ono._ = Help the recently born calf to suck. (1.-nyonkolezyegwa, 2.-nyonkolozyede, 3.-nyonkolezya, 4.-nyonkolezyezya, 5.-nyonkolezyezyalyo, 6.-nyonkolezyesya, 7.-nyonkolezya-nyonkolezya, 8.-nyonkolezyanya) Also: -nyonkelezya.

fall off, as feathers, _Mapepe aasikube wakafwa akamana kunyonkooka._ = The feathers of the vulture which died have completely fallen off. (1.-nyonkookwa, 2.-nyonkookede, 3.-nyonkoozya, 4.-nyonkookela, 5.-nyonkookelalyo, 6.-nyonkookesya, 7.-nyonkooka-nyonkooka) Also: -juka, -jundauka.

envy, _Ndabaa cintu nociceya, bamwi nkujana banyonoka kale._ = No matter how small a thing I possess, you find that others are envious. _Bantu bamwi balanyonoka kubona bantu basumpuka._ = Some people are envious to see people advancing. _Mukaintu mutaanzi kukwatwa mwaalumi wakamupede mpande. Mukazinyina wakanyonoka._ = The husband gave the first wife a cowry shell. Her co-wife was envious. Also: -ba amunyono. (1.-nyonokwa, 2.-nyonokede, 3.-nyonosya, 4.-nyonokela, 5.-nyonokelalyo, 6.-nyonokesya 7.-nyonoka-nyonoka, 8.-nyonokelana)
  • be twisted, as to dislocate, _Cilatondwa kuseka mudaala uulemenye nkaambo kuti walowa inga wanyonoka mulomo._ = It is taboo to laugh at a lame old man because if he uses witchcraft you can have your mouth twisted.

covet, be envious, rt. nyonoka, *Ncibi kunyonokela bamwi bantu.* = It is bad to envy other people. *Chibbwalu wakatalika kunyonokela nombe zya Chitebenta.* = Chibbwalu began to envy the cattle of Chitebenta. (1.-nyonokelwa, 2.-nyonokelede, 3.-nyonokelezya, 4.-nyonokelela, 5.-nyonokelelalyo, 6.-nyonokelesya, 7.-nyonokelanyonokela, 8.-nyonokelana) Also: -ba amunyono.
be envious of one another, rt. -nyonoka, *Bantu banyonokelana tabakkali kabotu.* = People who are mutually envious do not live peace.

turn back, *Atijaana kwamusinzo umwi, munyati ulanyononoka akutalika kubembeleka mukondo mwaali kwiinda kapiluka nkwazyila.* = When he runs away some distance, the buffalo turns back and follows the track he had taken, returning to where he came from.

twist, *Koleka kumunyononona maboko mwana, ulamutyola.* = Stop twisting the child's arm, you will break it. *Wali kunyononona kaambo limwi kaba kakubeja.* = He was twisting the statement so that it just became a lie. (1.-nyonononwa, 2.-nyononwede, 3.-nyononozya, 4.-nyononenena, 5.-nyononenenalyo, 6.-nyononenesya, 7.-nyononona-nyononona, 8.-nyonononana)
  • turn cattle back, *Basimpongo mbasungu kukunyononona akukubamba banyama babo.* = Goatherds are expert in turning and caring for their animals.

try to dodge, be unwilling, *Wali kunyonooka kutumwa.* = He was unwilling to be sent. (1.-nyonookwa, 2.-nyonookede, 3.-nyonoozya, 4.-nyonookela 5.-nyonookelalyo, 6.-nyonookesya, 7.-nyonooka-nyonooka, 8.-nyonookana) Also: -syolooka, -syimbula.
  • be carried away by lust, *Musimbi naa musankwa unyonooka ulafwambaana kufwa akaambo kasikalileke.* = A girl or a boy who is carried away by sexual desires will quickly die because of AIDS.
  • turn over and over, as in pain, *Wali kunyonooka akaambo kamwida mwali kucisa.* = She was turning over and over because of the stomach pains.
become jealous, *Bamwi bantu cilabanyonosya kuti musankwa ucili mwana wavwuba lubono lunji.* = Some people become jealous if a boy who is still young becomes very rich. Also: -nyononsya

peck, as with beak, *Cibengelele mbwaakavwubukila wakamunyonsola ampemo Sicibende.* = As the hammer-headed stork stooped down quickly it pecked Sicibende on the nose. (1.-nyonsolwa, 2.-nyonswede, 3.-nyonsozya, 4.-nyonsolela, 5.-nyonswedalyo, 6.-nyonsolesya, 7.-nyonsola-nyonsola, 8.-nyonsolana)

rest a little, *Chilekwa naakasika acikolo wakanyonsomana acuuno.* = When Chilekwa reached the school he rested for a while on a chair. (1.-nyonsomanwa, 2.-nyonsomede, 3.-nyonsomanya, 4.-nyonsomanina, 5.-nyonsomaninalyo, 6.-nyonsomanisya, 7.-nyonsomana-nyonsomana, 8.-nyonsomaninana) Also: -nyunsumana, -nyunzumana.

suckle, *Kamumunyonsya mwana aleke kulila.* = Suckle the child so that it stops crying. *Kumantoombwa basimbi bapati-pati bakali kulicengezya kunyonsya twana twakali tuniini.* = Big girls (at *mantoombwa* house-keeping game) used to pretend to breast-feed the girls who were small. (1.-nyonsyegwa, 2.-nyonsyede, 3.-nyonsyezya, 4.-nyonsyela, 5.-nyonsyelalyo 6.-nyonsyesya, 7.-nyonsya-nyonsya, 8.-nyonsyanya)
suckle, _Awa acamba busimbi bwakaciimvwi buya nci unakuti tananyonsele._ = There on her chest her womanhood stood out firmly as if she had not yet suckled a child with her breasts.

complain, _Bantu bakanyontooka akaambo kakubula meenda azilyo zinji._ = People complained because of lacking water and sufficient food. (1.-nyontookwa, 2.-nyontookede, 3.-nyotoosya, 4.-nyontookela, 5.-nyontookelalyo, 6.-nyontookesya, 7.-nyontooka-nyontooka, 8.-nyontookana) Also: -tongooka.

be brought back, _Kuti mwana walubizya ulanyonwa kutegwa alulame._ = If a child makes a mistake it is brought back so that he behaves correctly. (2.-nyonede, 3.-nyonezya, 4.-nyonena, 5.-nyonenalyo, 6.-nyonesya, 7.-nyonwa-nyonwa, 8.-nyonana)

destroy, _Bamwi bakali kwaamba kuti mwana amwami wamuunina muzike oyu Mutinta nkaambo takamukwati pe, ulamunyonyauna buyo._ = Some were saying that the son of the chief was deceiving this slave Mutinta because he would not marry her, he was just destroying her. (1.-nyonyaunwa, 2.-nyonyaukide, 3.-nyonyauzya, 4.-nyonyaunina, 5.-nyonyauninalyo, 6.-nyonyaunisya, 7.-nyonyauna-nyonyauna, 8.-nyonyaunana)

destroy, _Wakalilaukila mooye oyu cakusinizya naakabona kuti masimpe buumi bwakumadolopo bwiide kumunyonyaunina buumi abunkutwe bwakwe boonse._ = The young girl bitterly complained with sincerity when she saw that truly the life of the cities was just destroying her life and all her energy.

be difficult, _Musune wanyonyongana ciindi naatalika kwiile koonoona mumuunda._ = The ox became difficult to handle when it started lying down in the field. (1.-nyonyonganwa, 2.-nyonyongene, 3.-nyonyonganya, 4.-nyonyonganina, 5.-nyonyonganinalyo, 6.-nyonyonganisya, 7.-nyonyongana-nyonyongana)

sit lightly, _Kamunyonyomana kukkala asaka nkaambo kunsi kuli mabwe._ = Sit lightly on the sack as there are stones underneath. (1.-nyonyomanwa, 2.-nyonyomenye, 3.-nyonyomanya, 4.-nyonyomanina, 5.-nyonyomaninalyo, 6.-nyonyomanisya, 7.-nyonyomana-nyonyomana, 8.nyonyomaninana)
  • sit up after illness, _Mucimwi ciindi mulwazi uucisidwe kapati kuti wanywa musamu wacintu cisiya cifwumo-fwumo, wakali kukonzya kunyonyomana ciindi cakumazuba._ = Sometimes a patient who was very sick, if he drank traditional medicine in the morning, he would be able to sit up in the evening.
  • be in a place only for a short time, _Kuzwa buzuba Busiku mbwaakatambulwa mumunzi ooyu, kukkala kwakwe kwakali kwakunyonyomana mbuli muntu wakacili mulweendo._ = From the day Busiku was received into the village his staying was not permanent like a person still on a journey. _Bacembele mbomuyandaula tii-bakkala ciindi cilamfwu, banyonyomana buyo._ = The old woman whom you are looking for did not stay for a long time here, she was only staying for a while. Also: -nyanyamana, -nonomana.

act without full power, _Mufwuzi wakalinyonyomeka buyo jamba, taakalibikka kabotu._ = The black smith did not insert the hoe deeply, he did not fit it properly. (1.-nyonyomekwa, 2.-nyonyomekede, 3.-nyonyomezya, 4.-nyonyomekela, 5.-nyonyomekelalyo, 6.-nyonyomekesya, 7.-nyonyomeka-nyonyomeka, 8. *nyonyomekana*) Also: -nyonyomika.

do gently, Utajalisyi, *kocinyonyomika buyo cijazyo.* = Don't bang the door, just shut it gently. (1.-nyonyomika, 2.-nyonyomikide, 3.-nyonyomizya, 4.-nyonyomikila, 5.-nyonyomikilalyo, 6.-nyonyomikisya, 7.-nyonyomika-nyonyomika, 8.-nyonyomikana) Also: -nyonyomeka.

be destroyed or wasted, *Anyonyooka mali ngibabba babbi.* = The money the thieves stole has been wasted. *Meenda akanyonyooka akatika ansi.* = The water was wasted which was poured on the ground. (1.-nyonyookwa, 2.-nyonyookede, 3.-nyonyoozya, 4.-nyonyookela, 5.-nyonyokelalyo, 6.-nyonyookesya, 7.-nyonyooka-nyonyooka) Also: -takanika.

destroy, *Waunyonyoona mwiini wajamba ngwaapapula.* = He destroyed the handle of the hoe which he split. (1.-nyonyoonwa, 2.-nyonyoonede, 3.-nyonyoozya, 4.-nyonyoonena, 5.-nyonyoonenalyo, 6.-nyonyoonesya, 7.-nyonyoona-nyonyoona, 8.-nyonyoonana)

shave, *Malezu ndaanyoola cifwumofwumo.* = I shaved the beard this morning. *Ndiyanda kulinyoola malezu.* = I want to shave myself. Also: -nyola. (1.-nyoolwa, 2.-nyoolede, 3.-nyoozya, 4.-nyoolela, 5.-nyoolelalyo, 6.-nyoolesya, 7.-nyoola-nyoola, 8.-nyoolana.)
shave with, *Ndiya kukuula mbeli yakulinyoozya malezu.* = I am going to buy a blade for shaving myself.
shave one another, rt. nyoola, *Balongwe balanyoozyanya lubosya.* Friends shave one another with sharp razors. V - 382
eat much without working, *Kubeleka tacikonzyi, mulimo nkwiide kunyopola cakulya.* = He cannot work, his work is just to eat.
be envious of, *Bananyina bakali kumunyotelwa akuyanda kwiiya nzila zyakwe.* = His friends were envious of him and anxious to learn his methods.

be dried up, be drained, *Mubiana naakaambila beenzinyina makani aya, bakanyotwa kapati.* = When Mubiana told her friends this news, they were completely drained. (2.-nyotedwe, 3.-nyotwezya, 4.-nyotwela, 5.-nyotwelalyo, 6.-nyotwelesya, 7.-nyotwa-nyotwa, 8.-nyotwelana)
be drunk, rt. -nywa, *Kwa Nkuzwa kuya kunyugwa bukoko muli Bwane.* = On Thursday there will be beerdrinking at Nkuzwa. (2.-nywidwe, 4.-nywidwa, 5.-nywidwalyo, 8.-nywidana)

shake, *Koleka kumunyuka mwana uciswa mwida.* = Stop shaking the child who has stomach pains. *Wakanyuka-nyuka sumo.* = He shook the spear. *Wakanyuka mutwe kutondezya kuusa.* = He shook his head showing sadness. (1.-nyukwa, 2.-nyukide, 3.-nyukizya, 4.-nyukila, 5.-nyukilalyo, 6.-nyukisya, 7.-nyuka-nyuka, 8.-nyukana)

shake, *Kapaso wakamunyukaanya Mudolo kumwi kati, "Kopa bulemu kunkuta iwe."* = The kapaso shook Mudolo while he said, "You, give respect to the court." *Boonse bakali kunyukaanya mitwe oku akooku kutondezya kuusa.* = All were shaking their heads from side to side showing sorrow. (1.-nyukaanyizigwa, 2.-nyukaanyizyizye, 3.-nyukaanyizya, 4.-nyukaanyinya, 5.-nyukaanyinyalyo, 6.-nyukaanyisya, 7.-nyukaanya-nyukaanya, 8.-nyukaanyizyanya)

keep shaking, Ndamunyuka-nyuka mubbi wandinjide munkomo. I kept shaking the thief who put his hand in my pocket. Michelo wakanyuka-nyuka mweenzinyina mumaanza cakukkomana nibakabonana. = Michelo shook his firend by the hand happily when they saw one an other.

shake one another, Bantu bakatalika kwaanzyanya kabanyukana mumaanza kabaseka-seka kumwi kabaimba Iwiimbo. = The people began to greet one another, shaking hands with one another, smiling while singing a hymn. Basankwa aaba bobilo bakajatana mumaanza akunyukana-nyukana. These two boys caught each other by the hands and continued to shake them. (1.-nyukanwa, 2.-nyukanide, 3.-nyukanya, 4.-nyukanina, 5.-nyukaninalyo, 6.-nyukanisya, 7.-nyukana-nyukana)

shake, as a person, Kunyukaula mulwazi inga wamutendula. = To shake a sick person might make her worse. Wamunyukaula mpoona akumuwaalila ansi. He shook her and thereupon threw her on the ground. Nkaambo kakunyukaulwa oku mwana wakabuka akutalika kulila. Because of being shaken about, the child woke up and began to cry. (1.-nyukaulwa, 2.-nyukaulide, 3.-nyukauzya, 4.-nyukaulila, 5.-nyukalilalyo, 6.-nyukaulisya 7.-nyukaula-nyukaula, 8.-nyukaulana)

pull with a jerk, Musune naakandinyukula, ndakawa ansi. = When the ox pulled me sharply, I fell to the ground. Nicakanyukula citima ndakawa ansi. When the train jerked forward, I fell to the ground. (1.-nyukulwa, 2.-nyukwide, 3.-nyukuzya, 4.-nyukwida, 5.-nyukwidalyo, 6.-nyukulisya, 7.-nyukula-nyukula, 8.-nyukulana)
  • pull with strength, Nindakali kuloba yakandinyukula nswi mpati. When I was fishing, I was pulled sharply by a huge fish.
jump forward suddenly, Moota wakanyukuka canguzu. = The vehicle jumped forward with a jerk. (1.-nyukukwa, 2.-nyukukide, 3.-nyukuzya, 4.-nyukwida, 5.-nyukwidalyo, 6.-nyukukisya, 7.-nyukuka-nyukuka)

shake continually, Mukaintu ulaa da wakatumbuka nibakamunyukuula basimoota. The pregnant woman gave birth when the driver jostled her. (1.-nyukuulwa, 2.-nyukuulide, 3.-nyukuuzya, 4.-nyukwiida, 5.-nyukwiidalyo, 6.-nyukuulisya, 7.-nyukuula-nyuukula, 8.-nyukuulana)

lift, Konyumpula cibulo eeci. = Lift up this bucket. (1.-nyumpulwa, 2.-nyumpwide, 3.-nyumpuzya, 4.-nyumpwida, 5.-nyumpwidalyo, 6.-nyumpulisya, 7.-nyumpula-nyumpula, 8.-nyumpulana) Also: -nyamuna.
  • take by force, Musankwa wakanyumpula musimbi wakamukaka. = The boy took by force the girl who resisted him.

stand up from a sitting position, Basibukoko tabayandi kunyumuka kuti bukoko kabutanamana, = The beer drinkers do not want to get up if the beer is not yet finished. Also: -nyamuka. (1.-nyumukwa, 2.-nyumukide, 3.-nyumusya, 4.-nyumukila, 5.-nyumukilalyo, 6.-nyumukisya 7.-nyumuka-nyumuka, 8.-nyumusyanya)

win a race, Sicikolo wesu wakabanyundila beenzinyina mumuzundano. Our pupil won the race from his friends in the competition. (1.-nyundilwa, 2.-nyundwide, 3.-nyundizya, 4.-nyundilila, 5.-nyundi-lilalyo, 6.-nyundilisya, 7.-nyundila-nyundila, 8.-nyundilana) Also: -zunda
be competitive with one another, Babelesi bamwi balayanda kunyundilana ababelesinyina. = Some workers want to compete with their fellow-workers. Also: -zundikizya.

sprinkle, Walikunyunga lusu-lusu Iwamusamu muli cakulya. = S/he was sprinkling powdered medicine in the food. Also: -nyunya. (1.-nyungwa, 2.-nyungide, 3.-nyungizya, 4.-nyungila, 5.-nyungilalyo, 6.-nyungilisya 7.-nyunga-nyunga, 8.-nyungilana)

cut off, Wakamunyungula buyo kuboko komwe = He only cut off one of his arms. (1.-nyungulwa, 2.-nyungwide, 3.-nyunguzya, 4.-nyungwida, 5.-nyungwidalyo 6.-nyungulisya, 7.-nyungula-nyungula, 8.-nyungulana) Also: -nyongola.
be sprinkled, (2.-nyungide, 3.-nyungizya, 4.-nyungila, 5.-nyungilalyo, 6.-nyungilisya, 7.-nyungwa-nyungwa, 8.-nyungilana)

sprinkle, Wanyunina-nyunina musamu ujaya muli cakulya. S/he was sprinkling medicine that kills in the food. Also: -nyunya-nyunya (1.-nyuninwa-nyuninwa, 2.-nyunide-nyunide, 3.-nyunizya-nyunizya, 4.-nyunina 5.-nyunina-nyuninalyo, 6.-nyunisya-nyunisya, 7.-nyunina-nyunina, 8.-nyuninana-nyuninana)

pause, stay for a while, Mudaala wakanyunsumana ciindi cisyoonto buyo kalibambila kubweza Iweendo Iwakwe. The old man stayed for a short time whilst preparing for his journey. Also: -nyonsomana. (1.-nyunsumanwa, 2.-nyunsumanide, 3.-nyunsumanya, 4. -nyunsumanina, 5.-nyunsumaninalyo, 6.-nyunsumanisya, 7.-nyunsumana-nyunsumana, 8.-nyunsumaninana)

spatter, sprinkle, Kamucinyunya munyo umbi kutegwa cilweele cisyu. = Sprinkle more salt on the relish so that it becomes tasty. Unyunyenyunye musamu ooyu atalaa matuvwu acisyu. = Sprinkle this medicine on top of the leaves of relish. (1.-nyunyigwa, 2.-nyunyide, 3.-nyunyizya, 4.-nyunyina, 5.-nyunyinalyo, 6.-nyunyisya, 7.-nyunya-nyunya, 8.-nyunyana)
  • dribble a football, Uulya mwana ulabanyunya beenzinyina mubbola cinoneezya. That young one dribbles the ball beautifully through his friends. Teentaani wakali kunyunya bbola kapati. = Teentaani was a great dribbler of the ball.

spatter repeatedly, drizzle as rain, sprinkle, as pepper on food, drizzle, Mvwula tiiyakomena, ya-nyunya-nyunya buyo. = The rain did not get heavy, it was just drizzling. Also: -nyunina-nyunina, -nywantila, -nywantika.
sprinkle, rt. -nyunya, Mukwesu bakamunyunyila musamu mubukoko. They sprinkled poison in my brother's beer. (4.-nyunyila, 5.-nyunyilalyo, 8.-nyunyilana)

sprinkle continuously, Basimbi bakalibambila amuunde wakulinyunyiila akulinunkilizya kabotu mibili yabo. The girls prepared themselves with a scent for sprinkling themselves and perfuming their bodies. (1.-nyunyiilwa, 2.-nyunyiilide, 3.-nyunyiizya, 4.-nyunyiilila, 5.-nyunyiilalyo, 6.-nyunyiilisya, 7.-nyunyiila-nyunyiila, 8.-nyunyiilana)
sit for a while, Nkaaka kauno musa unyunyumane-nyunyumane. = Here is a stool, my friend, so that you can sit for a while.

delay for a while, Akaambo kakuti wakalibindide wakanyunzumana ciindi cisyoonto kuti amvwe makani akali kubandikwa. = Because he was in a hurry he delayed just a bit so that he could hear the news that was being discussed. Also: -nyunsumana, -sunsumana. (1.-nyunzumanwa, 2.-nyunzumene, 3.-nyunzumanya, 4.-nyunzumanina, 5.-nyunzumaninalyo, 6.-nyunzumanisya, 7.-nyunzumana-nyunzumana, 8.-nyunzumaninana)
delay, hang on, Munene unyunzumene buyo, kuli nkwaya. = The old man hanging on for a while, he is going somewhere.

arouse from a settled position, Kamunyunzumika buyo mwana, tuyanda kweenda. = Arouse the child, we are already going. (1.-nyunzumikwa, 2.-nyunzumikide, 3.-nyunzumika, 4.-nyunzumikila, 5.-nyunzumikilalyo, 6.-nyunzumikisya, 7.-nyunzumika-nyunzumika, 8.-nyunzumikana)

drink, Ndabasiya banywa bukoko kwa Mundale. = I left them drinking beer at Mundale's. (1.-nyugwa, 2.-nywide, 3.-nywinsya, 4.-nywida, 5.-nywidalyo, 6.-nywisya, 7.-nywaanywa, 8.-nywidana)
  • score, Musankwa naakalyuuma bbola lyakanywa. = When the boy struck the ball it went into the net.

drizzle, Imvwula yakali kunywatika Mudenda naakaunka. = The rain was drizzling when Mudenda left. (2.-nywatikide, 3.-nywatizya, 4.-nywatikila, 5.-nywatikilalyo, 6.-nywatikisya, 7.-nywatika-nywatika) Also: -sunsumuna, -sunsumuka, -sunsiilas, -lunda-lunda, -fwanta-fwanta.

drizzle, Yakali kunywantila mvwula nindakasika. = The rain was drizzling when I arrived. (1.-nywantilwa, 2.-nywantilide, 3.-nywantizya, 4.-nywantwida 5.-nywantwidalyo, 6.-nywantilisya, 7.-nywantila-nywantila) Also: -sunsumuna, -nywatika.

move in a hidden manner, Chinyama naakabona musilikani, wakanyweemuka akwiinda kunze ananda. = When Chinyama saw the policeman he moved furtively and passed behind the house. (1.-nyweemukwa, 2.-nyweemukide, 3.-nyweemusya, 4.-nyweemukila, 5.-nyweemukilalyo, 6.-nyweemukisya, 7.-nyweemuka-nyweemuka, 8.-nyeemukana) Also: -nyeemuka.

drink along with, Milambo wakatambula nkomeki yacibwantu, wakanywidilizya abunyenyene kwategwa 'mmusamu wamucamba'. = Milambo received the cup of sweet-beer, he drank it along with the ants which are called 'medicine for the chest.' (1.-nywidilizyigwa, 2.-nywidikizyide, 4.-nywidilizyizya, 5.-nywidilizyizyalyo, 6.-nywidilizyisya, 7.-nywidilizyanywidilizya, 8.-nywidilizyanya)

cause to drink, rt. -nywa, Bana bayakukunywisya nombe ampongo. The children are going to make the cattle and goats drink water. (1.-nyugwa, 2.-nywide, 3.-nywisya, 4.-nywida, 5.-nywidalyo, 6.nywisya, 7.-nwisya-nwisya, 8.-nywisyanya)
  • drink to excess, Bukoko kuti wabunywisya mbubi. It is bad to drink too much beer.
  • score a goal, e.g Muleya wakanywisya ziindi zyotatwe. Muleya scored three times.

trot, Mubbi wakali kunzeba-nzeba kumbele aamusilikani. = The thief was trotting in front of the policeman. Also: -zeba-zeba (1.-nzebwa-nzebwa, 2.-nzebede-nzebede, 3.-nzebya-nzebya, 4.-nzebela-nzebela, 5.-nzebela-nzebelalyo, 6.-nzebesyanzebesya, 7.-nzeba-nzeba, 8.-nzebezyanya-nzebezyanya)

pant, as when seized with fear, Wakalema kunzekama mubbi naakajatwa. The thief was weary with panting when he was caught. (1.-nzekamwa, 2.-nzekamide, 3.-nzekamya, 4.-nzekamina, 5.-nzekaminalyo, 6.-nzekamisya, 7.-nzekama-nzekama, 8.-nzekamizyanya) Also: -zekema, -kankamana, -fwooteka.
sparkle, shine, glisten, Bulungu bwangu bulaņaima. = My beads are sparkling. (2.-naimide, 3.-naimya, 4.-naimina, 5.-naiminalyo, 6.-naimisya, 7.-naima-naima) Also: -njelema.

open as a knife, pull as a trigger, Simamvwa naakanyema wakananamuna mesi kuti ayase musankwa ngwaakajana munanda. = When Sima-mvwa became angry he opened the knife so that he would stab the man whom he found in the house. (1.-nanamunwa, 2.-nanamwide, 3.-nanamuzya, 4.-nanamwida, 5.-nanamwidalyo, 6.-nanamunisya, 7.-nanamuna-nanamuna, 8.-nanamwidana) Also: -nanyuna.
. scorch continually, Izuba Iyanantuula citaambiki. = The sun was scorching severely. (1.-nantuulwa, 2.-nantwiide, 3.-nantuuzya, 4.-nantwiida, 5.-nantwiidalyo, 6.-nantuulisya, 7.-nantuula-nantuula)

open as a knife, pull trigger of a gun, (1.-nanyunwa, 2.-nanywide, 3.-nanyuzya, 4.-nanywida, 5.-nanwidalyo, 6.-nanyunisya, 7.-nanyuna-nanyuna, 8.-nanyunana) Also: -nanamuna.
  • rip open, Muvwimi wamunanyuna muzovwu. = The hunter ripped the elephant open.
scorch, as sun does, Izuba sunu lyananaula buya kubala. = Today the sun was just scorching. (1.-nanaulwa, 2.-nanawide, 3.-nanauzya, 4.-nanawida, 5.-nanawidalyo, 6.-nanaulisya, 7.-nanaula-nanaula)
buzz, as a mosquito, Mansenya alikunota masiku onse. The mosquitoes were buzzing all night. (1.-notwa, 2.-notede, 3.-notezya, 4.-notela, 5.-notelalyo, 6.-notesya, 7.-nota-nota) =

grumble, Bakamusiya mucembele kanunta akusyola. = They left the old lady, she grumbling and hissing. Bakaintu abana bakatalika kununta akulililila, pesi banalumi kabanyemena kuti, Amuumune mulatuletelezya. " = The women and children began to moan and sob, but the men were annoyed with them saying they should be quiet, they would bring him (the mad man) to them. (1.-nuntwa, 2.-nuntide, 3.-nuntya, 4.-nuntila, 5.-nuntilalyo, 6.-nuntisya, 7.-nunta-nunta)
growl, Babwa bakalizumenene kujoka munsi kumwi kabanuntauka. The dogs persisted in going backwards while growling.

mutter, hum, murmur, Kwaambisya, koleka kunununa kwaambaula. = Speak up, don't be muttering. Mutinta wakaunka kumwi kayaa bunununa kaimbo ansaansi. Mutinta went while humming a song. Bapati bakali kwiide kuuma nkwasi akunununa-nununa ansa-ansi kusola kwiingula akuzumina kumajwi akali kwaambwa. The elders were just clapping and murmuring in a low voice trying to answer and agree with the words which were being said. (1.-ŋununwa, 2.-nununide, 3.-nununya, 4.-nununina, 5.-nununinalyo, 6.-nununisya, 7.-nununa-nununa, 8.-nununinana)
  • grumble secretly, Mapande wakali kunununa nobakamutanda amulimo. = Mapande was grumbling secretly when they sacked him. Also: -nunuta

discuss privately, Masiku Mainza wakanununina mukaintu wakwe. At night Mainza discussed privately with his wife. (1.-nununinwa, 2.-nununide, 3.-nuŋunizya, 4.-nununina, 5.-nununinalyo, 6.-nununisya, 7.-nuŋunanununa, 8.-nununinana)

complain in suppressed way because of fear, grumble, Bana nibakapegwa cakulya cibi, bakali kununuta buyo nkaambo bakali kumuyoowa mwiiyi mupati. = When the children were given bad food, they were complaining in a hidden way because they feared the headmaster. Bakali kusunsila buyo kuti mukaintu wakajikide mundyoli atakataliki kununuta kuti tabamulidi nzyajika. = They were dipping into the mixture of pounded dried pumpkin leaves and groundnuts so that the woman who cooked it would not start to grumble saying that they had not eaten what she had cooked. (1.-nunutwa, 2.-nunutide, 3.-nunutya, 4.-nunutila, 5.-nunutilalyo, 6.-nunutisya, 7.-nunutanunuta, 8. nunutilana) Also: -nununa

show displeasure by some sign, Bantu banuntauka kukaka ncaamba. The people showed their displeasure in disgreeing at what he said. (1.-nuntaukwa, 2.-nuntaukide, 3.-nuntauzya, 4.-nuntaukila, 5.-nuntaukilalyo, 6.-nuntaukisya, 7.-nuntauka-nuntauka, 8.-ŋuntausyanya) Also: -lulauka, -nutauka.

grumble, Basicikolo balanuta-nuta, tabayandi kulya nyabo. = The pupils are grumbling, they don't like eating beans. (1.-nutwa-nutwa, 2.-nutidenutide, 3.-nutizya-nutizya, 4.-nutila-nutila, 5.-nutila-nutilalyo, 6.-nutisya-nutisya, 7.-nutanuta, 8.-nutilana-nutilana)

show displeasure, complain, Nibakamwaambila kuti asanzye mitiba wakatalika kunutauka. = When they asked her to wash the dishes, she began to complain. (1.-nutaukwa, 2.-nutaukide, 3.-nutauzya, 4.-ŋutaukila, 5.-nutaukilalyo, 6.-nutaukisya, 7.-nutauka-nutauka, 8.nutaukana) Also: -nuntauka.
ululate, Bantu bakanwanula nguluulu naakasika nabwiinga. = The people ululated when the bridegroom arrived.
buzzing around, Mizeezo yakwe yoonse yakali kwiide kunwiima mutwe woonse. = All his thoughts were just buzzing around in his head.

grumble, murmur, Mpanda zyuulu, nkabela bantu boonse bakanwinta. I am clearing the anthills for planting, hence all the people are grumbling. (1.-nwintwa, 2.-nwintide, 3.-nwintizya, 4.-nwintila, 5.-nwintilalyo, 6.-nwintisya, 7.-nwinta-nwinta, 8.-nwintilana)

surround, Bamooba mubbi naatiitije basicikolo. The pupils surrounded the thief when he was about to run away. Basikalumamba bakaoba munzi okwesu akuunyonyoona. The soldiers surrounded our village and destroyed it. Katooba coonde eci mukanjila kanyama. = Let us surround this thicket into which the little animal has entered. Also: -teenkana. (1.-obwa, 2.-obede, 3.-obya, 4.-obela, 5.-obelalyo, 6.-obesya, 7.-oba-oba, 8.-obaikana)
  • hook, bend, Muzeli wakooba nswi mumalakavwiya. The fisherman hooked the fish by the gills. Also: -loba, -goba.
  • surround game, Bavwimi nibakabona namusya kalede, bakafwambaana kumooba, mpoona bakamuyasa masumo. = When the hunters saw the duiker, they quickly surrounded it, thereupon they pierced it with spears. Also: -zinga
  • tether, restrain, Kobelesya intambo yakooba munyama ucela. = Use a rope to tether the animal which is grazing.
insert into, *Kamuloobaika masanzu lubaya olu nombe zitanjili mucisyu.* Insert the branches in this fence so that the cattle do not enter the garden. Also: -vwabaika.

spread out, as pumpkin vines, *Luungu loobaikana mumuunda.* The pumpkin vines have spread out in the field. *Zisamu zyabuluba zyakoobaikana kukomena.* Cotton plants spread out as they grow. *Babwa tabalunduki kabotu mumasanzu aakoogbaikana.* = Dogs do not run.well where the shrubs are webbed together. Also: -obeekana, -ombengana.
rush in a crowd, Bantu bakoobana kuya kukubona Munali = All the people rushed in a crowd to see Livingstone.

intertwine, rt. -oba, Kamuya kumbewu mukatalike kuobeeka mamvwa alukwakwa. = Go to the garden so that you start intertwining thorns in the fence. (1.-obeekwa, 2.-obeekede, 3.-obeezya, 4.-obeekela, 5.-obeekelalyo, 6.-obeekesya, 7.-obeeka-obeeka, 8.-obeekana)
intertwine with one another, Milibo yalungu yakaobeekana amilibo yanyabo = The pumpkin runners were intertwining with the bean runners. Also: -obaikana.

hang on an elevated support, Kotenda mitendu yanyama akwiiyobeka amulenga. = Cut the meat up into strips and hang them up on the rack. (1.-obekwa, 2.-obekede, 3.-obezya, 4.-obekela, 5.-obekelalyo, 6.-obekesya, 7.-obeka-obeka, 8.-obekana)
  • link up, Kamuobeka nketani kucilayi. = Link up the chain to the sledge. Also: -vwaka
  • cool the heart, Mudaala wakaobeka moyo naakanywa cibwantu. = The old man cooled his heart when he drank the sweet-beer.

accuse falsely of a crime, implicate in a crime, Choonde bakamoobekezya mulandu ngwaatakacita. = They falsely accused Choonde of a crime which he did not commit. (1.-obekezyegwa, 2.-obekezyede, 3.-obekezya, 4.-obekezyezya 5.-obekezyezyalyo, 6.-obekezyesya, 7.-obekezya-obekezya, 8.-obekezyanya) Also: -tamikizya, -lambauzya.

detain, nombe kamuzyoobela muciba, anze zilatija. = Impound the cattle in the kraal, outside they will run away. (1.-obelwa, 2.-obelede, 3.-obelezya, 4.-obelela, 5.-obelelalyo, 6.-obelesya, 7.-obela-obela, 8.-obelelana)
entangle, be caught up in, Cakusama caobelela amamvwa. = The cloth is caught up in thorns.

hold for, be detained, Ndakoobelwa musimbi wakali kunditija lyoonse. = The girl was caught for me who was always running away from me.
  • be engaged in, be occupied, Ndakoobelwa mumilimo, ncindatakali kusika kumuswaangano. = I was detained because of work, that is why I did not come for the meeting.
spread as pumpkin vines, e.g Luungu Iwakaobengana alutende. = The pumkins were spreading with runners. Also: -obaikana, -obeekana, -pambana, -tandabala

interrupt, impede, Milimo yakandoobezya ncindatakasikila. = The work blocked me, that is why I did not come. Guwo lyakandoobezya ncinda kamuka kusika. = The gale was blowing against me, that is why I was late. (1.-obezyegwa, 2.-obezyede, 3.-obezya, 4.-obezyezya, 5.-obezyezyalyo, 6.-obezyesya, 7.-obezya-obezya, 8.-obezyanya.)
  • quieten the heart, rt. -obeka, Koobezya moyo, cilainda. = Quieten the heart, it will pass. Also: -kkazika.
  • tire, Babwa bakamoobeyza syaambololo akumujaya. = The dogs made the kudu tired and killed it.

come down, Ndilanyamuka izuba lyaoboka. = I will start off when the sun is sinking. Muyuni wakaoboka kuzya ansi naakakatala. = The bird came down when it was tired. (1.-obokwa, 2.-obokede, 3.-obosya, 4.-obokela, 5.-obokelalyo, 6.-obokesya, 7.-oboka-oboka, 8.-obokelana)

stretch oneself in trying to reach something, Baya boobokela matobo mujulu muya. They stretch themselves to reach the matobo fruit above there. Kainga kakaobokela twana twankuku. An eagle swooped down to catch the chicks.

take down, hook a branch in order to bend it down, Kamoobola nkuni mumubombo. = Hook down a branch of the mubombo tree for firewood. Wakatuma muce wakwe kuti awobole nsuwa yamabisi. He sent his young brother to take down the gourd of sour milk. (1.-obolwa, 2.-obwede, 3.-obozya, 4.-obweda, 5.-obwedalyo, 6.-obolesya, 7.-obola-obola, 8.-obolana) Also: -ovwola.
  • beckon, bring to one's notice, Komoobola musimbi uulya apiluke. = Call out to that girl to return. Kunyina awandoobola kuti kuno kulubazu kulatondwa kusika. No one indicated to me that it was forbidden to enter this place.

unhook, Kofwambaana kundoobolola kamvwa kasikomwa kandioba kusule. = Quickly unhook the hooked thorn which has caught me on the back. (1.-obololwa, 2.-obolwede, 3.-obolozya, 4.-obolweda, 5.-obolwedayo, 6.-obololesya, 7.obolola-obolola, 8.-obololana) Also: -gobonona.

be set out to graze before milking, Mukupa uvwula liobosegwa nombe. Milk is plentiful during the time the cattle are set out to graze before milking. (2.-obosedwe, 3.-obosezya, 4.-obosedwa, 5.-obosedwalyo, 7.-obosegwa-obosegwa) Also: -yobosegwa

quench the thirst, Ngaaya meenda, koobosya moyo. = Here is water, quench your thirst. (1.-obosegwa, 2.-obosyede, 3.-obosyezya, 4.-obosyezya, 5.-obosyzyalyo, 7.-obosya-obosya)
  • graze cattle before milking, Mazuba nobaobosya nombe basankwa, inga mukupa mmunji. = The days when the boys bring the cows back after grazing, the milk is plentiful. Also: -obozya
be sent to graze, nombe zyoobosegwa zilazandulwa kuboombe kwaciindi cilamfwu. = The cows that are sent out to graze are separated from the calves for a long time.

graze cattle before milking, Kamuzyoobozya nombe tukame mukupa munji. Graze. the cattle before milking and we will milk plenty of milk. (1.-obozyegwa, 2.-obozyede, 3.-obozyesya, 4.-obozyezya, 5.-obozyezyalyo, 6.-obozyesya, 7.-obozya-obozya)

become blind, Munene Chooka wakoofwaala, sunu wanyikila mumulindi. = The old man Chooka, who has become blind, sunk into a hole today. (1.-ofwaalwa, 2.-ofweede, 3.-ofwaazya, 4.-ofwaalila, 5.-ofwaalilalyo, 6.-ofwaalisya, 7.-ofwaala-ofwaala, 8.-ofwaazyanya) Also: -baya.

be in a blind state, physically, spiritually or intellectually, Ndakoofwaala, alino ndoofweede, ajuu-nza ndinakoofweede. = I was blind, and now I am blind and tomorrow I will be blind. Muntu *uofweede* mumajwi aa Leza takonzyi kukambaukila bantu. = A person who is blind spiritually as regards the words of God is unable to preach to people.

bow low, Basika amulyango inga *nkooka* buya kutegwa bacikonzye kunjila. = When they reach the doorway they should bend down so that they can enter. Bana baleelede *kooka* nobapa zintu kubapati. = Children should bow when they give things to the elders. Eeci ciindi izuba lyakatalikide *kooka* kapati. = At that time the sun had begun to sink quickly. (1.-okwa, 2.-okede, 3.-okezya, 4.-okela, 5.-okelalyo, 6.-okesya, 7.-oka-oka, 8.-okezyanya.)

rest, Twakaima mucimvwule katusola kulyookezya. = We stopped in the shade trying to rest ourselves. Ndali *kulyookezya* nindamana kubeleka mulimo muyumu. = I was resting myself when I had finished doing hard jobs. (1.-okezyegwa, 2.-okezya, 3.-okezyesya, 4.-okezyezya, 5.-okezyezyalyo, 6.-okezyesya, 7.-okezya-okezya)
sun declining, Nolyako
zuba, ndakaunka kunanda yangu. = When the sun was declining, I went to my house.
decline as sun, Mbulya
biyo zuba, bantu bakatalika koompana alubuwa. = When the sun was declining the people started to gather in the courtyard.

cool down what is hot, Ceele cabana *coola* kale, kamubapa balye. = The porridge of the children has cooled down already, give it to them so that they eat. (1.-olezyegwa, 2.-olede, 3.-ozya, 4.-olela, 5.-olelalyo, 6.-olesya, 7.-ola-ola, 8.-olezyanya)
  • cease as pain or anger, *Ndilalya moyo wangu waola.* = I will eat when my heart has cooled off.
  • demolish, *Kamuola ciluli.* = Demolish the roof.

destroy, Badaala nobakamana kuyaka kaanda kamalende bana *bakakaolaula.* = When the old men had finished building a rain shrine, the children destroyed it. (1.-olaulwa, 2.-olawide, 3.-olauzya, 4.-olawida, 5.-olawidalyo, 6.-olaulisya, 7.-olaula-olaula, 8.-olaulana)

collapse, crumble, *nanda yabaacisya yakooleka jilo.* = The house of my uncle collapsed yesterday. (2.-olekede, 3.-olezya, 4.-olekela, 5.-olekelalyo, 6.-olekesya 7.-oleka-oleka) Also: -dilimuka, -kolomoka.

ululate, Bamakaintu *balaolobwezya kunkolola.* = The women are ululating at the initiation ceremony. cf. -uma ngoloolo, -ululuzya, -ulubwizya. (2.-olobwezyede, 3.-olobwezyezya, 4.-olobwezyela, 5.-olobwezyelalyo, 6.-olobwezyesya, 7.-olobwezya-olobwezya, 8.-olobwezyanya)

eat first maize, eat after a period of hunger, Swebo kono twakalifwambaanide *kooloka* kwiinda bamwi. = We were quick to eat the first maize before others this year. Ciindi ncibakayanda buyo *kooloka*, bantu bamu Gwembe bakanjililwa zyuuka zyiitwa kuti bacivwunye mumyuunda yabo. = Just when they were about to eat the first maize, the fields of the Gwembe people were invaded by grain-eating insects called
(green, fat, grain-eating insects, one and a half inch long, eaten by some people). (1.-olokwa, 2.-olokede, 3.-olosya, 4.-olokela, 5.-olokelalyo, 6.-olokesya, 7.-oloka-oloka, 8.-olosyanya)

straighten, stretch, Mulimi ulakonzya kukagogomeka naa kukoolola kasamu kweendelana abube bwamusamu ngwayanda kuti kakabe. = The farmer can bend or straighten a young tree according to the shape of the mature tree which he wants it to become. Bakaakumoolola kucibbadela basilisi. = The doctors straightened him out at the hospital. Munene ulalyoolola. = The old man stretched himself. Wakaamba Kagele kumwi kalyoolola. = Kagele spoke while stretching himself. Ndakaya kukweendeenda koolola maulu. = I went walking to stretch the legs. (1.-ololwa, 2.-olwede, 3.-olozya, 4.-olweda, 5.-olwedalyo, 6.-ololesya, 7.-olola-olola, 8.-ololana)
  • crack ones knuckles, Wakali kuolola minwe. = He was cracking his knuckles.
  • subjugate, control, Musankwa wakali kuyandisya kulwana bakamoolola beenzinyina bakamwiinda nguzu. = The boy who was fond of fighting was controlled by other boys who were stronger than him.
  • be protected by the ancestors, Sena walibatolede bana kukoololwa kumalende? = Did you take the children to be stretched at the rainshrine? (a special annual ritual in which the ancestors are asked to protect the child as the parents stretch the limbs of the children.)

become straight, Ijanza lyangu lyatalika koololoka sunu. = My hand has begun to become straight enough today. Mulema wakoololoka. = The cripple became straigtened. (1.-ololokwa, 2.-olokede, 3.-ololozya, 4.-ololokela, 5.-ololokelalyo, 6.-ololokesya, 7.-ololola-ololoka, 8.-ololosyanya)
  • become placated, Moyo wakwe wakaololoka naakapegwa mali aakwe. = He was placated when he received his money.

straighten out, as a wire, stretch out, Kamukoololola kasamu aaka katandabale. = Stretch that stick out to make it straight. Basankwa baololola ziyako zyananda. = The boys are straightening out the poles of the house.
iron as clothes, Kamubelesya nsimbi ikasaala koololosya zisani zyamwana. = Use the warm iron to remove the crease of the childs clothes.

be straightened, be controlled, Ziyako zidiimene, zyeelede koololwa kutegwa zikkale kabotu mubwaanda. = The poles should be straightened so that they fit properly into the wall. (2.-olwede, 3.-olozya, 4.-olweda, 5.-olwedalyo, 6.-ololesya, 7.-ololwa-ololwa, 8.-ololana)

shout, scream, Sibukoko wakali kooloma jilo naakakolwa bukoko. = The drunkard was roaring yesterday when he was drunk. Mwana wakali kooloma kulila. = The child was howling. (1.-olomenwa, 2.-olomede, 3.-olomya, 4.-olomena, 5.-olomenalyo, 6.-olomesya, 7.-oloma-oloma 8.-olomenana) Also: -ongolola

cause to come to, Ncicandoolomona biya. = It is just that which made me come. (1.-olomonwa, 2.-olomwede, 3.-olomozya, 4.-olomweda, 5.-olomwedalyo, 6.-olomonesya, 7.-olomona-olomona, 8.-olomonana)
  • demolish, Kamuolomona nanda eeyi. = Destroy this house.

become cool, Amulindile ceele kacicooloola nkaambo cicipya. = Wait for the porridge to cool because it is still hot. (1.-oloolwa, 2.-oloolede, 3.-oloozya, 4.-oloolweda, 5.-oloolwedalyo, 6.-oloolesya, 7.-oloola-oloola, 8.-oloolana)
  • demolish a building, Sincinko wacioloola caanda campongo. = The mad one is knocking down the goats shelter. Also: -vwinyauna.

cry out at a distance, Muntu wanyikila mumulindi waolopompa buzuba boonse. = The one who dropped into the hole was crying out all day. Also: -ompolola, -kwiila. (1.-olopompwa, 2.-olopopweda, 3.-olopompya, 4.-olopompela, 5.-olopompelalyo, 6.-olopompesya, 7.-olopompa-olopompa, 8.-olopompaninana)
  • deliver a message, Twatuma kale musankwa kuya koolopompa lufwu Iwasibbuku. = We have already sent a boy to deliver the message about the headman's death.

stretch, Bazyali bakacibikka ciyanda camucelo kunsi amatende a mwana ansi. Bakamulyatika mwana akumoolota. The parents put a medical root under the feet of the child on the ground. They made it walk on it and stretched the child. (1.-olotwa, 2.-olotede, 3.-olotya, 4.-olotela, 5.-olotelalyo, 6.-olotesya, 7.-olota-olota, 8.-olotana) Also: -olola.

bewail, cry out, "Maawe!" Bakoomba kulila lyakafwa basibbola bacisi. They lamented when the country's footballers died. Banyina balaomba cakutaleka kulila mwana. = The mother unceasingly laments for her child. (1.-ombwa, 2.-ombede, 3.ombezya, / ombya, 4.-ombela, 5.-ombelalyo, 6.-ombesya, 7.-omboomba, 8.-ombezyanya.)
  • masturbate, Basankwa bafwubafwuba balayanda kulyoomba. = Foolish boys want to masturbate.

dance a baby up and down, Kamumuomba-omba mwana aleke kulila. Dance the child up and down to stop it crying. Also: umbulizya.
  • abate, keep down as boiling water, Koomba-omba cinkomba citaunki. = Keep the okra down from boiling over.
  • cool down emotionally, Komoomba-omba mwana aleke kwaambaula. = Quieten the child so that she stops talking. Ndakali koombo-omba musankwa wakali kuyanda kuuma mudaala. = I was cooling down the temper of the boy who wanted to beat the old man. Also: -fwunta-fwunta.
  • pat, Bamaama bakandoombaomba andelo nindakanyemede kapati. = My mother patted me on the shoulder when I was extremely angry.
put a hem, Koombela musinsi wangu. = Put a hem on my skirt. (1.-ombelwa, 2.-ombede, 3.-ombezya, 4.-ombelela, 5.-ombelelalyo, 6.-ombelesya, 7.-ombela-ombela, 8.-ombelelana)

spread out, Lungu Iwaombengana mumuunda. Pumpkin runners spread over the field. Also: -obaikana. (1.-ombenganwa, 2.-ombenganide, 3.-ombenganya, 4.-ombenganina, 5.-ombenganinalyo, 6.-ombenganisya, 7.-ombengana-ombengana)

suspend oneself by the hands, Ndakalyoombetela amaanza kucisamu. = I suspended myself by the hands from a tree. (1.-ombetelwa, 2.-ombetede, 3.-ombetezya, 4.-ombetelela, 5.-ombetelelalyo, 6.-ombetelelesya, 7.-ombetela-ombetela, 8.-ombetelelana) Also: -gwambatila, -obokela, -lembetelas, -zambatila.

discuss at length, exact explanations from one who has slandered me, thrash out a question, judge a case, Matongo wakali koombolola muntu wakamutamikizya kaambo. Matongo was asking for a detailed explanation from the man who had slandered him. _Buzuba bwakoombolola mulandu oyu bwakasika._ = The day for cross-examining this case arrived. (1.-ombololwa, 2.-ombololede, 3.-ombolozya, 4.-ombolweda, 5.-ombolwedalyo, 6.-ombololesya, 7.-ombolola-ombolola, 8.-ombololana) Also: -ombolozya.
  • lessen the power, as of medicine, _Mukupa nguukonzya koombolola musamu ukola muntu._ = It is milk which can lessen the power of poison in a person. Also: -tontozya.

testify, elicit details and exact explanations, _Ndakamoombolozya kuli ncaakacitide kaindi limwi wazumina akulilekelela._ = I elicited a full explanation of what he had done in the past until he finally agreed and confessed. Also: -ombolola.
cross-examine, _Musankwa a musimbi baloombolozyanya kumakani akuyandana kwabo._ = The boy and the girl are demanding an explanation from each other as regards their love-pact.

complain, relate personal problems, _Ndakali kulyoombooka mapenzi angu._ = I was relating my problems. _Ndiombooka mapenzi aanjila mumukwasyi wangu._ = I relate the sufferings that I am experiencing in my family. _Ncibi kuombooka lyoonse._ It is bad to complain always. (1.-ombookwa, 2.-ombookede, 3.-ombookezya, 4.-ombookela, 5.-ombookelalyo, 6.-obookesya, 7.-ombooka-ombooka, 8.-ombookana)
share one's problems with, _Mainza naakasika wakabaombookela bausyi mapenzaakwe._ = When Mainza arrived he related his problems to his father.

cool down, _Toelede kumuka kuomboomba cinkomba nkaambo inga caunkila ansi._ = You ought not to be slow in cooling down the okra because it may flow over. Also: -omba-omba, -ombosya. (1.-omboombwa, 2.-omboombede, 3.-omboombya, 4.-omboombela, 5.-omboombelalyo, 6.-omboombesya, 7.-omboomba-omboomba, 8.-omboombana)

pacify, cause to cool down, _Ndakafwambaana kumoombosya kutegwa aleke kunyema._ = I was quick to pacify him so that he would cease to be angry. (1.-ombosyegwa, 2.-ombosyede, 3.-ombosyezya, 4.-ombosyela, 5.-ombosyelalyo, 6.-ombosyesya, 7.-ombosya-ombosya, 8.-ombosyanya Also: -ombozya.

keep down from boiling, _Koombozya nsima itaunki._ = Keep the nsima from boiling over. (1.-ombozyegwa, 2.-ombozyede, 4.-ombozyezya, 5.-ombozyezyalyo, 6.-ombozyesya, 7.-ombozya-ombozya. 8.-ombozyanya)
  • make quiet, _Koombozya mwana._ = Make the child quiet. Also: -umbulizya

bow down in gratitude, _Atukkale ansi toombwezeke, tuvwobele, nkaambo nguli zyesu zyatwiiminina._ = Let us bow down in respect, let us clap, because our ancestors have protected us. (1.-ombwezekwa, 2.-ombwezekede, 3.-ombwezesya, 4.-ombwezekela, 5.-ombwezekelalyo, 6.-ombwezekesya, 7.-ombwezeka-ombwezeka, 8.-ombwezekana)

make one cry out in pain, rt. omba, _Akamoombya maanko mwana._ = The hornets made the child cry out in pain. _Nzala yakamoombya._ = The hunger made her cry out in pain. Also: -omona. (1.-ombezyegwa, 2.-ombede, 3.-ombya, 4.-ombela, 5.-ombelalyo, 6.-ombesya, 7.-ombya-ombya, 8.-ombezyanya)

disappear, as into mud or water, Nyeleti yangu yaomenena mumavwu. My needle has disappeared into the soil. Mapopwe angu akaomenena mubulongo. My maize seedlings failed to germinate in the soil. (1.-omenenwa, 2.-omenede, 3.-omenezya, 4.-omenenena, 5.-omenenenalyo, 6.-omenenesya, 7.-omenena-omenena, 8.-omenezyanya.)

become choked with weed, Mukaalimine mapopwe aali mumbewu, aomfwokelwa syokwe. = You go and weed the maize in the garden, it is being choked with weed. (2.-omfwokedwe, 3.-omfwokezya, 4.-omfwokelelwa, 5.-omfwokelelwalyo, 7.-omfwokelwa-omfwokelwa) Also: -fwuba
describing overcast weather, Kulyoomfwokede. It is overcast.

drop one's head when hungry, Kumeso ndaomfwola akaambo kanzala. = My face is weak with the hunger. (1.-omfwolwa, 2.-omfwede, 3.-omfwozya, 4.-omfwolela, 5.-omfwolelalyo, 6.-omfwolesya, 7.-omfwola-omfwola)
  • drowse, Nindakali kubala bbuku ciindi cilamfwu ndakatalika koomfwola. = When I had been reading for a long time I began to drowse. Also: -umfwula, -uvwila.

become dark, Nsekonzyi kubona nkaambo kumeso kwandoomfwookela. = I cannot see because my eyes are becoming dim. (1.-omfwookelwa, 2.-omfwoolede, 3.-omfwookezya, 4.-omfwookelela, 5.-omfwookelelalyo, 6.-omfwookesya, 7.-omfwookela-omfwookela)
be in darkness, Nkoomfwookelwa kuli mumyoyo yabantu. = Darkness is in the hearts of the people. Also: -omfwokelwa.

nod, when sleepy, Kozwa munsi aacikko, watalika ku-omfwula. = Go away from the fire, you are beginning to nod. (1.-omfwulwa, 2.-omfwulide, 3.-omfwuzya, 4.-omfwulila, 5.-omfwulilalyo, 6.-imfwulisya, 7.-omfwula-omfwula) Also: -uvwila, -omfwola.

start lamenting at a funeral, Bakoomoka mvwiki yamana koo Chinyama. They began to lament last week at Chinyama's. Bantu bakoomoka jilo mangolezya. = The people began to lament yesterday evening. (1.-omoka, 2.-omokede, 3.-omosya, 4.-omokela, 5.-omokelalyo, 6.-omokesya, 7.-omokaomoka)
begin, as funeral lament, Idilwe lyakaomokwa jilo. = The funeral lament began yesterday.

make lament, Cakaboomona kulila nkufwa kwamwana musyoonto. It is the death of a young child that caused them to weep. Also: -ombya. (1.-omonwa, 2.-omonede, 3.-omonzya, 4.-omonena, 5.-omonenalyo, 6.-omonesya, 7.-omona-omona)
  • stop from doing or saying, quieten one down, appease, Kamumuomona ooyo, ulalitaya. = Stop him from speaking, he will make himself a slave. Twakamoomona buya ncaakaleka kutukila bantu. = We just stopped him that is why he ceased to insult the people.

call to somebody, Munene wakali koompa kunze amulundu, pesi bana tiibakamvwa. The old man was calling out behind the hill, but the children did not hear him. (1.-ompwa, 2.-ompede, 3.-ompya, 4.-ompela, 5.-ompelalyo, 6.-ompanisya, 7.-ompa-ompa, 8.-ompana)
gather around, Basikube balaompana amutunta. The vultures gather around the carcass. (1.-ompanwa, 2.-ompene, 3.-ompanya, 4.-ompanina, 5.-ompaninalyo, 6.-ompanisya, 7.-ompana-ompana)

construct, put a fence of branches around a garden or field, Kamoompela mbewu kutegwa mpongo zitalyi cisyu. Put a fence of branches around the garden so that the goats do not eat the vegetables. Ndalikuompela lubaya Iwangu. = I was making my fence with branches. (1.-ompelwa, 2.-ompede, 3.-ompezya, 4.-ompelela, 5.-ompelelelalyo, 6.-ompelesya, 7.-ompela-ompela, 8.-ompelana)

surround with bundles of thorn-bushes and grass to protect from cattle, Koompezya mamwa ncibotu nkaambo mpongo inga kaziyoowa kunjila mukati. Fencing with thorn-branches is good because the goats will fear to enter inside. (1.-ompezyegwa, 2.-ompezyede, 3.-ompezyezya, 4.-ompezyela, 5.-ompezyelalyo, 6.-ompezyesya, 7.-ompezya-ompezya, 8.-ompezyanya)

cry out to, shout, Kamumoompolola mwana ajoke ooko nkwaya. Call the child so that he returns from where he is going. (1.-ompololwa, 2.-ompolwede, 3.-ompolozya, 4.-ompolweda, 5.-ompolwedalyo, 6.-ompololesya, 7.-ompolola-ompolola, 8.-ompololana) Also: -olopompa, -woolola.

find solution by discussion, Basimabbuku bakakakilwa kuompoozya mulandu oyu. The headmen failed to resolve this crime. (1.-ompoozyegwa, 2.-ompoozyede, 3.-ompoozyesya, 4.-ompoozyezya, 5.-ompoozyezyalyo, 6.-ompoozyesya, 7.-ompoozya-ompoozya, 8.-ompoozyanya)

wander, as one who is blind, Muntu moofwu wakali kwiide koompoteka musyokwe. The blind person was just wandering around in the bush. Also: -impita, -umputila. (1.-ompotekwa, 2.-ompotekede, 3.-ompotesya, 4.-ompotekela, 5.-ompotekelalyo, 6.-ompotekesya, 7.-ompoteka-ompoteka)

sleep, Sunu ndiya koona kuli baama kutegwa nkalange uuciswa. = I am sleeping at my mother's tonight so that I can see the sick one. Wakazyoona nonzi zyabulowe. = He slept the sleep of being bewitched. Buzuboobo mbomwamvwa mwaaba ulila tako muntu uona pe; koona nkoonya kumaulu, mutwe ulalanga. = On that day when you heard the jackal there was no a person who slept; sleep was making the legs sleep while the head was looking. (1.-onwa, 2.-onede, 3.-onya, 4.-onena, 5.-onenalyo, 6.-onesya, 7.-onoona, 8.-onana)
  • lie fallow, as a field, Muunda wangu waona dima mwaka uno nkaambo yavwula myaka kaulimwa. My field is lying fallow this year because it has been ploughed for many years.
  • be left suspended or incomplete, Milimo yangu yoona akaambo kamadilwe manji. My jobs are left undone because of many funerals.
  • have sexual intercourse, Kuona bamuka bantu ncilengwa cibi. = To sleep with people's wives is an evil practice.
  • to sleep uncovered, koona mutundulu or kulala ntundubwi
  • sleep in a group, -ona kungubulo

destroy, (ety. Chibemba?) Mwiile koonaula zilengwaa Leza musyokwe amumaanda. = You are just destroying God's creatures both in the bush and in the houses. Taciyandiki kuonaula lubono ndoojana kale. It is not nec essary to waste goods which you have already got. (1.-onaulwa, 2.-onaulide, 3.-onauzya, 4.-onawida, 5.-onawidalyo, 6.-onaulisya, 7.-onaula-onaula, 8.-onaulana) Also: -nyonyoona, -zangaula.

work very hard to complete a work, *Wakaonda* mulimo wakujaya munyati. = He did a good job in killing the buffalo. (1.-ondwa, 2.-ondede, 3.-ondya, 4.-ondela, 5.-ondelalyo, 6.-ondesya, 7.-onda-onda, 8.-ondelana)
  • close the eyes of a dead person, Mwana naakafwa banyina bakafwambaana kumoonda *nkoye*. = When the child died the mother quickly closed the eyelids.

squeeze, *Wakaondelezya* munwe wakwe naakali kupwaya mabwe akuyasya. = He squeezed his finger when he was breaking stones for building. Syuumbwa naakatutanda twakaile *kuondelezya* mumasanzu. = When the lion chased us we were just pushing ourselves through the bushes. (1.-ondelezyegwa, 2.-ondelezyede, 4.-ondelezyezya, 5.-ondelezyezyalyo, 6.-ondelezyesya, 7.-ondelezya-ondelezya, 8.-ondelezyanya) Also: -syondelezya.
cause injury, Wandioondonga mubwa. = The dog has injured me. (1.-ondongwa, 2.-ondongede, 3.-ondonganya, 4.-ondongela, 5.-ondongelalyo, 6.-ondongesya, 7.-ondonga-ondonga, 8.-ondongana)
destroy, Kamulanga nombe zyanu, zyaondonganya muunda. Look at your cattle, they have destroyed the field.

crush, flatten, Mucembele wakali *koondoonda* miyanda atalaa ziyo. The old woman was crushing roots on a grinding stone. Wakanjila mukaanda akutalika kubamba-bamba akoondoonda bwizu bwaali mukati, waka lazika mwanaakwe, bakoona. = She entered the hut and began to clear it up and spread out the grass which was inside, she laid her child down, they slept. (1.-ondoondwa, 2.-ondoondede, 3.-ondoozya, 4.-ondweeda, 5.-ondweedalyo, 6.-ondoondesya, 7.-ondoonda-ondoonda, 8.-ondoondana)
suspend work, rt. -ona, <p-eg>Booneka
column3:
bulimo akaambo kamilimo imbi. = They have suspended work on the ploughed piece of land because of other works. (1.-onekwa, 2.-onekede, 3.-onezya, 4.-onekela, 5.-onekelalyo, 6.-onekesya, 7.-oneka-oneka, 8.-onekana)
  • invite or engage for a day's work, Ndakooneka bantu kuti bazyoondigwasye kulimina nyemu amapopwe mumuunda. = I invited people to come and help me weed the groundnuts and maize in the field. *Amutooneke*. = Invite us to come and work for you. Choopa wakazyooneka zisankwa zimwi kuti zizyoomugwasye kujaya muntu. Choopa hired some scoundrels to help him to kill a man.
  • cause one to fall asleep, put to rest, *Wakamooneka* mwana. = She put the child to sleep.
  • -oneka bubi = lie heavy on
  • -oneka masusu = smooth the hair Also: -lazika masusu.

column2: be invited, rt. -oneka, Kunze lyananda kwakaimvwi Bbandama ngubakoonekede jilo masiku kuti azikubanjilile mwana. Behind the house stood Bbandama whom they had invited last night to enter into the child, i.e. to break the sores in the child's throat when it had diptheria.
give information to, Njakumoonekela bamasilikani kuti bazikumujate. I will give information about him to the police so that they could catch him.
give instructions the night before, Katutanoona bataata bako
malailile aciyoocitika buzuba butobela. = Before we went to sleep father directed us with instructions as to what was to be done on the following day. Wafwuma kuunka nkaambo waka

kaambo. = She set out early because she was given instructions the previous night. (1.-onekezyegwa, 2.-onekezyede, 3.-onekezyesya, 4.-onekezyezya, 5.-onekezyezyalyo, 6.-onekezyesya, 7.-onekezya-onekezya, 8.-onekezyanya)

sleep soundly, Masiku aainda ndalyoonena kakunyina wandinyonganya. = Last night I slept well without anything disturbing me. Sunu ndilalyo*onena*, camana cipenzya. = Tonight I will sleep well, what was troubling me has passed. (1.-onenwa, 2.-onenede, 3.-onesya, 4.-onenena, 5.-onenenalyo, 6.-onenesya, 7.-onena-onena)

look after, rt. -ona, Koonenena mulwazi cilakatazya. = It is difficult to attend to the patient. (1.-onenenwa, 2.-onenede, 3.-onenesya, 4.-onenenena, 5.-onenenenalyo, 6.-onenenesya, 7.-onenena-onenena, 8.-onenenana) Also: -Iwazya.
  • sleep in the bush awaiting game, Ndakaboonenena banyama musyokwe ciindi nindakali kukuvwima. = I slept waiting for animals in the bush during the time when I was hunting.
  • sleep it out, Ndamuka kuunka kumulimo ndoonenena. = I was late for work because I slept it out.
entice, Bamadaala ba

bana basimbi amali. = Old men coax young girls with money. (1.-ongwa, 2.-ongede, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongela, 5.-ongelalyo, 6.-ongesya, 7.-onga-onga, 8.-ongana) Also: -nanyuna.
  • evade by dodging, Naakafwusa cisamu kuti anduume, ndakaonga_ansi. = When he threw a stick to hit me, I dropped down to avoid it. Also: -leya.
  • bend, Koonga mukobezyo wacibulo citekela meenda cilakatazya. = To bend the handle of the bucket for drawing water is difficult.

walk with slow steps, Kobinda kweenda, ncibi kuongaila buya ulamuka. = Hurry up as you walk, it is bad to walk with slow steps, you will be late. (1.-ongailwa, 2.-ongailide, 3.-ongaizya, 4.-ongailila, 5.-ongaililalyo, 6.-ongailisya. 7.-ongaila-ongaila)

be twisted out of shape, Mootokala nowakapwaya cisamu, waka*ongama*. = When the vehicle crashed into the tree, it was twisted out of shape. (1.-ongamwa, 2.-ongeme, 3.-ongamya, 4.-ongamina, 5.-ongaminalyo, 6.-ongamisya, 7.-ongama-ongama) Also: -gogama, -zyondongana.

be in a state of exhaustion, rt. -onga, Bakasika amunzi wakwe kumazuba kaboongedwe kapati anzala alimwi amusinzo mulamfwu. = They arrived at his village in the evening completely exhausted with the hunger and the long journey. (1.-ongelwa, 2.-ongedwe, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongedwa, 5.-ongedwalyo, 7.-ongedwe-ongedwe) Also: -gonkedwe.

entice, deceive, rt. -onga, Nseyandi muntu undoongela mwana kuti katukila bapati. = I don't like a person who deceives my child into insulting the elders. (1.-ongelwa, 2.-ongede, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongelela, 5.-ongelelalyo, 6.-ongelelesya, 7.-ongela-ongela, 8.-ongelana) Also: -yunga, -cenga.
coax, entice, Ndamo

mwana kutegwa aleke kulila. = I coaxed the child to stop crying. Beenzuma mbitwakali kweenda limwi kucikolo, bakandoongelezya kuti ntalike kufweba mbuli mbobakali kucita. = My friends with whom I was going to school enticed me to smoke as they were doing. Also: -ukauka (1.-ongelezyegwa, 2.-ongelezyede, 3.-ogelezyezya, 4.-ongelezyela, 5.-ongelezyelalyo, 6.-ongelezyesya, 7.-ongelezya-ongelezya, 8.-ongelezyanya)

be exhausted in vain, Ndakoongelwa kubbadelela mwana kucikolo walo wakacengwa abeenzinyina kuleka cikolo. I was exhausted in vain paying fees for my child who was deceived by the friends and stopped school. (2.-ongedwe, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongelelwa, 5.-ongelelwalyo, 6.-ongelelesya, 7.-ongelwa-ongelwa)
  • be led astray, Tiindakabotelwa koongelwa mwanaangu kuti kaya bweenda abasimakoko. = I was not pleased to have my son be led astray in going about with beer drinkers.
exhaust, Inzala anyota zyakamoongezya. Hunger and thirst exhausted him. (1.-ongezyegwa, 2.-ongezyede, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongezyezya, 5.-ongezyezyalyo, 6.-ongezyesya, 7.-ongezya-ongezya, 8.-ongezyanya)

live long, grow old, Kuti waloma inga waongola. If you are honest you will live long. Suntwe moowa nguongola. (proverb) = The cowardly hyena is the one who lives long. (2.-ongwede, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongweda, 5.-ongwedalyo, 6.-ongolesya, 7.-ongolaongola)

be in years of old age, Mukabbuku aka momuzikumvwa Naakkoyo mucembele woongolede. = In this little book is where you will hear how the old woman Naakkoyo grew old. (1.-ongeledwe, 3.-ongozya, 4.-ongoleda, 5.-ongoledalyo, 6.-ongolesya, 7.-ongolede-ongolede)
grow old, Kaindi bantu bakali koongoleka mane kusikila lufwunanda Iwalitolela. = In the past people were growing old until finally they died a natural death at home.

cry out in loud voice, Wakoongolola kwiita mweenzinyina ajwi pati. He cried out, calling his friend with a loud voice. Kuli basicikombelo baongolola mumilundu. There are churchgoers who are crying out in the hills. (1.-ongololwa, 2.-ongolwede, 3.-ongolozya, 4.-ongolweda, 5.-ongolwedalyo, 6.-ongololesya, 7.-ongolola-ongolola, 8.-ongololana)
  • straighten, Koongolola cibulo cidiimene. = Straighten the crooked piece of metal. Tacikatazyi koongolola cibulo nocicipya. It is not difficult to straighten the metal when it is still hot.

become stooped, become crooked or bent, sit with head inclined, Musamu wakoongomana lyakali kubbubbula muwo. The tree bent when there was a strong wind. Also: -konkomana, -gogomana. (1.-ongomanwa, 2.-ongomenye, 3.-ongomanya, 4.-ongomanina, 5.-ongomaninalyo. 6.-ongomanisya, 7.-ongomana-ongomana, 8.-ongomaninana)
  • persist, Walo taakaleka, wakoongomana biyo kulya. He himself did not stop, he just persisted in eating.
  • go down, as sun, Izuba nilyakaongomana wakayeeya kuti apiluke kuya kumunzi. = When the sun was sinking he thought of returning to the village.

bend down what is protruding, Wamana kwaanga luwaile awo anketani, koloongomeka kutegwa lutacisi muntu. = When you finish tying the wire there to the chain, bend it so that it does not protrude and hurt someone. (1.-ongomekwa, 2.-ongomekede, 3.-ongomezya, 4.-ongomekela, 5.-ongomekelalyo, 6.-ongomekesya, 7.-ongomeka-ongomeka, 8.-ongomekana)
bend down, Twakajana munene uloongomene munsaa musamu akaambo kakukatala. We found the old man bending down beside a tree because he was tired. Also: -konkomene

straighten up from bending position, Munene wakaongomoka naakamvwa muntu wiita. The old man straightened up when he heard someone calling. (1.-ongomokwa, 2.-ongomokede, 3.-ongomozya, 4.-ongomokela, 5.-ongomokelalyo, 6.-ongomokesya, 7.-ongomoka-ongomoka, 8.-ongomokana) Also: -sintamuka.

bend neck, Wakoongoonga nsingo amutwe kayeeya cakucita ciguminizya kuzumina naa kukaka. = She bent her neck and head repeatedly trying to decide whether to agree or refuse. (1.-ongoongwa, 2.-ongoongede, 3.-ongoongezya, 4.-ongoongela, 5.-ongoongelalyo, 6.-ngoongesya, 7.-ongoonga-ongoonga, 8.-ongoongelana)
  • bend neck repeatedly as a sign of love, Musimbi wakoongoonga munsi aamusankwa wakwe. The girl bent her neck beside her boy friend repeatedly (as a sign of shyness and love.)

make live long, rt. -ongola, Bulozi mbujayi, luyando luloongozya. = Witchcraft is a killer, love makes one to live long. (1.-ongozyegwa, 2.-ongozyede, 3.-ongozya, 4.-ongozyela, 5.-ongozyelalyo, 6.-ongozyesya, 7.-ongozya-ongozya)
help one another to live long, Muntu aumwi kuli muntu ngwapedwe ngociya koongozyanya limwi. = For each person there is a person given so that they help one another to live on.

be enticed, succumb to temptation, Naakabona mali, wakoongwa akuzumina kujaya mwana. When he saw the money he gave in to the temptation and agreed to kill the child. Mwana musimbi wakaongwa mali manji aakajisi mudaala. The young girl submitted due to the vast amount of money which the old man had. (2.-ongede, 3.-ongezya, 4.-ongela, 5.-ongelalyo, 6.-ongesya, 7.-ongwaongwa, 8.-ongana)
  • be bent, Cibulo cakoongwa amusankwa uzyandamene. The iron was bent by the sturdy boy.

be released, Ndilinda buniini ndileye mucisaka ndiligwasye. Mweenzuma ndoononokwa lino atweende. Wait for me a little while so that I go aside into the bush and relieve myself. My friend I have been relieved, now let's go. (2.-ononokede, 3.-ononozya, 4.-ononokela, 5.-ononokelalyo, 6.-ononokesya, 7.-ononokwa-ononokwa, 8. -ononokana) Also: -ubulukwa.
