wander about, Uyaabupetuuka muzyoonde kuyandaula zipama zyakulya. = She is wandering about through the thickets looking for edible roots. (1.-petuukwa, 2.-petuukide, 3.-petuusya, 4.-petuukila, 5.-petuukilalyo, 6.-petuukisya, 7.-petuuka-petuuka, 8.-petuuzyanya Also: -penauka, -petauka.

be blown away, Ndabona kapepa kapeuluka mumuwo. = I saw a bit of paper being blown away in the air. (1.-peulukwa, 2.-peulukide, 3.-peulukizya, 4.-peulukila, 5.-peulukilalyo, 6.-peulukisya, 7.-peuluka-peuluka) Also: -peluluka
tilt, Mwana wakapeyamika kabiya. = The child is tilting the little pot. Also: -cengamika
lean over, or to one side, Syaambololo waumwa ntobolo wapezyama. = The kudu, which was shot by a gun, leaned over to one side. Also: -cengama, -peama, -pesyama.
rush behind, Bakapiccukila kunze kwakali kulila mangoma. = They rushed behind where the drums were beating.

be burnt, rt. -pya, Muntu ulakonzya kupida munanda kakunyina aumuyokola. = A person can be burnt in the house without anyone taking him out of the ashes. (1.-pidwa, 2.-pide, 3.-pidizya, 4.-pida, 5.-pidalyo, 6.-pisya, 7.-pida-pida, 8.-pidana)
be in a burnt state, rt. -pya, Kaanda kulubazu lumwi kakalipide. = The hut was burnt on one side.

spurt in a jet, squirt or spit water from mouth, Kocenjela nzoka ilakupiila mate mumeso. = Take care the snake will spit saliva into your eyes. (1.-piilwa, 2.-piilide, 3.-piizya, 4.-piilila, 5.-piililalyo, 6.-piilisya, 7.-piila-piila, 8.-piilana)
  • offer libation to ancestors, Mwana wakapona nibakakumba bukoko bwakupiila muzimo wabanyinakulu. = The child was cured when they brewed beer for the spirit of its grandmother. Munene mukungulu nguwakajula muswaangano kwiinda mukupiila mizimo yabafwu kumwi kaswida-swida meenda ngaakafwubete mukanwa. = The wise old man was the one who opened the meeting by honouring the spirits of the dead while spitting out water which he had held in his mouth. Also: -tilila muzimo.

spit water from mouth ritually, (custom by which father of girl ratifies marriage), Bakamupiilila kabaamba kuti, "Twakusowa kuli Ndaba." = He spat water from his mouth saying, "We have given you away to So-and-so." Naaka sungulwa Mutinta basyaanene bakwe mbabakamupiilila. = When Mutinta was released for marriage her grandfather is the one who ritually spat water from his mouth. Cacaala nkumupiilila biyo musimbi kutegwa mizimo imubone. = It remains just for the father to bless the girl so that the spirits approve of her marriage.

be ritually blessed for marriage, Mutinta wakapiililwa mwakali. = Mutinta was given away in marriage last year. (2.-piililwa, 3.-piilizyigwa, 4.-piilililwa, 5.-piilililwalyo, 6.-piililisyigwa, 7.-piililwa-piililwa)
be spat at, Chimuka wapiilwa nzoka masiku. = Chimuka was spat at by a snake at night. (2.-piilidwe, 3.-piilizyigwa, 4.-piililwa, 5.-piililwalyo, 6.-piilisyigwa, 7.-piilwa-piilwa)

turn up as edge of hat, Munene wali kupiinika zyeete njasama. = The old man was turning up his hat which he was wearing. (1.-piinikwa, 2.-piinikide, 4.-piinikila, 5.-piinikilalyo, 6.-piinikisya, 7.-piinika-piinika, 8.-piinikana) Also: -piinyika.

be turned up, as lips or hat, rt. piinyika, Mudaala usamide ngowani ipiinyene. = The old man wears a turned up hat. (1.-piinyikwa, 2.-piinyene, 3.-piinyika, 4.-piinyanina, 5.-piinyaninalyo, 6.-piinyanisya, 7.-piinyeye-piinyene)

turn up, pout, Uulya muntu wiipiinyika caali milomo yakwe. = That one is deliberately turning up his lips in disgust. (1.-piinyika, 2.-piinyikide, 3.-piinyika, 4.-piinyikila, 5.-piinyikilalyo, 6.-piinyikisya, 7.-piinyika-piinyika, 8.-piinyikana) Also: -piinika, -bbebbula mulomo.

produce fire by friction, Notwakacili bana twakali kukonzya kujana mulilo kwiinda mukupika kasamu acisamunyina. = When we were children we were able to produce fire by rubbing one stick against another. Wakayeeya misamu yakupika mbuli mutobolo a musekese. = He thought of the trees for making fire by friction such as the carrot tree and the musekese. (1.-pikwa, 2.-pikide, 3.-pisya, 4.-pikila, 5.-pikilalyo, 6.-pikisya, 7.-pikapika, 8.-pikana or -pikilana) Also: -sika
  • put as load on shoulder, Muvwimi wakapika masumo wakeenda kumunzi. = The hunter put his spears over his shoulder and went home.
  • be jailed, Muntu mubbi wakapika muntolongo kwamyaka yotatwe. = The thief was jailed for three years. Nkuta ilabatuma basankwa aba kuntolongo kuya kupika kwamyezi yotatwe. = The court sends these boys to prison to be jailed for three months. Wakaipika ntolongo yamyaka yone. = He was jailed for four years.
  • challenge, Kunyina ukonzya kwiipika kuli Mwiinga. = No one is able to challenge Mwiinga.

wag the tail, Mubwa wangu ulapika-pika mucila kuti wandibona. = My dog wags its tail when I arrive. Also: -mizamiza
  • kill an insect by rubbing it between the fingers, Njina njaakabweza mumutwe wakaipika-pika akwiijaya. The louse which he took from his head he squeezed and killed it.

rub into, Mubbi bakamupikila mbala mumeso nibakamujana kabinga nombe zyabantu. They rubbed the liquid of the mbala tree into the eyes of the thief when they found him driving other people's cattle. Kuti muntu watoogwa mbala, balamupikila mukupa wamunkolo. If a person is blinded by the liquid of the mbala tree, they rub the eyes with breast-milk.

try, struggle to do something, Kubweza cintu cilemu nkupikilisya buya alimwi nkutalekelezyanya. = To take up a difficult task is a matter of trying hard and not giving up in supporting one another. Bakali kupikilisya kumujata. = They were trying hard to catch him. (1.-pikilisyigwa, 2.-pikilisyide, 4.-pikilisyizya, 5.-pikilisyizyalyo 6.-pikilisyisya, 7.-pikilisya-pikilisya, 8.-pikilisyanya)

rub, Ndalipikisa nindatoogwa kauka muliso. = I rubbed my eyes when an insect got into my eyes. Kamupikisa musamu mumeso amwana. = Rub medicine into the child's eyes. (1.-pikisigwa, 2.-pikiside, 3.-pikisya, 4.-pikisila, 5.-pikisilalyo, 6.-pikisisya, 7.-pikisa-pikisa, 8.-pikisana) Also: -sikisa.
  • wag tail, Kabwa kakatalikide kale kupikisa-pikisa mucila. The dog had already begun to wag its tail.
bewitch one another, = Kamupikisana kutegwa tukabone naa nguni wazunda. Bewitch one another so that we see who wins. Also: -lowana.
bore a hole by friction, Kubamba mulilo nkupikisila atusamu twamupondo. To make fire is to bore a hole by friction with sticks from the mupondo tree.

counsel, advise, Nguni wakamupila maanu akuti asandule kaambo munkuta. = Who advised him to change the story in the court. (1.-pilwa, 2.-pilide, 3.-pilisya, 4.-pilila, 5.-pililalyo, 6.-pilisya, 7.-pila-pila, 8.-pilana) Also: -cenjezya, -syangila.

be overturned, Inzoka yakapilamuka noyakakosolwa mutwe. = The snake was turned upside down when it's head was cut off. (1.-pilamukwa, 2.-pilamukide, 3.-pilamusya, 4.-pilamukila, 5.-pilamukilalyo, 6.-pilamukisya, 7.-pilamuka-pilamuka, 8.-pilamusyanya)
struggle to overpower one another, Tandiyoowi musankwa, inga tulapilamusyanya. = I am not afraid of the man, we can contend with him.

move, Kopilaula liso ndibone mpokabede kakutowa. = Move your eye so that I see what is blocking it. Musune mubombe inga kopilaula. = You can move a trained ox easily. (1.-pilaulwa, 2.-pilaukide, 3.-pilausya, 4.-pilaulila, 5.-pilaulilalyo, 6.-pilaulisya, 7.-pilaula-pilaula, 8.-pilaulana)

cause to move, Nobakali kweembela mpongo, bana bakali kwiide kuzipilausya kubusena bomwe. = When the children were herding the goats, they were just moving them to one place. (1.-pilausyigwa, 2.-pilaisyide, 3.-pilausya, 4.-pilausyizya, 5.-pilausyizyalyo, 6.-pilausyisya, 7.-pilausya-pilausya, 8.-pilausyanya)

carry a load, Muka Moolo wakapilika zintu zyakwe zyoonse akupiluka kwabo. = The wife of Moolo carried all her possessions and returned to her home. (1.-pilikwa, 2.-pilikide, 3.-pilikizya, 4.-pilikila, 5.-pilikilalyo, 6.-pilikisya, 7.-pilika-pilika, 8.-pilikana)

be thrown about, as stones, Ilyakatalika lumamba, akapililika mabwe. = When the fight started, stones were thrown everywhere. Twakabona buyo mabwe nkwaapililika, bakali kwaafwusa bakali kunze acuulu. = We just saw where the stones were being thrown from, those who were throwing them were behind the ant-hill. (1.-pililikwa, 2.-pililikide, 3.-pililisya, 4.-pililikila, 5.-pililikilalyo, 6.-pililikisya, 7.-pililika-pililika, 8.-pililisyanya)

turn to and fro, Mutinta taoni kabotu abulo, wiide kupilimuka. = Mutinta doesn't sleep properly, she turns from left to right. Also: -sandauka, -bbutauka. (1.-pilimukwa, 2.-pilimukide, 3.-pilimusya, 4.-pilimukila, 5.-pilimukilalyo, 6.-pilimukisya, 7.-pilimuka-pilimuka, 8.-pilimukizyanya)

be agitated, Toonse twakapilingana notwakatambula lufwu Iwasibbuku wesu. = We were all agitated when we heard of the death of our headman. Mudaala watambaika, apilingana maboko mbubwena buteede banyama bakwe. = The old man raised his arms and moved them about just like the way his cattle did. (imitating the movement of the horns of a beast of which he is so proud) (1.-plinganwa, 2.-pilingenye, 3.-pilinganya, 4.-pilinganina, 5.-pilinganinalyo, 6.-pilinganisya, 7.-pilinganapilingana, 8.-pilinganyizyanya)
agitate, cause one to be worked up, Zintu zinji zyandipilinganina. = Many things have upset me.

cause confusion, rt. -pilingana, Kwandipilinganya kuciswa kwabaama. = The sickness of my mother upsets me. Kuti bantu nokunyina cibapilinganya, balakkala akuliiba. = If there is nothing which disturbs people, they live in freedom.

be in a confused state, be complicated, be twisted, rt. -pilingana, Mizeezo yakalipilingene mumutwe. = The thoughts were confused in the head. Nzila iiya koo Mutinta ilipilingene kapati. = The road to Mutinta's home is very twisted. Cisamu eeci cilipilingene, tucisiye. = This pole is very twisted, let's leave it.
  • be crippled, Mangobe wakali mulema, maulu akwe akalipilingene. = Mangobe was a cripple, his legs were crooked.
be in a twisted state, rt. pilingana, Meja asyaambololo alipilingenye. = The horns of a kudu are twisted.

return, turn back, Kapiluka buyo, uyakuunka juunza. = Let him just return, he can go tomorrow. (1.-pilukwa, 2.-pilukide, 3.-pilusya, 4.-pilukila, 5.-pilukilalyo, 6.-pilukisya, 7.-piluka-piluka, 8.-pilukana)

turn a thing back, Kamuzipilula nombe oko nkoziya. = Turn the cattle back from where they are going over there. (1.-pilulwa, 2.-pilwide, 3.-pilusya, 4.-pilwida, 5.-pilwidalyo, 6.-pilulisya, 7.-pilula-pilula, 8.-pilulana) Also: -pindula
  • translate, interpret, Muntu wakapilula kabbuku aaka mu Chikuwa, ulicizyi kapati. = The person who translated this book into English is an expert. Also: -sandulula.
cause to return, Musimbi ngwaakatizya Chimuka bakamupilusya jilo kumazuba. = They returned the girl yesterday afternoon with whom Chimuka eloped. Also: -josya, -boozya.

weigh, measure, examine, Kamupima tubone mbwalema ooyu. = Weigh him to see how heavy he is. Twakajana musilisi wamupima kale mulwazi. = We found that the doctor had already examined the patient. (1.-pimwa,2.-pimide, 3.-pimya, 4.-pimina, 5.-piminalyo, 6.-pimisya, 7.-pima-pima, 8.-pimana)

fold up, as a cloth, e.g Kobupimpa buluke butagumi mumeenda. = Tuck up the trousers so that they do not touch the water. Kopimpa buluke bulateta, meenda asikwa mumagondo. = Roll up the trousers they are wet, the water is knee-level. Koide biyo kupimpa hempe lyako, liswide mate mumaanza, ubweze piki tukasye mugodi. Just roll up your shirt, spit on your hands, take a pick so that we go and dig the well. (1.-pimpwa, 2.-pimpide, 3.-pimpya, 4.-pimpila, 5.-pimpilalyo, 6.-pimpisya, 7.-pimpa-pimpa, 8.-pimpana)

align in opposite directions, Basilisi bakabapimpanya bana bakalede abulo bomwe. The nurse laid the childen in opposite directions who were lying in the one bed. (1.-pimpanyizyigwa, 2.-pimpanyide, 3.-pimpanyizya, 4.-pimpanyizyizya, 5.-pimpanyizyizyalyo, 6.-pampanyizyisya, 7.-pimpanya-pimpanya, 8.-pimpanyizyanya) Also: -impanya.

be undone, as stitching, Ufwambaane kusuma buluke bwamwana nkaambo bwakapimpuluka. = Be quick to sew the trousers of the child because the stitching has been undone. Also: petuluka. (1.-pimpulukwa, 2.-pimpulukide, 3.-pimpulukizya, 4.-pimpulukila, 5.-pimpulukilalyo, 6.-pimpulukisya, 7.-pimpuluka-pimpuluka, 8.-pimpulukana)

unfold, Kopimpulula buluke ono nkaambo walanduka. = Unfold the trousers now as you have reached the other side. (1.-pimpululwa, 2.-pimpulwide, 3.-pimpuluzya, 4.-pimpulwida, 5.-pimpulwidalyo, 6.-pimpululisya, 7.-pimpulula-pimpulula, 8.-pimpululana)

overturn, Mootokala wakakunkulika ajeleele mbuli kuti ulapindamuka. = The vehicle was free-wheeling on the escarpment as if it would overturn. Bakali kwaambaula makani aajatikizya cisi mbucakapindamuka. = They were talking about matters concerning the country how it had been turned upside down. (1.-pindamukwa, 2.-pindamukide, 3.-pindamukizya, 4.-pindamukila, 5.-pindamukilalyo, 6.-pindamukisya, 7.-pindamuka-pindamuka, 8.-pindamukilana)

invert, twist, Kacila wakalijisi busongo bwakupindamuna twaambo kutegwa azwidilile nguwe lyoonse. Kachila had the cleverness of twisting statements so that they came out in his favour. (1.-pindamunwa, 2.-pindamwide, 3.-pindamuzya, 4.-pindamwida, 5.-pindamwidalyo, 6.-pindamunisya, 7.-pindamunapindamuna, 8.-pindamunana)

go from place to place in doing business, Ndipindauka kuuzya mabbusu. = I am going about from place to place selling shoes. (1.-pindaukwa, 2.-pindaukide, 3.-pindaukizya, 4.-pindaukila, 5.-pindaukilalyo, 6.-pindaukisya, 7.-pindauka-pindauka, 8.-pindaukilana)
  • become swollen and inverted, Bana nibakali kusobana ntuntulwa, musinza wayo wakanjila mumeso nkabela meso akapindauka. When the children were playing with the ntuntulwa fruit, the juice got in their eyes and the eyes became swollen and inverted.

exchange merchandise, Musambazi ulapindaula makwebo aakwe kutegwa ajane mpindu. = The trader is exchanging his wares to make profit. (1.-pindaulwa, 2.-pindawide, 3.-pindauzya, 4.-pindawida, 5.-pindawidalyo, 6.-pindaulisya, 7.-pindaulapindaula, 8.-pindaulana)
  • turn head backwards, Ooyu musune mmutolo, takweli ciindi cilamfwu, wiide kupindaula. This ox is lazy, it does not pull for a long time, it just turns its head back.

be reversed, Ndapinduka kale mebo, ndayeeya bumbi. = I have retracted, I have thought of another plan. (1.-pindukwa, 2.-pindukide, 3.-pindukizya, 4.-pindukila, 5.-pindukilalyo, 6.-pindukisya, 7.-pinduka-pinduka, 8.-pindukilana)
  • swell out, Mulomo wakapinduka naakalumwa maanko. The lip became swoolen when he was bitten by hornets.

twist someone's arm (behind back), *Ndamupindula kwaanza kutegwa andipe mali.* = I have twisted his arm so that he gives me money. *Moonde naakaangwa basilikani bakamupindula maboko akumwaanga nsimbi.* When Moonde was arrested the police twisted his arms behind his back and handcuffed him. (1.-pindulwa, 2.-pindwide, 3.-pinduzya, 4.-pindwida, 5.-pindwidalyo, 6.-pindulisya. 7.-pindula-pindula, 8.-pindulana)
  • turn round, turn a thing back, reverse, *Basune bapindula mumuunda.* = The oxen reversed in the field. *Mweelede kukwelela antoomwe kakubula aupindula pe.* You ought to pull together without one reversing. Also: -*fwutula*.
  • make from, *Misamu yesu ipindulwa buya kuzwa kumatu a miyanda yazisamu.* = Our medicines are made from leaves and the roots of trees. (make gunpowder, pindula musili)

exchange continually, *Uleelede kupinduula zintu zinji mumakwebo.* = You are supposed to always exchange different goods in the market. (1.-pinduulwa, 2.-pindwiide, 3.-pinduu-zya, 4.-pindwiida, 5.-pidwiidalyo, 6.-pinduulisya, 7.-pinduula-pinduula, 8.-pinduulana) Also: -*pindaula*.
  • turn inside out, as a bag, *Kolipinduula saka akulivwukumuna kazwe kasuko.* = Continue to turn the bag inside out and shake out the dust.

bolt as a door, *Kamupinga zisamu ziyumu amulyango wacaanda campongo kutegwa zitazwi.* = Bolt the door of the goats house with strong sticks so that they don't come out. (1.-pingwa, 2.-pingide, 3.-pingizya, 4.-pingila, 5.-pingilalyo, 6.-pingisya, 7.-pinga-pinga, 8.-pingilana) Also: -*inga*.
  • strike something flying in the air, *Ndakaipinga nziba kayuuluka mujulu ankoli kumane ndayuuma yawa ansi.* = I threw a stick at a flying dove and struck it and it fell to the ground.
be bolted as a door, rt. - *pinga*, *Kumulyango bakajana kuli bukwazi, kakuli nibakoona bakalipingide.* = They found the door open, although when they went asleep it was bolted.

tie hands behind back, *Bakamupingula maboko kunze ciindi naakaangwa.* = They twisted his arms behind his back when he was arrested. Also: -*pindula*. (1.-pingulwa, 2.-pingwide, 3.-pinguzya, 4.-pingwida, 5.-pingwidalyo, 6.-pingulisya, 7.-pingula-pingula, 8.-pingulana)
  • treat severely, *Mukaintu utalomenye upingula bamucaala mbuli mbwayanda.* = A rough woman treats orphans cruelly. Also: -*tundulula*.
  • impose a fine, *Kumulandu wakumisya, inkuta ipingula nombe yomwe.* = For the offence of making a girl pregnant the court imposes a fine of one cow.

be turned in a different direction, *Mvwula yapinguluka kuya kujwe.* = The rain has turned away going eastwards. (1.-pingulukwa, 2.-pingulukide, 3.-pingulusya, 4.-pingulukila, 5.-pingulukilalyo, 6.-pingulukisya, 7.-pinguluka-pinguluka, 8.-pingulukana)

turn in a different direction, *Nkubotu awalo asozye kukapingulula kaambo kwiinda kunikuumwine buyo.* = It would be good if she also tried to turn the conversation in a different direction rather than just to remain silent.

take a different way, *Joojo wakapinya akugama kambi kazila naakabona bamakwaakwe.* = Joojo took a different path when he saw his in-laws approaching. (1.-pinyizyigwa, 2.-pinyide. 3.-pinyizya, 4.-pinyina, 5.-pinyinalyo,

7.-pinya-pinya) Also: -leya.
  • emit wind from anus, Bana bakapinya munanda mwaali bapati. = The children farted in the house where there were elders. Also: -sula.

be busily occupied, Twana twankuku twakali kupipilika kulinununa. The chicks were busily occupied in saving themselves. Munene oyu napipilika boobu ani kuti cimwi cigwebenga cakalimubwene kale. = When this old man was so caught up in what he was doing, a certain thief had already seen him.

try to do something, Chilala wakajisi bubi kupipilisya kujika cilalilo. Chilala was busy cooking the evening meal. Mucembele wakali kupipilisya kutebba nkuni. = The old woman was trying to gather firewood.

be spirally twisted, Cilakatazya kweenzya moota mukazila kapipingene. = It is difficult to drive a car on a twisted road. (1.-pipinyanizyigwa, 2.-pipingene, 3.-pipinganya, 4.-pipinganyizyizya, 5.-pipinganyizyizyalyo, 6.-pipingansyisya, 7.-pipingene-pipingene) Also: -pitingana.

show facial expression of revulsion, Mucembele wapipinyana kumeso naanywa musamu ulula. = The old woman screwed up her face when she drank the bitter medicine. (1.-pipinyanizyigwa, 2.-pipinyene, 3.-pipinyanizya, 4.-pipinyanina, 5.-pipinyaninalyo, 6.-pipinyanisya, 7.-pipinyana-pipinyana, 8.-pipinyanizyanya) Also: -bbebbenyana, -memenyana.
twist slightly, as a person's neck, Bamasilikani bakamupipinyuna maboko mubbi bamane bamwaanga nsimbi. The police twisted the arms of the thief and then handcuffed him.

suffer stomach pains, Ndakaalilwa koona kabotu nkaambo mwida mwakali kupisa kapati. I failed to sleep well because my stomach was twisting a lot. Tiindafwuma kulya, nzala yandipisa. I did not eat early, the hunger is twisting my stomach. (1.-piswa, 2.-piside, 3.-pisya, 4.-pisila, 5.-pisilalyo, 6.-pisisya, 7.-pisa-pisa) Also: -myonga.
  • twist, Mubetesi wakapisa malezu akwe alya akapaanyene mumbali amulomo. The judge twisted his handle-bar shaped moustache.

struggle to do a hard job, Twalikupisya mulimo wakatwaalide jilo. = We were struggling with the work which we failed to do yesterday. (1.-pisyigwa, 2.-pisyide, 3.-pisyizya, 4.-pisyila, 5.-pisyilalyo, 6.-pisyisya, 7.-pisya-pisya, 8.-pisyanya)
  • be very hot, rt. -pya, Mulilo wacipisya cakulya kapati. The fire made the food very hot indeed. Nsekonzyi kwaasamba meenda apisya. = I cannot wash in this very hot water.
  • produce a fire by means of, rt. -pika, Nitwakali kweembela mpongo musyokwe, twakali kupisya kasamu kasyoonto kucisamu cipati. = When we were herding goats in the bush we were using a small stick to rub it against a bigger one to produce fire.

supervise, (ety. Chilapa-lapa, kapitau), Kapitau upitaula babelesi mumugwagwa. The foreman supervises the workers on the road. (1.-pitaulwa, 2.-pitawide, 3.-pitauzya, 4.-pitawida, 5.-pitawidalyo, 6.-pitaulisya, 7.-pitaula-pitaula, 8.-pitaulana)

become twisted, Haambololo nacili mwana inga meja taapitingene, pesi akomena alapitingana. = When the kudu is young the horns are not twisted, but when it grows it becomes twisted. (1.-pitinganwa, 2.-pitingene, 3.-pitinganya, 4.-pitinganina, 5.-pitinganinalyo, 6.-pitinganisya, 7.-pitinganapitingana, 8.-pitinganinana) Also: -pilingana
be in a spirally twisted form, Meja a syaambololo alipitingene. The horns of the kudu are spirally twisted.

agitate, Koleka kupitinganya basicikolo, balabamba manyongwe. = Stop agitating the pupils, they will cause a riot. Also: -pilingenye, -pipingene, -pilinganya.
  • twist the truth, Bamwi bantu balayanda kupitinganya zintu ziluzi. = Some people wish to distort things which are true.

mwida turn in the womb, Mukaintu wangu nibakaanzyanya abaneene, mwana uli mwida wakapituka. = When my wife greeted her grandmother, the child in the womb turned. (as a sign of happiness) (1.-pitukwa, 2.-pitukide, 3.-pitusya, 4.-pitukila, 5.-pitukilalyo, 6.-pitukisya, 7.-pituka-pituka) Also: -samba.

maulu bend the legs, Bayi bakaambila bana kuti nkupiyana maulu banoosobana. The teacher told the children to bend their legs when they were playing. (1.-piyanwa, 2.-piyanide, 3.-piyanya, 4.-piyanina, 5.-piyaninalyo, 6.-piyanisya, 7.-piyana-piyana)

dislocate a limb, Kuboko kwamwana kwapizuka naawa. The arm of the child was dislocated when he fell. (1.-pizukwa, 2.-pizukide, 3.-pizusya, 4.-pizukila, 5.-pizukilalyo, 6.-pizukisya, 7.-pizuka-pizuka, 8.-pizukana)
  • become inverted, Liso lyangu lyapizuka nindalumwa maanko. = My eyelid became inverted when I was stung by hornets. Also: -pinduka.

rebel, Ooyu mwana walipoba nkaambo tatobeli malailile abapati bakwe. This child rebels because it does not follow the advice of its elders. Also: -zanga. (1.-pobwa, -2.-pobede, 3.-pobya, 4.-pobela, 5.-pobelalyo, 6.-pobesya, 7.-poba-poba, 8.-pobezyanya)
  • do something unsuitable, Oyu musankwa wakalipoba kuyanda bacembele bapati kule-kule. This boy fell in love with an old woman who is far beyond his age.
  • penetrate, Twalikupoba musyokwe lilamfwu kuyandaula nombe, pesi tiitwazijana. We were penetrating into thick bush searching for the cattle, but we did not find them.

be crooked, Bacembele aaba bakapobana meebo nkaambo menyo akamana. This old woman's jaw is crooked because her teeth are finished. (1.-pobanwa, 2.-pobanide, 3.-pobanya, 4.-pobanina, 5.-pobaninalyo, 6.-pobanisya, 7.-pobana-pobana, 8.-pobanizyanya) Also: -bbobana,-poonkana
  • move about in long grass, Basicikolo bakali kwiide kupobana mubwizu bulamfwu. = The pupils were moving about in the long grass.

be shattered, Wakapoboka mumutwe naakaumwa nkoli. = His head was shattered when he was beaten with a club. (1.-pobokwa, 2.-pobokede, 3.-pobozya, 4.-pobokanina, 5.-pobokaninalyo, 6.-pobokesya, 7.-poboka-poboka)

shatter, as a bottle, Naanyema wacipobola cinkuli camabisi. = When he was annoyed he smashed the calabash of sour milk. (1.-pobolwa, 2.-pobwede, 3.-pobozya, 4.-pobweda, 5.-pobwedalyo, 6.-pobolesya, 7.-pobola-pobola, 8.-pobolana) Also: -pwaya, -pwacula.
  • feast for a whole day or longer, Bakapobola naakasika Dingani kuzwa kuntolongo. = They celebrated when Dingani got out of prison. *Twakapobola* naakaula moota Joni. = We celebrated when John bought a car.

feast for somebody, rt. pobola, Cakali kunoneenzya ciindi nobakamupobweda. = It was nice when they celebrated for him. Bakamutola kumunzi kukumupobweda. = They took him to the village to make a feast for him. Bantu *bapobweda* moota wa Joni. = The people celebrated for the car of John.

give a fowl to a visitor, Sena *wakamupobwela* mweenzu wako. = Did you offer a chicken to your visitor. (1.-pobwelwa, 2.-pobwele, 3.-pobozya, 4.-pobwela, 5.-pobwelalyo, 6.-pobwelesya, 7.-pobwela-pobwela, 8.-pobwelana)
make a small hole, Kamu

cilayi tubikke nkanka. = Make a hole in the sledge so that we insert a peg. Bana balayandisya *kupokola* ansi azisamu. = Children like to make small holes in the ground with sticks. (1.-pokolwa, 2.-pokwede, 3.-pokozya, 4.-pokweda, 5.-pokwedalyo, 6.-pokolesya, 7.-pokola-pokola, 8.-pokolana) Also: -pakula.

sit, Kaceta kalayandisya *kupokomana* atalaa musamu. = A monkey likes to sit on top of a tree. (1.-pokomanwa, 2.-pokomene, 3.-pokomanya, 4.-pokomanina, 5.-pokomaninalyo, 6.-pokomanisya, 7.-pokomana-pokomana, 8.-pokomaninana)
  • be morose or downcast, Mubbi naakali kubetekwa munkuta wakaile ku
kaambo nikakamulya. = When the thief was been tried in court he was just downcast when the verdict went against him. Also: -ungumana
be perched, Ndabona moomba *ulipokomene* mumusamu mulamfwu. = I saw a turkey buzzard perched on top of a big tree.
search as in pocket, Kamupokomona mali nkwaali munkomo zyanu. = Search around for the money which is in your pockets. Bakatalika ku

mali mucisinsi ncibakasamide. = She started to fumble for money in the dress she was wearing. (1.-pokomonwa, 2.-pokomwede, 3.-pokomozya, 4.-pokomweda, 5.-pokomwedalyo, 6.-pokomonesya, 7.-pokomona-pokomona, 8.-pokomonana)

poke, Kulipokonyona mumeno akasamu kacibulo nkubi. = To poke your teeth with a metal stick is bad. (1.-pokonyonwa, 2.-pokonywede, 3.-pokonyozya, 4.-pokonyonena, 5.-pokonyonenalyo, 6.-pokonyonesya, 7.-pokonyona-pokonyona, 8.-pokonyonana)
continue to make a small hole, as with a stick Musankwa wakamwaambauzya musimbi. Musimbi waka

ansi akezu kumwi kavwuwa. = The boy was proposing to the girl. The girl was occupied making a hole with a blade of grass while answering. Imvwula ilawa simpongo *napokoola* miyanda yabbonga. = It is when the rain falls that the goat herd makes small holes for the roots of the bbonga plants. (1.-pokoolwa, 2.-pokweede, 3.-pokoozya, 4.-pokweeda, 5.-pokweedalyo, 6.-pokoolesya, 7.-pokoola-pokoola, 8.-pokoolana)

shift residence, Bakapola kuzwa ku Nabooye kuya ku Nabukuyu. = They moved from Nabooye going to Nabukuyu. Matimba wakali kukkala ku Nadezwe, ino *wakapola* uli kwa Ndema. = Matimba was living at Nadezwe, but has now moved, she is at Ndema. (1.-polwa, 2.-polede, 3.-pozya, 4.-polela, 5.-polelalyo, 6.-polesya, 7.-pola-pola, 8.-pozyanya) Also: -longa, -sukuluka.
  • break open, Masiku ŋombe zyacipola ciba nkaambo tiizyakakkuta jilo. = At night the cattle broke open the kraal because they did not eat to satisfaction yesterday. Also: -polaula.

break through, rt. -pola, ŋombe ziile kupolaula mumambewu aabantu. Cattle are just breaking into people's gardens. (1.-polaolwa, 2.-polaolede, 3.-polaozya, 4.-polawida, 5.-polawidalyo, 6.-polaolisya, 7.-polaola-polaola, 8.-polaolana)

go through, rt. -pola, Nindali kudonkola mwiini wakeembe, kabulo kapya kapolela ambi. = When I was piercing the handle of an axe, the hot iron went through to the other side.
  • shift residence to, rt. -pola, Batonga mbantu balupola-pola. Balafwaambaana kupolela kooko kuli macezezyo mabotu. = The Tonga are a people who shift residence frequently. They are quick to move over there where there are good grazing areas.
  • at sunrise Wakaakusika ku Chiyobola alya mpolipolela zuba. = He reached Chiyobola at sunrise.

penetrate, Muvwimi naakayasa syuumbwa, isumo lyakapolelela. = When the hunter pierced the lion, the spear penetrated. (1.-polelelwa, 2.-polelede, 3.-polelezya, 4.-polelela, 5.-polelelalyo, 6.-polelesya, 7.-polelela-polelela, 8.-polelelana)

be opened up, Idamu lyakapolola, lyakoola minzi yobilo. = The dam which broke open, destroyed two villages. (1.-pololwa, 2.-polwede, 3.-polozya, 4.-polweda, 5.-polwedalyo, 6.-pololesya, 7.-polola-polola, 8.-polwedana) Also: -bbukilila
  • overflow, Meenda akapolola kunkomwe yalwaanje akaambo kamvwula yakavwulisya. = The water overflowed the banks of the lake because the rain was so much.
open up, Ndakapolweda meenda kuti anjile mumubundu wacisyu. = I opened up the water so that it would enter into a row of vegetables. Also: -pawida, -tulwida.

rustle, Bacembele bakamvwa cipolyaanya kubutala. = The old woman heard something rustling in the maize-bin. (1.-polyaanyizigwa, 2.-polyaanyide 3.-polyaanyizya, 4.-polyaanyizyizya, 5.-polyaanyizyizyalyo, 6.-polyaanyizyisya, 7.-polyaanya-polyaanya, 8.-polyaanyizyanya) Also: -sokonya.

rob one continually, Bantu bapombola kubba kwa Timooti. = People continue robbing at Timothy's place. (1.-pombolwa, 2.-pombwede, 3.-pombozya, 4.-pombweda, 5.-pombwedalyo, 6.-pombolesya, 7.-pombola-pombola, 8.-pombolana)
  • do whatever you want, Aba bana bapombola akaambo kakutapegwa cisubulo mazubaano. These children do whatever they want because they are not punished nowadays. Also: -pakala, -twanga, -bbombola.

change bad behaviour, Chaazu wakapomboloka, sunu wakaleka kubba. Chaazu has reformed, today he has stopped robbing. (1.-pombolokwa, 2.-pombolokede, 3.-pombolozya, 4.-pombolokela, 5.-pombolokelalyo, 6.-pombolokesya, 7.-pomboloka-pomboloka, 8.-pombolosyanya) Also: -bomboloka.

cry out in anguish, Banyina mwana ulya wakafwa bakapomoka kulila mumona munkuta nibakateelela makani aya. The mother of that child who had died, cried out in anguish there in the court when she heard that information. (1.-pomokwa, 2.-pomokede, 3.-pomozya, 4.-pomokela, 5.-pomokelalyo, 6.-pomokesya, 7.-pomoka-pomoka, 8.-pomokana)

accuse, Naanga ceelo cangu tacimuleki limwi nimwaakwiide kulipomokela nobeni nyolikke kuti ntuswe twakamujaya. = For certain my spirit will not leave you until you yourselves alone admit that it was we who killed him.

bring out water, Kopompa kutegwa meenda azwe. = Pump so that water comes out. Also: -sauka (1.-pompwa, 2.-pombede, 3.-pompya, 4.-pompela, 5.-pompelalyo, 6.-pompesya, 7.-pompa-pompa, 8.-pompana)
  • appear on scene, Wakapompa munene katuciliko. The old man came forth when we were still there. Tiikakaba kaindi ulaa cindongwe wakapompa akujaya basokwe boonse. In a short time the owner of the groundnut plot appeared and killed all the monkeys. Also: -bbuka
  • rise as the sun, Muntu oyu wasika lyapompa zuba. When the sun had risen that is when this person arrived. Also: -polela
  • pump, (ety. Eng.) Niwakaceya muya muvwili lyamootokala, basibbola bakaseluka akutalika kupompa muya kutegwa beende kabotu. = When there was insufficient pressure in the tyre, the footballers dismounted and began to pump air so that they would travel well.
take by surprise, appear suddenly, as a lion, Watupompela syuumbwa mucisaka. A lion suddenly appeared before us in the woods. (1.-pompelwa, 2.-pompelede)

cause anger to subside, Wakabupompolola bukali bwabo. = He cooled down their anger. (1.-pompololwa, 2.-pompolwede, V - 436 3.-pompolozya, 4.-pompolweda, 5.-pompolwedalyo, 6.-pompololesya, 7.-pompolola-pompolola, 8.-pompololana)
  • take air out of tyre, Babbi bakapompolola ncinga yokwa Busiku. = Thieves took out the air from Busiku's bicycle.
be deflated, Naakaamvwa makani aaya, wakapompoloka. = When he heard this news, he was deflated.

sound as water running over rapids, Meenda alapompoma ampoompo yamabwe mumulonga. = The water flows and rumbles over the rapids in the river. (1.-pompomwa, 2.-pompomede, 3.-pompomya, 4.-pompomena, 5.-pompomenalyo, 6.-pompomesya, pompoma-pompoma) Also: -bbobboma.

sit as tired or hungry, Ulapompomana kukkala mbuli kuti wakatala. = You sit worn out as if you are tired. (1.-pompomanwa, 2.-pompomene, 3.-pompomanya, 4.-pompomanina, 5.-pompomaninalyo, 6.-pompomanisya, 7.-pompomana-pompomana, 8.-pompomaninana)
be in a weary state, Twakajana mudaala ulipompomene amupando. = We found an old man sitting wearily on a chair.
sitting disappointedly without words, Bakacaala buyo fweee, bapompoloka akupompoloka. = They remained devastated, sitting without words to say.

smash, break up into pieces, Basinkolola bapompoola mutwe wanjombe. The people at the initiation ceremony smashed the head of a cow into pieces. (1.-pompoolwa, 2.-pompoolede/-pompweede, 3.-pompoozya, 4.-pompoolela, /-pompweeda, 5.-poompolelalyo/
6.-pompoolesya, 7.-pompoola-pompoola, 8.-pompoolana) Also: -sabaula, -kankaula.

live, be well, Mwana angu wakali kuciswa, wakapona sunu. = My child who was sick is well today. (1.-ponwa, 2.-ponede, 3.-ponya, 4.-ponena, 5.-ponenalyo, 6.-ponesya, 7.-pona-pona, 8.-ponezyanya)
  • recover health, Sunu mbasyoonto bantu bapona bulwazi bwakusoomona. = Today there are few people who recover from diarrhoea.

open eyes forcibly, Mainza wapondomona meso kulanga. = Mainza forcibly opened her eyes to look. (1.-pondomonwa, 2.-pondomwede, 3.-pondomozya, 4.-pondomweda, 5.-pondomwedalyo, 6.-pondomonesya, 7.-pondomona-pondomona, 8.-pondomonana)

dance continually, Basankwa baku Zambezi balapondooka muciindi cadilwe. = The Zambezi men dance continually during a funeral ritual. Also: -zemba (1.-pondookezyegwa, 2.-pondookede, 3.-pondookezya, 4.-pondookela, 5.-pondo-okelalyo, 6.-pondookesya, 7.-pondoola-pondoola, 8.-pondoolana)
  • be inverted, Cikoye cakwe caka-pondooka naakatoogwa mbala. = His eyelids were turned outwards when he was blinded by the mbala sap.
  • be smashed, Ndacijaya cibiya, capondooka. = I broke the pot, it was smashed. Also: pwayika, -syondooka.

crush by repeated blows, crumple, Mutwe wagombe bakau-pondoola amwiini wapiki. = They smashed the head of the cow open with many blows with a pick-handle. (1.-pondoolwa, 2.-pondoolede, /-pondweede, 3.-pondoo-zya, 4.-poondoolela/-pondweeda, 5.-pon-doolelalyo/-pondweedalyo, 6.-pondoolesya 7.-pondoola-pondoola, 8.-pondoolana) Also: -syondoola,-syondoonda, -pondoonda.

crush, e.g Muzovwu wakaipondoonda nondo njaakali munzila. = The elephant crushed the tortoise which was on the path. (1.-pondoondwa, 2.-pondoondede, /-pondweede, 3.-pondoozya, 4.-pondoondela. /-pondweeda, 5.-pondoondelalyo, /-pondweedalyo, 6.-pondoolesya, 7.-pondoonda-pondoonda, 8.-pondoondana) Also: -syondoonda.

fiddle with something, Bana balayanda lyoonse kupono-ngozya kantu kamwi. = Children always want to play around with something. (1.-ponongozyegwa, 2.-ponongozyede, 3.-ponongozya, 4.-ponongozyezya, 5.-ponongozyezyalyo, 6.-ponongozyesya, 7.-ponongozya-ponongozya, 8.-ponongozyanya) Also: -puta.

walk aimlessly or blindly, Twajana umwi musankwa usondo-kede ulapontyaila musyokwe. = We found a mad boy wandering about the bush. (1.-pontyailwa, 2.-pontyailide, 3.-pontya-izya, 4.-pontyailila, 5.-pontyaililalyo, 6.-pontyailisya, 7.-pontyaila,-pontyaila, 8.-pontyailizyanya) Also: -impita, -ingaila.

heal, rt. -pona, Bananga tabacikonzyi kuponya bantu baciswa sikalileke. Witchdoctors cannot heal people who are suffering from AIDS. (1.-ponwa, 2.-ponede, 3.-ponya, 4.-ponena, 5.-ponenalyo, 6.-ponesya, 7.-ponya-ponya, 8.-ponezyanya) Also: -silika, -sengula.

crush with fingers, Tulaponyauna mapiilusi notuyanda kusili-sya mwana. We crush the tablets with the fingers when we want to heal a child. (1.-ponyaunwa, 2.-ponyawide, 3.-ponyauzya, 4.-ponyawida, 5.-ponyawidalyo, 6.-ponyaunisya, 7.-ponyauna-ponyauna, 8.-ponyaunana) Also: -pwaya-pwaya, -syondoonda.

crush as between hands, Koponyonga ndongwe kutegwa makwa azwe. Crush the groundnuts so that the skins come off. Also: -puka-puka (1.-ponyongwa, 2.-ponyongede, 3.-ponyongezya, 4.-ponyongela, 5.-ponyongelalyo, 6.-ponyongesya, 7.-ponyonga-ponyonga, 8.-ponyongana) Also: -ponyauna.

search for lice, Bamacembele bayanda kuponyongola njina muzisani. Old women like to search for lice in clothes. (1.-ponyongolwa, 2.-ponyongwede, 3.-ponyongozya, 4.-ponyongweda, 5.-ponyongwedalyo, 6.ponyongolesya, 7.-ponyongola-ponyongola, 8.-ponyongolana) Also: -salangunya.
  • search for seeds as maize-cobs grow, Bana balayandisya kuponyongola mapopwe kutegwa babone nseke. Children like to search the maize-cobs to see if they have seeds.

be worn away as metal or clothes, Ceembe cakaponyooka, tacigonki. The old axe is worn away, it does not cut. Keembe aaka kayaabuponyooka aniini-niini akaambo kakutakabelesya kabotu. This axe is gradually wearing out because it is used carelessly. Also: -sinauka

be suddenly aroused, Moonze naakamvwa kuti bausyi balimbwa mootokala, wakaponzomoka kulila. When Moonze heard that his father has been run over by a car, he burst out crying. (1.-ponzomokwa, 2.-ponzomokede, 3.-ponzomokezya, 4.-ponzomokela, 5.-ponzomokelalyo, 6.-ponzomokesya 7.-ponzomoka-ponzomoka, 8.-ponzomokana) Also: -ontomoka.

ooze out, as yeast fizzing out of a bottle, Cuute cakapooka nicakatyankwa. The abcess oozed out when it was squeezed. (1.-pookwa, 2.-pookede, 3.-poosya, 4.-pookela, 5.-pookelalyo, 6.-pookesya, 7.-pooka-pooka, 8.-pookezyanya)

abate, go down, as a swelling, Kuulu kwamubwa kwapooloka. The swelling in the dog's leg has gone down. (1.-poolokezyegwa, 2.-poolokede, 3.-poolosya, 4.-poolokela, 5.-poolokelalyo, 6.-poolokesya, 7.-pooloka-pooloka, 8.-poolosyanya) Also: -zimbuluka

gush out, Mukupa wapoomoka kuzwa mukagumbuli nibakasulamika. The milk gushed out of the container when they leaned it to one side. Meenda apoomoka kuzwa mupompi. The water gushed out of the pump. (1.-poomokwa, 2.-poomokede, 3.-poomozya, 4.-poomokela, 5.-poomokelalyo, 6.-poomokesya, 7.-poomoka-poomoka, 8.-poomokelana) Also: -dukumuka, -dudumuka

make gush out, Mboomana kusunsumana-sunsumana "pooo" nkupoomona, nkukuna meenda, casanzigwa casalala, kunyina kununka pe. When you have finished sitting (on the toilet) you make the water gush out, the water pours out and it is clean and bright, there is no smell. (1.-poomonwa, 2.-poomwede, 3.-poomozya, 4.-poomweda, 5.-poomwedalyo, 6.-poomo-nesya, 7.-poomona-poomona, 8.-poomwedana)

be out of shape, Cibulo cameenda capoonkana nicaloka kuzwa a mutwe. The bucket of water was put out of shape when it fell from the head. (1.-poonkanwa, 2.-poonkene, 3.-poonkanya, 4.-poonkanina, 5.-poonkaninalyo, 6.-poonkanisya, 7.-poonkana-poonkana, 8.-poonkanizyanya) Also: -pobana, -bbobbana, bbobana.

crush out of shape, Ciindi canzala basambazi bamapopwe balazipoonkanya zigabba kutegwa bajane mali manji. During a time of hunger the traders depress the tins to make extra money. Cisamu cakamulimba cakuti cakapoonkanya mutwe wakwe. = The tree fell on him so that it crushed his head. (1.-poonkanyizyigwa, 2.-poonkenye, 3.-poo-nkanya, 4.-poonkanyizyizya, 5.-poonkanyizyizyalyo, 6.-poonkanyizyisya, 7.-poonkanya-poonkanya, 8.-poonkanyizyanya) Also: -bbobya, -bbonana.

yoke oxen, Kamupopa basune tukalime. = Yoke the oxen so that we plough. (1.-popwa, 2.-popede, 3.-popya, 4.-popela, 5.-popelalyo, 6.-popesya, 7.-popa-popa, 8.-popana) Also: -sunga, -vwoleka.
  • bind up, Kamupopa misunta yabwizu kutegwa ibwezegwe kabotu. = Bind up the bundles of grass so that they can be carried easily.

yoke oxen for, Ndipopela basimbi kuti baye kucigayo ino. = I have yoked up the oxen for the girls so that they go to the mill. (1.-popelwa, 2.-popedwe, 3.-popezyegwa, 4.-popeledwa, 5.-popeledwalyo, 6.-popesya, 7.-popela popela,8.-popelana)

unyoke, Kamupopolola basune aabo nkaambo bakatala. Unyoke those oxen because they are tired. (1.-popololwa, 2.-popolwede, 3.-popolozya, 4.-popolweda, 5.-popolwedalyo, 6.-popololesya, 7.-popolola-popolola, 8.-popololana) Also: -kkulula.

flow along quickly, Meenda apopoma mumulonga niyawa mvwula. Water flowed down the river quickly when the rain fell. (1.-popomwa, 2.-popomede, 3.-popomya, 4.-popomena, 5.-popomenalyo 6.-popomesya, 7.-popoma-popoma, 8.-popomezyanya) Also: -bbobboma

ask insistantly, Mwiinga wakali kupoposya kuti ajane mali kumudaala. Mwiinga was insistent in asking for money from the old man. (1.-poposyegwa, 2.-poposyede, 3.-poposya, 4.-poposyezya, 5.-poposyezyalyo, 6.-popozyesya, 7.-poposya-poposya, 8.-poposyanya) Also: -kombelezya, -sombelezya.

talk incessantly, Mudaala wali kupopota buzuba boonse. = The old man was talking unceasingly all day. (1.-popotwa, 2.-popotede, 3.-popotya, 4.-popotela, 5.-popotelalyo, 6.-popotesya, 7.-popota-popota, 8.-popotelana) Also: -topota.

cast a charm on someone, Naposela muntu swe, inga wafwa Iwakwe. If someone tries to cast a charm on us, he will die himself instead. Bamuposela musamu. = They bewitched him with a charm. Wakaposela zyeelo zyaba Kasai kuli Mainza kuti bazikumulye kumusana. He sent spirits of Kasai to Mainza to eat him in the back. (1.-poselwa, 2.-posede, 3.-posezya, 4.-poselela, 5.-poselelalyo, 6.-poselesya, 7.-posela-posela, 8.-poselana)

burst, as an abcess, Cuute camwana caposoka masina. = The abcess of the child discharged pus. (1.-posokezyegwa, 2.-posokede, 3.-pososya, 4.-posokela, 5.-posokelalyo, 6.-posokesya, 7.-posoka-posoka, 8.-posokana) Also: -posyoka.

burst as an abcess, Nindakkala acuuno cambwalakasa caposyoka cuute cila atako lyangu. = When I sat on the traditional stool the abcess on my buttock burst. (1.-posyokezyegwa, 2.-posyokede, 3.-posyosya, 4.-posyokela 5.-posyokelalyo, 6.-posyokesya, 7.-posyoka-posyoka, 8.-posyokelana) Also: -posoka.

travel aimlessly, Ooyu mwana ulaciyanda kupota mumaanda abantu. This child likes to move around people's houses without a purpose. Muntu utakwete takkali arjanda, wiide kupota. = A man who is not married does not stay at home, he wanders around. Basankwa aba bobile tabalimi mainza, baile kupota musyokwe kuyandaula basulwe. = During the rains these two boys do not plough, they just wander about the bush looking for rabbits. (1.-potwa, 2.-potede, 3.-potya, 4.-potela, 5.-potelalyo, 6.-potesya, 7.-pota-pota, 8.-potelana)

be entangled, be confused, Mizeezo ilapotana mumutwe wako webo ncolibonya boobo. = Your thoughts are mixed up, that is why you look like that. Bantu bakaile kupotana lyakasika kaambo kalufwu lokwa Kasyimbi. = The people were just confused when the news arrived of the death of Kasyimbi. (1.-potanwa, 2.-potene, 3.-potanya, 4.-potanina, 5.-potaninalyo, 6.-potanisya, 7.-potana-potana, 8.-potanizyanya)
cause to be tangled, confused, Wandipotanya akaambo kakutakanana kabotu. You have confused me because you do not speak properly. Sincinko waabapotanya bantu. = The mad one disturbed the people.
be in a confused state, Sena bongo bwakwe bulipotene? = Is his brain confused? Kaambo kakwe nkayumu alimwi kalipotene kapati. His case is difficult and very complicated.

disentangle, Kondipotonona mamvwa asikomwa andoobelela kucisani. Disentangle me from the thorns of the sikomwa tree which have caught my dress. Also: -popolola, -patununa. (1.-potononwa, 2.-potonwede, 3.-potonozya, 4.-potonweda, 5.-potonwedalyo, 6.-potononesya, 7.-potonona-potonona, 8.-potononana)
  • search, Kopotonona munkomo yabuluke, antela ulajana mali. = Search in the pocket of the trousers, maybe you will find some money.

eat greedily without leaving anything, Ani ciya ciindi nobakacili kusiyana ajule walo syaanza musyule wakapotyoola nyama yamudaala. = But at the time when he was running away from the secretary bird, a lion also came up behind and ate all the meat of the old man. (1.-potyoolwa, 4.-poptyoolela, 5.potyoolelalyo, 6.-potyoolesya, poptyoola-potyoola)

eat greedily, Naakaswena mpaakasiide mukuli wakwe, wakamvwa cintu cipovwoola mafwuwa kumwi cilavwitima. = When he reached where he had left his luggage he heard something gobbling up the bones while growling. (1.-povwoolwa, 2.-povweede, 3.-povwoozya, 4.-povweeda, 5.-povweedalyo, 6.-povwoolesya, 7.-povwoola-povwoola, 8.-povwoolana)

be massacred, crushed, Muntu wakalyatwa moota wakapozauka mubili oonse. The entire body of the person who was hit by a vehicle was crushed. Also: -pwasyauka, -fwunzauka. (1.-pozaukwa, 2.-pozaukide, 3.-pozaukizya, 4.-pozaukila, 5.-pozaukilalyo, 6.-pozaukisya, 7.-pozauka-pozauka)

massacre, smash, Moota wakamupozaula maulu oonse. = The vehicle broke both his/her legs. (1.-pozaulwa, 2.-pozawide, 3.-pozauzya, 4.-pozawida, 5.-pozawidalyo, 6.-pozaulisya, 7.-pozaula-pozaula, 8.-pozaulana)

cry with loud voice, Cheelo niyakamuluma nzoka, wakapozomoka kulila. = When the snake bit Cheelo, he cried out with a loud voice. (1.-pozomokwa, 2.-pozomokede, 3.-pozomozya, 4.-pozomokela, 5.-pozomokelalyo, 6.-pozomokesya, 7.-pozomoka-pozomoka, 8.-pozomokelana)

transfer, transpose, transcribe, rt. -pola, Ndakamupozya mwana angu kuti akayiile kumbi. = I transferred by child so that s/he goes to learn somewhere else. Kayuni nkindakeenena ndajana kakapozya. = I find that the little bird which I had spied had transferred her young.
  • release, express, Mweenzuma wakapozya majwi anyemya bantu. = My friend emitted words which annoyed the people. Taakayanda kupozya kwaamba ncaakali kuyeeya. = He did not want to express what he was thinking. Limwi nikakaba kaindi kapenga mumoyo, wakapozya kuti wakali kundiyanda. = Finally after he had suffered for a while in the heart, he spoke openly that he loved me. (1.-pozyegwa, 2.-pozyezye, 3.-pozyesya, 4.-pozyela, 5.-pozyelalyo, 6.-pozyesya, 7.-pozya-pozya, 8.-pozyanya)
express to, rt. -pozya, Ku Chikuni musankwa nkwakaapozyezya makani akwe aluyando kuli Mutinta. = It was at Chikuni where the boy revealed the fact that he loved Mutinta.
be burst open, (2.-pozyokede, 3.-pozyosya, 4.-pozyokela, 5.-pozyokelalyo, 6.-pozyokesya, 7.-pozyokapozyoka) Also: -posyoka.

burst open, Musilisi wakafwambaana kupozyola cuute. = The doctor was quick to lance the abcess. (1.-pozyolwa, 2.-pozyolede, 3.-pozyosya, 4.-pozyolela, 5.-pozyolelalyo, 6.-pozyolesya, 7.-pozyola-pozyola, 8.-pozyolana) Also: -tozoka.

struggle, be restless, Inombe eyi ilapubauka kukamwa. = This cow struggles when it is being milked. (1.-pubaukwa, 2.-pubaukide, 3.-pubaukizya, 4.-pubaukila, 5.-pubaukilalyo, 6.-pubaukisya, 7.-pubauka-pubauka, 8.-pubaukizyanya) Also: -pukauka.

repent, feel sorry, Ndakapubuka cisubulo ncibaandipa bataata. = I repented because of the punishment which father gave me. (1.-pubukwa, 2.-pubukide, 3.-pubusya, 4.-pubukila, 5.-pubukilalyo, 6.-pubukisya, 7.-pubuka-pubuka. 8.-pubukana)

punish, Komupubula acileke ncacita. = Punish him so that he stops what he is doing. Bakabapubula basankwa bakabbide nombe. = They punished the boys who had stolen the cattle. (1.-pubulwa, 2.-pubwide, 3.-pubuzya, 4.-pubwida, 5.-pubwidalyo, 6.-pubulisya, 7.-pubula-pubula, 8.-pubulana)

be left in misery Nzala bantu yakabapubya kapati. = The hunger left the people in misery. (1.-pubizyigwa, 2.-pubizyide, 3.-pubya, 4.-pubizyila, 5.-pubizyilalyo, 6.-pubizyisya, 7.-pubyapubya, 8.-pubizyanya)

pour out a little, Kamupugula mukupa musyoonto wamulwazi. = Pour out a little milk for the patient. (1.-pugulwa, 2.-pugwide, 3.-puguzya, 4.-pugwida, 5.-pugwidalyo, 6.-pugulisya, 7.-pugula-pugula, 8.-pugulana) Also: -pungula, -ungula.

rub, Musilisi upuka mulwazi wakwe musamu. = The doctor is rubbing his patient with medicine. (1.-pukwa, 2.-pukide, 3.-pusya, 4.-pukila, 5.-pukilalyo, 6.-pukisya, 7.-puka-puka, 8.-pukana)
  • make rain, Ijilo kwakanyina makumbi manji aamvwula, nokuba boobu twakaugwa nkaambo bananga bakali kupuka. Yesterday there were not many rain-clouds, nonetheless we were drenched because the rainmakers were making rain.
  • shake head, Wakapuka mutwe kutondezya kuti cakamucima. = He shook his head indicating that it irritated him. Also: -pika mutwe, -tika mutwe.
  • deprive, Babbi bakandipuka mali angu oonse. The thieves deprived me of all my money. Also: -nyanga.
  • stir, as sour milk, Bacembele bakabweza mpizyo akutalika kupuka mabisi. = The elderly women brought a stirringstick and began to stir the sour milk. Also: -kopa.

shake the head, rt. -puka, Wakali kupukaanya mutwe nkaambo kukanana cakali kwaala. = He shook his head because he was unable to talk. (1.-pukaanyizigwa, 2.-pukeenye, 3.-pukaanya, 4.-pukaanyizyizya, 5.-pukaanyizyizyalyo, 6.-pukaanyisya, 7.-pukaanyapukaanya, 8.-pukaanyizyanya)

be wide awake, be alert, Kamupukamana kukkala nobatanasika basinkondonyoko. Be alert as you sit before your enemies arrive. (1.-pukamanwa, 2.-pukamenye, 3.-pukamanya, 4.-pukamanina, 5.-pukamaninalyo, 6.-pukamanisya, 7.-pukamana-pukamana, 8.-pukamaninana) Also: -pukumana.

struggling with one another, Basimpongo bakali kupukana kulya buci. The goatherds were struggling with one another to get the honey. Baceta bakali kupukana zipopwe. = The monkeys were pulling away the maize. from one another. (1.-pukwa, 2.-pukide, 3.-pusya, 4.-pukila, 5.-pukilalyo, 6.-pukisya, 7.-pukana-pukana, 8.-pukana) Also: -nyangana, -nyaana.
shake, Wakapukanya mutwe. He shook his head. (1.-pukanyizyigwa, 2.-pukenye, 3.-pukanya, 4.-pukanyizyizya, 5.-pukanyizyizyalyo, 6.-pukanyisya, 7.-pukanya-pukanya, 8.-pukanyizyanya)

twist repeatedly, as a stick when cooking nsima, twirl a thing between fingers. Koleta mpusyo akupuka-puka nsima kutegwa makoto apwaike Bring the twirling-stick to stir the nsima to break the lumps. Naakamana kwaanzya basimbi wakalipuka-puka mu maanza. = After he had greeted the girls he rubbed his hands together. (1.-pukwa-pukwa, 2.-pukide-pukide, 3.-pukizya-pukizya, 4.-pukila-pukila, 5.-pukilalyo-pukilalyo, 6.-pukisya-pukisya, 7.-pukapuka-pukapuka, 8.-pukana)
  • rub oneself with soap, medicine, Ndali kulipuka-puka matu amuwaama mu mutwe kutegwa uleke kucisa. = I was rubbing leaves of the muwaama tree on my head so that it would stop paining.

struggle, nombe nsomona ilapukauka kukamwa. = A cow which has given birth to its first-born struggles when being milked. (1.-pukaukwa, 2.-pukaukide, 3.-pukausya, 4.-pukaukila, 5.-pukaukilalyo, 6.-pukaukisya, 7.-pukauka-pukauka) Also: -pubauka.

rub the hair with milk, design one's hair by making it into little tufts, Wakamujana musimbi mubotu kalipukila busuki bwakwe kumutwe. = He found a beautiful girl designing her hair by making it into little tufts. (Mazubaano bakubusi balayandisya kupanga masusu abo kuti ibe mpuki. = In modern days the youth like to have their hair twisted in short tufts.) (1.-pukilwa, 2.-pukwide, 3.-pukizya, 4.-pukilila, 5.-pukililalyo, 6.-pukilisya, 7.-pukila-pukila, 8.-pukilana)
  • use powdered medicine, Bantu bamwi balapukila musamu ukola nswi mumeenda. = Some people put poisonous medicine into the water to kill fish.

punish, Basicikolo bapati bapukula basicikolo bapya. The older school boys torment the new ones. (1.-pukulwa, 2.-pukwide, 3.-pukuzya, 4.-pukwida, 5.-pukwidalyo, 6.-pukulisya, 7.-pukula-pukula, 8.-pukulana) Also: -penzya.
  • dust itself, as a hen does, Bakwale bali kupukula mubulimo bwandongwe. = The partridges dusted themselves in the groundnut plot.
  • scramble for, *Inkuku zyaapukula mapopwe oonse ali mucisuwo.* = The chickens scrambled for all the maize which was in the basket.

smooth and twist one another *Basimbi bakapukulana busuki kumitwe akwaangana tukata twambaanyina amitwe akuzingwa ninga kumaulu akumaboko.* = The girls smoothed and twisted one another's hair by making it into little tufts, tying pads of cowry shells on their heads and putting rings on their legs and on their arms.

sit in a careless manner or adopt an insolent pose, *Ncibi omuntu kupukumana mbuli citumba.* = It is bad to sit like a foolish owl. (1.-pukumanwa, 2.-pukumenye, 3.-pukumanya, 4.-pukumanina, 5.-pukumaninalyo, 6.-pukumanisya, 7.-pukumanapukumana, 8.-pukumaninana)
  • become alert, *Malambo wakapukumana akuswiilila majwi nkwaakali kweetezya.* = Malambo became alert listening to where the voices were coming from. Also: -pukamana.

shake oneself to remove dust, *Kolipukumuna, kumutwe kuli kasuko.* = Shake yourself, there is dust on your head. (1.-pukumunwa, 2-pukumwide, 3.-pukumuzya, 4.-pukumwida, 5.-pukumwidalyo, 6.-pukumunisya, 7.-pukumuna-pukumuna, 8.-pukumunana) Also: -bbukumuna, -sansamuna.

shake the head, *Wakasyaala wiide kupukunya mutwe nkaambo twaambo otu twakamukola.* = He was left just shaking his head because these statements had devastated him. (1.-pukunyizyigwa, 2.-pukunyizyide, 3.-pukunyizyizya, 4.-pukunyizyizya, 5.-pukunyizyizyalyo, 6.-pukunyisya, 7.-pukunya-pukunya, 8.-pukunyizyanya)

rub on, apply oil or ointment, *Kolipukusa mafwuta mubili oonse.* = Rub oil over the whole body. Also: -nanika. (1.-pukusigwa, 2.-pukuside, 3.-pukusya, 4.-pukusila, 5.-pukusilalyo, 6.-pukusisya, 7.-pukusa-pukusa, 8.-pukusana)

rub, wipe, *Komupukuta mwana ayume, ulafwa mpeyo mboomana kumusanzya.* = Rub the child down so that s/he becomes dry, she is dying with the cold after you washed him/her. *Kopukuta mabbusu angu kazwe kasuko.* = Wipe my shoes to take off the dust. *Wakaleta cipukutizyo cakupukuta bulowa.* She brought a cloth to wipe away the blood. (1.-pukutwa, 2.-pukutide, 3.-pukutizya,/-pukutya, 4.-pukutila, 5.-pukutilalyo, 6.-pukutisya, 7.-pukuta-pukuta, 8.-pukutana.) Also: -juusya, -sansamuna.

tranfer nsima from cooking-pot to dish, *Kopula nsima mumutiba.* = Dish out all the nsima. Also: -apula. (1.-pulwa, 2.-pulide, 3.-puzya, 4.-pulila, 5.-pulilalyo, 6.-pulisya, 7.-pula-pula, 8.-pulilana)
  • cast off old skin, slough, *Imbooma yakali kupula mapapa.* = The python was casting off its old skin. Also: -kwama.

pull off, as leaves from stalks, *Kamupulaula matuvwu aya tukasilisye mwana kunanda.* = Pull off the leaves so that we can go and treat the child at home. *Kamupulaula matu aacinkomba tujike.* = Pull off okra leaves so that we can cook. (1.-pulaulwa, 2.-pulawide, 3.-pulauzya, 4.-pulawida, 5.-pulawidalyo, 6.-pulaulisya, 7.-pulaula-pulaula, 8.-pulawidana)
dish out food for, rt. -pula, *Sena baama, bataata ndibapulile yabo nsima?* = Mother, should I dish out for father his nsima?

slip off, be peeled off, Zikanda zyankuku zyapuluka nibazitila meenda apya. = The skin of the chicken was peeled off when they poured hot water on it. Sokwe wakapuluka mucila = The baboon's tail was stripped of it's skin. Also: -yupuluka, -pululuka, -subuluka. 1.-pulukwa, 2.-pulukide, 3.-pulusya, 4.-pulukila, 5.-pulukilalyo, 6.-pulukisya, 7.-puluka-puluka, 8.-pulusyanya)
  • be saved from, Twakapuluka acooIwe kuzwa muntenda yamootokala. = We were fortunately saved from a motoraccident. Ndakapuluka kakunyina kakwambu. I was saved without the slightest scratch. Also: -fwutuka.

gnaw, nibble, Kulya mangamwe aatabizwa nkupulukuta. = You have to gnaw to eat half-cooked maize grains. Amuleke kunyeela ntuntuIwa aku-pulukuta munyengele. = Stop chewing inedible fruit and gnawing grass. (1.-pulukutwa, 2.-pulukutide, 3.-pulukutya, 4.-pulukutila, 5.-pulukutilalyo, 6.-pulukutisya, 7.-pulukuta-pulukuta, 8.-pulukutana) Also: -nyemfwuta.

strip off, as a branch of its leaves, clean grass for thatching, Mwana naakalumwa nzoka, bausyi bakapulula matu amucecete kutegwa atafwune. When the child was bitten by a snake, the father stripped leaves from a mucecete tree so that it could chew them. (1.-pululwa, 2.-pulwide, 3.-puluzya, 4.-pulwida, 5.-pulwidalyo, 6.-pululisya, 7.-pulula-pulula, 8.-pulwidana)
  • strip off, as clothes, unthread, as a strip of beads, Kopulula munyoonyo ndilye. = Strip off the munyoonyo fruit so that I eat.

fly away together as little birds, Inziba zilapululuka mpozinywa meenda. Doves fly away together from where they have been drinking water. (1.-pululukwa, 2.-pululukide, 3.-pululukizya, 4.-pululukila, 5.-pululukilalyo, 6.-pululukisya 7.-pululuka-pululuka) Also: -bbululuka.
  • slip off, as a ring from finger, Ntasa yangu yakapululuka kukanwe nindakali kujwa bwizu. The ring slipped from my finger when I was cutting the grass. Also: -puluka, -fwumuka.
  • peel off, Lukanda Iwamwana Iwakapululuka naakapya ceele. = The skin of the child peeled off when it was burnt by the porridge. Also: -yubbuluka.

ululate, Bamakaintu balapululusya nobazyana Iwiindi. = The women ululate as they dance at the Iwiindi ceremony. Also: -ulubwizya, -uma ngoloolo. (1.-pululusyigwa, 2.-pululusyide, 3.-pululuzya, 4.-pululusyizya, 5.-pululuzyizyalyo, 6.-pululusyisya, 7.-pululusya-pululusya)

ululate, Bantu bakapululuzya kusekelela kusidwa meenda. = People ululated in happiness because of the well which was dug for them. Kamupululuzya kutambula beenzu banu. = Ululate as you receive your visitors. (1.-pululuzyigwa, 2.-pululuzyide, 3.-pululuzya, 4.-pululuzyizya, 5.-pululuzyizyalyo, 6.-pululuzyisya, 7.-pululuzya-pululuzya, 8.-pululuzyanya) Also: -olobwezya, lizya ngoloolo, -lizya nguluulu.

become alert and suprised, Musimbi wakapulumana naakaitwa. = The girl paid attention when she was called. Muvwimi naakabona kanamusya kacela wakasiba mulosi, mpoona kakapulumana. = A hunter whistled when he saw a duiker, thereupon it stood alert. (a riddle, Ndaita, ndapulumana .....Ninkoye. = I called, I stood alert..... It is the eyebrow.) (1.-pulumanwa, 2.-pululmenye, 3.-pulumanya, 4.-pulumanina, 5.-pulumaninalyo, 6.-pulumanisya, 7.-pulumana-pulumana, 8.-pulumaninana)

be watery as a badly cooked potatoe, Zimbwali zisigwa mainza zilapulumba. = Sweet potatoes which are dug up in the rainy season are watery. (1.-pulumbwa, 2.-pulumbide, 3.-pulumbya, 4.-pulumbila, 5.-pulumbilalyo, 6.-pulumbisya, 7.-pulumba-pulumba) Also: -bwaya.
  • get diarrhoea, Mwana wakasotokwa, ulapulumba. = If a parent of a sucking child becomes pregnant, the child gets diarrhoea. (traditional belief). Bana bakapulumba kapati nibakalya nswi yakabola. = When children ate rotten fish, they got diarrhoea. Also: -soomona.

abort, bear a still-born offspring, Munyama wakapulumuna mumwezi wabili. The animal bore a still-born offspring in its second month. (1.-pulumunwa, 2.-pulumwide, 3.-pulumuzya, 4.-pulumwida, 5.-pulumwidalyo, 6.-pulumunisya, 7.-pulumuna-pulumuna, 8.-pulumunana) Also: -sowa.

be white with dust or ashes, unkempt, Masusu angu apulungana akaambo kabana bali kundijatauka mumutwe. My hair is messed up because of the children who were catching me by the head. Joojo wabucesya kunkolola, waile kupulungana mubili oonse. = Joojo who was at the initiation ceremony until dawn, was covered all over in dust. Also: -bbulungana. (1.-pulunganizyigwa, 2.-pulungenye, 3.-pulunganya, 4.-pulunganina, 5.-pulunganinalyo, 6.-pulunganisya, 7.-pulungana-pulungana, 8.-pulunganizyanya)
put things in disorder, Ba Matebele nobakasika kubusena oko kwakali kubikkwa tubiya, bakatupulunganya. = When the Matebele came to that place where small pots were placed, they disturbed them.
be in a state of disorder, Masusu akali kwiide kupulungene mbuli sikalalu. Her hair was tossed about like a mad woman.

deny a person something, Kuti muntu wafwa nzala, tayelede kupuluzigwa cakulya. If a person is hungry, she ought not to be denied food. Muzolani wako wakulolezya nyama teelede kupuluzigwa akusiswa tubotu a tunono. Your friend who shared meat with you should not be denied or have hidden from him good and sweet little things. (2.-puluzyide, 3.-puluzya, 4.-puluzyizya, 5.-puluzyizyalyo, 6.-puluzyisya, 7.-puluzigwa-puluzigwa, 8.-puluzyanya)

ululate, Bamwi bakapuluzya bakati, "Wi-li-li-li-li! = Some ululated by emitting the sound, "Wi-li-li-lili!" Also: -ulubwizya, -pululuzya. (1.-puluzyigwa, 2.-puluzyizye, 4.-puluzyizya, 5.-puluzyizyalyo, 6.-puluzyisya, 7.-puluzya-puluzya, 8.-puluzyanya)

braid the hair, Insiku balombe bakali kupumba busuki. = Long ago the boys used to braid the hair. (1.-pumbwa, 2.-pumbide, 3.-pumbya, 4.-pumbila, 5.-pumbilalyo, 6.-pumbisya, 7.-pumba-pumba, 8.-pumbana)

pluck nuts from stem, shell as mealies, Babelesi bangu bapumbula ndongwe mazubaano. = These days my workers are plucking groundnuts. (1.-pumbulwa, 2.-pumbwide, 3.-pumbuzya, 4.-pumbulila, pumbulilalyo, 6.-pumbulisya, 7.-pumbula-pumbula, 8.-pumbwidana) Also: -sonzola.
  • clean fields/gardens, Balimi banji balapumbula myuunda yabo mumwezi wa Kavwumbi-kaniini. Many farmers clean their fields in the month of October. Also: -gunkaula.

revolve, Ivwili lilapumbulika kabotu sunu. The wheel is revolving well today. (1.-pumbulikwa, 2.-pumbulikide, 3.-pumbulisya, 4.-pumbulikila, 5.-pumbulikilalyo, 6.-pumbulikisya, 7.-pumbulika-pumbulika) Also: - tendeleka.

grab quick, e.g Nobana kamuleka kupumpa. Children stop grabbing things. (1.-pumpwa, 2.-pumpide, 3.-pumpya, 4.-pumpila, 5.-pumpilalyo, 6.-pumpisya, 7.-pumpa-pumpa, 8.-pumpana) Also: -pupa, -nyaana, -fwumpa.

sit on the haunches, squat, Wakajanika mbwaapumpumana kuyota mulilo. She was found sitting on her haunches warming herself at the fire. Also: -sunsumana. (1.-pumpumanwa, 2.-pumpumene, 3.-pumpumanya, 4.-pumpumanina, 5.-pumpumaninalyo, 6.-pumpumanisya, 7.-pumpumana-pumpumana, 8.-pumpumaninana)

be over-quick in grabbing food, rt. -pumpa, Basinzala bapumpumina kuvwola busu. Hungry people are over anxious to earn mealiemeal. (1.-pumpuminwa, 2.-pumpumide, 3.-pumpumizya, 4.-pumpumina, 5.-pumpuminalyo, 6.-pumpumisya, 7.-pumpumina-pumpumina, 8.-pumpuminana) Also: -pupumina.
rest, Bakaintu bangu bakaunka kwabo kukupumuna. My wife went to her home to rest. Nomutaningamana mulimo oyu, tamweelede kupumuna pe. You ought not to rest before you finish this work.

rest, take holiday. Bantu banji balaunka kukupumwida kumavwuumina. Many people go for a holiday at the waterfalls. (1.-pumunwa, 2.-pumunide/-pumwide, 3.-pumunizya/pumuzya, 4.-pumunina,/pumwida, 5.-pumuninalyo/pumwidalyo, 6.-pumunisya, 7.-pumuna-pumuna, 8.-pumunizyanya) Also: -okezya.

go under, evade an obstacle, Musimbi wakapuna mumaulu aabasa nkwa akutija. = The girl passed under the legs of the boys and ran away. Bacita kupuna buya muluwaile kuti bakamuzwisye wali kupya munanda. = They passed under the wire in order to rescue the one who was being burnt in the house. (1.-punwa, 2.-punide, 3.-punya, 4.-punina, 5.-puninalyo, 6.-punisya, 7.-puna-puna, 8.-puninana)
  • slip through a hole, Simbi yajamba yapuna alimwi = The screw of the plough has slipped through the hole again. (i.e. it is worn away)
  • escape from a crime, Syaanasulwe wakatija akupuna mulandu wakuuzya bana. = The hare ran away from the crime of selling the children.

mention by name, Bakapunda Munsanje kuti nguwakabba njombe yakasweeka. = They mentioned Munsanje as the one who stole the cow that had gone astray.
  • shout for help, Wakaumwa kapati limwi wakapunda kutegwa bantu bamuvwune. = He cried out for help so that the people would save him. (1.-pundwa, 2.-pundide, 3.-pundya, 4.-pundila, 5.-pundilalyo, 6.-pundisya, 7.-punda-punda, 8.-pundana)

become untreatable, Bulwazi bwako bwakapundila, wakamuka kusilikwa kabotu. = Your disease has become untreatable, you were late in getting proper attention. Also: -tundila.
  • be poorly cooked, Myungu yapundila. = The pumpkins have not been cooked properly. Also: -tundila.

be named, as the person on whom the charm is applied, Ooyu musamu wakali kwiitwa kuti 'kamusalaule'. Nokuba kuti mbanji baulya, nkuuya kubeleka nkuuli yooyo alikke wapundwa. = This medicine was called 'kamusalaule' (You must choose). Even though there be many who eat it, it will only work on that one who has been named.
  • be set aside for someone, *Mbwaa-sikila makoto yapundwa nongo yoonse yabukoko, nkabela baya batuba buu ulajana bamuvwoomanina mucende.* = As soon as this man arrives a whole pot of beer is set aside for him, and you find the inexperienced ones crowding around this bull of a man.
  • shout for help, *Michelo wakaumwa calufwu limwi wakapunda kutegwa bantu bamuvwune.* = Michelo was beaten in danger of death until he cried out so that people would save him.

wait for a long time, as when boss is away, *Twali kupunduka katu-syoma kuti basololi balafwambaana kusika.* = We were waiting a long time hoping that leaders would arrive. (1.-pundukwa, 2.-pundukide, 3.-pundu-sya, 4.-pundukila, 5.-pundukilalyo, 6.-pundukisya, 7.-punduka-punduka, 8.-pundukisyanya) Also: -bunduka.

be first to do, build a village on a new site, begin to eat a particular food, *Bataata bakapunga buya kukkala awa kunyina wakakkede.* = My father just built a village there where no one lived. *Twakapunga biya kulya mapopwe matete mumwezi wa Kavwumbi-kaniini.* = We began to eat fresh maize in the month of October. *Mebo sunu nkokupunga kusika akuswaangana anduwe okuno.* = This is the first time for me to reach here and meet you here. *Wakali kwiide kuzilaika mbuli muntu wapunga kutanta bbaasi.* = He was just akward like a person trying to mount a bus for the first time. (1.-pungwa, 2.-pungide, 3.-pungizya, 4.-pungila, 5.-pungilalyo, 6.-pungisya, 7.-punga-punga, 8.-pungilana) Also: -soma.
  • invent a story, tell lies, *Ino waile kukapunga buya kaambo katako akuliko.* = You are just inventing a tale which is not there and never was. *Mazuba asunu twaleka kupunga mazina ambi pe.* = Nowadays we have stopped inventing new names. *Bakapunga aziimbo zilumba-izya mwami.* = They composed songs in praise of the chief.
  • wear a tuft of hair on the crown of the head, *Basankwa bakaindi bakali kuyandisya kupunga zisumpa.* = Long ago the men were very fond of wearing tufts of hair on the top of the head. Also: -enga cisumpa

taste food before giving it to guest, *Ncibotu kupungila mweenzu cakulya notanamupa.* = It is good to taste food before you give it to a visitor. (1.-pungilwa, 2.-pungilide, 3.-pungilizya, 4.-pungilila, 5.-pungililalyo, 6.-pungilisya, 7.-pungila-pungila, 8.-pungililana) Also: -labilila,
  • accuse without evidence, *Wandi-pungila kaambo nkindatacita.* = You have accused me without evidence of something of which I did not do.

pour out a little, *Pungula meenda ubape bacembele banywe.* = Pour out a little water for the old women to drink. (1.-pungulwa, 2.-pungwide, 3.-punguzya, 4.-pungwida, 5.-pungwidalyo, 6.-pungulisya, 7.-pungula-pungula, 8.-pungwidana) Also: ungula, -punula.
  • cause to change into, transform *Wakamupungula mwanaakwe lyaba domba.* = He turned his child into a medium of witchcraft. Also: -fwungula.

sit quietly, *Uleelede kujana cigubbu mwanikugubbila, kwiinda kupungumana buyo mucisi cabene kakunyina akakoli kakulisoozya nzinini.* = You ought to find something to protect yourself, rather than sit quietly in someone's country without even a stick to drive away the flies.
sit quietly, Ulacibona ncatanabwene kapungumene kati tatumubwene. = He will see what he has never seen as he sits quietly thinking that we have not seen him.

shake one's head, e.g Mwana naakabuzigwa kuti naa waalide kale, wakapungunya mutwe. = When the child was asked whether he had already eaten, he shook his head. (1.-pungunyizyigwa, 2.-pungunyizyide, 3.-pungunyizya, 4.-pungunyizyizya, 5.-pungunyizyizyalyo, 6.-pungunyizyisya, 7.-pungunya-pungunya, 8.-pungunizyanya) Also: -gwenaula, -zungaanya, -puka.

be irritated, as an eye, Inga watiiti kulisikisa liso kunyina akuzwa mamvwu pe, dee kupunya-punya biyo. = When he tried to rub his eye to get the dust out, it only became more irritated. Kupunya-punya kwakaima ayalo yacizike yakaima. = The irritation stopped and also the tears stopped. (1.-punyigwa-punyigwa, 2.-punyidepunyide, 3.-punyizya-punyizya, 4.-punyinina-punyinina, 5.-punyininapunyininalyo, 6.-punyinisya-punyinisya, 7.-punyapunya-punyapunya, 8.-punyinana-punyinana)

pour out a little, Mudaala naakafwa nyota, wakapunula meenda munongo mulufwulu kuti anywe. = When the old man was thirsty, he poured out a little water from the pot into the drinking gourd so that he would drink. (1.-purnulwa, 2.-punwide, 3.-punuzya, 4.-puŋwida, 5.-puŋwidalyo, 6.-punulisya, 7.-punula-punula, 8.-puŋwidana) Also: -pungula, -ungula.

swarm, scramble for, struggle to get in or out, Bantu balikupupa biya kuula busu. = The people were struggling in an effort to get mealie-meal. (1.-pupwa, 2.-pupide, 3.-pupizya, V - 448 4.-pupanina, 5.-pupaninalyo, 6.-pupanisya, 7.-pupa-pupa, 8.-pupana)

struggle with one another or compete in doing something, rt. -pupa, Nzuki zyapupana kunjila mudola. = The bees compete with one another trying to get into the hive. Mwiiyi wakali kwiile kulangilila bantu nkobapupana kutanta mootokala. = The teacher was just watching the people as they struggled with one another to get on to the truck.

be snatched away, Bulowa bwakwe, buzumi bwakwe bulapupauka mbuli kakweelele mukambizyi. = His blood, his life is snatched away like a leaf of maize in a whirlwind. (1.-pupauka, 2.-pupaukide, 3.-pupausya, 4.-pupaukila, 5.-pupaukilalyo, 6.-pupaukisya, 7.-pupauka-pupauka, 8.-pupaukilana)

rush to do or acquire something, be eager, rt. -pupa, Baama bapupila mwana kuti aye kucikolo. = Mother is eager for the child to go to school. Bantu bapupila munyo nkaambo taulibonyi sunu. = The people are eager to get salt as it is not to be seen today. (1.-pupilwa, 2.-pupide, 3.-pupizya 4.-pupilila, 5.-pupililalyo, 6.-pupilisya, 7.-pupila-pupila, 8.-pupizyanya)

scramble for something in a group, rt. -pupa, Bali kupupizyanzya lyasika mapopwe aacivwole-vwole. = They were scrambling for the maize when the time came to get food for work. Abaya bantu bapupizyanya kuula mapopwe. = Those people are eager to buy maize.

run very fast, Mudyaka wakapupuka mbuli muwo kutandila Mutinta. = Mudyaka ran like the wind chasing Mutinta. (1.-pupukwa, 2.-pupukide, 3.-pupusya, 4.-pupukila, 5.-pupukilalyo, 6.-pupukisya, 7.-pupukapupuka, 8.-pupukizyanya)

nod in sleepiness, Ciindi Mulembwe naakali kusobana cisolo wakali kupupukilwa-pupukilwa akaambo kakuti nonzi zyakali zyakuvwuluzya ciindi camasiku. = At the time when Mulembwe was playing cisolo he was nodding because he did not have enough sleep the previous night. Also: -gunka. (2.-pupukidwe, 3.-pupukizya, 4.-pupukilila, 5.-pupukililalyo, 6.-pupukilisya, 7.-pupukilwa-pupukilwa)
  • quiver, Nacita boobu, mubili wakwe wakatalika kupupukilwa kapeyopeyo. = When she did this her body began to quiver with a chill.

harvest crops, Ciindi camupeyo bakali kulimina maila muceme: bunji bwabo bakali kumanina kupupulapupula tupopwe. In the cold season people were weeding sorgum, most of them had finished harvesting maize. (1.-pupulwa, 2.-pupukilide, 3.-pupulizya, 4.-pupwida, 5.-pupwidalyo, 6.-pupulisya, 7.-pupula-pupula, 8.-pupulanina)

look with desire to have, Mwana uulaa nzala ulapupulala kulanga balya. The hungry child looks with desire at those who are eating. (1.-pupulalwa, 2.-pupulalide, 3.-pupulazya, 4.-pupulalila, 5.-pupulalilalyo, 6.-pupulalisya, 7.-pupulala-pupulala, 8.-pupulalilana) Also: -langila

be freed from, Mainza wakapupuluka naakapegwa musamu wakupupululwa. Mainza was freed from the spirit (of the one he had killed), when he was given the medicine of purification from the avenging spirit. Mizeezo yabuzangi yakaide kupupuluka yamumana doo. He was freed from thoughts of rebelliousness which had finished him. (1.-pupulukwa, 2.-pupulukide, 3.-pupuluzya, 4.-pupulukila, 5.-pupulukilalyo, 6.-pupulukisya, 7.-pupuluka-pupuluka)

remove the power of the spirit who has been offended by a crime, remove witchcraft, Murnanga wakabapupulula balozi bakajaya bana. = The witchdoctor cleansed the witches who killed the children. Moonde ulicizyi kupupulula wajaya muntu. = Moonde knows how to remove the evil of a person who killed another. Ndakupupulula bulozi bwako. I remove your witchcraft. (1.-pupululwa, 2.-pupulwide, 3.-pupuluzya, 4.-pupulwida, 5.-pupulwidalyo, 6.-pupululisya, 7.-pupulula-pupulula, 8.-pupululana)
  • winnow, Kamupupulula musozya usalale kutegwa utatutingi twatalika kulya. Winnow the samp to clean it so that it does not choke us when we start eating. Kamupupulula mapopwe aaya tutole kucigayo. Winnow the maize which is going to the mill. Also: -beeta, -kwaapula.

eat voraciously, Ooyu mwana upupululwa biya kulya nkaambo jilo taakalide. This child is eating ravenously before others because s/he did not eat yesterday.
  • talk energetically, Kambela upupululwa biya kukanana mumuswaangano. = Kambela talks energetically in a meeting.
  • be delivered from using witchcraft and be freed from the spirit of the victim, Muntu ulowa atolwe kukupupululwa aleke kulowa. A person who bewitches should be taken to be purified so that s/he stops bewitching.

blow into/towards, Kambizi kakamupupulwida mulwizi. = The whirlwind blew her into the lake.
  • winnow for someone, Kamubapupulwida musozya bacembele. = Winnow samp for the old woman.

rush to do, swarm out, flap wings, Inswa zilapupuma kunjila mumbiya. The flying edible insects flap their wings as they enter the clay pots in large numbers. Kamuleka kupupuma kulya nsima, ninji, mulakkuta. = Stop rushing to eat the nsima, there is plenty, you will have enough. Nindakaimika cimbayambaya ndakabaambila kuti baleke kupupuma kutanta. = When I stopped the vehicle I told them that they should not be rushing to get on. (1.-pupumwa, 2.-pupumide, 3.-pupumya, 4.-pupumina, 5.-pupuminalyo, 6.-pupumisya, 7.-pupuma-pupuma, 8.-pupuminana)
  • rise as yeast or bread, foam, Bumena buli kabotu bulafwambaana kupupuma. = Good yeast rises quickly. Also: -fwufwuma, -tutumuka, -fwutumuka, -fwuta..
be anxious to, Mazuba aanzala bantu banji balapupumina kuyandaula cakulya. In days of famine many people are anxious to search for food. Also: -pumpumina.

grow fast, grow genetically, Moombe ooyu ulapupumuka kukomena. This calf is growing fast. Ndayanda kulya makuku amumunzi ayaalya amudolopo apupumuka kukomena. = I like to eat big village chickens and those ones in town which are genetically grown.(1.-pupumukwa, 2.-pupumikide, 3.-pupumuzya, 4.-pupumukila, 5.-pupumukilalyo, 6.-pupumukisya, 7.-pupumuka-pupumuka)

surround secretly, Lweendo lutaanzi ba Matebele bakapupunda akufwumpa alimwi akujaya. = On the first expedition the Matebele secretly surrounded and took captives and killed. (1.-pupundwa, 2.-pupundide, 3.-pupundya, 4.-pupundila, 5.-pupundilalyo, 6.-pupundisya, 7.-pupunda-pupunda, 8.-pupundana)

be unkempt, become thin, become wasted, Mubili wa mwana wapupungana akaambo kakuciswa. The body of this child has become emaciated because of sickness. Mwaneesu wakaboola mbuli kuti wakalisweekede, matombe akupupungana kwamubili. Our daughter came like one lost, dirty and in an unkempt state. BuIwazi bwakayandilila mubili onse nkujana oyo muntu wakajisi mubili mubotu wakaide kupupungana. The disease affected the whole body so that the one who had a fine body just wasted away. (1.-pupunganizyigwa, 2.-pupungene, 3.-pupunganya, 4.-pupunganina, 5.-pupunganinalyo, 6.-pupunganisya, 7.-pupungana-pupungana, 8.-pupunganizyanya) Also: -pulungana.
ruffle the hair, Koleka kupupunganya masusu aamweenzinyoko, uulikamwide kabotu. = Stop upsetting your friend's hair, she has combed it nicely.
be in a disordered state, rt. -pupungana, Masusu aamusimbi ngutwakajana mumugwagwa jilo akalipupungene. = The hair of the girl who we found on the road yesterday was unkempt.

be dried up and shrunk, Kuulu kwamulwazi kwakapuputila. = The leg of the patient had shrunk. (1.-puputizyigwa, 2.-puputide, 3.-puputizya, 4.-puputilila, 5.-puputililalyo, 6.-puputilisya, 7.-puputila-puputila, 8.-puputizyanya) Also: -puutila.

wither, as plants under boiling sun, Mapopwe apusama nkaambo kakubala kwazuba. = The maize has withered because of the shining of the sun.(1.-pusamizyigwa, 2.-puseme, 3.-pusamya, 4.-pusamina, 5.-pusaminalyo, 6.-pusamisya, 7.-pusama-pusama) Also: -neta, -pusana.
  • wither, as a limb, *Nsafwu zyaa Mutinta zilapusama.* = The calves of Mutinta's legs have withered.

miss meeting one another, *Twakapusana, tiitwakabonana ku Kaumba.* = We missed one another, we did not see one another at Kaumba. Also: -impana.
  • wither, *Mapopwe apusana nkaambo kakubala kwazuba.* = The maize has withered because of the sunshine. Also: -pusama.

stir, as sour milk, rt. -puka, *Kobelesya mpusyo kupusya nsima.* = Use the stirring-stick to stir the nsima. (1.-pusyigwa, 2.-pusyide, 3.-pusya, 4.-pusyizya, 5.-pusyizyalyo, 6.-pusyisya, 7.-pusya-pusya, 8.-pusyana)
  • make an effort, *Twali kupusya buya kugusya cibulo canyikide mumugodi.* = We were just trying to take out the bucket which had dropped into the well.
  • give trouble, *Aaba bana basunu baapusya mawisi.* = The children of today are troubling their fathers.

slip out, escape, *Mutiba wandipusyuka kuzwa mumaanza, waloka ansi wapwaika.* = The dish slipped out of my hands, it fell on the ground and broke. *Inga watiisole kutanta, wiide kupusyuka.* = When he tried to get on, he just slipped. *Kandipusyuka kayuni nkindajisi mumaanza.* = The little bird escaped which I held in my hands. *Nobakwesu katunga katujatisya kwiiya ciindi netucijisi coolwe nkaambo coolwe ciboola buyo kaindi komwe, naa, kuti cakupusyuka cuunkila limwi.* = Friends let us hold on to learning during the time when we are fortunate because the opportunity only comes once, if it slips away it goes forever. (1.-pusyukwa, 2.-pusyukide, 3.-pusyusya, 4.-pusyukila, 5.-pusyukilalyo, 6.-pusyukisya, 7.-pusyuka-pusyuka, 8.-pusyukana) Also: -syupuka, -pusuka.

move, be alive, *Kuulu kwaleka kuputa.* = The leg has stopped moving. *Sena uciputa mulwazi?* = Is the patient still alive? *Musune uciputa taningafwa.* = The ox is still alive. (1.-putwa, 2.-putide, 3.-putya, 4.-putila, 5.-putilalyo, 6.-putisya, 7.-puta-puta, 8.-putana)
  • be troublesome, *Ooyu mwana ulaputa.* = This child is naughty. Also: -sunda, -ponongozya.
  • collect workmen for forced labour, *Kaindi bama Bbunu bakali kuputa bantu kucibbalo.* = In the past the Boers were collecting the people by force to work for them.

rap up, as in a cloth, *Katuputaila nyama mumapepa aya.* = Let us rap up the meat in these papers. *Nceciindi bantu nobaligonya akuliputaila mumapayi akaambo kampeyo.* = That is the time when people draw up their legs and wrap themselves up in blankets because of the cold. (1.-putailwa, 2.-putailide, 3.-putaizya, 4.-putailila, 5.-putaililalyo, 6.-putailisya, 7.-putaila-putaila, 8.-putaililana)

be alive, *Uulya muntu wacisidwe uciputa-puta.* = That person who was so sick is still alive. *Inzoka iciputa-puta, ilaluma umwi.* = The snake is still alive, it will bite someone.
  • be playful, crack jokes, *Cheelo ulasesya kapati akaambo kakuputa-puta kwakwe.* = Cheelo makes others laugh because of his comic behaviour.

be active, *Muntu uputauka tapengi kapati munzala.* = A person who is active does not suffer much in a famine. (1.-putaukwa, 2.-putaukide, 3.-putausya, 4.-putaukila, 5.-putaukilalyo, 6.-putaukisya, 7.-putauka-putauka, 8.-putaukilana)
  • be alive, Ndali kuti ooyu muntu ulifwide ani uciputauka. = I thought this person is dead, in fact he is still living.

turn inside out continuously, Asole kuputaula nkomo zyakwe zyoonse, pesi tanaakakajana. = When he tried to turn his pockets inside out continuously, he did not find it. (1.-putaulwa, 2.-putawide, 3.-putauzya, 4.-putawida, 5.-putawidalyo, 6.-putaulisya, 7.-putaula-putaula, 8.-putaulana)

make pregnant, play with another's property, Musimbi ooyu bakamuputila basankwa. = The boys made this girl pregnant. Matimba wakaputilwa kumwanaa Haasuntwe. = Matimba was made pregnant by the son of Haasuntwe. Tusimbi tulaputila mibili yato tucili twana. = Young girls play with their bodies when they are still children. (1.-putilwa, 2.-putide, 3.-putizya, 4.-putilila, 5.-putililalyo, 6.-putilisya, 7.-putila-putila, 8.-putilana)
  • wrap up in, Kamuputila zilyo zyanu muntebe zyaloozi Iwamubombo. = Wrap your food up in the fibres of a mubombo tree. Netoona masiku tatweelede kuliputila kumutwe. = When we are sleeping at night we should not cover our heads. Bana banji balafwa nkaambo kakubaputila mitwe yoonse angubo zilemu. = Many children die because of people wrapping up their heads with heavy blankets. Also: -putaila.

wrap around, Basimbi bakaliputilila andumba. The girls wrapped themselves up in blankets. Musankwa wakaiputilila nkaya yomwe yakutela kumwami wakwe. = The boy wrapped up one bangle for paying tax to his chief.

transform, Muzyamba wakaputula mwanaakwe cakaba zinya. = Muzyamba changed his son to become an idiot. Also: -fwungula. (1.-putulwa, 2.-putwide, 3.-putuzya, 4.-putwida, 5.-putwidalyo, 6.-putulisya, 7.-putula-putula, 8.-putulana)
  • turn inside out, as a bag, Mufwambaane kwaputula masaka nkaambo ajisi kasuko. Be quick to turn the sacks inside out because they are full of dust. Also: -pinduula, -fwutumuna.
