build up after illness, Bantu bakafwulukide bakaputuluka lyakamana nzala. = People who were thin build themselves up again when the famine was over. (1.-putulukwa, 2.-putulukide, 3.-putulu-sya, 4.-putulukila, 5.-putulukilalyo, 6.-putulukisya, 7.-putuluka-putuluka, 8.-putulusyanya) Also: -putunuka.
  • straighten out, Kuboko kwangu kwakavwungenye, sunu kwakaputuluka. = My arm which was bent, is now straightened out.

untie, Wakatola ciputu catombwe munanda akuciputumuna. = He took the bundle of tobacco into his house and untied it. (1.-putumunwa, 2.-putumwide, 3.-putumuzya, 4.-putumwida, 5.-putumwidalyo, 6.-putumunisya, 7.-putumuna-putumuna, 8.-putumunana)

recover from severe famine, Wakalikokede, sunu waputunuka waneneya. He was so thin, today he has recovered from the famine and is fat. (1.-putunukwa, 2.-putunukide, 3.-putunusya, 4.-putunukila, 5.-putunukilalyo, 6.-putunukisya, 7.-putunuka-putunuka, 8.-putunukana) Also: -putuluka.

unfold, as letter or cloth, unwrap, Koputununa kapepa ako tulange cili mukati. = Unfold the paper so that we see what is inside. Wakatola ciputu munanda akuciputununa. = She took the bundle into the house and unwraped it. Also: -pasununa, -vwungulula (1.-putununwa, 2.-putunwide, 3.-putunuzya, 4.-putunwida, 5.-putunwidalyo, 6.-putununisya, 7.-putununa-putununa, 8.-putununana)

be active, agile, industrious, Ncibotu kuputuuka lyoonse inga kojana ziyandika. = It is good to be energetic always so that you may fulfill your needs. (1.-putuukwa, 2.-putuukide, 3.-putuusya, 4.-putuukila, 5.-putuukilalyo, 6.-putuukisya, 7.-putuuka-putuuka, 8.-putuukilana) Also: -putauka.

shake, Komusinsimuna kwiinda mukumuputuunya uuwona. = Awaken the one who sleeps by giving him/her a good shake. (1.-putuunyizyigwa, 2.-putuunyizyizye, 3.-putuunya, 4.-putuunyizyizya, 5.-putuunyizyizyalyo, 6.-putuunyisya, 7.-putuunya-putuunya, 8.-putuunyizyanya)

sinking, as the sun, Tunyama twakamuleyauka mane do nolyakapuuka. The animals avoided him until the sun was sinking. (1.-puukwa, 2.-puukide, 3.-puuzya, 4.-puukila, 5.-puukilalyo, 6.-puukisya, 7.-puuka-puuka)

be restless in sleep, Mutinta walikupuukizya masiku oonse akaambo kakukatala kapati. = Mutinta was restless the whole night because she was so tired. (1.-puukizyigwa, 2.-puukizyide, 3.-puukizya, 4.-puukizyizya, 5.-puukizyizyalyo, 6.-puukizyisya, 7.-puukizya-puukizya, 8.-puukizyanya) Also: -wizila.

(1.-puumizyigwa, 2.-puumide, 3.-puumya, 4.-puumina, 5.-puuminalyo, 6.-puumisya, 7.-puuma-puuma, 8.-puumizyanya)

become stupid, Kuyeeya kwenu kulipuutide. Your thinking has become stupid. (1.-puutizyigwa, 2.-puutide, 3.-puutizya, 4.-puutilila, 5.-puutililalyo, 6.-puutilisya, 7.-puutide-puutide, 8.-puutizyanya)
wither, as a reed, Matete apuutila azuba. = The reeds are withered by the sun. Also: -nyana.
make thin, Mbulwazi bwakamupuutisya tuulu. It is the disease which made his legs thin.

make thin, Nyina yakapuutizya kana akaambo kakutakanyonsya kabotu. = That calf has been made thin by the mother which does not suckle it well. Ndusinga Iwakandipuutizya kuboko. = It is a nerve problem which has made my arm to shrink.

turn aside in disgust, Nobakasika munsi amubwa ubolede, bakapuwa akulisinka mpemo. = When they came near the rotten dog, they turned aside in disgust and held their noses. (1.-puwigwa, 2.-puwide, 3.-puwizya, 4.-puwila, 5.-puwilalyo, 6.-puwisya, 7.-puwa-puwa, 8.-puwaminana) Also: -luwa.

turn head aside, keep the head inclined to the side, Webo opuwama neamba, mwati ulimvwide buya nceamba? = You who turn the head aside when I am speaking, are you hearing what I am saying? Wakapuwama akaambo kakutayanda kulanga udonkolwa cuute. She turned her head aside because of not wanting to see the one whose abcess was being lanced. (1.-puwamikwa, 2.-puwamide, 3.-puwamya, 4.-puwamina, 5.-puwaminalyo, 6.-puwamisya, 7.-puwama-puwama, 8.-puwaminana)

be rubbed off as bits of skin when burnt, Mwana naakapya, wakapuzauka lukanda. = When the child was burnt, pieces of skin came off. (1.-puzaukwa, 2.-puzaukide, 3.-puzauzya, 4.-puzaukila, 5.-puzaukilalyo, 6.-puzaukisya, 7.-puzauka-puzauka, 8.-puzausyanya)

rub off as bits of skin, Kamwiipuzaula nkuku mumaulu mbumwaitila kale meenda apya. = Rub the skin off the chicken's legs as you have already poured the hot water. (1.-puzaulwa, 2.-puzawide, 3.-puzauzya, 4.-puzawida, 5.-puzawidalyo, 6.-puzaulisya, 7.-puzauka-puzauka, 8.-puzaulana)

scorch as fire does, Bamupuzula ameenda apya mubwa nibamukupila amubili. = They scorched the dog with the hot water when they sprayed its body. Cibwantu cipya kapati cilapuzula mukanwa. cause to lose one's grip on something, slip out of one's grasp, Wandipuzumuka mutiba waloka ansi. = The dish slipped out of my hands and fell to the ground. Imondo ilapuzumuka mumaanza. slip out from one's grip, Wandipuzyumuka mutiba, waloka ansi. The dish slipped down, it fell on the ground. (1.-puzyumukwa, 2.-puzyumukide, 3.-puzyumuzya, 4.-puzyumukila, 5.-puzyumukilalyo, 6.-puzyumukisya, 7.-puzyumuka-puzyumuka, 8.-puzyumukana) Also: -puzumuka, -puzuka.

play a game with stones, *Bana bakali kupwa kunze ajanda cisyu nicakaida.* = Children were playing a game with stones behind the house when the relish got burnt. Also: -yaata. (1.-pwa, 2.-pwaide, 3.-pwaizya, 4.-pwaila, 5.pwailalyo, 6.-pwaisya, 7.-pwa-pwa)

stuff one's mouth, *Wakazipwaakizya ndongwe naakabona beenzinyina kababoola kulomba.* = He stuffed his mouth with the groundnuts when he saw his friends coming to ask for them. (1.-pwaakizyigwa, 2.-pwaakizyizye, 3.-pwaakizyisya, 4.-pwaakizyila, 5.-pwaakizyilalyo, 6.-pwaakizyisya, 7.-pwaakizya-pwaakizya, 8.-pwaakizyanya) Also: -pwakanizya.

gush out, ooze out, *Meenda akapwaamuka kuzwa mumugonti ngubakali kusya.* The water gushed forth from the well which they were digging. *Bulowa bwakapwaamuka mumpemo naakaumwa cisako amutwe.* = The blood oozed out from the nose when he was beaten on the head with a stick. (1.-pwaamuzyigwa, 2.-pwaamukide, 3.-pwaamuzya, 4.-pwaamukila, 5.-pwaamukilalyo, 6.-pwaamukisya, 7.-pwaamuka-pwaamuka, 8.-pwaamuzyanya)

shatter, as a bottle, *Walipwacula bbodela.* = She smashed the bottle. (1.-pwaculwa, 2.-pwacwide, 3.-pwacuzya, 4.-pwacwida, 5.-pwacwidalyo, 6.-pwaculisya, 7.-pwacula-pwacula, 8.-pwaculana) Also: -pwasyula.

be smashed, break up, *Buci wakabupwacuuka naakalikugwisya.* = When he was removing the honey-comb he broke it. (1.-pwacuukwa, 2.-pwacuukide, 3.-pwacuukizya, 4.-pwacuukila, 5.-pwacuukilalyo, 6.-pwacuukisya, 7.-pwacuuka-pwacuuka, 8.-pwacuukilana) Also: -pwasyuuka.

smash, rt. -pwaya, *Waipwaida nzi nanda yesu?* = Why did you smash our house?

fill one's mouth greedily *Wakaipwakanizya nyama, taakamuzawida mweenzinyina.* = He put the whole piece of meat in his mouth at once, he did not share it with his friend. be discharged, as an abcess, *Busina bwapwampwamuka kuzwa acuute.* Pus was discharged from the abcess. (1.-pwapwamuzyigw 2.-pwampwamukide, 3.-pwampwamuzya, 4.-pwampwamukila, 5.-pwampwamukilalyo, 6.-pwampwamukisya, 7.-pwampwamuka-pwampwamuka, 8.-pwampwamusyanya) Also: -pwapwamuka.
be discharged, *Baama nibaatyanka cuute camwana, busina bwakapwapwamuka.* = When mother squeezed the abcess of the child, the pus was discharged.

go into exile, Banji bantu kucisi ca Angola bakapwanika mumazuba ankondo. = Many people from the country of Angola went into exile during the days of war. (1.-pwanikwa, 2.-pwanikide, 3.-pwanisya, 4.-pwanikila, 5.-pwanikilalyo, 6.-pwanikisya, 7.-pwanika-pwanika, 8.-pwanikana)
go into exile to, Bantu bapenzegwa mumanyika ookwabo, bapwanikila mumasi aambi. = People tortured in their own countries have gone into exile into other countries.

bubble up, Meenda apwapwama kuzwa mukantolo. = The water was bubbling up out of the spring. (1.-pwapwamwa, 2.-pwapwamide, 3.-pwapwamuzya, 4.-pwapwamina, 5.-pwapwaminalyo, 6.-pwapwamisya, 7.-pwapwama-pwapwama)
pour out very little, Kopwasya meenda masyoonto mucisyu. = Pour a little water into the relish. Also: -pyasya

be crushed, Mwana naaloka mucisamu, wawida abbwe nkabela mutwe wakwe wapwasyauka. = When the child dropped frons the tree, he fell on a rock and as a result his head was crushed. crush, Madeede onse abolede ndaapwasyaula akwaasowa. = I smashed all the tomatoes which were rotten and threw them away. (1.-pwasyaulwa, 2.-pwasyawide, 3.-pwasyauzya, 4.-pwasyawida, 5.-pwasyamwidalyo, 6.-pwasyaulisya, 7.pwasyaula-pwasyaula, 8.-pwasyaulana) Also: -pozaula, -fwunzauka, -fwunzaula.

(1.-pwasyulwa, 2.-pwaswide, 3.-pwasyuzya, 4.-pwaswida, 5.-pwaswidalyo, 6.-pwasyulisya, 7.-pwasyula-pwasyula, 8.-pwasyulana)

be smashed, Madeede ngobabikkide musaka apwasyuuka oonse. All the tomatoes which you had put in the sack are crushed. (2.-pwasyuukide, 3.-pwasyuukizya, 4.-pwa-syuukila, 5.-pwasyuukilalyo, 6.-pwasyuukisya, 7.-pwasyuukapwasyuuka)

pour as rain, Mvwula yapwatamuna kuwa sunu. = Today it rained heavily. Also: -soomoka (1.-pwatamunwa, 2.-pwatamwide, 3.-pwatamuzya, 4.-pwatamwida, 5.-pwatamwidalyo, 6.-pwatamumisya, 7.-pwatamuna-pwatamuna)

open eyes wide, Wakaapwatula meso kayanda kufwa. She opened her eyes wide when she was about to die. Kapongo kadinwa kalapwatula meso. = When a goat is choked it opens its eyes wide. (1.-pwatulwa, 2.-pwatwide, 3.-pwatuzya, 4.-pwatwida, 5.-pwatwidalyo, 6.-pwatulisya, 7.-pwatula-pwatula, 8.-pwatwidana) Also: -bwazula.

look blankly as a half-wit, be stunned, Mundanda naakali kubetekwa, wakapwauka biyo nkaambo wakajana mulandu. When Mundanda was judged, he just looked stunned because he was found guilty. (1.-pwaukwa, 2.-pwaukide, 4.-pwaukila, 5.-pwaukilalyo, 6.-pwaukisya, 7.-pwauka-pwauka)
be in a stunned state, rt. pwauka, Nitwali mumuswaangano kunyina ncindali kukonzya kwaambaula, ndalipwaukide. When we were in the meeting I was not able to say anything, I was blank in mind.

shatter, smash, crush, *Wacipwaya cibiya cabacembele mwana.* = The child smashed the pot of the old woman. *Mubwa ulakonzya kupwaya tunwe twamwana.* = A dog can crush a child's fingers. *Bazyali bapwaya mabwe kucikolo.* = The parents are crushing stones at the school. (1.-pwaigwa, 2.-pwayide, 3.-pwaizya, 4.-pwayila, 5.-pwayilalyo, 6.-pwayisya, 7.-pwaya-pwaya.)
  • slap one's face, *Wakamupwaya lubayi.* = She slapped his face.
  • drink beer continuously, Nakumulomo uile kupwaya makoko mazuba oonse. = Nakumulomo is just drinking beer continually every day.
  • ritually blessing of the grave by breaking a gourd, help one recover by traditional ritual when one has had a shock, *Muntu afwa, usyi nguupwaya cinkuli aasidwa cuumbwe.* = When a person dies, it is the father who breaks the gourd at the place where the grave is to be dug. *Mutinta naakali muntenda yamumugwagwa, bakamupwaila cinkuli kutegwa abe kabotu.* = When Mutinta was in a road accident they broke the gourd on her for her to recover from the shock.
  • throw oneself on the ground in grief, *Banyina Jonasi bakatalika kulila kumwi babuwa-buwa bbokesi mwaakabede akulipwaya mizinga.* = The mother of Jonas began to cry while stroking the coffin where he was and flinging herself hard against the ground.
  • make a journey, *Sunu ulajana kana kaniini kayabupwaya misinzo yakalampa nkalekale, akasako mumaanza nkuya kukusenga bukoko.* = Nowadays you find a young child going on journeys which are long, with a staff in his hand, going to drink beer.
  • force mouth open by pressing jaws, *Chipwetenge wakamupwaya ntwino mwana.* = Chipwetenge forced the child's mouth open.
  • crush, make into powder, *Musilisi wakapwaya mapiilusi kutegwa mulwazi anywe kabotu.* = The doctor crushed the pills so that the patient could drink them easily. (1.-pwayigwa, 2.-pwayide, 3.-pwazya, 4.-pwayila, 5.-pwailalyo, 6.-pwayisya, 7.-pwaya-pwaya, 8.-pwayana) Also: -kusa

slap continually, *Wisi Mutinta wakayumuka akumupwayaula mabayi.* = The father of Mutinta arose and slapped her about. (1.-pwayaulwa, 2.-pwayawide, 3.-pwayauzya, 4.-pwayawida, 5.-pwayawidalyo, 6.-pwayaulisya, 7.-pwayaula-pwayaula, 8.-pwayaulana)

move about lustfully, *Wakali kupwenauka abasankwa mbuli kuti kuli wakayasaula bbakumba lyabasankwa.* = She was going about with boys lustfully as if she had been tattooed with the sex charm for boys. (1.-pwenaukwa, 2.-pwenaukide, 3.-pwenaukizya, 4.-pwenaukila, 5.-pwenaukilalyo, 6.-pwenaukisya, 7.-pwenauka-pwenauka, 8.-pwenausyanya)

behave in childish way, *Koleka kupwepwenyana kuseka mbuli mwana.* = Stop laughing in an immature way like a child. (1.-pwpwenyanwa, 2.-pwepwenyene, 3.-pwepwenyeka, 4.-pwepwenyanina, 5.-pwepwenyaninalyo, 6.-pwepwenyanisya, 7.-pwepwenyana-pwepwenyana, 8.-pwepwenyaninana)

run about, *Bana balapwilimbilika anze mvwula noiwa.* = The children run about outside when the rain falls. Also: -pwimbwilika.

rush out of a burrow, *Nitwali kusya, mbeba zinji zyapwilipwida musyokwe, nkabela twajaya yomwe biyo.* = When we were digging, many rats rushed out of the burrow, but then we killed only one. (1.-pwilipwidwa, 2.-pwilipwidide, 3.-pwilipwidizya, 4.-pwilipwidila, 5.-pwilipwidilalyo, 6.-pwilipwidisya, 7.-pwilipwida-pwilipwida, 8.-pwilipwidilana)
(1.-pwilimbilika, 2.-pwilimbilikide, 3.-pwilimbilikizya, 4.-pwilimbilikila, 5.pwilimbilikilalyo, 6.-pwilimbilikisya, 7.-pwilimbilikapwilimbilika, 8.-pwilimbilikisyanya)

run about naked, *Bana baniini balayanda kupwimbwilika noiwa mvwula.* = Little children like to run about naked in the rain. (1.-pwimbwilikwa, 2.-pwimbwilikide, 3.-pwimbwilikizya, 4.-pwimbwilikila, 5.-pwimbwilikilalyo, 6.-pwimbwilikisya, 7.-pwimbwilika-pwimbwilika, 8.-pwimbwilikizyanya)
squeeze through, *Cakaceya cibaka mpakapwina.* There was no place for him to squeeze through.

sip, *Kopwita musamu ooyu, noulula ulayumya.* Sip this medicine, though it be bitter you will be healed. (1.-pwitwa, 2.-pwitide, 3.-pwitya, 4.-pwitila, 5.-pwitilalyo, 6.-pwitisya, 7.-pwita-pwita, 8.-pwitilana) Also: -sipa, -vwipa.
sipping slowly, *Sicibende wakalindila kaindi kasyoonto buyo mpongo nozyakali kupwita-pwita.* = Sicibende waited only a little, while the goats were drinking.

burn, be scalded, be hot, *Ndapya mulilo nindali kusola kuliyanikizya akaambo kampeyo njindamvwide.* = I was burnt when I was trying to warm myself up because of the cold which I felt. (1.-pizyigwa, 2.-pyide, 3.-pizya, 4.-pida, 5.-pidalyo, 6.-pisya, 7.-pyaapya.)
  • desire strongly, *Moyo wangu ulapya kuti kubota ndaba dokotela.* = My heart strongly desires that it would be a good thing for me to be a doctor.

sweep, *Kamufwambaana kupyaanga acibuye nkaambo beenzu balaboola sunu.* = Hurry and sweep the floor because visitors are coming today. Also: -kukula. (1.-pyaangwa, 2.-pyaangide, 3.-pyaangizya, 4.-pyaangila, 5.-pyaangilalyo, 6.-pyaangisya 7.-pyaanga-pyaanga, 8.-pyaangana)

wet one's tongue, *Mubila wakali kunga ayeeya kwaambaula utaanguna kupyala mulaka ciindi coonse kubombeka milomo yakwe yalo yakali kutuba mbuli kuti njamuntu wafweba lubanje, naa wafwa nzala.* Mubila when he thought of speaking he used to wet his tongue all the time to soften his lips which were white like those of a man who was smoking dagga or was dying with the hunger. (1.-pyalwa, 2.-pyalide, 3.-pyazya, 4.-pyalila, 5.-pyalilayo, 6.-pyalisya, 7.-pyala-pyala, 8.-pyalilana)

pour out a very small amount, *Kopyasya tubisi kutegwa mwana alye kabotu ceele.* Pour out a little of the sour milk so that the child can eat the porridge easily. *Kopyasya buyo meenda masyoonto mucisyu.* Pour only a little water into the relish. (1.-pyasyigwa, 2.-pyasyide, 3.-pyasyizya 4.-pyasyila, 5.-pyasyilalyo, 6.-pyasyisya, 7.-pyasya-pyasya, 8.-pyasyilana)

give orders, command, *Beembezi bapati mbabapyolola bana baniini nobaunka kukweembela.* The older herds are the ones who instruct the young ones when they go to herd. blow as a musical instrument, or train or whistle, Mooye, upyoola mweembo murnanda. An initiate is blowing a musical horn in the seclusion hut. explain fully, Banene tabajisi maanu akupyoolola makani alukwato. = The old man has not the intelligence to explain clearly about marriage. (1.-pyoololwa, 2.-pyoolwede, 3.-pyoolozya, 4.-pyoololela, 5.-pyoololelalyo, 6.-pyoololesya, 7.-pyoolola-pyoolola, 8.-pyoololana)

rub, Mbubakamanina kulipyotola milomo bakafwa. When they had finished rubbing their own lips they died.

devastate, loot, Basilumamba bakacisaala cisi ca Chipembele. = The warriors destroyed the land of Chipembele. (1.-saalwa, 2.-saalide, 3.-saazya, 4.-saalila, 5.-saalilalyo, 6.-saalisya, 7.-saala-saala, 8.-saalizyanya)

  • move as wings, Mutinta wakali kuteelela kulyatauka kwabayuni akusaala kwamababa alimwi amankotyo. = Mutinta was sensitive to the steps of birds and the sound of wings and the droppings.

incite to fight, Basankwa basaalizya sulwe. = The boys set the dogs after the hare. Mutinta wakamusaalizya babwa munene acaali. = Mutinta set the dogs on the old man deliberately. Musankwa uutalomenye usaalizya bana kuti kabalwana. A bad boy encourages children to fight. (1.-saalizyigwa, 2.-saalizyide, 3.-saalizya, 4.-saalizyizya, 5.-saalizyizyalyo, 6.-saalizyisya, 7.-saalizyasaalizya, 8.-saalizyanya) Also: -sibilizya,-soozya, -sweezya, -usilizya.
  • condemn, Muli zyoonse nzyotumvwa anzyotubona cintu cakutaanguna nkutungumana, nkumena mate. Ino mbubona akubangwa kuli mu Butonga. Utaide kukusaalizya, kukusampula kotanakubuzisya kuti kwaamba nzi alimwi kwakatalika buti. Among all the things that you hear and see, the first thing is to reflect, to swallow spittle. Now it is the same as regards the custom of knocking out the front teeth among the Batonga. Just don't support its condemnation before you have investigated carefully what it means and how did it begin.

be seated aside, Chindolo naakabona kuti makani ngobakali kukanana taalomenye, wakazwa waakusaama alikke. When Chindolo saw that the matter they were discussing was not honest, he went aside and sat alone. (1.-saamwa, 2.-saamene, 3.-saamya, 4.-saamina, 5.-saaminalyo, 6.-saamisya, 7.-saama-saama, 8.-saaminana)
rebel, Kuti bana batusaandila, inga Leza wabauma muluso. = If the childen rebel against us, God will beat them with a cane

be first to, Ndakasaanguna kunjila munanda masiku. = I was the first one to enter the house at night. Mweemba nguwasaanguna kusika kucikolo. Mweemba was the first to arrive at the school. (1.-saangunwa, 2.-saangunide, 3.-saangunya, 4.-saangunina, 5.-saanguninalyo, 6.-saangunisya, 7.-saanguna-saanguna, 8.-saanguninana)
wait a while, Saansina ndibabuzye. = Wait a while, let me ask them first. (2.-saansinide, 3.-saansinya, 4.-saansinina, 5.-saansininalyo, 6.-saansinisya, 7.-saansina-saansina)
spread out over, Basimunyewu bakasaantika koonse-koonse kuyandaula mumoma. = The black ants spread out everywhere looking for white ants.

spread out, Inkuku zyasaantikizyanya kuya musyokwe kuyandaula cakulya. The chickens scattered off into the bush searching for food. Bakabona mpumba yabantu kaisaantikizyanya kuya kusyokwe kuyandaula mwana. = They saw a crowd of people spreading off into the bush looking for the child. Also: -sansala. (1.-saantikwa, 2.-saantikide, 3.-saantikizya, 4.-saantikila, 5.-saantikilalyo, 6.-saantikisya, 7.-saantika-saantika, 8.-saantikizyanya)

lie with arms or legs outstretched, Mumulange nkwaasaanyana maanza kubee wafwa kale. = Look at how she she is lying with hands outstretched as if she is already dead. Kacula kaile kusaanyana nikalyatwa cikkocci. The frog lies spread out when it was crushed by a scotch-cart. (1.-saanyanwa, 2.-saanyene, 3.-saanyika, 4.-saanyanina, 5.-saanyaninalyo, 6.-saanyanisya, 7.-saanyana-saanyana, 8.-saanyaninana)
lie outstretched, Wakajana Tiki usaanyene buya kuyota dilo lyakali kuyaka kapati. He found Tiki lying outstretched warming himself at the big fire which was burning very well.

stretch out limbs or open hand with fingers spread out, Kosaanyika maboko kutegwa uyote kabotu. = Spread out your arms so that you warm yourself properly. Bavwimi bakasaanyika kasulwe kuti kayume. = The hunters opened up the hare and stretched it out to dry.
incite, Wakali kusaazila nombe yamuntu. He was setting the dogs on someone's cattle. Also: -sibilizya

incite dogs to attack, "Isaa! Isaa!" Wakasaazya Mubekwabekwa." = "Isaa! Isaa!" Mubekwabekwa incited the dogs. (1.-saazyigwa, 2.-saazyide, 3.-saazya, 4.-saazyizya, 5.-saazyizyalyo, 6.-saazyisya, 7.-saazyasaazya, 8.-saazyanya)

make a noise, Basicikolo bakali kusaba. = The pupils were making noise. Koumuna ino, wasaba kapati. = Be quiet, you make too much noise. (1.-sabwa, 2.-sabide, 3.-sabya, 4.-sabila, 5.-sabilalyo, 6.-sabisya, 7.-saba-saba, 8.-sabilana) Also: -sabila.
  • cut off, as branches for firewood; *Kamusaba zisamu kumuunda, nkuni zyaceya.* = Cut off some branches in the field, the firewood is insufficient.
  • cut up as meat, *Mweendi wakamupa mesi akumugwasya kufwunda lubondwe akusaba nyama.* = Mweendi gave him a knife to skin the deer and to cut up the meat

disimprove in appearance, *Ooyu musankwa wakali mupaale kaindi, pesi mazubaano wakasabaana.* = This man was a neat dresser long ago but now he has disimproved. (1.-sabaanwa, 2.-sabaanide, 3.-sabaanya, 4.-sabaanina, 5.-sabaaninalyo, 6.-sabaanisya, 7.-sabaana-sabaana, 8.-sabaanizyanya) Also: -sauka.
disgrace another, *Ooyu mwana wandisabaanya akati kabantu.* = This child has disgraced me among the people. Also: -sampuzya.

move from one point to another, *Eeci catugwasya kutasabaila oku akooku akusowelwa muzeezo waciiyo kumasimpilo.* = This helps us not to be moving from one point to another and in the end to loose the thought of the lesson. Also: -yabaana. (1.-sabailwa, 2.-sabailide, 3.-sabaizya, 4.-sabailila, 5.-sabaililalyo, 6.-sabailisya, 7.-sabaila-sabaila, 8.-sabailizyanya)

eat without chewing, *Mudaala uunyina menyo ulasabanta munsale acinsiniini.* = The old man without teeth crushes the sugar cane with the gums. (1.-sabantwa, 2.-sabantide, 3.-sabantya, 4.-sabantila, 5.-sabantilalyo, 6.-sabantisya, 7.-sabanta-sabanta, 8.-sabantana) Also: -sabata
  • crush, hit hard, *Citima cakazisabanta nombe zyokwa Sialyoonda.* = The train crushed the cattle of Sialyoonda.

hit hard, beat hard on one spot, *Wakatalika kusabanya mpemo yamubwa limwi yafwunzauka.* = He started hitting the dog hard on the nose until it finally crushed. Also: -sabaula. (1.-sabanyigwa, 2.-sabanyide, 3.-sabanyizya, 4.-sabanyina, 5.-sabanyinalyo, 6.-sabanyisya, 7.-sabanya-sabanya, 8.-sabanyaninana)

eat without chewing, bolt food, *Baneene balasabata kulya akaambo kakubula menyo.* = My grandmother eats without chewing because of having no teeth. Also: -sabanta. (1.-sabatwa, 2.-sabatide, 3.-sabatya, 4.-sabatila, 5.-sabatilalyo, 6.-sabatisya, 7.-sabata-sabata, 8.-sabatana)
  • crush, *Kamusabata mutwe wanombe ujikwe.* = Crush the head of the cow so that it be cooked. Also: -sabanta.

be cut up, be broken, be crushed, *Kano kaindi nyika yasabauka yakwamauka mbuli nyama yarņombe yagonkwa keembe.* = In a short time the land was crushed and cut up like a cow that has been axed. (1.-sabaukwa, 2.-sabaukide, 3.-sabaukizya, 4.-sabaukila, 5.-sabaukilalyo, 6.-sabaukisya, 7.-sabauka-sabauka)

hit hard, *Ndakasabaula kayuni abbwe lyamalekani.* = I struck the bird with a stone from the catapult. (1.-sabaulwa, 2.-sabawide, 3.-sabauzya, 4.-sabawida, 5.-sabawidalyo, 6.-sabaulisya, 7.-sabaula-sabaula, 8.-sabaulana) Also: -sabanya.
  • cut into pieces, dissect, *Baama basabaula myungu yakujika.* = Mother is cutting the pumpkins into pieces for cooking. Also: -kankaula, - pompoola.
  • outline points, *Taakali kuyeeya kuti musimbi mbwabuka inga ulakonzya kusabaula boobu twaambo tuli mbuli bwatootu.* = He did not think that a girl could arise who would be able to pick out the main points such as these.

ridicule or make fun off one another, Kusaanguna atwiiye ijwi eli lya *'bujwanyina'*. Kujwana nkokuti kutukilana, kapati lyaamba kusabauzyanya. First of all let us learn about this word *'bujwanyina'*. Kujwana means to insult one another, but it especially means to make fun of one another. (1.-sabauzyigwa, 2.-sabauzyenye, 3.-sabauzyizya, 4.-sabauzyizyanya, 5.-sabauzyizyanyalyo, 6.-sabauzyanyizyisya, 7.-sabauzyanya-sabauzyanya, 8.-sabauzyanya)

be scattered about, rt. sabaana, Cilimo wakali kunga aboola matende asasa kuyaswa ziyasabavwimi azincenya zyakapya zyakali kusabeene muluya. In the dry season he used to come home with his feet pierced with burnt thorn-fruits which were scattered all over the burnt bush. Mikowa yakali kusabeene pele bakali kuzyibene, tiiyakali kusowana. Although people of the same clan were scattered far and wide they knew one another, they did not disown one another. (1.-sabaanyizyigwa, 2.-sabeene, 3.-sabaanya, 4.-sabaanizyila, 5.-sabaanizyilalyo, 6.-sabaanizyisya, 7.-sabeene, 8.-sabaanizyanya)

make noise to annoy another, pester, rt. -saba, Kamuleka kuyoba, mwandisabila ndabala. = Stop shouting, you are too noisy for me, I am reading. (1.-sabilwa, 2.-sabilide, 3.-sabizya, 4.-sabilila, 5.-sabililalyo, 6.-sabilisya, 7.-sabila-sabila, 8.-sabilana)
  • chop for, Bana bandisabila masamu mumuunda. = The children are cutting trees for me in the field.

set dogs on, Bana balikusabilizya babwa kumpongo zya bantu. The children are setting the dogs on the goats of the people. (1.-sabilizyigwa, 2.-sabilizyide, 3.-sabilizya, 4.-sabilizyizya, 5.-sabilizyizyalyo, 6.-sabilizyisya, 7.-sabilizya-sabilizya, 8.-sabilizyanya) Also: -siilizya, -sibilizya.

move away to the back, as children, Bana bakasabuka mulilo niwakayaka kapati. The children went away to the back when the fire blazed up. (1.-sabukwa, 2.-sabukide, 3.-sabukizya, 4.-sabukila, 5.-sabukilalyo, 6.-sabukisya, 7.-sabuka-sabuka, 8.-sabukisyanya) Also: -sosoloka.

jokingly provoke, as in 'joking relationship', Mungoni wali kusabula adilwe lya Mubemba. = A MuNgoni has been verbally attacking a MuBemba at a Bemba funeral (according to the custom of the joking relationship between the tribes.)
  • make fun, Ndali kusabula buyo. = I was only making fun. (1.-sabulwa, 2.-sabwide, 3.-sabwizya, 4.-sabwida, 5.-sabwidalyo, 6.-sabulisya, 7.-sabulasabula, 8.-sabulana)

cut up, as meat into pieces, Mulamu, kosabuula mutwe wampongo ujikwe. My in-law, cut the head of a goat into pieces so that it can be cooked. Also: -sabaula. (1.-sabuulwa, 2.-sabwiide, 3.-sabuuzya, 4.-sabwiida, 5.-sabwiidalyo, 6.-sabuulisya, 7.-sabuula-sabuula, 8.-sabuulana)

sign a document, discharge as from hospital, (ety. Eng.) Sena walusaina kale lugwalo nduwalemba cifwumofwumo? = Have you already signed the letter which you wrote this morning? Musilisi wakamuka kumusaina mulwazi nkaambo bulwazi bwakaciliko. = The doctor was slow to discharge the patient because the disease was still there. (1.-sainwa, 2.-sainide, 3.-sainizya, 4.-sainina, 5.-saininalyo, 6.-sainisya, 7.-saina-saina, 8.-sainana) Also: -simba
  • sacrifice oneself, Noyakapya nanda, banyina bakalisaina kunjila mukati kuvwuna mwana wakali koona. = When the house was burning, the mother sacrificed herself by going inside to save the child who was sleeping. Also: -sungula.

be discharged from hospital, Musyoonto wangu wakasainwa kuzwa mucibbadela jilo. = My young brother /sister was discharged from hospital yesterday. Mulwazi wakasainwa katani-ngapona. = The patient was discharged before s/he was healed.

be driven into doing something, Ncinzi candisaka, icandisontomona kuti mboole? = What drove me to do this, that has brought misery to me that I should have come? (1.-sakwa, 2.-sakide, 3.-sakizya, 4.-sakila, 5.-sakilalyo, 6.-sakilisya, 7.-saka-saka, 8.-sakilana)
  • stir up water when fishing, Bamacembele bakajaya nswi zinji nibakamana kusaka meenda. = The elderly women killed many fish when they stirred up the water.

spread out, permeate, Musimbi walumwa nzoka wazimba mubili oonse nkaambo busaki bwasakamina. = The girl who was bitten by a snake became swollen all over the body because the venom spread. Ooku kuyoowa kwalufwu bakakukona bana abana babazyukulu limwi cakaide kusakamina kubulowa amumaanu a Batonga boonse. = The children inherited this fear of death down to the children of the grandchildren until it just permeated the blood and intelligence of all the Batonga people. (1.-sakaminwa, 2.-sakamide, 3.-sakamizya, 4.-sakaminina, 5.-sakamininalyo, 6.-sakaminisya, 7.-sakamina-sakamina, 8.-sakaminizyanya)

have sour or bitter taste, Bukoko busakamuka tabukondi bantu. = The beer which is sour does not please people. Mabisi asakamuka. = The sour milk has gone bad. Eeyi misamu nokuba kuti yakali kusakamuka wakainywa. = Even though these medicines were bitter he drank them. (1.-sakamukwa, 2.-sakamukide, 3.-sakamusya, 4.-sakamukila, 5.-sakamukilalyo, 6.-sakamukisya, 7.-sakamuka-sakamuka) Also: -nyemuka.
  • be refreshed, Naakamana kufweba wakaliinza akumvwa mubili wakwe woonse wakasakamuka, wakanyanyaala. = When he had finished smoking he was refreshed and felt his whole body come alive, he became very sensitive.

pull out, as one spear, Kosakamuna sumo undipe. = Draw one spear from the quiver and give it to me. Also: -sokomona, -fwumuna. (1.-sakamunwa, 2.-sakamwide, 3.-sakamuzya, 4.-sakamwida, 5.-sakamwidalyo, 6.-sakamunisya, 7.-sakamuna-sakamuna, 8.-sakamwidana)
  • clean one's gums and cheeks of food (not with tongue), Amutupe mabisi, tuyanda kulisakamuna mukanwa. = Give us some sour milk we want to cleanse our mouths.
  • change taste for the better, make one saliviate, Mabisi andisakamuna mukanwa. = The sour milk has pleasantly changed the taste in my mouth. Wakajana kuti bwaawo bwanyama busakamuna mate mukanwa. = She found that there was meat which makes one saliviate. Kamuleta nyama, tuyanda kulisakamuna nkaambo twalikulisya cisyumani lyoonse. = Bring meat, we want to enjoy the taste because we have been using vegetables as relish all the time.

make desireable or pleasant to the taste, rt. -sakamuna, Candisakamusya mukanwa mbusiikka mbundalya. = What makes my mouth saliviate is the busiika which I ate. Zintu zinona zisakamusya mate. = Tasty things make one's mouth water. (Yeast = cisakamusya cinkwa a bukoko.) (1,-sakamusyigwa, 2.-sakamusyizye, 3.-sakamuzya, 4.-sakamusyizya, 5.-sakamusyizyalyo, 6.-sakamusyisya, 7.-sakamusya-sakamusya, 8.-sakamusyanya)

go off, Moonde wakasakana. = Moonde went far away. Twakazikusakana jilo nitwaali kukuvwima. = We wandered far off yesterday when we were hunting. Bamwi bantu bakazwa, pesi bamwi tiibakasakana, bakaimina buyo kulaale kutegwa bateelele kuzwangana kwasibbuku amwana wakwe. = Some went out, but some did not go far, they stood at a distance so that they could hear the quarrel between the headman and his son. (1.-sakanwa, 2.-sakene, 3.-sakanya, 4.-sakanina, 5.-sakaninalyo, 6.-sakanisya, 7.-sakana-sakana, 8.-sakanizyanya)

pick one's teeth, Naakamana kulya nyama, wakatalika kulisakanuna. = When he had finished eating meat, he began to pick his teeth. (1.-sakanunwa, 2.-sakanwide, 3.-sakanuzya, 4.-sakanwida, 5.-sakanwidalyo, 6.-sakanunisya, 7.-sakanuna-sakanuna, 8.-sakanunana)

make mouth water, Alanga mukaintu nkwakomoona zyeeyazyeeya zyamyungu, wamvwa kwasakasa mate mukanwa. = When he looked at the woman breaking off pieces of pumpkins, his mouth began to water. (1.-sakaswa, 2.-sakaside, 3.-sakasizya, 4.-sakasila, 5.-sakasilalyo, 6.-sakasisya, 7.-sakasa-sakasa, 8.-sakasizyanya)
  • flow freely, Moombe mubutu wakabbalamukila kuli banyina nkwaakali kudunta nkolo zyabanyina kuti mukupa ufwambaane kusakasa. = The unweaned calf trotted over to its mother where it was pushing at the teats of the mother so that the milk would flow freely.

be scattered as seeds, be spread over, Basimunyewu basakatika nanda yoonse. = The ants are spread over the whole house. Tutasakatili casimweendanzila. = Let us not be scattered like the traveller. Also: -saantika, -bumbilila, -milila. (1.-sakatikwa, 2.-sakatikide, 3.-sakatikizya, 4.-sakatikila, 5.-sakatikilalyo, 6.-sakatikisya, 7.-sakatika-sakatika, 8.-sakatikisyanya)

be far removed, rt. -sakana, Mizeezo yangu yalisakene, ncindatali kwaambaula. = My thoughts were far off, that is why I do not talk. (1.-sakanwa, 2.-sakene, 3.-sakanya, 4.-sakanina, 5.-sakaninalyo, 6.-sakanisya, 7.-sakenesakene, 8.-sakanizyanya)

glue or stick into, as a spear or hoe head, Mudaala wasakila masumo one. = The old man stuck the heads of four spears into their shafts. Also: -kwiikka. (1.-sakilwa, 2.-sakilide, 3.-sakizya, 4.-sakilila, 5.-sakililalyo, 6.-sakilisya, 7.-sakila-sakila, 8.-sakililana)
  • insert false teeth, Mazubaano bacembele bakabangidwe balayanda kusakila menyo ankaya. = Nowadays the old women whose teeth were knocked out wish to have ivory teeth inserted.
  • put on clothes, Kosakila cibaki eeci cilakweelela. = Put on this shirt it suits you. Also: -sama, -goga. (In Ila -sakila means to adorn oneself as opposed to -sama which simply means to dress oneself)

cut hair with scissors, shave hair as with razor, Kamundisakula masusu. = Cut my hair. Bakaintu bakaleka kusakulwa minkulu. = Women have stopped having their heads shaved. (1.-sakulwa, 2.-sakwide, 3.-sakuzya, 4.-sakwida, 5.-sakwidalyo, 6.-sakulisya, 7.-sakula-sakula, 8.-sakulana)
  • comb hair, Kamulisakula masusu, alipulungene. = Comb your hair, it is untidy. Also: -kamuna.
  • weed, Bamwi balimi balamuka kusakula mumyuunda yabo. = Some farmers are late in weeding their fields. Also: -limina.

be undressed, Zikobela zyabo zyasakunuka. Their clothes came off their bodies. (1.-sakununwa, 2.-sakunukide/-sakunwide, 3.-sakunuzya, 4.-sakunukila/-sakunwida, 5.-sakunukilalyo /- sakunwidalyo, 6.-sakunukisya, 7.-sakunuka-sakunuka, 8.-sakununana)
shout with joy, Ino wasakwa nzi ncookkomana boobo? = What makes you shout for joy that you are so happy? (2.-sakide, 3.-sakizya, 4.-sakilila, 5.-sakililalyo, 6.-sakisyigwa, 7.-sakwa-sakwa)

weed, as in a field, rt. sakula, Kosakwida mapopwe mumbewu. Weed the maize in the garden. Wakabyala akusakwida kabotu muunda ngwaakamupede wisizyala. = She sowed and weeded carefully the field which she had been given by her father-in-law. Bansaku bakaluujisi kusakwida. = The weeders were busy weeding. (1.-sakwida, 2.-sakwide, 3.-sakwizya 4.-sakwidila, 5.-sakwidilalyo, 6.-sakwidisya, 7.-sakwida-sakwida, 8.-sakwidana) Also: -limina.

pick, choose, Ndakasala kale musimbi wakukwata. I have already chosen a girl to marry. Ndakasala kuunka ku Monze muciindi cakuya ku Choma. I decided to go to Monze instead of going to Choma. (1.-salwa, 2.-salide, 3.-salizya, 4.-salila, 5.-salilalyo, 6.-salisya, 7.-sala-sala, 8.-salana) Also: -nomona, -laula.
  • crush a louse, Bacembele bakalikusala njina mucipaya cabo. = The old woman was killing lice in her skin skirt.

be clean, Eeci cisani cilasalala. This cloth is clean. (1.-salalwa, 2.-salalide, 3.-salazya, 4.-salalila, 5.-salalilayo, 6.-salalisya, 7.-salala-salala, 8.-salazyanya)
  • have light-coloured skin, be fair, Moombela wakakwata musimbi uusalala. = Moombela married a light-skinned girl.
  • be bright, Twatalika Iweendo Iwesu nikwasalala kujwe. We started our journey when it was becoming bright in the east.
  • be innocent, Muntu ngubanjizya muntolongo ulasalala, takwe akabi. = The person whom they jailed is innocent, he is without fault.
be bright, Mwezi wakali kuyanda kubbila kumbo, akwalo kujwe kwakalisalalide kale. The moon was about to sink in the west, and to the east it was already bright.

• be clear, Tiicakandisalalila mbwaakapegwa mulandu mwanaangu munkuta. = It was not clear to me how my son was sentenced in court. Wakajana ciindi cakubuzya zimwi zintu zyatakali kumusalalila. = He found time to ask about certain things which were not clear to him.
  • be clean, Eeci cisani casalalilalyo, mutaciindululi kucisanzya. = This cloth is spotless, don't wash it again.
  • become bright at dawn, Mbukwasalalila buyo kujwe, twatalika Iweendo Iwesu. As soon as it dawned, we started our journey.
be very bright, Nibakamana kusanzya zisani zyakasalalisya nkaambo meenda akali kukasaala. = When they had finished washing the clothes they were very bright as the water was warm.

lie on one's back, recline, Muntu wakolwa bukoko tayelede kusalama aona. = A drunk person should not sleep on his/her back. *Wasalama ulilede a bulo, watalika kuyeeya zyoonse zyalikucitika masiku.* = He lay back, lying on the bed, he began to think of all that had happened during the night. (1.-salamikwa, 2.-saleme, 3.-salamika, 4.-salamina, 5.-salaminalyo, 6.-salamisya, 7.-salama-salama, 8.-salaminana) Also: -gadama, -gandama, -ngandama.

cause to lie face upwards, throw down on the back to the ground, *Kamumusalamika mwana kuti ayoye kabotu.* = Put the child lying face upwards so that it breathes properly. (1.-salamikwa, 2.-salamikide, 3.-salamika, 4.-salamikila, 5.-salamikilalyo, 6.-salamikisya, 7.-salamika-salamika, 8.-salamikana)
  • turn upside down or inside out, *Eezi mpende kamuzisalamika buya kuziyanika.* = Turn these bream fish upside down to dry them. *Kolisalamika jamba tubikke vwili lipya.* = Turn the plough upside down so that we put on a new wheel. Also: -sandamika.

be overturned, Mootokala wasalamuka niwauma cuumbusu. = The car overturned when it hit an ant-hill. (1.-salamukwa, 2.-salamukide, 3.-salamusya, 4.-salamukila, 5.-salamukilalyo, 6.-salamukisya, 7.-salamuka-salamuka, 8.-salamukizyanya.) Also: -sandamuka, -bbindamuka.

turn over, *Bakai-salamuna nzoka kuti ilibonye ada.* = They turned the snake upside down to also see the stomach. *Bakamusalamuna muntu* *kuti babone naa wafwida lyo.* = They turned the person over to see if s/he was really dead. (1.-salamunwa, 2.-salamwide, 3.-salamuzya, 4.-salamwida, 5.-salamwidalyo, 6.-salamunisya, 7.-salamunasalamuna, 8.-salamunana)

be discriminated against, Bantu basiya bakapenga mubuzike bwakudyaamininwa kwiinda mukusalana mubala. = Black people suffered in the oppression of slavery by being discriminted against because of colour. (1.-salanwa, 2.-salenye, 3.-salanya, 4.-salanina, 5.-salaninalyo, 6.-salanisya, 7.-salana-salana, 8.-salana)

delouse, pick out, select, *Ciindi cacifwumofwumo twakajana mucembele umwi usalangunya njina.* = We found a certain old woman delousing herself early in the morning. *Omu mucimvwule munanga wakali kusalangunya micelo akwiibikka mutulwi-tulwi.* = There in the shade the witchdoctor was picking out medicines and putting them in small heaps. Also: -ponyongola. (1.-salangunyizyigwa, 2.-salanguzyide, 3.-salangunyizya, 4.-salangunyizyila, 5.-salangunyizyilalyo, 6.-salangunyizyisya, 7.-salangunya-salangunya, 8.-salangunyana)

examine as before buying, pick out one from others, *Balikusalaula cakuula.* = They were choosing what to buy. *Kamusalaula zisani zibotu.* = Choose good clothes. (1.-salaulwa, 2.-salaulide, 3.-salauzya, 4.-salawida, 5.-salawidalyo, 6.-salaulisya, 7.-salaulasalalula, 8.-salaulana)

clean away, *Kamundisalazizya lubuwa nomutanaunka kucikolo* = Clear away the dirt for me from the courtyard before you go to school. (1.-salazizyilwa, 2.-salazizye, 3.-salazizyizya, 4.-salazizyila, 5.-salazizyilalyo, 6.-salazizyisya, 7.-salazizya-salazizya, 8.-salazizyanya) Also: -sansamwida.

cleanse, purify, Kamusalazya mpulungwido. = Clean the windows. (1.-salazyigwa, 2.-salazyide, 3.-salazyisya, 4.-salazyizya, 5.-salazyizyalyo, 6.-salazyisya, 7.-salazya-salazya, 8.-salazyanya) Also: -bosya.
  • cleanse widow or widower ritually, Mbaani basalazya mukamufwu? = Who will cleanse the widow? Juunza nguwakasalazya kuli muka Kaniini. = Juunza was the one who cleansed the wife of the late Kaniini.
  • cleanse village from defilement by the corpse of a visitor by killing an ox, Basibbuku bakaambila basazinyina muntu wakajaigwa kuti bafwambaane kusalazya munzi. The headman told the relatives of the murdered man that they should quickly purify the village.

be in the position of lying on one's back, rt. -salama, Bamwi koona inga boona busaleme. = Some when they sleep, sleep on their backs. (1.-salamwa, 2.-saleme, 3.-salamya, 4.-salamina, 5.-salaminalyo, 6.-salamisya, 7.-salemesaleme, 8.-salaminana)

choose for, rt. -sala, Bakandisalila ndyasyo zibotu ku Monze. = They chose nice sandals for me at Monze. Bantu babi bakandisalila mbuto mbi. = Bad people chose bad seed for me. (1.-salilwa, 2.-salilide, 3.-salizya, 4.-salilila, 5.-salililalyo, 6.-salilisya, 7.-salila-salila, 8.-salilana)

sort out, Basimbi basalulula zisani nzibasalide kale. = The girls are sorting out the clothes they had already chosen. Ndaasalulula kale mapopwe. = I have already sorted out the maize grains. (1.-salululwa, 2.-salulwide, 3.-saluluzya, 4.-salululila, 5.-salululilalyo, 6.-salululisya, 7.-salulula-salulula, 8.-salululana)
  • discriminate, Muleli wacisi tayelede kusalulula akati kamisyobo. = The leader of the country should not discriminate between the tribes.
dress oneself, wear, put on clothes, Kamusama zisani ziluzi kupobwe lyabwiinga. Wear suitable clothes for the wedding ceremony. (1.-samwa, 2.-samide, 3.-samya or

4.-samina, 5.-saminalyo, 6.-samisya, 7.-sama-sama, 8.-saminana.)
  • cut meat into strips, Baama basama nyama kunanda. Mother is cutting the meat into strips at the house. Also: -senda.

become cheerful, be pleased, Mukaintu ooyu ulasamauka naswaigwa beenzu. This woman becomes cheerful when she is visited by visitors. Mainza nokuba kuti wakali mubotu, taakali kuliyanda mbuli bamwi alimwi wakali kusamauka kubantu lyoonse. = Even though Mainza was beautiful, she was not selfish like others and again she was friendly towards people always. (1.-samausyigwa, 2.-samaukide, 3.-samaukizya,/-salamusya, 4.-samaukila, 5.-samaukilalyo, 6.-samaukisya, 7.-samauka-samauka, 8.-samausyanya) Also: -sangabala.

cause mouth to water, Cisyu cajikwa kabotu cilasamausya mukanwa. Relish which is well cooked gives a good taste to the mouth. Baliindene kapati bantu bamudolopo abantu bakumunzi kusamausya. People in towns are very different from those in villages in being friendly towards the people. (1.-samausyigwa, 2.-samausyide, 3.-samausyizya, 4.-samauzyizya, 5.-samauzyizyalyo, 6.-samausyisya, 7.-samausya-samausya, 8.-samausyanya)

wash oneself, Kosamba usalale. Wash yourself so that you be clean. Bana balasamba mumulonga. = The children are washing in the river. (1.-sambwa, 2.-sambide, 3.-sambya, /sambizya, 4.-sambila, 5.-sambilalyo, 6.-sambisya, 7.-samba-samba, 8.-sambilana.)
  • move, as child in womb, Mukaintu ulaa da naalikoona, mwana walikusamba mwida. = When the pregnant woman was asleep, the child moved in the womb. Also: -pituka mwida.
  • clean out, Mwakasamba mwida naakatombolwa. = The stomach was purified when he drank medicine which made him purge.
  • swim, Bana bakali kusamba mumulonga. = The children were swimming in the river. Also: -yamba, -saya. (-samba nkulubalwa = thread water; *-samba njumwa* = swim in deep water; *-samba bwiimvwi* = swim in a standing position,)
  • disown, Ndakusamba, tocili mukowaangu. = I disown you, you are no longer my relative. Mazubaano ndakamusamba, nsecimuzyi biya kuti nguni. = These days I have disowned her, I no longer know who she is.

trade, sell, negotiate, Ooyu usambala ngulube. = This one is selling a pig. Kamubweza matobo akusambala kudolopo. Take the matobo fruit and sell it in town. (1.-sambalwa, 2.-sambalide, 3.-samba-zya, 4.-sambalila, 5.-sambalilalyo, 6.-sambalisya, 7.-sambala-sambala, 8.-sambalana)

trade with something, Mebo nseli musimbi simeso-meso, naa caamba lufwu inga ndati nkafwe buyo kutali kuti nditalike kulisambazya. = I am not a like a prostitute, even if it means death, I would rather die than begin to trade myself.

washing with, rt. -samba, Insazi ezi zyakajisi mafwuta aku sambizya; impawo zyakajisi mafwuta akunana. These containers had oil for washing with, the (containers called) impawo had oil for anointing. (1.-sambizyigwa, 2.-sambizyide, 3.-sambizya, 4.-sambizyizya, 5.-sambizyizyalyo, 6.-sambizyisya 7.-sambizya-sambizya, 8.-sambizyanya)

lose power, as old medicine, Musamu wamwana wasambuluka taucibeleki pe. The child's medicine has expired. Also: -sampuka. (1.-sambulukwa, 2.-sambulukide, 3.-sambulusya, 4.-sambulukila, 5.-sambulukilalyo, 6.-sambulukisya, 7.-sambuluka-sambuluka, 8.-sambulukana)
  • unwind, Mukkwilo wangu wasambuluka. My whip has become unwound. Also: -zambuluka.

dress someone, rt. -sama, Kamumusamika zisani mwana. = Put clothes on the child. Banyina basamika mwana uuciswa. The mother is dressing the sick child. (1.-samikwa, 2.-samikide, 3.-samika, 4.-samikila, 5.-samikilayo, 6.-samikisya, 7.-samika-samika, 8.-samikana)

be dressed, Kamwale ulasyobwa kabotu-kabotu akusamikwa mpande kumutwe, malanda kumaulu, inkonokono, maingankwa alimwi abugwali-gwali bumwi. = The initiated girl is rubbed with oil and dressed with an mpande shell on the head, fibre leggings, armlets, shoulder cords and other ornaments.

rape, Mudaala mufwubafwuba wali kusampa kasimbi kacili kana. = The foolish old man was having sex with a young girl. Also: -jata (1.-sampwa, 2.-sampide, 3.-sampya, 4.-sampila, 5.-sampilalyo, 6.-sampisya, 7.-sampa-sampa, 8.-sampana)

insult, mock, ridicule, *Cilatondwa kusampaula uso.* = It is taboo to insult your father. *Wakandisampaula mubantu kaamba kuti ndakabbukilwa kumukaintu wakwe.* = He insulted me in public saying that I was caught committing adultery with his wife. Also: -kwama. (1.sampaulwa, 2.-sampawide, 3.-sampauzya, 4.-sampawida, 5.-sampawidalyo, 6.-sampaulisya, 7.-sampaula-sampaula, 8.-sampaulana)

be despised, *Wakasampuka mwami naakajanika kweenda amukamuntu.* = The chief was despised when he was found committing adultery with someone's wife. *Michelo kuti kotayandi kusampuka munsi amusimbi wako, koumuna.* = Michelo, if you do not want to be disgraced in front of your girl-friend, be quiet. (1.-sampukwa, 2.-sampukide, 3.-sampuzya, 4.-sampukila, 5.-sampukilalyo, 6.sampukisya, 7.-sampuka-sampuka)
  • lose power, effectiveness, as medicine, *Mucelo oyu wakasampuka.* = This medicine has lost its power. Also: -sambuluka.
  • become tasteless, lose flavour, *Musinza wankuku wasampuka nkuwatilwa meenda manji.* = This chicken soup has lost its taste as too much water has been added to it.

dishonour, destroy one's name, *Basicikolo basampula bayi babo mbabi.* = The pupils who destroy their teachers reputation are bad. *Eeci ncotalilemeki ulisampula buyo omwini.* = By dishonouring yourself like this you are only destroying your name. (1.-sampulwa, 2.-sampwide, 3.-sampuzya, 4.-sampwida, 5.-sampwidalyo, 6.-sampulisya, 7.-sampula-sampula, 8.-sampulana)
  • exhaust, as weeds in field, or birds eating grain or lack of crop rotation, *Casampula muunda wangu nkusyanga cisyango comwe kwamyaka minji.* = What has exhausted my field is planting one crop for many years. *Casampula muunda wangu ninsaku.* = What destroys my field are weeds.

ridicule, *Bamwi bamakaintu balasampuula bamalumi babo abuleya.* = Some wives ridicule their husbands in public. Also: -sampaula. (1.-sampuulwa, 2.-sampwiide, 3.-sampuuzya, 4.-sampwiida, 5.-sampwiidalyo, 6.-sampuulisya, 7.-sampuula-sampuula, 8.-sampuulana)

be a disgrace to, *Kukolwa kapati cilasampuzya akati kabantu.* = Getting exceedingly drunk destroys one's reputation among people. *Mutumbu, kubba kwako kwandisampuzya.* = Woman, your stealing is destroying my reputation. Also: -ubika. (1.-sampuzyigwa, 2.-sampuzyizye, 3.-sampuzya, 4.-sampuzyizya, 5.-sampuzyizyalyo, 6.-sampuzyisya, 7.-sampuzya-sampuzya, 8.-sampuzyanya)
  • spoil a field, rt. -sampula, *Kulima cisyango comwe amwaka amwaka mumuunda omwe nkusampuzya muunda.* = To plant the same crop year by year spoils a field.

satisfy one's longing for meat, *Inga mukanwa mwasamuka kuti walya nyama.* = When you eat meat, you satisfy the appetite for it. (2.-samukide, 3.-samusya, 4.-samukila, 5.-samukilalyo, 6.-samukisya, 7.-samukasamuka, 8.-samusyanya)

satisfy, *Inyama yalweela munyo ilasamuna.* = Meat which is seasoned with salt satisfies the appetite. *Sunu tuyanda kulisamuna nyama njibajika baama.* = Today we want to satisfy our longing for meat by eating the meat which mother has cooked. (1.-samunwa, 2.-samwide, 3.-samuzya, 4.-samwida, 5.-samwidalyo, 6.-samunisya, 7.-samuna-samuna, 8.-samunana)

undress, *Samununa cisani eeco, tacikweeleli.* = Take off that dress, it does not suit you. *Ulalisamununa zyakusama akutalika kutijaana kuya musyokwe.* = He takes off his clothes and runs into the bush. (1.-samununwa, 2.samunwide, 3.-samunuzya, 4.-samununina/-samunwida, 5.-samununinalyo,/-samunwidalyo, 6.-samununisya, 7.-samununa-samununa, 8.-samununana.) Also: -gogolola, -suula,tubula,-tukula, -zuununa.

undress for, *Kamubasamunwida mwana kutegwa dokotela amusilike nkaambo banyina mbaIwazi.* = Undress the child so that doctor can treat him because his mother is sick. (1.-samunwidwa, 2.-samunwidwe, 3.-samunuzya, 4.-samunwidwa, 5.-samunwidwalyo, 6.-samununisya, 7.-samunwida-samunwida, 8.-samunwidana)
  • give presents of old clothes, *Ndakamusamunwida zisani akumupa naakandeetezya.* = When I felt pity for her I gave her a present of clothes to wear.

branch out, *Buluba bwamunene bwakasanda citaambiki.* = The cotton of the old man has branched out in an undescribeable way. Also: -panda. (2.-sandide, 3.-sandya, 4.-sandila, 5.-sandilalyo, 6.-sandisya, 7.-sandasanda, 8.-sandilana)

turn wrong way up or inside out, rt. -sandamuna, *Kocisama kabotu, cisani wacisandamika.* = My friend, dress properly, you have turned the dress the wrong way. (1.-sandamikwa, 2.-sandamikide, 3.-sandamisya, 4.-sandamikila, 5.-sandamikilalyo, 6.-sandamikisya, 7.-sandamika-sandamika, 8.-sandamikana) Also: -salamika.

overturn, *Cimbayambaya cakasandamuka munzila.* = The vehicle overturned on the way. *Kambwalakasa nkaakakkede kakasandamuka naakazyatuka.* = The little stool he was sitting on overturned when he lifted his leg. *Aakusika oko kubukoko ulajana nongo ziluujisi kusandamuka tapu-tapu.* = When he arrived at the beer-party you would find the beer containers were being emptied one by one and turned upside down (as he was a heavy drinker) Also: -salamuka, -vwuntamuka, -bbindamuka. (1.-sandamukwa, 2.-sandamukide, 3.-sandamuzya, 4.-sandamukila, 5.-sandamukilalyo, 6.-sandamukisya, 7.-sandamuka-sandamuka, 8.-sandamukilana)

invert, turn over, *Kamusandamuna nombe tufwunde kubbazu eeli.* = Turn the cow over so that we skin it on this side. (1.-samdamunwa, 2.-sandamwide, 3.-sandamuzya, 4.-sandamwida, 5.-sandamwidalyo, 6.-sandamunisya, 7.-sandamunasandamuna, 8.-sandamunana) Also: -bbindamuna,-salamuna,-wuntamuna.

be turned upside down, "*Wee tandilyi nsima yasandamunwa, ncibi kukwela mitiba ilaa nsima.*" = I do not eat nsima that has been turned upside down, it is bad to pull the dishes around containing nsima.

change position repeatedly, *Sunu masiku ndali kwiile kusandauka nkumwali kucisa mwida.* = Last night I was just changing position all the time as the stomach was paining. (1.-sandaukwa, 2.-sandaukide, 3.-sandauzya, 4.-sandaukila, 5.-sandaukilalyo, 6.-sandaukisya, 7.-sandauka-sandauka, 8.-sandaulana) Also: -pilimuka, -bbutauka.

turn a thing over and over, *Notuyoka nyama inga tulaisandaula kutegwa ibizwe kabotu koonse-* koonse. = When we are roasting meat we turn it over and over so that it is roasted on all sides. (1.-sandaulwa, 2.-sandamwide, 3.-sandauzya, 4.sandawida, 5.-sandawidalyo, 6.-sandaulisya 7.-sandaula-sandaula, 8.-sandaulana)
  • change, Naluntaambwe ulalisandaula mibala. = The chameleon changes colours.
  • rotate, Kutasandaula zisyango mumuunda ncintu cileta ansi kubutebuzi. = The lack of rotation of crops in a field is a thing which reduces the harvest.
cause to change, Bamakaintu bayandisya kulisandauzya mbobasama banji. = Women delight in changing with the fashion.

take turns in visiting alternate wives as a polygamist, Mwati bausyi mwana balasanduka kuya mubakaintu basyoonto? = Is the father of the child taking his turn to go to the house of the second wife? (1.-sandukwa, 2.-sandukide, 3.-sanduzya, 4.-sandukila, 5.-sandukilalyo, 6.-sandukisya, 7.-sanduka-sanduka, 8.-sandukilana)
  • become changed, Mukupa wasanduka waba mabisi. = The milk went sour. Mucelo wasampuka ulasanduka akuleka kulula. = The medicine that loses strength changes and loses it's bitterness. Nyika yasanduka, tiicili mbuli kaindi pe. = The world has changed, it is not what it used to be in the past. Ngooyu muntu utasanduki buyo moyo wakwe. = Here is a constant person. Bakasika akaandabwe kabusiku. Bantu bamwi bakalisandukide kale mumalo aabo. They arrived at midnight. Some people had already gone to bed.

migrate as game, Nibakavwula bantu muno mucisi, banyama bakasandukila kuunka kwakanyina bantu. When the population increased in this area, the animals migrated to quieter places. (1.-sandukilwa, 2.-sandukide, 3.-sanduzya, 4.-sandukila, 5.-sandukilalyo, 6.-sandukisya, 7.-sandukila-sandukila, 8.-sandukilana)
  • turn against, Syaansima wakasandukila mweenzinyina. Syaansima turned against his friend
  • change, Buumi bwakukkala mubunji bwakamusandukila. The life of living with others changed her.

change into, Cibbadela bakacisandula kuba cikolo. = They changed the hospital into a school. Syaacinyama wakali mwaalumi wakali kulisandula kuba mulavwu, naa suntwe, naa siluwe, naa ntale. = Syaacinyama was a man who used to change himself into a lion, or a hyena, or a leopard or a crocodile. (1.-sandulwa, 2.-sandulide,/-sandwide, 3.-sanduzya, 4.-sandulila,/-sandwida, 5.-sandulilalyo/-sandwidalyo, 6.-sandulisya, 7.-sandula-sandula, 8.-sandulana.)
  • answer, respond, Bamwi bantu balamuka kusandula magwalo. = Some people are late in answering letters. Bamaama bakaamba majwi manji-manji akundilaya, mebo ndiide kuumunye akusandula ajwi pe. My mother said many words to advise me, but I was just quiet and did not answer a word at all.

translate, interpret, Muleli wacisi naakali kukanana mu Chikuwa, Moonga nguwakali kusandulula mu Chitonga. When the president was speaking in English, Moonga was the one who was translating into Chitonga. (1.-sandululwa, 2.-sandulwide, 3.-sanduluzya, 4.-sanduluzyizya, 5.-sanduluzyizyalyo, 6.-sandululisya, 7.-sandula-sandula, 8.-sandulwidana) Also: -pilula, -pandulula.

revolve, turn over and over, Kamusanduula cipopwe eco citaidi. = Turn the maize cob over so that it does not burn. (1.-sanduulwa, 2.-sandwiide, 3.-sanduuzya, 4.-sandwiida, 5.-sandwiidalyo, 6.-sanduulisya, 7.-sanduulasanduula, 8.-sanduulana) Also: -sandaula.

be pleased, be delighted, Inziba ilya yasanga, nkokuti kuli mpiikumba. = That dove is contented, it must be sitting on eggs somewhere. Nziba cisaasa, usanga kubalombe, kubanene cilakaka coolwe. = The female dove in mating delights in young males, she refuses to please the old ones. (1.-sangwa, 2.-sangide, 3.-sangizya, 4.-sangila, 5.-sangilalyo, 6.-sangisya, 7.-sanga-sanga, 8.-sangilana)
  • contribute, offer, dedicate, Kamusanga mali aumwi ngakonzya kubikka. = Let each one contribute what he is able to. Ndakasanga buzumi bwangu, ndakabupa kuli Leza kuti mbelekele ndinywe. = I have dedicated my life, I have offered it to God so that I work for you. Njina wakaisanina amalowa akali kusanga bantu bakwe. = He fed the louse with the blood which was offered by his people. Bantu bakatalika kusanga mali aazitina, samende, museenga, mabwe a zintu zimwi. = People began to contribute money for bricks, cement, sand and other things.

rejoice greatly, exult, be thrilled, Ndakasangabalilwa nkaambo ndakamubona mwanookwesu ngundakabwene kaindi. = I was delighted because I saw my brother whom I last saw a long time ago. Kuti waboola kubantu bakuyanda inga wasangabalilwa. = If you come to people who like you, you are full of joy. (2.-sangabalidwe, 3.-sangabalizya, 4.-sangabalilwa, 5.-sangabalilwalyo, 6.-sangabalilisya, 7.-sangabalilwasangabalilwa, 8.-sangabalizyanya)

cause to rejoice greatly, Bantu baunyu tabayandi kusangabalizya beenzu. = Stingy people do not want to make visitors feel welcome. Musobano oyu ulasangabalizya cinicini. = This play really brings joy. (1.-sangabalizyigwa, 2.-sangabalizyide, 3.-sangabalizya, 4.-sangabalizyizya, 5.-sanagabalizyizyalyo, 6.-sangabalizyisya, 7.-sangabalizya-sangabalizya, 8.-sangabalizyanya)

be happy, Kamunga kamusangalala kwaanzya beenzu. = Be happy as you greet visitors. Kumoyo kwangu kwasangalala, ndajana nceyanda. = I was deeply pleased, I found what I wanted. (1.-sangalalwa, 2.-sangalalide, 3.-sangalazya, 4.-sangalalila, 5.-sangalalilalyo, 6.-sangalalisya, 7.-sangalala-sangalala, 8.-sangalilana)

cheer someone up, encourage, welcome, Ciimbo ncitwali kwiimba cali kusangalazya kubantu. = The song which we were singing made people happy. Ndakacebuka kuli mbabo kuti ndibasangalazye. = I turned to them to make them happy. Aba balibonya mbantu ba Mwami Mwenda kabasangalazya ba Kaunda a zizyano zyacisi. = These who are seen are the people of Chief Mwenda welcoming President Kaunda with traditional songs. (1.-sangalazyigwa, 2.-sangalazyide, 3.-sangalazyisya, 4.-sangalazyizya, 5.-sangalazyizyalyo, 6.-sangalazyisya, 7.-sangalazya-sangalazya, 8-sangalazyanya)

mix together, mate, Impwizi abasune zyasangana kale. = The cows and oxen have already come toge ther. Kamusangana mutani kulizanduli kubeenzinyoko. = Mingle and do not separate yourselves from your friends. (1.-sanganwa, 2.-sangenye, 3.-sanganya, 4.-sanganina, 5.-sanganinalyo, 6.-sanganisya, 7.-sangana-sangana, 8.-sangana)
  • unite as man and wife on marriage day, Kupana kasima akanyama banabwiinga buzuba bwakukwatana, citondezya kusangana kuti baba omwe. = Giving one another a small lump of nsima with meat, shows that the bridegroom and the bride have become one. Kumantoombwa bana baniini bakali kusangana antoomwe mbuli kuti mbanalumi abamakaintu. = At the place where children played homemanagement games, they used to mix together pretending to be husbands and wives. Bakasangana mumusalo. = They joined in the conversation.

mix up, Ncibi kusanganizya mapopwe anyabo. = It is bad to mix the maize with the beans. (1.-sanganizyigwa, 2.-sanganizyide, 3.-sanganizya, 4.-sanganizyizya, 5.-sanganizyizyalyo, 6.-sanganizyisya, 7.-sanganizya, 8.-sanganizyanya)

mix, Beembezi bazisanganya mpongo ambelele. = The shepherds mixed the goats with the sheep. (1.-sanganyizyigwa, 2.-sangenye/ne, 3.-sanganya, 4.-sanganyizyizya, 5.-sanganyizyizyalyo, 6.-sanganyisya, 7.-sanganya-sanganya, 8.-sanganyizyanya)
  • add, Bana bacikolo balaiya nombolo zyakusanganya. = School-children learn addition in mathematics.

be broken up, as a tribe, be scattered, be eroded, Bantu bakali kukkala antoomwe, sunu bakasangauka. = The people who lived together, today have scattered. Makumbi alisangaukide. = The clouds have dispersed. Balimi beelede kubaa mizeezo kutegwa bulongo kabutasangauki. = Farmers should make plans so that the soil does not become eroded. Also: -mwaikizyanya. (1.-sangaukwa, 2.-sangaukide, 3.-sangaukizya, 4.-sangaukila, 5.-sangaukilalyo, 6.-sangaukisya, 7.-sangauka-sangauka, 8.-sangaukana)

dismiss as a crowd. Mwiiyi wakabasangaula basicikolo nicakamana cisobano. = The teacher dismissed the pupils after the game.
  • waste money, give generously, Mali ndakaasangaula kale. = I have already wasted the money. Cintu camitukuta yako inga tocisangauli kusowasowa nkaambo uzyi mbuli mbocakakupenzya. = A thing of your sweat you will not waste it by throwing it around because you know how it made you suffer. Bana bamwi nibakomena tabayandi kubagwasya bazyali babo; bazyali bayeeya mali abo ngobakasangaula ciindi nobakali kuyiisya bana babo. = Some childen when they grow up do not want to help their parents: their parents think of their money which they gave generously when they were having their children educated. (1.-sangaulwa, 2.-sangawide, 3.-sangauzya, 4.-sangawida, 5.-sangawidalyo, 6.-sangaulisya, 7.-sangaula-sangaula, 8.-sangaulana)

give presents to a girl when she goes out as a bride, Baama basangila mwanaabo. = My mother gave presents to her daughter as she went out as a bride. (1.-sangilwa, 2.-sangilide, 3.-sangizya, 4.-sangilila, 5.-sangililalyo, 6.-sangilisya, 7.-sangila-sangila, 8.-sangilana)
  • make a cigarette, Munene usangila musanga. = The old man is making a cigarette. Also: -pangila.
  • fly over, Nindakaboola okuya ndakainda kukuyunza nkaambo ndakabona nziba nkozindisangila lyoonse. = When I came from there I passed by to inspect my traps because I had always seen doves flying over me there.
(1.-sangukilwa, 2.-sangulide, 3.-sangukizya, 4.-sangukila, 5.-sangukilalyo, 6.-sangukisya, 7.-sanguka-sanguka, 8.-sangukilana)

take other people's goods inconsiderately, Sikansondo wasangukila zintu zyabantu. = A madman took people's good's inconsiderately. (usangukide = one who takes other people's things freely)
  • change behaviour for the worse, Mwana wangu wasanguka akaambo kabantu bamuyunga. = My child has changed his behaviour because of the people who enticed him into their bad company. Also: -bisigwa (rt. -bija)

corrupt the young, Bamusangula beenzinyina mwana. = His friends have corrupted the boy. (1.-sangulwa, 2.-sangwide, 3.-sanguzya, 4.-sangwida, 5.-sangwidalyo, 6.-sangulisya, 7.-sangula-sangula, 8.-sangulana) Also: -bisya (rt.-bija)
  • spoil by giving too much, Bacembele bamusangula muzyukulu wabo akaambo kakumuzyibizya ccuka. = The grandmother spoiled her grandchild by always giving her sugar.
  • waste wealth, be prodigal, Tacili cibotu kusangula lubono Iwamufwu. = It is not good to waste the wealth of a dead person. Also: -sangaula.

feed, nourish, Kamusanina mwana ceele kusikila akkute. = Feed the child with porridge until it is satisfied. Bamatumbu basanina kabotu bana babo. = The mothers are nourishing their children. Kuli bulonga-longa bunji busanina milonga yoonse eyi. = There are many little streams which feed all these rivers. (1.-saninwa, 2.-sanide/-saninide, 3.-sanizya, 4.-saninina, 5.-sanininalyo, 6.-sanininsya, 7.-sanina-sanina, 8.-saninana.)
  • manure, Mulimi ulicizyi kusanina muunda wakwe kutegwa mapopwe akomene kabotu. = The farmer knows how to manure his field so that the maize grows well. Also: -sanyina.
feed one's eyes with, Wakasanizya meso kumusanza lyaciguju cina Sinandu aalya mpolilomba moombe. = At sunset he fed his eyes on the view to the south of the borehole of Sinandu village.

insult, jeer, Akaka kamumulesya oyo usanka mweenzinyina. = Would you please stop that one who is mocking his friends. Bamusanka kuti, kumeso kubee wakafwidwa. = They insulted her saying that her face looked like a widow's." Also: -nonga. (1.-sankwa, 2.-sankide, 3.-sankizya, 4.-sankila, 5.-sankilalyo, 6.-sankisya, 7.-sanka-sanka, 8.-sankana)
  • be arrogant, Ulalisanka akaambo kalubono ndwajisi. = He is arrogant because of the wealth which he has.

be excessive in height, Ciluli cabutala casankama. = The roof of the granary is too high. (1.sankamwa, 2.-sankeme, 3.-sankamya, 4.-sankamina, 5.-sankaminalyo, 6.-sankamisya, 7.-sankama-sankama) Also: -tankama, -sunkumana.

be too high as a roof, Aaka kaluli kakasankamana kapati, takayusiki. = That little roof is too high, it is not able to give shelter. (1.-sankamanwa, 2.-sankamanide, 3.-sankamanya, 4.-sankamanina, 5.-sankamaninalyo, 6.-sankamanisya, 7.-sankamana-sankamana, 8.-sankamaninana) Also: -sunkumana.
stand against, oppose, Wamusankamina mulumyaako. = You have opposed your husband.

take a handful from a heap, Ndakacisankamuna cikata catombwe kuti mbambe cilundu. = I took a bundle of tobacco to make a cake of it. Kosankamuna ndongwe acilwi. = Take a handful of groundnuts from the heap. Ndasankamuna civwaki candongwe akuziyoka. I took a handful of groundnuts and roasted them. (sankamunwa, 2.-sankamwide, 3.-sankamuzya, 4.-sankamwida, 5.-sankamwidalyo, 6.-sankamunisya, 7.-sankamuna-sankamuna, 8.-sankamwidana) Also: -sonkomona, -senkemuna.

toss away, shake off, Ndakasansa kwaanza kutegwa kauka kazwe. I shook my hand to remove the insect. Kosansa meenda wamana kusamba. Shake off the water when you have finished washing. Wakasansa mudaala ciindi naakabilila kukanana. = The old man rejected it the time he became angry when talking. Also: -tapula. (1.-sanswa, 2.-sanside, 3.-sansya, 4.-sansila, 5.-sansilalyo, 6.-sansisya, 7.-sansa-sansa, 8.-sansana or -sansilana)
  • kick, Mwanaa moombe nabbalamuka kutija, nasansa buti, bana bakali kukonzya kumujata. = The young calf, when it jumped up to run, no mater how it kicked, the children were able to catch it. Maulu atalika kuyuma akusansa misembele canguzu. = The legs began to grow strong and to throw vigourous kicks. Wakasotoka kumwi usansa mweendo mbuli kuti kuli cimulumide. He jumped up while kicking about with his leg as if something had bitten him.
  • get rid of, abandon, Moomba wakali mulozi naakaciswa basimukowa wakwe bakamusansa. = When Moomba, who was a witch, became sick, his relatives abandoned him.
  • sprinkle, shake over, Wakasaanguna kubasansa basimbi maanzi amatu amusampizya. = He first of all sprinkled the girls with water mixed with musampizya leaves.
  • cool oneself by drinking, Ndakajana bamadaala balisansa tukoko mukkoce. I found old men cooling off by drinking beer on the verandah.

fall and scatter like leaves or seeds, Nsangu nizyatika zyasansaana cakutayoleka. = When the seeds fell they scattered so that it was difficult to pick them up. Impongo zyaile kusansaana mumusena. = The goats were just scattered in the vlei. (1.-sansaanwa, 2.-sanseenye/-sansaanide, 3.-sansaanya, 4.-sansaanina, 5.-sansaaninalyo, 6.-sansaanisya, 7.-sansaanasansaana) Also: -sansala.

sprinkle repeatedly, Nsangu nimwasyanga-syanga, kwiida nkusansaila buya. When you plant the seeds you should water them just by sprinkling them. Simbewu usansaila musamu kucisyu kutegwa tuuka tufwe. = The gardener is sprinkling insecticide on the vegetables so that the insects die. Also: -iila, nyunya-nyunya, -tuntulwida. (1.-sansailwa, 2.-sansailide, 3.-sansaizya, 4.-sansailila, 5.-sansaililalyo, 6.-sansailisya, 7.-sansaila-sansaila, 8.-sansailana)

spread out, Muntu naakazimina, bantu banji bakasansala mumusena oonse kumuyandaula. = When the person got lost, the people went about everywhere in the vlei searching for him. (1.-sansalwa, 2.-sansele, 3.-sansazya, 4.-sansalila, 5.-sansalilalyo, 6.-sansalisya, 7.-sansala-sansala, 8.-sansazyanya) Also: -saantika.
  • spread out, as seed, Bacembele basansala mimena kuti iyume. = The old woman is spreading out fermented maize seeds to dry. Also: -yanga.

go for a stroll, Basimbi bali kusansalika kweenda lyakaamuka mvwula. The girls went strolling about when the rains eased off. (1.-sansalikwa, 2.-sansalikide, 3.-sansalikizya, 4.-sansalikila, 5.-sansalikilalyo, 6.-sansalikisya, 7.-sansalika-sansalika)

improve in health, Sunu ndajana mulwazi wasansama. Today I found the patient had improved. (1.-sansamwa, 2.-sanseme, 3.-sansamya, 4.-sansamina, 5.-sansaminalyo, 6.-sansamisya, 7.-sansama-sansama, 8.-sansaminana) =
  • dry up, Mutalekeli mwana kusobana anze nkaambo takunasansama. = Do not allow the child to play outside because it has not yet dried up.

be blown away, Koonse kasuko kakali atafwule kakasansamuka nkaambo muwo wakali munji. = All the dust that was on the table was blown off because the wind was strong. (1.-sansamukwa, 2.-sansamukide, 3.-sansmukizya, 4.-sansamukila, 5.-sansamukilalyo, 6.-sansamukisya, 7.-sansamuka-sansamuka, 8.-sansamukana)

wash out, as a dish with hand, wipe, rub off, dust, Kolisansamuna kumulomo. = Wipe your mouth. Kolisansamuna mavwu kumatako bwabija buluke. Wipe the soil off your behind, the trousers are dirty. Mainza wakali kulisansamuna ccovwu lyansipa kumutwe. Mainza was washing off the suds of soap from his head. Also: -pukuta. (1.-sansamunwa, 2.-sansamunide, /-sansamwide, 3.-sansamuninzya/-sansamuzya, 4.-sansamunina,/sansamwida, 5.-sansamuninalyo, /-sansamwi-dalyo, 6.-sansamuninsya, 7.-sansamunasansamuna, 8.-sansamunana)
  • wipe oneself, wipe one's feet on a mat. Kotaninganjila munanda, kolisansa muna maulu akasasa. = Before you enter the house, wipe your feet on the mat.

clean off, Kobasansamwida mobalida babwa, wamana ubikke cimbi cakulya. = Clean the place where the dogs eat, when you have done that put fresh food. Kosansamwida mucikko tuuka tufwe. Clean off the insects into the fire so that they die. (1.-sansamunwa, 2.-sansamwide, 3.-sansamuzya, 4.-sansamwida, 5.-sansamwidalyo, 6.-sansamunisya, 7.-sansamwida-sansamwida, 8.-sansamwidana) Also: -salazizya.

beat as a child or millet, Mwana naakalila kwaciindi cilamfwu, banyina bakacimwa, bakatema kaluso akumusansaula kumaulu. When the child cried for a long time, the mother was annoyed, she cut a small stick and beat the child on the legs. Also: -cancaula, -cwankaula, -cwapuula. (1.-sansaulwa, 2.-sansawide, 3.-sansauzya, 4.-sansa-wida, 5.-sansawidalyo, 6.-sansaulisya, 7.-sansaula-sansaula, 8.-sansaulana)
  • clean grass by removing leaves from stem, Nomujwa bwizu kamubusansaula kutegwa butakakatazyi kuvwumba. Clean that grass so that it will not be difficult to thatch with.

sprinkle once, Kosansila meenda acikuni ciyaka cizime. = Sprinkle water on the burning log so that it goes out.
  • shake Mwana wasansila kuulu, naalumwa nzoka. The child shook his leg, when he was bitten by a snake. (1.-sansilwa, 2.-sansilide, 3.-sansizya, 4.-sansilila, 5.-sansililayo, 6.-sansilisya, 7.-sansila-sansila, 8.-sansilana) Also: -tapula

beat with a little stick, Banyina mbabamusansula kaluso mwana. = It is the mother who beat the child with a small stick. Also: -sansaula, -cancaula, -cwapula. (1.-sansulwa, 2.-sanswide, 3.-sansuzya, 4.-sanswida, 5.-sanswidalyo, 6.-sansulisya, 7.-sansula-sansula, 8.-sansulana)

revert to a question to make it completely clear, explain clearly, Bayi bakasansulula kuti amvwe sicikolo. = The teacher explained so that the pupil could understand. Kamukasansulula kaambo aaka bamvwe babetesi. = Explain this matter clearly to the judges so that they understand. Uli muntu uli buti ozima twaambo tupati, konga waliiba twasansululwa twamvwa toonse zintu mbozibede. = What sort of a person are you who hides important matters when you are free to explain them so that we understand how things are? Also: -pandulula. (1.-sansululwa, 2.-sansulwide, 3.-sansuluzya, 4.-sansuIwida, 5.-sansulwidalyo, 6.-sansululisya, 7.-sansulula-sansulula, 8.-sansulwidana)

explain for, Kamusansulwida sicikolo amvwe. = Explain for the pupil so that s/he understands. (1.-sansulwidwa, 2.-sansulwide, 3.-sansuluzya, 4.-sansulwida, 5.-sansuIwidalyo, 6.-sansululisya, 7.-sansulwidasansulwida, 8.-sansulwidana)

sit lazily as when there is no work, lounge, be idle when boss is away, Mubelesi wali kulisanta. = A worker was idle when the boss was away. (1.-santwa, 2.-santide, 3.-santya, 4.-santila, 5.-santilalyo, 6.-santisya, 7.-santa-santa, 8.-santizyanya)

be in heat, as an animal, Ingulube yasantula iyandaula mucende. = The sow which is in heat is looking for a boar. Nobamwi cintanda cibaba mbuli kabwa kasantula. Some of you, your nakedness itches like a dog in heat. (1.-santulwa, 2.-santwide, 3.-santuzya, 4.-santwida, 5.-santwidalyo, 6.-santulisya, 7.-santula-santula, 8.-santuzyanya)

manure a field, Mulimi usanyina muunda wakwe. = The farmer is manuring his field. Also: -sanina muunda. (1.-sanyina, 2.-sanyinide, 3.-sanyizya, 4.-sanyinina, 5.-sanyininalyo, 6.-sanyinisya, 7.-sanyina-sanyina, 8.-sanyinana)

slice and grill meat, Kamwiisanza nyama iyanikwe. = Slice and grill the meat so that it can be dried. (1.-sanzwa, 2.-sanzide, 3.-santizya, 4.-sanzila, 5.-sanzilalyo, 6.-sanzisya, 7.-sanza-sanza, 8.-sanzana)
  • form a friendship. Muka Mbiya wakasanza cilongwe kuli Muka Matimba. = Mrs. Mbiya formed a friendship with Mrs. Matimba. Iso -pangana bulongwe.
make a pact of friendship, rt. -sanza, Chimuka wakasanzana bulongwe amweenima. Chimuka made a pact of friendship with my cousin. Also: -pangana bulongwe.
speak with certainty, Kamunga kamusanzaula kwaamba. = You should be sure of what you are talking about.

broil, rt. -sanza Bazeli basanzika nswi. = The fishermen are broiling the fish. Also: - temeka. (1.-sanzikwa, 2.-sanzikide, 3.-sanzikizya, 4.-sanzikila, 5.-sanzikilalyo, 6.-sanzikisya, 7.-sanzika-sanzika, 8.-sanzikilana)
  • be washable, rt. -sanza, Ooyu mutiba ulasanzika nkaambo tautezemuki. = This dish is easily washed because it is not slippery.

lop off, cut down, Kamusanzula mateo mumuunda. = Cut down the shrubs in the field. (1.-sanzulwa, 2.-sanzwide, 3.-sanzuzya, 4.-sanzwida, 5.-sanzwidalyo, 6.-sanzulisya, 7.-sanzulasanzula, 8.-sanzulana) Also: -duntaula, -gunkaula.

wash, Kamubasanzya bana batolwe kucipimo. = Wash the children so that they can be taken to the clinic. Kamusanzya zimbuzi zisalale. = Wash the toilets so that they are clean. Chuumangoma wakakkede kunze aņanda yakwe kasanzya zikobela. = Chuumangoma was sitting behind his house washing clothes. (1.-sanzyigwa, 2.-sanzyide, 3.-sanzyisya, 4.-sanzyila/-sanzyizya, 5.-sanzyilalyo,/-sanzyizyalyo, 6.-sanzyisya, 7.-sanzya-sanzya, 8.-sanzyanya)
  • cleanse a village from evil, Munanga wakaboola kusanzya munzi nkaambo bantu banji bakali kunjilwa zyeelo. = When the witchdoctor came he purified the village because many people were possessed by evil spirits. Also: -kupaula.
washing up, Awo mpaakali kusanzyila wakalibabwene bantu nkobakali kwiinsauka mumugwagwa. = There where he was washing up he saw the people walking to and fro on the road.

jeer, Basankwa bafwubafwuba balayandisya kusapa basimbi. = Foolish boys take great delight in jeering girls. (1.-sapwa, 2.-sapide, 3.-sapizya, 4.-sapilila, 5.-sapililalyo, 6.-sapilisya, 7.-sapa-sapa, 8.-sapana) Also: -sanka, -nonga.

show distaste for something, Ooyu mwana ulasapula, tayandi kulya mangamwe. = This child turns up her nose, she does not want to eat boiled grains of maize. (1.-sapulwa, 2.-sapwide, 3.-sapuzya, 4.-sapwida, 5.-sapwidalyo, 6.-sapulisya, 7.-sapula-sapula, 8.-sapulana) Also: -kwena
cause one to be ridiculed, rt. -sapula, Mukaintu usapwida mulumi wakwe. The wife causes her husband to be ridiculed. V - 478

become sour, Mukupa wasasa aba mabisi. The milk became sour. (1.-sasikwa, 2.-saside, 3.-sansya, 4.-sasila, 5.-sasilalyo, 6.-sasisya, 7.-sasa-sasa, 8.-sasilana)
  • become bad, Cisyu kuti coona kacitavwunikidwe cilasasa. Relish becomes bad when it is left uncovered.

lie flat on stomach or face, turn reverse side, Zyasasabala kuyanikwa nswi zyabacembele. The fishes of the old lady were laid flat to dry. (1.-sasabalwa, 2.-sasabele, 3.-sasabazya, 4.-sasabalila, 5.-sasabalilalyo, 6.-sasabalisya, 7.-sasabala-sasabala, 8.-sasabilana)
  • become flat, Muntu ufwide nzala inga ida lyasasabala. When a person is hungry the stomach becomes flat. Kwamusasabala bukome. Her waist had become flat. Also: -zanzabala, -yanzabala, -papalala.

make sour, make distasteful, rt. -sasa, Balasasika mukupa munsuwa. = They make milk sour in a calabash. (1.-sasikwa, 2.-sasikide, 3.-sasikizya, 4.-sasikila, 5.-sasikilalyo, 6.-sasikisya, 7.-sasika-sasika, 8.-sasikilana)

become distasteful or repugnant to, Chikosola nyama yakwe yakamusasila, wakanjila syokwe akulisina. = Chikosola's flesh was repugnant to him, he entered the bush and hung himself. (1.-sasilwa, 2.-sasilide, 3.-sasilizya, 4.-sasilila, 5.-sasililalyo, 6.-sasilisya, 7.-sasila-sasila, 8.-sasililana)

have eruptions on the body, Mwana ulasasuka kuti wababwa lubabangwe. A rash comes out on the skin of a child when the lubabangwe plant irritates it. (a plant which grows by rivers and is like the velvet plant) (1.-sasukwa, 2.-sasukide, 3.-sasusya, 4.-sasukila, 5.-sasukilalyo, 6.-sasukisya, 7.-sasuka-sasuka, 8.-sasukizyanya)

exasperate, annoy, irritate, as vermin do, Bungu bwamulala bulasasula. = The dust of the black mamba causes a rash. (1.-sasulwa, 2.-saswide, 3.-sasuzya, 4.-saswida, 5.-saswidalyo, 6.-sasulisya, 7.-sasula-sasula, 8.-sasulana)

eat what is left over, Bana basasulula musozya walekedwe masikati. = The children are eating the samp which was left at midday. (1.-sasululwa, 2.-sasulwide, 3.-sasuluzya, 4.-sasulwida, 5.-sasulwidalyo, 6.-sasululisya, 7.-sasulula-sasulula, 8.-sasuluzyanya)

be sick, Akaambo kakusata mwana wakakkala buyo myaka misyoonto. = The child lived only a few years because of illness. (1.-satwa, 2.-satide, 3.-satya, 4.-satila, 5.-satilalyo, 6.-satisya, 7.-sata-sata)

issue, as water from a spring, Meenda alasauka kunsi abbwe. = The water is coming out from under the stone. Also: -mimita, -pompa. (2.-saukide, 3.-sausya, 4.-saukila, 5.-saukilalyo, 6.-saukisya, 7.-sauka-sauka, 8.-sausyanya)
  • deteriorate, Joni wakali mupaale, sunu wakasauka. = John was smart, nowadays he has gone down. Also: -sabaana.

give presents for work done, Basimbi bamusaula musankwa ooyu. = The girls give a present to this boy for the work done. (1.-saulwa, 2.-sawide, 3.-sauzya, 4.-saulila, 5.-saulilalyo, 6.-saulilalyo, 7.-saula-saula, 8.-saulana)
  • make poor, Kalume bakamusaula basimbi nkaambo wakali kwiile kubapa mali. = The girls made Kalume poor because he was just giving them money.

be upset, Eeci ciyanza candinyemya icakuti aliino buya ndicisaukide. = This custom annoyed me so much that even now I am still upset. (1.-saulwa, 2.-saukide, 3.-sausya, 4.-saukila, 5.-saukilalyo, 6.-saukisya, 7.-saukide-saukide, 8.-sausyanya)

give a final blow to finish off, Kamumusaulula mubwa uuciswa. = Finish off the dog who is sick. Ndakayuuma nzoka eni amutwe, kwacaala buyo kusaulula. = I hit the snake right on the head, it just remained to finish it off. Kanji-kanji balwazi bakali kusaululwa akaambo kakuti bakali kufwa mukubula muya mubotu wakuyeeka. = Usually sick people were killed before their time because they were dying because of lack of fresh air. (1.-saululwa, 2.-saulwide, 3.-sauluzya, 4.-saulwida, 5.-saulwidalyo, 6.-saululisya, 7.-saulula-saulula, 8.-saululana)

swim, Bana balasaya muzyiba. = The children are swiming in the pond. Also: -yamba, -samba. (1.-sayigwa, 2.-sayide, 3.-sayizya, 4.-sayila, 5.-sayilalyo, 6.-sayisya, 7.-sayasaya, 8.-sayiyana)
  • work a paddle towards oneself, Bwato buleenda kabotu kuti basaya kabali bayumu = The boat moves well if the paddlers are strong. Also: -sunda, -kwasula
  • hesitate, ponder as to what to do, Mutumwa taelede kusaya. = The one who is sent ought not hesitate. Nkamu yazigwebenga eyi tiiyakali kusaya-saya kujaya bantu. = This group of thieves did not hesitate to kill people. Also: -enkela.
remove, as earth with hands or feet, Twajana bana balasea mumulonga. = We found the children removing the light clay from the river. (1.-seagwa)

rest by leaning back against something, Tacili cibotu kuseama kucitendele camootokala nkaambo kuti cajaluka inga waloka ansi. = It is not good to lean against the door of the car because if it opens you will fall out. Also: -yaama,-seyama. (1.-seamwa, 2.-seamide, 3.-seamya, 4.-seamina, 5.-seaminalyo, 6.-seamisya, 7.-seama-seama, 8.-seamana)
  • sit while making space for another Koseama buya kukkala awalo oyu akkale. = Give room where you are sitting so that this one finds space as well. Also: -peama.

sift, clean grain by removing dirt, Musimbi useba busu. = The girl is sifting the mealie meal. Bacembele baseba bukoko kutegwa masenga azwe. = The old woman is straining the beer so that the husks are taken out. (1.-sebwa, 2.-sebede, 3.-sebezya/-sebya, 4.-sebela, 5.-sebelalyo, 6.-sebesya, 7.-seba-seba/sebulula, 8.-sebelana.)
  • settle a matter, Bamadaala balicizyi kuseba twaambo mumbeta. = The old men know how to settle cases in court.

destroy, devastate, Naa ulakaka uyakupona mukusebaana kutaambiki. If you refuse you will live in unspeakable chaos. (1.-sebaanwa, 2.-sebaanide, 3.-sebaanya, 4.-sebaanina, 5.-sebaaninalyo, 6.-sebaanisya, 7.-sebaana-sebaana, 8.-sebaanizyanya)

destroy another's character, Wakanditanda akundaambila kuti tayandi kuti nkeya busebaanya zina lyakwe kuti nguwakandilemeka. He drove me out and told me that he did not want me going around destroying his name saying that it was he who had made me pregnant. (1.-sebaanyizyigwa, 2.-sebaanide, 3.-sebaanya, 4.-sebaanina, 5.-sebaaninalyo, 6.-sebaanisya, 7.-sebaanyasebaanya, 8.-sebaanyizyanya)
