look with eyes wide open at, stare at, fix the eyes upon, Ncibi kutunamina mumena, cilalumya. = It is bad to look wide-eyed into holes, it can cause you to be bitten. Ncibi kutunamina zuba nolibaide. = It is bad to focus on the sun when it is being eclipsed. (tunaminwa, 2.-tunamide, 3.-tunaminya, 4.-tunaminina, 5.-tunamininalyo, 6.-tunaminisya, 7.-tunamina-tunamina, 8.-tunaminana)

be famous, Magwaza wa-tunda nkaambo ujisi mali manji mubbanga. Magwaza is famous because he has much money in the bank. (1.-tundizyigwa, 2.-tundide, 3.-tundizya, 4.-tundila, 5.-tundilalyo, 6.-tundisya, 7.-tunda-tunda, 8.-tundilana)
  • make resistant, Eyi nsiki ninkali kapati, ndiizyi. Kwiipa mucelo utali wayo, ilatunda kapati. This sickness is very fierce, I know it. To give the medicine which does not suit it, makes more resistant.

be proud, as one with a swoolen neck (head), Mapuwo apa muntu kutundaila. Pride gives one a swollen head. (1.-tundailwa, 2.-tundailide, 3.-tundaizya, 4.-tundailila, 5.-tundaililalyo, 6.-tundailisya, 7.-tundaila-tundaila, 8.-tundailana) Also: -tuntaila.

become resistant, Bantu bagonka zisamu lyoonse, maanzaabo akatundila. The hands of people who always cut trees become resistant to blistering. Kuti bulwazi bwamuka kusilikwa inga bwatundila. If a disease is slow to be treated it becomes resistant. (1.-tundizyigwa, 2.-tundide, 3.-tundizya, 4.-tundilila, 5.-tundililalyo, 6.-tundilisya, 7.-tundila-tundila, 8.-tundizyanya) Also: -pundila.
  • be uncooked, be watery as badly cooked potatoes, Zitende tiizyabizwa kabotu, zyatundila. = These pumpkins are not well cooked, they are watery. Also: -fwuba
  • be stained Cisani citafwambi kusanzigwa cilatundila. = A cloth which is not washed quickly remains stained.

become recidivistic, Wakatundizigwa azyuumo, kunyina nanga wacinca pe. = Beatings have turned him into a recidivist, he will not change now.
  • be stained, Cisani cilatundizigwa abubaya. A cloth is stained through carelessness.

make sore and painful, Zilakutundizya zyuumo kuti kotamvwi. = Beatings will make you sore if you do not comply.
  • stain, Mukaintu mubaya utundizya zisani. A careless woman stains the clothes.
be relieved of pain, Mubili wangu wakatunduka. My body has been freed of pain.
suffer pain, Sena muyeeya nzi nkomubee mwatunduluka? = What are you thinking about which seems to show that you are suffering?

inflict physial or mental pain, Ulamutundulula mwana ngwalela. She inflicts physical punishment on the child she is looking after. Ncibi kapati kutundulula bamucaala. It is bad to illtreat orphans. Also: -penzya. (1.-tundululwa, 2.-tundulwide, 3.-tunduluzya, 4.-tundulwida, 5.-tundulwidalyo, 6.-tundululisya, 7.-tundulula-tundulula, 8.-tundululana)

make a string of beads, Bacembele batunga bulungu bwamiemba. The old woman is threading strings of beads for a face-veil for the initiate. (1.-tungwa, 2.-tungide, 3.-tungizya, 4.-tungila, 5.-tungilalyo, 6.-tungilisya, 7.-tunga-tunga, 8.-tungilana,/-tungana) (-tunga cimpwampwa = string beads in the hair)
  • thread as cotton, Sunu tandicikonzyi kutunga bunweba munyeleti nkaambo meso angu acembaala. = Today I can no longer thread a needle because my eyes have become dim.
  • go ahead, Haanausyi nguutunga bantu nobaya kukulamba adilwe. = The person from the father's clan is the one leading when people go to smear themselves at a funeral. Also: -solweda.
  • grow as plants, Mapopwe angu atalika kutunga miyanda mipya. = My maize has started to shoot new roots.
  • go in a line, Bayuni bakatunga muongo kuya kukunywa meenda. = Birds were going in a line to drink water. Bana bacikolo batunga mulongo kunjila mucikolo. = The pupils are forming a line on entering the school.

make a line, walk in single file, Bakatungana mulongo kuya kumulonga. They make a line going to the river. Kamutungana milongo yobilo. = Make two lines. (1.-tunganwa, 2.-tungene, 3.-tunganya, 4.-tunganina, 5.-tunga ninalyo, 6.-tunganisya, 7.-tunganatungana, 8.-tungana)
move in a line, Beenzu balanjila mumunzi kabatungene mulongo angoma zyabo zyakuzyana cinande. The visitors enter the village in a line with their drums to dance the cinande.

moving in a line, rt.-tunga, Naakabona kuti nombe zyauzubuka mulonga zyalulama munzi, kazyuutungide mulongo, wakakkomana cini-cini. = When he saw that the cattle had crossed the river, heading for the village moving in a line, he was truly happy.

thread as beads, Banditungila kale bulungu bwakuyoosobanya. = They have already threaded the beads which I am going to play with. Bacembele batungila bulungu busubila. = The old lady has threaded red beads. (1.-tungwa, 2.-tungide, 3.-tungizya, 4.-tungila, 5.-tungilalyo, 6.-tungilisya, 7.-tungila-tungila, 8.-tungilana)
  • start a song, lead the singing, Mweemba nguutungila baimbi mucikombelo. Mweemba is the person who starts hymns for the singers in the church. Also: -angula.
  • thatching a roof by using a wooden needle = Bamatebele balicizyi kutungila ziluli zyamaanda. = The Matebele people know how to thatch roofs with the wooden needle.

transfer fire, light a candle from another candle, light a fire, Kotungilila mulilo. = Transfer the fire. (1.-tungililwa, 2.-tungilide, 3.-tungilizya, 4.-tungilila, 5.-tungililalyo, 6.-tungilisya, 7.-tungilila-tungilila, 8.-tungililana)

set alight, Kacumbika ulaanga muzenge wakutungilizya mulilo. Kacumbika is binding a grass torch for setting a fire alight. Also: -tunginizya. (1.-tungilizyigwa, 2.-tungilizyide, 3.-tungilizya, 4.-tuingilizyizya, 5.-tungilizyizyalyo, 6.-tungilizyisya, 7.-tungilizya-tungilizya, 8.-tungilizyanya)
  • string along with, Wakali kuyanda kumujanina mbaanyina zyakutungilizya mubulungu. = He wanted to find her cowry shells for stringing along with the beads.

set alight, Kamutunginizika muzwenge ankandela. = Light the burning brand from the candle. (1.-tunginizikwa, 2.-tunginizikide, 3.-tunginizikizya, 4.-tunginizikila, 5.-tunginizikilalyo, 7.-tunginizikisyatunginizikisya, 8.-tunginizyanya) Also: -tungilila, -donekezya.

throw light on something, Kotunginizya mumuni aawa tubone naa mbeba mpoibede. Shine the light there to see if that is where the rat is. (1.-tunginizyigwa, 2.-tunginizyide, 3.-tunginizya, 4.-tunginizyizya, 5.-tunginizyizyalyo, 6.-tunginizyisya, 7.-tinginizya-tunginizya, 8.-tunginizyanya) Also: -munika.

unthread a string of beads, Bacembele batungulula bulungu busiya. The old woman unthreaded the black beads. (1.-tungululwa, 2.-tunguIwide, 3.-tunguluzya, 4.-tungulwida, 5.-tungulwidalyo, 6.-tungululisya, 7.-tungulula-tungulula, 8.-tungulwidana) Also: -pulula.

be sorry through grief or shame, look down, Watungumana nkaambo ncaacita cilausisya. = He felt remorse because what he did was shameful. Ndajana nkuku zilatungumana. = I found the hens looking downcast. Wakatungumana kalisukete. He was in a sad humour with his head resting on his arm. (1.-tungumanwa, 2.-tungumene, 3.-tungumanya, 4.-tungumanina, 5.-tungumaninalyo, 6.-tungumanisya, 7.-tungumana-tungumana, 8.-tungumaninana)
be dejected, Mainza mbwaakali kutungumanina mbuli muntu wakolwa mantabe. = That is the way Mainza was so downcast like a person who was drunk with beer.

be downcast, rt. -tungumana, Usyi naafwa, Mainza wali kwiide kutungumene wabulilwa ankwatozya. When the father of Mainza died he was just downcast not knowing where to go. Choolwe wakalitungumene ulangide ansi kumwi kayeenda yacizike. = Choolwe was discouraged looking down while the tears flowed.
make one look sorrowful, Ino kayi ncinzi ncoyeeya cakutungumika boobo? Now what is it that you are thinking about that makes you look so sad?

take aim at, Mulombwana taakeelede kusubila kucisubilo. Weelede kutungwinizya mukapulo kakalidonkwedwe kubulo. A man is not supposed to urinate anywhere in the homelatrine, but ought to urinate directly into the hole which was beside the bed. (1.-tungwinizyigwa, 2.-tungwinizyide, 3.-tungwinizya, 4.-tungwinizyizya, 5.-tungwinizyizyalyo, 6.-tungwinizyisya, 7.-tungwinizya-tungwinizya, 8.-tungwinizyanya)

become strange, rt. -tuna, Ndakajana musimbi wiide kunditunide biya. I found that the girl had just become strange to me. (1.-tunwa, 2.-tunide, 3.-tunya, 4.-tunina, 5.-tuninalyo 6.-tunisya, 7.-tunide-tunide, 8.-tuninana)

knock with fist, Kutunka mwana muniini inga wamucisa. = You can hurt a child when you hit it with a fist. (1.-tunkwa, 2.-tunkide, 3.-tunkizya, 4.-tunkila, 5.-tunkilalyo, 6.-tunkisya, 7.-tunka-tunka, 8.-tunkana) Also: -gonkola

swell as corpse, Katufwambaana kugusya mubili wamufwu noutanatunta. = Let us quickly remove the body of the dead person before it decomposes. (1.-tuntwa, 2.-tuntide, 3.-tuntya, 4.-tuntila, 5.-tuntilalyo, 6.-tuntisya, 7.-tunta-tunta, 8.-tuntizyanya)
  • transfer as liquid or grain, Kamwaatunta meenda ayo mwaabikke mumbi. Transfer that water and put it into another container. Kamutunta mabisi munsawa. Pour out the sour milk from the milk gourd.

go eagerly, as a cow to new grass, Inombe zilatuntaana kuya kumweemvwe mubotu. The cattle go eagerly to fresh grass. (1.-tuntaanwa, 2.-tunteene, 3.-tuntaanya, 4.-tuntaanina, 5.-tuntaaninalyo, 6.-tuntaanisya, 7.-tuntaana-tuntaana, 8.-tuntaanizyanya)

swagger about, Mweendelezi wacisobana wakali kutuntaila kweenda basankwa bakwe nibakazunda. = The coach of the game was swaggering about when his team won the match. (1.-tuntailwa, 2.-tuntailide, 3.-tuntaizya, 4.-tutailila, 5.-tuntaililalyo, 6.-tuntailisya, 7.-tuntaila-tuntaila, 8.-tuntaililana)

shoot upwards as a spring, Meenda akatuntamuka kuzwa mu-pompi. = The water shot up out of the pump. (1.-tuntamukwa, 2.-tuntamukide, 3.-tuntamukizya, 4.-tuntamukila, 5.-tuntamukilalyo, 6.-tuntamukisya, 7.-tuntamuka-tuntamuka, 8.-tuntamukilana) Also: -tuntumuka.

beat quickly, as heart, Moyo alatuntauka kuti wayoowa. = The heart beats fast if you fear. Moyo wangu wali kutuntauka nilyataningatalika bbola. = My heart was beating quickly before the match began. Also: -duntauka. (1.-tuntaukwa, 2.-tuntaukide, 3.-tuntaukisya, 4.-tuntaukila, 5.-tuntaukilalyo, 6.-tuntaukisya, 7.-tuntauka-tuntauka, 8.-tutaukilana)

pour out for someone, as liquid or grain, rt. -tunta, Kamumutuntila mukupa awalo oyu mwana. = Pour out milk for this child also. Kamundituntila mukupa mucigabba. Pour milk for me into this tin. (1.-tuntwa, 2.-tuntide, 3.-tuntya, 4.-tuntila, 5.-tuntilalyo, 6.-tuntisya, 7.-tuntila-tuntila, 8.-tuntilana)

moving from one place to another, Magwaza takkede kabotu mwaka uno, wiile kutuntulika. = Magwaza is not well settled this year, he is just roaming about. Twajana munene ulatuntulika ciindi cacifwumofwumo nkaambo wafwide mpeyo. We found the old man in the early morning moving about because he was feeling cold. Also: -fwumfwulika - tuntumauka. (1.-tuntulikwa, 2.-tuntulikide, 3.-tuntulisya, 4.-tuntulikila, 5.-tuntulikilalyo, 6.-tuntulikisya, 7.-tuntulika-tuntulika, 8.-tuntilisyanya)

be shifted from, rt. - tuntulika, Ndakakatala kutuntulisigwa nindakali kukkala mu Monze akaambo kakubula nanda. I was tired of being shifted from place to place when I was living in Monze because of lacking a house. (1.-tuntulisigwa, 2.-tuntulisyide, 3.-tuntulisya, 4.-tuntulisyizya, 5.-tuntulisyizyalyo, 6.-tuntulisyisya, 7.-tuntulisigwa-tuntulisigwa, 8.-tuntulisyanya)

cause to move from place to place continuously, Bakali kutuntulisya bana akubatola kucikolo cimbi nibakapola. They were moving the children and taking them to another school when they moved from their home.

transfer, as a liquid or grain, Bakatuntulula mungwimba akuubikka mucibulo cimbi. They transferred the fuel and poured it into another container. Kamutuntulula mapopwe mubikke musaka bbotu. = Transfer the maize and put it in a good sack. (1.-tuntululwa, 2.-tuntulwide, 3.-tuntuluzya, 4.-tuntuIwida, 5.-tuntulwidalyo, 6.-tuntululisya, 7.-tuntulula-tuntulula, 8.-tuntulwidana)
transfer into, rt. -tuntulula, *Kotuntulwida* meenda mucibiya cizumi. = Transfer the water and put it in an undamaged earthen pot.

shiver with cold, Mwana utuntuma mpeyo, kamumupa nkausu asame. = The child is shivering with the cold, give him a vest/sweater to wear. Also: -zyangama, -kankama. (1.-tuntumizigwa, 2.-tuntumide, 3.-tuntumya, 4.-tuntumina, 5.-tuntuminalyo, 6.-tuntumisya, 7.-tuntuma-tuntuma, 8.-tuntumizyanya)
  • shake someone, Impeyo yamupa kutuntuma mulwazi. = The cold has caused the patient to shiver.

begin sitting up as convalescent, Mulwazi ulatuntumana sunu. = The patient is recovering today. (1.-tuntumanwa, 2.-tuntumene, 3.-tuntumanya, 4.-tuntumanina, 5.-tuntumaninalyo, 6.-tuntumanisya, 7.-tuntumanatuntumana, 8.-tuntumaninana)
  • be uncomfortably seated, Ulatuntumana nkaambo kwasika makwe. = He was sitting uncomfortably because his in-law had arrived. Also: -sunsumana, -nongomana.

wander about, Muntu oyu unyina mpakkede, ula-tuntumauka. = This person has no permanent residence, he is just wandering about. (1.-tuntumaukwa, 2.-tuntumaukide, 3.-tuntumaukizya, 4.-tuntumaukila, 5.-tuntumaukilalyo, 6.-tuntumaukisya, 7.-tuntumauka-tuntumauka, 8.-tuntumausyanya) Also: tuntumana, -tuntulika
be seated in an uncomfort-able position, *Chimuka ulituntumene a cipingili kumulyango.* = Chimuka is seated uncomfortably on the crossbar of the entrance.

make bend down in respect, *Bamutuntumika bamakwe nibamwiita.* = The in-laws caused him to bend down in respect when they called him. *Muzike wakali kwiile kulituntumika kumbele amwami.* = The slave was just bowing low before the chief. (1.-tuntumikwa, 2.-tuntumikide, 3.-tuntumika, 4.-tuntumikila, 5.-tuntumikilalyo, 6.-tuntumikisya, 7.-tuntumika-tuntumika, 8.-tuntumikana)
  • transfer, *Nocakacili cifwumofwumo, bakamubweza mulwazi akuya kumutuntumika anze kutegwa akaumwe muwo.* = When it was still morning, they transferred the patient outside for fresh air.

discharge as an abscess, *Bwatuntumuka busina kuzwa acuute.* = Pus was discharged from the abcess. *Cilonda cakatuntumuka busina bunji.* = The wound was discharging a lot of pus. (1.-tuntumukwa, 2.-tuntumukide, 3.-tuntumukizya, 4.-tuntumukila, 5.-tuntumukilalyo, 6.-tuntumukisya, 7.-tuntumuka-tuntumuka, 8.-tuntumukilana)
  • be poured out from, *Ccuka lyatuntumuka kuzwa musaka.* = Sugar poured out from the sack.
be poured out, rt. -tuntumuka, *Mukupa onse watuntumukila ansi.* = All the milk poured out on to the ground. Also: -dudumukila.
pour out, *Wakatuntumuna tuniini tusu amane atwalo nkutulabila.* = He poured out a little mealiemeal and thereupon he tasted it.

be covered with, *Bakamwale bakaindi bali kunga nomulanga omusankwa nkujana kumutuntunkene simpuke wakwe, kumweelede impande ankumu ulati yakazyalilwa mpawo.* = The girl-initiates of the past were such that when you, young man, boy looked at one you would find her with a beaded face-veil which suited her and a mpande shell on the forehead you would say she was born with it. (1.-tuntunkanwa, 2.-tuntunkene, 3.-tuntunkanya, 4.-tuntunkanina, 5.-tuntunkaninalyo, 6.-tuntunkanisya, 7.-tuntunkene-tuntunkene, 8.-tuntunkaninana)

be proud, in a good sense, Basankwa bakatuntwa nibakazunda mumusobano wabbola. The boys were proud when they won a football match. (used as noun, Bakaba amatunta nibakazunda. They became proud when they won.) (1.-tuntwa, 2.-tuntide, 3.-tuntya, 4.-tuntila, 3.-tuntya, 4.-tuntila, 5.-tuntilalyo, 6.-tuntisya, 7.-tuntwa-tuntwa 8.-tuntilana)
  • be poured, Bukoko bwatuntwa kale mubbulo. The beer has already been poured out of the drum. Mabisi atuntwa kale kuzwa munsuwa. = The sour milk has already been poured out of the calabash.

be devastated, bewildered, ashamed, feel guilty, Wakatunuka naakajatwa bulale mukaintu ulya. = That woman was ashamed when she was caught committing adultery. Sunu wakatunuka buvwubi nkubwamana. = Today he is devastated, his wealth is finished. Wakatunuka naakamana kukongwa asyuumbwa. He was in shock when he was frightened by the lion. Bantu banji bakaboola kumubona mulozi ciindi naakatunuka nkaambo kamicito yakwe mibi. = Many people came to see the witch during the time he was shamed because of his evil deeds. (1.-tunukwa, 2.-tunukide, 3.-tunusya, 4.-tunukila, 5.-tunukilalyo, 6.-tunukisya, 7.-tunuka-tunuka, 8.-tunusyanya)

be in a confused or dark state, Wakalitunukide, maanu aabuntu akazwa, cakaba ciyanga. = He was confused in himself, human understanding had gone, he had become an idiot. Kumeso wakali kwiide kutunukide mbuli muntu walikuzima syokwe. = His face was just dark like a man who had been putting out a bush-fire. (1.-tunukwa, 2.-tunukide, 3.-tunusya, 4.-tunukila, 5.-tunukilalyo, 6.-tunukisya, 7.-tunukidetunukide, 8.-tunusyanya)
be unsuitable, Cikwaangala
mpande yakwe. The ring of the crow (on its neck) is not unsuitable to it. (proverb) (1.-tunwa, 2.-tunukide)

be unusual, *Cilatunya* kujana kuti sunu Ncimunya wasama cisani cipya. It is strange to find that today Ncimunya has put on a new dress. Cilatunya kuti mvwula yawa mumwezi wa Itwi. It is unusual if the rain falls in August.

cut away, lance, Ndali kutunzula cikoto akuulu kwamwana. = I was lancing a lump on the child's leg. Nindamana kufwunda nombe ndaita mudaala ucizyi kutunzula. Having skinned the animal I called the old man to disembowel it. (1.-tunzulwa, 2.-tunzwide, 3.-tunzuzya, 4.-tunzwida, 5.-tunzwidalyo, 6.-tunzulisya, 7.-tunzula-tunzula, 8.-tunzulana)

string with, rt. -tunga, Tumwi toozi twakutunzya bulungu, tumwi kubambya mantimbwa. = Some fibres were for stringing beads with, others were for making musical instruments for female initiation. (1.-tungwa, 2.-tungide, 3.-tunzya, 4.-tungila, 5.-tungilalyo, 6.-tungisya, 7.-tunzya-tunzya, 8.-tungana)
  • make proud, Kwakaba kumutunzya, kwakaba kumupa ntunda. = It only made him feel proud, it only gave him to think he was great.
be aroused, rt.-tupula, *Basankwa bakali kutupukwa nibakabona basimbi kabasamide tusani tubangalala.* = The boys were aroused (sexually) when they saw the girls wearing transparent dresses.

agitate, arouse, Munene wafwuma kutupula bana kuti baye kucikolo. = The old man aroused the children early so that they would go to school. (1.-tupulwa, 2.-tupwide, 3.-tupuzya, 4.-tupwida, 5.-tupwidalyo, 6.-tupulisya, 7.-tupula-tupula, 8.-tupulana)

crowd at the opening when coming out, *Inzuki zyatupuluka mubwina.* = The bees are crowding at the entrance as they come out of the hole. Nowakamana muswaangano bantu boonse bakatupulukila anze. = When the meeting was finished all the people came crowding out at the exit. (1.-tupulukwa, 2.-tupulukide, 3.-tupulusya, 4.-tupulukila, 5.-tupulukilalyo, 6.-tupulukisya, 7.-tupuluka-tupuluka, 8.-tupulusyanya) Also: -tupunuka

crowd at entrance when coming out, *Inombe zilatupunuka kuzwa muciba.* = The cattle were crowding at the entrance when coming out of the kraal. Also: -tupuluka. (1.-tupunukwa, 2.-tupunukide, 3.-tupunusya, 4.-tupunukila, 5.-tupunukilalyo, 6.-tupunukisya, 7.-tupunuka-tupunuka, 8.-tupunukizyanya)

bring small loads into heap, *Basankwa batuta zitina akuzilundika ayakwa.* = Boys are bringing bricks and heaping them at the building-site. (1.-tutwa, 2.-tutide, 3.-tutya, 4.-tutila, 5.-tutilalyo, 6.-tutisya, 7.-tuta-tuta, 8.-tutilana) Also: -susa
  • leave with one's possessions, *Mukaintu wakwe wakatuta naakalekwa* = The wife went off with her possessions when she was left by her husband.

tremble, *Mubbi wakatutama lyakasika ulaa nanda.* = The thief was trembling when the owner of the house arrived. Also: -tuntuma, -bimba. (1.-tutamwa, 2.-tutamide, 3.-tutamya, 4.-tutamina, 5.-tutaminalyo, 6.-tutamisya, 7.-tutama-tutama, 8.-tutamizyanya)

have eyes opened wide, cause to bulge or roll, *Mulumi wakatalika kuuma mwinakwe mane nkujana liso lyakatutuluka alimwi awalo mulomo wakazimba.* = The husband began to beat his wife until an eye bulged and also her mouth swelled. Wakabona meso amunene nkwaatutuluka mbuli muntu uciswa kasuntu. = He saw the eyes of the old man roll like one who was suffering from an attack of epilepsy. (1.-tutulukwa, 2.-tutulukide, 3.-tutulusya, 4.-tutulukila, 5.-tutulukilalyo, 6.-tutuluki-sya, 7.-tutulukatutuluka, 8.-tutulukizyanya)

take things out of house when cleaning, *Kamututulula zintu zyoonse zili munanda, mwamana mukukule.* = Remove everything which is in the house and when you have finished sweep it. (1.-tutululwa, 2.-tutulwide, 3.-tutuluzya 4.-tutulwida, 5.-tutulwidalyo, 6.-tutululisya 7.-tutulula-tutulula, 8.-tutulwidana) Also: -longolola, -longomona, -tutununa.
  • open eyes wide, *Cheendega wakatutulula meso kuti abone mwanaakwe mubuleya.* = Cheendega opened his eyes wide so that he would see his son in the crowd.
  • bulge, as eyes, *Naakatingwa nyama wakaatutulula meso.* = When she was choked with the meat, her eyes bulged. Also: -pwatula
look fixedly, rt. -tutulula, *Walikunditutulwida meso kutegwa ndimugwasye mukaambo kakwe.* = He fixed his eyes on me so that I would help him with his problem.

froth, Ndajana moombe ututuma makovwu kumulomo = I found a calf frothing at the mouth. Also: -tutama (1.-tutumwa, 2.-tutumide, 3.-tutumya, 4.-tutumina, 5.-tutuminalyo, 6.-tutumisya, 7.-tutuma-tutuma, 8.-tutumizyanya)

rise as yeast, Bwatutumuka bukoko nkaambo kabumena bwabikkwa. = The beer rose because of the fermented mealie-meal which had been put in. Notwakali kukulanga mulwazi, twakajana kututumuka makovvu kumulomo. = When we went to see the patient, we found he was frothing at the mouth. (1.-tutumukwa, 2.-tutumukide, 3.-tutumusya, 4.-tutumukila, 5.-tutumukilalyo, 6.-tutumukisya, 7.-tutumuka-tutumuka, 8.-tutumukizyanya) Also: -fwufwumuka.

take things out, Kamubututununa busu kuzwa mukasaka, mubuikke mukanongo. = Remove the meal from the sack and put it in the clay pot. Also: -tuntumuna, -tutula. (1.-tutununwa, 2.-tutunwide, 3.-tutunuzya, 4.-tutunwida, 5.-tutunwidalyo, 6.-tutununisya, 7.-tutununa-tutununa, 8.-tutunwidana)

make repeated efforts, pull something heavy, strife to pull through difficulties, Basankwa bakakwelana akututunyana canguzu. = The boys pulled against one another and strained with effort. (tug-of-war) Twakajana basune balatutunyana kukwela cilayi cilemu. = We found the oxen were pulling hard to drag the heavy sledge. (1.-tutunyanwa, 2.-tutunyanide, 3.-tutunyika, 4.-tutunyanina, 5.-tutunyaninalyo, 6.-tutunyanisya, 7.-tutunyana-tutunyana, 8.-tutunyaninana) Also: -tatanyana, -duunyana.

pull with force, Kubweza cintu cilemu nkututuyana. = To take something heavy requires strength. (1.-tutuyanwa, 2.-tutuyanide, 3.-tutuyanya, 4.-tutuyanina, 5.-tutuyaninalyo, 6.-tutuyanisya, 7.-tutuyana-tutuyana, 8.-tutuyaninana) Also: -tatanyana.

be in a sitting position while thinking deeply, Ngooyu waboola makoto, kuzwa kooko nkwaali kutuumene. = There comes the great man from the place where he was sitting pondering on some issue. (1.-tuumanwa, 2.-tuumene, 3.-tuumanya, 4.-tuumanina, 5.-tuumaninalyo, 6.-tuumanisya, 7.-tuumene-tuumene, 8.-tuumaninana)

be stored in, Maila atuumikwa buyo mumatala. = The sorgum grains are just kept in grain-bins. (1.-tuumikwa, 2.-tuumikide, 3.-tuumika, 4.-tuumikila, 5.-tuumikilalyo, 6.-tuumikisya, 7.-tuumikwa-tuumikwa, 8.-tuumikilana)

be fully grown, Maila okwesu akatuwa kale. = Our sorgum is fully grown already. Kaindi bakamwale bakali kuvwundikwa ciindi cilamfwu cini-cini mumaanda limwi mibili yabo yakali kunga yatuwa, yakomena. = In the past the girls were kept in the initiation houses for a real long time until their bodies were fully developed and had matured. (2.-tuwide, 3.-tuwizya, 4.-tuwila, 5.-tuwilalyo, 6.-tuwisya, 7.-tuwa-tuwa, 8.-tuwizyanya) Also: -ilika, -langazya, -kola.
pound in mortar, Kamutwa musozya, nobasimbi, tubone naa mwakomena kale. = Pound the samp, girls, so that we see whether you have already grown up.
= pound corn;
= pound with water;
majiji/magaga = 3 pound togethers, -one after another in the same mortar.)
sogola = pound of the husks;
guya, gwiya = pound as red ochre;
= pound rhythmically in twos (1.-tugwa (twigwa), 2.-twide, 3-twizya, 4.-twida, 5.-twidalyo, 6.-twisya, 7.-twaatwa, 8.-twana.)

marry, Wakatwala mwana a Chigabala. He married the daughter of Chigabala. Munene wakatwala ijilo. = The old man got married yesterday. (1.-twalwa, 2.-twele, 3.-twazya, 4.-twalila, 5.-twalilalyo, 6.-twalisya, 7.-twala-twala, 8.-twalana) Also: -kwata.

be marrigable, rt. -twala, Mukowa wa Bakonka ulatwalika nkaambo mbayumu kubeleka. The clan of the Bakonka are suitable for marriage as they are hard-working. (1.-twalikwa, 2.-twalikide, 3.-twalikizya, 4.-twalikila, 5.-twalikilalyo, 6.-twalikisya, 7.-twalikatwalika, 8.-twalikana)

help to marry, Mupati wakwe nguwakamutwalila akumupa lubono lunji. His elder brother helped him to marry and gave him much wealth. (1.-twalilwa, 2.-twalilide, 3.-twallilizya, 4.-twalilila, 5.-twalililalyo, 6.-twalilisya, 7.-twalila-twalila, 8.-twalilana)

be arrogant, Kambela ulatwanga mazuba ano nkaambo bausyi bakamuulila mootokala. Kambela is arrogant these days because his father bought him a car. (1.-twangwa, 2.-twangide, 3.-twangizya, 4.-twangila, 5.-twangilalyo, 6.-twangisya, 7.-twangatwanga, 8.-twangilana) Also: -pakala.
act arrogantly towards, Ncibi kutwangila bantu kuti wabaa lubono lunji. It is bad to be arrogant towards people if you become wealthy.

be blinded momentarily by something, rt. -towa, Mazuba akutaanguna inga kamwale wajana kukatazigwa kulyata anyika njumu alimwi akutweegwa zuba mumeso akaambo kakukkkala munanda ciindi cilamfwu. = During the first days the initiated woman finds it hard to step on the hard earth and in being blinded by the sun because of staying in the house for a long time. (1.-tweegwa, 2.-towede, 3.-towezya, 4.-towela, 5.-towelalyo, 6.-towesya, 7.-tweegwa-tweegwa, 8.-towana)

puff, pant, Wakaceezye buyo kufwesa akutweeka mbuli muntu wali kutijaana. He was just left exhausted and panting like a person who had been running. Also: -tweta. (1.-tweekwa, 2.-tweekede, 3.-tweesya 4.-tweekela, 5.-tweekelalyo, 6.-tweekesya 7.-tweeka-tweeka, 8.-tweesyanya)
be married, rt. -twala, Tanaakatwele. He had not yet got married.

be determined, Moyo wangu utweluka kuya kucikombelo lyoonse. My heart is set on going to church always. Also: -sukamina. (1.-twelukwa, 2.-twelukide, 3.-twelusya, 4.-twelukila, 5.-twelukilalyo, 6.-twelukisya 7.-tweluka-tweluka, 8.-twelusyanya)
  • become weak, Ndazyangama, ndayoowa, ndatweluka, mumagondo mulawiima alimwi mate andimana mukanwa. = I am shaking, I fear, I lose power, my knees are trembling and the spittle in my mouth has dried up.

beat as pulse or heart, Akaambo kakuyoowa kapati mumoyo ndiile kutweta. Because of the great fear, my heart was just pulsating. Muntu taningafwa, ucitweta. = The person is not yet dead, he is still breathing. Nacuumwine wakalilede ansi wakacili kutweta. Nacuumwine was lying on the ground and was still alive. (1.-twetesyegwa, 2.-twetede, 3.-twetezya, 4.-twetela, 5.-twetelalyo, 6.-twetesya, 7.-tweta-tweta)

sigh, groan, Mulwazi wacaazya kutweteka kwalo. = The patient remained just groaning. (1.-twetekwa, 2.-twetekede, 3.-twetezya, 4.-twetekela, 5.-twetekelalyo, 6.-twetekesya, 7.-tweteka-tweteka) Also: -yoyeka,-yokela, -sintimuka, -tongela

add pounded groundnuts to another food, rt. -twa, Nindazwa kucikolo ndajana baama bautwida kale musozya. = When I came from school I found mother had already added the pounded groundnuts to the samp. Inswi yatwidwa buntele ilandibotela. = Fish which has been mixed with pounded groundnuts delights me. (1.-twidwa, 2.-twidide, 3.-twidizya, 4.-twidila, 5.-twidilalyo, 6.-twidisya, 7.-twida-twida, 8.-twidilana)
  • use a pounded poisoned root for fishing which makes fish drunk, Kutwida nswi ncibi nkaambo kufwa zinji. = Using a pounded root for fishing is bad as it kills many fish.
  • Mutinta nguwakabatwida buntele bakaapa. = Mutinta is the one who pounded powdered groundnuts for my grandmother.

be pounded, rt. -twa, Musozya wakatwigwa kakucili mafwumina. The samp was pounded when it was still early in the morning. (1.-twigwa, 2.-twide, 3.-twisya, 4.-twida, 5.-twidalyo, 6.-twisya, 7.-twigwa-twigwa,8.-twidana) Also: -tugwa. twiimana remain silently attentive, Babwa nibakamana kwiitanda ngulube, yakatwiimana ciindi cilamfwu kunze acaanda. = When the dogs had stopped chasing the pig, it stood motionless beside the hut.
  • pierce with the eyes, Mubetesi wakamutwiimanina kumulanga cakugambwa. The judge stared at him silently in astonishment. (1.-twiimanwa, 2.-twiimene, 3.-twiimanya 4.-twiimanina, 5.-twiimaninalyo, 6.-twiimanisya, 7.-twiimana-twiimana, twiimaninana)

be in a silent attentive state, Kacitwiimene kuyeeya cakucita, wakamvwa kulila kwamwana kunze acuulu. When he was still remaining silent, thinking what to do, he heard the crying of a child behind the termite hill. Also: -tungumene

help a person to lift a load onto her head, Kamunditwikka cileye cankuni eci. Put this load of firewood on my head. Baama batwikka musimbi cileye cankuni. Mother put the load of firewood on the girl's head. Wakazyaanga antoomwe akulitwikka. She tied them together and put the load on her head. (1.-twikkwa, 2.-twikkide, 3.-twikkizya, 4.-twikkila, 5.-twikkilalyo, 6.-twikkisya, 7.-twikka-twikka, 8.-twikkana)
  • beat severely, Wanditwikka fwaindi yampobe. = He hammered me with his fist on the cheek.
have load on head, rt.twikka, Wakabona bamakaintu botatwe mbaabo baselemuka kumwi kabatwikkide azingomo. = He saw three women coming down having three containers loaded on their heads.

manure a field, Ooyu muunda bakautwikkila bufwumba bunji. = They manured this field with plenty of dung.
  • load for me, rt.-twikka, Konditwikkila cileye cankuni kumwana ooyu. = Assist me in loading the child with the bundle of firewood. (1.-twikkilwa, 2.-twikkilide, 3.-twikkizya, 4.-twikkilila, 5.-twikkililalyo, 6.-twukkilisya, 7.-twikkila-twikkila, 8.-twikkilana)

pound with, rt. -twa, Kwesu ndatwisya kansi kalubulo, nsitwisyi munsi wacisamu pe. At our home I pound with a small metal pestle, I do not pound with a pestle of wood. Misamu imwi ilatwisyika. = Some trees are good for pounding. (1.-twisyigwa, 2.-twisyide, 3.-twisya, 4.-twisyizya, 5.-twisyizyalyo, 6.-twisyisya, 7.-twisya-twisya, 8.-twisyanya)

mislead, Ooyu musankwa bakamutya banyina. = This boy was misled by his mother. (1.-tigwa, 2.-tide, 3.-tizya, 4.-tida, 5.-tidalyo, 6.-tilisya, 7.-tya-tya, 8.-tilana)
  • pour out onto the ground, Kotya meenda ayo taasalali. = Pour that water out, it is not clean. Bana baatya mabisi. = The children have poured out the sour milk on the ground. Also: -kununa, -tila.

press with finger, Kotyaamika munwe acilonda buzwe busina. = Press the finger on the wound so that the pus comes out. Also: -dyaamika. (1.-tyaamikwa, 2.-twaamikide, 3.-tyaamizya, 4.-tyaamikila, 5.-tyaamikilalyo, 6.-tyaamikisya, 7.-tyaamika-tyaamika, 8.-tyaamikana)

be in abundance, Akaambo kabunkutwe bwakwe, kulya kwabo kwakali kwakutyaatya biya. = Because of his energetic work, their food was very plentiful. (1.-tigwa-tigwa, 2.-tide-tide, 3.-tizya-tizya, 4.-tida-tida, 5.-tidilalyotidilalyo, 6.-tilisya-tilisya, 7.-tyaatyatyaatya, 8.-tilana-tilana)

interrupt, Munene wakacili kuyanda kukanana pele bakamutyaba. = Munene still had much to say but they interrupted him. Also: -tyokezya. (1.-tyabizyigwa or -tyabwa, 2.-tyabide, 3.-tyabya, 4.-tyabila, 5.-tyabilalyo, 6.-tyabilisya, 7.-tyaba-tyaba, 8.-tyabana)
  • press down upon, Kamutyaba cikanci acilonda. = Press with the pith on the wound.

stretching as one awakes, Musankwa wiile kutyabanuka, wabuka ino. = The boy is just stretching, he has just woken up. (1.-tyabanukwa, 2.-tyabanukide, 3.-tyabanuzya, 4.-tyabanukila, 5.-tyabanukilalyo, 6.-tyabanukisya, 7.-tyabanuka-tyabanuka, 8.-tyabanukisyanya)

bring chest forward, Basikalumamba balatyabanuna zyamba nobafwoolwa. = Soldiers bring chests forward when marching. Also: -bbakamana (1.-tyabanunwa, 2.-tyabanwide, 3.-tyabanuzya, 4.-tyabanwida, 5.-tyabanwidalyo, 6.-tyabanunisya, 7.-tyabanuna-tyabanuna, 8.-tyabanunana)

become spoiled, Maanu aamudaala akatyabila akaambo kakukomena. The old man has become senile because of old age. Cisani cakatyabila, kunyina nociya kusalala. = The cloth has become spoiled, it will never be clean. (1.-tyabizyigwa, 2.-twabilide, 3.-yabizya, 4.-tyabilila, 5.-tyabililalyo, 6.-tyabilisya, 7.-tyabila-tyabila, 8.-tyabizyanya)

press, Ndaminwa nkaambo nitwakali kutingaana jilo, mweenzuma wakandityamba kapati. = I am exhausted because when we were wrestling yesterday my friend pressed me very much. (1.-tyambwa, 2.-tyambide, 3.-tyambya, 4.-tyambila, 5.-tyambilalyo, 6.-tyambisya, 7.-tyamba-tyamba, 8.-tyambana)
  • bring the chest forward, kulityamba. Also: -tyabanuna, -tyabanuka.

press down continuously, Ndakamutyambilila mumeenda limwi wafwundilila. = I pushed him under the water until he was gasping for breath. Njakukutyambilila ncobeni, cikakuzwe coonse cimpangwe. = I will really squeeze you until all the insolence comes out of you. (1.-tyambililwa, 2.-tyambilide, 3.-tyambilizya, 4.-tyambililila, 5.-tyambilililalyo, 6.-tyambililisya, 7.-tyambililatyambilila, 8.-tyambililana)

be made concave, stand with back hollowed, Musana wamu daala wakatyambuka akaambo kazyuumo naakali mubuzike. = The back of the old man was bent inwards because of the beatings when he was in slavery. (1.-tyambukwa,2.-tyambukide 3.-tyambukizya, 4.-tyambukila, 5.-tyambukilalyo, 6.-tyambukisya, 7.-tyambuka-tyambuka, 8.-tyambusyanya) Also: -alama
stand with hollowed back, Musana wasuntwe ulityambukide. = The back of the hyena is hollowed.

make concave, Bazyali bakacibikka ciyanda amusana wamwana akumutyambula. = The parents put medicine on the back of the child to make it concave. (1.-tyambulwa, 2.-tyambwide, 3.-tyambya, 4.-tyambwida, 5.-tyambwidalyo, 6.-tyambulisya, 7.-tyambulatyambula, 8.-tyambulana)

squeeze, press down upon, Kamucityanka cuute eco buzwe busina. = Squeeze that abcess so that the pus comes out. Balombe batyanka masaya abasimbi. = Boys squeeze the cheeks of the girls. Imbooma yakatyanka mbelele, imbelele yakatamba. = The boa constrictor squeezed the sheep, the sheep was overcome. Also: -dina.
liso = shut one eye to aim better. (1.-tyankwa, 2.-tyankide, 3.-tyankizya, 4.-tyankila, 5.-tyankilalyo, 6.-tyankisya, 7.-tyanka-tyanka,8.-tyankilana.)

squeeze the breast to bring out milk for the child, Kamumutyankila mukupa mulisyo mwana nokatiizwe kamutowa. = Squeeze milk from the breast into the child's eye so that the speck comes out which is troubling him.
stalk, Chimuka wakalibanda kuti, "Ndime Tyaila nkukutyayaila kweenda." Chimuka praised himself saying, "I am the stalker. The way I walk is like stalking." Also: -sobelela

break, Cakatyoka cifwuwa mukati naakawa. = He broke a bone inside when he fell. Musankwa watyoka kuulu naali kusobana bbola. = The boy broke a leg while playing football. (1.-tyokwa, 2.-tyokede, 3.-tyokezya, /tyozya, 4.-tyokela, 5.-tyokelalyo, 6.-tyokesya, 7.-tyoka-tyoka, 8.-tyokelana.)

be in a broken state, rt. tyoka, Moyo wakwe Mainza wakalityokaukide kuzwa ciindi mukaintu wakwe naakamulekelezya. = Mainza's heart was broken from the time his wife betrayed him. (1.-tyokaulwa, 2.-tyokaukide, 3.-tyokauzya, 4.-tyokaukila, 5.-tyokaukilalyo, 6.-tyokaukisya, 7.-tyikaukidetyokaukide, 8.-tyokaukilana)

be cracked, break into pieces, Cifwuwa cakatyokooka mubupandu-pandu. = The bone was splintered in many pieces. Impesele yangu yatyokooka. = My pencil was broken up in pieces. (1.-tyokookwa, 2.-tyokookede, 3.-tyokookezya, 4.-tyokookela, 5.-tyokookelalyo, 6.-tokookesya, 7.-tyokooka-tyokooka, 8.-tyokookana)

break bone or stick, twist a mealie-cob off stem, Kamutyola munsale ooyu ambeyo mundipe. = Break off a sugar-cane stick so that you also give me a piece. (1.-tyolwa, 2.-tyolede, 3.-tyolezya,-/-tyozya, 4.-tyolela, 5.-tyolelalyo, 6.-tyolesya, 7.-tyola-tyola, 8.-tyolana.)
  • break the law, Tulakonzya kuutyola mulawo kabatazyi bamwi kuti tuutyola. = We can break the law without others knowing we are breaking it.
  • restrict one's freedom, Kuti kamukkede munsi kwategwa mwakkalisya munsi mulatutyola boya tobapati. = If you sit near where the elders are sitting they say you are 'breaking our hair', i.e., we cannot discuss matters which you should not listen to.
  • make pregnant, Musankwaako aakuboola takakuzumini aakubona kuti waalemana nkaambo taasyi waakutyola. = When your boy-friend comes he will not agree to marry you when he sees that you are pregnant because it is not him who has made you so.
  • use an instrument (to eat, to write) Kufwumbwa mpaajana *ityola* muungo walo nkoona kwamana kwaba kwabo buzuba obo. = Wherever he found a spoon to eat he would sleep there and make the place his own for the day. (*ityola mpesulo* = use a pencil to write)

be tired, become tired, Mubili watyolauka nkaambo tiindoona pe. = The body is tired because I did not sleep. (1.-tyolaukwa, 2.-tyolaukide, 3.-tyolaukizya, 4.-tyolaukila, 5.-tyolaukilalyo, 6.-tyolaukisya, 7.-tyolauka-tyolauka, 8.-tyolauzyanya)

be broken up, Impongo yatyolooka niyalyatwa musune. = The goat was broken up when the ox walked on it. Also: -tyolauka. (1.-tyolookwa, 2.-tyolookede, 3.-tyolookezya, 4.-tyolookela, 5.-tyolookelalyo, 6.-tyolookesya, 7.-tyolooka-tyolooka, 8.-tyolookezyanya)
  • be deeply discouraged, be heartbroken, be devastated, e.g Mweenima Mutinta, ndalendelelwa, utandisiyi, moyo wangu watyolooka. = My cousin, Mutinta, I am lonely, don't leave me, my heart is broken.
  • curtsy, O Musimbi, ncibotu kutyolooka mazwi beenzu nobasika kutondezya bulemu. = Girl, it is good to curtsy when the visitors arrive to show respect.

break up in pieces, Kamutyoloola nkuni tusikke. = Break up the firewood into pieces so that we can stick them in the fire. Kwakawide mvwula mpati alimwi yakajisi guwo pati lyakali kutyoloola masamu. = There was a heavy fall of rain and again it was accompanied by a mighty wind which broke up the trees. (1.-tyoloolwa, 2.-tyolweede, 3.-tyoloozya, 4.-tyolweeda, 5.-tyolweedalyo, 6.-tyoloolesya, 7.-tyoloola-tyoloola, 8.-tyoloolana)
  • display oneself, Basimbi balikwiile kulityoloola nibabona basankwa. = The girls were showing off when they saw the boys. Also: -meka
  • be lazy in working, Koleka kwiile kulityoloola, kobeleka mbuli munkutwe. = Don't be lazy while working, work energetically.

be broken into pieces, Juni ndiinga moomba lyakatyoloolwa mababa. = The wings of the big turkey buzzard were broken.
  • entice to be loved, Musimbi wakavwiila kumwi kalityoloola kasana. = The girl answered while showing movements to attract attention to be loved.

discourage, rt. -tyompwa, Bantu bakali kutyompeeka musimbi kuti taakeelede kuzumina musankwa uyiide, nkaambo Iwiiyo lupa kutwanga kumusankwa. = The people were discouraging the girl saying that she ought not marry an educated boy, because education makes a boy boastful. (1.-tyompeeka, 2.-tyompeekede, 3.-tyompeezya, 4.-tyompeekela, 5.-tyompeekelalyo, 6.-tyompeekesya, 7.-tyompeeka-tyompeeka, 8.-tyompeekana) Also: -bbumpaika, -tyompya.

be disappointed, Bakatyompwa bantu nibakamvwa kuti ndiyanda kukwata cakolwa. = The people were disappointed when they heard I wanted to marry a drunkard. Bana bakatyompwa nibatakaunka kukuzundana bbola. = The children were disappointed on being unable to go to the football competition. (1.-tyompwa, 2.-tyompede, 3.-tyompya, 4.-tyompelwa, 5.-tompelwalyo, 6.-tyompesya, 7.-tyompwa-tyompwa, 8.-tyompezyanya)

disappoint, Wakandityompya nkaambo taakaboola nkutwakapangenye. = He disappointed me because he did not come to where we had agreed. _Bamayi batayiisyi kabotu, batyompya bazyali._ = Teachers who do not teach poperly, disappoint the parents. (1.-tyompezyegwa)

walk in mud, _nombe zyalikutyopola mumankandya._ = The cattle were walking in the mud. (1.-tyopolwa, 2.-tyopwede, 3.-tyopozya, 4.-tyopweda, 5.-tyopwedalyo, 6.-tyopolesya, 7.-tyopola-tyopola, 8.-tyopozyanya)

cause to break, Bakamwaambila Mwami Siame kuti kana kamuzike aaka kayakutyozya bana babantu mungazi nzyokayaka musyokwe. = They told Chief Siame that this brat of a slave will cause the children of the chief's people to be hurt on the look-out platforms which he had built in the bush. (1.-tyolwa, 2.-tyolede, 3.-tyozya, 4.-tyokela, 5.-tyokelalyo, 6.-tyokesya, 7.-tyozya-tyozya, 8.-tyolana)

fall down into, Mpongo yatyumpukila mumugodi wameenda. = The goat fell down into the well. (1.-tyumpukilwa, 2.-tyumpukilide, 3.-tyumpukizya, 4.-tyumpukilila, 5.-tyumpukililalyo, 6.-tyumpukilisya, 7.-tyumpukilatyumpukila, 8.-tyumpukizyanya) Also: -culukila, -selemukila.

influence a person either by encouraging or discouraging, Komutyungilila mwana akake kuya kuli bausyi, ndiza inga kaya kupenga. = Persuade the child so that it refuses to go to the father, perhaps it might suffer. Bakatiisole kumutyungilila bantu kuti amuleke mukaintu wakwe pesi walo kwiina ncaakaamba pe. = They tried to discourage him so that he would leave his wife but he said nothing. Mainza nguwaali kutyungilila mweenzinyina kuti amuume musimbi. = Mainza was the one who was encouraging his friend to beat the girl. (1.-tyungililwa, 2.-tyungilide, 3.-tyungilizya, 4.-tyungilila, 5.-tyungililalyo, 6.-tyungililisya, 7.-tyungi-lila-tyungilila, 8.-tyumgililana) Also: -cilaika.

be carried away, Chimuka naali kwiimba bobuya takesyi kankobela antela kalumbu kalikke kali kulila pe, awalo Iwakwe wali kulila akutyuuma, ilaloka akweenda misozi. = When Chimuka was singing in this way, it was not only the hand-piano or the one-stringed musical bow which was sounding, he also was weeping and was carried away with emotion, the tears were falling and running down. (1.-tyuumwa, 2.-tyuumide, 3.-tyuumya, 4.-tyuumina, 5.-tyuuminalyo, 6.-tyuumisya, 7.-tyuuma-tyuuma, 8.-tyuuminana)

be light, easy, Cibwantu eeci cauba kapati. = This sweet-beer is very light. Kuti bantu babeleka antoomwe, mulimo ulauba. = If people work together the work becomes easy. (1.-ubizyigwa, 2.-ubide, 3.-ubya, 4.-ubila, 5.-ubilalyo, 6.-ubisya, 7.-uba-uba, 8.-ubizyanya)

treat lightly, rt. -uba, Nchimunya uubaasya kaambo kakali kalemu. = Nchimunya is treating lightly a matter which is serious. Also: -ubya-ubya. (1. ubaasigwa, 2.-ubaasyide, 3.-ubaasyizya, 4.-ubaazyizya, 5.-ubaazyizyalyo, 6.-ubaasyisya, 7.-ubaasya-ubaasya, 8.-ubaasyanya)

be easy, be light, be soft, rt.uba, Cauba-uba cibulo eeci kubweza sunu. = Today this bucket is easy to carry. Ncuuba-uba kwiiya Chinyanja kwiinda kwiiya Chitonga. = It is easier to learn Nyanja than Tonga. (Used as noun: Mapepe aankuku mmauba-uba kwiinda musenga = The feathers of chickens are lighter than sand. Masusu akwe akali kusalala alimwi mauba-uba. = Her hair was bright and also soft.)

slight a person, show disrespect, Ncibi kuubaula bantu bapati. = It is bad to show disrespect to the elders. Also: -epula, -uula. (1.-ubaulwa, 2.-ubaulide, 3.-ubauzya, 4.-ubawida, 5.-ubawidalyo, 6.-ubaulisya, 7.-ubaula-ubaula, 8.-ubaulana)
  • relieve pain, Wakanjila nzila yakali kuya kujwe kwakali tunambi kutegwa akaubaule mutwe. = He entered the path going eastwards where there was beer so that he could relieve the head's troubles.

be disgraceful, Kulwana mubbola ncintu cuubika kapati. = Fighting during a football match is quite despicable. (1.-ubikwa, 2.-ubikide, 3.-ubikizya, 4.-ubikila, 5.-ubikilalyo, 6.-ubikisya, 7.-ubika-ubika, 8.-ubikana) Also: -sampuzya
  • make light, Koubika mundyoli, utalemi kapati. = Make the mundyoli light, let it not be thick. Also: -ubya-ubya.

crowd, as children around a person, Baleli bacisi kuti basika kucibaka kumwi, bana inga baile kuubila mbuli nzinini. = When the leaders of the country come to a certain place, the children just crowd around like flies. (1.-ubililwa, 2.-ubilide, 3.-ubilizya, 4.-ubilila, 5.-ubililalyo, 6.-ubililisya, 7.-ubila-ubila, 8.-ubililana)
  • be easy, Wakazyiba kuti mulimo wakwe ulamuubila. = He knew that the work was easy for him.
  • form, as skin on liquid, Naakaakulanga munongo mwakali cibwantu, wakajana caubila. = When he went over to look in the pot where the sweet-beer was, he found it had a skin on top.

surround, Bantu baubilila muntu uzyana. The people are surrounding the dancer. Nziniini zyaubilila answi zibolede. Flies cluster around rotten fish.
  • form cream, as milk, Mafwuta aubilila atalaa mabisi. The butter has formed on top of the milk.

smoke, become misty or hazy, Ijulu lyoonse lyaubingana sikunku. = The whole sky has become hazy with a mist. (1.-ubinganwa, 2.-ubingene, 3.-ubinganya, 4.-ubinganina, 5.-ubinganinalyo, 6.-ubinganisya, 7.-ubingana-ubingana, 8.-ubinganizyanya)
become soft or light, Masusu akwe akatalikide kusubila camana kaaubukide kapati. Her hair began to go brown and became very light.

harm a person's name, show disrespect, Basankwa baubula nabutema. = The boys are showing disrespect to the unmarried. Cintu cakali kumuubula kapati mbucakolwa bwakwe. = The thing which really gave him a bad name was his drunkenness. Bana bavwuule inga baile kulyuubula bulemu. = Promiscuous people are just ruining their own dignity. Amwi mapenzi ngotubona tulyeetela caali, tulyuubula tobeni. = Some sufferings we deliberately bring upon ourselves, we. drag ourselves down. Also: -sampula. (1.-ubulwa, 2.-ubwide, 3.-ubuzya, 4.-ubwida, 5.-ubwidalyo, 6.-ubulisya, 7.-ubula-ubula, 8.-ubulana)

release pressure, Cisyu ncindayumwide cali cilemu ono caubuluka nkaambo cimwi casambalwa. = The vegetables which I carried were heavy now they are lightened because some has been sold. (1.-ubulukwa, 2.-ubulukide, 3.-ubulusya, 4.-ubulukila, 5.-ubulukilalyo, 6.-ubulukisya, 7.-ubuluka-ubuluka, ubulusyanya) Also: -ononoka.

be released, Nindataningabetekwa munkuta ndaliyoowede, ono ndaubulukwa nkaambo tiindajanwa mulandu. = Before I was tried in court I was afraid, but now I am released because I was found innocent. Also: -ononokwa.

relieve a person of part of a load, Ndabaubulula mukuli ngubajisi nindabanyamwida zimwi. = I relieved them of part of the load when I carried some things for them. Basimbi baubulula bacembele kubweza zintu. = The girls are helping the old lady to carry things. (1.-ubululwa, 2.-ubulwide, 3.-ubuluzya, 4.-ubulwida, 5.-ubulwidalyo, 6.-ubululisya, 7.-ubulula-ubulula, 8.-ubululana) Also: -lemununa.

show disrespect, Ncibi kuubuula bapati. = It is bad to disrespect the elders. Also: -ubaula, -ubula. (1.-ubuulwa, 2.-ubwiide, 3.-ubuuzya, 4.-ubwiida, 5.-ubwiidalyo, 6.-ubuulisya, 7.-ubuula-ubuula, 8.-ubuulana)

make light of, belittle, Kaambo aaka nkapati, nywe mwiile kukaubya. = This affair is serious, but you are just making little of it. (1.-ubizyigwa, 2.-ubide, 3.-ubya, 4.-ubila, 5.-ubilalyo, 6.-ubisya, 7.-ubya-ubya, 8.-ubizyanya)
  • make thin or watery, Uujika wacuubya kapati cisyu. = The one who is cooking has made the vegetables very watery.

dishonour, Kuubyaubya majwi abapati mbufwubafwuba. = It is foolishness to disrespect the words of the elders. Kulyuubya-ubya tacipi bulemu. = To belittle oneself is not honourable. Also: -ubaasya.
  • make light, Bacuubya-ubya cintele, ncicatanona akunona. = They have made the mash of groundnuts too light, that is why it has no taste at all.
  • speak softly, Koubya-ubya jwi nolaya bana. = Soften your voice when you are giving advice to children.
  • utter an unvoiced sound as b,g,d,z.
release tension or tiredness, Nobakamulemununa wakalyuufwide. Wakati, "Ifwuu!" = When they took the load from him he expressed his relief. He said "Ifwuu."

be caught in the rain, rt -wa (fall), Waugwa mvwula ncali mutete mubili oonse. = S/he was caught in the rain that is why the whole body is wet. (1.-ugwa, 2.-ugidwe, 3.-ugwizya, 4.-ugwilwa, 5.-ugwilwalyo, 6.-ugwisyigwa, 7.-ugwa-ugwa, 8.-ugwizyanya)

persuade, entice, Nokuba kuti ooyu mweenzu ulaula bukoko bunji, mmusilikani, alimwi uukauka bantu kutegwa bamwaambile twamaseseke. = Though this visitor buys much beer, he is a policeman, and he is enticing the people to tell him secret information. (1.-ukaukwa, 2.-ukaukide, 3.-ukauzya, 4.-ukaukila, 5.-ukaukilalyo, 6.-ukaukisya, 7.-ukauka-ukauka, 8.-ukaukana) Also: -ongelezya, -sepa-sepa.
  • pretend to be sincere, Musimbi ooyu ukuukauka buyo, takuyandi. = The girl is only pretending, she does not love you.

pretend, be insincere, Bamwi basankwa balayanda kuukaula basimbi kutegwa babazumine. = Some men like to pretend to be sincere towards girls so that they agree to their wishes. (1.-ukaulwa, 2.-ukawide, 3.-ukauzya, 4.-ukawida, 5.-ukawidalyo, 6.-ukaulisya, 7.-ukaula-ukaula, 8.-ukaulana) Also: -upaika.
  • gather secret information Also: -una-una

buy, Musimbi waula cisani cibotu. The girl has bought a nice dress. Ndakaula cisani camyeengwe-myeengwe. = I bought a striped dress. (1.-ulwa, 2.-ulide, 3.-ulisya,/-uzya 4.-ulila, 5.-ulilalyo, 6.-ulisya, 7.-ula-ula, 8.-ulana)
  • bribe, (-ula makulo), Tacili cintu cibotu kuula makulo kutegwa uvwunwe mulandu. = It is not good to bribe so as to avoid being given a case.
barter, trade in kind, Twaulana nkuku abaacisya amali masyoonto. = I traded a chicken with my uncle today for a small amount of money.

name, Ino uulya bakamuulika kuti nguni? = What name did they give that one? Bamacembele baulika mwana munanda. = The old women are naming the child in the house. Bantu bakamuulika mucembele izina lya Naakkoyo mbobakamubona kuti ulaa moyo muyumu. = The people gave the old lady the name of Naakkoyo since they say she had a strong heart. (1.-ulikwa, 2.-ulikide, 3.-ulisya, 4.-ulikila, 5.-ulikilalyo, 6.-ulikisya, 7.-ulika-ulika, 8.-ulikana)

name one another, rt. ulika, Swebo mumukowa wesu tulaulikana kubelesya mazina abamasyaaneene. Within our clan we name one another using the names of our ancestors. (1.-ulikanwa, 2.-ulikanide, 3.-ulikanya, 4.-ulikanina, 5.-ulikaninalyo, 6.-ulikanisya, 7.-ulikana-ulikana, 8.-ulikaninana)
  • sell at fair price, be affordable, Cisani eeci cilaulikana. = This cloth is sold at a fair price.

nickname, rt. -ulika, Eeli zina talili lyakwe, ndyakuulikizya buyo. = This name is not her ritual name it is just a nick-name. Also: -antikizya. (1.-ulikizyigwa, 2.-ulikizyide, 3.-ulikizyisya, 4.-ulikizyizya, 5.-ulikizyizyalyo, 6.-ulikizyisya, 7.-ulikizya-ulikizya, 8.-ulikizyanya)

buy for somone, rt. -ula, Mwakkomana basa nomujisi basankwa bamuulila madeleensi. = You are happy, my friends, who have boys to buy you dresses. (1.-ulilwa, 2.-ulilide, 3.-ulilizya, 4.-ulilila, 5.-ulililalyo, 6.-ulilisya, 7.-ulilaulila, 8.-ulilana)
have bought for, rt. -ula, Mainza wakalomba Michelo kuti amupe Mutinta zintu zyakusama nzyaakamuulilide. Mainza asked Michelo to give Mutinta things to wear which he had bought for her.

sell, cause to buy, rt. -ula, Mebo ndaulisya nkuku zyobilo. = I have sold two chickens myself. (1.-ulisyigwa, 2.-ulisyide, 3.-ulisya, 4.-ulisyizya, 5.-ulisyizyalyo, 6.-ulisyisya, 7.-ulisya-ulisya, 8.-ulisyanya)

scorch, apply smoke to bees, Wazwisya ceeya cabuci mumpako, kuyandika kuzyuuluba nzuki amulilo kutegwa zizwe. = When you are removing a honey-comb from a hole, you need to smoke the bees so that they come out. Basankwa bauluba ngulube kutegwa cuubaube kugusya boya. = The boys are scorching the pig so that it becomes easy to remove the hair. Also: -uluzya, -puzula (as fire does)s, -nanaula or -natuula (as the sun does) (1.-ulubwa, 2.-ulubide, 3.-ulubya, 4.-ulubila, 5.-ulubilalyo, 6.-ulubisya, 7.-uluba-uluba, 8.-ulubana)

run headlong, Chakolwa waulubala kutija kuumwa. Chakolwa ran headlong fleeing from the attack. (1.-ulubalwa, 2.-ulubele, 3.-ulubazya, 4.-ulubalila, 5.-ulubalilalyo, 6.-ulubalisya, 7.-ulubala-ulubala, 8.-ulubalilana.
char, rt. -uluba, Kamuuluba-uluba ngulube boya bupye. = Singe the pig so that the hair is burnt.

welcome by ululating, Kamuulubwizya beenzu basika. = Ululate, the visitors have arrived. Bamakaintu balaulubwizya nobakuzyika mooye. = The women ululate when they initiate a girl. (1.-ulubwizyigwa, 2.-ulubwizyide, 3.-ulubwizya, 4.-ulubwizyizya, 5.-ulubwizyizyalyo, 6.-ulubwizyisya, 7.-ulubwizya-ulubwizya, 8.-ulubwizyanya) Also: -uma ngoloolo, -olobwezyas, -pululusya, -cuulubwizya.

scorch with, rt. -uluba, Twali kubelesya muzenge kuulubya boya bwangulube. = We were using a flaming torch of grass to remove the hair of the pig. (1.-ulubwa, 2.-ulubide, 3.-ulubya, 4.-ulubila, 5.-ulubilalyo, 6.-ulubisya, 7.-ulubya-ulubya, 8.-ulubana) cf. -uluzya.

fly, Tuyuni tulauluka. = The birds are flying. Ba Kaunda bakauluka andeke kuzwa ku Zambia kuya ku Tanzania. = The president flew by plane from Zambia going to Tanzania. (1.-ulukwa, 2.-ulukide, 3.-ulusya, 4.-ulukila, 5.-ulukilalyo, 6.-ulukisya, 7.-uluka-uluka, 8.-ulusyanya)
  • be beyond one's understanding, fly over one's head, (idiomatic) Mebo cikananwa waawa canduuluka. = As for myself, what is being discussed here is beyond my understanding.

swoop down in flight, Kainga kaulukila kujata nkuku. = The falcon is swooping down to catch the chicken. (1.-ulukilwa, 2.-ulukilide, 3.-ulukizya, 4.-ulukila, 5.-ulukilalyo, 6.-ulukilisya, 7.-ulukila-ulukila, 8.-ulukilana)
fly a lot, Inkanga tiiulukisyi pe. = A guinea-fowl does not fly much. (1.-ulukwa, 2.-ulukide, 3.-ulusya, 4.-ulukila, 5.-ulukilalyo, 6.-ulukisya, 7.-ulukisya-ulukisua, 8.-ulusyanya)

ignore, Ooyu mwana tafwambaani kuvwiila, ulaulula nobaita bapati. = This child does not respond quickly, it ignores the elders when they call. (1.-ululwa, 2.-ulwide, 3.-uluzya, 4.-ulwida, 5.-ulwidalyo, 6.-ululisya, 7.-ulula-ulula, 8.-ululana) Also: -uzya, -wiika.

loose focus, Naakalema kuswiilila, wakatalika kuululala. = When he was tired of listening, he began to loose concentration. (1.-ululalwa, 2.-ululele, 3.-ululazya, 4.-ululalila, 5.-ululalialyo, 6.-ululalisya, 7.-ululala-ululala, 8.-ululalinana)

be blown away, rt. -uluka, e.g Caululuka ciluli lyasika muwo munji. = The roof was blown away when the great wind came. Makweelele akaululuka lyakaboola kambizyi. = The maize leaves were blown away when the whirlwind came. (1.-ululukwa, 2.-ululukide, 3.-ululuzya, 4.-ululukila, 5.-ululukilalyo, 6.-ululukisya, 7.-ululuka-ululuka, 8.-ululusyanya) Also: -peuluka, peepuka, -peluluka.

blow away, as wind does to something, Kambizyi kazyuululula zisani. = The whirlwind blew away the clothes. Bakaululula mavwu kutegwa babone muwo nkowakali kuya. = They threw the soil in the air to see to where the wind was blowing. (1.-ulululwa, 2.-ululwide, 3.-ululuzya, 4.-ululwida, 5.-ululwidalyo, 6.-ulululisya, 7.-ulululaululula, 8.-ulululana)

wave, as flag or handkerchief, rt. -uluka, Nguni ululuşya kasani? = Who is waving a handkerchief? Basicikolo baululusya tusani kulaya bayi babo. = The pupils are waving flags to say goodbye to their teachers. (1.-ululusyigwa, 2.-ululusyide, 3.-ululusya, 4.-ululusyigwa, 5.-ululusyizyalyo, 6.-ululusyisya, 7.-ululusya-ululusya, 8.-ululusyanya)

ululate, Basimpongo balaululuzya kunze amulundu. = The herders are ululating behind the hill. (1.-*ululuzyıgwa*, 2.-*ululuzyide*, 3.*ululuzya* 4.-*ululuzyızya*, 5.-*ululuzyızyalyo*. 6.-*ululuzyisya*, 7.-*ululuzya-ululuzya*, 8.-*ululuzyanya*) Also: -*uma ngoloolo*.

jump about, as hens for food from place to place, *Eezi nkuku zilaulumpila*. = These chickens are jumping from place to place looking for food. (1.-*ulumpilwa*, 2.-*ulumpilide*, 3.-*ulumpizya*, 4.-*ulumpilila*, 5.-*ulumpililalyo*, 6.-*ulumpilisya*, 7.-*ulumpila-ulumpila*, 8.-*ulumpizyanya*)
  • grow without producing seeds, *Mapopwe akaile kuulumpila, taakabbala*. = The maize stalks grew high, they did not produce grain in the cobs.

make oneself busy, be occupied doing something, *Mubbi ulalyuulunganya munanda yabantu batako*. = The thief is making himself busy in the house when the owner is not there. *Nzala yabaulunganya babwa*. = The hunger keeps the dogs busy foraging for food. (1.-*ulunganyizyigwa*, 2.-*ulungenye*, 3.-*ulunganya*, 4.-*ulunganina*, 5.-*ulunganinalyo*, 6.-*ulunganisya*, 7.-*ulunganyaulunganya*, 8.-*ulunganyizyanya*)
  • be unkempt, *Aaba bana tabalikamuni, baide kuulunganya masusu*. = These children have not combed their hair, they are just unkempt. Also: -*vwulunganya*, -*upunganya*, -*pupunganya*.

cause to fly away, rt. -*uluka*, e.g *Kotuulusya tuyuni, tulazimana nyemu*. = Chase those little birds away, they will finish off the groundnuts. (1.-*ulusyigwa*, 2.-*ulusyide*, 3.-*ulusya*, 4.-*ulusyizya*, 5.-*ulusyizyalyo*, 6.-*ulusyisya*, 7.-*ulusya-ulusya*, 8.-*ulusyanya*)
  • cause to fly, rt. -*uluka*, *Sunu abalo basimbi balaulusya ndeke*. Nowadays women also fly aeroplanes. *Muwo waulusya mapepa*. = The wind makes the papers blow away.

scorch with, rt. -ulula, Basankwa bakayuuluzya muzwenge ngulube kutegwa boya bufwambaane kuzwa. = The boys scorched the pig with a bundle of lighted grass so that the hair would come off easily. (1.-uluzyigwa, 2.-uluzyizye, 3.-uluzya, 4.-uluzyizya, 5.-uluzyizyalyo, 6.-uluzyisya, 7.-uluzyauluzya, 8.-uluzyanya) Also: -ulubya.
  • ignore, Kuuluzya kulaigwa ciletela mapenzi. = To ignore advice brings sufferings. Also: -wiika.

beat, Kamukauma kabwa kalya mayi aankuku. = Beat the dog which is eating the chickens eggs. Munsanje *uuma* bana bazimizya ŋombe = Munsanje is beating the children who lost the cattle. (1.-umwa, 2.-umide, 3.-umya, 4.-umina, 5.-uminalyo, 6.-umisya, 7.-uma-uma, 8.-umana)
  • fight with fists, Chitebenta wakalicizyi *kuuma nyindi* akutingaana kamando. = Chitebenta knew how to box and to wrestle.
  • shake the head, Munene wakauma

naakamvwa makani. = The old man shook his head when he heard the news.
  • ululate, Bamakaintu bakali kuuma

basololi nibakasika. = The women were ululating when the leaders arrived. Also: -ulubwizya, -ululula, -pululuzya.
  • fail to rise, (idiomatic use) Naakamana kuluka mulwazi wakali kwiide kuuma mutwe ansi. = When the patient had vomited he was just banging his head off the ground, i.e. unable to rise from the ground.
  • kick, Naakalikutambisya mbongolo, yakamuuma mulazyi. = When he was training the donkey, it kicked him.
  • beat water with hands, -uma ntinta, uma nkubu.
  • fool, Wakazyiba kuti bakamuuma *pemba.* = He knew that they had fooled him.
  • beat the elbow, Wakalyuuma ku*kakokola.* = She beat her elbow. i.e. She was grateful for having escaped a danger.
  • be fortunate, *Ndalyuuma ankumo.* = I strike myself on the forehead, i.e. a sign that one has been fortunate.

cause to fight with one another, rt. -uma Sunu njanda kubaumanya bana mbone utiikomwe. = Today I want to make the children fight to see who will be defeated. Also: -Iwanisya. (1.-umanyizigwa, 2.-umanyizide, 3.-umanya, 4.-umanyizyizya, 5.-umanyizyizyalyo, 6.-umanyizyisya. 7.-umanya-umanya, 8.-umanyizyanya)
  • smash together, Musankwa mubi waumanya mitwe bana. = The bad boy banged the heads of the children together.
  • reason together, Aano mpotukkede kuli kaambo, katuumanya mitwe. = There is a problem here where we are seated, let us bring our heads together to solve it.

plait or smooth one's hair by making it into little tufts, smear hair with red ochre, Basimbi bakaindi bakali kuyandisya *kuumba nsuki.* = Girls of long ago were fond of plaiting their hair into little tufts. (1.-umbwa, 2.-umbide, 3.-umbya, 4.-umbila, 5.-umbilalyo, 6.-umbisya, 7.-umba-umba, 8.-umbana) Also: -pukila masusu, -zinga muntiki
  • plait hair into long tapering cone, Kaindi Baila bakali *kuumba nsuku* amitwe yabo kwiinda mukunanika masusu abo amaumba avwelenganizidwe amusila kutegwa kababonwa mubwizu bulamfwu. = Long ago the Baila used to plait their hair into long tapering cones which was formed by mixing butter and red ochre to enable them to be seen in tall grass. (while hunting)
soothe, Koumbaumba mwana aleke kulila. = Soothe the child so that it stops crying. Also: -umbulizya.

heap firewood on the fire, Baumbika *nkuni* amulilo kutegwa cibizwe cisyu. = They heap firewood on the fire so that the vegetables get cooked. Basankwa bakaumbika *nkuni* nibakali kwaana masiku. = The boys heaped firewood on the fire when they were telling stories at night. (1.-umbikwa, 2.-umbikide, 3.-umbikizya, 4.-umbikila, 5.-umbikilalyo, 6.-umbikisya, 7.-umbika-umbika, 8.-umbikilana)

be lonely, Nobakamwaika basicikolo, bamayi bakaumbilwa. = When the pupils had gone away, the teachers were lonely. Also: -lendelelwa. (2.-umbilide, 3.-umbilizya, 4.-umbilila, 5.-umbililalyo, 6.-umbilisya, 7.-umbilwaumbilwa, 8.-umbililana)

fade away, Mapenzi anzala akaumbuka mbuli kuti ngusikunku. = The pains of hunger disappeared as if it was a mist. (1.-umbukwa, 2.-umbukide, 3.-umbusya, 4.-umbukila, 5.-umbukilalyo, 6.-umbukisya, 7.-umbuka-umbuka, 8.-umbukana)

quieten a baby by rocking it, caressing it, singing to it, etc. Batusiila kuumbulizya mwana baama. = Mother left us to quieten the baby. Batumbu baumbulizya mwana uuciswa. = The mother is rocking the sick child. Eci ciimbo ncakuumbulizya mwana nalila. = This song (lullaby) is used to soothe the child when it is crying. (1.-umbulizyigwa, 2.-umbulizyide, 3.-umbulizya, 4.-umbulizyizya, 5.-umbulizyizyalyo, 6.-umbulizyisya, 7.-umbulizya-umbulizya, 8.-umbulizyanya) Also: -umba-umbas, -bumba-bumba,-omba-omba.

dry up, as dew, Izuba nilyakatalika kutanta, mume wakatalika kuumbuluka. = When the sun began to rise the dew began to dry up. (1.-umbulukwa, 2.-umbulukide, 3.-umbulukizya, 4.-umbulukila, 5.-umbulukilalyo, 6.-umbulukisya, 7.-umbuluka-umbuluka, 8.-umbulukana)

shell mealies, Bamacembele baumbulula mapopwe aamweesyo. = The old women are shelling maize for the last funeral ritual. (1.-umbululwa, 2.-umbulwide, 3.-umbuluzya, 4.-umbulwida, 5.-umbulwidalyo, 6.-umbululisya, 7.-umbulula-umbulula, 8.-umbululana or -umbulwidana) Also: -buulula, -senkemuna, -bumbulula.

shell by using something, rt. -umbulula, Kamundipa cinkonti, ndayanda kuumbuluzya mapopwe. = Give me a shelled cob of maize, I want to use it to shell the maize. Also: -buuluzya.
  • make quiet, Kamuumbuluzya bana bacimvwa kulila. = Quieten the children they are tired crying. Also: -umbulizya.

be round and smooth, Kabwe nkumwali kukwiya takanaumbusana. = The stone which you were grinding is not yet round and smooth. (1.-umbusanwa, 2.-umbusene, 3.-umbusanya, 4.-umbusanina, 5.-umbusaninalyo, 6.-umbusanisya, 7.-umbusana-umbusana, 8.-umbusanizyanya) Also: -bumbusana, -bulungana.

make round, Twacikonzya kuumbusanya kabwe nkutwali kukwiya. = We have managed to make the little stone smooth and round with which we were grinding. (1.-umbusanyizyigwa, 2.-umbusanyizyizye, 3.-umbusanya, 4.-umbusanyizyizya, 5.-umbusanyizyizya-lyo, 6.-umbusanyizyisya, 7.-umbusanya-umbusanya, 8.-umbusanyizyanya)
be in a round and smooth state, Kabwe aka kaliumbusene. = That pebble is round and smooth.

plane wood, make smooth, Basimbi balapwaya atubwe ntubaumbusika. = The girls crush with little stones which they made smooth. (1.-umbusikwa, 2.-umbusikide, 3.-umbusikizya, 4.-umbusikila, 5.-umbusikilalyo, 6.-umbusikisya, 7.-umbusika-umbusika, 8.-umbusikana)
swing, rt. -umba, Bana ba-lalyuumbwa mumusamu. = The children are swinging themselves on the tree. (2.-umbide, 3.-umbizya, 4.-umbizyizya, 5.-umbizyizyalyo, 6.-umbisya, 7.-umbwaumbwa, 8.-umbizyanya)

drowse, drop one's head when hungry, Ulaumfwula oyo wafwa nonzi. = That one is dozing who is sleepy. Bacembele balaumfwula nkaambo bali kunkolola. = The old woman is drowsy because she was at the initiation ceremony. Also: -uvwila, -omfwola. (1.-umfwulwa, 2.-umfwide, 3.-umfwizya, 4.-umfwida, 5.-umfwidalyo, 6.-umfwulisya, 7.-umfwula-umfwula, 8.-umfwidana)

throw oneself down on the ground, rt. -uma, Ciindi cadilwe bamakaintu balalyuumina mizinga ansi. = During the funeral the women throw themselves on the ground. (1.-uminwa, 2.-uminide, 3-uminizya, 4.-uminina, 5.-umininalyo, 6.-uminisya, 7.-umina-umina, 8.-uminana)
  • make bricks for, Kamunduumina zitina ndiyake caanda cangulube. = Make bricks for me so that I build a pig-sty.

drive cattle out for grazing, Mumwezi wa Kunkumuna-masamu balimi baumizya nombe zyabo mumyuunda. = In the month of July the farmers send out their cattle into the fields. (1.-umizyigwa, 2.-umizyide, 3.-umizya, 4.-umizyizya, 5.-umizyizyalyo, 6.-umizyisya, 7.-umizya-umizya, 8.-umizyanya)

burn, *Baumpa syokwe* *bana nibali kusobana.* = The children burned the bush when they were playing. *Kamuumpa mabibi kumuunda.* = Set fire to the piles of chopped wood at the field. (1.-umpwa, 2.-umpide, 3.-umpya, 4.-umpila, 5.-umpilalyo, 6.-umpisya, 7.-umpa-umpa, 8.-umpana)
  • brand cattle, *Kamuumpa nombe* *zyanu ansimbi kutegwa zyaando kazili-* *bonya.* = Brand your cattle with a branding iron so that the mark can be easily seen. Also: -ccisa.

cleanse by celebrating, *Bakayanda kuti bamuumpaule bajaye* *kantu kakumusekelela akaambo kakuzwa* *kwakwe muntolongo.* = They wanted to cleanse him by killing some little thing to celebrate because of his release from prison. (1.-umpaulwa, 2.-umpawide, 3.-umpauzya, 4.-umpawida, 5.-umpawidalyo, 6.-umpaulisya, 7.-umpaula-umpaula, 8.-umpawidana) Also: -umpuula.
cast off evil spirits, *Kwakacitwa pobwe lyakulyuumpauzya.* = A feast was celebrated to cast off evil spirits.

make a feast for, *Muvwimi naakajoka kubanamizyaabo, ba-* *mausyi bakamuumpawida bakamwaanga* *mpola isubila kululyo.* = When the hunter returned to his relatives, those on his father's line made a feast for him, they tied a red bracelet on his right arm.

weld, *Baumpilila cibu-* *lo canamutendele bataata.* = Father is welding a metal part of the bicycle. *Bataata baumpilila jamba lyakatyoka.* = Father is welding a broken plough. (1.-umpililwa, 2.-umpilide, 3.-umpilizya, 4.-umpililila, 5.-umpilililalyo, 6.-umpililisya, 7.-umpilila-umpilila, 8.-umpililana)
  • produce smoke for keeping out bad spirits, *Wakaleta musamu waku-* *samba akuumpilila.* = He brought medicine for washing and fumigating to produce smoke for driving out evil spirits. Also: -fwukutila.

fumigate under a blanket with charms, *Bakamuumpilizya mu-* *samu waluwo.* = They fumigated him with the smoke of charms to drive out the evil spirits.
  • cause to weld, *Mulilo waku-* *umpilizya taujaniki koonse-koonse, alimwi* *oomu muujanika uladula.* = The fire for welding is not found everywhere and again where it is found it is expensive.

bang against, *Ibbwe* *lyanduumpula amunwe.* = The stone had banged against my toe. *Mwana wawa* *naalyuumpula amunwe.* = The child fell when he knocked her toe against something. Also: -fwumpula, -nontola. (1.-umpulwa, 2.-umpwide, 3.-umpuzya, 4.-umpwida, 5.-umpwidalyo, 6.-umpulisya, 7.-umpula-umpula, 8.-umpulana)
  • shave off completely, *Bakaintu* *bakali kusakulwa minkulu, kuumpulwa.* = Women used to have their hair cut and shaved off completely.

strip off bark, beat bark as for making cloth, *Kamuumputa zisa-* *mu makwa azwe.* = Strip the trees so that the bark comes off. (1.-umputwa, 2.-umputide, 3.-umputya, 4.-mputila, 5.-umputilalyo, 6.-umputisya, 7.-umputa-umputa, 8.-umputana)
  • beat, as bark when making clothes, *Basimbi bakaindi bakalicizyi kuu-* *mputa loozi Iwakulusya maaya.* = The girls of long ago knew how to make the fibres soft for weaving the maaya skirts. *Naakamana kukama, wakaumputa miya-* *nda yamundolomena, elyo malosi asa-lala* *azwa kumiyanda wakaalosezya mulukaye* *mwakali mukupa.* = When he had finished milking he beat the roots of the

tree, thereupon bright drops came out from the roots which he made drop into the potsherd where the milk was. Also: -umpula.
  • hit heavily, *Kamuumputa* *cibulo* *eeci coongomane*. = Hammer this iron to bend it. *Luube wayumuka wabweza munsi uyanda kuumputa Malusi*. = Luube arises and takes a pestle wanting to beat Malusi. *Wakalyuumputa mizinga itaambiki*. = She threw herself many times on the ground with great force.

break into pieces, *Baumputa-umputa mabwe limwi bwaba bupandupandu*. = They continued to crush the stones until they were broken into pieces. *Basimbi baumputa-umputa loozi Iwamaaya*. = The girls are scutching the fibres for a maaya skirt. Also: -pwaya-pwaya.

be breakable, Magomwe aabulongo alaumputika kwiinda magomwe aabufwumba bwakaindi. = Clods of clay are more easily broken than clods of old dung. (1.-umputikwa, 2.-umputikide, 3.-umputikizya, 4.-umputikizyizya, 5.-umputikizyizyalyo, 6.-umputikizyisya, 7.-umputika-umputika, 8.-umputikana)

wander about, Muntu moofwu ulaumputila musyokwe. = A blind man is wandering about in the bush. Also: -impita, -ompoteka, -poozeka. (1.-umputilwa, 2.-umputilide, 3.-umputizya, 4.-umputilila, 5.-umputililalyo, 6.-umputilisya, 7.-umputila-umputila, 8.-umputilana)
  • throw oneself down on ground, *Nibasika bacizyi bamufwu, balyuumputila mizinga minji ansi mikali*. = When the sisters of the deceased arrived, they threw themselves heavily on the ground many times.
  • break up for, *Kamunduumputila bufwumba kutegwa ndibikke kabotu* mukalimo kacisyu. = Break up the lumps of dung for me so that I put it in my garden.
rebreak, *Baama baumputula bulongo bwazibiya.* = My mother is rebreaking the lumps of clay for a pot.

hit with, *Naakali kujaya sicinsuungwe, wakamuumputya mwiini wakeembe.* = When he was killing the mad dog, he used the handle of an axe to hit it. (1.-umputwa, 2.-umputide, 3.-umputya, 4.-umputila, 5.-umputilalyo, 6.-umputisya, 7.-umputya-umputya, 8.-umputana)

cleanse by celebrating, rt. umpaula, *Ncilengwa ca Batonga kuumpuula kuti muntu wazwa muntolongo.* = It is the custom for the Batonga to cleanse a person by celebrating on his/ her release from prison. (1.-umpuulwa, 2.-umpwiide, 3.-umpuuzya 4.-umpwiida, 5.-umpwiidalyo, 6.-umpuulisya, 7.-umpuula-umpuula, 8.-umpwiidana) Also: -umpaula.

keep silence, *Koumuna buyo taata, zilacitika zintu eezi.* = Be quiet my friend, these things happen. *Bantu bakaumuna lyakasika mwami.* = The people were quiet when the chief arrived. (1.-umunwa, 2.-umwine, 3.-umuzya, 4.-umunina, 5.-umuninalyo, 6.-umunisya, 7.-umuna-umuna, 8.-umunizyanya)
  • become peaceful, *Mazuba ano cisi cakaumuna nkaambo nkondo zyakamana.* = These days the country is at peace because the wars have ended.

be quiet, rt. -umuna, *Mwezi noubala nciyumu-yumu bana kuti kabaumunye.* = When the moon shines it is difficult for the children to keep quiet. (1.-umunwa, 2.-umunye, 3.-umuzya, 4.-umunina, 5.-umuninalyo, 6.-umunisya)

appease, silence, pacify, *Kamumuumuzya kulila mweenzinyoko.* = Quieten down your friend so that s/he ceases weeping. Sibbuku ulaumuzya bantu bazwangana. = The headman is pacifying those who are quarreling.
be beaten, Naakali kukama, wakaumwa mulazyi acamba. = When he was milking, he was kicked on the chest. (1.-umwa, 2.-umide, 3.-umya, 4.-umina, 5.-uminalyo, 6.-umisya, 7.-umwa-umwa, 8.-umana)

be in a quiet state, rt, umuna, Bantu bakaile buyo kulangana kumeso, bakatola ciindi kabaumwine buyo. = The people just looked at one another's faces, they took time just being silent. Wakajana amunzi kucuumwine buya wii mbuli kuti kwaanyina bantu. = She found that it was completely quiet at the village as if there were no people. (1.-umunwa, 2.-umwine, 3.-umuzya, 4.-umuzyizya, 5.-umuzyizyalyo, 6.-umuzyisya, 7.-umwine-umwine, 8.-umuzyanya)

beat with a stick, Tacili cibotu kuumya zimboko naa mutatula kubantu. = It is not good to use sjamboks or a whip to beat people. (1.-umwa, 2.-umide, 3.-umya, 4.-umina, 5.-uminalyo, 6.-umisya, 7.-umya-umya, 8.-umana)
  • (idiom) *-umya* musako, Mutinta, mmukaintu wangu, tanduumyi musako. = Mutinta, she is my wife concerning whom no one can beat me with a stick. (Mutinta is legally my real wife and no one can challenge the fact that I have paid the full bride wealth or lubono.)

listen secretly, Mumpelenge ulauna-una nkwatiamvwe maseseke. = A deceitful person listens secretely so that he may pick up hidden information. (1.-unwa-unwa, 2.-unideunide, 3.-unya-unya, 4.-uninina-uninina, 5.-unininalyo-unininalyo, 6.-uninisyauninisya, 7.-una-una- -una-una, 8.-uninana-uninana) Also: -ukaula

cycle fast, Wakabweza ncinga yakwe yauncula kuya kumweenzinyina. = He took his bike and cycled off quickly to his friend. (1.-unculwa, 2.-unculide, 3.-uncuzya, 4.-unculila, 5.-unculilalyo, 6.-unculisya, 7.-unculauncula, 8.-unculana)

smoke, Busi bulaunda ku Musiotunya. = Vapour rises at the Victoria Falls. Murnanda muunda busi, bantu tabayoti kabotu. = In a house where the fire is smoking, people cannot warm themselves properly. Azikulange nkujana kuunduunda biyo kasima munkwandi. = When he looked he found a little nsima steaming in a wooden plate. (1.-undwa, 2.-undide, 3.-undya, 4.-undila, 5.-undilalyo, 6.-undisya, 7.-unda-unda, 8.-undizyanya) Also: -unta, -sunta.

trying to avoid smoke or bad smell, Mulwazi wakakatala kuundauka naakali kufwukutilwa. = The patient was tired of avoiding the smoke when being treated over a steaming pot. (1.-undaukwa, 2.-undaukide, 3.-undausya 4.-undaukila, 5.-undaukilalyo, 6.-undaukisya, 7.-undauka-undauka, 8.-undaukana)

lose one's attractiveness, Bunajempa bwamukopa oyu, waile kuunduka. = Prostitution has disfigured her, she is no longer attractive. (1.-undukwa, 2.-undukide, 3.-undusya, 4.-undukila, 5.-undukilalyo, 6.-undukisya, 7.-unduka-unduka, 8.-undusyanya) Also: -jujuka, -zakala.

rise as smoke from fire, rt. unda, Musanga oyu wakali kuunduluka busi butuba buu. = This cigarette was producing a very white smoke. (1.-undulukwa, 2.-undulukide, 3.-undulusya, 4.-undulukila, 5.-undulukilalyo, 6.-undulukisya, 7.-undulukaunduluka, 8.-undulusyanya)

refuse to listen, Mutinta ulaunduluzya bapati nobasola ku mulaya. = Mutinta refuses to listen to the elders when they give her advice. Ndakomba mutaunduluzyi, mutaciti muuzyamvwide. = I ask you not to refuse to listen, do not pretend you do not hear. (1.-unduluzyigwa, 2.-unduluzyide, 3.-unduluzya, 4.-unduluzyizya, 5.-unduluzyizyalyo, 6.-unduluzyisya, 7.-unduluzya-unduluzya, 8.-unduluzyanya) Also: -wiika.

blaze as bush fire, Butala bwamapopwe boonse bwakaunduma. The whole maize bin was blazing. (1.-undumizyigwa, 2.-undumide, 3.-undu-mya, 4.-undumina, 5.-unduminalyo, 6.-undumisya, 7.-unduma-unduma. 8.-undumizyanya)

be unkempt, Masusu amulwazi akaundungana nkaambo kwakabula umukamuna. = The hair of the patient was unkempt because there was no one to comb it for him. (1.-undunganwa, 2.-undungene, 3.-undunganya, 4.-undunganina, 5.-undunganinalyo, 6.-undunganisya, 7.-undungana-undungana, 8.-undunganizyanya)
be in an unkempt state, Masusu asincinko aluundungene. = The hair of a mad person is unkempt.

blow as wind, buzz, Muwo ulaunga kapati sunu. = The wind is blowing strongly today. Sunu kuunga kawo kabotu. Today a little breeze is blowing nicely. Nzuki zinji zyakali kuunga akuccilila mudaala. Many bees were buzzing around and following the old man. Wakali kunga aboola nkujana mumutiba kuunga nzinini. = When he used to come he would find the flies buzzing around in the dish. (1.-ungwa, 2.-ungide, 3.-ungizya, 4.-ungila, 5.-ungilalyo, 6.-ungisya, 7.-unga-unga, 8.-ungilana)
  • catch the tail of a running beast, Muvwimi naakalwana syuumbwa waka fwambaana kumuunga kumucila mpoona wakamuyasa sumo munsingo akumujaya. = The hunter grabbed the tail of the lion quickly and wounded him in the neck and killed him.
  • rub feet as bees on flowers, Twajana nzuki zinji zyuunga buluba. = We found many bees collecting the nectar.
  • collect, Bana balaunga nseke zyaluyuni. The children are collecting seeds from the luyuni plant.

become withered, Kanene naakaciswa ciindi cilamfwu, mubili wakwe wakaungana. When Kanene was sick for a long time, his body shrivelled up. Also: -babankana. (1.-unganwa, 2.-ungenye, 3.-ungizya, 4.-unganina, 5.-unganinalyo, 6.-unganisya 7.-ungana-ungana, 8.-unganizyanya)
  • change one's facial expression, Akaambo kakubba nombe yabantu, mubbi wakaungana basilikani nibakasika. Because of stealing people's cattle, the thief changed his expression when the police arrived. =

become cool as the sun sinks, Nolyakaunga-unga zuba, wakabasiya. = When it cooled off with the setting of the sun, he left them.
  • without hesitation, Ndaubeleka kabotu mulimo wangu kakunyina abuungwa-ungwa pe. I will carry out my mission without proceeding with less determination.

buzzing around, rt. -unga, Bana bakanyandwa kubona nzuki zinji zyakali kuungilila akuccilila mudaala oyu Namanzuka. The childen were amazed to see bees buzzing around and following the old man Namanzuka. (1.-ungililwa, 2.-ungilide, 3.-ungizya, 4.-ungililila, 5.-ungililalyo, 6.-ungilisya, 7.-ungilila-ungilila, 8.-ungililana
  • drive someone forcibly to do wrong, *Musangu wakali kuungilila Jolezya wakali mukali.* = The ancestral spirit who was driving Jolezya was uncontrollable.

become foolish or dull, *Waunguka musimbi akaambo kakweempuka.* = The girl has become foolish because of immoral behaviour. (1.-ungukwa, 2.-ungukide, 3.-unguzya. 4.-ungukila, 5.-ungukilalyo, 6.-ungukisya, 7.-unguka-unguka, 8.-ungukizyanya)

pour out, remove as water from pot, *Kamuungula meenda mumpoto.* Pour out the water from the pot. *Kamuungula cibwantu tunywe.* = Pour out the sweet beer so that we drink it. (1.-ugulwa, 2.-ungwide, 3.-unguzya, 4.-ungwida, 5.-ungwidalyo, 6.-ungulisya, 7.-ungula-ungula, 8.-ungwidana)
  • cause someone to become foolish, *Ooyu mwana bakamuungula ncatakwe maanu kucikolo.* = They have made this child stupid (with traditional medicines), that is why she has no intelligence at school. *Chigamba wakali muntu ucenjede, mazubaano lubanje Iwamuungula.* = Chigamba was a clever person, nowadays drugs have made him stupid.

be abnormal in behaviour, wander aimlessly, *Muntu wakavwubide ulaungulika nkaambo Iwamumanina lubono Iwakwe.* = The rich man behaved somewhat confused when he lost his wealth. *Twalo otu tucembele nkujana akamwi kayaa kuungulika kuyandaula kazyukulu kako.* = Each of these little old women is found going about in a panic searching for her grandchild. *Ino inga muntu mucembele mbuli bwayooyu uyabuungulika muno mukati kadolopo, ulya nzi?* = Now a person like this old woman who is wandering about in the middle of the town, what does she eat? Also: -ingaila. (1.-ungulikwa, 2.-ungulikide, 3.-ungulisya, 4.-ungulikila, 5.-ungulikilalyo, 6.-ungulikisya, 7.-ungulika-ungulika, 8.-ungulisyanya)
  • be easy to pour, rt. -ungula, *Eeci ceele cilaungulika nkaambo ncuubauba.* = This porridge is easily poured because it is light.
be poured out, recede, rt. ungula, *Cibwantu caunguluka, coonse camanina.* = The sweet-beer was poured out, it is all gone.

pour out the last of the contents, *Koungulula cibwantu kuzwa munongo mpati ucibikke mumunkuli.* = Pour out the last of the sweet-beer from the pot and put it into the large gourd. (1.-ungululwa, 2.-ungulwide, 3.-unguluzya, 4.-ungulwida, 5.-ungulwidalyo, 6.-ungululisya, 7.-ungulula-ungulula, 8.-ungulwidana)

jerk, as the head, *Nibakayanda kufwa bacembele, mutwe wakali kuunguma.* = When the old woman was about to die, the head was jerking. (1.-ungumwa, 2.-ungumide, 3.-ungumya, 4.-ungumina, 5.-unguminalyo, 6.-ungumisya, 7.-unguma-unguma, 8.-ungumizyanya)
  • be lost in thought, *Nibakakkede bakali kwiide kuunguma akaambo kamizeezo njibakajisi mumoyo wabo.* = When he was seated he was just lost because of the thoughts which he had in his heart.
  • wander about, *Iziyanga zinji zilaunguma mumadolopo.* = Many crazy people wander about the towns. *Banyama bakaunguma kuya kooko syuumbwa nkwaakali kutegwa nkwaafwida.* = The animals wandered about over there where it was said the lion had died.

be depressed, sit downcast, *Nkuku yangu yiile kuungumana, ambweni yaciswa.* = My chicken is despondent, it may be sick. Kugunwa kwalo camupa kuungumana. = It is the shame which makes him depressed. (1.-ungumanwa, 2.-ungumene, 3.-ungumanya, 4.-ungumanina, 5.-ungumaninalyo, 6.-ungumanisya, 7.-ungumana-ungumana, 8.-ungumanizyanya) Also: -tungumana.
be in a depressed state, rt. -ungumana, Nsekonzyi kuti bantu kabandilanga lyoonse nseungumene pe. = I am not able to have people always looking at me in the depressed state that I am in.

be shy in having met one's lover, Ino sunu ba Mutinta cilafwa kuungumwa. = To-day Mutinta will die with embarrassment. (2.-ungumide, 3.-ungumya, 4.-ungumina, 5.-unguminalyo, 6.-ungumisya, 7.-ungumwaungumwa, 8.-ungumizyanya)

be foolish, be drugged, Koleka kuunguta mudolopo nkaambo kuli babbi banji. = Stop behaving stupidly in the city because there are many thieves.
